context_brief: whether self-inverting series are automatically Hessian nilpotent
original_question: Suppose P(z) is a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent, so that its inversion pair Q(z) is defined by the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) and its formal inverse G(z) = z + grad Q(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning that its inversion pair satisfies Q(z) = P(z), must every self-inverting polynomial or formal power series automatically be Hessian nilpotent?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the ring $\mathbb{C}[[z]] = \mathbb{C}[[z_1,\dots,z_n]]$ of formal power series in $n$ variables. For $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$, let $\nabla P = (\partial P/\partial z_1,\dots,\partial P/\partial z_n)$ denote its gradient and $\operatorname{Hes} P = (\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\partial z_j)$ its Hessian matrix. Write $o(P)$ for the order of $P$ (the lowest total degree of a nonzero monomial). 

Assume $o(P) \geq 2$ and that $(\operatorname{Hes} P)(0)$ is a nilpotent matrix. Define the formal symmetric map 
$$F(z) = z - \nabla P(z).$$ 
Under these hypotheses $F$ has a formal inverse $G(z)$, which can be written uniquely in the form 
$$G(z) = z + \nabla Q(z)$$ 
for some $Q(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ with $o(Q) \geq 2$. The series $Q$ is called the inversion pair of $P$.

The series $P$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if $\operatorname{Hes} P$ is nilpotent as a matrix over $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ (not merely at $0$). The series $P$ is called self-inverting if its inversion pair satisfies $Q(z) = P(z)$.

Question: Must every self-inverting formal power series (or polynomial) $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ be Hessian nilpotent?
status_search_result: The question was posed as an open problem in the literature on Hessian nilpotent polynomials and their connection with the Jacobian conjecture (via the vanishing conjecture). Available search results discuss this circle of problems but do not indicate a published resolution of whether every self-inverting formal power series is automatically Hessian nilpotent. Status could not be definitively verified.

context_brief: possible failure of the vanishing conjecture for non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent series
original_question: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C such that the quantities Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) do not eventually vanish, or prove that no such example exists?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}[[z]] = \mathbb{C}[[z_1,\dots,z_n]]$ denote the ring of formal power series in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\Delta = \sum_{i=1}^n \partial^2/\partial z_i^2$ be the standard Laplacian. The Hessian of a formal power series $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ is the matrix $\mathrm{Hess}(P) = (\partial^2 P/\partial z_i \partial z_j)_{1 \le i,j \le n}$, and $P$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if $\mathrm{Hess}(P)$ is nilpotent as a matrix over $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ (equivalently, all its eigenvalues are zero, or all coefficients of its characteristic polynomial except the leading one vanish). The Vanishing Conjecture (VC) for $P$ asserts that
$$\Delta^m\bigl(P(z)^{m+1}\bigr) = 0 \quad \text{for all sufficiently large } m \ge 1.$$

Problem. Either exhibit a Hessian nilpotent formal power series $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]] \setminus \mathbb{C}[z]$ (i.e., not a polynomial) for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails — that is, $\Delta^m(P^{m+1}) \ne 0$ for infinitely many $m$ — or prove that no such formal power series exists.
status_search_result: Search results show ongoing study of the Vanishing Conjecture for Hessian nilpotent series, including extensions to Laurent series (where counterexamples exist) and to differential operators (de Bondt's counterexample for non-constant coefficient operators). However, no source found exhibits a non-polynomial HN formal power series in $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ for which VC fails, nor a proof that none exists. The problem appears still open.

original_question: Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 written in the form P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h alpha_i, z i^d with isotropic vectors alpha_i in C^n, and define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k} with an edge between i and j exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero. What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that P(z) is Hessian nilpotent?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n,d,k$ be positive integers with $d\geq 2$. Call a vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n$ isotropic if $\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^2=0$, and write $X(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for the set of isotropic vectors. Consider a homogeneous polynomial $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ of degree $d$ of the special form
$$P(z)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\langle\alpha_i,z\rangle^{d},\qquad \alpha_i\in X(\mathbb{C}^n).$$
(Any such $P$ is automatically harmonic, i.e. $\Delta P=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\partial^2 P/\partial z_j^2=0$.) Say that $P$ is Hessian nilpotent (HN) if its Hessian matrix $\bigl(\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\partial z_j\bigr)_{1\le i,j\le n}$ is a nilpotent matrix of polynomial entries.

Associate to such a representation of $P$ the labeled graph $G(P)$ on vertex set $[k]=\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ in which vertices $i$ and $j$ ($i\neq j$) are joined by an edge if and only if $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\neq 0$.

Problem: Find nontrivial necessary conditions, and find nontrivial sufficient conditions, on the labeled graph $G(P)$ that guarantee $P(z)$ is Hessian nilpotent.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on Hessian nilpotent polynomials connected to the Jacobian conjecture. Subsequent works on HN polynomials and the vanishing conjecture (e.g., Zhao's papers in Annales Polonici Mathematici and J. Pure Appl. Algebra) continue to list characterizing HN polynomials of the form $\sum\langle\alpha_i,z\rangle^d$ via combinatorial/graph data as unresolved; partial results exist (e.g., for small $k$ or linearly independent $\alpha_i$), but no general necessary-and-sufficient graph-theoretic criterion is known.

context_brief: barriers for epsilon times the number of distinct prime factors
original_question: Fix a real number epsilon > 0, let v(m) denote the number of distinct prime factors of the integer m, and call an integer n a barrier for the arithmetic function epsilon v(m) when m + epsilon v(m) <= n for every integer m < n. Are there infinitely many such barriers for at least one choice of epsilon > 0?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer m ≥ 2, let v(m) denote the number of distinct prime factors of m, with v(1) = 0. Given an arithmetic function f : ℤ_{>0} → ℝ_{≥0}, call a positive integer n a barrier for f if 
  m + f(m) ≤ n  for every positive integer m < n.

Question: Does there exist a real number ε > 0 such that there are infinitely many barriers for the arithmetic function f(m) = ε · v(m)?
status_search_result: The question is one of Erdős's open problems on barriers of arithmetic functions. Available sources discuss partial remarks (e.g., that for ε ∈ (0,1] some nontrivial barriers exist, and that the number of barriers grows as ε → 0), but no proof or disproof of the existence of an ε > 0 for which infinitely many barriers exist appears to be established. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Does the collection of known polynomial invariants of degree at most 9 cut out the algebraic variety of 4×4×4 contingency tables (pijk) over C that have tensor rank at most 4, equivalently tables admitting a decomposition pijk = ρAi·σAj·θAk + ρCi·σCj·θCk + ρGi·σGj·θGk + ρTi·σTj·θTk for i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the 64-dimensional complex vector space $V = \mathbb{C}^4 \otimes \mathbb{C}^4 \otimes \mathbb{C}^4$ of $4\times 4\times 4$ tensors $(p_{ijk})_{i,j,k \in \{A,C,G,T\}}$. Let $X \subseteq V$ denote the (Zariski closure of the) set of tensors of tensor rank at most $4$, i.e. tensors admitting a decomposition
$$p_{ijk} = \rho^A_i \sigma^A_j \theta^A_k + \rho^C_i \sigma^C_j \theta^C_k + \rho^G_i \sigma^G_j \theta^G_k + \rho^T_i \sigma^T_j \theta^T_k$$
for some vectors $\rho^a, \sigma^a, \theta^a \in \mathbb{C}^4$ ($a \in \{A,C,G,T\}$). Among the polynomials known to vanish identically on $X$ are: (i) the Strassen commutation relations of degree $5$; (ii) the Landsberg–Manivel polynomials of degree $6$; and (iii) certain symmetrization-type polynomials of degree $9$. Let $J$ be the ideal generated by all such known invariants of degree at most $9$. Question: does the zero locus $V(J) \subseteq V$ coincide set-theoretically with $X$?
status_search_result: The set-theoretic Salmon conjecture for the variety of 4×4×4 complex tensors of border rank at most 4 has been proved. Friedland and Gross gave a proof (arXiv:1104.1776, J. Algebra 2012) showing this variety is cut out by polynomials of degrees 5, 6, and 9 (Strassen, Landsberg–Manivel, and symmetrization equations). A complementary computational proof appears in Bates–Oeding, "Toward a Salmon Conjecture" (Experimental Mathematics, 2011). The ideal-theoretic version (full generators of the prime ideal) remained more delicate, but the set-theoretic question posed here is resolved affirmatively.

original_question: Which projective varieties M in projective space P^n have maximum likelihood degree 1, meaning that for generic data vector (u0, u1, ..., un) the restriction of the likelihood function L(p0, p1, ..., pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · ... · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + ··· + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un) to M has exactly one complex critical point after excluding singular points of M and points where L has poles or zeros?
self_contained_problem:
Work in complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ with homogeneous coordinates $(p_0:p_1:\cdots:p_n)$. For a generic data vector $(u_0,u_1,\ldots,u_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$, define the likelihood function
$$L(p_0,p_1,\ldots,p_n) \;=\; \frac{p_0^{u_0}\, p_1^{u_1}\cdots p_n^{u_n}}{(p_0+p_1+\cdots+p_n)^{u_0+u_1+\cdots+u_n}},$$
which is a rational function on $\mathbb{P}^n$. For an irreducible projective variety $M \subset \mathbb{P}^n$, the maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) of $M$ is defined to be the number of complex critical points of the restriction $L|_M$, where one excludes singular points of $M$ and points at which $L$ has a pole or a zero, and where $(u_0,\ldots,u_n)$ is generic.

Give a geometric characterization of all irreducible projective varieties $M \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ whose ML degree equals $1$.
status_search_result: June Huh (arXiv:1301.2732, "Varieties with maximum likelihood degree one") characterized varieties of ML degree one as exactly the images of reduced A-discriminantal varieties under monomial maps with finite fibers, with the corresponding maximum likelihood estimator given by Kapranov's Horn uniformization. This provides the geometric characterization sought.

original_question: What relationship, if any, does the maximum likelihood degree of an algebraic statistical model have to the convergence properties of numerical statistical algorithms such as iterative proportional scaling and the EM algorithm?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M} \subset \Delta_{n-1}$ be an algebraic statistical model, that is, the intersection with the probability simplex of an irreducible algebraic variety $V \subset \mathbb{C}^n$. Given a data vector $u = (u_1,\dots,u_n) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n$, the maximum likelihood estimation problem on $\mathcal{M}$ consists of maximizing the log-likelihood $\ell_u(p) = \sum_i u_i \log p_i$ over $p \in \mathcal{M}$. The maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) of $\mathcal{M}$ is defined as the number of complex critical points of $\ell_u$ on the smooth locus of $V$ for generic $u$; equivalently, it is the degree of the likelihood correspondence projecting onto data space.

Two classical iterative numerical procedures for approximating maximum likelihood estimates are:
(i) Iterative proportional scaling (also known as iterative proportional fitting), used for hierarchical/log-linear models, which cyclically rescales an estimate so that selected marginals match the empirical marginals;
(ii) The EM algorithm, which alternates between forming the expected complete-data log-likelihood given current parameters and maximizing it.

Determine whether there is a precise mathematical relationship between the ML degree of $\mathcal{M}$ and the convergence properties (e.g., rate of convergence, number of attracting fixed points, basin structure, or global convergence) of iterative proportional scaling and/or the EM algorithm applied to maximum likelihood estimation on $\mathcal{M}$. In particular, formulate and prove (or disprove) quantitative statements connecting the ML degree to such convergence behavior.
status_search_result: No systematic theory linking the ML degree of an algebraic statistical model to the convergence behavior of iterative proportional scaling or the EM algorithm appears to be established. Convergence results for EM (monotone increase, possible local-maximum trapping) and IPS (convergence under positivity and model conditions) are well-studied, but a direct, general quantitative relationship to the ML degree was not identified in available sources. Status appears unverified/unknown.

original_question: For the DNA alignment example whose model M is the set of positive 4×4 matrices (pij) of rank at most 2 and whose likelihood function is L = (∏i pii)^4 · (∏i≠j pij)^2 · (∑i,j pij)^−40, is the matrix (1/40)·[[3,3,2,2],[3,3,2,2],[2,2,3,3],[2,2,3,3]] a global maximum of L?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be the set of positive real $4\times 4$ matrices $P=(p_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le 4}$ of rank at most $2$, with all entries strictly positive. Define the likelihood function
$$L(P) \;=\; \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{4} p_{ii}\Bigr)^{4} \cdot \Bigl(\prod_{i\ne j} p_{ij}\Bigr)^{2} \cdot \Bigl(\sum_{i,j} p_{ij}\Bigr)^{-40}.$$
Determine whether the matrix
$$\hat P \;=\; \frac{1}{40}\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$$
is a global maximum of $L$ on $M$.

status_search_result: The "100 Swiss Francs problem" of Sturmfels was resolved in 2008 by Mingfu Zhu (and elaborated in subsequent work, e.g., Gross–Drton–Sullivant and Hauenstein–Rodriguez–Sturmfels), confirming that the proposed matrix is indeed a global maximum of the likelihood function. The published account "Solving the 100 Swiss Francs Problem" (Math. in Computer Science, 2011) presents the solution.

original_question: Which conditional independence models can actually be realized by multivariate Gaussian distributions on R^n? Equivalently, how can one study the geometry of Gaussian conditional independence models, that is, semi-algebraic subsets of the cone PD_n of positive definite symmetric n×n matrices defined by equations of the form [i ⊥⊥ j | K] = 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{PD}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric positive definite $n\times n$ matrices, identified with the parameter space of centered nondegenerate Gaussian distributions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via their covariance matrices $\Sigma=(\sigma_{ij})$. For a Gaussian random vector $X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ with covariance $\Sigma$, indices $i\neq j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, and a subset $K\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{i,j\}$, the conditional independence statement $X_i\perp\!\!\!\perp X_j\mid X_K$ holds if and only if the $(|K|+1)\times(|K|+1)$ subdeterminant
$$[i\perp\!\!\!\perp j\mid K](\Sigma)\;:=\;\det\Sigma_{(\{i\}\cup K),\,(\{j\}\cup K)}\;=\;0.$$
Define a Gaussian conditional independence (GCI) model to be any semi-algebraic subset of $\mathrm{PD}_n$ that can be defined by a finite collection of polynomial equations of the form $[i\perp\!\!\!\perp j\mid K]=0$.

Problem: Develop a characterization of all conditional independence models on $n$ random variables that are realizable by some multivariate Gaussian distribution on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and study the geometry (irreducible decomposition, dimension, smoothness, singular locus) of GCI models as semi-algebraic subsets of $\mathrm{PD}_n$.
status_search_result: The problem is an active research program in algebraic statistics. Substantial progress has been made: Sullivant and collaborators studied the algebraic geometry of Gaussian CI ideals; Drton and Xiao established smoothness results for many GCI models; and Šimeček proved that the class of Gaussian-representable CI structures admits no finite complete axiomatic characterization, ruling out a finite-rule characterization. A complete characterization of realizable Gaussian CI models remains open in general.

original_question: What is the image of the entropy map H: PD_n → SubMod_n given by H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I) for each principal minor Σ_I of a positive definite symmetric matrix, how does that image intersect the faces of the submodular cone SubMod_n, and what are the fibers of H?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $\mathrm{PD}_n$ denote the open cone of real symmetric positive definite $n\times n$ matrices. For a subset $I\subseteq[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $\Sigma=(\sigma_{ij})\in\mathrm{PD}_n$, write $\Sigma_I$ for the principal submatrix of $\Sigma$ indexed by rows and columns in $I$, with the convention $\det(\Sigma_\emptyset)=1$.

Let $\mathrm{SubMod}_n\subset\mathbb{R}^{2^{[n]}}$ denote the submodular cone, i.e. the set of functions $h:2^{[n]}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $h(\emptyset)=0$ and
$$h(I\cup J)+h(I\cap J)\le h(I)+h(J)\qquad\text{for all }I,J\subseteq[n].$$

Define the entropy map
$$H:\mathrm{PD}_n\longrightarrow\mathrm{SubMod}_n,\qquad H(\Sigma)_I=-\tfrac12\log\det(\Sigma_I)\;\text{(equivalently, up to a constant, }-\log\det(\Sigma_I)\text{)},\quad I\subseteq[n].$$
(The image lies in $\mathrm{SubMod}_n$ because Gaussian entropy is submodular.)

Solve the following:

(a) Characterize the image $H(\mathrm{PD}_n)\subseteq\mathrm{SubMod}_n$ as a semialgebraic subset of $\mathbb{R}^{2^{[n]}}$ (i.e. determine the algebraic and inequality conditions cutting out its closure).

(b) Describe how $H(\mathrm{PD}_n)$ intersects each face of the polyhedral cone $\mathrm{SubMod}_n$ (where faces are defined by setting collections of submodularity inequalities to equality).

(c) Describe the fibers $H^{-1}(h)$ for $h\in H(\mathrm{PD}_n)$: their dimension, topology, and any group action (e.g. by signed diagonal conjugation) whose orbits coincide with generic fibers.
status_search_result: The problem has been actively investigated. Subsequent work (e.g., El Maazouz on the Gaussian entropy map in valued fields, 2021; Ahmadieh–El Maazouz–Sturmfels et al., "Tropicalizing Principal Minors of Positive Definite Matrices," 2024) describes the tropicalization of the image and its relation to the submodular cone via matroid subdivisions, and produces new algebraic inequalities among principal minors. A complete semialgebraic description of the image, of its intersections with all faces of $\mathrm{SubMod}_n$, and of the fibers for general $n$ does not yet appear to be available, so the general problem remains only partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For completely positive trace-preserving (CPT) maps Φ: M_{d1} → M_{d2}, let E(d1,d2) denote the extreme points of the convex set of such channels, and let the closure of E(d1,d2) consist exactly of the CPT maps whose Choi matrix has rank at most d1. How can one characterize, classify, or parameterize this closure for all input dimensions d1 > 2 and arbitrary output dimensions d2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M_d$ denote the algebra of $d\times d$ complex matrices. A linear map $\Phi: M_{d_1} \to M_{d_2}$ is called completely positive and trace-preserving (CPT) if $\Phi \otimes \mathrm{id}_{M_n}$ maps positive semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices for every $n \ge 1$, and $\mathrm{tr}(\Phi(X)) = \mathrm{tr}(X)$ for all $X \in M_{d_1}$. The set of CPT maps from $M_{d_1}$ to $M_{d_2}$ is convex; let $\mathcal{E}(d_1,d_2)$ denote its set of extreme points.

The Choi matrix of $\Phi$ is $C(\Phi) = \sum_{i,j=1}^{d_1} E_{ij} \otimes \Phi(E_{ij}) \in M_{d_1} \otimes M_{d_2}$, where $\{E_{ij}\}$ are the standard matrix units. The Choi rank of $\Phi$ is the rank of $C(\Phi)$, equivalently the minimal number of Kraus operators in a representation $\Phi(X) = \sum_k A_k X A_k^*$.

It is known that the closure $\overline{\mathcal{E}(d_1,d_2)}$ in the topology of the convex set of CPT maps coincides exactly with the set of CPT maps $\Phi: M_{d_1} \to M_{d_2}$ whose Choi rank is at most $d_1$.

Problem: For every $d_1 > 2$ and every $d_2 \ge 1$, give an explicit characterization, classification, or parameterization of the closure $\overline{\mathcal{E}(d_1,d_2)}$ — equivalently, of all CPT maps $\Phi: M_{d_1} \to M_{d_2}$ with Choi rank at most $d_1$.
status_search_result: The case $d_1 = 2$ admits an explicit Kraus parameterization, but for $d_1 > 2$ the problem of characterizing/parameterizing the closure of extreme CPT maps (equivalently, CPT maps with Choi rank at most $d_1$) appears still open. Subsequent work by Ruskai and others (e.g., on extreme points of unital quantum channels) addresses partial cases but not a full parameterization.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Let A be a positive semidefinite block matrix on a d1 d2-dimensional space, written as d2 × d2 blocks A_jk of size d1 × d1, with Σ_j A_jj = M. Can one always find d2 block vectors X_m, each composed of d2 blocks X_jm of size d1 × d1, such that A = (1/d2) Σ_{m=1}^{d2} X_m X_m† and, for every m, Σ_k X_km X_km† = M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d_1, d_2$ be positive integers and let $A$ be a positive semidefinite matrix acting on $\mathbb{C}^{d_1}\otimes \mathbb{C}^{d_2}$. Write $A$ as a $d_2\times d_2$ array of blocks $A_{jk}\in M_{d_1}(\mathbb{C})$ (so $A_{kj}=A_{jk}^\dagger$ and $A=(A_{jk})_{j,k=1}^{d_2}$ is positive semidefinite as an operator on $\mathbb{C}^{d_1 d_2}$), and set
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{d_2} A_{jj}\in M_{d_1}(\mathbb{C}).$$
Prove or disprove: there always exist $d_2$ "block vectors" $X_m$ ($m=1,\dots,d_2$), each consisting of $d_2$ blocks $X_{jm}\in M_{d_1}(\mathbb{C})$ stacked vertically (so $X_m$ is a $d_1 d_2 \times d_1$ matrix with blocks $X_{1m},\dots,X_{d_2 m}$), such that
$$A \;=\; \frac{1}{d_2}\sum_{m=1}^{d_2} X_m X_m^\dagger,$$
and, for every $m\in\{1,\dots,d_2\}$,
$$\sum_{k=1}^{d_2} X_{km} X_{km}^\dagger \;=\; M.$$
(When $d_1=1$ this reduces to the classical Horn lemma stating that any positive semidefinite matrix can be written as an average of rank-one matrices having equal diagonals.)
category_tag: Block matrix decompositions in quantum information
status_search_result: Web searches for this specific block-matrix generalization of Horn's lemma did not yield a definitive resolution. While there is substantial related literature on positive semidefinite block matrix decompositions and quantum analogues of Horn's conjecture, no source directly confirming a proof or disproof of this particular conjecture was found.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Let M_ε be a channel whose output is always ε-close to the maximally mixed state, in the sense ||M_ε(ρ) − I/d|| < ε, and define its polarization Φ_{x,ε} = x I + (1−x) M_ε. For maximal output p-norm multiplicativity, ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), does Φ_{x,ε} satisfy this property for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, at least when ε is sufficiently small? If it does not always satisfy the property, for which values of x and p does it hold, and how do those values depend on ε?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a finite dimension d ≥ 2 and let M_d denote the algebra of d×d complex matrices. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map Φ : M_d → M_d. For a state ρ (density operator) and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, the Schatten p-norm of Φ(ρ) is ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p = (Tr|Φ(ρ)|^p)^{1/p}, and the maximal output p-norm of Φ is

  ν_p(Φ) = sup_ρ ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,

where the supremum is over density operators on C^d. The channel Φ is said to satisfy maximal output p-norm multiplicativity if, for every quantum channel Ω (acting on any finite-dimensional matrix algebra),

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ω).   (*)

For ε > 0, let M_ε be a quantum channel on M_d whose output is always ε-close to the maximally mixed state in the sense that for every density operator ρ,

  ‖M_ε(ρ) − I/d‖ < ε

(in the operator norm). For x ∈ [0,1] define the "polarized" channel

  Φ_{x,ε}(ρ) = x ρ + (1 − x) M_ε(ρ).

Question. Does Φ_{x,ε} satisfy the multiplicativity identity (*) for all 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, at least when ε is sufficiently small? If not, determine for which values of x ∈ [0,1] and p ∈ [1,2] the identity (*) holds for Φ_{x,ε}, and describe the dependence of these values on ε.
status_search_result: The general maximal output p-norm multiplicativity conjecture has been refuted: Hayden–Winter and Hastings showed that for every p > 1 there exist quantum channels (built from random unitaries that produce nearly-maximally-mixed outputs, very much in the spirit of the M_ε construction) whose maximal output p-norm is not multiplicative. Thus the strong form of the question for p > 1 fails in general. The case p = 1 is trivial (ν_1 ≡ 1). The fine question of exactly which (x, p, ε)-regimes for the polarized channels Φ_{x,ε} preserve multiplicativity does not appear to have a complete published answer; partial results for qubit and depolarizing-type channels exist but a full characterization remains unresolved.

original_question: Find new counterexamples to maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω) in which Φ is a random sub-unitary channel with Kraus operators A_k = (1/(d−1)) X^k [[U_k,0],[0,0]], with U_k arbitrary unitaries in M_{d−1}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ be an integer and let $X \in M_d(\mathbb{C})$ denote the cyclic shift operator defined by $X|j\rangle = |j+1 \bmod d\rangle$ for $j = 0,1,\dots,d-1$. For each choice of unitaries $U_0,U_1,\dots,U_{d-1} \in M_{d-1}(\mathbb{C})$, define operators $A_0,\dots,A_{d-1} \in M_d(\mathbb{C})$ by
$$A_k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d-1}}\, X^k \begin{pmatrix} U_k & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad k = 0,1,\dots,d-1,$$
where the block structure is with respect to the decomposition $\mathbb{C}^d = \mathbb{C}^{d-1} \oplus \mathbb{C}$. One checks that $\sum_k A_k^* A_k \leq I_d$, so $\Phi(\rho) = \sum_{k=0}^{d-1} A_k \rho A_k^*$ defines a sub-unital completely positive trace-non-increasing map (a "sub-unitary channel"). 

For a completely positive map $\Psi$, define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Psi) = \sup_{\rho \geq 0,\ \mathrm{tr}\,\rho = 1} \|\Psi(\rho)\|_p,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_p$ is the Schatten $p$-norm.

Problem: Exhibit a choice of $d$, of unitaries $U_0,\dots,U_{d-1} \in M_{d-1}(\mathbb{C})$, of $p > 1$, and of an auxiliary completely positive map $\Omega$, such that the resulting channel $\Phi$ of the above form together with $\Omega$ violates multiplicativity:
$$\nu_p(\Phi \otimes \Omega) > \nu_p(\Phi)\, \nu_p(\Omega).$$
status_search_result: The general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture was disproved for all p > 1 by Hayden–Winter (2008) using random unitary channels, and earlier for p > 2 by Hayden. However, these counterexamples do not specifically use the structured sub-unitary Kraus form A_k = (d−1)^{-1/2} X^k diag(U_k, 0). No source was found explicitly producing counterexamples within this restricted Kraus family, so the specific question appears unresolved in the literature surveyed.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Find a proof of maximal output p-norm multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel that does not rely on unitary equivalence to channels with negative multipliers.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-Pauli qubit channel, the completely positive trace-preserving map on 2x2 density matrices defined, for parameters p_I, p_X, p_Y >= 0 with p_I + p_X + p_Y = 1, by

  Φ(ρ) = p_I ρ + p_X X ρ X + p_Y Y ρ Y,

where X and Y are the Pauli matrices σ_x and σ_y. Equivalently, Φ acts on the Bloch representation ρ = (I + r·σ)/2 by multiplying the Bloch components (r_x, r_y, r_z) by nonnegative multipliers (λ_x, λ_y, λ_z) with λ_x = p_I + p_X − p_Y, λ_y = p_I − p_X + p_Y, λ_z = p_I − p_X − p_Y after suitable choice of parameters; here all multipliers can be arranged so that the channel is unitarily equivalent to one with all multipliers nonnegative.

For a quantum channel Ψ and p > 1, define the maximal output p-norm

  ν_p(Ψ) := sup_ρ ||Ψ(ρ)||_p,

where ||A||_p = (Tr |A|^p)^{1/p} and the supremum is over input density matrices.

Provide a proof, valid for all p in some nontrivial range p > 1, that the maximal output p-norm is multiplicative for tensor products of the two-Pauli qubit channel with itself and with arbitrary other channels:

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) ν_p(Ω)   for every channel Ω,

without using a reduction by unitary equivalence to channels having one or more negative Bloch multipliers. That is, find a direct proof of multiplicativity of ν_p for the two-Pauli channel that operates within the regime of nonnegative multipliers.
status_search_result: Multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm for the two-Pauli qubit channel is known via the unitary-equivalence reduction to channels with negative multipliers (King and collaborators), and the global maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is now known to be false for general channels (Hastings; Hayden-Winter). However, no published proof of multiplicativity for the two-Pauli channel that avoids the negative-multiplier reduction has been located. The status of finding such an alternative proof appears unresolved in available sources.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For random sub-unitary channels, prove maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), at least at p = 2, or determine whether these channels yield additional counterexamples to multiplicativity.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}^n)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}^m)$. Any such channel admits a Kraus representation $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{k=1}^{K} A_k \rho A_k^*$ with $\sum_k A_k^* A_k = I_n$. For $p\ge 1$, the maximal output $p$-norm of $\Phi$ is
$$\nu_p(\Phi)\ :=\ \sup_{\rho}\ \|\Phi(\rho)\|_p,$$
where the supremum is over density matrices $\rho$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$.

A random sub-unitary channel is constructed as follows. Fix integers $n,K\ge 1$ with $K\le n^2$. Sample $K$ independent $n\times n$ matrices $\{A_k\}_{k=1}^K$ whose entries are i.i.d.\ complex Gaussians (suitably normalized), and rescale so that $\sum_{k=1}^K A_k^* A_k = I_n$ (equivalently, take Kraus operators of "sub-unitary" form, namely properly normalized truncations of Haar-random unitaries, so that each $A_k$ is, up to scaling, a contraction). The resulting channel $\Phi$ is called a random sub-unitary channel.

Problem. Let $\Phi$ and $\Omega$ be independent random sub-unitary channels. Prove that with probability one (or in expectation, in the appropriate scaling regime),
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes \Omega)\ =\ \nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega),$$
at least in the case $p=2$. If this multiplicativity fails, exhibit random sub-unitary channels that provide explicit counterexamples to multiplicativity of the maximal output $p$-norm.
status_search_result: General multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm is known to fail for all p>1 (Hayden–Winter and follow-ups), and random quantum channels are known to provide violations for p>2. For p=2 some weak multiplicativity results for random channels exist (e.g., Montanaro and Collins–Nechita), but a definitive proof or disproof of multiplicativity at p=2 specifically for the random sub-unitary class described does not appear in the located literature, so the status of this specific question is unclear.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For each fixed dimension bound d, does there exist a number p_d > 0 such that additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy, S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω), holds uniformly for all channels Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'} with d' ≤ d either throughout p_d < p < 1 when p_d < 1 or throughout 1 < p < p_d when p_d > 1?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer n, let M_n denote the algebra of n×n complex matrices. A quantum channel Φ : M_n → M_m is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map. For p > 0 with p ≠ 1, the minimal output Rényi p-entropy of a channel Φ is defined by
  S^p_min(Φ) = inf_ρ (1/(1−p)) log Tr[Φ(ρ)^p],
where the infimum is taken over density matrices ρ (positive semidefinite matrices of trace 1) on the input space. For two channels Φ and Ω, one says that Rényi p-additivity holds for the pair if
  S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω).

Question. Does the following statement hold? For every fixed positive integer d there exists a real number p_d > 0 such that exactly one of the following two cases occurs:
 (i) p_d < 1, and S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω) holds for every pair of channels Φ : M_{d'} → M_{d'} and Ω : M_{d''} → M_{d''} with d', d'' ≤ d, and for every p with p_d < p < 1; or
 (ii) p_d > 1, and the same equality holds whenever d', d'' ≤ d and 1 < p < p_d.

Decide whether such a threshold p_d exists for each fixed d.
status_search_result: Known counterexamples to additivity of minimal output Rényi p-entropy (Hayden–Winter for p>1; Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter and subsequent work for p<1, with violations in intervals such as (1−p₀,1) for p₀≈0.2855, and recent constructions for all p>1) all rely on input dimensions growing with the desired closeness to p=1. For each fixed input dimension bound d, no proof or disproof of dimension-uniform Rényi additivity in a one-sided neighborhood of p=1 is reported, so the conjecture appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: First tensor-power failure of Rényi additivity
original_question: Find a quantum channel Φ, an integer m, and a real p > 0 such that minimal output Rényi entropy is additive for fewer than m tensor powers, S^p_min(Φ^{⊗n}) = n S^p_min(Φ) for n < m, but fails exactly at m copies in the sense S^p_min(Φ^{⊗m}) < m S^p_min(Φ).
self_contained_problem:
For a quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ (a completely positive trace-preserving linear map between matrix algebras) and a real number $p>0$, define the minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy by
$$S^{p}_{\min}(\Phi)\;=\;\inf_{\rho}\;\frac{1}{1-p}\,\log\,\mathrm{Tr}\!\left[\Phi(\rho)^{p}\right],$$
where the infimum is over all density matrices $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ (and the limit $p\to 1$ recovers the von Neumann entropy). For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $\Phi^{\otimes n}$ denote the $n$-fold tensor product channel acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A^{\otimes n})$.

Exhibit a quantum channel $\Phi$, an integer $m\ge 2$, and a real number $p>0$ such that the minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy is exactly additive for fewer than $m$ tensor copies but fails to be additive at $m$ copies, namely
$$S^{p}_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes n})\;=\;n\,S^{p}_{\min}(\Phi)\quad\text{for all }1\le n<m,$$
while
$$S^{p}_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes m})\;<\;m\,S^{p}_{\min}(\Phi).$$
Equivalently, find a quantum channel for which the first failure of Rényi additivity occurs at exactly $m$ copies, with $m\ge 2$.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has produced many counterexamples to additivity of minimum output Rényi $p$-entropy (random Stinespring constructions for $p>1$, antisymmetric-subspace channels for all $p>2$, and small-dimensional examples for $p$ near $0$), and Hayden–Winter showed non-additivity for all $p>1$. However, no source located addresses the specific structural question of producing a channel whose Rényi additivity holds for all $n<m$ tensor copies and first fails at exactly $n=m$ for some prescribed $m\ge 2$. The problem appears not to have been explicitly resolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For all counterexamples to maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), must the counterexample channels have non-negative completely bounded (CB) entropy and/or zero coherent information?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the bounded operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, and let a quantum channel be a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$. For $p\geq 1$ define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Phi)\;=\;\sup_{\rho}\,\bigl\|\Phi(\rho)\bigr\|_p,$$
where the supremum runs over density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$. Say that a pair of channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ is a $p$-multiplicativity counterexample if
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)\;>\;\nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega).$$

For a channel $\Phi$ with Stinespring isometry $V:\mathcal{H}_A\to\mathcal{H}_B\otimes\mathcal{H}_E$ such that $\Phi(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_E(V\rho V^*)$, define the complementary channel $\Phi^c(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_B(V\rho V^*)$. The completely bounded (CB) entropy of $\Phi$ is
$$S_{CB}(\Phi)\;=\;\inf_{\rho_{RA}}\Bigl[S\bigl((\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\Phi)(\rho_{RA})\bigr)-S(\rho_R)\Bigr],$$
taken over all bipartite states $\rho_{RA}$, where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$. The coherent information of $\Phi$ at input $\rho$ is
$$I_c(\rho,\Phi)\;=\;S(\Phi(\rho))-S(\Phi^c(\rho)),$$
and $I_c(\Phi)=\sup_\rho I_c(\rho,\Phi)$.

Question: Is it true that for every $p>1$ and every $p$-multiplicativity counterexample $(\Phi,\Omega)$, at least one of the channels $\Phi$, $\Omega$ must have non-negative CB entropy, or have zero coherent information? Equivalently, can a counterexample to multiplicativity exist in which both channels simultaneously have negative CB entropy and non-zero coherent information?
status_search_result: The maximal $p$-norm multiplicativity conjecture has been disproved for all $p>1$ (Hayden–Winter 2008, and earlier Werner–Holevo for large $p$), and the additivity of minimum output entropy was disproved by Hastings (2009). However, no source surveyed addresses the specific structural question of whether all such counterexample channels must have non-negative CB entropy or zero coherent information. The status appears to be unknown/unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Find pairs of quantum channels M and N that are mutually degradable, meaning that there exist channels X and Y for which X ∘ M equals the complementary channel N^C and Y ∘ N equals the complementary channel M^C; in particular, find nontrivial examples beyond the known case M = I, such as pairs where both channels have Choi rank d but are not individually degradable.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A, \mathcal{H}_B, \mathcal{H}_C$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map between spaces of bounded operators on such Hilbert spaces. Every channel $\Phi : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ admits a Stinespring isometry $V : \mathcal{H}_A \to \mathcal{H}_B \otimes \mathcal{H}_E$ with $\Phi(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_E(V\rho V^\ast)$; the complementary channel is $\Phi^C(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_B(V\rho V^\ast)$, and the Choi rank of $\Phi$ is the minimal such $\dim \mathcal{H}_E$. A channel $\Phi$ is degradable if there exists a channel $D$ with $D \circ \Phi = \Phi^C$.

Call an ordered pair of channels $(M, N)$, with $M : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ and $N : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$, mutually degradable if there exist channels $X$ and $Y$ such that
$$ X \circ M = N^C \quad\text{and}\quad Y \circ N = M^C. $$

Exhibit nontrivial examples of mutually degradable pairs $(M, N)$ beyond the trivial family in which $M$ is the identity channel (in which case $N$ may be arbitrary). In particular, find such pairs in which both $M$ and $N$ have Choi rank equal to $d = \dim \mathcal{H}_A$ and neither $M$ nor $N$ is individually degradable.
status_search_result: A web search for "mutually degradable" quantum channel pairs returns general literature on degradable channels, complementary channels, and Choi rank, but no source explicitly resolving the existence of nontrivial mutually degradable pairs (with both channels of Choi rank $d$ and neither individually degradable). No clear progress on this specific question was located, so the status is taken to be unknown.

context_brief: Single-exponential algorithms for all Betti numbers
original_question: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k defined by s polynomial equalities and inequalities whose degrees are bounded by d. Is there an algorithm that computes all Betti numbers of S in time single exponential in k? More concretely, can the currently known single-exponential methods for computing only the first l Betti numbers for fixed l be extended to compute the full Betti sequence of S within a single-exponential running time in the ambient dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set, defined as a Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities involving $s$ polynomials in $\mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$, each of degree at most $d$. For each $i \ge 0$, let $b_i(S) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$ denote the $i$-th Betti number of $S$ (with respect to singular homology with rational coefficients). The input size of $S$ is measured by $s$, $d$, $k$, and the bit-size of the coefficients of the defining polynomials.

An algorithm running on a real RAM (or in the bit complexity model with appropriate adjustments) is said to have single-exponential complexity in $k$ if its running time is bounded by $(sd)^{k^{O(1)}}$.

It is known that:
(i) the zeroth Betti number $b_0(S)$ (the number of connected components) and the first Betti number $b_1(S)$ can each be computed in single-exponential time in $k$;
(ii) more generally, for every fixed nonnegative integer $\ell$, there exists an algorithm with complexity $(sd)^{k^{O(\ell)}}$ that computes the sequence $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_\ell(S)$;
(iii) a doubly-exponential algorithm (e.g.\ via cylindrical algebraic decomposition) computes all Betti numbers $b_0(S),\dots,b_k(S)$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input a description of a semi-algebraic set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ as above, computes all Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_k(S)$ in time single-exponential in $k$ (i.e.\ bounded by $(sd)^{k^{O(1)}}$)?
status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as a major open question in algorithmic semi-algebraic geometry. Single-exponential algorithms are known only for the first $\ell+1$ Betti numbers for any fixed constant $\ell$ (with complexity $(sd)^{k^{O(\ell)}}$), and recent work (through 2024) extends this to compute bases of the first $\ell$ homology groups and induced maps, but no single-exponential algorithm computing all Betti numbers (especially the middle-dimensional ones) has been found; the only known algorithms for the full Betti sequence remain doubly exponential.

original_question: Consider a semi-algebraic set in R^k defined by l quadratic inequalities. Can the number of connected components of such a set be computed by an algorithm with complexity k^O(l), or even k^O(l^2), rather than the currently best known k^(2^O(l)) type bound coming from the available all-Betti-number methods? Equivalently, is there a substantially more efficient algorithm for counting connected components in the quadratic case than the general-purpose approach currently provides?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k,\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $P_1,\dots,P_\ell \in \mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$ be polynomials each of degree at most $2$. Consider a semi-algebraic set
$$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$$
defined by a Boolean combination of the sign conditions $\{P_i \,\square\, 0 : 1 \le i \le \ell,\ \square \in \{<,=,>\}\}$ (in particular, sets defined by conjunctions of $\ell$ quadratic inequalities $P_i \le 0$).

Currently:
- Algorithms are known that decide emptiness of $S$ and compute a set of sample points meeting every connected component of $S$ in time $k^{O(\ell)}$.
- The Euler–Poincaré characteristic $\chi(S)$ can be computed in time $k^{O(\ell)}$.
- The number $b_0(S)$ of connected components of $S$ can be computed by specializing general algorithms for all Betti numbers, which run in time $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$.

Question. Does there exist an algorithm that, given the polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_\ell$ as input (in a standard bit-cost or arithmetic complexity model over an ordered field where the relevant arithmetic is performed exactly), outputs the number $b_0(S)$ of connected components of $S$ in time bounded by $k^{O(\ell)}$, or at least by $k^{O(\ell^2)}$, thereby substantially improving on the current $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$ bound?
status_search_result: Recent literature on algorithms for semi-algebraic sets defined by quadratic inequalities (Basu and coauthors) achieves polynomial-time algorithms for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic and for the top few Betti numbers, but the best known complexity for computing the full count of connected components of such sets remains $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$, inherited from the all-Betti-numbers algorithm. Moreover, exact counting of connected components in the quadratic case is known to be #P-hard, but no algorithm with complexity $k^{O(\ell)}$ or $k^{O(\ell^2)}$ has been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let Ω be an open connected subset of C^n, and let Γ: Ω -> C^n be a holomorphic mapping such that the maximal rank of its Jacobian DΓ is an integer k with 1 <= k <= n - 1. For each point ξ in the maximal-rank set Ω^(k) = {ξ in Ω : rank DΓ(ξ) = k}, assume the level set Γ^{-1}(Γ(ξ)) is an affine (n-k)-dimensional space through ξ, equivalently of the form ξ + κ(ξ) where κ(ξ) = ker DΓ(ξ). Under these hypotheses, when does the resulting affine fibration extend analytically from Ω^(k) to all of Ω?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be an open connected subset, and let $\Gamma : \Omega 	o \mathbb{C}^n$ be a holomorphic mapping. Define
$$k := \max_{\xi \in \Omega} \operatorname{rank} D\Gamma(\xi),$$
and assume $1 \le k \le n-1$. Let
$$\Omega^{(k)} := \{\xi \in \Omega : \operatorname{rank} D\Gamma(\xi) = k\},$$
which is an open dense subset of $\Omega$. Assume the following geometric condition:

(A) For every $\xi \in \Omega^{(k)}$, the level set
$$\Gamma^{-1}(\Gamma(\xi)) = \{\eta \in \Omega : \Gamma(\eta) = \Gamma(\xi)\}$$
is an affine $(n-k)$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{C}^n$ passing through $\xi$; equivalently, $\Gamma^{-1}(\Gamma(\xi)) \cap \Omega = (\xi + \kappa(\xi)) \cap \Omega$, where $\kappa(\xi) := \ker D\Gamma(\xi)$.

Under these hypotheses, the assignment $\xi \mapsto \xi + \kappa(\xi)$ defines an analytic affine fibration of $\Omega^{(k)}$ by $(n-k)$-planes. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which this affine fibration extends analytically from $\Omega^{(k)}$ to all of $\Omega$, in the sense that there exists a holomorphic mapping $\xi \mapsto L(\xi)$ on $\Omega$, with values in the Grassmannian-affine bundle of $(n-k)$-dimensional affine subspaces of $\mathbb{C}^n$, such that $L(\xi) = \xi + \kappa(\xi)$ for all $\xi \in \Omega^{(k)}$. In particular, does such an extension always exist, and if not, characterize the obstructions.
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem in complex analytic geometry motivated by regularity theory of Fourier integral operators. A subsequent survey by the same author ("Singularities of affine fibrations in the regularity theory of Fourier integral operators") still discusses this as an open problem with only partial results, and no later publication appears to claim a complete resolution.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two conditions equivalent: first, that (A, A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every operator T in L(E, Y), and every epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and an operator S in L(E, N) with T = J_N^Y S and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T); and second, that (A, A) satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle described in Definition 1.1?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach operator ideal is a pair $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ where $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\mathfrak{L}$ is a two-sided ideal and $A:\mathfrak{A}\to[0,\infty)$ is an ideal-norm making each component $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ a Banach space and satisfying the usual ideal axioms (containing finite-rank operators with $A(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\|y\|$, and $A(RTS)\le \|R\|A(T)\|S\|$). The ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is called maximal if for every operator $T\in\mathfrak{L}(X,Y)$,
$$A(T)=\sup\{A(Q^Y_F\, T\, J^X_M)\,:\, M\subseteq X\text{ finite-dimensional},\ F\subseteq Y\text{ finite-codimensional closed}\},$$
where $J^X_M:M\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion and $Q^Y_F:Y\to Y/F$ is the quotient map, with the convention that $T\in\mathfrak{A}$ iff this supremum is finite.

For a closed subspace $N\subseteq Y$ let $J^Y_N:N\hookrightarrow Y$ denote the inclusion. The ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is right-accessible if for every finite-dimensional Banach space $E$, every Banach space $Y$, every $T\in\mathfrak{L}(E,Y)$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq Y$ and $S\in\mathfrak{L}(E,N)$ with $T=J^Y_N S$ and $A(S)\le(1+\varepsilon)A(T)$.

For an operator ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$, one says that $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle (A-LRP) if for every Banach space $X$, every Banach space $Y$, every finite-dimensional subspace $M\subseteq X^{**}$, every finite-dimensional subspace $F\subseteq Y^*$, every operator $T\in\mathfrak{A}(X^{**},Y)$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an operator $\tilde T\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ such that
(i) $\langle \tilde T x, y^*\rangle = \langle T x, y^*\rangle$ for all $x\in X$, $y^*\in F$,
(ii) $\langle \tilde T^{**} m, y^*\rangle = \langle T m, y^*\rangle$ for all $m\in M$, $y^*\in F$, and
(iii) $A(\tilde T)\le (1+\varepsilon)\,A(T)$.

Question. Let $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two statements equivalent?
(i) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is right-accessible.
(ii) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle.

It is known that (i) implies (ii). Determine whether (ii) implies (i).
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of the converse implication (A-LRP implies right-accessibility) for maximal Banach ideals. The forward direction (right-accessibility implies A-LRP) is established in the literature on accessibility of operator ideals (e.g., Oertel's work), but the equivalence question appears not to have a confirmed resolution in available sources.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
context_brief: Normed product ideal with L2 factor
original_question: Does the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 admit an ideal norm? Equivalently, is the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 normed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{L}_p$ ($1\le p\le \infty$) denote the Banach operator ideal of absolutely $p$-summing operators between Banach spaces, equipped with its natural ideal norm. For a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$, let $\mathfrak{A}^{**}$ denote its bidual (regular hull / second dual ideal). For two quasi-Banach operator ideals $\mathfrak{A}$ and $\mathfrak{B}$, the product ideal $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ consists of all bounded operators $T$ between Banach spaces that admit a factorization $T=AB$ with $B\in\mathfrak{B}$ and $A\in\mathfrak{A}$.

Set $\mathfrak{A}:=(\mathfrak{L}_1\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}$. By Grothendieck's inequality (in operator form) one has $\mathfrak{L}_2\subseteq\mathfrak{A}^*$ (the adjoint ideal of $\mathfrak{A}$).

Question: Does the product operator ideal
$$(\mathfrak{L}_1\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}\circ\mathfrak{L}_2$$
admit an ideal norm — that is, is this product ideal a normed (Banach) operator ideal?
status_search_result: A web search surfaces the related work "On normed products of operator ideals which contain L_2 as a factor" by F. Oertel (arXiv:math/0108123), which discusses exactly such product ideals and the question of whether they are normed, but no source found resolves the specific question of whether $(\mathfrak{L}_1\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}\circ\mathfrak{L}_2$ admits an ideal norm. No published resolution was located.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (B, B) be a maximal Banach ideal, and let X0 and Y0 be Banach spaces such that X0' and Y0 are of cotype 2 and B*(X0, Y0) is not contained in L2(X0, Y0). If B ◦ L∞ has property (I), does it already follow that the B-LRP is not satisfied, even without assuming that B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible? In other words, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on B ◦ L∞ be removed from this implication?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach operator ideal $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ is a subclass $\mathfrak{B}\subseteq\mathfrak{L}$ together with an ideal norm $\mathbf{B}$ such that each component $\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)$ is a Banach space, $\mathfrak{B}$ contains all finite-rank operators (with $\mathbf{B}(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\|y\|$), and $\mathfrak{B}$ is two-sided ideal-stable under composition with bounded operators. The adjoint ideal $\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}$ is the maximal hull of the dual procedure and $\mathfrak{B}$ is called maximal if $\mathfrak{B}=\mathfrak{B}^{\ast\ast}$ isometrically. The ideal $\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ denotes the maximal Banach ideal of $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-factorable operators, and $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ is the product ideal. The ideal $\mathfrak{L}_2$ consists of operators factoring through a Hilbert space.

A Banach space $Z$ is said to be of cotype 2 if there exists $C>0$ such that for every finite sequence $(z_i)\subseteq Z$,
$$\Big(\sum_i\|z_i\|^2\Big)^{1/2}\le C\Big(\int_0^1\Big\|\sum_i r_i(t)z_i\Big\|^2dt\Big)^{1/2},$$
where $(r_i)$ are the Rademacher functions.

A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is right-accessible if for every finite-rank operator $T\in\mathfrak{A}$ between Banach spaces $X,Y$, every finite-dimensional subspace $E\subseteq X$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a Banach space $Z$, an operator $L\in\mathfrak{L}(X,Z)$ with $\|L|_E\|\le 1$ and $S\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,Y)$ such that $T|_E=SL|_E$ and $\mathbf{A}(S)\le(1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}(T)$. The ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to have property (I) if a certain (fixed) injectivity-type stability condition for trace dualities holds; specifically, the canonical map between trace functionals on finite rank operators extends consistently to $\mathfrak{A}$-valued operators on $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-spaces.

Finally, given a maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ and Banach spaces $X_0,Y_0$, the $\mathfrak{B}$-Local Reciprocity Property (the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP) at $(X_0,Y_0)$ is the assertion that the natural local trace duality between $\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}(X_0,Y_0)$ and the finite-rank component holds in a specified isometric way (so that, in particular, $\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}(X_0,Y_0)$ is properly identified through $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$).

Question. Let $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ be a maximal Banach operator ideal, and let $X_0,Y_0$ be Banach spaces such that the dual $X_0'$ and $Y_0$ are both of cotype 2 and
$$\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}(X_0,Y_0)\not\subseteq\mathfrak{L}_2(X_0,Y_0).$$
Suppose that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ has property (I). Does it follow that the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP fails at $(X_0,Y_0)$, without any additional assumption that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ is right-accessible? Equivalently, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ be removed from this implication?

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For random matrix ensembles with symmetry classes β=1 and β=4, prove bulk and edge universality for general potentials of the form Q(x)=N V(x), especially when the associated equilibrium measure is supported on several disjoint intervals, rather than only for the already understood polynomial-potential cases with one-cut support. More broadly, determine whether the newer methods developed for unitary ensembles can be adapted to these orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, and resolve the long-standing conjecture that Wigner matrices also exhibit bulk universality.
self_contained_problem:
Consider random matrix ensembles on the space of N×N real symmetric matrices (symmetry class β=1) and on the space of N×N quaternion self-dual matrices (symmetry class β=4) with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

  ∏_{1≤i<j≤N} |x_i − x_j|^β · exp(−∑_{i=1}^N Q(x_i)),

where the external potential has the scaling form Q(x) = N·V(x) for a sufficiently regular function V: ℝ → ℝ (e.g. polynomial or real-analytic) such that the corresponding equilibrium measure μ_V (the unique minimizer of the logarithmic energy functional with external field V) has compact support that may consist of several disjoint intervals (the "multi-cut" regime).

(a) Bulk universality. Prove that for any point x_0 in the interior of the support of μ_V where the equilibrium density ρ_V(x_0) > 0, the rescaled k-point correlation functions

  (1/(Nρ_V(x_0)))^k · R_k^{(N)}(x_0 + y_1/(Nρ_V(x_0)), …, x_0 + y_k/(Nρ_V(x_0)))

converge as N → ∞ to the universal sine-kernel correlation functions of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (β=1) and Gaussian Symplectic Ensemble (β=4) respectively.

(b) Edge universality. Prove that at a soft edge of supp(μ_V), the rescaled correlation functions converge to the universal Airy-type correlation functions associated to the GOE (β=1) and GSE (β=4).

(c) Determine whether the analytic / Riemann–Hilbert / resolvent / Dyson Brownian motion methods that have been developed for the unitary (β=2) ensembles can be adapted to obtain (a) and (b) for the orthogonal and symplectic ensembles in the multi-cut, non-polynomial case.

(d) Wigner bulk universality. Let W_N be an N×N real symmetric (resp. complex Hermitian, resp. quaternion self-dual) random matrix whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent, centered, with variance 1/N (suitably normalized), and otherwise of arbitrary common distribution (a "Wigner matrix"). Prove that, after rescaling by the local density of the semicircle law at any energy x_0 in the bulk (−2, 2), the local k-point eigenvalue correlation functions converge as N → ∞ to those of the GOE (resp. GUE, resp. GSE).
status_search_result: Both parts have been largely resolved since the problem was posed. The Wigner–Dyson–Mehta bulk universality conjecture for Wigner matrices was proved around 2009–2012 by Erdős–Schlein–Yau (with Péché, Ramírez, Yin) and independently by Tao–Vu, for all symmetry classes under mild moment conditions. For invariant β=1 and β=4 ensembles with general potentials, bulk and edge universality have been established by Shcherbina (multi-cut polynomial and analytic potentials), Krishnapur–Rider–Virág, Bourgade–Erdős–Yau (general β-ensembles, including bulk and edge universality for analytic and C^4 potentials), and via transport methods by Bekerman–Figalli–Guionnet, covering the multi-cut regime as well. Thus the open problem is essentially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop a systematic and computationally reliable theory for the six Painlevé equations, analogous in spirit to the Bateman project or Abramowitz-Stegun for classical special functions. In particular, build dependable software and accompanying asymptotic and algebraic infrastructure for computing Painlevé transcendents, such as determining features like the pole locations in the complex plane for the Painlevé II solution asymptotic to the Airy function as x→+∞.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic and computationally reliable theory of the six Painlevé equations

  P_I:  u'' = 6u^2 + x,
  P_II: u'' = 2u^3 + xu + α,
  P_III, P_IV, P_V, P_VI (in their standard forms),

analogous in scope and reliability to classical handbooks of special functions (such as the Bateman Manuscript Project or the Abramowitz–Stegun Handbook). The goal is twofold:

(a) Produce dependable software and an accompanying asymptotic and algebraic infrastructure that, given any of the six Painlevé equations together with a choice of monodromy/Stokes data (or equivalently a choice of distinguished one-parameter family of solutions), reliably evaluates the corresponding Painlevé transcendent at arbitrary points of its domain, including connection formulas between asymptotic regimes and locations of movable singularities.

(b) As a concrete benchmark instance, for the Painlevé II equation
   u''(x) = 2u(x)^3 + x u(x)
let u(x) be the unique (Hastings–McLeod-type) real solution satisfying
   u(x) ∼ Ai(x) as x → +∞,
where Ai is the Airy function. Determine the locations in the complex x-plane of all poles of the meromorphic continuation of u, including their distribution, asymptotics, and an algorithm for computing them to prescribed accuracy.
status_search_result: The "Painlevé Project" envisioned as a community-wide handbook/software analogue of Bateman or Abramowitz–Stegun was formally launched at an ICMS workshop in Edinburgh (May 2010), with a coordinating site hosted at NIST and ongoing integration into the DLMF (chapter on Painlevé transcendents under revision). Substantial partial progress exists: numerical Riemann–Hilbert methods (Olver, Trogdon and others) reliably compute Painlevé II transcendents and their poles, and asymptotic/connection-formula knowledge for the tritronquée and Hastings–McLeod solutions has advanced. However, a complete, uniformly reliable handbook-plus-software covering all six Painlevé equations across all parameter regimes is still a work in progress rather than a finished product, so the broader programmatic problem remains partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For general β-ensembles, equivalently log gases at inverse temperature β>0, use the stochastic Schrödinger operator H_β = d^2/dx^2 - x - √(2/β) dB(x)/dx on L^2((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition at x=0 to obtain structural information about the edge statistics of the ensemble. In particular, derive the Tracy-Widom distribution for the top eigenvalue in the case β=2 directly from H_β.
self_contained_problem:
Let β > 0, and consider the stochastic Schrödinger operator (the stochastic Airy operator) defined formally by
  H_β = -d²/dx² + x + (2/√β) · B'(x),
acting on functions f ∈ L²((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition f(0) = 0, where B(x) is a standard Brownian motion on [0,∞) and B'(x) is its (distributional) white-noise derivative. (Equivalently, H_β = d²/dx² − x − √(2/β) dB/dx with appropriate sign conventions.) The operator H_β has a discrete spectrum, almost surely, with smallest eigenvalue λ_1(β); the random variable −λ_1(β) is the Tracy–Widom_β law and is known to describe the limiting fluctuation of the largest eigenvalue at the soft edge of the Gaussian β-ensemble (the log-gas at inverse temperature β).

Problem. Working directly from the operator H_β at β = 2, derive the Tracy–Widom distribution for the top eigenvalue, namely the identity
  P(−λ_1(2) ≤ s) = F_2(s) = det(I − K_Airy)_{L²(s,∞)} = exp(−∫_s^∞ (x−s) q(x)² dx),
where K_Airy is the Airy kernel and q is the Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II (q'' = x q + 2 q³, q(x) ~ Ai(x) as x → ∞), without invoking the determinantal/Airy-kernel structure of GUE as an external input. More generally, use H_β to extract structural information (such as a Painlevé/Fredholm-type representation) about the edge statistics of the β-ensemble.
category_tag: Stochastic Airy operator and Tracy-Widom distributions
status_search_result: The stochastic Airy operator was introduced by Edelman–Sutton and rigorously analyzed by Ramírez–Rider–Virág (2011), who proved that its bottom eigenvalues describe Tracy–Widom_β fluctuations for general β > 0. However, recovering the explicit Painlevé II / Fredholm determinant formula F_2 directly from the operator H_β (rather than from the determinantal structure of GUE) does not appear to have been carried out in the literature; the standard derivation of F_2 still proceeds via the Airy kernel determinantal point process. Subsequent works (e.g., Bloemendal–Virág on hard-edge and soft-edge PDEs, Rumanov on β = 6 Painlevé representations) give related characterizations but not a direct β = 2 Painlevé II derivation from H_β. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Determine the long-time behavior of integrable systems when the initial data are non-generic and the associated Lax operator has singular spectral features not covered by the standard generic theory. In particular, for focusing nonlinear Schrödinger evolution, understand how spectra that accumulate on the real line at essentially arbitrary rates affect long-time asymptotics, and similarly clarify the situation for higher-order self-adjoint Lax operators such as those for the Boussinesq equation.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
  i q_t + q_{xx} + 2|q|^2 q = 0,  (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ_+,
with initial data q(x,0) = q_0(x) decaying as |x| → ∞. The associated Lax operator is the Zakharov–Shabat operator
  L = i σ_3 (∂_x − Q(x)),  Q(x) = ((0, q_0(x)),(−\bar q_0(x), 0)),
whose spectral data (reflection coefficient and discrete eigenvalues) determine q(x,t) via inverse scattering.

The standard nonlinear steepest-descent theory yields detailed long-time asymptotics under "generic" assumptions on q_0 (e.g., reflection coefficient smooth on ℝ, finitely many simple discrete eigenvalues off ℝ, no spectral singularities). 

(a) Suppose q_0 is non-generic in the sense that the discrete spectrum (or, more generally, spectral singularities of L) accumulates on the real axis at an essentially arbitrary prescribed rate. Determine the leading-order long-time behavior of q(x,t) in each region of the (x,t)-plane, expressed in terms of this accumulation rate.

(b) Consider the Boussinesq equation
  u_{tt} = u_{xxxx} + (u^2)_{xx},
which admits a self-adjoint Lax operator of order three. For general (non-generic) decaying initial data (u(x,0), u_t(x,0)), determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t).

The problem is to provide rigorous asymptotic formulas (with error estimates) covering these non-generic settings that are not handled by the existing generic theory.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed several non-generic cases for focusing NLS: long-time asymptotics in the presence of real spectral singularities have been derived (with O((log t/t)^{1/2}) corrections near stationary phase points), and asymptotics in the solitonic region with high-order discrete eigenvalues have been obtained via Riemann–Hilbert/steepest-descent methods. For the Boussinesq equation, long-time asymptotics for Schwartz-class initial data have been studied. However, the full problem—covering arbitrary accumulation rates of eigenvalues to the real line for focusing NLS, and general (non-generic) initial data for Boussinesq—remains only partially resolved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Find a probabilistic operation X on an i.i.d. sequence (a_1,a_2,...) that plays a role for random-matrix statistics analogous to summation in the classical central limit theorem: after applying X to the first n inputs, the resulting random variables should converge, as n→∞, to the Gaudin distribution or to a Tracy-Widom distribution. In other words, characterize random-matrix universality in purely probabilistic terms.
self_contained_problem:
Background. The classical central limit theorem can be cast as follows: there is a probabilistic operation, namely normalized summation S_n(a_1,...,a_n) = (a_1+...+a_n - n μ)/(σ √n), such that for any i.i.d. sequence (a_i) with mean μ and finite variance σ^2, the law of S_n converges as n→∞ to the standard Gaussian distribution. The Gaussian distribution is therefore a universal attractor under the operation of summation.

In random matrix theory, two distributions play a comparably universal role for spectral statistics: 
(i) the Gaudin (sine-kernel gap) distribution, describing the limiting spacing between consecutive eigenvalues in the bulk of large Hermitian random matrices; 
(ii) the Tracy–Widom distributions F_β (β = 1, 2, 4), describing the limiting fluctuations, after appropriate centering and scaling, of the largest eigenvalue of large random matrices from the classical β-ensembles. Equivalently, F_2 is the limit law of the rescaled length of the longest increasing subsequence of a uniformly random permutation, and of various last-passage percolation times.

Problem. Exhibit a probabilistic operation X — that is, for each n, a measurable map X_n : R^n → R (or into a suitable state space) — with the following property:
For every i.i.d. sequence (a_1, a_2, ...) of real-valued random variables in some natural class (e.g. with sufficiently many finite moments, possibly normalized), the random variable X_n(a_1,...,a_n), after deterministic centering and scaling, converges in distribution as n→∞ to:
- the Gaudin (sine-kernel) distribution, or
- a Tracy–Widom distribution F_β for some β ∈ {1,2,4}.

The operation X should be intrinsically probabilistic (not requiring as input a random matrix model or an integrable structure), and should make the universality of Tracy–Widom / Gaudin laws as transparent as the role of summation in the classical CLT. In short, characterize random-matrix universality in purely probabilistic terms by identifying such an operation X.
status_search_result: The problem is generally still considered open, but partial progress exists. Baik–Suidan (2005) and independently Bodineau–Martin proved a GUE central limit theorem implying Tracy–Widom universality for last-passage percolation in thin rectangles, by coupling random walks to Brownian motion via Tusnády-type approximations. Subsequent work has extended such universality results, but no fully general probabilistic operation X playing the role of summation in the classical CLT — yielding Tracy–Widom or Gaudin limits for arbitrary i.i.d. inputs — has been identified.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop perturbation theory for infinite-dimensional integrable systems in settings where solitons are present and the perturbation no longer becomes asymptotically negligible. A central instance is the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an added perturbation term ε V(|u|)u, especially for solutions lying near k-soliton states with k≥2, together with a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics; related questions include the persistence of Toda shocks and rarefactions under perturbations and perturbations of the sine-Gordon equation relevant to the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam problem.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation perturbed by a small nonlinear lower-order term:

   i u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u + ε V(|u|) u = 0,    (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ,

where ε > 0 is a small parameter and V: [0,∞) → ℝ is a smooth real-valued function (so that the perturbation εV(|u|)u preserves the L^2 norm but is, in general, non-integrable and does not decay or become asymptotically negligible compared to the integrable nonlinearity). The unperturbed equation (ε = 0) is completely integrable by the inverse scattering transform and admits k-soliton solutions for every k ≥ 1.

Develop a perturbation theory for this equation in the regime where solitons are present and the perturbation is not asymptotically negligible. Specifically, accomplish the following:

(a) For initial data u(x,0) lying in a sufficiently small neighborhood (in a suitable function space, e.g. a weighted Sobolev space) of a k-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS with k ≥ 2, prove global existence and produce a detailed description of the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t → ±∞: identify the emerging soliton parameters (positions, velocities, phases, amplitudes), the dispersive radiation contribution, and any corrections due to the perturbation εV(|u|)u, with explicit error estimates uniform in ε small.

(b) Establish an analogous perturbation theory for the Toda lattice in the presence of shocks and rarefaction waves, showing that such structures persist under small non-integrable perturbations of the lattice equations.

(c) Establish an analogous perturbation theory for the sine-Gordon equation under perturbations of the form relevant to the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam problem, again describing long-time asymptotics in the presence of multi-kink (soliton) configurations.

The goal is a unified asymptotic theory extending the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent / perturbed Riemann–Hilbert methodology to settings with multi-soliton backgrounds and non-decaying perturbations.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Deift–Zhou-style perturbative long-time asymptotic results have been extended to perturbations of mKdV and to focusing NLS with nonzero boundary conditions and discrete spectrum, and soliton-resolution results have been obtained. However, a full perturbation theory for the focusing cubic NLS near k-soliton states (k ≥ 2) with general non-decaying perturbation εV(|u|)u, plus the Toda shock/rarefaction and sine-Gordon FPU components, is not fully established and remains an active area of research.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For integrable equations on a half-line, resolve the mismatch between the well-posed initial-boundary data and the additional dependent boundary quantities required by the Fokas method. In particular, for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on x≥0,t≥0 with smooth compactly supported initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x) and periodic boundary forcing u(0,t)=sin(ω t) with ω≠0, determine the long-time behavior of the solution and decide whether a fully explicit description is possible for general data.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the quarter plane,
    i u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u = 0,    x ≥ 0,  t ≥ 0,
(with either focusing or defocusing sign fixed) supplemented by:
  • initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x), where u_0 is smooth and compactly supported on [0,∞);
  • Dirichlet boundary forcing u(0,t) = sin(ω t), with a fixed real frequency ω ≠ 0.

The Fokas unified transform method represents the solution through a Riemann–Hilbert problem whose data require knowledge of additional boundary values (e.g. u_x(0,t)) beyond the initial-boundary data above. The "Dirichlet-to-Neumann" map needed to recover these unknown boundary quantities from the well-posed data is in general not explicit.

Problem. Determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t → ∞, for (x,t) in the quarter plane (in all relevant asymptotic sectors, e.g. x/t fixed). In particular:
  (a) Describe u(x,t) in the limit t → ∞ for general smooth compactly supported initial data u_0.
  (b) Decide whether a fully explicit description of this long-time behavior (including the asymptotics of the unknown Neumann boundary value u_x(0,t)) can be obtained for arbitrary such u_0.
category_tag: Integrable boundary value problems / Fokas method
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Boutet de Monvel, Its, and Kotlyarov, and later Lenells–Fokas, treated the focusing NLS on the half-line with t-periodic Dirichlet data of the form a·exp(2iωt). They computed the long-time asymptotics via nonlinear steepest descent for the associated Riemann–Hilbert problem and obtained perturbative explicit formulas for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map (asymptotically periodic Neumann values) in special regimes. A complete, fully explicit description for general smooth compactly supported initial data with sin(ωt) boundary forcing does not appear to be available; the underlying Dirichlet-to-Neumann problem is known to be nonlinear and, in some regimes, unstable. The problem is thus partially solved.
