context_brief: Typical paths producing large stationary delays
original_question: For the two-server queue regimes just described, namely the case rho = 1 with a subexponential service-time distribution and the case rho in (1, 2) with a heavy-tailed service-time distribution having all power moments finite, what are the typical sample paths that lead to large values of the stationary waiting time D?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a FCFS GI/GI/2 queue with two identical servers. Jobs arrive at epochs of a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times having mean 1/λ, and require i.i.d. service times {σ_n} (independent of the arrivals) with common distribution F on [0,∞) and mean Eσ. Define the traffic intensity ρ = λ Eσ/2 across the two servers (so the per-server load is ρ). Assume the queue is stable and let D denote the stationary waiting time (the steady-state delay before a typical arriving customer's service begins).

Determine, in each of the following two regimes, the structure of the "typical" sample paths of the input that produce a large value of D, in the sense of describing the conditional behavior of the interarrival and service-time sequences (e.g. how many service times become atypically large, of which order, and on what time scale relative to x) given the rare event {D > x}, as x → ∞:

(a) The critically loaded case ρ = 1 with the integrated-tail (residual) service distribution F^I subexponential.

(b) The overloaded case ρ ∈ (1,2) with service-time distribution F heavy-tailed but possessing all power moments E[σ^k] < ∞ for every k ≥ 1.

In each case, identify the most probable mechanism (number, sizes, and timing of "big jumps" in the service-time sequence, and any associated behavior of the arrival process) leading to {D > x}, and give the resulting asymptotics of P(D > x) as x → ∞.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Foss and Korshunov (and by Boxma, Foss et al.) developed a "principle of s−k big jumps" for GI/GI/s queues and obtained, for the half-loaded GI/GI/2 case (ρ=1) with intermediate regularly varying tails, sharp tail asymptotics for the stationary waiting time, identifying typical paths with one or two big service jumps depending on the variance. The case ρ ∈ (1,2) with service times having all moments finite (e.g. Weibull-type tails) is treated in later works on Weibullian multi-server queues, but a complete description of typical paths in full generality is not established. The status is therefore partially solved.

original_question: For the same join-the-shortest-queue model with stationary ergodic input, what are the minimal assumptions that guarantee uniqueness of the stationary regime?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with two identical servers fed by a single stationary and ergodic marked point process of arrivals $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$, where $t_n$ denotes the arrival time of the $n$-th customer (with $t_n<t_{n+1}$, $t_n\to\pm\infty$) and $\sigma_n\geq 0$ denotes its service requirement. Upon arrival, each customer is routed under the join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) discipline: customer $n$ enters the server whose current workload (residual work) is the smaller of the two, with ties broken by a fixed deterministic rule. Each server is work-conserving and serves its assigned customers in FCFS order at unit rate. Let $W_n=(W_n^{(1)},W_n^{(2)})$ denote the workload vector seen by the $n$-th arriving customer.

A stationary regime is a distribution on $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ that is invariant under the Palm-stationary dynamics induced by the input $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}$ and the JSQ routing rule, i.e. a probability measure $\pi$ such that if $W_0\sim\pi$ on the Palm probability space of the input, then the resulting bi-infinite workload process is jointly stationary and ergodic with the input.

Determine minimal assumptions on the stationary ergodic input $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}$ (e.g., on the joint law of inter-arrival times and service times, beyond the natural stability condition $\mathbb{E}[\sigma_0]<2\,\mathbb{E}[t_1-t_0]$) under which the stationary regime of the two-server JSQ system is unique.
status_search_result: A literature search did not turn up a result establishing minimal assumptions for uniqueness of the stationary regime of the two-server join-the-shortest-queue system under general stationary ergodic input. Existing work treats either i.i.d./Markovian inputs, heavy-traffic/Halfin–Whitt diffusion limits, or stability and tail asymptotics, but the minimal-assumption uniqueness question for the stationary ergodic JSQ model appears not to have been resolved.

context_brief: Stability of a greedy server on a circle
original_question: A single server moves on a circle. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate lambda and are placed uniformly on the circle. Serving a particle takes one unit of time, and after each service the server moves at positive finite constant speed to the nearest waiting particle, ignoring new arrivals while moving. Is this greedy-server model stable for every lambda < 1?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single server moving on a circle of finite circumference. Particles (customers) arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda > 0$ in time, and each arriving particle is placed at a location chosen uniformly at random on the circle, independently of everything else. The server operates as follows:

- Serving any single particle takes exactly one unit of time. While the server is serving a particle, it does not move.
- Immediately after completing a service, the particle being served is removed from the system, and the server selects, among all particles currently waiting, the one whose distance along the circle from the server's current position is smallest (ties broken arbitrarily).
- The server then travels along the circle toward that nearest waiting particle at a fixed positive finite speed $v$. New arrivals occurring during this travel are not considered for re-selection until the server reaches and begins serving the chosen particle.
- Upon arrival at the chosen particle, the server begins serving it (taking one unit of time), and the cycle repeats. If the system is empty when a service ends, the server waits in place until the next arrival, then proceeds toward it.

The system is said to be stable if the underlying Markov process describing the server position together with the configuration of waiting particles is positive recurrent.

Prove or disprove: for every $\lambda < 1$ and every fixed speed $v \in (0, \infty)$, this greedy-server model is stable.
status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Coffman and Gilbert, 1987) that the greedy server on the circle is stable whenever the service rate exceeds the arrival rate was proven by Rojas-Nandayapa, Foss, and Kroese in "Stability of the Greedy Algorithm on the Circle" (arXiv:1112.2389, 2011), who established positive recurrence for any positive finite speed under the condition λ < 1.

original_question: Consider the following queueing system. There are three servers and a Poisson arrival process of rate lambda. Each arrival becomes class 1, 2, or 3 with probability 1/3. Class 1 customers may be served by servers 1 and 2, class 2 customers by servers 2 and 3, and class 3 customers by servers 3 and 1. Upon arrival, a customer chooses the accessible server with the shorter workload. If served by its left server, the service time has distribution F_l; if served by its right server, the service time has distribution F_r. In this model, can stability depend on both the initial state and the full service-time distributions F_l and F_r rather than only on coarse summary parameters?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following continuous-time queueing system with three servers, labeled 1, 2, and 3. Customers arrive according to a Poisson process of intensity $\lambda > 0$. Each arriving customer is independently assigned a class $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ with probability $1/3$ each. Class $i$ may only be served by two of the three servers, according to the cyclic rule:
- class 1 customers may be served by servers 1 or 2,
- class 2 customers may be served by servers 2 or 3,
- class 3 customers may be served by servers 3 or 1.

For each class, designate one of its two accessible servers as the "left" server and the other as the "right" server (consistently across the cycle). Upon arrival, a customer inspects the current workloads of its two accessible servers and joins the one with the smaller workload (breaking ties by some fixed rule). The service time of a customer is an independent random variable whose distribution depends on which server serves it: it has distribution $F_l$ on $[0,\infty)$ if served by its left server, and distribution $F_r$ on $[0,\infty)$ if served by its right server. Each server processes its queue in FIFO order at unit speed.

Question: Is it the case that the stability of this system (for instance, the property that the workload process is positive recurrent or remains tight in distribution) can depend not merely on the mean service times and the arrival rate $\lambda$, but genuinely on the full distributions $F_l$ and $F_r$, and moreover on the initial state of the workloads? Equivalently, do there exist choices of $\lambda$ and pairs $(F_l, F_r)$ with prescribed means for which the system is stable from some initial conditions but unstable from others, or for which two distinct distribution pairs with identical first moments produce different stability behavior?
status_search_result: A web search returned the original list of open problems in stochastic stability but no follow-up paper that explicitly resolves this three-server cyclic Join-the-Shortest-Workload conjecture about dependence on initial state and full service-time distributions. The status appears unresolved in the public literature, but no definitive verification of openness was located.

original_question: Consider a slotted multi-access channel in which packets have unit service time, arrivals during each slot are Poisson with parameter lambda, W_n is the number of packets in the system at the beginning of slot n, and each packet attempts transmission in slot n with probability p_n. A transmission succeeds if exactly one packet transmits, collides if two or more transmit, and is empty if none transmits. Suppose p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and on the binary information of whether slot n contained a successful transmission. Does there exist a protocol of this form for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent for some lambda > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a slotted multi-access communication channel operating in discrete time slots n = 0, 1, 2, …. All packets have unit service time equal to one slot. The number of new packets arriving during each slot is independent and Poisson distributed with parameter λ > 0. Let W_n denote the number of packets present in the system at the beginning of slot n.

At the beginning of slot n, each packet currently in the system independently attempts to transmit with the same probability p_n ∈ (0,1). The outcome of slot n is:
- successful, if exactly one packet attempts to transmit (this packet then leaves the system);
- a collision, if two or more packets attempt to transmit (all such packets remain in the system);
- empty, if no packet attempts to transmit.

The retransmission probabilities {p_n} are defined inductively by a feedback rule of the following restricted form: p_{n+1} is a (deterministic) function of p_n and of the single bit S_n ∈ {0,1} indicating whether slot n contained a successful transmission (S_n = 1) or did not (S_n = 0). Under any such rule, the pair (W_n, p_n) forms a time-homogeneous Markov chain.

Question: Within the class of all such success-only-feedback protocols, does there exist a protocol and some λ > 0 for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent (ergodic)?
status_search_result: A brief web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the stability question for slotted ALOHA-type protocols restricted to success-only (one-bit) feedback. Existing literature on generalized slotted-ALOHA stability typically assumes ternary feedback (idle/success/collision) or full feedback, and no explicit positive or negative resolution of the stated success-only-feedback problem was located. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: Let k be a field of characteristic zero. Is the group GAn(k) generated by tame automorphisms together with finitely many one-parameter subgroups of automorphisms?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and for an integer $n \geq 1$ let $\mathrm{GA}_n(k) = \mathrm{Aut}_k(k[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$ denote the group of polynomial automorphisms of affine $n$-space over $k$; equivalently, $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ consists of all $k$-algebra automorphisms $\varphi$ of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, identified with $n$-tuples $(\varphi(x_1),\ldots,\varphi(x_n))$ of polynomials whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero element of $k$. 

Within $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$, the subgroup of tame automorphisms $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ is the subgroup generated by the affine linear automorphisms (the group $\mathrm{Aff}_n(k) = \mathrm{GL}_n(k) \ltimes k^n$) together with the elementary (triangular) automorphisms of the form $(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}, x_i + f(x_1,\ldots,\hat{x_i},\ldots,x_n), x_{i+1},\ldots,x_n)$ for $f \in k[x_1,\ldots,\hat{x_i},\ldots,x_n]$.

A one-parameter subgroup of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is a group homomorphism $\rho: (k,+) \to \mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ such that the map $k \times k^n \to k^n$, $(t, x) \mapsto \rho(t)(x)$, is polynomial in $t$ and in $x$.

Question: Does there exist a finite collection $\rho_1, \ldots, \rho_m$ of one-parameter subgroups of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ such that $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is generated, as an abstract group, by $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ together with the images of $\rho_1, \ldots, \rho_m$?
status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The question of generating the polynomial automorphism group $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ in characteristic zero by tame automorphisms together with finitely many one-parameter subgroups appears to remain open; for $n=3$ it is known (Shestakov–Umirbaev) that wild automorphisms exist, so $\mathrm{GA}_n(k) \neq \mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ in general, but no result establishing or refuting generation modulo finitely many one-parameter subgroups was found.

original_question: Classify normal affine equivariant embeddings of connected solvable linear algebraic groups for which all isotropy groups are semisimple.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected solvable linear algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. By an equivariant embedding of $G$ we mean a normal algebraic variety $X$ equipped with a $G$-action together with a $G$-equivariant open embedding of a homogeneous space $G/H$ into $X$ as a dense orbit. Such an embedding is called affine if $X$ is an affine variety.

Problem: Classify, up to $G$-equivariant isomorphism, all normal affine equivariant embeddings $X$ of connected solvable linear algebraic groups $G$ (i.e., embeddings of homogeneous spaces $G/H$ for various closed subgroups $H \subseteq G$) with the property that for every point $x \in X$ the isotropy subgroup $G_x = \{g \in G : g\cdot x = x\}$ is a semisimple algebraic group.

In particular, treat first the case in which a maximal torus of $G$ has dimension one.
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published classification matching this exact problem. Related work on equivariant embeddings of commutative linear algebraic groups of corank one and on spherical/toroidal embeddings of solvable groups exists, but no source confirming a complete classification of normal affine equivariant embeddings of connected solvable linear algebraic groups with semisimple isotropy was located. The current status is therefore unclear.

original_question: Using the same subgroups Gi from the previous problem, define Hi = Gi cap TAn(k). Is TAn(k) generated by H1, ..., Hn? If so, is TAn(k) the amalgamated product of the Hi along pairwise intersections?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ denote the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ (equivalently, polynomial automorphisms of affine $n$-space over $k$). Let $\mathrm{TA}_n(k) \le \mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ be the tame subgroup, that is, the subgroup generated by all affine automorphisms together with all elementary (triangular) automorphisms of the form $x_i \mapsto x_i + f(x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n)$ (with the other variables fixed).

For each $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, define
$$G_i \;=\; \{\,\varphi \in \mathrm{GA}_n(k) \;:\; \varphi(V_i)=V_i\,\},\qquad V_i := k \oplus kx_1 \oplus kx_2 \oplus \cdots \oplus kx_i,$$
the subgroup of polynomial automorphisms that stabilize the $k$-subspace $V_i \subset k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ setwise. Set
$$H_i \;=\; G_i \cap \mathrm{TA}_n(k).$$

Answer the following two questions:

(a) Is $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ generated by $H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n$, i.e. $\mathrm{TA}_n(k) = \langle H_1,\dots,H_n\rangle$?

(b) If so, is $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ isomorphic to the amalgamated product of the subgroups $H_1,\dots,H_n$ along their pairwise intersections $H_i \cap H_j$?
status_search_result: The question is part of a list of open problems on automorphisms of affine spaces (2009). For $n=2$, the Jung–van der Kulk theorem gives an amalgamated free product structure (and $\mathrm{TA}_2(k)=\mathrm{GA}_2(k)$). For $n\ge 3$, the structure of $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ is much less understood; recent work on combinatorics of the tame automorphism group (e.g. Bisi–Furter–Maubach, Lamy and collaborators) studies such generation/amalgamation questions but no general affirmative answer for arbitrary $n\ge 3$ has been published. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be a commutative R-algebra, and call an R-subspace M of A a Mathieu subspace if for any a, b in A, whenever a^m belongs to M for all sufficiently large m, one also has a^m b in M for all sufficiently large m. Let M = {f in C[x] | integral over Cn of f(x) dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra. An $R$-subspace $M \subseteq A$ is called a Mathieu subspace of $A$ if for every $a, b \in A$ the following implication holds: whenever $a^m \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$, one also has $a^m b \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$.

Setup. Fix a positive integer $n$, let $C^n := [0,1]^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be the closed unit $n$-cube, and consider the polynomial algebra $A = \mathbb{C}[x] = \mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$. Define the $\mathbb{C}$-linear subspace
$$ M \;:=\; \Bigl\{\, f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n] \;\Big|\; \int_{C^n} f(x)\,dx = 0 \,\Bigr\}. $$

Question. Is $M$ a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$? That is, does it hold that for every $f, g \in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, if $\int_{C^n} f(x)^m\,dx = 0$ for all sufficiently large $m$, then $\int_{C^n} f(x)^m g(x)\,dx = 0$ for all sufficiently large $m$?
status_search_result: A web search for results on this specific cube-integral Mathieu subspace question did not return a definitive resolution. Subsequent work has developed Mathieu–Zhao subspaces in polynomial rings, but no source clearly confirms that this particular question (vanishing of integrals of f^m over the unit n-cube implying vanishing of integrals of f^m g) has been resolved either way; status is therefore inconclusive.

paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
original_question: How can stellar evolutionary models provide a robust physical treatment of the third dredge-up in Thermally Pulsing Asymptotic Giant Branch stars by correctly describing convection and mixing across regions with strong composition and opacity discontinuities, so that the efficiency of the third dredge-up does not have to be represented by arbitrary methods and tunable free parameters?
self_contained_problem:
In the theory of stellar evolution, a Thermally Pulsing Asymptotic Giant Branch (TPAGB) star is a low- to intermediate-mass star (initial mass roughly 0.8–8 solar masses) in a late evolutionary phase characterized by alternating hydrogen- and helium-shell burning around an electron-degenerate carbon–oxygen core. After each helium-shell flash (thermal pulse), the convective envelope of the star may penetrate inward into layers previously processed by nuclear burning, dredging freshly synthesized elements (notably ^12C and s-process elements) to the surface. This mixing event is called the third dredge-up (3DU).

The physical region where 3DU occurs presents a sharp discontinuity in chemical composition and in the radiative opacity κ between the H-rich convective envelope and the underlying He/C-rich intershell. Standard one-dimensional stellar evolution models describe convection through local prescriptions (such as mixing-length theory) supplemented by ad hoc criteria for the convective boundary (Schwarzschild or Ledoux), and treat penetration/overshooting beyond the formal boundary by parameterized algorithms. As a consequence, in current fully evolutionary AGB codes, the depth and efficiency of the 3DU is set by one or more tunable free parameters (e.g. an overshooting length, a minimum core mass for dredge-up, or a dredge-up efficiency parameter λ).

Problem. Formulate, from first physical principles, a treatment of convection and convective–radiative boundary mixing in a 1D stellar evolution framework that:

(i) correctly handles turbulent mixing across an interface with simultaneous strong gradients in mean molecular weight μ and opacity κ;
(ii) determines the location and motion of the convective boundary, and the resulting chemical mixing profile, without invoking arbitrary parameterizations or freely adjustable efficiency parameters; and
(iii) when applied through a sequence of thermal pulses on the TPAGB, predicts the depth and chemical yield of each third dredge-up episode as a deterministic outcome of the equations governing the stellar structure, hydrodynamics, and microphysics.

Provide such a treatment, prove that it reduces to known limits in regimes without composition/opacity discontinuities, and demonstrate that the resulting 3DU efficiency λ (defined as the ratio of the mass dredged up to the mass by which the H-exhausted core grew during the preceding interpulse) is fixed uniquely by the stellar parameters (mass, metallicity, evolutionary state) with no free tuning.
status_search_result: The treatment of convective boundary mixing during the third dredge-up in TPAGB stars remains an open modeling problem. Recent reviews and papers (e.g., Karakas & Lattanzio 2014; Cinquegrana & Karakas 2022; 3D hydrodynamic simulations by Freytag, Herwig, and collaborators through the mid-2020s) continue to report that 1D AGB evolution codes use parameterized overshooting or dredge-up efficiency parameters, and that a fully first-principles description of mixing across the composition/opacity discontinuity at the base of the convective envelope is still lacking.

original_question: What is the predictive power of synthetic Asymptotic Giant Branch models outside the parameter space covered by the populations used to calibrate them, given that these simulations still inherit the same unresolved physical problems as full evolutionary AGB models and require multiple parameters to be tuned by hand to match selected observations?
self_contained_problem:
Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are evolved low- and intermediate-mass stars whose structure and chemical yields depend on physical processes (convective boundary mixing, third dredge-up efficiency, mass-loss rates, hot bottom burning, etc.) that are not yet determined from first principles. Two classes of models are used to describe AGB evolution:

(i) Full evolutionary AGB models, which integrate the stellar structure equations through the thermally pulsing phase but contain several unresolved physical uncertainties.

(ii) Synthetic AGB models, which parameterize the outcome of each thermal pulse and interpulse phase using analytic or fitted relations, with a finite collection of free parameters p = (p_1, …, p_n) (e.g., the minimum core mass for third dredge-up, the dredge-up efficiency lambda, mass-loss prescriptions, and HBB temperature). These free parameters are calibrated on a chosen set of observed AGB populations P_cal (for example, the carbon-star luminosity functions of the Magellanic Clouds), by selecting p so that model predictions reproduce the chosen observables.

Let Theta denote the full physical parameter space of an AGB star (initial mass, metallicity, mixing length, helium content, etc.), and let Theta_cal ⊂ Theta be the region populated by the calibration set P_cal.

Question: Quantify and characterize the predictive power of synthetic AGB models outside Theta_cal. Specifically, given that synthetic models inherit the same unresolved physical uncertainties as full evolutionary models and require hand-tuning of parameters p on P_cal, determine to what extent (and under what conditions on the parameterization, the choice of calibration observables, and the structure of Theta_cal) predictions made for points in Theta \ Theta_cal — such as integrated yields, surface chemical abundances, lifetimes, and luminosity functions for stellar populations at metallicities, ages, or initial-mass ranges not represented in P_cal — remain reliable.
status_search_result: This is an open scientific modeling question rather than a closed mathematical problem. The literature on synthetic AGB models (e.g., Marigo & Girardi, Cristallo et al., Karakas, Pastorelli et al.) continues to refine calibrations using Magellanic Cloud and Milky Way data, but the extrapolation reliability of synthetic AGB models outside calibrated regions remains acknowledged as an unresolved issue, and recalibrations are repeatedly needed when new observational datasets (e.g., from JWST, Gaia, or new MC surveys) become available.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: For the boundary-value problem for an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium governed by equations (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), and the objective-derivative constitutive law (2.18), does the initial-boundary value problem admit a global strong solution in dimensions n ≥ 2 without imposing any restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $T>0$. Consider the initial-boundary value problem for an incompressible viscoelastic medium of Jeffreys type, in which the velocity field $v:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^n$, the pressure $p:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}$, and the extra (deviatoric) stress tensor $\sigma:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_{\mathrm{sym}}$ satisfy:

(i) The momentum balance and incompressibility:
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla)v - \nu\,\Delta v + \nabla p = \operatorname{Div}\sigma + f, \qquad \operatorname{div} v = 0,\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),$$
where $\nu>0$ is a Newtonian viscosity and $f$ is a given external body force.

(ii) The no-slip boundary condition and initial data:
$$v\big|_{\partial\Omega} = 0,\qquad v\big|_{t=0} = v_0\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad \sigma\big|_{t=0}=\sigma_0\quad\text{in }\Omega,$$
with $\operatorname{div} v_0 = 0$.

(iii) A Jeffreys-type constitutive law for $\sigma$ involving an objective (frame-indifferent) time derivative $\mathcal{D}_a$ of the form
$$\mathcal{D}_a \sigma := \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla)\sigma + \sigma\,W(v) - W(v)\,\sigma - a\bigl(\sigma\,E(v)+E(v)\,\sigma\bigr),$$
where $E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^\top)$, $W(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v-\nabla v^\top)$, and $a\in[-1,1]$ is a fixed parameter, and the relation
$$\sigma + \lambda\,\mathcal{D}_a\sigma = 2\eta\,E(v),$$
with positive relaxation time $\lambda$ and elastic viscosity $\eta>0$.

A strong solution on $[0,T]$ is a triple $(v,p,\sigma)$ such that $v\in L^\infty(0,T;H^1_0(\Omega)^n)\cap L^2(0,T;H^2(\Omega)^n)$ with $\partial_t v\in L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$, $\sigma\in L^\infty(0,T;H^1(\Omega)^{n\times n})$ with $\partial_t\sigma\in L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$, the equations hold a.e., and the initial conditions are attained.

Question: For every $n\ge 2$, every bounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, every $T>0$, and arbitrary positive coefficients $\nu,\lambda,\eta$, parameter $a\in[-1,1]$, external force $f$ in a natural class (e.g. $L^2(0,T;L^2(\Omega)^n)$), and arbitrary admissible initial data $(v_0,\sigma_0)$, does the above initial-boundary value problem admit a global strong solution on $[0,T]$, with no smallness or other restriction on the data, coefficients, or force?
status_search_result: Recent literature (including a 2025 study of flow-through problems for Jeffreys fluids with objective derivatives and surveys on viscoelastic models) explicitly notes that for differential viscoelastic models with an objective time derivative in the constitutive law, no global strong solvability results without restrictions on data are known. Even global weak existence for related incompressible viscoelastic systems is described as a longstanding open problem. No source confirms a resolution of the unrestricted global strong solvability problem in dimensions $n\ge 2$.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: For weak solutions of the initial-boundary value problem for the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18), can one prove uniqueness in dimensions n ≥ 2 without imposing any restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $T>0$. Consider the initial–boundary value problem for the motion of an incompressible viscoelastic medium of Jeffreys type:
$$
\partial_t v+(v\cdot\nabla)v=-\nabla p+\operatorname{Div}\sigma+f\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),
$$
$$
\operatorname{div} v=0\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),
$$
together with the rheological (constitutive) relation of Jeffreys type
$$
\sigma+\lambda_1\bigl(\partial_t\sigma+(v\cdot\nabla)\sigma+\sigma W(v)-W(v)\sigma\bigr)=2\eta\bigl(\mathcal{E}(v)+\lambda_2(\partial_t\mathcal{E}(v)+(v\cdot\nabla)\mathcal{E}(v)+\mathcal{E}(v)W(v)-W(v)\mathcal{E}(v))\bigr),
$$
where $\mathcal{E}(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^{\top})$, $W(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v-\nabla v^{\top})$, $\eta>0$, and $0<\lambda_2<\lambda_1$ are constants. Impose the no-slip condition
$$
v|_{\partial\Omega\times(0,T)}=0,
$$
and the initial conditions
$$
v|_{t=0}=v_0\in L^2_{\mathrm{div}}(\Omega),\qquad \sigma|_{t=0}=\sigma_0,
$$
with external force $f\in L^2(0,T;H^{-1}(\Omega))$. A weak solution is a pair $(v,\sigma)$ in the natural energy class satisfying the system in the standard distributional/integral sense.

Question: For all dimensions $n\ge 2$, can one establish uniqueness of weak solutions of this initial–boundary value problem without imposing any additional smallness or smoothness restrictions on the coefficients $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\eta$, the external force $f$, or the initial data $(v_0,\sigma_0)$?
status_search_result: Available literature on Jeffreys-type viscoelastic models (Vorotnikov–Zvyagin and follow-ups) establishes existence of weak solutions, regularization, and attractor results, but unconditional uniqueness of weak solutions in dimensions $n\ge 2$ without restrictions on coefficients, force, or data is not reported as resolved. Like the analogous Navier–Stokes uniqueness problem (open for $n\ge 3$), this remains a listed open problem for the Jeffreys system in $n\ge 2$.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: Can one construct any generalized solution of the stationary boundary-value problem for the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18) without imposing restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type occupying a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The motion is governed by the stationary system

$$\rho(v\cdot\nabla)v - \mathrm{Div}\,\sigma = \rho f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\,v=0\quad\text{in }\Omega,$$

with the Jeffreys constitutive law for the deviatoric stress $\sigma$,

$$\sigma + \lambda_1 \big((v\cdot\nabla)\sigma + \sigma W(v) - W(v)\sigma\big) = 2\eta\Big(\mathcal E(v) + \lambda_2\big((v\cdot\nabla)\mathcal E(v) + \mathcal E(v)W(v) - W(v)\mathcal E(v)\big)\Big),$$

where $\mathcal E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v + \nabla v^\top)$ is the rate-of-strain tensor, $W(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v - \nabla v^\top)$ is the vorticity tensor, $\rho>0$ is the density, $\eta>0$ is the viscosity, and $0<\lambda_2<\lambda_1$ are the relaxation and retardation times. The system is closed with the no-slip boundary condition $v\big|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ together with appropriate boundary conditions for $\sigma$ on the inflow part of $\partial\Omega$, and a prescribed external body force $f$.

Question: Does there exist a generalized (weak) solution $(v,\sigma)$ of this stationary boundary-value problem for arbitrary admissible coefficients $\rho,\eta,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ and arbitrary external force $f$, without imposing any smallness, regularity, or other restrictive conditions on the coefficients or the data?
status_search_result: Existence of weak solutions for the stationary boundary-value problem of the Jeffreys-type viscoelastic system has been established in several settings (e.g., inhomogeneous Dirichlet conditions via elliptic regularization and topological degree, and flow-through problems in bounded domains without smallness assumptions on forcing/boundary data). However, these constructions typically rely on specific regularizations (such as replacing the vorticity tensor by a spatial average in Jeffreys' law) or particular boundary configurations, so a fully unrestricted construction for the original (non-regularized) Jeffreys system with arbitrary coefficients and data is not yet available in full generality.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: Does the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18) admit time-periodic solutions without restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following Jeffreys-type model for the motion of an incompressible viscoelastic fluid in a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The unknowns are the velocity field $v(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and the pressure $p(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}$, and the system reads:

(i) Equation of motion:
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla) v = \operatorname{Div}\sigma + f,$$

(ii) Incompressibility: $\operatorname{div} v = 0,$

(iii) Constitutive law of Jeffreys type: the deviatoric stress tensor $\tau$ obeys
$$\tau + \lambda_1 \frac{D\tau}{Dt} = 2\eta\Big(\mathcal E(v) + \lambda_2 \frac{D\mathcal E(v)}{Dt}\Big),$$
with total Cauchy stress $\sigma = -pI + \tau$, where $\mathcal E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^T)$ is the symmetric strain-rate tensor, $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>0$ are retardation/relaxation times, $\eta>0$ is the viscosity, and $D/Dt$ denotes an objective (e.g. upper- or lower-convected, or Jaumann) time derivative including transport along $v$,

(iv) No-slip boundary condition: $v|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$

(v) The external force $f(t,x)$ is given and time-periodic with period $T>0$, i.e. $f(t+T,x)=f(t,x)$.

Question: Without imposing any smallness or other restrictions on the coefficients $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\eta$, on the external force $f$, or on the data, does this system always admit at least one (weak) time-periodic solution $(v,p)$ of period $T$?
status_search_result: Surveys on Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid models list the existence of time-periodic solutions without restrictions on coefficients, force, or initial data among the unresolved problems. Web searches return work on related elastic wave equations with viscoelastic terms and on control/throughflow problems for Jeffreys fluids, but no general existence theorem of time-periodic weak solutions for the full Jeffreys system without smallness or regularity restrictions has been located. The status appears to remain open.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: If one succeeds, even partially, in proving global existence for the Jeffreys-type evolutionary problem, can one then construct attractors, at least generalized ones, and/or inertial manifolds for that system?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type, occupying a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary, and governed by the system
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t}+(v\cdot\nabla)v=\operatorname{Div}\sigma-\nabla p+f,\qquad \operatorname{div} v=0,\qquad v|_{\partial\Omega}=0,\qquad v|_{t=0}=v_0,$$
where the deviatoric stress tensor $\sigma$ obeys a Jeffreys-type constitutive relation
$$\sigma+\lambda_1\,\frac{\mathcal{D}\sigma}{\mathcal{D}t}=2\eta\Bigl(\mathcal{E}(v)+\lambda_2\,\frac{\mathcal{D}\mathcal{E}(v)}{\mathcal{D}t}\Bigr),$$
with $\mathcal{E}(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^\top)$, relaxation time $\lambda_1>0$, retardation time $\lambda_2\in(0,\lambda_1)$, viscosity $\eta>0$, and $\mathcal{D}/\mathcal{D}t$ an objective (e.g. upper-convected, lower-convected, or Jaumann) time derivative.

Suppose that, for a given choice of objective derivative and on a given class of initial data and external forces $f$, one has established (possibly only partial) global-in-time existence of weak solutions to this system.

Problem. Under such global existence, construct dynamical objects describing the long-time behaviour of the system: namely, prove the existence of a global attractor — or, failing that, of a generalized attractor (e.g. a trajectory attractor, or an attractor in the sense of multivalued semiflows / semigroups acting on a set of admissible trajectories) — for the resulting (possibly multivalued) dynamical system associated with the weak solutions. Moreover, determine whether the system admits a finite-dimensional inertial manifold, i.e. a finite-dimensional, Lipschitz, positively invariant manifold in the phase space that contains the global attractor and attracts all trajectories at a uniform exponential rate.
status_search_result: Existence of (trajectory and global) attractors for weak solutions of the autonomous Jeffreys-type viscoelastic motion equations has been established, and non-autonomous versions with memory have been treated as well. The inertial-manifold part of the question appears not to have been resolved for the Jeffreys system: standard results require a spectral gap condition that has not been verified in this setting, so to current knowledge no inertial manifold has been constructed. Hence the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
original_question: Are Dirac’s Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity, formulated using the original metric variables, and the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, which reparametrizes gravitational variables using lapse and shift functions together with the spatial three-metric, equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of the same theory despite the claim that the transformation from the four-metric variables to ADM variables is not canonical in the usual phase space?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity on a globally hyperbolic spacetime, given by the Einstein–Hilbert action

S = (1/16πG) ∫ R √(−g) d⁴x,

with dynamical field the Lorentzian four-metric g_{μν}.

Two standard Hamiltonian formulations of this theory are:

(A) Dirac's formulation. Carry out the Legendre transform directly in the variables g_{μν}, treating the ten components of the four-metric as configuration variables, introducing momenta π^{μν} conjugate to g_{μν}, and applying Dirac's algorithm for constrained Hamiltonian systems to obtain primary and secondary constraints together with a total Hamiltonian.

(B) ADM formulation. Perform a 3+1 decomposition of g_{μν} into the lapse N, the shift vector N^i, and the spatial three-metric γ_{ij} via
  g_{00} = −N² + γ_{ij} N^i N^j,  g_{0i} = γ_{ij} N^j,  g_{ij} = γ_{ij},
take (N, N^i, γ_{ij}) as configuration variables, and carry out the Dirac–Bergmann constrained-Hamiltonian analysis, yielding the familiar Hamiltonian and momentum (diffeomorphism) constraints.

A change of variables (g_{μν}) ↦ (N, N^i, γ_{ij}) is well-defined and invertible at the Lagrangian level, but extending it to a transformation of the phase-space variables (g_{μν}, π^{μν}) ↦ (N, N^i, γ_{ij}, π_N, π_{N^i}, π^{ij}_γ) is, in the standard phase space, not a canonical transformation: the induced map does not preserve the symplectic structure (Poisson brackets), and the gauge symmetries generated by the constraints in the two formulations differ.

Question. Are the Dirac formulation (A) and the ADM formulation (B) nevertheless equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of General Relativity, in the sense of describing the same physical theory with the same gauge structure and the same reduced phase space? In particular, is the apparent non-canonicity of the change of variables relating them an artifact that can be removed by a suitable extension or modification of the phase space, or does it reflect a genuine inequivalence of the two Hamiltonian formulations?
status_search_result: The question has been actively debated. One line of work (Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin and collaborators) argues that the Dirac and ADM Hamiltonian formulations are genuinely inequivalent because the change of variables to lapse/shift/three-metric is non-canonical and changes the gauge symmetry from full four-diffeomorphisms to a different (field-dependent) symmetry. A counter-line (e.g. Frolov–Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin, Shestakova) proposes that the non-canonicity disappears in an extended phase space where gauge degrees of freedom are treated on equal footing, recovering canonical equivalence. There is no universally accepted resolution, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved / actively discussed rather than definitively closed.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
context_brief: Phase-space transformations versus Einstein gauge transformations
original_question: Is the group of transformations generated in Hamiltonian phase space the same as, or at least inclusive of, the gauge-transformation group of Einstein General Relativity, including the diffeomorphism-type transformations of all gravitational variables such as g_{0μ} and the ADM lapse and shift variables?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Hilbert action for general relativity, viewed both in its Lagrangian (covariant) form, where the gauge group is the group of spacetime diffeomorphisms acting on the metric components $g_{\mu\nu}$ (including the components $g_{0\mu}$), and in its Hamiltonian (ADM) form, where one performs a $3+1$ decomposition introducing the lapse $N$, shift $N^i$, the spatial three-metric $h_{ij}$, and their conjugate momenta. In the Hamiltonian formulation, first-class constraints (the Hamiltonian constraint and the momentum/diffeomorphism constraints) generate a group $G_{\rm phase}$ of transformations on phase space (e.g., via the Dirac or Castellani prescription combining primary and secondary first-class constraints with appropriate parameters).

Let $G_{\rm Einstein}$ denote the gauge group of the Einstein theory, namely the group of spacetime diffeomorphism-type transformations acting on all gravitational variables, including $g_{0\mu}$ and equivalently the lapse and shift $(N,N^i)$.

Determine whether $G_{\rm phase} = G_{\rm Einstein}$, or at least whether $G_{\rm phase} \supseteq G_{\rm Einstein}$. Equivalently: is there a construction of the canonical generator on phase space such that the induced transformations of all components $g_{\mu\nu}$ — in particular of $g_{0\mu}$ (the lapse and shift) — coincide with (or contain) those produced by the spacetime diffeomorphism group of the Lagrangian theory?
status_search_result: The relationship between phase-space (canonical) gauge transformations and Lagrangian diffeomorphisms in GR has been studied extensively (Castellani's algorithm, Pons–Salisbury–Shepley, Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin and others). It is known that with appropriate combinations of first-class constraints one can generate transformations that include the spacetime diffeomorphisms of all metric components, including $g_{0\mu}$ and the lapse/shift, though typically through field-dependent (lapse/shift-dependent) reparametrizations of the gauge parameters. Thus the question is partially settled: inclusion $G_{\rm phase}\supseteq G_{\rm Einstein}$ can be achieved, but full equality and the conceptual interpretation remain debated in the literature.

paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
context_brief: Whether to abandon ADM and other parametrizations
original_question: Should the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, or other Hamiltonian formulations based on parametrizations whose canonicity is unproved in the usual phase space, be abandoned or treated as independent models rather than as valid formulations of Einstein General Relativity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Einstein's General Relativity, whose Lagrangian is the Einstein–Hilbert action on a globally hyperbolic spacetime. The standard Arnowitt–Deser–Misner (ADM) Hamiltonian formulation arises by performing a 3+1 decomposition of the spacetime metric g_{\mu
u} into the lapse N, shift N^i, and spatial 3-metric h_{ij}, taken as new configuration variables in place of the components of g_{\mu
u}. A Hamiltonian formulation is said to be canonically equivalent to another if the change of variables on phase space (together with the corresponding redefinition of momenta) is a canonical transformation in the standard sense — i.e. preserves the symplectic form / Poisson brackets — on the full phase space without restriction to constraint surfaces.

It is known that the change of variables from (g_{\mu
u}, \pi^{\mu
u}) to the ADM variables (N, N^i, h_{ij}) and their conjugate momenta has not been shown to be a canonical transformation on the full unconstrained phase space; analogous statements hold for various other 3+1 parametrizations (e.g. tetrad/triad-based, or those using different combinations of metric components).

Question. Determine whether the following position is mathematically justified: any Hamiltonian formulation of gravity built from a parametrization of the spacetime metric whose relation to the original metric variables is not implemented by a canonical transformation on the usual phase space should be regarded as an independent dynamical model (not equivalent to the Hamiltonian formulation of Einstein's General Relativity), rather than as a legitimate Hamiltonian reformulation of Einstein's theory. Equivalently, decide whether the ADM formulation and similar parametrization-based Hamiltonian formulations must be abandoned as formulations of Einstein General Relativity, or whether they remain physically and mathematically equivalent to it despite the absence of a proven canonical transformation between the variables.
status_search_result: The question is a methodological/foundational one in the canonical formulation of general relativity. The literature (Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin and responses) shows the issue is debated rather than settled by a definitive theorem; no widely accepted resolution proving that ADM must be abandoned, nor a complete proof of canonical equivalence on the full phase space, has been established. Status remains unclear.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: For a rotationally scalar nuclear Hamiltonian, the energy minimization can be restricted to scalar many-body density operators, so the associated one-body density is a radial monopole profile ρ0(r) and the resulting scalar functional is F0[ρ0]. What features of such radial density profiles determine whether the underlying nucleus is deformed, and can one formulate precise criteria, possibly using profile slopes at the nuclear surface or moments of the profiles, that distinguish spherical from deformed nuclei, hard from soft nuclei, and identify triaxial or halo nuclei?
status_search_result: The problem of identifying deformation signatures purely from the monopole/radial density profile in scalar nuclear DFT remains a recognized open problem in nuclear density functional theory, with no general criteria established. While studies have related radial moments and surface diffuseness to deformation, no precise mathematical criteria distinguishing spherical, deformed, soft/hard, triaxial, and halo nuclei from ρ₀ alone have been demonstrated. No published resolution was located.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: Let Φ be a simple intrinsic nuclear state, such as a Slater determinant or Hartree-Bogoliubov state, from which rotationally projected states ΦJMK are built by angular-momentum projection. Define an intrinsic-density functional FJMK[ρ] by minimizing the projected-state energy over simple intrinsic states Φ with intrinsic density ρ; this functional depends on the allowed class of Φ and, a priori, on the angular-momentum labels J, M, and K. Under what conditions can the intrinsic state or intrinsic density be practically independent of J, M, and K so that one density ρ is valid for many projected rotational states, and how does such an intrinsic-density functional relate to the traditional three-dimensional nuclear energy density functionals used for deformed nuclei?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a many-body Hamiltonian acting on an A-fermion Hilbert space, and let S be a class of "simple" intrinsic states Φ (for example, Slater determinants or Hartree–Bogoliubov quasiparticle vacua) on this space. For Φ ∈ S, let ρ_Φ(x) denote the one-body density associated with Φ. For each triple of angular-momentum labels (J, M, K) with |M|, |K| ≤ J, let P^J_{MK} denote the standard angular-momentum projection operator built from rotation operators R(Ω) and Wigner D-functions, so that Φ_{JMK} := P^J_{MK} Φ is a state of definite total angular momentum J and projection M (with intrinsic projection K).

Define the projected energy
  E[Φ; J, M, K] := ⟨Φ_{JMK}| H |Φ_{JMK}⟩ / ⟨Φ_{JMK}|Φ_{JMK}⟩,
and define the intrinsic-density functional
  F_{JMK}[ρ] := inf { E[Φ; J, M, K] : Φ ∈ S, ρ_Φ = ρ },
with associated minimum E_{JMK} := inf_ρ F_{JMK}[ρ]. A priori F_{JMK}[ρ] depends on the class S and on the labels (J, M, K).

(a) Determine sufficient conditions on the Hamiltonian H, the class S, and the range of labels (J, M, K) under which there exists a single density ρ* (or a single intrinsic state Φ* ∈ S) that is, to a controlled approximation, a minimizer of F_{JMK}[·] simultaneously for a large family of values of (J, M, K), so that one intrinsic density ρ* serves as a common minimizer for many projected rotational states Φ_{JMK}.

(b) Establish a precise relationship between such an intrinsic-density functional F_{JMK}[ρ] and the standard three-dimensional energy density functionals E[ρ] employed for deformed many-body systems, in which the deformed (intrinsic) density is treated as the fundamental variable without explicit angular-momentum projection.
status_search_result: The question concerns the foundations of projected/intrinsic-density functional theory for deformed nuclei. The literature on multi-reference and projected EDFs (e.g., works by Duguet, Bender, Lacroix and collaborators) discusses partial results and self-consistency issues, but no general theorem characterizing when one intrinsic density can serve a large family of (J,M,K) projected states, nor a rigorous derivation linking such a functional to standard 3D deformed EDFs, has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: In a finite harmonic-oscillator shell-model construction, the neutron and proton densities are represented by finite density-polynomial coefficients, the Levy-Lieb density constraints and normalization constraint become algebraic polynomial equations in configuration-mixing coefficients, and eliminating constrained variables and survivor coefficients yields an implicit polynomial relation R(η, Cn1, …, CnNn, Cp1, …, CpNp) = 0 linking the minimal energy η to density parameters. What practical algebraic strategies can handle the resulting large multivariate polynomials, compare distinct polynomial relations R obtained from different finite-basis choices, extrapolate when direct calculations become too cumbersome, and make rigorous polynomial density functionals useful in larger nuclear models?
status_search_result: The question is posed as a programmatic open challenge about algebraic-computational strategies (handling, comparing, and extrapolating large implicit polynomial density functionals). No literature was found establishing a general solution; standard tools (Gröbner bases, resultants, numerical algebraic geometry) exist but no rigorous, general framework targeted at this nuclear-density-functional construction has been identified. Status appears open.

paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
original_question: Can the same algebraic polynomial method for constructing nuclear density functionals from finite configuration-mixing models and polynomial density constraints be applied to nuclear cluster-model calculations?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a finite-dimensional configuration-mixing framework for a self-bound many-body fermion system (such as an atomic nucleus). Suppose one has a finite family of trial many-body states {|Φ_i⟩}_{i=1}^N, each producing a one-body density ρ_i(r), and one forms mixed states by superposition with coefficients that are determined by enforcing a finite set of polynomial constraints on the total density ρ(r) (for instance, constraints of the form ∫ P_k(r) ρ(r) d^3r = c_k for prescribed polynomials P_k and values c_k). Within this setting, one can construct an energy density functional E[ρ] purely algebraically: the functional is obtained by eliminating the mixing parameters from the polynomial density constraints, yielding E[ρ] as an algebraic (polynomial) function of moments of ρ. Call this construction the "algebraic polynomial method" for energy density functionals.

Question. Does there exist an analogous algebraic polynomial construction in the context of nuclear cluster models — i.e., many-body trial states built from a finite set of pre-formed cluster substructures (such as α-particle clusters) with relative coordinates and antisymmetrization between clusters — such that:
(i) the cluster-model trial states play the role of the finite configuration-mixing basis;
(ii) a finite set of polynomial constraints on the total one-body density (or on cluster-collective coordinates) plays the role of the density constraints; and
(iii) elimination of the mixing/cluster parameters yields a closed-form polynomial energy density functional E[ρ] reproducing the cluster-model energies?

Determine whether such an algebraic polynomial construction of an energy density functional from cluster-model calculations exists in general, and if so describe the class of cluster models and polynomial density constraints for which it is well-defined.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of whether the algebraic polynomial construction of energy density functionals from finite configuration-mixing/polynomial-density-constraint setups can be extended to nuclear cluster models. While constrained DFT is used to study cluster phenomena (e.g., α-cluster configurations via density-constrained Hartree-Fock) and there is recent work on cluster models within DFT frameworks, none of the located sources establish (or refute) a general algebraic polynomial construction of the desired type. Status appears unresolved in publicly accessible literature.

original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A2 ([S11e]). (i) If p is a prime and a is a positive integer with pa ≡ 1 (mod 3) , then ⌊ 2 3 pa⌋∑ k=0 (21k + 8) (2k k ) 3 ≡ 8pa (mod pa+5+(−1)p ). (ii) Any integer n > 1 satisfying the congruence ∑ n−1 k=0 (21k + 8) (2k k ) 3 ≡ 8n (mod n4) must be a prime.
self_contained_problem:
Prove or disprove the following two statements.

(i) Let $p$ be a prime and $a$ a positive integer with $p^a \equiv 1 \pmod 3$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor 2p^a/3 \rfloor} (21k+8)\binom{2k}{k}^{3} \;\equiv\; 8\,p^a \pmod{p^{\,a+5+(-1)^p}},$$
where the modulus exponent is $a+6$ when $p$ is odd and $a+4$ when $p=2$.

(ii) If an integer $n>1$ satisfies
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (21k+8)\binom{2k}{k}^{3} \;\equiv\; 8n \pmod{n^{4}},$$
then $n$ is prime.
status_search_result: The conjecture is part of Zhi-Wei Sun's series of supercongruence conjectures involving sums of (21k+8)·C(2k,k)^3. While related results (e.g., integrality of the average and weaker mod p^4 supercongruences) have been established, the strengthened modulus in part (i) and the primality characterization in part (ii) do not appear to have been proven in the literature; they are still listed among Sun's open conjectures.

If p ≡ 1 (mod 6) and p = x2 + 3y2 with x, y ∈ Z, then p−1∑ k=0 (2k k ) 3 16k ≡ 4x2 − 2p (mod p2) and p−1∑ k=0 k (2k k ) 3 16k ≡ p − 4x2 3 (mod p2). If p ≡ 5 (mod 6) , then p−1∑ k=0 (2k k ) 3 16k ≡ 0 (mod p2) and p−1∑ k=0 k (2k k ) 3 16k ≡ p 3 (mod p2). Furthermore, pa pa−1∑ k=0 3k + 1 16k (2k k ) 3 ≡ 1 + 7 6p3Bp−3 (mod p4) for all a ∈ Z+, and (p−1)/ 2∑ k=0 (3k + 1) (2k k ) 3 16k ≡ p + 2 (−1 p ) p3Ep−3 (mod p4). Also, 2n (2n n ) n−1∑ k=0 (3k + 1) (2k k ) 3 16n−1−k ∈ Z for all n = 2 , 3, 4, . . . .
self_contained_problem:
Let $p>3$ be a prime. Prove or disprove the following statements.

(1) If $p\equiv 1\pmod 6$ and $p=x^2+3y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 4x^2-2p\pmod{p^2}\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv \frac{p-4x^2}{3}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(2) If $p\equiv 5\pmod 6$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 0\pmod{p^2}\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv \frac{p}{3}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(3) For every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 1+\frac{7}{6}p^3 B_{p-3}\pmod{p^4},$$
where $B_n$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli number.

(4) One has
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv p+2\Big(\frac{-1}{p}\Big)p^3 E_{p-3}\pmod{p^4},$$
where $E_n$ denotes the $n$th Euler number and $\big(\frac{\cdot}{p}\big)$ is the Legendre symbol.

(5) For every integer $n\geq 2$,
$$\frac{2n}{\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^{n-1-k}}\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
status_search_result: Several parts of this multi-part conjecture have been addressed in the literature. The Dwork-type supercongruence in part (3) (the $p^a$ statement) is related to work of Guo–Zudilin and a proof by Y. Zhang and P. Yuan establishing $\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\equiv p\sum_{k=0}^{p^{r-1}-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\pmod{p^{3r+1-\delta_{p,3}}}$, and Beukers' method has been applied to similar families. However, no single reference verified in the search establishes the full set of statements (the precise mod $p^2$ identities for the unweighted sums in terms of $p=x^2+3y^2$, the mod $p^4$ refinement involving $B_{p-3}$ and $E_{p-3}$, and the integrality assertion), so the conjecture as a whole appears only partially resolved.

Let $p>3$ be a prime. Denote by $\left(\tfrac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)$ the Legendre/Jacobi symbol, and let $B_n(x)$ denote the Bernoulli polynomial of degree $n$. Prove or disprove the following three statements.

(i) The congruence

holds, where $x,y\in\mathbb Z$ in the first two cases.

(ii) For every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\frac{615k+53}{(-48)^{3k}}\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}\equiv 53\,(p^a)+(p^{a-1})\cdot\tfrac{5}{12}\,p^2 B_{p-2}(\tfrac{1}{18})\pmod{p^3}.$$

is an integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n$ is an integer not divisible by $3$.

self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Consider the multinomial coefficient $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}=\frac{(4k)!}{(k!)^4}$ and the Bernoulli polynomial $B_{n}(x)$.

Prove or disprove the following statements.

(1) If $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right)=1$ (equivalently $p\equiv 1,3\pmod 8$) and $p=x^{2}+2y^{2}$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, then
$$\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{3}}{(-64)^{k}}\;\equiv\;\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{28^{4k}}\;\equiv\;4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(2) If $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right)=-1$ (equivalently $p\equiv 5,7\pmod 8$), then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{3}}{(-64)^{k}}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}},$$
and, provided $p\neq 7$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{28^{4k}}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(3) For every positive integer $a$ and every odd prime $p\notin\{3,7\}$,
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{40k+3}{28^{4k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\;\equiv\;3\!\left(\frac{p^{a}-(p^{a-1})}{?}\right)\;-\;\frac{5p^{2}}{392}\,B_{p-2}(1)\pmod{p^{3}}$$
(where the right-hand side is to be interpreted as in the standard formulation: $3(p^{a})-(p^{a-1})\cdot\frac{5p^{2}}{392}B_{p-2}(1)$ modulo $p^{3}$, with $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ extended multiplicatively).

(4) The numbers
$$a_{n}\;:=\;\frac{1}{2n(2n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(40k+3)\,\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\,28^{4(n-1-k)}$$
are integers for all $n=2,3,4,\dots$.
status_search_result: Web search did not yield a definitive proof or disproof of this specific multi-part conjecture (Sun's Conjecture A28) involving the sums $\sum\binom{2k}{k}^3/(-64)^k$ and $\sum\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}/28^{4k}$ together with the representation $p=x^2+2y^2$. Related Sun supercongruences (e.g. $\sum (4k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/64^k\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2r}}$) have been proven, but the precise statements (1)–(4) above do not appear to be fully resolved in the available literature.

For a nonnegative integer n, define
$$P_n \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}^{2}\binom{2k}{k}.$$
Let $p$ be an odd prime. For an integer $a$ not divisible by $p$, let $a^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $a$ modulo $p^2$, and interpret rational expressions of the form $r/s$ (with $\gcd(s,p)=1$) modulo $p^2$ as $r\cdot s^{-1} \pmod{p^2}$.

Decide whether the following two congruences hold.

(i) Suppose $p\equiv 3\pmod 8$ and write $p = x^2 + 2y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb Z$ chosen so that $y\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{P_k}{32^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2} \;\equiv\; (-1)^{(y-1)/2}\!\left(2y - \frac{p}{4y}\right)\pmod{p^2}.$$

(ii) Suppose $p\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$ and write $p = x^2 + 2y^2$ with $x\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$, and additionally $y\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$ when $p\equiv 3\pmod 8$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\,P_k}{32^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2} \;\equiv\; \begin{cases} (-1)^{(p-1)/8}\!\left(\dfrac{p}{4x} - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 1\pmod 8,\\[4pt] (-1)^{(y+1)/2}\, y \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 3\pmod 8. \end{cases}$$

Are both conjectured congruences true for every such prime $p$?

For integers $b,c$ and a nonnegative integer $n$, let the generalized central trinomial coefficient $T_n(b,c)$ be the coefficient of $x^n$ in $(x^2+bx+c)^n$, and write $T_n = T_n(1,1)$. Let $C_k = \binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ denote the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $\left(\tfrac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol.

Prove or disprove the following statements for every prime $p>3$.

(i) The following congruences hold:
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{12^k}T_k \equiv \left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)\frac{p-1+3}{4}\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{16^k}T_{2k}(4,1)\equiv 1\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k}{16^k}T_{2k}(4,1)\equiv 4\!\left(\!\left(\tfrac{3}{p}\right)-p\!\left(\tfrac{-1}{p}\right)\!\right)\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{4^k}T_{2k}(3,4)\equiv \left(\tfrac{-1}{p}\right)\frac{7-3p}{4}\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{16^k}T_{2k}(8,9)\equiv \left(\tfrac{3}{p}\right)\pmod{p^2}.$$

(ii) Moreover,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{16^k}T_{2k}(2,3)\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{16^k}T_{2k}(4,-3)\equiv \begin{cases}\left(\tfrac{-1}{p}\right)\!\left(2x-\tfrac{p}{2x}\right)\pmod{p^2} & \text{if } p\equiv 1\pmod 3,\ p=x^2+3y^2,\ 3\mid x-1,\\ 0\pmod{p} & \text{if } p\equiv 2\pmod 3;\end{cases}$$

For integers $b,c$ define the Chebyshev-like polynomials $T_n(b,c)$ by $T_0(b,c)=1$, $T_1(b,c)=b$, and
$$T_{n+1}(b,c)=bT_n(b,c)-cT_{n-1}(b,c)\quad(n\geq 1),$$
and define the Lucas sequences $u_n(b,c)$, $v_n(b,c)$ by $u_0=0$, $u_1=1$, $u_{n+1}=bu_n-cu_{n-1}$, and $v_0=2$, $v_1=b$, $v_{n+1}=bv_n-cv_{n-1}$. Let $\left(\tfrac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol.

Prove or disprove the following statements for every prime $p>3$.

(i) The three sums
$$S_1=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_k(10,1)}{(-64)^k},\quad S_2=\left(\tfrac{-1}{p}\right)\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_{2k}(6,1)}{256^k},\quad S_3=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_{2k}(6,1)}{1024^k}$$
are congruent mod $p^2$, and equal mod $p^2$ to:
- $4x^2-2p$ if $p\equiv 1,7\pmod{24}$ and $p=x^2+6y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$;
- $8x^2-2p$ if $p\equiv 5,11\pmod{24}$ and $p=2x^2+3y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$;
- $0$ if $\left(\tfrac{-6}{p}\right)=-1$, i.e. $p\equiv 13,17,19,23\pmod{24}$.

Moreover,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(3k+1)\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_k(10,1)}{(-64)^k}\equiv p\!\left(\left(\tfrac{-6}{p}\right)+1\right)\pmod{p^2},$$
and for every integer $n\geq 2$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_k(10,1)(-64)^{n-1-k}\equiv 0\pmod{2n\binom{2n}{n}}.$$
If $\left(\tfrac{-6}{p}\right)=1$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(16k+5)\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_{2k}(6,1)}{256^k}\equiv \tfrac{8}{3}p\left(\tfrac{-1}{p}\right)\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(16k+3)\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_{2k}(6,1)}{1024^k}\equiv -\tfrac{2}{3}p\pmod{p^2}.$$

(ii) If $p=x^2+6y^2$ with $x\equiv 1\pmod 3$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{108^k}k\,u_k(4,2)\equiv \tfrac{2x-p/x}{1}\pmod{p^2},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{108^k}v_k(4,2)\equiv 4x-\tfrac{p}{x}\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(3k-1)\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{108^k}v_k(4,2)\equiv -2x\pmod{p^2}.$$
If $p=2x^2+3y^2$ with $x\equiv 1\pmod 3$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{108^k}u_k(4,2)\equiv 2x-\tfrac{p}{4x}\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{108^k}k\,u_k(4,2)\equiv \tfrac{x}{3}\pmod{p^2},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{108^k}k\,v_k(4,2)\equiv \tfrac{4}{3x}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(I) Setting $S_1(p)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\dfrac{\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_{2k}(18,1)}{256^k}$, one has
$$S_1(p)\equiv\begin{cases}4x^2-2p\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=1\text{ and }p=x^2+30y^2,\\ 12x^2-2p\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)=1,\ \left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=-1\text{ and }p=3x^2+10y^2,\\ 2p-8x^2\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=1,\ \left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=-1\text{ and }p=2x^2+15y^2,\\ 2p-6x^2\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{p}{5}\right)=1,\ \left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)=-1\text{ and }2p=3x^2+10y^2,\\ 0\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{-30}{p}\right)=-1,\end{cases}$$

paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Complexity of fixed-point and cohomological data for Z_p-actions
original_question: Fix a simply connected 4-manifold X and let a Z_p-action determine associated data Γ = (ρ, X_G, {ρ_x}), where ρ is the induced action on H^2(X) preserving cup product, X_G is the singular set of points with nontrivial isotropy, and ρ_x records the local linear isotropy representation near each singular point x. How complicated can the set of all such associated data Γ become when one ranges over all Z_p-actions on X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a closed, simply connected, oriented topological 4-manifold, and let $p$ be a prime. Consider all locally linear actions of the cyclic group $G=\mathbb{Z}_p$ on $X$ that preserve orientation. To each such action one associates the triple
$$\Gamma=(\rho,\,X_G,\,\{\rho_x\}_{x\in X_G}),$$
where:
- $\rho:G\to\mathrm{Aut}(H^2(X;\mathbb{Z}),\cup)$ is the induced action on second integral cohomology, preserving the cup-product intersection form;
- $X_G=\{x\in X:G_x\neq\{1\}\}$ is the singular set of points with nontrivial isotropy subgroup $G_x\le G$;
- for each $x\in X_G$, $\rho_x:G_x\to GL(4,\mathbb{R})$ is the linear isotropy representation modeling the action on a $G_x$-invariant neighborhood of $x$.

Two such triples are considered equivalent if there is a compatible identification of the cohomology lattices, an equivariant bijection of singular sets, and conjugacy of the corresponding local representations.

Problem: Describe, as $G=\mathbb{Z}_p$ ranges over all such actions on a fixed $X$, the set $\mathcal{D}(X,p)$ of equivalence classes of associated data $\Gamma$. In particular, determine effective bounds or structural constraints on $\mathcal{D}(X,p)$ (e.g., finiteness, parametrization, restrictions among the components $\rho$, $X_G$, and $\{\rho_x\}$ imposed by the topology of $X$), and assess whether $\mathcal{D}(X,p)$ admits a uniform classification valid for all simply connected 4-manifolds $X$.
status_search_result: The question of classifying the full set of associated data (cohomological action, singular set, and local isotropy representations) for all $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions on a general simply connected closed 4-manifold appears to remain open. Partial results exist: the Borel spectral sequence collapses under suitable conditions, p-rank bounds for pseudofree homologically trivial actions are known, and effective compact Lie group actions on simply connected 4-manifolds with $b_2\geq 3$ embed in $S^1\times S^1$. However, no general classification of $\Gamma$ for arbitrary $X$ and $p$ has been established.

original_question: Is every smooth action of a finite group on S^4 that has an isolated fixed point smoothly conjugate to a linear action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting smoothly on the 4-sphere $S^4$, and suppose this action has at least one isolated fixed point (i.e., a point $p\in S^4$ fixed by every element of $G$ such that $\{p\}$ is a connected component of the fixed-point set $(S^4)^G$). A linear action of $G$ on $S^4$ is one obtained from an orthogonal representation $G\to O(5)$ via the standard inclusion $S^4\subset\mathbb{R}^5$. Two smooth $G$-actions on $S^4$ are smoothly conjugate if there exists a $G$-equivariant diffeomorphism between them.

Question: Is every smooth action of a finite group $G$ on $S^4$ that possesses an isolated fixed point smoothly conjugate to a linear action of $G$ on $S^4$?
status_search_result: The conjecture that smooth finite group actions on $S^4$ with an isolated fixed point are smoothly conjugate to linear actions remains open in general. Recent works (e.g., 2025 paper on involutions on $S^4$) treat partial cases such as locally linear involutions with prescribed fixed-set dimensions, and related rank conjectures, but no general resolution is reported.

context_brief: Pseudofree metacyclic symplectic actions on CP^2
original_question: Let Γ_{n,r} be the metacyclic group presented by Γ_{n,r} = {x, u | x^n = u^3 = 1, u^{-1}xu = x^r, r^2 + r + 1 ≡ 0 (mod n)}. Is every pseudofree symplectic action of Γ_{n,r} on CP^2 smoothly conjugate to a linear action?
self_contained_problem:
For integers n ≥ 1 and r with r² + r + 1 ≡ 0 (mod n), let Γ_{n,r} be the metacyclic group of order 3n with presentation
    Γ_{n,r} = ⟨ x, u | x^n = u^3 = 1, u^{-1} x u = x^r ⟩.
Equip CP² with its standard Fubini–Study symplectic form ω_FS. A smooth action of a finite group G on a symplectic 4-manifold (M,ω) is called symplectic if every group element acts by a symplectomorphism, and pseudofree if the action is effective and, for every non-identity g ∈ G, the fixed-point set Fix(g) is a (possibly empty) discrete subset of M. A linear action of Γ_{n,r} on CP² is one induced from a representation Γ_{n,r} → PU(3); it is known that, up to conjugation in PU(3), there is (for each admissible (n,r)) a pseudofree linear action of Γ_{n,r} on CP² without fixed points, and these are the only pseudofree linear actions on CP² without a global fixed point.

Question: Is every pseudofree symplectic action of Γ_{n,r} on (CP², ω_FS) smoothly conjugate to a linear action of Γ_{n,r} on CP²? Equivalently, does there exist a diffeomorphism of CP² conjugating any given pseudofree symplectic Γ_{n,r}-action to a linear one?
status_search_result: Web search did not return clear evidence that the question has been resolved. The problem is attributed to W. Chen and appears in surveys of group actions on 4-manifolds; related work by Chen and Kwasik on symplectic finite group actions on CP² and K3 exists, but no source found explicitly confirms a complete affirmative or negative answer for all admissible (n,r). Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Whether A5 symmetry forces a standard symplectic homotopy K3
original_question: Suppose a symplectic homotopy K3 surface X admits a symplectic action of A5. Must X be standard, meaning that its exoticness invariant satisfies r_X = 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a symplectic homotopy K3 surface, i.e. a closed smooth 4-manifold homeomorphic to a K3 surface and equipped with a symplectic form ω. Define the lattice
  L_X = span_{ℤ}{ β ∈ H_2(X; ℤ) : SW_X(β) ≠ 0 },
where SW_X denotes the Seiberg–Witten invariant, and let r_X be the rank of L_X. Call X "standard" if r_X = 0.

Suppose X admits a symplectic action of the alternating group A_5 (i.e. a faithful action by diffeomorphisms preserving ω). Must X be standard, that is, must r_X = 0?
status_search_result: Related work by Chen and Kwasik establishes that effective symplectic actions by various maximal K3 groups force the homotopy K3 to be minimally exotic, and follow-up papers (e.g. on S_5 actions) extend this. However, no source found explicitly resolves the A_5 case in full. The status of this specific question is not clearly settled in the literature consulted.

paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Non-holomorphic fixed-point structures for K3-group actions
original_question: Are there smooth or symplectic actions of a K3 group on a homotopy K3 surface whose fixed-point set structure (X_G, {ρ_x}) is different from the fixed-point set structure of a holomorphic action?
self_contained_problem:
A homotopy K3 surface is a closed smooth 4-manifold homeomorphic to a K3 surface. A K3 group is a finite group that admits a faithful holomorphic and symplectic action on some K3 surface (equivalently, a finite group that occurs as a group of symplectic automorphisms of some complex K3 surface; by Mukai's theorem these are precisely the subgroups of the Mathieu group M_23 having at least five orbits in their natural action on 24 letters).

Given a smooth (resp. symplectic) action of a finite group G on a homotopy K3 surface X, define its fixed-point set structure to be the pair (X^G, {ρ_x}_{x ∈ X^G}), where X^G is the fixed-point set of G and, for each x ∈ X^G, ρ_x is the isotropy representation of G on the tangent space T_x X (viewed as a real, resp. symplectic, representation up to equivalence).

Question: Does there exist a K3 group G, a homotopy K3 surface X, and a smooth (or symplectic) action of G on X such that the fixed-point set structure (X^G, {ρ_x}) does not coincide with the fixed-point set structure of any holomorphic action of G on any complex K3 surface?
status_search_result: Searches reveal substantial work by Chen–Kwasik and others establishing rigidity theorems showing fixed-point set structures of symplectic K3-group actions often match those of holomorphic actions for prime-order elements and certain groups, but no source confirms a complete resolution of the general question. Status appears unresolved in full generality.
