paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Fiber-preserving Z_p-actions on the standard K3 surface
original_question: Suppose a smooth Z_p-action on the standard K3 surface preserves a C^∞ elliptic fibration. Must that action be smoothly conjugate to a holomorphic action, and what can be said about the induced action on the K3 lattice?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ denote the standard K3 surface, i.e., a closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold diffeomorphic to a smooth quartic hypersurface in $\mathbb{CP}^3$. Recall that $H^2(X;\mathbb{Z})$ equipped with the intersection form is isometric to the K3 lattice $-2E_8 \oplus 3H$, where $H$ is the hyperbolic plane.

By a $C^\infty$ elliptic fibration on $X$ we mean a smooth map $\pi : X \to S^2$ whose generic fiber is a smoothly embedded 2-torus and which has only finitely many singular fibers, each of a type appearing in Kodaira's list (so that $\pi$ is locally modeled on a holomorphic elliptic fibration).

Let $p$ be a prime and suppose $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ acts smoothly and effectively on $X$ in such a way that the action preserves a given $C^\infty$ elliptic fibration $\pi : X \to S^2$ (i.e., there is a smooth $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-action on $S^2$ making $\pi$ equivariant).

(a) Must such an action be smoothly conjugate, by a self-diffeomorphism of $X$, to a holomorphic $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-action on some complex K3 surface structure on $X$?

(b) What constraints, if any, does the hypothesis impose on the induced $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-representation on the K3 lattice $H^2(X;\mathbb{Z})$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. Related work classifies holomorphic and non-symplectic automorphisms of elliptic K3 surfaces and studies smoothability of locally linear $\mathbb{Z}/p$-actions, but no source explicitly establishes (or refutes) smooth conjugacy of fibration-preserving $\mathbb{Z}/p$-actions on the standard K3 to holomorphic actions, nor pins down the induced K3-lattice representation in this generality. Status appears to remain unknown/open based on available evidence.

paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Upper bounds on prime-order smooth actions
original_question: Let X be a smooth 4-manifold that admits no smooth S^1-actions. Does there exist a constant C > 0 such that X admits no nontrivial smooth Z_p-actions for any prime p > C? If such a constant exists, on which structures of X does C depend?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a closed smooth 4-manifold that admits no nontrivial smooth action of the circle group S^1. For a prime number p, denote by Z_p the cyclic group of order p, and consider nontrivial smooth actions of Z_p on X.

(a) Does there exist a constant C > 0, depending on X, such that X admits no nontrivial smooth Z_p-action for any prime p > C?

(b) If such a constant C exists, determine on which invariants or structures of X (for instance, the homeomorphism type, the smooth structure, additional geometric structures such as symplectic or complex structures) the constant C depends.
status_search_result: The general smooth case of the question appears to remain open. Affirmative answers are known under additional structure: W. Chen ("On the orders of periodic diffeomorphisms of 4-manifolds", Duke Math. J. 156 (2011)) established the bound for holomorphic actions (with C of topological nature) and for symplectic actions (with C also depending on the smooth structure). No source found establishes the result for general smooth actions.

paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Describing bounds for smooth Z_p-actions via manifold invariants
original_question: For general smooth Z_p-actions, can the constant C from Question 4.1 be described in terms of invariants of the manifold? In particular, which invariants of the smooth structure, such as Seiberg-Witten basic classes or Seiberg-Witten invariants, enter that bound, and in what way do they enter it?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a closed, smooth, oriented 4-manifold. Consider smooth, effective actions of cyclic groups Z_p of prime order p on X. Suppose that for X (or for a suitable class of such 4-manifolds, for instance those admitting no smooth circle action) there exists a constant C = C(X) > 0 such that X admits no smooth Z_p-action whenever p > C; that is, the orders of prime-order smooth periodic diffeomorphisms of X are bounded by C.

Question: For general smooth Z_p-actions, can such a bound C be described explicitly in terms of invariants of the 4-manifold X? More precisely, identify which invariants of the smooth structure of X — for example the set of Seiberg–Witten basic classes of X, the values of the Seiberg–Witten invariants, or other gauge-theoretic invariants — must enter any such bound, and give an explicit formula or estimate showing how these invariants control the constant C.
status_search_result: The question, attributed to W. Chen, asks how the bound on orders of prime smooth Z_p-actions on a 4-manifold depends on smooth invariants such as Seiberg–Witten basic classes. Chen's Duke 2011 paper established such bounds in the holomorphic (topological) and symplectic (involving smooth structure) cases, but a general description of C in terms of SW invariants for arbitrary smooth Z_p-actions does not appear to have been obtained, and no later resolution was found in available searches. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
context_brief: Homologically trivial prime-order smooth actions on homotopy K3 surfaces
original_question: For any prime number p > 2, are there nontrivial smooth Z_p-actions on a homotopy K3 surface that act trivially on homology?
self_contained_problem:
A homotopy K3 surface is a closed, smooth, simply connected 4-manifold that is homotopy equivalent to a smooth K3 surface (equivalently, a closed simply connected smooth spin 4-manifold with Euler characteristic 24 and signature -16). A smooth action of a finite group G on such a manifold X is said to be homologically trivial if the induced action on H_*(X; Z) is the identity, and nontrivial if the action of G on X is not the identity action.

Question: Does there exist an odd prime p and a homotopy K3 surface X admitting a nontrivial smooth action of the cyclic group Z/pZ that is homologically trivial? Equivalently, for every odd prime p, determine whether some homotopy K3 surface supports a nontrivial smooth Z/pZ-action acting as the identity on integral homology.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that the analogous question for involutions (p=2) has been studied, with results showing strong restrictions, but no published resolution of the odd-prime case for homotopy K3 surfaces was located. The problem appears to remain open, consistent with its formulation as an open question in the surveyed literature on smooth finite group actions on 4-manifolds.

paper_title: Some open questions concerning biological growth
context_brief: Explicit solution and decorrelation threshold for dilution KPZ growth
original_question: For the KPZ equation on a uniformly growing domain with dilution, ∂ₜh = ν(t₀/t)^(2γ)∇²h + (λ/2)(t₀/t)^(2γ)(∇h)² − (dγ/t)h + γF t^(γ−1) + (t₀/t)^(dγ/2)ξ(x,t), the Hopf-Cole transformation leads to a nonlinear equation resembling a time-dependent, spatially distributed Gompertz differential equation. Can one find an explicit deterministic solution for this dilution KPZ dynamics, and what is its decorrelation threshold?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the KPZ equation on a uniformly growing $d$-dimensional domain with dilution, written in comoving coordinates as
$$\partial_t h(x,t) = \nu\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{2\gamma}\nabla^2 h + \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{2\gamma}(\nabla h)^2 - \tfrac{d\gamma}{t}\,h + \gamma F\, t^{\gamma-1} + \left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{d\gamma/2}\xi(x,t),$$
where $h(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}$ is the height field, $\nu>0$ is the surface tension, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ the nonlinear coupling, $\gamma\ge 0$ the domain growth exponent, $t_0>0$ a reference time, $F\in\mathbb{R}$ a constant drive, and $\xi$ a Gaussian space-time white noise with $\langle\xi(x,t)\xi(x',t')\rangle=\delta^d(x-x')\delta(t-t')$.

Apply the Hopf–Cole transformation $u=\exp\!\left(\tfrac{\lambda}{2\nu}h\right)$ to obtain the multiplicative-noise equation
$$\partial_t u = \nu\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{2\gamma}\nabla^2 u - \tfrac{d\gamma}{t}\,u\ln(u) + \tfrac{\gamma F\lambda}{2\nu}\,t^{\gamma-1}\,u + \tfrac{\lambda}{2\nu}\left(\tfrac{t_0}{t}\right)^{d\gamma/2}\xi(x,t)\,u,$$
which is a time-dependent, spatially distributed analogue of the Gompertz ODE.

(a) Find an explicit closed-form solution of the deterministic version of this equation (i.e., with $\xi\equiv 0$), giving $u(x,t)$ and consequently $h(x,t)$ in terms of the initial data and the parameters $(\nu,\lambda,\gamma,F,t_0,d)$.

(b) Determine the decorrelation threshold of this deterministic dilution KPZ dynamics, i.e., the time scale (as a function of the parameters) beyond which spatial correlations of $h(x,t)$ inherited from the initial condition cease to be effectively transmitted by the dynamics.
status_search_result: A targeted web search for explicit solutions and decorrelation thresholds of the dilution KPZ equation on a uniformly growing domain (in its Hopf–Cole/Gompertz form) returned only general references on the standard KPZ equation, Hopf–Cole transform, and spatial decorrelation results — none addressing this specific dilution/growing-domain variant. No published resolution was identified, but absence of search hits is not conclusive evidence of openness.

paper_title: Some open questions concerning biological growth
context_brief: Role of Galilean invariance in KPZ scaling exponents
original_question: If the dilution KPZ equation on a growing domain obeys traditional KPZ scaling in some suitable limit even though Galilean invariance is lost, what does that imply about the role of Galilean invariance in fixing the KPZ critical exponents and the scaling relation α + z = 2?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) equation for an interface height field h(x,t) on a d-dimensional substrate,
  ∂_t h = ν Δh + (λ/2)|∇h|^2 + η(x,t),
where η is Gaussian white noise. Its stationary scaling is characterized by a roughness exponent α and a dynamic exponent z, satisfying h(bx, b^z t) ≃ b^α h(x,t) in distribution. The exact relation
  α + z = 2
is conventionally derived from the invariance of the KPZ equation under the infinitesimal Galilean (tilt) transformation h(x,t) → h(x + λv t, t) + v·x, which forces λ to be unrenormalized.

Now consider a "dilution" variant of the KPZ equation that models a growing domain, in which the nonlinear and noise terms are dressed by a time-dependent dilution factor associated with domain growth. This modification breaks the standard Galilean (tilt) invariance.

Question: Suppose one establishes (in some appropriate scaling limit) that this dilution KPZ equation exhibits the same critical exponents α and z as the standard KPZ universality class, in particular the scaling relation α + z = 2. What does such a result imply about the necessity of Galilean invariance for fixing the KPZ critical exponents and for the scaling relation α + z = 2? Specifically, can α + z = 2 be derived from a principle independent of Galilean invariance, and if so, identify the symmetry, Ward identity, or non-perturbative mechanism that enforces it.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has argued, via dynamic renormalization-group analyses of non-Galilean-invariant KPZ-like models (including discretized and dilution-type variants), that the relation α+z=2 can emerge from exact cancellations in vertex renormalization without requiring Galilean invariance. This supports the interpretation that Galilean invariance is sufficient but not necessary for the KPZ scaling relation. A complete, rigorous identification of the underlying mechanism in all dimensions remains incomplete, so the broader question is best regarded as partially resolved.

paper_title: Some open questions concerning biological growth
context_brief: Critical growth index for pinning and unpinning
original_question: For quenched-disorder KPZ equations on uniformly growing domains whose propagation velocity scales like t^γ, does γ = 1 play a critical role in the dynamics by separating interfaces that are always pinned for γ < 1 from interfaces that are always moving for γ > 1, or does pinning/unpinning still depend on model parameter values? If parameter dependence remains, are there other critical values of the growth index γ?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) equation with quenched disorder posed on a uniformly growing spatial domain. Concretely, let h(x,t) denote the height of an interface satisfying

  ∂_t h(x,t) = ν Δh(x,t) + (λ/2) |∇h(x,t)|^2 + F + η(x,h),

where ν,λ>0, F is a constant driving force, and η(x,h) is a quenched random field (time-independent, depending on the spatial position x and on the local height h). The spatial domain on which the equation is posed grows uniformly in time so that its linear size L(t) ~ t^γ for some growth exponent γ>0; equivalently, in comoving coordinates the propagation velocity scales like t^γ rather than being constant.

For the classical case of a static domain, it is known that there is a critical driving force F_c such that for F<F_c the interface is pinned (asymptotically immobile) and for F>F_c the interface propagates. On a uniformly growing domain, address the following:

(a) Does the value γ = 1 play a critical role in the depinning dynamics, in the sense that for every choice of model parameters (ν, λ, F, and disorder distribution) the interface is always pinned whenever γ < 1 and always moving whenever γ > 1?

(b) If, instead, the pinned/moving outcome continues to depend on the parameters (in particular on F relative to F_c) for γ in some range, determine whether there exist other critical values of the growth exponent γ at which a transition between always-pinned, parameter-dependent, and always-moving regimes occurs, and identify such values.
status_search_result: A web search returned recent work on quenched KPZ depinning (e.g., 2022 and 2025 arXiv preprints on QKPZ universality and depinning in fractional Brownian landscapes), but none directly addresses the role of a uniform domain-growth exponent γ in separating always-pinned from always-moving regimes for the quenched KPZ equation. No source could be located that resolves whether γ=1 is critical or identifies other critical values of γ, so the status remains unverified.

paper_title: Some open questions concerning biological growth
original_question: How can the theoretical predictions for growing-interface dynamics be experimentally verified in biological growth systems by measuring the roughness exponent α, the growth exponent β, the dynamic exponent z = α/β, and the growth index γ? Can the long-time dependence of interface variance on initial system size and time be used to estimate the distance from correlation and the necessary strength of a control protocol?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional stochastic interface $h(x,t)$ representing a growing biological front (for example, the edge of a colony, tissue, or tumor) on a substrate of linear size $L(t)$, where $L(t)$ may itself grow in time as $L(t)\sim t^{\gamma}$ for some growth index $\gamma>0$. Assume the interface fluctuations obey Family–Vicsek-type scaling characterized by a roughness exponent $\alpha$, a growth exponent $\beta$, and a dynamic exponent $z=\alpha/\beta$, with initial system size $L_0$. Suppose the long-time behavior of the interface variance is given by
$$\langle h(x,t)^2\rangle-\langle h(x,t)\rangle^2 \sim \begin{cases} L_0^{2\alpha}\, t^{2\beta}\sim L(t)^{2\alpha}\, t^{2\beta-2\gamma\alpha}, & \gamma>1/z,\\[4pt] L_0^{2\alpha}\, t^{2\gamma\alpha}\sim L(t)^{2\alpha}, & \gamma<1/z. \end{cases}$$

Design and analyze an experimental protocol that, by measuring the time and initial-size dependence of the interface variance in such a biological growth system, allows one to:

(a) extract the exponents $\alpha$ and $\beta$ (and hence $z=\alpha/\beta$) in the fast-growth regime;
(b) independently measure the growth index $\gamma$ from the temporal scaling of $L(t)$;
(c) use the difference $\gamma-1/z$ as a quantitative measure of the "distance from correlation," i.e., how far the system is from the regime in which the substrate growth keeps pace with lateral correlations along the interface; and
(d) translate this distance into a lower bound on the strength of an external control protocol required to drive the system into (or out of) the correlated regime.

Specifically: Can biological growth experiments be performed in which all four quantities $\alpha,\beta,z,\gamma$ are simultaneously and reliably measured from variance scaling, validating the predicted crossover at $\gamma=1/z$, and can the quantity $\gamma-1/z$ be operationally converted into a quantitative requirement on a control protocol's strength?

original_question: Does every complex cubic polynomial admit a square iterative root? Equivalently, if f is a complex polynomial of degree 3, must there exist a function φ such that φ(φ(z)) = f(z) for all complex z? The survey states that this basic existence question is still open even though quadratic polynomials are known not to have square roots.
self_contained_problem:
An iterative square root of a function $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ is a function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $\varphi(\varphi(z)) = f(z)$ for every $z\in\mathbb{C}$. (No regularity such as continuity, holomorphy, or polynomiality is imposed on $\varphi$ a priori.) It is known that there exist complex polynomials of degree 2 (for example, suitable quadratic polynomials) that admit no iterative square root in this sense.

Question: Does every complex polynomial $f$ of degree exactly $3$ admit an iterative square root? That is, given any $f(z) = a_3 z^3 + a_2 z^2 + a_1 z + a_0$ with $a_3 \neq 0$ and $a_i \in \mathbb{C}$, does there always exist a function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\varphi\circ\varphi = f$?
status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a definitive resolution of whether every complex cubic polynomial admits an iterative square root. Existing literature on iterative square roots (e.g., density results for continuous self-maps lacking square roots, and general results on iterative roots) does not appear to settle the cubic-polynomial case, and the question is described as open in surveys on functional equations in a single variable. No paper claiming a complete proof or counterexample for the cubic case was located.

paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
context_brief: Dimension of extended replicativity solution space
original_question: Suppose λ assigns to each positive integer n a complex-valued arithmetic sequence λn(j), and consider the extended replicativity system (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} φ((x+k)/n) = Σ_{j=1}^∞ λn(j) φ(jx). Is it true that the complex vector space of all solutions φ in L1(R/Z) is at most two-dimensional?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ and let $L^1(\mathbb{T})$ denote the complex Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable, $1$-periodic functions $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$. For each positive integer $n$, let $\lambda_n:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$, $j\mapsto \lambda_n(j)$, be a fixed complex-valued arithmetic sequence such that, for every $\varphi\in L^1(\mathbb{T})$, the series $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n(j)\,\varphi(jx)$ converges (in the $L^1$ sense, say) and defines an element of $L^1(\mathbb{T})$.

Consider the "extended replicativity" system of functional equations
$$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\varphi\!\left(\frac{x+k}{n}\right) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n(j)\,\varphi(jx),\qquad n=1,2,3,\dots,$$
to be satisfied for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, simultaneously for all $n\geq 1$.

Let $V(\{\lambda_n\}) \subset L^1(\mathbb{T})$ denote the $\mathbb{C}$-vector space of all $\varphi\in L^1(\mathbb{T})$ which solve this system.

Question: Is it true that, for every choice of the family $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ for which the above system is well-posed, one has
$$\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V(\{\lambda_n\}) \;\leq\; 2\,?$$

paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
context_brief: Embedding linear functional equations into flows
original_question: Given functions f, g, and h in the linear functional equation φ(f(x)) = g(x)φ(x) + h(x), under what weak assumptions on f, g, and h can this discrete-time equation be embedded into a continuous-time family φ(F(t,x)) = G(t,x)φ(x) + H(t,x), where F, G, and H satisfy the natural flow and cocycle identities and interpolate the original data at t = 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a nonempty set (e.g. an interval of the real line or an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$) and consider the linear functional equation in a single unknown function $\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$:
$$\varphi(f(x)) = g(x)\,\varphi(x) + h(x), \qquad x \in X, \tag{1}$$
where $f : X \to X$, $g : X \to \mathbb{R}$ and $h : X \to \mathbb{R}$ are given.

Say that equation (1) can be embedded in a continuous-time family if there exist functions
$$F : T \times X \to X, \quad G : T \times X \to \mathbb{R}, \quad H : T \times X \to \mathbb{R},$$
defined on $T \times X$ where $T$ is an interval containing $\{0,1\}$ (e.g. $T=[0,\infty)$ or $T=\mathbb{R}$), satisfying the cocycle/flow identities
$$F(t+s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)),$$
$$G(t+s, x) = G(s, x)\,G(t, F(s, x)),$$
$$H(t+s, x) = G(t, F(s, x))\,H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x)),$$
together with the interpolation conditions
$$F(1, \cdot) = f, \quad G(0, \cdot) = 1, \quad G(1, \cdot) = g, \quad H(0, \cdot) = 0, \quad H(1, \cdot) = h,$$
such that every solution $\varphi$ of (1), within a prescribed regularity class, also satisfies the continuous-time equation
$$\varphi(F(t, x)) = G(t, x)\,\varphi(x) + H(t, x), \qquad (t,x) \in T \times X. \tag{2}$$

Problem. Determine the weakest possible regularity/structural assumptions on $f$, $g$, $h$ (and on the considered class of solutions $\varphi$) under which such an embedding into a continuous-time family $(F, G, H)$ exists; equivalently, characterize those triples $(f, g, h)$ for which (1) embeds into (2) in the above sense.

original_question: Fix r ∈ N ∪ {∞} and k > 1, and let D^r_k be the class of C^r maps f:R^k→R^k with positive Jacobian determinant everywhere. Must every f in D^r_k admit a factorization f = φ_1^2 ◦ ··· ◦ φ_n^2 for some n and some maps φ_1, ..., φ_n also belonging to D^r_k? paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let S− be the backward shift on z(N0). Determine whether case 4 from Section 2.1 can occur; that is, determine whether the range M(I − 2S−|z) can be closed and have infinite codimension.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the linear space of all scalar sequences $x=(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)$. A linear subspace $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\mid\mathfrak{z}\|$ is called a quasi-Banach sequence ideal if it is complete and if, whenever $x\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $y\in\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ satisfy $|\eta_k|\le|\xi_k|$ for all $k$, one has $y\in\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|y\mid\mathfrak{z}\|\le\|x\mid\mathfrak{z}\|$.

The forward shift $S_+$ and backward shift $S_-$ act on $\omega(\mathbb{N}_0)$ by
$$S_+(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)=(0,\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots),\qquad S_-(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)=(\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3,\dots).$$
The quasi-Banach sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if both $S_+$ and $S_-$ map $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ continuously into itself.

For a continuous linear operator $T:\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)\to\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, denote by $M(T)$ its range. Consider the operator $I-2S_-$ acting on $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and its range $M(I-2S_-\mid\mathfrak{z})$.

Question. Does there exist a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the range $M(I-2S_-\mid\mathfrak{z})$ is closed in $\mathfrak{z}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and has infinite codimension? Equivalently, can this case occur, or is it impossible?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem (Problem 2) in a 2023 work on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces. A web search did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving whether the range of $I-2S_-$ on a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal can be closed and of infinite codimension. No solution appears to be available as of the search date.

original_question: For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S+ and S− be the forward and backward shifts on z(N0). If σΦ denotes the Φ-spectrum, determine whether the Φ-spectrum of each shift is exactly the annulus σΦ(S±|z) = { λ ∈ C : r(S∓|z)^−1 ≤ |λ| ≤ r(S±|z) }.
self_contained_problem:
Let $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be a quasi-Banach sequence ideal on $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$; that is, $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of $\mathbb{C}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ equipped with a complete quasi-norm such that $\ell_1 \subseteq z(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq \ell_\infty$ continuously, and $|x_n| \le |y_n|$ for all $n$ with $y \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ implies $x \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|x\| \le \|y\|$. Assume further that $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is shift-monotone, i.e. both the forward shift
\[ S_+(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots) := (0,\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots) \]
and the backward shift
\[ S_-(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots) := (\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3,\dots) \]
act as bounded linear operators on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a quasi-Banach space $X$, denote by $\Phi(X)$ the class of Fredholm operators on $X$ (those with closed range and finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel), and define the $\Phi$-spectrum
\[ \sigma_\Phi(T\,|\,X) := \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda I - T \notin \Phi(X)\}. \]
Let $r(T\,|\,X)$ denote the spectral radius of $T$ on $X$.

Determine whether
\[ \sigma_\Phi(S_\pm\,|\,z(\mathbb{N}_0)) = \bigl\{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : r(S_\mp\,|\,z(\mathbb{N}_0))^{-1} \le |\lambda| \le r(S_\pm\,|\,z(\mathbb{N}_0))\bigr\}. \]

original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Determine whether every trace on LAPP_z is spectral, in the sense that for each operator S the trace is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of S through the dyadic block sums described in Section 2.4.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ making it complete is called a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal if:
(i) it contains the canonical unit vectors;
(ii) it is solid: $|a_n|\le|b_n|$ for all $n$ with $b\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ implies $a\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $\|a\|_z\le c\|b\|_z$;
(iii) it is invariant under the dyadic averaging shift: writing $D_k=\{2^k,2^k+1,\dots,2^{k+1}-1\}$ and $T:(a_n)\mapsto\bigl(2^{-k}\sum_{n\in D_k}a_n\bigr)_{k\ge 0}$ (or its adjoint expansion), both $T$ and its right-inverse act boundedly on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

For a Banach space $X$, let $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}(X)$ consist of operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(X)$ whose approximation-number sequence $(a_n(S))_{n\ge 0}$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, with $\|S\|_{L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}}:=\|(a_n(S))\|_z$. Letting $X$ vary, $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ is a quasi-Banach operator ideal. A trace on $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ on the component $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}(\ell_2)$ (extended in the standard way to all components) which vanishes on commutators $[A,B]$ whenever the trace is defined.

For a diagonal operator $D_a$ on $\ell_2$ with diagonal $a\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, set $\varphi(a):=\tau(D_a)$. The trace $\tau$ is called spectral if for every $S\in L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}(X)$ with eigenvalue sequence $(\lambda_n(S))_{n\ge 0}$ (counted with algebraic multiplicity and ordered by decreasing modulus),
$$\tau(S)\;=\;\varphi\!\left(\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{2^k}\sum_{n\in D_k}\lambda_n(S)\Bigr)_{k\ge 0}\right).$$

Problem. Prove that whenever $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, every trace on $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ is spectral in the above sense.

A web search reveals related work on shift-invariant functionals on Banach sequence spaces and on traces of Marcinkiewicz-type ideals, but no source establishing spectrality of all traces on $L_z^{\mathrm{APP}}$ for general quasi-Banach shift-monotone $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ was found. It thus appears to remain open.

original_question: For 1 ≤ r ≤ 2, let P_{r,2} be the ideal of (r,2)-summing operators, and let (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal from Theorem 2.4. Determine whether every trace on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces constructed in Theorem 2.4, so that no additional traces exist on this ideal.
self_contained_problem:
Let $1 \le r \le 2$. Recall that a (bounded linear) operator $T : X \to Y$ between Banach spaces is called $(r,2)$-summing if there is a constant $c \ge 0$ such that for every finite family $x_1,\dots,x_n \in X$ one has
$$\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n \|Tx_k\|^r\Bigr)^{1/r} \le c \sup_{\|x^*\|\le 1}\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n |\langle x_k, x^*\rangle|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The class of all such operators forms a Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}$.

For an operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ with approximation numbers $a_n(T) := \inf\{\|T-A\| : A \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\}$, define the ideal $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}^{\mathrm{APP}}{}_{r,\infty}$ to consist of those operators $T$ which factor as $T = AB$ with $B \in \mathfrak{P}_{r,2}$ and $A$ in the approximation ideal $\mathcal{L}^{(\mathrm{app})}_{r,\infty}$, i.e. $\sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} a_n(A) < \infty$ (equivalently the natural composition of the Banach ideals $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}$ and $\mathcal{L}^{(\mathrm{app})}_{r,\infty}$).

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ defined on the class of all Banach spaces is a linear functional $\tau$ on the components $\mathfrak{A}(X,X)$ ($X$ Banach) such that:
(i) $\tau(x^* \otimes x) = \langle x, x^*\rangle$ for every rank-one operator,
(ii) $\tau(BA) = \tau(AB)$ whenever $A \in \mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$, $B \in \mathcal{L}(Y,X)$.

For each $1 \le r \le 2$ there is a canonical construction producing a trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\,|\mathfrak{P}_{r,2})$ on $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}^{\mathrm{APP}}{}_{r,\infty}$ obtained from a dilation/averaging procedure applied to the ideal $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}$ (one such trace for each suitable Banach limit / dilation-invariant mean).

Problem. Prove that every trace on the operator ideal $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}^{\mathrm{APP}}{}_{r,\infty}$ is of the form $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\,|\mathfrak{P}_{r,2})$ produced by this construction; equivalently, show that no other traces exist on this ideal.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving the uniqueness/classification of traces on the ideal $\mathfrak{P}_{r,2}^{\mathrm{APP}}{}_{r,\infty}$; related work by Pietsch and others addresses traces on Hilbert-space ideals and general frameworks but does not establish that the constructed traces exhaust all traces on this specific Banach-space ideal.

original_question: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let LWEYL_{r,∞} be the quasi-Banach operator ideal defined by the dyadic Weyl-number condition x_{2^k}(S) = O(2^{-k/r}). Determine whether the interpolated ideals (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} strictly increase as r varies over [2,∞), or whether they become constant on that range; in particular, decide whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞} might already equal LWEYL_{1,∞}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. For an operator $S \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, the $n$-th Weyl number $x_n(S)$ is defined by
$$x_n(S) = \sup\{a_n(S A) : A \in \mathcal{L}(\ell_2, X),\ \|A\| \le 1\},$$
where $a_n(\cdot)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number, i.e. $a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - R\| : R \text{ has rank} < n\}$.

For $1 \le r < \infty$, define the quasi-Banach operator ideal
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty} := \{S \in \mathcal{L} : x_{2^k}(S) = O(2^{-k/r}) \text{ as } k \to \infty\}.$$

For an operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$, let $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ denote the ideal obtained from $\mathcal{A}$ by the $(r,\infty)$-approximation-number interpolation procedure: $S \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ if and only if there exists a factorization-type representation such that the approximation numbers $a_{2^k}(S)$ decay like $2^{-k/r}$ relative to operators in $\mathcal{A}$ (equivalently, $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is the Lorentz-type ideal of order $(r,\infty)$ generated from $\mathcal{A}$ via approximation numbers).

Question: Does the family of ideals
$$\bigl(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty},\qquad r \in [2,\infty),$$
strictly increase with $r$, or is it constant on the interval $[2,\infty)$? In particular, decide whether the equality
$$\bigl(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{2,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{2,\infty} = \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$$
holds.
status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific question about the monotonicity (or constancy) of the interpolated Weyl-generated ideals $(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ for $r \in [2,\infty)$ was found. It is listed as one of the open problems in the recent survey on traces of operator ideals on Banach spaces and no follow-up work resolving it appears in standard searches.

original_question: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal carrying the traces from Theorem 2.8. Determine whether every trace on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces given by Theorem 2.8.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X$ range over all (complex) Banach spaces. For a bounded linear operator $T: X \to X$, recall the approximation numbers
$$a_n(T) := \inf\{\|T-A\| : A \in \mathcal{L}(X,X),\ \mathrm{rank}(A) < n\}, \qquad n=1,2,\dots,$$
and the Weyl numbers
$$x_n(T) := \sup\{ a_n(T B) : B \in \mathcal{L}(\ell_2, X),\ \|B\| \le 1 \}.$$

Fix $1 \le r < \infty$. The Lorentz–Weyl operator ideal $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}$ consists of all operators $T \in \mathcal{L}(X,X)$ (over all Banach spaces $X$) such that
$$\sup_{n \ge 1} n^{1/r}\, x_n(T) < \infty.$$

For an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$, let $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ denote the component obtained by intersecting with the Lorentz–approximation ideal
$$\{T : \sup_n n^{1/r} a_n(T) < \infty\},$$
i.e. operators in $\mathfrak{A}$ whose approximation numbers also satisfy $a_n(T) = O(n^{-1/r})$.

It is known that on the ideal $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ there exists a family of (continuous, unitarily/ideal) traces obtained as follows: for each generalized limit $\mathrm{Lim}$ on $\ell_\infty$, the rule
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(T) := \mathrm{Lim}_{N\to\infty}\, \frac{1}{\log N} \sum_{n=1}^{N} \lambda_n(T)$$
(where $\lambda_n(T)$ are the eigenvalues of $T$ arranged in non-increasing order of modulus, with multiplicities) defines a trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Prove that every trace on the operator ideal $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is of the above form; equivalently, show that there are no traces on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ other than those induced by generalized limits via the eigenvalue Cesàro–logarithmic averaging rule.

original_question: Determine whether the Weyl-number ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing traces; the author explicitly conjectures that it should even support non-vanishing singular spectral traces.
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space and, more generally, let X, Y be Banach spaces. For a bounded linear operator T : X → Y and an integer n ≥ 1, the n-th Weyl number is defined by
  x_n(T) = sup { a_n(T A) : A : ℓ_2 → X, ‖A‖ ≤ 1 },
where a_n(S) denotes the n-th approximation number of S, i.e. a_n(S) = inf{ ‖S − R‖ : rank R < n }. The Lorentz–Weyl operator ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} is the class of operators T (between arbitrary Banach spaces) for which
  ‖T‖_{LWEYL_{1,∞}} := sup_{n ≥ 1} n · x_n(T) < ∞.

A trace on an operator ideal I (defined on the class of all Banach spaces) is a linear functional τ : I(X,X) → ℂ for every Banach space X, satisfying the trace property τ(AB) = τ(BA) whenever the composition makes sense, and which is consistent under restriction to subspaces. The trace τ is called non-vanishing if there exists some Banach space X and some T ∈ I(X,X) with τ(T) ≠ 0. A trace is called a spectral trace if τ(T) depends only on the eigenvalue sequence of T, and singular if it vanishes on all finite-rank operators.

Problem. Decide whether the operator ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} admits a non-vanishing trace. More strongly, decide whether LWEYL_{1,∞} admits a non-vanishing singular spectral trace.

original_question: Find shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0) for which the entropy-number ideal LENT_z carries non-vanishing singular traces.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ denote the space of real sequences $a=(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$. A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ is called a shift-monotone sequence ideal if it contains all eventually zero sequences, is complete, and is invariant under the forward and backward shifts $S_+(a_0,a_1,\dots)=(0,a_0,a_1,\dots)$ and $S_-(a_0,a_1,\dots)=(a_1,a_2,\dots)$ with $\|S_\pm a\|_z\le\|a\|_z$ for all $a\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and moreover satisfies the monotonicity condition $|b_n|\le|a_n|$ for all $n$ and $a\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ implies $b\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|b\|_z\le\|a\|_z$.

For Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bounded linear operator $T:X\to Y$, let $e_n(T)$ denote the $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number of $T$, defined by
$$e_n(T)=\inf\{\varepsilon>0:\ T(B_X)\text{ is covered by }2^{n-1}\text{ closed balls of radius }\varepsilon\text{ in }Y\},\qquad n\ge 1,$$
with $e_0(T)=\|T\|$. Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, the associated entropy-number operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ is the class of operators $T$ between arbitrary Banach spaces such that the sequence $(e_n(T))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with the quasi-norm $\|T\|_{\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z}=\|(e_n(T))_n\|_z$.

A trace on a two-sided operator ideal $\mathcal{I}$ (defined on the components $\mathcal{I}(X)$ for each Banach space $X$) is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X:\mathcal{I}(X)\to\mathbb{C}$ that vanishes on commutators, i.e. $\tau_Y(AB)=\tau_X(BA)$ whenever $A:X\to Y$ and $B:Y\to X$ with $AB\in\mathcal{I}(Y)$ (equivalently $BA\in\mathcal{I}(X)$). A trace is called singular if it vanishes on every finite-rank operator.

Problem. Determine all shift-monotone sequence ideals $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ for which the entropy-number ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ admits a non-zero singular trace.

original_question: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large families Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that (i) Z contains every Lorentz-type ideal d_{r,w}(N0), and (ii) the map z(N0) ↦ LAPP_z(X,Y) is injective on Z.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of real (or complex) sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ tending to zero. A quasi-Banach sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of $c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ under which it is complete, such that whenever $a \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $b \in c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ satisfies $|b_n| \le |a_n|$ for all $n$, then $b \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|b\|_z \le \|a\|_z$. The ideal is called shift-monotone if, in addition, for every $a = (a_n)_{n\ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ the shifted sequence $Sa := (0, a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots)$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|Sa\|_z \le \|a\|_z$.

For parameters $0 < r < \infty$ and a non-increasing weight $w = (w_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of positive reals with $w_0 = 1$, $\sum_{n} w_n = \infty$, the Lorentz-type sequence ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ consists of all $a \in c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ whose decreasing rearrangement $(a_n^*)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{d_{r,w}} := \Big(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (a_n^*)^r w_n\Big)^{1/r} < \infty.$$
Each $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal.

For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X, Y$, let $\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$ denote the operator ideal component consisting of all bounded linear operators $T: X \to Y$ for which there exists a sequence of finite-rank operators $(T_n)$ with $\|T - T_n\| \to 0$ such that the sequence $(\|T - T_n\|)_{n \ge 0}$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, normed in the natural way associated with $z$.

Problem. Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$. Identify large families $\mathcal{Z}$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that:
(i) every Lorentz-type ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ belongs to $\mathcal{Z}$; and
(ii) the assignment $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \mapsto \mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$ is injective on $\mathcal{Z}$ (i.e., distinct ideals in $\mathcal{Z}$ yield distinct operator ideal components).

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence and nevertheless have few approximable operators in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than c0*(N).
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Denote by $\mathfrak{L}(X)$ the Banach algebra of all bounded linear operators on $X$, and by $\mathfrak{App}(X)$ the closed two-sided ideal of approximable operators, i.e. the closure (in the operator norm) of the ideal of finite-rank operators on $X$. 

Let $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denote the operator ideal consisting of all bounded linear operators $T \in \mathfrak{L}(X)$ such that for every bounded sequence $(x_n)$ in $X$ and every bounded sequence $(x_n^*)$ in $X^*$, the sequence $(\langle Tx_n, x_n^*\rangle)$ tends to $0$; equivalently, the component on $X$ of the operator ideal of all operators which factor through (or are uniformly approximable by) $c_0$-type evaluations.

Say that $X$ has "few approximable operators" if 
$$\mathfrak{App}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X),$$
i.e. the inclusion is strict.

Problem. Construct (or prove the existence of) an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ such that:
(i) $X$ contains an unconditional basic sequence, and
(ii) $X$ has few approximable operators in the above sense.
status_search_result: Existing constructions of Banach spaces with "few operators" (e.g. Gowers–Maurey-type spaces and Argyros's sequentially unconditional space) are designed precisely to avoid unconditional basic sequences, or have unconditionality only sequentially. No construction was found combining the presence of an unconditional basic sequence with the strict inclusion App(X) ⊊ c_0^*(N). The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let LLEX_z = H ◦ LWEYL_z be the old-fashioned left-hand extension ideal built from operators factoring through Hilbert spaces. Determine whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞}, or even the smaller ideal LAPP_{1,∞}, fails to be contained in LLEX_{1,∞}.
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. Work in the category of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. For an operator ideal $\mathcal A$, denote by $\mathcal A(X,Y)$ its component on a pair $(X,Y)$. Write $\mathrm H$ for the operator ideal of operators that factor through a Hilbert space. For $0 < p < \infty$ and $0 < q \le \infty$, the Lorentz scale of approximation numbers gives the (quasi-Banach) ideal $\mathrm{APP}_{p,q}$ of operators $T$ whose approximation numbers $(a_n(T))$ lie in the Lorentz sequence space $\ell_{p,q}$. The Weyl-number ideal $\mathrm{WEYL}_{p,q}$ is defined analogously via Weyl numbers, and the "left-Weyl" ideal $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{p,q}$ is defined by requiring that for every operator $S$ from a Banach space into a Hilbert space, the composition with $T$ lies in $\mathrm{WEYL}_{p,q}$ (equivalently, $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{p,q} = \mathrm{WEYL}_{p,q} \circ \mathrm H^{-1}$ in the appropriate sense). Likewise define $\mathrm{LAPP}_{p,q}$ from $\mathrm{APP}_{p,q}$. For an index $z = (p,q)$, set
$$\mathrm{LLEX}_z := \mathrm H \circ \mathrm{LWEYL}_z,$$
the left-hand extension ideal.

Problem. Show that the product ideal $(\mathrm{LWEYL}_{2,\infty}) \circ \mathrm{APP}_{2,\infty}$, and even the smaller ideal $\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}$, fails to be contained in $\mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}$. That is, exhibit operators in these ideals that do not admit factorizations of the form required by $\mathrm H \circ \mathrm{LWEYL}_{1,\infty}$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. No subsequent work was found resolving the non-inclusion of $\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}$ (or the larger product ideal) in $\mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}$, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: For every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), determine whether there always exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that the reiteration identity (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z holds.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{A}=(\mathcal{A},\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{A}})$ is, in the sense of Pietsch, a subclass of $\mathcal{L}$ equipped with a complete quasi-norm satisfying the usual ideal axioms (containment of finite-rank operators with $\|x\otimes y\|_{\mathcal{A}}=\|x\|\,\|y\|$, the two-sided ideal property $\|BTC\|_{\mathcal{A}}\le\|B\|\,\|T\|_{\mathcal{A}}\,\|C\|$, additivity up to a quasi-norm constant, and completeness of each component).

Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace, equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{x}$, that is solid (if $|s_n|\le|t_n|$ for all $n$ and $(t_n)\in x$ then $(s_n)\in x$ with $\|s\|_x\le\|t\|_x$). It is called shift-monotone if for the right-shift $S(s_0,s_1,s_2,\dots)=(0,s_0,s_1,\dots)$ one has $\|S s\|_x\le\|s\|_x$ for every $s\in x$.

For a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$, let $a_n(T;\mathcal{A})$ denote the $n$-th approximation number of $T$ relative to $\mathcal{A}$, defined by
$$a_n(T;\mathcal{A}):=\inf\{\|T-L\|_{\mathcal{A}} : L\in\mathcal{A},\ \mathrm{rank}(L)<n\},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$
Given a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the approximation procedure
$$\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x}:=\{T\in\mathcal{L} : (a_n(T;\mathcal{A}))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in x(\mathbb{N}_0)\},\qquad \|T\|_{\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x}}:= igl\|(a_n(T;\mathcal{A}))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0} igr\|_x.$$
This $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x}$ is again a quasi-Banach operator ideal.

Problem. Decide whether the following statement is true: for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ and every pair $x(\mathbb{N}_0),\, y(\mathbb{N}_0)$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the reiteration identity
$$ igl(\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x} igr)^{\mathrm{APP}_y}\;=\;\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_z}$$
holds as quasi-Banach operator ideals (with equivalent quasi-norms). If true, exhibit such a $z$ in terms of $x$ and $y$; if false, provide a counterexample.
status_search_result: The question is posed as one of a list of open problems on traces and operator ideals; no resolution appears in the literature, and it remains open as far as can be verified.

paper_title: The combinatorics of discrete time-trees: theory and open problems
context_brief: Distance complexity in discrete time-tree graphs
original_question: A discrete time-tree is a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on a fixed labeled leaf set in which every node is assigned a distinct non-negative integer time and each child has smaller time than its parent. The paper studies graph families on such trees, including DtTm, DtTum, RNNI, and RNNIu, where two trees are adjacent when one can be obtained from the other by one allowed local move such as changing the length of one event interval by 1, swapping the ranks of two nodes that bound a unit-length interval, or performing a nearest-neighbor interchange move on a unit-length interval, with graph-specific restrictions. Given two discrete time-trees in one of these graph families, what is the computational complexity of computing their graph distance, meaning the minimum number of allowed moves needed to transform one tree into the other?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a fixed finite set of leaf labels with |X| ≥ 2. A discrete time-tree on X is a rooted binary tree whose leaves are bijectively labeled by X and in which every node (internal node or leaf) is assigned a distinct non-negative integer time, such that every non-root node has a strictly smaller time than its parent and the times of the leaves are prescribed (e.g., all equal to 0, or given as part of the input). For a discrete time-tree T with internal-node times t_1 < t_2 < … < t_k, the i-th event interval is the set of edges of T that are crossed by a horizontal line at any time strictly between t_i and t_{i+1} (with the 0-th interval lying below t_1 and the k-th interval lying above t_k); call an event interval a unit interval if t_{i+1} − t_i = 1.

Define four graphs whose vertices are discrete time-trees on X:

(1) DtTm: T and T' are adjacent iff T' is obtained from T by exactly one of the following local moves:
   (a) length move: increase or decrease the length of one event interval by 1 (subject to the times remaining a valid strictly increasing sequence of distinct non-negative integers);
   (b) rank move: choose a unit-length event interval that is bounded above and below by two internal nodes x and y, and swap the times (ranks) of x and y;
   (c) NNI move: perform a nearest-neighbor interchange across an edge belonging to a unit-length event interval.

(2) DtTum: the subgraph of DtTm induced on discrete time-trees in which all event intervals have unit length (only rank and NNI moves apply).

(3) RNNI: same as DtTm but with length moves disallowed (only rank and NNI moves are permitted).

(4) RNNIu: the analogue of RNNI restricted to ultrametric/unit-interval discrete time-trees.

For each of these four graph families G ∈ {DtTm, DtTum, RNNI, RNNIu}, determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given two vertices T, T' of G as input, compute the graph distance d_G(T, T'), i.e., the minimum number of allowed moves needed to transform T into T'.
status_search_result: For the RNNI graph (rank and NNI moves on ranked phylogenetic trees), Collienne and Gavryushkin (J. Math. Biol., 2021) showed that the FINDPATH algorithm computes shortest paths/distances in O(n^2) time, giving a polynomial-time algorithm and resolving the RNNI case. Subsequent work on a weighted variant RNNI(ρ) shows the shortest-path problem is NP-hard at one extreme (RNNI(0), where it reduces to NNI) and quadratic at the other (RNNI(1)). Complexity for the discrete time-tree variants DtTm and DtTum (which also include length moves on event intervals) does not appear to be settled in the literature found. Hence the problem is partially solved: settled for RNNI (polynomial), open in general.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
context_brief: BRAVO for critically loaded finite-buffer GI/G/1/K queues
original_question: Consider a finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queue with one server, renewal arrivals, independent and identically distributed service times, K-1 waiting places, and loss of customers who arrive when the system is full. In the critically loaded case λ = μ, where c_a^2 and c_s^2 denote the squared coefficients of variation of the inter-arrival and service times, does the queue exhibit the BRAVO effect (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs), and in particular, for light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, is the long-run departure-process variability parameter γ* equal to (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (one server in service plus K−1 waiting positions). Customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2. Service times are i.i.d., independent of the arrival process, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. A customer who arrives to find the system full (K customers present) is lost. Let D(t) denote the number of customers that depart (i.e., complete service) by time t, and define the asymptotic variability parameter of the departure process by

  γ* := lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / (λ_eff · t),

where λ_eff is the effective throughput (departure rate) in steady state.

Assume the queue is critically loaded, i.e. λ = μ, and assume the interarrival and service time distributions are light-tailed (e.g. have finite moment generating functions in a neighborhood of 0).

(a) Does this system exhibit the BRAVO effect: namely, is γ* strictly smaller than the variability parameter that would arise in the corresponding stable or unstable (non-critical) regimes, due to the balancing of arrival and service rates?

(b) More precisely, prove or disprove the conjecture that, as K → ∞,

  γ* = (1/3) (c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).
status_search_result: The conjecture for the general GI/G/1/K critically loaded queue appears to remain open. While BRAVO has been established with the factor 1/3 for M/M/1/K (Markovian case) and with a factor (1−2/π) for the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical queue, recent work (e.g. on busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and on phase transitions in critically loaded queues) does not establish the 1/3 (c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) asymptotics for the general finite-buffer GI/G/1/K case. No located source claims a proof of the full conjecture.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
context_brief: Heavy-tail behavior outside the conjectured regime
original_question: In critically loaded finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queues, what explains the apparent split between heavy-tailed Weibull and light-tailed examples, which seem to agree with Conjecture 1, and Lognormal and Pareto examples, which appear to behave differently? Is the discrepancy for Lognormal and Pareto caused by very slow convergence of γ*(t) to γ* as t → ∞, by the finite-buffer correction term vanishing much more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞, or by a genuinely different asymptotic limit for those distributions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a GI/G/1/K queue: a single-server queue with i.i.d. interarrival times having distribution A and i.i.d. service times having distribution B (independent of arrivals), a single server working at unit rate, and a finite buffer of capacity K (customers arriving when the system holds K customers are lost). Assume the queue is critically loaded, i.e., E[A] = E[B] =: 1/λ, and that A and B have finite second moments with squared coefficients of variation c_a^2 and c_s^2. Let D(t) denote the number of customer departures (service completions) by time t in stationarity, and define the asymptotic variance rate
   γ*(K) := lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t))/t,
and the time-dependent variance rate γ*(t,K) := Var(D(t))/t.

A widely studied conjecture (the BRAVO conjecture for critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues) asserts that, for sufficiently light-tailed interarrival/service distributions,
   γ*(K) = λ (c_a^2 + c_s^2)/3 + o_K(1) as K → ∞,
with the correction term o_K(1) believed to be of order O(1/K).

Empirical simulation evidence indicates that:
 (i) heavy-tailed Weibull (with shape parameter < 1) interarrival/service distributions and light-tailed distributions appear to obey the formula above;
 (ii) Lognormal and Pareto interarrival/service distributions appear to deviate, in that the simulated γ*(t,K) does not converge to λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 within the studied ranges of t and K.

Determine which of the following explains the observed deviation for Lognormal and Pareto distributions:
 (a) the conjectured limit γ*(K) → λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 still holds, but the convergence γ*(t,K) → γ*(K) as t → ∞ is genuinely very slow;
 (b) the conjectured limit holds for each fixed K, but the finite-buffer correction γ*(K) − λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 vanishes much more slowly than 1/K as K → ∞;
 (c) the asymptotic limit lim_{K→∞} γ*(K) is genuinely different from λ(c_a^2+c_s^2)/3 for these distributions, so that the BRAVO 1/3 factor fails in this regime.

Provide a proof identifying the correct alternative, together with rigorous rates (for (a) the rate of convergence in t; for (b) the rate in K; for (c) the corrected limiting value).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues with Lognormal and Pareto distributions. Subsequent literature (e.g., asymptotic variance results for GI/G/1 BRAVO under 2+ε moments, work on second-order terms of variance curves, and recent work on phase transitions and generalized BRAVO with oscillating cumulants) extends the BRAVO theory but does not appear to definitively resolve which of the three explanations (slow convergence in t, slow vanishing of the finite-buffer correction in K, or a genuinely different limit) accounts for the Lognormal/Pareto behavior. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Solutions to open problems of Yang concerning inverse nodal problems
context_brief: Inverse nodal problem for Sturm-Liouville operators
original_question: Consider the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem L(q, α, β) on (0,1), given by -y''(x) + q(x)y(x) = λy(x) with real-valued q in L¹(0,1) and boundary conditions y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0 and y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0. Fix b in (1/2,1]. If one knows a subset of the nodal set of eigenfunctions inside (0,b) that is dense in (0,b), but not necessarily s-dense there, is that weaker dense nodal data still sufficient to determine the left boundary parameter α uniquely?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem L(q,α,β) on the interval (0,1):

  -y''(x) + q(x) y(x) = λ y(x),  x ∈ (0,1),

with real-valued potential q ∈ L¹(0,1), and separated boundary conditions

  y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0,
  y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0,

where α ∈ [0,π) and β ∈ (0,π]. For each eigenvalue λ_n let y_n be a corresponding eigenfunction, and let X_n = { x_{n,k} : 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1 } ⊂ (0,1) denote its nodal set (the zeros of y_n in (0,1)). The total nodal set is X = ⋃_n X_n.

Fix b ∈ (1/2, 1]. A subset S ⊂ X ∩ (0,b) is called dense in (0,b) if its closure contains [0,b]. (A stronger notion, "s-dense", requires that for every x ∈ (0,b) there is a sequence x_{n_j, k_j} ∈ S with k_j/n_j → x as j → ∞.)

Question: Suppose one is given only a subset S of the nodal set X ∩ (0,b) that is dense in (0,b), but not necessarily s-dense there. Is this dense (but not necessarily s-dense) nodal data sufficient to determine the left boundary parameter α uniquely? That is, if L(q,α,β) and L(q̃,α̃,β̃) share such a common dense nodal subset in (0,b), must α = α̃?
category_tag: Inverse nodal problems for Sturm-Liouville operators
status_search_result: The problem was answered affirmatively: a dense (not necessarily s-dense) subset of the nodal set in (0,b) with b ∈ (1/2,1] suffices to uniquely determine the left boundary parameter α. This resolution is attributed to Cheng et al., who strengthened the earlier nodal uniqueness theorem by weakening the s-dense hypothesis to a dense hypothesis.

(see Theorem 3.2 in [6]).", "claim": "The dense-nodal-subset version of the uniqueness problem for the boundary parameter α has been resolved affirmatively."}]

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: Classify all recurrent one-sided and two-sided sequences over a finite alphabet whose maximal pattern complexity satisfies p*(n)=2n for every n≥1; equivalently, determine all one-sided and two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $x = (x_n)$ be an infinite sequence over $A$, either one-sided ($n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) or two-sided ($n \in \mathbb{Z}$). For an integer $k \ge 1$ and a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative integers $\tau = (\tau(0), \tau(1), \ldots, \tau(k-1))$ with $\tau(0) = 0$, define the $\tau$-pattern set of $x$ as
\[
F_\tau(x) = \{(x_{n+\tau(0)}, x_{n+\tau(1)}, \ldots, x_{n+\tau(k-1)}) : n \text{ in the index set of } x\}.
\]
The maximal pattern complexity of $x$ is
\[
p^*_x(k) = \sup_{\tau} \#F_\tau(x),
\]
where the supremum is over all such $\tau$ of length $k$. The sequence $x$ is called recurrent if every finite factor occurring in $x$ occurs infinitely often (in both directions, in the two-sided case). Call $x$ pattern Sturmian if $p^*_x(n) = 2n$ for all $n \ge 1$.

Classify (up to relabeling of the alphabet) all recurrent one-sided infinite sequences and all recurrent two-sided infinite sequences over a finite alphabet that are pattern Sturmian; equivalently, give an explicit structural description of every such sequence.
status_search_result: The classification problem for pattern Sturmian sequences (those with maximal pattern complexity p*(n) = 2n for all n) was raised by Kamae and collaborators; partial results characterize the language structure of pattern Sturmian words and show Sturmian words form a strict subclass, but no complete classification of one-sided or two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences appears in the literature. The problem is listed as an open problem in surveys on mathematical quasicrystals, and no resolution was found.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: Let (V,E) be the graph of the Penrose tiling and define H on l²(V) by [Hψ](v)=∑_{w:(v,w)∈E}(ψ(w)-ψ(v)). Determine the spectrum σ(H) of this operator.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(V,E)$ be the (undirected) graph whose vertex set $V$ consists of the vertices of a Penrose tiling of the plane (taken, e.g., as a fixed rhombic Penrose tiling), and whose edge set $E$ consists of the unordered pairs $\{v,w\}$ such that $v$ and $w$ are endpoints of a common edge of a tile. The graph is locally finite (each vertex has bounded degree). Define the bounded self-adjoint operator $H$ on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(V)$ by
$$[H\psi](v) \;=\; \sum_{w:\,\{v,w\}\in E}\bigl(\psi(w)-\psi(v)\bigr), \qquad \psi\in\ell^2(V),\ v\in V.$$
Determine the spectrum $\sigma(H)\subset\mathbb{R}$ of this graph Laplacian.
category_tag: Spectra of Laplacians on aperiodic tilings
status_search_result: The full spectrum of the Penrose-tiling graph Laplacian is not known. Recent work (e.g., Embree et al., Experimental Mathematics 33 (2024)) studies the integrated density of states for graph Laplacians on Penrose and Ammann–Beenker tilings, exhibiting locally-supported eigenfunctions and lower bounds on jumps in the IDS, but does not give a complete description of σ(H). The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: Does every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ have pure point spectrum whenever its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M has irreducible characteristic polynomial, equivalently whenever the algebraic degree of λ equals the dimension of M?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let A = {1, 2, ..., n} be a finite alphabet with associated prototiles (closed intervals) of positive lengths ℓ_1, ..., ℓ_n. A one-dimensional self-similar inflation rule with scaling factor λ > 1 is a map that sends each prototile of length ℓ_i to a finite concatenation of prototiles whose total length is λℓ_i. Its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^{n×n} has entries M_{ij} equal to the number of tiles of type i appearing in the inflation of the prototile of type j; the vector (ℓ_1, ..., ℓ_n) is a positive eigenvector of M with eigenvalue λ. Assume M is primitive (so λ is the simple Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue). The associated tiling dynamical system is the orbit closure under translation of any fixed point of the inflation, equipped with the unique invariant probability measure; one says the tiling has pure point (pure discrete) dynamical spectrum if the Koopman representation of the translation action on L^2 of this measure decomposes as a direct sum of one-dimensional eigenspaces.

Assume further that λ is a Pisot number (a real algebraic integer > 1 all of whose Galois conjugates lie strictly inside the open unit disk) and that the characteristic polynomial of M is irreducible over ℚ — equivalently, the algebraic degree of λ over ℚ equals n.

Question. Under the above hypotheses, does the tiling dynamical system necessarily have pure point spectrum?
status_search_result: The irreducible Pisot substitution conjecture remains open in general. Special cases are known: it holds for two-letter (binary) Pisot substitutions and for β-substitutions when β is a Pisot number. Algorithms exist to verify pure discrete spectrum for individual substitutions, and various reformulations have been given, but no general proof or counterexample is known.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: For a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, must the coincidence rank divide the algebraic norm of λ?
self_contained_problem:
Let T be a one-dimensional primitive inflation tiling of the real line with inflation (scaling) factor λ, where λ is a Pisot number (a real algebraic integer greater than 1 all of whose Galois conjugates have modulus strictly less than 1). Let Ω be the associated tiling space (the orbit closure of T under translations) and let cr(Ω) denote the coincidence rank of the tiling, defined as the maximal cardinality of a collection of pairwise distinct tilings in Ω that share the same image under the maximal equicontinuous factor map (equivalently, the number of sheets of the canonical map from Ω to its maximal equicontinuous factor). Let N(λ) denote the absolute value of the algebraic norm of λ over ℚ, that is, the absolute value of the product of all Galois conjugates of λ.

Question: Must cr(Ω) divide N(λ)?
status_search_result: The Coincidence Rank Conjecture remains open in general. Partial results are known: Barge and collaborators have verified the conjecture when λ is a (rational) integer (degree one case) and for all Pisot λ when the coincidence rank equals 2. A weaker form—that the coincidence rank divides some power of the norm of λ—has also been studied via homological Pisot substitutions and the Exact Regularity Property. No proof of the full conjecture for general one-dimensional Pisot inflation tilings appears in the literature.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: Does the diffraction measure of the Pinwheel tiling have a nonzero absolutely continuous component?
self_contained_problem:
The Pinwheel tiling is the non-periodic tiling of the plane introduced by Conway and Radin, generated by an inflation rule on a right triangle with legs 1 and 2, in which tiles appear in infinitely many orientations (a dense set of rotations in SO(2)). To any such tiling T one associates its Dirac comb $\omega_T = \sum_{x \in \Lambda} \delta_x$, where $\Lambda$ is a representative point set (e.g., the set of control points of the tiles). The autocorrelation measure is $\gamma = \lim_{R\to\infty} \frac{1}{|B_R|}\, \omega_T|_{B_R} * \widetilde{\omega_T|_{B_R}}$, and the diffraction measure is $\widehat{\gamma}$, a positive translation-bounded measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. By the Lebesgue decomposition, $\widehat{\gamma} = \widehat{\gamma}_{pp} + \widehat{\gamma}_{sc} + \widehat{\gamma}_{ac}$, with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$.

It is known that $\widehat{\gamma}$ is rotation-invariant (circularly symmetric) and that its pure point part is concentrated only at the origin.

Question: Is the absolutely continuous component $\widehat{\gamma}_{ac}$ of the Pinwheel diffraction measure nonzero?
status_search_result: The status of the absolutely continuous component of the Pinwheel diffraction appears to remain open. The diffraction is known to be circularly symmetric with trivial pure point part (only at the origin) and to contain singular continuous rings; numerical investigations suggest possible additional components, but no rigorous proof of presence or absence of an absolutely continuous part is established in the literature found.

original_question: With the same cut-and-project setup and notation as in Problem 2.4.1, is there a choice of α and β for which the supremum over all aligned rectangles Ω of the number of distinct frequencies #ξ_(α,β)(Ω) is infinite?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ be irrational. Consider the canonical codimension-$2$ cut-and-project scheme in which $\mathbb{R}^{4}=E^{\parallel}\oplus E^{\perp}$ is decomposed so that the "physical" $2$-plane $E^{\parallel}\simeq\mathbb{R}^{2}$ is the graph
$$E^{\parallel}=\{(s,t,\alpha s,\beta t):s,t\in\mathbb{R}\},$$
and $E^{\perp}\simeq\mathbb{R}^{2}$ is its orthogonal complement; let $\pi^{\parallel}:\mathbb{R}^{4}\to E^{\parallel}$ and $\pi^{\perp}:\mathbb{R}^{4}\to E^{\perp}$ be the natural projections. Fix a bounded window $W\subset E^{\perp}$ with non-empty interior whose boundary has measure zero (for instance, a fixed unit square aligned with the coordinate axes of $E^{\perp}$). Define the cut-and-project point set
$$\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}=\bigl\{\pi^{\parallel}(\mathbf{v}):\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{Z}^{4},\;\pi^{\perp}(\mathbf{v})\in W\bigr\}\subset E^{\parallel}\simeq\mathbb{R}^{2}.$$

For a bounded set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ and a point $x\in\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}$, the $\Omega$-patch at $x$ is the finite set
$$P_{\Omega}(x)=\bigl(\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}-x\bigr)\cap\Omega.$$
Two $\Omega$-patches $P_{\Omega}(x)$ and $P_{\Omega}(y)$ are declared equivalent if they are equal as subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{2}$. Each equivalence class $[P]$ has a well-defined asymptotic frequency
$$\mathrm{freq}([P])=\lim_{R\to\infty}\frac{\#\{x\in\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}\cap B_{R}(0):P_{\Omega}(x)=P\}}{\mathrm{vol}(B_{R}(0))},$$
which exists for almost every choice of $\alpha,\beta$. Let
$$\xi_{\alpha,\beta}(\Omega)=\{\mathrm{freq}([P]):P\text{ an equivalence class of }\Omega\text{-patches in }\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}\}\subset\mathbb{R}_{>0}$$
and let $\#\xi_{\alpha,\beta}(\Omega)$ denote its cardinality. Let
$$\mathcal{R}=\{\,[a_{1},b_{1}]\times[a_{2},b_{2}]:a_{i}<b_{i}\,\}$$
be the collection of all axis-aligned rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$.

Question: Does there exist an irrational pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ such that
$$\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal{R}}\#\xi_{\alpha,\beta}(\Omega)=+\infty\,?$$
status_search_result: The question is the "easier" variant of an open problem on patch-frequency cardinality for two-dimensional cut-and-project sets with aligned rectangular windows. Subsequent work by Haynes, Koivusalo, Julien, Walton and Sadun on gaps problems and statistics of patterns in typical cut-and-project sets gives bounds on the number of distinct patch frequencies (typically polylogarithmic in the patch size) but does not appear to settle whether, for some specific choice of $(\alpha,\beta)$, the supremum over aligned rectangular regions can be infinite. No source found explicitly resolves this particular question, so its status is recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: For an aperiodic repetitive tiling of dimension d, does polynomial patch complexity growth p(n)=O(n^d) force the rational Čech cohomology of the tiling space to be finitely generated, i.e. rk(H*(Ω,Q))<∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let T be a tiling of R^d with finite local complexity (only finitely many tile types up to translation, and only finitely many two-tile patches up to translation). Assume T is aperiodic (no nonzero translation maps T to itself) and repetitive (for every patch P appearing in T, there exists R>0 such that every ball of radius R in R^d contains a translate of P). Let the patch-counting (complexity) function p: N → N be defined by

  p(n) = number of distinct patches of T of diameter at most n, counted up to translation.

Let Ω denote the continuous hull (tiling space) of T, namely the completion of the orbit {T - x : x ∈ R^d} in the local topology. Let H*(Ω, Q) denote the Čech cohomology of Ω with rational coefficients.

Question: Does the polynomial complexity bound p(n) = O(n^d) imply that the total rational Čech cohomology has finite rank, i.e. rk(H*(Ω, Q)) < ∞?
status_search_result: A one-dimensional counterexample by Julien ("Complexity and cohomology for cut-and-projection tilings", Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems) shows that polynomial patch-counting complexity does not in general force the rational Čech cohomology of the tiling space to be finitely generated; the implication does hold within the restricted class of cut-and-project tilings, but fails for general aperiodic repetitive tilings, answering the question in the negative.

We show that such a link cannot be established for more general tilings, and we present a counter-example in dimension one.", "claim": "There exists a one-dimensional aperiodic repetitive tiling with polynomial complexity whose tiling space has cohomology that is not finitely generated over Q, refuting the implication in general."}]

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
context_brief: Pattern properties invariant under tiling equivalence
original_question: Identify and classify tilings that possess some strengthened geometric pattern property—motivated by properties such as bounded displacement equivalence, bi-Lipschitz equivalence, linear repetitivity, or similar notions—with the feature that every tiling mutually locally derivable from it, topologically conjugate to it, or homeomorphic to it also has that same property.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by polytopal tiles drawn from a finite set of prototiles up to translation. Two tilings $\mathcal{T}_1,\mathcal{T}_2$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ are said to be:

(a) Mutually locally derivable (MLD) if there exists $R>0$ such that for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the patch of $\mathcal{T}_2$ inside the ball $B(x,1)$ is determined by the patch of $\mathcal{T}_1$ inside $B(x,R)$, and vice versa.

(b) Topologically conjugate if their associated tiling dynamical systems (the orbit closures in the local-topology hull under the $\mathbb{R}^d$-translation action) are conjugate as topological dynamical systems.

(c) Homeomorphic if their hulls are homeomorphic as topological spaces.

A pattern property $P$ for tilings is, for instance, one of the following:

• Bounded displacement (BD) equivalence to a lattice: there exists a bijection $\phi$ from the set of tile-centers of $\mathcal{T}$ to a lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\sup_x \|\phi(x)-x\|<\infty$.

• Bi-Lipschitz (BL) equivalence to a lattice: such a bijection $\phi$ exists which is bi-Lipschitz when extended appropriately.

• Linear repetitivity (LR): there exists $C>0$ such that every patch of $\mathcal{T}$ of diameter $r$ that occurs in $\mathcal{T}$ already occurs in every ball of radius $Cr$.

Problem. For each such pattern property $P$ (and for analogous strengthened variants), determine and classify all tilings $\mathcal{T}$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the following invariance feature: every tiling $\mathcal{T}'$ that is MLD to $\mathcal{T}$ (respectively, topologically conjugate to $\mathcal{T}$, respectively, homeomorphic to $\mathcal{T}$ in the hull sense) also satisfies property $P$. In other words, characterize those tilings for which property $P$ is preserved under the chosen equivalence relation, and identify a strengthening of $P$ that is automatically invariant under MLD equivalence, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism of hulls.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open classification/research problem on identifying invariant strengthenings of bounded-displacement, bi-Lipschitz, and linear-repetitivity properties under MLD, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism. No comprehensive classification has been located in the literature; partial results exist for linear repetitivity (which is known to be MLD-invariant and has connections with topological conjugacy results due to Aliste-Prieto, Coronel, Gambaudo, and others), while BD/BL invariance is more subtle. Overall the problem remains open in its general classification form.
