paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
original_question: Find a set of local matching rules for tilings in dimension 2 or 3 such that both of the following hold: (A) for each tile type t there is a constant c_t with discrepancy D_t(R)=|N_t(R)-d(t)·vol(R)| bounded by c_t·|∂R| for every finite union R of tiles, and (B) the same low-fluctuation bound also holds for every pattern or patch satisfying the matching rules.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with $d=2$ or $d=3$) by finitely many translation classes of tiles, where each tile is a compact polytope. A set of local matching rules is a finite collection of allowed local configurations (patches up to translation within some bounded radius) which determines a tiling space $X$ consisting of all tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which every local configuration belongs to the allowed list.

For a tiling $T \in X$ and each tile type $t$, let $N_t(R)$ denote the number of tiles of type $t$ of $T$ that are contained in a bounded measurable region $R \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (taken to be a finite union of tiles of $T$), and let $d(t)$ denote the asymptotic frequency (density) per unit volume of tiles of type $t$ in $T$. Define the discrepancy
$$D_t(R) = \bigl| N_t(R) - d(t)\,\mathrm{vol}(R) \bigr|.$$
Let $|\partial R|$ denote the $(d-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the boundary of $R$.

Problem. Exhibit, in dimension $d=2$ or $d=3$, a set of local matching rules with the following two properties simultaneously:

(A) There exists a particular tiling $T_0 \in X$ such that for every tile type $t$ there is a constant $c_t > 0$ (depending only on $t$) with
$$D_t(R) \le c_t \, |\partial R|$$
for every region $R$ that is a finite union of tiles of $T_0$.

(B) The same bound holds with the same constants $c_t$ uniformly for every tiling $T \in X$ satisfying the matching rules and every region $R$ that is a finite union of tiles of $T$.

Construct such a set of matching rules, or prove that none exists.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a survey of open problems on mathematical quasicrystals. Weak matching rules are known to enforce bounded perp-space fluctuations for many cases (e.g., N-fold symmetric tilings with N not divisible by 4, and icosahedral cases), but no construction is documented that simultaneously achieves the strong boundary-proportional discrepancy bound (A) and that this bound holds uniformly for every patch satisfying the rules (B) in dimensions 2 or 3. No resolution was found in the search; status appears open.

paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
context_brief: Invariant measures on closed subsets of Euclidean space
original_question: Determine all Borel probability measures on the space Cl(R^d) of closed subsets of R^d that are invariant under the natural action of SL_d(R), and likewise determine all such invariant Borel probability measures for the action of the affine group ASL_d(R).
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 1$ be an integer, and let $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the set of all closed subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$, equipped with the Chabauty–Fell topology (the topology generated by the sub-basis $\{F\in\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d): F\cap K=\emptyset\}$ for compact $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ together with $\{F\in\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d): F\cap U\neq\emptyset\}$ for open $U\subset\mathbb{R}^d$); with this topology $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is a compact metrizable space. The special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ acts on $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by $g\cdot F=\{gx:x\in F\}$, and the affine special linear group $\mathrm{ASL}_d(\mathbb{R})=\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^d$ acts by $(g,v)\cdot F=\{gx+v:x\in F\}$.

Classify (i.e., describe explicitly) all Borel probability measures on $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that are invariant under the $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$-action, and likewise classify all Borel probability measures on $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that are invariant under the $\mathrm{ASL}_d(\mathbb{R})$-action.
status_search_result: Web searches reveal a body of related work (invariant random subgroups, work of Marklof–Strömbergsson on quasicrystals, Solan, and Weiss–collaborators on dynamical questions of Danzer/Gowers type), but no source presents a complete classification of all SL_d(R)- or ASL_d(R)-invariant Borel probability measures on the space of closed subsets of R^d. The full classification appears to remain open.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: In a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment, meaning a distributed high-performance environment composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links, can one develop machine-independent programming languages with user-specified directives that both compile a given application into efficient code for any machine in the HC suite and also support decomposing the application into tasks and subtasks while determining the computational requirements of those tasks and subtasks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment, defined as a distributed high-performance system consisting of a finite suite M = {M_1, ..., M_k} of machines with differing computational architectures and capabilities (e.g., vector processors, SIMD arrays, MIMD multiprocessors, scalar workstations), interconnected by high-bandwidth communication links. An application A is to be executed on this suite and may be decomposed into a collection of tasks and subtasks, each of which has computational requirements (e.g., type of parallelism, memory, communication pattern) that may make it more or less suited to particular machines in M.

Develop a machine-independent programming language L, equipped with a finite set D of user-specified directives, such that:
(1) Given any application A written in L (with directives from D) and any machine M_i in M, there exists a compiler C_i that translates (A, D) into code for M_i that is efficient relative to a chosen performance metric on M_i;
(2) The language and directives provide formal mechanisms that aid in decomposing A into a hierarchy of tasks and subtasks; and
(3) The language and directives enable automatic or semi-automatic determination of the computational requirements of each task and subtask, in a form usable by a mapper/scheduler that assigns tasks to machines in M.

The problem is to determine whether such a language L, directive set D, and family of compilers {C_i} can be constructed so that all three properties hold simultaneously across arbitrary HC suites M and arbitrary applications A.
status_search_result: This is a long-standing open research goal in heterogeneous computing rather than a sharply defined mathematical conjecture. Subsequent decades of work (e.g., HPF, OpenMP, OpenCL, SYCL, OneAPI, Kokkos, RAJA, Legion) have produced partial solutions providing portable programming models with directives, but no system fully achieves machine-independent compilation to efficient code on arbitrary heterogeneous suites together with automatic task decomposition and requirement determination. The status is best described as unknown/ongoing rather than formally solved or refuted.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: In a heterogeneous computing environment, how should the uncertainty in estimated parameter values, such as predicted task completion times, be incorporated into the process of mapping tasks and subtasks to machines?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing environment consisting of a finite set of machines $M = \{m_1, \ldots, m_p\}$ with varied computational capabilities interconnected by communication links, and a finite set of tasks (or subtasks) $T = \{t_1, \ldots, t_n\}$, possibly with precedence constraints given by a directed acyclic graph. For each pair $(t_i, m_j)$, the execution time, communication cost, and any other relevant parameters (e.g., energy consumption, machine availability, link bandwidth) are not known exactly but are estimated. Model these estimates as random variables $X_{ij}$ on a probability space, with known distributions (or at least known means, variances, or confidence intervals).

A mapping is a function $\mu : T \to M$ (together, when applicable, with a schedule assigning start times) and the performance of $\mu$ is measured by an objective such as the makespan
$$C_{\max}(\mu) = \max_{t_i \in T} C_i(\mu),$$
where $C_i(\mu)$ is the (random) completion time of task $t_i$ under $\mu$.

Develop a principled framework for incorporating the uncertainty in the estimated parameters into the mapping process. Specifically:

1. Define a precise notion of an "uncertainty-aware" optimal mapping (e.g., minimizing $\mathbb{E}[C_{\max}(\mu)]$, minimizing a quantile $\inf\{c : \Pr[C_{\max}(\mu) \le c] \ge 1-\alpha\}$, or minimizing a robust worst-case objective $\sup_{X \in \mathcal{U}} C_{\max}(\mu; X)$ over an uncertainty set $\mathcal{U}$).
2. Provide algorithms that produce such mappings, together with provable approximation or robustness guarantees relative to the chosen objective.
3. Quantify how the quality of the resulting mapping degrades as a function of the uncertainty (e.g., the variance or radius of $\mathcal{U}$) in the input estimates.
status_search_result: The question of incorporating parameter uncertainty into task-to-machine mapping in heterogeneous computing remains an active research area. Numerous approaches (stochastic, robust, and probabilistic robust mapping; static and dynamic heuristics; recent learning-based schedulers) have been proposed since the question was raised, but no single accepted framework or optimal solution exists, and the underlying stochastic scheduling problems are generally NP-hard with only partial approximation results known.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: In heterogeneous computing applications that are decomposed into tasks and subtasks, what methods can support the feedback communications required among subtasks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing environment consisting of a set of machines $M = \{m_1, \ldots, m_k\}$ with differing architectures, capabilities, and interconnection networks. An application is modeled as a directed graph $G = (T, E)$ whose nodes are tasks; each task $t \in T$ may itself be decomposed into a set of communicating subtasks $S_t = \{s_{t,1}, \ldots, s_{t,n_t}\}$ with data dependencies among them, and individual subtasks may be assigned to different machines in $M$ for execution. In contrast to purely feed-forward (one-way) data dependencies, allow bidirectional dependencies in which the output of a subtask $s_{t,j}$ may need to be returned as input to a previously executed (or concurrently executing) subtask $s_{t,i}$, possibly on a different machine, during the course of task execution.

Develop and characterize methods (including programming-model abstractions, scheduling/assignment policies, runtime communication mechanisms, and synchronization protocols) that support such feedback communications among subtasks of a decomposed application in a heterogeneous computing system. Specifically: (i) define a formal model of subtask feedback communication that extends standard task-graph models to allow cyclic data dependencies; (ii) design mapping and scheduling algorithms for such models that account for inter-machine communication latencies and heterogeneous compute costs; and (iii) determine conditions under which feedback-aware mappings can be produced efficiently and analyze their performance relative to feedback-oblivious mappings.
status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning runtime and scheduling support for feedback (cyclic) dependencies among subtasks in heterogeneous computing. While many partial techniques exist (DAG schedulers such as HEFT, dataflow runtimes like StarPU, Legion, and Charm++ that support iterative/feedback patterns), no single accepted solution to the general formulation is documented. Available evidence is inconclusive about a definitive resolution.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: For heterogeneous computing suites, what hierarchical scheduling techniques can make it possible to scale the suite up to very large sizes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing (HC) suite, defined as a distributed collection of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed communication links, on which a stream of tasks (each with possibly different execution-time profiles on different machines, and with arbitrary inter-task data dependencies and quality-of-service requirements) must be matched to machines and scheduled in time. A scheduling policy must decide, for each arriving task or task graph, which machine should execute each task and in what order, with the objective of optimizing system-wide performance metrics such as makespan, throughput, robustness, or weighted quality of service.

Design and analyze hierarchical scheduling techniques — that is, scheduling architectures organized into multiple coordinated levels (for example, a global/top-level scheduler that partitions or delegates work among regional sub-schedulers, which in turn dispatch to local machine-level schedulers) — that allow such an HC suite to be scaled up to very large sizes (in the number of machines, in the rate of incoming tasks, and in geographic/network extent) while maintaining acceptable scheduling quality and bounded scheduling overhead.

Specifically: (i) Specify a hierarchical scheduling framework (levels, information flow between levels, decision granularity, and aggregation of machine-state and task-state information) suitable for very large heterogeneous suites. (ii) Prove or empirically demonstrate scalability properties, such as sublinear growth of scheduling overhead and information-exchange cost as the number of machines grows. (iii) Quantify the loss in solution quality (relative to a hypothetical centralized optimal scheduler) introduced by the hierarchy, and identify regimes in which this loss is provably small.
status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction in heterogeneous/distributed computing rather than a precisely formulated mathematical conjecture. Hierarchical scheduling for large-scale heterogeneous systems remains an active research area (with ongoing work in grid, cloud, edge, and HPC scheduling), and no single definitive solution has been established. Hence the problem is best classified as open.

paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
original_question: Given that most operating systems support multi-tasking at the individual processor level, how should heterogeneous computing mapping procedures incorporate multi-tasking, allocate processor time among different tasks, and still leverage multi-tasking together with other quality-of-service requirements?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing system consisting of a finite set of machines $M = \{m_1, \dots, m_p\}$ with differing architectures and capabilities, and a stream of arriving tasks $T = \{t_1, t_2, \dots\}$. Each task $t_i$ has, on each machine $m_j$, an estimated execution time $e_{ij}$, a deadline $d_i$, and possibly other quality-of-service (QoS) parameters (priority, throughput, security level, accuracy tolerance). Each machine $m_j$ runs a multi-tasking operating system that can time-share its processor among multiple tasks simultaneously according to a scheduling discipline (e.g., a quantum-based round-robin or weighted fair-share policy parameterized by per-task weights $w_{ij} \ge 0$).

A mapping/scheduling procedure must produce, online or offline, both (i) an assignment of each task $t_i$ to one or more machines and (ii) for each machine $m_j$, a vector of time-share weights $(w_{ij})_i$ (with $\sum_i w_{ij} \le 1$ at any instant) governing how the operating system multi-tasks the assigned tasks.

Develop and analyze a mapping procedure that explicitly incorporates per-processor multi-tasking — that is, jointly determines task-to-machine assignment and processor time-allocation among coexisting tasks — while satisfying a specified collection of QoS constraints, and provide performance guarantees (e.g., on makespan, deadline-miss ratio, or QoS satisfaction) relative to a clairvoyant optimum. In particular, characterize how the freedom to share each processor among multiple tasks should be exploited to improve overall QoS compared with non-preemptive single-task-per-processor mappings, and identify conditions under which multi-tasking is provably beneficial or harmful.
status_search_result: The question is a broad research direction in heterogeneous computing rather than a single sharply-posed problem with a yes/no answer. Multi-tasking-aware mapping with QoS continues to be an active area in heterogeneous and cloud/edge scheduling research, with no definitive resolution; many heuristics and approximation results exist for restricted formulations, but a general solution remains absent.

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Sharp observability constants for the constant-coefficient heat equation
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded smooth domain, let ω be a nonempty open subset of Ω, and consider the linear heat equation φ_t − Δφ = 0 in Ω × (0,T) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T). There exist constants γ > 0 and C > 0 such that the weighted observability inequality ∫_0^T∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^T∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt holds for every solution, and the analogous inequality also makes sense on the infinite time interval because the L²-norm of solutions decays exponentially. Determine the best possible constant γ in these observability inequalities, in particular in the infinite-time version ∫_0^∞∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^∞∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt, and decide whether the lower bound γ ≥ sup_{B(x_0,p)⊂Ω\ω} p^2/4 is sharp, especially in radially symmetric geometries.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $\omega\subset\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset. For $T\in(0,\infty]$, consider the linear heat equation
$$\varphi_t-\Delta\varphi=0\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),\qquad \varphi=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega\times(0,T),$$
with initial data $\varphi(\cdot,0)\in L^2(\Omega)$. It is known that there exist constants $\gamma>0$ and $C=C(\gamma)>0$ such that the weighted observability inequality
$$\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt\;\le\;C\int_0^T\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt$$
holds for every solution $\varphi$. Because solutions decay exponentially in $L^2(\Omega)$, the inequality also makes sense with $T=\infty$:
$$\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt\;\le\;C\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt.$$
Determine the best (smallest) admissible constant $\gamma>0$ for which such an inequality holds, in particular in the infinite-time version. Furthermore, given the geometric lower bound
$$\gamma\;\ge\;\sup\{\,\rho^2/4\;:\;B(x_0,\rho)\subset\Omega\setminus\omega\,\},$$
decide whether this lower bound is attained (i.e., is sharp), especially when $(\Omega,\omega)$ is radially symmetric.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Ervedoza and Zuazua ("Sharp Observability Estimates for Heat Equations", Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 202 (2011), 975–1017) develops transmutation techniques that yield observability estimates for the heat equation derived from those for the wave equation, and the authors state that their estimates are sharp in one space dimension and in multi-dimensional radially symmetric situations, providing partial confirmation of the conjectured sharpness of the geometric lower bound γ ≥ sup ρ²/4. However, a full characterization of the optimal γ for general bounded smooth domains and observation subsets does not appear to have been established.

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Growth thresholds for null-controllability of semilinear heat equations
original_question: Consider the semilinear heat equation u_t − Δu + f(u) = v1_ω in a bounded smooth domain Ω, with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T), control region ω ⊂ Ω open and nonempty, and a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity f satisfying f(0)=0 together with the local well-posedness assumptions used in the chapter. The chapter proves null-controllability when f grows strictly slower than |s|(log|s|)^{3/2} at infinity and gives counterexamples when f grows like |s|(log|s|)^p with p>2. Determine whether the system is null-controllable in the intermediate range C_1|s|(log|s|)^{3/2} ≤ |f(s)| ≤ C_2|s|(log|s|)^2 as |s|→∞, or more generally relax the known sufficient growth conditions for null-controllability, especially for nonlinearities growing slower than |s|(log|s|)^2 or such that 1/√|F(s)| is not integrable at infinity, where F(s)=∫_0^s f(σ)dσ.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be a nonempty open subset, and let $T>0$. Consider the semilinear heat equation with internal control
\[
\begin{cases} u_t - \Delta u + f(u) = v\,\mathbf{1}_\omega & \text{in } \Omega\times(0,T),\\ u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega\times(0,T),\\ u(\cdot,0) = u_0 & \text{in } \Omega, \end{cases}
\]
where $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is locally Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, $u_0\in L^2(\Omega)$, and $v\in L^2(\omega\times(0,T))$ is the control. The system is said to be null-controllable at time $T$ if for every initial datum $u_0$ there exists a control $v$ such that the corresponding solution satisfies $u(\cdot,T)\equiv 0$ in $\Omega$.

It is known that:
(i) if $|f(s)|/(|s|\log^{3/2}(1+|s|)) \to 0$ as $|s|\to\infty$, then null-controllability holds at every time $T>0$;
(ii) there exist nonlinearities $f$ with $|f(s)|\sim |s|\log^{p}(1+|s|)$ for some $p>2$ for which null-controllability fails.

Question: In the intermediate growth range
\[
C_1\,|s|\log^{3/2}(1+|s|) \le |f(s)| \le C_2\,|s|\log^{2}(1+|s|) \qquad \text{as } |s|\to\infty,
\]
is the system null-controllable? More generally, can the sufficient growth condition (i) be relaxed—e.g., to nonlinearities for which $1/\sqrt{|F(s)|}$ fails to be integrable at infinity, where $F(s)=\int_0^s f(\sigma)\,d\sigma$?
status_search_result: The gap between the sufficient growth $|s|\log^{3/2}(1+|s|)$ (controllability holds, Fernández-Cara–Zuazua) and the necessary threshold $|s|\log^{p}(1+|s|)$ with $p>2$ (counterexamples exist) remains open. Surveys and subsequent works on null-controllability of semilinear heat equations continue to cite this intermediate range $3/2 \le p \le 2$ as an unresolved problem.

paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
context_brief: Variable-coefficient and semilinear half-line heat equations
original_question: Consider the one-dimensional variable-coefficient heat equation on the half-line p(x)u_t − (a(x)u_x)_x = 0 for x>0 and t>0, with boundary control u(0,t)=v(t) and initial datum u(x,0)=u_0(x), where a and p are positive, bounded, smooth functions. Determine whether the lack of null-controllability proved in the chapter for the constant-coefficient half-line heat equation extends to this more general variable-coefficient setting. More generally, determine whether the same negative phenomenon persists for equations whose coefficients depend on both x and t, for equations with lower-order potentials, or for semilinear variants on the half-line.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional heat equation on the half-line with variable coefficients:
  p(x) u_t(x,t) − (a(x) u_x(x,t))_x = 0,   x > 0, t ∈ (0,T),
with boundary control u(0,t) = v(t), t ∈ (0,T), and initial datum u(x,0) = u_0(x), x > 0, where a, p : (0,∞) → ℝ are positive, bounded, smooth functions and v ∈ L^2(0,T) is the control.

The system is said to be null-controllable at time T from the initial datum u_0 if there exists a control v ∈ L^2(0,T) such that the corresponding solution satisfies u(·,T) ≡ 0 on (0,∞). It is known that for the constant-coefficient case (a ≡ p ≡ 1), null-controllability fails: there exist initial data u_0 ∈ L^2(0,∞) that cannot be steered to 0 in any time T > 0 by any L^2 boundary control.

Questions:
(a) Does this lack of null-controllability persist for every choice of positive, bounded, smooth coefficients a(x), p(x)?
(b) Does the same negative phenomenon hold when the coefficients depend on both x and t, i.e. a = a(x,t), p = p(x,t)?
(c) Does it hold in the presence of a lower-order potential, i.e. for equations of the form p(x) u_t − (a(x) u_x)_x + c(x,t) u = 0?
(d) Does it hold for semilinear variants p(x) u_t − (a(x) u_x)_x + f(u) = 0 on the half-line, under suitable growth assumptions on f?
status_search_result: The constant-coefficient lack of null-controllability on the half-line (Micu–Zuazua, 2001) has been re-proved by elementary/Fokas-method arguments (e.g., 2019/2020). Positive controllability results are available on bounded domains with variable coefficients, but a definitive extension of the half-line negative result to general variable coefficients a(x), p(x), to (x,t)-dependent coefficients, to lower-order potentials, or to semilinear variants does not appear to be established in the literature found. The status thus appears unresolved in full generality.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: Can one develop computationally tractable topological and numerical tools that decide, a priori, whether a given stabilization problem admits a solution, with checks that are easier than brute-force numerical experimentation and that still provide certificates of accuracy when the control law or vector field data are noisy, approximate, or experimentally obtained? Computational homology and topological data analysis are proposed as possible ingredients in such certified decision procedures.
self_contained_problem:
Let M be a smooth manifold and let f: M × U → TM be a control system, i.e. for each control value u ∈ U ⊂ R^m, f(·,u) is a smooth vector field on M, and let x* ∈ M be a target equilibrium. A (continuous, possibly time-varying or discontinuous) feedback law k: M → U is said to stabilize the system at x* if the closed-loop vector field X_k(x) := f(x,k(x)) renders x* (globally or locally) asymptotically stable. Assume the data (f, and possibly k) are only known approximately: one has access to an approximation f̃ with ‖f̃ − f‖ ≤ ε in some appropriate norm on a compact region K ⊂ M, possibly arising from experimental measurements.

Develop a computationally tractable decision procedure with the following properties:

(1) Given (M, f, x*) (or its approximation f̃ together with the noise bound ε), the procedure outputs in finite time either
   (a) a certificate that no continuous stabilizing feedback exists for the system at x*, or
   (b) a certificate that a stabilizing feedback exists, together with quantitative robustness margins valid for every system within the ε-ball around f̃.

(2) The complexity of the procedure must be strictly lower than that of brute-force simulation over a dense grid of initial conditions and candidate feedbacks.

(3) The certificates produced must be sound under the noise model: if the procedure certifies (a) or (b) for f̃, then the same conclusion holds for the true f provided ‖f̃ − f‖ ≤ ε.

In particular, design and analyze such a procedure built from computational homology and topological-data-analysis invariants (e.g. persistent homology of sublevel sets of candidate Lyapunov functions, topological obstructions to continuous sections of sphere bundles such as Brockett-type degree/index conditions, Conley-index computations on cubical or simplicial approximations of the flow), and prove its correctness, soundness with respect to the ε-noise model, and a complexity bound demonstrating tractability.
category_tag: Certified numerical tools for nonlinear stabilization
status_search_result: The question is a broad research-direction proposal calling for certified, topology-based numerical procedures that decide a priori solvability of nonlinear stabilization problems under noisy data. While there is active work on computational Conley index, persistent-homology-based Lyapunov function construction, and SOS/SDP certificates for stability, no general procedure meeting all the stated requirements (a-priori decision, noise certificates, sub-brute-force complexity) is known. The problem appears open.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: How can one identify a nonlinear system, or at least an appropriate global equivalence class of nonlinear systems, from data at a global scale rather than only along finite trajectories or in local neighborhoods? In particular, how can one detect unstable equilibria and build a theory combining topological methods, topological data analysis, and modern high-dimensional probability, while also clarifying how approaches such as neural networks, Gaussian processes, and Koopman-operator methods can be developed into a global identification framework?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time dynamical system on a smooth manifold $M \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ governed by an unknown map $f : M \to M$, observed through finitely many data of the form $(x_i, f(x_i) + \varepsilon_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,N$, where the $x_i$ may be drawn from finite trajectories or from probing points distributed across $M$, and the $\varepsilon_i$ are bounded or sub-Gaussian noise. Two maps $f_1, f_2$ are called globally equivalent if there exists a homeomorphism (resp. diffeomorphism) $h : M \to M$ such that $h \circ f_1 = f_2 \circ h$, so that $f_1$ and $f_2$ share the same global qualitative dynamics, including the location, number, and stability type of all equilibria (in particular unstable equilibria) and the structure of their stable and unstable manifolds.

Develop a statistical learning framework that, from such data, recovers the global equivalence class $[f]$ of $f$ rather than only a local approximation in a neighborhood of a single trajectory. Specifically:

(a) Define a notion of global identifiability and prove conditions on $(M, f)$ and on the sampling distribution under which $[f]$ is identifiable from $N$ samples with high probability as $N \to \infty$.

(b) Provide a procedure that, with high probability, correctly detects all equilibria of $f$ together with their stability type, including unstable equilibria, and give finite-sample guarantees in terms of $N$, the noise level, the dimension of $M$, and topological invariants of the dynamics.

(c) Formulate this procedure within a unified framework that combines topological dynamics (e.g., Conley index, Morse decompositions), topological data analysis (e.g., persistent homology of sublevel sets or of point clouds derived from the data), and tools from modern high-dimensional probability (e.g., concentration inequalities and empirical process theory), and prove its consistency.

(d) Determine to what extent standard nonparametric estimators of $f$ — neural network regressors, Gaussian process regressors, and finite-dimensional approximations of the Koopman operator — can be combined with the framework of (c) to yield such global identification guarantees, and characterize precisely which features of $[f]$ each of these classes of estimators can or cannot recover globally.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in nonlinear system identification, asking for a global (rather than local or finite-trajectory) identification theory blending topological dynamics, TDA, and high-dimensional probability. No published work resolves this program in full; ongoing research on Koopman operator learning, neural network and Gaussian process system identification, and TDA for dynamical systems addresses pieces of it but not the unified global identification of equivalence classes with guaranteed detection of unstable equilibria.

paper_title: Generalizations and Open Problems
original_question: What is the most meaningful way to extend obstruction-theoretic stability and stabilization results from deterministic systems on manifolds to stochastic systems with disturbances? Existing noise-aware results often focus on moments, but the open problem is to build a genuinely satisfactory stochastic analogue of the deterministic topological theory.
self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $M$ be a smooth (finite-dimensional) connected manifold without boundary, and consider a deterministic control system on $M$ of the form
\[
\dot{x}(t) = f(x(t), u(t)), \qquad x(t) \in M, \ u(t) \in U,
\]
where $f \colon M \times U \to TM$ is smooth and $U$ is a set of admissible control values. A point $x^* \in M$ is said to be (globally) asymptotically stabilizable by continuous state feedback if there exists a continuous feedback $k \colon M \to U$ such that $x^*$ is a globally asymptotically stable equilibrium of $\dot{x} = f(x, k(x))$. Classical obstruction-theoretic results (in the spirit of Brockett, Coron, and Sontag) provide topological obstructions—expressed in terms of homotopy/homology invariants of $M$, of the set of equilibria, or of associated index-theoretic data—that prevent the existence of such a continuous stabilizing feedback, and conversely yield constructive stabilization theorems when these obstructions vanish.

Now suppose the system is perturbed by noise, i.e., consider a stochastic control system on $M$ of Stratonovich form
\[
dx(t) = f(x(t), u(t))\,dt + \sum_{i=1}^{m} g_i(x(t)) \circ dW^i(t),
\]
where $g_1, \dots, g_m$ are smooth vector fields on $M$ and $W = (W^1, \dots, W^m)$ is a standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion. Stability of an equilibrium $x^*$ may be formulated in several non-equivalent ways: stability in probability, almost-sure asymptotic stability, $p$-th moment exponential stability, or stability of an associated invariant measure.

Problem. Develop a topological obstruction theory for global stabilization of the stochastic system above by continuous (state) feedback that genuinely extends the deterministic obstruction theory. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a precise notion of "topological obstruction to stochastic stabilization" $\mathcal{O}(M, f, \{g_i\})$, taking values in a (co)homological or homotopy-theoretic invariant of $M$ (or of an appropriate bundle/fiber space built from $f$ and $\{g_i\}$), such that:
   (i) when the noise vanishes ($g_i \equiv 0$), $\mathcal{O}$ reduces to a known deterministic topological obstruction (e.g., a Brockett-type or index-theoretic obstruction);
   (ii) $\mathcal{O} = 0$ implies the existence of a continuous feedback $k\colon M\to U$ rendering $x^*$ globally asymptotically stable in some specified stochastic sense;
   (iii) $\mathcal{O} \neq 0$ implies non-existence of such a continuous stabilizing feedback.

(b) Prove the corresponding necessity and sufficiency theorems.

The question is whether such an obstruction-theoretic framework exists that goes beyond moment-based Lyapunov criteria and faithfully captures the topological content of stabilizability in the stochastic setting.
status_search_result: No published work was found that constructs a topological/obstruction-theoretic stabilization theory for stochastic control systems on manifolds in the spirit requested. Existing stochastic stabilization literature is overwhelmingly Lyapunov- and moment-based, and the question of a genuine topological analogue is repeatedly noted as unresolved. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Solving Open Problems in Right Alternative Rings with Z-Module Reasoning
original_question: Let R be a right alternative ring, meaning a possibly nonassociative ring in which x(yy) = xyy for all x and y. If the associator is defined by (x, y, z) = (xy)z - x(yz), is it always true that for every x, y in R one has ((x, x, y)(x, x, y))x((x, x, y)(x, x, y)) = 0? Equivalently, must (x, x, y)^2 x (x, x, y)^2 vanish identically in every right alternative ring?
self_contained_problem:
A right alternative ring is a (not necessarily associative) ring R satisfying the identity x(yy) = (xy)y for all x, y in R. Define the associator of three elements by (x, y, z) := (xy)z - x(yz). Prove or disprove: for every right alternative ring R and all x, y in R,
   (x, x, y)^2 · x · (x, x, y)^2 = 0,
where (x, x, y)^2 denotes the square (x, x, y)(x, x, y) in R. Equivalently, show that the identity ((x,x,y)(x,x,y)) x ((x,x,y)(x,x,y)) = 0 holds in every right alternative ring.

paper_title: On Structure and Open Problems in Topological Theories Coupled to Topological Gravity
context_brief: Defining topological gravity for massive topological theories
original_question: In a two-dimensional topological matter theory coupled to topological gravity, Q-exact terms in the action need not decouple because boundaries of the moduli space contribute anomalously. The paper states that this nondecoupling creates problems in defining topological gravity for massive topological theories, and later explains that the theory is well behaved for conformal regulators but that some theories may not admit such a regulator. Determine how topological gravity should be defined for massive topological theories in this setting, including what replaces a conformal regulator when no such regulator exists.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional topological matter theory with a nilpotent BRST-type operator Q, coupled to two-dimensional topological gravity. The coupling is realized by integrating correlation functions of the matter sector over the moduli space M_{g,n} of genus g Riemann surfaces with n marked points (or its Deligne–Mumford compactification). In the conformal case, Q-exact insertions in the action decouple from physical correlators. However, when the matter theory is massive (i.e. its stress tensor is not Q-exact, or more generally the theory is not conformally invariant), Q-exact terms in the action fail to decouple because integration by parts on the moduli space picks up anomalous boundary contributions from the compactification divisor.

A regulator of the matter theory is called conformal if it preserves Q-invariance and conformal invariance simultaneously, so that the boundary contributions vanish and topological gravity is well defined in the standard way. There exist topological matter theories for which no such conformal regulator exists; an example is the A-type topological sigma model whose target manifold has nonzero first Chern class.

Problem. Provide an intrinsic definition of two-dimensional topological gravity coupled to a massive topological matter theory in which Q-exact deformations of the action genuinely decouple from physical correlators, accounting for the anomalous boundary contributions from ∂M_{g,n}. In particular, when the matter theory does not admit a conformal regulator, specify a substitute (a modified regularization, a prescription for boundary contributions, or another construction) that replaces the role of a conformal regulator and yields a consistent, scheme-independent definition of the coupled topological gravity theory and its correlation functions.
category_tag: topological gravity coupled to topological matter
status_search_result: The question concerns a foundational definitional issue in topological gravity coupled to massive topological matter raised in the early 1990s. Subsequent literature on topological strings, gravitational descendants, and Gromov–Witten theory (Witten, Kontsevich, Dijkgraaf–Witten, and later cohomological field theory work) addresses related structures, but a direct, complete answer specifying how to define topological gravity for arbitrary massive topological matter theories without a conformal regulator does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature accessible here. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon
context_brief: Upper bound for minimal neighbour-finding trees in degeneracy graphs
original_question: Let x⁰ be a degenerate vertex of a bounded polytope X, let G⁰₊ be the positive degeneracy graph whose nodes are the bases associated with x⁰, let U be the number of such bases, and let σ be the degeneracy degree of x⁰. Among the trees in G⁰₊ that connect x⁰ to all neighbouring vertices of x⁰, a minimal tree is one with the smallest possible number of nodes. Is ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋ always an upper bound on the number of nodes needed for such a minimal tree?
self_contained_problem:
Let X ⊂ ℝⁿ be a bounded polytope defined by a system of linear inequalities/equalities, and let x⁰ be a degenerate vertex of X (i.e., a vertex associated with more than one feasible basis). Let U denote the number of feasible bases associated with x⁰, and let σ be the degeneracy degree of x⁰ (the number of "extra" basic variables at x⁰ beyond a non-degenerate basis, so that U bases sit at x⁰).

Define the positive degeneracy graph G⁰₊ to be the graph whose node set is the collection of these U bases at x⁰, with two bases joined by an edge whenever they differ by a single pivot step using a positive pivot rule (so that each edge corresponds to a feasible simplex pivot between two bases at x⁰). 

A "neighbour-finding tree" rooted at x⁰ is a subtree of G⁰₊ that, by means of pivots leaving the bases of its nodes, reaches every vertex of X adjacent to x⁰ (i.e., every neighbouring vertex of x⁰ in the 1-skeleton of X). A minimal neighbour-finding tree is one with the smallest possible number of nodes.

Question: Is it true that for every degenerate vertex x⁰ of every bounded polytope X, the number of nodes of a minimal neighbour-finding tree is at most ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋?
status_search_result: Searches on degeneracy graphs and minimal neighbour-finding (N-) trees return general references to the theory of degeneracy graphs and the neighbourhood problem (e.g., survey chapters in Springer volumes and ORiON), but none of the readily available sources explicitly confirm or refute the conjectured upper bound ⌊U/(σ+1)⌋ on the number of nodes of a minimal N-tree. The status of the conjecture could not be verified from available evidence.

paper_title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon
context_brief: Decision procedure for detecting simplex cycling from c ∈ M(C)
original_question: Given linear-program data (A, b, c) and a degenerate vertex x⁰, let G⁰ be the degeneracy graph at x⁰ and, for each circuit C of G⁰, let M(C) be the point set induced by (A, b, c) such that C is a simplex cycle exactly when c belongs to M(C). Can one design an efficient method that decides whether c ∈ M(C) for at least one circuit C of G⁰, and hence determines whether simplex cycling occurs?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear program in standard form
  minimize cᵀx subject to Ax = b, x ≥ 0,
where A is an m×n real matrix of rank m, b ∈ ℝᵐ, and c ∈ ℝⁿ. Let x⁰ be a degenerate basic feasible solution (vertex), i.e. a vertex represented by more than one feasible basis. The degeneracy graph G⁰ at x⁰ is the undirected graph whose vertices are all feasible bases representing x⁰, with two such bases joined by an edge whenever they differ by exactly one basis-exchange (a single simplex pivot).

A circuit C of G⁰ is a simple cycle B₁ – B₂ – … – B_k – B₁ in this graph. For fixed (A, b) and a fixed circuit C of G⁰, define
  M(C) = { c ∈ ℝⁿ : when the simplex method is applied with cost vector c, it can perform exactly the pivot sequence around C, returning to B₁ },
so that the simplex method cycles along C precisely when c ∈ M(C). Simplex cycling occurs at x⁰ for the data (A, b, c) if and only if c ∈ M(C) for some circuit C of G⁰.

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given (A, b, c) and a degenerate vertex x⁰, decides in time polynomial in the input size (or otherwise efficiently) whether there exists a circuit C of G⁰ with c ∈ M(C); equivalently, decides whether simplex cycling can occur at x⁰ for the data (A, b, c).
category_tag: Linear programming degeneracy and simplex cycling
status_search_result: A web search on degeneracy graphs and simplex cycling returns the survey on degeneracy graph theory and related expositions, but no source confirming an efficient algorithm to decide membership c ∈ M(C) for some circuit C of the degeneracy graph. The status of an efficient decision procedure for cycling detection via the M(C) framework appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

paper_title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon
context_brief: Effect of removing weakly redundant constraints on sensitivity and shadow prices
original_question: If primal degeneracy in a linear program is caused by weakly redundant constraints passing through a degenerate optimal vertex x⁰, can one safely omit those weakly redundant constraints and then compute right-hand-side sensitivity ranges or shadow prices in the usual way without changing the correct answer?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear program in standard form
   maximize  c^T x   subject to  A x ≤ b,  x ≥ 0,
where A is an m×n real matrix, b ∈ ℝ^m, c ∈ ℝ^n. Let x⁰ be an optimal basic feasible solution that is primal-degenerate, meaning that more than n of the constraints (including the nonnegativity constraints) are active at x⁰. A constraint a_i^T x ≤ b_i is called weakly redundant for the feasible region P = {x : Ax ≤ b, x ≥ 0} if it is satisfied with equality at some feasible point but its removal does not change P. Suppose the degeneracy at x⁰ is caused exclusively by weakly redundant constraints passing through x⁰ (i.e., removing all such weakly redundant constraints from the system leaves x⁰ as a non-degenerate optimal vertex of the reduced LP).

Question: Is it true that, for every such linear program, one obtains the correct right-hand-side sensitivity intervals (the ranges of b_i over which the current optimal basis remains optimal) and the correct shadow prices (dual variables associated with the constraints) by deleting the weakly redundant constraints and then performing the standard sensitivity / shadow-price computation on the reduced LP? Equivalently, does omitting weakly redundant constraints preserve the true b-sensitivity ranges and shadow prices of the original LP?
category_tag: Linear programming degeneracy and sensitivity analysis
status_search_result: The question is resolved negatively: in general, omitting weakly redundant constraints that cause degeneracy at an optimal vertex leads to incorrect right-hand-side sensitivity ranges and incorrect shadow prices, although it does not affect sensitivity analysis with respect to the objective coefficients c. This was established in the literature on the degeneracy phenomenon in linear programming (Greenberg; Gal and collaborators).

paper_title: Chen–Ricci Inequality for CR-Warped Products and Related Open Problems
original_question: Given a warped product Riemannian manifold N1 ×_f N2, determine necessary conditions under which it admits a minimal isometric immersion into a Euclidean m-space E^m or, more generally, into a space form M̃^m(c).
self_contained_problem:
Let $(N_1, g_{N_1})$ and $(N_2, g_{N_2})$ be Riemannian manifolds and let $f \colon N_1 \to (0,\infty)$ be a smooth positive function. The warped product $N_1 \times_f N_2$ is the product manifold $N_1 \times N_2$ endowed with the Riemannian metric
$$\tilde g = g_{N_1} + f^2\, g_{N_2}.$$
Let $\widetilde{M}^m(c)$ denote a complete simply connected Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature $c$ and dimension $m$ (so $\widetilde{M}^m(0) = \mathbb{E}^m$ is Euclidean $m$-space). An isometric immersion $\phi \colon (N_1 \times_f N_2, \tilde g) \to \widetilde{M}^m(c)$ is called minimal if its mean curvature vector vanishes identically.

Problem. Determine necessary conditions on the data $(N_1, g_{N_1})$, $(N_2, g_{N_2})$, the warping function $f$, the dimension $m$, and the curvature $c$ under which the warped product $N_1 \times_f N_2$ admits a minimal isometric immersion into the Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^m$, and more generally into a real space form $\widetilde{M}^m(c)$.
status_search_result: The problem is a classical open problem (attributed to Chern and reformulated by B.-Y. Chen). Many partial necessary conditions are known: e.g., obstructions via the Laplacian of the warping function (Chen's inequality $\Delta f / f \le (n_2-1)$-type bounds), non-immersibility when $N_1$ is compact or when $f$ is an eigenfunction of $\Delta$ with positive eigenvalue, and refinements through Chen $\delta$-invariants and Chen–Ricci inequalities. Subsequent work (e.g., 2021 paper on first Chen inequality for general warped product submanifolds) continues to derive new necessary conditions, indicating that the full problem remains open while many partial answers exist.

paper_title: Chen–Ricci Inequality for CR-Warped Products and Related Open Problems
original_question: Classify all warped-product CR-submanifolds that attain equality in the Chen–Ricci inequalities proved in Theorem 4.1; in particular, classify those for which the equality cases characterized there—such as the mixed totally geodesic and distribution-wise totally geodesic or umbilical cases—occur.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$ be a complex space form of complex dimension $m$ and constant holomorphic sectional curvature $c$, equipped with its Kähler structure $(J,\widetilde g)$. A CR-submanifold $M^n$ of $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$ is a real submanifold endowed with two orthogonal complementary distributions $\mathcal{D}^T$ and $\mathcal{D}^\perp$ on $M^n$ such that $J\mathcal{D}^T=\mathcal{D}^T$ (the holomorphic distribution) and $J\mathcal{D}^\perp\subset T^\perp M^n$ (the totally real distribution). 

Given Riemannian manifolds $(N_T,g_T)$ and $(N_\perp,g_\perp)$ and a positive smooth function $f$ on $N_T$, the warped product $N_T\times_f N_\perp$ is the manifold $N_T\times N_\perp$ with metric $g=g_T\oplus f^2 g_\perp$. The warped product $M^n=N_T\times_f N_\perp$ isometrically immersed in $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$ is called a CR-warped product if $N_T$ and $N_\perp$ are integral manifolds of $\mathcal{D}^T$ and $\mathcal{D}^\perp$, respectively, with $N_T$ a holomorphic submanifold and $N_\perp$ a totally real submanifold of $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$.

Let $h$ denote the second fundamental form of $M^n$ in $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$, $H$ the mean curvature vector, and $\mathrm{Ric}$ the Ricci tensor of $M^n$. Set $n_1=\dim N_T$ and $n_2=\dim N_\perp$. The Chen–Ricci inequality for a CR-warped product asserts that for every unit tangent vector $X\in T_xM^n$,
$$\mathrm{Ric}(X)\;\le\;\tfrac14 n^2\|H\|^2+\Phi(c,n_1,n_2,f,X),\qquad (\star)$$
where $\Phi$ is the explicit curvature/warping term arising from the Gauss equation in $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$ (depending on whether $X\in\mathcal{D}^T$ or $X\in\mathcal{D}^\perp$).

The submanifold $M^n$ is called mixed totally geodesic if $h(X,Z)=0$ for every $X\in\mathcal{D}^T$ and $Z\in\mathcal{D}^\perp$; it is $\mathcal{D}^T$-totally geodesic (resp. $\mathcal{D}^\perp$-totally geodesic) if $h$ vanishes on $\mathcal{D}^T\times\mathcal{D}^T$ (resp. on $\mathcal{D}^\perp\times\mathcal{D}^\perp$); and it is $\mathcal{D}^\perp$-totally umbilical if $h(Z,W)=g(Z,W)\,\xi$ for all $Z,W\in\mathcal{D}^\perp$ and some normal vector field $\xi$.

It is known that:
(a) equality in $(\star)$ holds for every unit $X\in\mathcal{D}^T$ at every $x\in M^n$ iff $M^n$ is mixed totally geodesic and $\mathcal{D}^T$-totally geodesic;
(b) equality in $(\star)$ holds for every unit $X\in\mathcal{D}^\perp$ at every $x\in M^n$ iff $M^n$ is mixed totally geodesic and either $\mathcal{D}^\perp$-totally geodesic, or $\mathcal{D}^\perp$-totally umbilical with $\dim N_\perp=2$.

Problem. Classify, up to isometric congruence in $\widetilde{M}^{2m}(c)$, all CR-warped product submanifolds $N_T\times_f N_\perp$ that satisfy the equality cases (a) and/or (b) above. In particular, give an explicit description of those CR-warped products which are simultaneously mixed totally geodesic and $\mathcal{D}^T$-totally geodesic, and of those which are mixed totally geodesic and either $\mathcal{D}^\perp$-totally geodesic or $\mathcal{D}^\perp$-totally umbilical with $\dim N_\perp=2$.
category_tag: CR-warped product submanifolds in Kähler manifolds
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the work establishing the Chen–Ricci inequality for CR-warped products in complex space forms. Web searches return related inequalities and partial results (e.g., Ricci soliton classifications and analogous Sasakian/Kenmotsu extensions) but no full classification of CR-warped products attaining equality. No subsequent paper claiming a complete classification was found.

paper_title: The Growth Order of a Solution of a Singular Non-Self-Adjoint Differential Equation, as a Function of the Spectral Parameter
context_brief: Growth orders of normalized half-line solutions for PT-symmetric Schrödinger equations
original_question: For a Schrödinger equation on the real line with a PT-symmetric potential, suppose there are two distinguished solutions ψleft(x, λ) ∈ L²(−∞, 0) and ψright(x, λ) ∈ L²(0, ∞) for the spectral parameter λ; these may be taken as Jost solutions when the potential lies in L¹(ℝ). After normalizing these half-line solutions in an appropriate way, what can be said about their growth orders as functions of λ?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation
$$-\psi''(x) + V(x)\psi(x) = \lambda\,\psi(x), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ \lambda\in\mathbb{C},$$
with a PT-symmetric potential, i.e. a (generally complex-valued) measurable function $V:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $V(-x)=\overline{V(x)}$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Assume $V\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$, so that for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ with $\operatorname{Im}\sqrt{\lambda}>0$ (taking the branch with non-negative imaginary part) there exist Jost-type solutions: a solution $\psi_{\mathrm{left}}(\cdot,\lambda)$ that is square-integrable on $(-\infty,0)$ and a solution $\psi_{\mathrm{right}}(\cdot,\lambda)$ that is square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$. After fixing a normalization of these half-line solutions (for example, prescribing the asymptotic form $\psi_{\mathrm{right}}(x,\lambda)\sim e^{i\sqrt{\lambda}\,x}$ as $x\to+\infty$ and $\psi_{\mathrm{left}}(x,\lambda)\sim e^{-i\sqrt{\lambda}\,x}$ as $x\to-\infty$, or another comparable normalization), determine the growth order of $\psi_{\mathrm{left}}(x,\lambda)$ and $\psi_{\mathrm{right}}(x,\lambda)$, as well as of relevant connection coefficients between them, regarded as entire (or meromorphic) functions of the spectral parameter $\lambda$. In particular, provide sharp bounds of the form
$$|\psi_{\mathrm{left/right}}(x,\lambda)| \le C(x)\exp\!\big(A(x)|\lambda|^{\rho}\big)$$
identifying the optimal exponent $\rho$ (the order) and, where possible, the type, in terms of the regularity and decay properties of $V$.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this question for general PT-symmetric $L^1$ potentials on $\mathbb{R}$ was located in available sources; classical results give order $1/2$ growth for Jost solutions of selfadjoint Schrödinger problems on a half-line, but a definitive PT-symmetric whole-line analogue with sharp growth orders for normalized half-line solutions does not appear to be conclusively settled in the literature reviewed.

paper_title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems
original_question: Consider a weak solution u of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ with the non-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition u|∂Ω = 0. Let ω(x,t) = ∇×u(x,t) be the vorticity, and let θ(x,y,t) denote the angle between the vorticities at two points x and y at time t. In the region where |ω(x,t)| and |ω(y,t)| are both larger than a fixed positive constant K, is it sufficient for regularity that the vorticity directions satisfy the 1/2-Hölder coherence condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^(1/2) for almost every t? Is even the stronger Lipschitz coherence condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y| sufficient?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \mathbb{R}^3_+ = \{x = (x_1,x_2,x_3) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x_3 > 0\}$ be the open upper half-space, and consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes system
$$\partial_t u - \Delta u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega\times(0,T),$$
together with the no-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition $u|_{\partial\Omega} = 0$ and a divergence-free initial datum $u(\cdot,0) = u_0 \in L^2(\Omega)$. Let $u$ be a Leray–Hopf weak solution and let $\omega = \nabla\times u$ denote its vorticity. Where $\omega(x,t)\neq 0$, set the vorticity direction $\xi(x,t) = \omega(x,t)/|\omega(x,t)|$, and define $\theta(x,y,t) \in [0,\pi]$ as the angle between $\xi(x,t)$ and $\xi(y,t)$.

Fix a constant $K > 0$ and consider the set $D_K(t) = \{(x,y) \in \Omega\times\Omega : |\omega(x,t)|>K \text{ and } |\omega(y,t)|>K\}$.

(a) Suppose there exists a constant $c>0$ such that for almost every $t\in(0,T)$,
$$\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y|^{1/2} \quad \text{for all } (x,y)\in D_K(t).$$
Does this 1/2-Hölder coherence condition imply that $u$ is regular on $\Omega\times(0,T)$ (i.e., free of singularities up to the boundary)?

(b) Suppose, more strongly, that there exists $c>0$ such that for almost every $t\in(0,T)$,
$$\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y| \quad \text{for all } (x,y)\in D_K(t).$$
Does this Lipschitz coherence condition imply regularity of $u$ on $\Omega\times(0,T)$?
status_search_result: Subsequent works extended Constantin–Fefferman type vorticity-direction regularity criteria to boundary value problems for the Navier (slip) boundary condition in the half-space (e.g., Beirão da Veiga, 2012/2013, Lipschitz-continuous case). The literature explicitly notes that extension to the non-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition remains open. paper_title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems
context_brief: Best Hölder exponent for slip-boundary regularity
original_question: Consider weak solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ under the slip boundary condition u_3 = 0 and ∂u_j/∂x_3 = 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ 2. Suppose that in the region where the vorticity at both points is larger than a fixed positive constant K one has the coherence estimate sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^β, where θ(x,y,t) is the angle between the vorticities at x and y and β lies in [0, 1/2]. What is the smallest exponent β for which this geometric assumption alone, without additional hypotheses such as ω ∈ L^2(0,T;L^r), is sufficient to guarantee regularity? In particular, can the threshold be improved below β = 1/2?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u − Δu + ∇p = 0,   ∇·u = 0,
in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ = { x = (x_1,x_2,x_3) : x_3 > 0 }, on a time interval (0,T), under the slip (Navier-type) boundary conditions
  u_3(x_1,x_2,0,t) = 0,    ∂u_j/∂x_3 (x_1,x_2,0,t) = 0   for j = 1,2,
together with a smooth, divergence-free, compatible initial datum u(·,0) = u_0. Let ω = curl u denote the vorticity, and for points x,y ∈ Ω with ω(x,t) ≠ 0 and ω(y,t) ≠ 0 let θ(x,y,t) ∈ [0,π] be the angle between ω(x,t) and ω(y,t).

Fix a constant K > 0 and a constant β ∈ [0, 1/2]. Suppose u is a Leray–Hopf weak solution satisfying the geometric coherence condition: there exists c > 0 such that for almost every t ∈ (0,T) and for all x, y ∈ Ω with |ω(x,t)| > K and |ω(y,t)| > K one has
  sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c |x − y|^β.        (∗)

It is known that under the additional integrability hypothesis ω ∈ L^2(0,T; L^r(Ω)) (for an appropriate r depending on β), condition (∗) implies that u is strong, hence regular, on [0,T]; and that for β = 1/2 the additional hypothesis is superfluous, i.e. (∗) alone yields regularity.

Determine the infimum of values β ∈ [0, 1/2] for which condition (∗) by itself, with no further integrability assumption on ω, suffices to guarantee that u is regular on [0,T]. In particular, decide whether the threshold β = 1/2 can be lowered: does there exist β < 1/2 such that (∗) alone implies regularity?

paper_title: Structural Theory of Degrees of Unsolvability: Advances and Open Problems
original_question: Fix n ≥ 1 and finite posets P, Q_0, ..., Q_m such that each Q_i extends P. Is there an algorithm that, given these finite posets, determines whether every embedding f: P → D_n can be extended to an embedding g: Q_i → D_n for some index i ≤ m, where the successful index i is allowed to depend on the chosen embedding of P into D_n?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and let D_n denote the partial order of n-computably enumerable Turing degrees (so D_1 is the partial order of c.e. Turing degrees, D_2 is the partial order of d.c.e. degrees, and in general D_n is the partial order of n-c.e. degrees). For finite partially ordered sets P and Q, write P ↪ Q to indicate that P is a subposet of Q (i.e., Q extends P). 

Question: Does there exist an algorithm with the following input/output behavior?

• Input: a finite poset P, a positive integer m, and finite posets Q_0, Q_1, …, Q_m, each extending P (i.e., P ↪ Q_i for every i ≤ m).

• Output: "yes" if every order-preserving embedding f : P → D_n can be extended to an order-preserving embedding g : Q_i → D_n for some index i ≤ m (where the index i may depend on the embedding f), and "no" otherwise.

Determine whether such a decision procedure exists for each fixed n ≥ 1.
status_search_result: The recognition problem for the possibility of embedding extensions into the n-c.e. degrees is listed as an open problem in the 2015 survey on the structural theory of degrees of unsolvability. Related decidability results are known for the existential and ∀∃-theories of c.e. degrees in restricted forms, but no algorithm answering this exact extension-of-embeddings recognition question is reported in the literature found via search; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Structural Theory of Degrees of Unsolvability: Advances and Open Problems
context_brief: Two-sided strong minimal pairs of c.e. degrees
original_question: For some n > 1, or even for every n > 1, do there exist computably enumerable degrees a_0 and a_1 that form a two-sided strong minimal pair inside the n-c.e. degrees, meaning that whenever x is a nonzero n-c.e. degree with x < a_i, one has x ∪ a_{1-i} = 0'? Equivalently, in the preceding theorem, can the degree a_1 be chosen to be computably enumerable rather than merely d-c.e.?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let ω denote the natural numbers. A subset A ⊆ ω is computably enumerable (c.e.) if it is the domain of a partial computable function. For a fixed integer n ≥ 1, a set A is n-c.e. if there exists a computable function f(x,s) such that for every x, f(x,0) = 0, lim_s f(x,s) = χ_A(x), and the number of s for which f(x,s) ≠ f(x,s+1) is at most n. (Thus 1-c.e. = c.e. and 2-c.e. is also called d-c.e.) Turing reducibility ≤_T induces equivalence classes called Turing degrees; the Turing degree of a c.e. (resp. n-c.e.) set is called a c.e. degree (resp. n-c.e. degree). The least degree is 0, the join of two degrees a, b is denoted a ∪ b, and 0' denotes the degree of the halting problem.

Definition. Given an integer n > 1, a pair (a_0, a_1) of nonzero c.e. degrees is called a two-sided strong minimal pair inside the n-c.e. degrees if for each i ∈ {0,1} and every n-c.e. degree x with 0 < x < a_i one has
   x ∪ a_{1-i} = 0'.

Question. Determine whether the following holds:
(a) There exists some integer n > 1 such that there are c.e. degrees a_0, a_1 forming a two-sided strong minimal pair inside the n-c.e. degrees.
(b) For every integer n > 1, there exist c.e. degrees a_0, a_1 forming a two-sided strong minimal pair inside the n-c.e. degrees.

Equivalently, given that there are known constructions producing such pairs (a_0, a_1) where a_0 is c.e. but a_1 is only guaranteed to be d-c.e., can a_1 always be taken to be c.e.?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any paper resolving the question of whether two c.e. degrees can form a two-sided strong minimal pair inside the n-c.e. degrees for some/every n > 1. Related results concern strong minimal pairs in c.e. or enumeration degrees, but not this specific two-sided variant within the n-c.e. degrees, so the status remains unverified.

paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective algebraic surface defined over a number field k. Must there exist a proper Zariski-closed subset Z of X such that every k-rational point of X lies in Z?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a number field, and let $X$ be a smooth projective algebraic surface of general type defined over $k$ (i.e., the canonical line bundle $K_X$ is big). Denote by $X(k)$ the set of $k$-rational points of $X$.

Question: Must there exist a proper Zariski-closed subset $Z \subsetneq X$ such that $X(k) \subseteq Z$? Equivalently, is the set $X(k)$ never Zariski-dense in $X$?
status_search_result: This is the surface case of the Bombieri–Lang conjecture, posed by Bombieri in a 1980 Chicago lecture. It remains unproven in general; even for smooth projective surfaces of general type over number fields, no proof of non-Zariski-density of rational points is known. Recent work (e.g., a 2025 arXiv preprint on the geometric Bombieri–Lang) addresses geometric/function-field analogues but not the arithmetic conjecture.

paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
original_question: Does there exist a commutative ring of type 2, meaning a ring for which Büchi’s problem has a negative answer because there are nontrivial Büchi sequences of arbitrarily large finite length, but there is no infinite nontrivial Büchi sequence?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unit. A sequence $(x_n)_{n\in I}$ indexed by an interval $I\subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ of elements of $A$ is called a Büchi sequence if the second difference of the sequence of squares is the constant $2$, i.e.\ for every three consecutive indices $n-1, n, n+1 \in I$,
$$x_{n+1}^{2} - 2 x_{n}^{2} + x_{n-1}^{2} = 2.$$
A Büchi sequence is called trivial if there exist $a\in A$ and a choice of sign $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ such that $x_n = \varepsilon n + a$ for all $n\in I$ (equivalently, $x_n^{2} = (n+a)^{2}$ for all $n\in I$). Büchi's problem for $A$ asks whether there exists a positive integer $M = M(A)$ such that every Büchi sequence in $A$ of length at least $M$ is trivial.

Call a commutative ring $A$ of type 2 if Büchi's problem has a negative answer for $A$ in the following specific way:
\begin{itemize}
\item for every positive integer $N$, there exists a nontrivial Büchi sequence in $A$ of finite length at least $N$; and
\item there is no nontrivial Büchi sequence in $A$ indexed by an infinite interval.
\end{itemize}

Question: Does there exist a commutative ring of type 2?
status_search_result: The problem appears in a survey of Büchi's problem as an explicitly stated open question ("Do there exist rings of type 2?"). Subsequent literature on Büchi's problem (e.g., works on optimal bounds in modular arithmetic and for quadratic polynomials) does not record a resolution. No source identifies a ring of type 2 nor proves their nonexistence, so the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
context_brief: Passing from domains to fraction fields
original_question: Let A be an integral domain and let K be its field of fractions. Whenever Büchi’s problem has a positive answer over A, can one solve Büchi’s problem over K as well?
self_contained_problem:
Büchi's problem over a commutative ring R with unity asks for the existence of a positive integer M = M(R) with the following property: whenever x_1, x_2, ..., x_M are elements of R such that the second difference of the sequence (x_n^2)_{n=1}^M is constant and equal to 2, i.e.

  x_{n+2}^2 - 2 x_{n+1}^2 + x_n^2 = 2  for all 1 ≤ n ≤ M-2,

then there exists x ∈ R such that x_n^2 = (x + n)^2 for every n = 1, ..., M. Denote by B(R) the assertion that such an integer M exists for R.

Now let A be an integral domain and let K = Frac(A) be its field of fractions. Assuming that B(A) holds (i.e. Büchi's problem has a positive answer over A), does it follow that B(K) holds (i.e. Büchi's problem has a positive answer over K)?
status_search_result: Büchi's problem remains open in general (over Z and over many rings). The transfer question from a domain A to its fraction field K is listed as an open problem; no resolution is reported in the literature found.

paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
original_question: Fix n ≥ 2. Whenever the usual square-version of Büchi’s problem has a positive answer over a ring A, must the higher-power analogue B_n(A) also have a positive answer over A? The paper explicitly highlights polynomial rings, rational function fields, function fields, and meromorphic-function settings as the main cases of interest.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let A be a commutative ring with unit, and fix an integer n ≥ 2. For a sequence (x_0, x_1, x_2, …) of elements of A, define its first forward difference by Δ x_k = x_{k+1} − x_k and, inductively, its m-th forward difference by Δ^m x_k = Δ(Δ^{m−1} x_k). 

The classical (square) Büchi problem B(A) asks: does there exist a positive integer M = M(A) such that, whenever (x_0, …, x_{M−1}) is a sequence in A with
   Δ^2 (x_k^2) = 2   for all k = 0, …, M−3,
there must exist a, b ∈ A with x_k^2 = (a + k)^2 + b for every k? (Equivalently, the sequence of squares is forced to be the sequence of squares of consecutive elements of A, up to an additive constant.)

The higher-power Büchi problem B_n(A) is the analogous statement with squares replaced by n-th powers: does there exist M = M_n(A) such that, whenever (x_0, …, x_{M−1}) is a sequence in A with
   Δ^n (x_k^n) = n!   for all k = 0, …, M−n−1,
the sequence (x_k^n) must coincide with the sequence of n-th powers of consecutive elements of A, up to an additive constant?

Question. Fix n ≥ 2. Is it true that, whenever the square Büchi problem B(A) has a positive answer over the ring A, the higher-power Büchi problem B_n(A) also has a positive answer over A? In particular, does this implication hold in each of the following settings:
 (i) polynomial rings A = K[t] over a field K;
 (ii) rational function fields A = K(t);
 (iii) function fields of curves over a field K;
 (iv) rings of meromorphic functions over C and over C_p?
status_search_result: The implication has been established in several function-field settings: a 2011 result (Pasten–Pheidas–Vidaux) solves a generalization of Büchi's problem for any exponent n in function fields of curves of characteristic zero, providing the first instance where the higher-power problem is settled for n > 3 in rings of functions. Earlier work of Vojta, Pheidas–Vidaux, and Shlapentokh handled specific small exponents and polynomial-ring/rational-function-field cases. However, the general implication "B(A) positive ⟹ B_n(A) positive for all n" remains open in full generality, particularly for meromorphic functions over C and over C_p, which the survey identifies as the hardest cases.

paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
original_question: For every ring A such that the corresponding Büchi problem has a positive answer, does the associated representation problem C_n(A) also admit a positive answer?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unit. A sequence $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_M)$ of elements of $A$ is called a Büchi sequence if the second difference of the sequence of squares is constantly $2$, i.e., $x_{n+2}^2 - 2x_{n+1}^2 + x_n^2 = 2$ for all $n = 1, \dots, M-2$. A Büchi sequence is called trivial if there exist $a, b \in A$ such that $x_n^2 = (a+n)^2$ for all $n$. Büchi's problem for $A$ asks whether there exists a positive integer $M_0 = M_0(A)$ such that every Büchi sequence in $A$ of length at least $M_0$ is trivial.

For an integer $n \ge 2$, the associated representation problem $C_n(A)$ is the following: does there exist a positive integer $M = M(n,A)$ such that, for any $M$-tuple $(z_1, \dots, z_M) \in A^M$ for which there exist $x_1, \dots, x_M, y \in A$ satisfying
$$z_k = x_k^n + \binom{n}{2}\bigl((k-1)^{\,n-2}\,y\bigr) \quad \text{(or, more generally, the natural higher-order analogue characterizing $n$-th powers of elements in arithmetic progression up to a shift)},$$
the tuple is forced to come from $n$-th powers of $M$ consecutive elements of $A$ (the trivial solutions)?

Equivalently, $C_n(A)$ is the natural generalization of Büchi's problem to $n$-th powers, asking whether the only long enough sequences in $A$ whose $n$-th differences of $n$-th powers equal $n!$ are sequences of $n$-th powers of consecutive elements.

Question: Is it true that for every commutative ring with unit $A$ for which Büchi's problem (the case $n=2$) has a positive answer, the representation problem $C_n(A)$ also has a positive answer for every $n \ge 2$?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the survey on Büchi's problem. Subsequent work has addressed Büchi's $n$-th power problem in particular settings (polynomial rings, meromorphic and algebraic functions, modular arithmetic), but no general result is known asserting that a positive answer for the quadratic Büchi problem over a ring $A$ implies a positive answer for $C_n(A)$ for all $n$. No source found indicates a resolution of this implication in general.

paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
original_question: Whenever Büchi’s problem has a positive answer over a ring A, what is the optimal bound M such that every Büchi sequence over A of length at least M must be trivial?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a commutative ring (with 1). A Büchi sequence over A is a sequence (x_1, x_2, ..., x_N) of elements of A whose squares have constant second difference equal to 2, i.e.

   x_{n+2}^2 - 2 x_{n+1}^2 + x_n^2 = 2   for all 1 ≤ n ≤ N-2.

Such a sequence is called trivial if there exists a ∈ A and ε ∈ {-1, +1} (or, more generally, a square root of 1 in A) such that x_n = ε(a + n) for all n.

Büchi's problem over A, denoted B(A), asks: does there exist a positive integer M = M(A) such that every Büchi sequence over A of length at least M is trivial?

Problem. Suppose B(A) has a positive answer. Determine the optimal (smallest) such bound M = M(A), as a function of the ring A, for which every Büchi sequence over A of length at least M is necessarily trivial.

In particular, settle the case A = Z: assuming that every sufficiently long Büchi sequence of integers is of the form (±(a+1), ±(a+2), ...), find the smallest integer M with this property.
status_search_result: For A = Z the question is widely open: it is not even known unconditionally that B(Z) has a positive answer, and no nontrivial Büchi sequence of length 5 is known, while Hensley (1983) constructed infinitely many nontrivial sequences of length 4, suggesting M(Z) = 5 conjecturally. Optimal bounds have been established in special settings (e.g., modular arithmetic mod p^s for p ≥ 5, and for arbitrary quadratic polynomials over Z/p^sZ), but the general problem of determining the optimal M(A) for every ring A where B(A) holds remains open.

paper_title: Evolutionary dynamics of cancer: From epigenetic regulation to cell population dynamics—mathematical model framework, applications, and open problems
context_brief: Entropy production and dissipation in heterogeneous cancer dynamics
original_question: For the same non-delay model, let Q(t)=∫_Ω Q(t,x)dx be the total cell number, let f(t,x)=Q(t,x)/Q(t) be the fraction of cells with epigenetic state x, and define the multicellular entropy by E(t)=-∫_Ω f(t,x) log f(t,x)dx. Determine how to decompose the entropy derivative dE/dt into an entropy production rate epr and an entropy dissipation rate edr such that dE/dt=epr-edr and both epr and edr are always nonnegative, and characterize under what conditions the developmental dynamics described by the model—especially cancer development—produce increasing entropy.
self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^n be a bounded domain representing the space of epigenetic states of cells. Consider a heterogeneous cell population whose density Q(t,x) ≥ 0 (number of cells per unit epigenetic state at time t) evolves according to the integro-differential dynamics

  ∂_t Q(t,x) = β(x) ∫_Ω p(y,x) Q(t,y) dy − (β(x) + d(x)) Q(t,x),   t > 0, x ∈ Ω,

with prescribed nonnegative birth rate β(x), death rate d(x), and inheritance kernel p(y,x) ≥ 0 satisfying ∫_Ω p(y,x) dx = 1 for every y ∈ Ω (so that p(y,·) is the probability density of the epigenetic state of a daughter cell given that of its mother y). Let

  Q(t) = ∫_Ω Q(t,x) dx,    f(t,x) = Q(t,x)/Q(t),    E(t) = − ∫_Ω f(t,x) log f(t,x) dx

denote the total cell number, the population fraction at epigenetic state x, and the multicellular (Shannon) entropy of the population, respectively.

(a) Find an explicit decomposition

  dE/dt = epr(t) − edr(t)

of the time derivative of E(t) into an "entropy production rate" epr(t) and an "entropy dissipation rate" edr(t), expressed in terms of Q, f, β, d, and p, such that epr(t) ≥ 0 and edr(t) ≥ 0 hold for all t > 0 and all admissible initial data.

(b) Characterize the conditions on β, d, and p (and on the initial distribution f(0,·)) under which the developmental dynamics yield monotonically increasing entropy E(t), i.e. dE/dt ≥ 0 for all t > 0.
category_tag: entropy production in cell population dynamics
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open question in the cancer evolutionary dynamics literature: a general definition of nonnegative entropy production and dissipation rates for such heterogeneous cell-population models, and conditions under which the entropy is increasing, is stated to be unknown. No subsequent work establishing such a general decomposition for this model class was located.
