paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
original_question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space that is boundedly distortable, meaning distortable for some λ > 1 but not arbitrarily distortable for all λ > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. For $\lambda > 1$, the space $X$ is called $\lambda$-distortable if there exists an equivalent norm $|\cdot|$ on $X$ such that for every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $Y \subseteq X$,
$$\sup\left\{\frac{|y|}{|z|} : y, z \in Y,\ \|y\| = \|z\| = 1\right\} \geq \lambda.$$
The space $X$ is said to be distortable if it is $\lambda$-distortable for some $\lambda > 1$, and arbitrarily distortable if it is $\lambda$-distortable for every $\lambda > 1$. A distortable Banach space that is not arbitrarily distortable is called boundedly distortable.

Question: Does there exist a boundedly distortable infinite-dimensional Banach space?
status_search_result: The existence of a boundedly distortable Banach space remains a well-known open problem in Banach space theory. Tsirelson's space is a long-standing candidate (known to be (2−ε)-distortable for all ε > 0), but it is not known whether it is arbitrarily distortable. Recent surveys and papers (2019, 2023) on distortion in Banach spaces still list this question as open.

paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
original_question: Let X be a separable Banach space such that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of X. Must X contain a copy of c_0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real sequences converging to zero, equipped with the supremum norm. A map $f:(M,d_M)\to(N,d_N)$ between metric spaces is a Lipschitz isomorphism onto its image if there exist constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ such that $a\,d_M(x,y)\le d_N(f(x),f(y))\le b\,d_M(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in M$. By Aharoni's theorem, every separable metric space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of $c_0$.

Suppose $X$ is a separable Banach space with the following universality property: every separable Banach space $Y$ is Lipschitz isomorphic to some subset of $X$. Must $X$ contain a closed linear subspace isomorphic to $c_0$?

Partial results exist (e.g., subspaces of $c_0$ are stable under Lipschitz isomorphism, and any Banach space Lipschitz isomorphic to $c_0$ is linearly isomorphic to it), but the general question remains unresolved.

original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over the real or complex field. A quotient of X is a Banach space of the form X/M, where M is a closed linear subspace of X, equipped with the canonical quotient norm. Such a quotient is called non-trivial and infinite-dimensional separable if X/M is infinite-dimensional, separable (i.e., contains a countable dense subset), and not isomorphic to a finite-dimensional space.

Question: Must every infinite-dimensional Banach space X admit a closed subspace M ⊂ X such that the quotient X/M is infinite-dimensional and separable?

paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
original_question: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy, namely that for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of some set S, either there is an uncountable set T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or S can be decomposed into countably many pieces with no infinite subset in I. Under this assumption, are the following equivalent: (1) every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system; and (2) b = ℵ_2, where b is the minimum cardinality of an unbounded family in N^N under eventual domination?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A family $\mathcal I$ of countable subsets of a set $S$ is called a P-ideal if $\mathcal I$ is closed under finite unions, hereditary (closed under taking subsets), and $\sigma$-directed modulo finite (for every sequence $\{A_n\}_{n\in\omega}\subseteq\mathcal I$ there exists $A\in\mathcal I$ with $A_n\setminus A$ finite for every $n$). The P-ideal Dichotomy (PID) is the assertion that for every set $S$ and every P-ideal $\mathcal I$ of countable subsets of $S$, at least one of the following holds:
(a) there exists an uncountable $T\subseteq S$ such that every countable subset of $T$ belongs to $\mathcal I$;
(b) $S$ can be written as a countable union $S=\bigcup_{n\in\omega} S_n$ such that no $S_n$ contains an infinite subset belonging to $\mathcal I$.

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number, i.e. the least cardinality of a family $\mathcal F\subseteq \mathbb N^{\mathbb N}$ that is unbounded under eventual domination $\le^*$ (where $f\le^* g$ means $f(n)\le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$).

A biorthogonal system in a Banach space $X$ is a family $\{(x_\alpha,x_\alpha^*)\}_{\alpha\in\Gamma}\subseteq X\times X^*$ such that $x_\alpha^*(x_\beta)=\delta_{\alpha\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Gamma$.

Problem. Assume PID. Are the following two statements equivalent?
(1) Every non-separable Banach space admits an uncountable biorthogonal system.
(2) $\mathfrak{b}=\aleph_2$.
status_search_result: Brech and Todorcevic established under PID that the equivalence with $\mathfrak{b}=\aleph_2$ holds when "non-separable Banach space" is restricted to non-separable Asplund spaces; more generally, under PID, every non-separable Banach space of density strictly smaller than $\mathfrak{b}$ with weak*-sequentially compact dual ball admits an uncountable biorthogonal system. The full equivalence for arbitrary non-separable Banach spaces does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
original_question: Does every Banach space of density strictly greater than ℵ_1 have a support set?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. The density of $X$, denoted $\mathrm{dens}(X)$, is the least cardinality of a norm-dense subset of $X$. A subset $S \subseteq X$ is called a support set if $S$ is convex and every point of $S$ is a support point of $S$ — that is, for every $x \in S$ there exists a continuous linear functional $f \in X^*$ with $f \neq 0$ on $S$ such that $f(x) = \inf_{y \in S} f(y)$ (equivalently, $S$ has a supporting hyperplane through $x$).

Question: Does every Banach space $X$ with $\mathrm{dens}(X) > \aleph_1$ contain a support set?

Ann. 2006) a generic Banach space $C(K)$ of density $\aleph_1$ with no support set, motivating the question for densities above $\aleph_1$. A targeted web search did not return a published resolution of the question for densities strictly greater than $\aleph_1$; the problem appears to still be open, but no definitive recent statement was found, so the status is recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
original_question: Does every Banach space of density greater than c, and does every reflexive Banach space of density greater than ℵ_1, contain an infinite sub-symmetric basic sequence?
self_contained_problem:
A Schauder basic sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in a Banach space is called sub-symmetric if it is unconditional and equivalent to each of its infinite subsequences; equivalently, there is a constant $C\ge 1$ such that for every strictly increasing sequence $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ of positive integers, every choice of signs $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,+1\}$, and every finitely supported sequence of scalars $(a_i)$, 
$$C^{-1}\Big\|\sum_i a_i x_i\Big\|\le \Big\|\sum_i \varepsilon_i a_i x_{n_i}\Big\|\le C\Big\|\sum_i a_i x_i\Big\|.$$
The density of a Banach space $X$ is the smallest cardinality of a norm-dense subset of $X$. Let $\mathfrak c=2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the cardinality of the continuum and $\aleph_1$ the first uncountable cardinal.

(a) Does every Banach space whose density is strictly greater than $\mathfrak c$ contain an infinite sub-symmetric basic sequence?

(b) Does every reflexive Banach space whose density is strictly greater than $\aleph_1$ contain an infinite sub-symmetric basic sequence?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of either part of this problem on the existence of infinite sub-symmetric basic sequences in Banach spaces of large density. The problem appears in lists of open problems in Banach space Ramsey theory, but no published solution was located that confirms or refutes either statement, so the current status is unclear.

paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
original_question: Is there a compact hereditary family F of finite subsets of ω_1 that contains every singleton and has the property that every finite subset of ω_1 contains a member of F of at least half its size?
self_contained_problem:
A family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite subsets of $\omega_1$ is called:
- hereditary if $A \in \mathcal{F}$ and $B \subseteq A$ imply $B \in \mathcal{F}$;
- compact if, viewed as a subset of $2^{\omega_1}$ via characteristic functions, $\mathcal{F}$ is closed in the product topology (equivalently, every sequence of members of $\mathcal{F}$ has a pointwise-convergent subsequence whose limit is the characteristic function of an element of $\mathcal{F}$).

Question: Does there exist a compact hereditary family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite subsets of $\omega_1$ such that
1. $\{\alpha\} \in \mathcal{F}$ for every $\alpha \in \omega_1$, and
2. for every finite set $S \subseteq \omega_1$ there exists $T \in \mathcal{F}$ with $T \subseteq S$ and $|T| \geq |S|/2$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of this question. It appears in Fremlin's well-known problem list and in surveys of open problems connecting Banach space theory and Ramsey theory on ω₁, but no source found confirms a positive or negative solution. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: If an F-division algebra has prime period, must it be a crossed product? In other words, for each prime p, is every central division algebra whose Brauer class has order p necessarily obtained from a Galois crossed-product construction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $D$ be a central division algebra over $F$, i.e., a finite-dimensional associative $F$-algebra with center exactly $F$ in which every nonzero element is invertible. The period (or exponent) of $D$ is the order of its class $[D]$ in the Brauer group $\mathrm{Br}(F)$. The algebra $D$ is called a crossed product if it contains a maximal subfield $K \subset D$ such that $K/F$ is a Galois extension; equivalently, $D \cong (K/F, G, c)$ for some Galois group $G = \mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$ and some 2-cocycle $c \in Z^2(G, K^\times)$.

Question: For every prime number $p$, every field $F$, and every central $F$-division algebra $D$ whose period in $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ equals $p$, must $D$ be a crossed product?
category_tag: Central simple algebras and crossed products
status_search_result: The problem of whether central division algebras of prime period must be crossed products is widely regarded as open. While Amitsur (1972) constructed noncrossed products in general, no noncrossed product of prime period (or prime degree, for odd primes) is known, and no proof that such algebras are always crossed products exists. Recent literature (e.g., work on noncyclic division algebras of prime degree) continues to treat this as an outstanding open question.

original_question: If a field F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every central simple F-algebra a crossed product?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field. Recall that the cohomological dimension of $F$, denoted $\mathrm{cd}(F)$, is the supremum of integers $n$ such that there exists a torsion Galois module $M$ over $F$ with $H^n(\mathrm{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{sep}}/F), M) \neq 0$. A central simple $F$-algebra $A$ is said to be a crossed product if it contains a maximal subfield $K$ that is Galois over $F$; equivalently, $A \cong (K/F, G, c)$ for some finite Galois extension $K/F$ with Galois group $G = \mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$ of order $[A:F]^{1/2}$ and some 2-cocycle $c \in Z^2(G, K^\times)$.

Question: If $F$ is a field with $\mathrm{cd}(F) \le 2$, is every central simple $F$-algebra a crossed product?

status_search_result: The question appears in published surveys of open problems on central simple algebras and is generally regarded as open. All known examples of non-crossed-product central simple algebras (going back to Amitsur) are constructed over fields whose cohomological dimension is at least 3, and no counterexample is known over fields of cohomological dimension at most 2; conversely, no general proof that every central simple algebra over such a field is a crossed product has been obtained.

original_question: For a field F and positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) generated by Brauer classes of cyclic algebras of degree dividing n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and $n$ a positive integer. Recall that the Brauer group $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ is the group of equivalence classes of finite-dimensional central simple $F$-algebras under tensor product, where two such algebras are equivalent if they have isomorphic matrix algebras over a common division algebra. Let ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F) = \{[A] \in \mathrm{Br}(F) : n \cdot [A] = 0\}$ denote the $n$-torsion subgroup.

A central simple $F$-algebra $A$ of degree $m$ (i.e., $\dim_F A = m^2$) is called cyclic if it contains a maximal commutative subfield $L \subset A$ such that $L/F$ is a cyclic Galois extension of degree $m$. Equivalently, $A \cong (L/F,\sigma,a)$ for some generator $\sigma$ of $\mathrm{Gal}(L/F)$ and some $a \in F^\times$.

Question: Is ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F)$ generated, as an abelian group, by the Brauer classes of cyclic $F$-algebras of degree dividing $n$? Equivalently, can every $n$-torsion Brauer class over $F$ be written as a sum of classes of cyclic algebras of degree dividing $n$?
status_search_result: The question, going back to Albert (1936), is classical. By the Merkurjev–Suslin theorem, if $F$ contains a primitive $n$th root of unity then ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F)$ is generated by cyclic (symbol) algebras of degree $n$. Without this hypothesis, the problem remains open in general; positive results are known in special cases (e.g., small $n$, particular classes of fields such as global/local fields), but no general answer is known.

original_question: For primes p >= 3, can one prove a finite upper bound for the symbol lengths l_F(p, p^2) and l_F(p^2, p^2)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $p \ge 3$ be a prime. Assume that $F$ contains a primitive $p^2$-th root of unity. Recall that for positive integers $e$ and $i$ with $e \mid i$, a central simple $F$-algebra is said to have exponent $e$ if its class in the Brauer group $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ has order $e$, and to have index $i$ if its underlying division algebra has degree $i$ over its center. A symbol algebra of degree $n$ over $F$ is a cyclic $F$-algebra of the form
$$ (a, b)_{n, \zeta_n} = F\langle x, y \mid x^n = a,\ y^n = b,\ yx = \zeta_n xy\rangle, \qquad a, b \in F^\times,$$
where $\zeta_n$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unity in $F$. By the Merkurjev–Suslin theorem, every central simple $F$-algebra of exponent dividing $n$ is Brauer-equivalent to a tensor product of finitely many symbol algebras of degree $n$.

Define the symbol length
$$ \ell_F(e, i) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \cup \{\infty\} $$
to be the least integer $\ell$ such that every central simple $F$-algebra of exponent dividing $e$ and index dividing $i$ is Brauer-equivalent to a tensor product of at most $\ell$ symbol algebras of degree $i$ over $F$; set $\ell_F(e, i) = \infty$ if no such finite $\ell$ exists.

Question: Does there exist a finite upper bound, depending only on $p$ (and not on the field $F$), for $\ell_F(p, p^2)$ and for $\ell_F(p^2, p^2)$, valid for every field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ containing a primitive $p^2$-th root of unity?

original_question: What structural consequences for central simple algebras can be deduced from bounds on essential dimension or essential p-dimension? In particular, can one bound ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), compute ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and determine whether equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) forces every degree-n algebra over every field extension of F to be a crossed product?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and $n \geq 2$ an integer. For a covariant functor $\mathcal{F}: \mathrm{Fields}/F \to \mathrm{Sets}$, the essential dimension $\mathrm{ed}(\mathcal{F})$ is defined as the smallest integer $d \geq 0$ such that for every field extension $K/F$ and every $\alpha \in \mathcal{F}(K)$, there exists a subextension $F \subseteq K_0 \subseteq K$ with $\mathrm{trdeg}_F(K_0) \leq d$ and an element $\alpha_0 \in \mathcal{F}(K_0)$ mapping to $\alpha$. For a smooth algebraic group $H$ over $F$, $\mathrm{ed}(H) := \mathrm{ed}(H^1(-,H))$.

Define the following functors on field extensions $K/F$:
- $\mathrm{Alg}_n(K)$ = isomorphism classes of central simple $K$-algebras of degree $n$ (so $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_n) = \mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{PGL}_n)$);
- $\mathrm{CPAlg}_n(K)$ = isomorphism classes of central simple $K$-algebras of degree $n$ that are crossed products (i.e., contain a strictly maximal Galois subfield);
- For a finite group $G$ of order $n$, $\mathrm{Alg}_G(K)$ = isomorphism classes of $G$-crossed product central simple $K$-algebras of degree $n$.

Address the following:
(1) Provide upper and lower bounds for $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{CPAlg}_n)$ and for $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_G)$ as functions of $n$ and $G$.
(2) Compute the difference $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_G) - \mathrm{ed}(G)$.
(3) Suppose that $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{CPAlg}_n) = \mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{PGL}_n)$. Does it follow that every central simple algebra of degree $n$ over every field extension of $F$ is a crossed product?

Analogous questions are posed for the essential $p$-dimension $\mathrm{ed}_p$ in place of $\mathrm{ed}$.
category_tag: Essential dimension of central simple algebras
status_search_result: The problem appears largely open. While partial results are known—such as Merkurjev's computation of the essential $p$-dimension of $\mathrm{PGL}_{p^2}$ (equal to $p^2+1$) and various upper bounds for $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{PGL}_n)$—no complete bounds for $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{CPAlg}_n)$ and $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_G)$ in general are available, the difference $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_G) - \mathrm{ed}(G)$ has not been computed in general, and the implication from equality $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{CPAlg}_n) = \mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{PGL}_n)$ to every degree-$n$ algebra being a crossed product is not established.

original_question: If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal or symplectic involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to every odd-degree field extension of F?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over $F$. Recall that an $F$-linear involution $\sigma\colon A\to A$ (i.e., an anti-automorphism of order $2$ fixing $F$) is said to be of orthogonal or symplectic type according to the conjugacy class of its restriction over an algebraic closure. The involution $\sigma$ is called isotropic if there exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ with $\sigma(a)a=0$ that lies in a nonzero right ideal $I\subseteq A$ satisfying $\sigma(I)\cdot I=0$; otherwise $\sigma$ is called anisotropic. For a field extension $L/F$, let $\sigma_L$ denote the involution on $A_L=A\otimes_F L$ obtained by extending scalars.

Question: Suppose $\sigma$ is an anisotropic involution of orthogonal or symplectic type on $A$. Must $\sigma_L$ be anisotropic for every finite field extension $L/F$ of odd degree?
status_search_result: The problem (a Springer-type question for involutions) is known in several cases but remains open in general. Positive answers have been established for hermitian forms over quaternion algebras with involutions of the first kind (including in characteristic two), and equivalences with other major conjectures (e.g., preservation of anisotropy under generic splitting fields, due to Karpenko, Tignol, and Karpenko–Zhykhovich) have been proved. No general resolution for arbitrary central simple algebras with orthogonal or symplectic involutions appears in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Let G be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Does G remain anisotropic over every finite extension K/F whose degree is not divisible by any prime in the set S(G) of homological torsion primes of G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $G$ be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group defined over $F$ (i.e. a connected linear algebraic $F$-group such that, after base change to an algebraic closure of $F$, the group becomes a simple algebraic group, with no nontrivial connected normal subgroups). Recall that $G$ is called anisotropic over $F$ if $G$ contains no nontrivial $F$-split torus, equivalently the $F$-rank of $G$ is zero.

To $G$ one associates a finite set $S(G)$ of "torsion primes" (the homological/cohomological torsion primes of $G$): these are the primes appearing in the torsion of the integral cohomology of a compact form of $G$, and they depend only on the Killing–Cartan type of $G$. Explicitly, the torsion primes are: $\{2\}$ for type $B_n,C_n,D_n$ ($n\ge 2$), $G_2$; $\{2,3\}$ for types $D_n$ ($n\ge 4$ in some conventions), $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$; and $\{2,3,5\}$ for $E_8$; together with primes dividing the order of the fundamental group when $G$ is not simply connected/adjoint as appropriate.

Question: Suppose $G$ is anisotropic over $F$. Is it true that for every finite field extension $K/F$ whose degree $[K:F]$ is not divisible by any prime in $S(G)$, the group $G$ remains anisotropic over $K$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution (positive or negative) of this question on prime-avoiding extensions and anisotropy of absolutely almost simple groups. Related results on torsion primes and behavior of anisotropic groups under field extensions exist (Chernousov, Merkurjev, Gille and others), but no source verifying this specific question as solved was located, so the status is reported as unknown.

original_question: Is there a structural criterion that decides when the tensor product A tensor_F B of two F-division algebras contains a zero divisor, equivalently when it fails to remain a division algebra?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ and $B$ be associative division algebras over $F$ (so $F$ is contained in the center of each). Form the tensor product $A \otimes_F B$ as an $F$-algebra.

Provide a structural criterion, in terms of intrinsic invariants of $A$ and $B$ (such as their centers, maximal subfields, Brauer classes, splitting fields, or other algebraic data), that decides exactly when $A \otimes_F B$ contains a nonzero zero divisor — equivalently, when $A \otimes_F B$ fails to be a division algebra.
status_search_result: The problem of finding a structural criterion for when the tensor product of two F-division algebras has zero divisors remains open in general. While specific cases have been resolved—e.g., Rowen and Saltman constructed examples of finite-dimensional division algebras over a common algebraically closed subfield whose tensor product has zero divisors, refuting one form of the question—a general structural criterion characterizing this phenomenon has not been established. Subsequent work (e.g., on tensor products of division algebras and fields) continues to study related Brauer-group and Picard-group invariants without yielding a complete criterion.

context_brief: Common splitting fields in tensor-product collapse
original_question: If ind(A tensor_F B) is strictly smaller than ind(A) ind(B), what common splitting fields can the division algebras A and B have?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ and $B$ be finite-dimensional central division algebras over $F$. For a central simple $F$-algebra $C$, denote by $\mathrm{ind}(C)$ its Schur index, i.e., the degree of the central division $F$-algebra Brauer-equivalent to $C$. A field extension $L/F$ is called a splitting field of a central simple $F$-algebra $C$ if $C \otimes_F L$ is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over $L$; a common splitting field of $A$ and $B$ is an extension $L/F$ that splits both $A$ and $B$.

Suppose that 
$$\mathrm{ind}(A \otimes_F B) < \mathrm{ind}(A)\,\mathrm{ind}(B).$$
Characterize, as completely as possible, the field extensions $L/F$ that can arise as common splitting fields of $A$ and $B$ under this hypothesis. In particular, determine what constraints (e.g., on the degree, structure, or existence of subfields of given degree) the strict inequality forces on common splitting fields of $A$ and $B$, generalizing the classical fact that when the tensor product of two quaternion division algebras is not a division algebra, the two algebras share a common quadratic splitting field.
category_tag: central simple algebras and Brauer group
status_search_result: The problem of describing common splitting fields of two central division algebras whose tensor product has index strictly less than the product of indices appears to remain open in general. Partial results exist: the classical case of two quaternion algebras (where a common quadratic splitting field exists) is known, and recent work (e.g., Florence; Chapman and others on symbol algebras; the 2013 paper "Tensor products of division algebras and fields") provides further partial results in special cases such as symbol algebras and certain prime-degree settings, but no complete characterization is reported.

original_question: If two division algebras have the same splitting fields inside a specified class of field extensions, for example finite extensions or extensions of transcendence degree at most one, must they generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group?
self_contained_problem:
Let K be a field and let Br(K) denote its Brauer group. For a central simple K-algebra A, a field extension L/K is called a splitting field of A if A⊗_K L is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over L. Fix a class C of field extensions of K (for example, the class of finite-dimensional extensions of K, or the class of extensions of transcendence degree at most one over K).

Suppose D₁ and D₂ are finite-dimensional central division algebras over K with the property that, for every L/K in the class C, L splits D₁ if and only if L splits D₂. Determine whether [D₁] and [D₂] must generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(K); that is, whether ⟨[D₁]⟩ = ⟨[D₂]⟩ in Br(K).
status_search_result: The question (a "genus"-type problem for division algebras restricted to a class of splitting fields) appears to remain open in general. Recent work, including a 2024 preprint constructing infinite families of division algebras sharing all finite splitting fields and all splitting fields of transcendence degree at most one, indicates that the answer can fail in some settings, but the precise question of whether shared splitting fields in such restricted classes force the algebras to generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group is not fully resolved; in particular the quaternion case over finitely generated fields remains open.

original_question: If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, must any two quaternion division algebras over F that have the same finite splitting fields, or even just the same maximal subfields, already be isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field that is either finitely generated over its prime field or finitely generated over an algebraically closed field. A quaternion algebra over $F$ is a $4$-dimensional central simple $F$-algebra; it is a division algebra if it has no nonzero zero-divisors. A field extension $L/F$ is called a splitting field of a quaternion division $F$-algebra $D$ if $D \otimes_F L \cong M_2(L)$. A maximal subfield of $D$ is a subfield $K \subseteq D$ containing $F$ that is maximal among commutative subfields (equivalently, a quadratic extension of $F$ embedding into $D$).

Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be two quaternion division algebras over $F$. Suppose that $D_1$ and $D_2$ have the same set of finite splitting fields (i.e., for every finite extension $L/F$, $L$ splits $D_1$ if and only if $L$ splits $D_2$); or, more strongly, suppose merely that $D_1$ and $D_2$ have the same set of (isomorphism classes of) maximal subfields.

Must $D_1$ and $D_2$ be isomorphic as $F$-algebras?
status_search_result: The question, posed by Prasad and Rapinchuk, remains open in general. Significant partial results are known: Garibaldi and Saltman proved an affirmative answer when $F$ is an extension of a global field $K$ such that $F/K$ is unirational with trivial unramified Brauer group, and Krashen–McKinnie and others have established related cases. Counterexamples exist for very large (non-finitely-generated) fields, but for the finitely generated setting in the problem the question is still considered open.

original_question: For a given field F, which finite groups G are F-admissible, meaning that there exists a G-crossed-product F-division algebra?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field. A finite group $G$ is called $F$-admissible if there exists a central division algebra $D$ over $F$ that is a $G$-crossed product; equivalently, $D$ contains a maximal subfield $L$ such that $L/F$ is a Galois extension with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/F) \cong G$.

Problem: For an arbitrary field $F$, determine (characterize intrinsically) the class of finite groups $G$ that are $F$-admissible. In particular, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a finite group $G$ for it to be realizable as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some finite-dimensional central division algebra over $F$.
category_tag: Admissible groups and crossed product division algebras
status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing $F$-admissible groups remains open. Schacher (1968) proved that every $\mathbb{Q}$-admissible group has metacyclic Sylow subgroups, and the converse — the $\mathbb{Q}$-admissibility conjecture — is still open in general, though many partial results exist (e.g. for solvable groups by Sonn, and recent work on number fields including the 2024 preprint "Admissible groups over number fields"). No complete characterization is known for arbitrary $F$.

original_question: If SK_1(A tensor_F L) vanishes for every field extension L/F, must the index of the central simple algebra A be square-free?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ be a central simple $F$-algebra. Recall that $A \cong M_n(D)$ for a unique (up to isomorphism) central division $F$-algebra $D$, and the index of $A$ is $\mathrm{ind}(A) = \deg(D) = \sqrt{\dim_F D}$. For any field extension $L/F$, set $A_L = A \otimes_F L$, and let $\mathrm{SK}_1(A_L) = \mathrm{SL}_1(A_L)/[A_L^\times, A_L^\times]$ denote the reduced Whitehead group, where $\mathrm{SL}_1(A_L)$ is the group of elements of $A_L^\times$ of reduced norm $1$.

Prove or disprove: if $\mathrm{SK}_1(A \otimes_F L) = 0$ for every field extension $L/F$, then $\mathrm{ind}(A)$ is square-free (i.e., not divisible by $p^2$ for any prime $p$).
category_tag: Reduced Whitehead group SK_1 of central simple algebras
status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Suslin) remains open in general. It is equivalent to showing that whenever $\mathrm{ind}(A)$ is not square-free, $\mathrm{SK}_1(A_L) \ne 0$ for some extension $L/F$. Merkurjev established the case where the index is divisible by $4$, and further partial results exist for certain primes, but a complete resolution is not known.

paper_title: Open problems in hot QCD
context_brief: Systematic treatment of multi-loop thermal sum-integrals
original_question: Can one develop a systematic, preferably computer-algebraic, method for evaluating the multi-loop thermal sum-integrals that arise in perturbative finite-temperature QCD and related finite-temperature field theories, instead of continuing to solve the needed master sum-integrals one case at a time? Such a method would need to work in the presence of discretized Matsubara frequencies and the additional temperature scale, reuse more of the analytic machinery that is successful at zero temperature than integration-by-parts relations alone, and provide a reusable way to separate ultraviolet and infrared divergent pieces so that higher-order perturbative computations can be streamlined.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic, preferably computer-algebraic, method for evaluating multi-loop thermal sum-integrals of the form
\[
\sumint_{P_1,\dots,P_L} f(P_1,\dots,P_L),\qquad \sumint_P \equiv T\sum_{p_0\in 2\pi T\,\mathbb{Z}\,\text{or}\,(2\mathbb{Z}+1)\pi T}\int\!\frac{d^{d}\mathbf p}{(2\pi)^d},
\]
that arise in perturbative finite-temperature quantum field theory (in particular hot QCD), where each loop momentum carries a discrete bosonic or fermionic Matsubara frequency $p_0$ and a continuous spatial momentum $\mathbf p$ in $d=3-2\epsilon$ dimensions, and the temperature $T$ provides an additional scale relative to vacuum integrals.

The method should:

1. Apply uniformly to entire classes of master sum-integrals (vacuum and with external Matsubara/spatial momenta) at three loops and beyond, rather than addressing them case by case.

2. Beyond integration-by-parts (IBP) identities and a Laporta-type reduction adapted to the broken Lorentz symmetry of the thermal setting, incorporate further analytic machinery known to be effective at zero temperature (e.g., differential equations, Mellin–Barnes representations, dimensional shift relations, hypergeometric/symbolic summation techniques) in a way that respects the discreteness of $p_0$.

3. Provide a reusable, ideally automated, prescription for separating ultraviolet and infrared divergent contributions of each sum-integral, so that the divergent parts are matched against effective-theory (e.g., dimensionally reduced) counterparts and the finite parts are isolated for numerical or analytic evaluation.

Question: Can such a systematic, automatable framework be constructed, in a form that streamlines higher-order perturbative computations at finite temperature?
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: IBP/Laporta-type reductions adapted to Matsubara sums, tensor reduction via dimensional shifts, and partial automation (e.g., "Automated computation meets hot QCD", PoS LL2012; recent 3-loop dimensional reduction work, 2024-2025) have enabled new higher-order thermal QCD results. However, no fully general computer-algebraic framework with automated UV/IR subtraction for all multi-loop master sum-integrals exists; master sum-integrals beyond two loops are still tackled in part case by case. The problem is therefore partially solved and remains an active area of research.

original_question: For an open dynamical system with a hole H ⊂ Ω, survival probability P(t), escape rate γ = - lim_{t→∞} (1/t) ln P(t), and natural invariant measure ν on the repeller, for which classes of maps and flows does the escape-rate formula γ = ∑_{i:λ_i>0} λ_i - h_KS remain valid, where the sum runs over positive Lyapunov exponents and h_KS is the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy computed with respect to ν?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, T)$ be a discrete-time dynamical system (or, alternatively, a smooth flow) on a Riemannian manifold $\Omega$, and let $H \subset \Omega$ be a measurable subset (the "hole"). Define the survival set up to time $t$ as the set of points whose orbit up to time $t$ never enters $H$, and let $P(t)$ denote the Lebesgue (or a fixed reference) measure of this set, called the survival probability. Define the escape rate by
$$\gamma = -\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{t}\ln P(t),$$
assuming the limit exists. Suppose there exists a natural conditionally invariant probability measure $\nu$ supported on the repeller (the set of points that never escape under either forward or backward iteration). Let $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $T$ with respect to $\nu$, and let $h_{KS}(\nu)$ denote the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$ with respect to $\nu$.

Determine the broadest classes of maps and flows (in particular beyond the uniformly hyperbolic setting, including non-uniformly hyperbolic maps and continuous-time flows) for which the escape rate formula
$$\gamma = \sum_{i:\, \lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i - h_{KS}(\nu)$$
holds. Specifically, identify hypotheses on $T$, $H$, and $\nu$ under which this identity remains valid.
category_tag: escape rate formula in open dynamical systems
status_search_result: The escape rate formula is classical for uniformly hyperbolic open systems and has been extended in special non-uniformly hyperbolic cases, but a general characterization across non-uniformly hyperbolic maps and flows has not been established. Surveys on non-uniform hyperbolicity list related questions (e.g., Eckmann–Ruelle-type conjectures) as still open in full generality, supporting the view that the question of how general the escape rate formula is remains open.

original_question: Does every triangular billiard, or more generally every polygonal billiard, contain at least one periodic orbit?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygon (a compact, simply connected planar region whose boundary is a finite union of line segments). The billiard flow on $P$ is the dynamical system describing a point particle moving with unit speed in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting off the boundary $\partial P$ according to the law of equal angles (with reflections at vertices left undefined). A billiard trajectory is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections at smooth boundary points, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial direction.

Question: Does every polygonal billiard table $P$ admit at least one periodic billiard trajectory? In particular, does every triangle $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ admit a periodic billiard trajectory?
status_search_result: The problem is a well-known long-standing open question. Periodic orbits are known to exist for all rational polygons, all acute and right triangles, and (by computer-assisted work of R. E. Schwartz) for all triangles whose angles are at most 100 degrees. The general case for arbitrary obtuse triangles and arbitrary (irrational) polygons remains open.

original_question: For stadium-like billiards that contain marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one comprehensively characterize their dynamical and escape properties in terms of the reinjection dynamics of trajectories that leave and later return to the neighborhood of those periodic orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a planar billiard table whose boundary is piecewise smooth (a "stadium-like" table), and consider the billiard flow inside $Q$ (free motion along straight lines with elastic reflection on $\partial Q$). Suppose that $Q$ admits a one-parameter family $\mathcal{F}$ of marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs): periodic trajectories whose linearized Poincaré map has eigenvalues equal to $1$ but which are not Lyapunov stable, so that nearby trajectories escape from a neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal{F}$ in phase space at a polynomial (rather than exponential) rate. Let $T_U$ denote the first-return time to $U$ for trajectories that leave $U$ and later return, and let $\Phi:\partial U\to\partial U$ denote the induced reinjection map describing the angle and position with which exiting trajectories return to $U$. The classical example is the Bunimovich stadium, where trajectories leaving the "bouncing-ball" region are reinjected with an angle approximately governed by an independent stochastic process; other reinjection mechanisms arise for different boundary curvatures near the endpoints of the MUPO family.

Problem. Provide a comprehensive characterization of the dynamical properties of marginally unstable periodic orbit families in stadium-like billiards — including the asymptotic decay of correlations, the distribution of Poincaré recurrence times, and the asymptotics of the survival probability when a hole is opened in the table (escape dynamics) — purely in terms of the reinjection map $\Phi$ and the statistics of the return time $T_U$.
category_tag: billiards and marginally unstable periodic orbits
status_search_result: Searches return work establishing prevalence of MUPOs in chaotic billiards and partial results on bouncing-ball reinjection in the stadium (e.g., polynomial decay of correlations, KAM-like phase-space structures), but no comprehensive characterization of dynamics and escape for general stadium-like billiards in terms of arbitrary reinjection mechanisms appears to have been given. The problem appears to remain open as posed.

original_question: In mushroom billiards and related systems with mixed phase space, how does the boundary between regular and chaotic regions affect escape, including the slowing of survival decay caused by stickiness from marginally unstable periodic orbits and by the regular-chaotic interface itself?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar mushroom billiard: the billiard table is the union of a half-disk ("cap") of radius R with a rectangular "stem" of width 2r < 2R attached symmetrically to the diameter of the half-disk, and a point particle moves at unit speed in straight lines inside the table, reflecting elastically at the boundary. The phase space (parametrized by arclength on the boundary and the sine of the angle of incidence) decomposes into a regular component (orbits that remain in the cap forever, those whose chord to the diameter has length greater than 2r) and a chaotic component (orbits that enter the stem). On the interface between these two components there sit families of marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs): periodic orbits in the cap whose chord just touches the corners of the stem, with vanishing Lyapunov exponent. 

Now make the billiard "open" by removing a small hole H from the boundary: a trajectory escapes when it first hits H. Let P(t) denote the survival probability at time t for an initial condition distributed uniformly (with respect to the Liouville measure) on the chaotic component, conditional on not yet having escaped. It is known that when a hole is placed in the chaotic region, the asymptotic decay of P(t) can be slowed both by stickiness produced by MUPOs and by stickiness produced by the regular–chaotic interface itself.

Problem: Give a precise quantitative characterization of the escape properties associated with the boundary between the regular and chaotic regions in mushroom billiards (and analogous mixed-phase-space billiards). In particular, characterize the contribution of the interface (separately from, and together with, the MUPO contribution) to the long-time asymptotics of the survival probability P(t), determining the resulting decay law and how it depends on the geometric parameters (R, r) and on the location and size of the hole.
status_search_result: Recent literature on mushroom billiards (e.g., works on MUPOs and on tilted-hat / web-like hierarchical mixed phase spaces, as well as 2025 works on quantum chaos in mushroom billiards) continues to investigate stickiness from MUPOs and from the regular–chaotic interface, but no definitive characterization of the escape properties of the regular–chaotic boundary itself appears to have been obtained. The problem appears still open.

original_question: For an open quantum billiard, let k_n denote the resonances of the Helmholtz equation (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Is it true that the number of resonant states satisfying Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C grows on the order of k^(d_H+1) as k → ∞, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open two-dimensional quantum billiard: a domain Ω ⊂ ℝ² (for example, the exterior of a finite collection of compact obstacles, with Ω unbounded so that classical trajectories may escape to infinity). On Ω, study the Helmholtz equation

  (∇² + k²) ψ = 0,

with Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω. Because Ω is open, the spectrum is described by resonances: complex wavenumbers {k_n} with Im(k_n) < 0, obtained as poles of the meromorphic continuation of the resolvent (or scattering matrix) of the Dirichlet Laplacian.

Let K ⊂ Ω denote the classical non-escaping set, i.e. the set of points whose forward and backward billiard trajectories remain in a bounded region for all time (the trapped set). Let d_H denote its partial Hausdorff dimension (the Hausdorff dimension of K intersected with a Poincaré section, equivalently dim K = 2 d_H + 1 in phase space for a flow with one trapped direction).

Fix any constant C > 0 and define

  N(k, C) = #{ n : Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C }.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic statement (the fractal Weyl conjecture): as k → ∞,

  N(k, C) = Θ( k^{ d_H + 1 } ),

i.e. there exist constants c₁, c₂ > 0 (possibly depending on C and on the billiard) such that c₁ k^{d_H+1} ≤ N(k,C) ≤ c₂ k^{d_H+1} for all sufficiently large k.
category_tag: fractal Weyl law for quantum resonances
status_search_result: The fractal Weyl conjecture is generally regarded as still open in full generality. A fractal Weyl upper bound of order k^{d_H+1} has been proved in several settings (e.g. for open quantum chaotic maps by Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski, and for several convex obstacles satisfying a no-eclipse condition), and the conjecture is supported by extensive numerical evidence (three-disk scatterer, open baker's map, open kicked rotor). However, a matching lower bound — and hence the full conjecture — has not been established in general.

original_question: How do recurrences in a dynamical system, including periodic orbits and more general recurrent structures either near the hole or elsewhere in phase space, affect escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, T, \mu)$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system on a phase space $M$ with an invariant probability measure $\mu$, and let $H \subset M$ be a measurable subset (the "hole"). Define the survival set up to time $n$ by
$$S_n(H) = \{x \in M : T^k(x) \notin H \text{ for all } 0 \le k \le n\},$$
and define the escape rate (when the limit exists) by
$$\gamma(H) = -\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \mu(S_n(H)).$$
For systems $(M,T,\mu)$ that exhibit little or no hyperbolicity (for example, parabolic, intermittent, or mixed-phase-space systems with elliptic islands, zero or weak Lyapunov exponents, or polynomial mixing), give a general quantitative description of how $\gamma(H)$ and the finer asymptotics of $\mu(S_n(H))$ are affected by recurrent structures of $T$. In particular, characterize the contribution to escape of:
(a) periodic orbits intersecting or close to the boundary of $H$;
(b) periodic orbits and more general recurrent invariant sets (e.g. KAM tori, almost-invariant sets, neutral fixed points) located elsewhere in $M$;
(c) the interplay between such recurrence and the geometry/location of $H$,
and obtain a unifying formula or correction principle (analogous to the hyperbolic escape-rate formulas involving sums over periodic orbits) that applies in the non-hyperbolic regime.
category_tag: open dynamical systems and escape rates
status_search_result: The web search reveals active research on escape rates and periodic orbits, including periodic-orbit formulas in chaotic (hyperbolic) settings and case studies of escape in Hamiltonian and almost-periodic systems, but no general theory describing the influence of recurrent structures on escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity. The problem appears to remain open, with only partial progress in specific model classes.

paper_title: Seminar Notes on Open Questions in Iwasawa Theory - SNOQIT I: The Λ[G]-modules of Iwasawa theory II: Units and Kummer theory in Iwasawa extensions
original_question: Beyond the class-group modules that arise in classical Iwasawa theory, which other Λ-modules have Property F, and what general hypotheses guarantee that a submodule of a free Λ-module has Property F? The question asks for intrinsic structural criteria, not just isolated examples, so that one can recognize when a projective-limit Λ-module has the same rigidity and decomposition behavior that the paper proves for the standard Iwasawa modules.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$ be the Iwasawa algebra. Say that a $\Lambda$-module $M$ has Property F if it satisfies the following axiomatic rigidity/decomposition condition: $M$ embeds as a $\Lambda$-submodule of a free $\Lambda$-module $\Lambda^n$, and every $\Lambda$-linear endomorphism of $M$ extends uniquely to a $\Lambda$-linear endomorphism of the ambient free module compatible with the natural decomposition into isotypic components under any compatible Galois action; equivalently, $M$ shares the structural rigidity established for the standard projective-limit modules of classical Iwasawa theory (such as the inverse limits, along the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-tower, of $p$-parts of ideal class groups of CM fields).

Beyond the class-group modules of classical Iwasawa theory, exhibit further natural examples of $\Lambda$-modules that possess Property F, and formulate intrinsic structural hypotheses on a $\Lambda$-submodule $M \subseteq \Lambda^n$ of a free $\Lambda$-module that are sufficient to guarantee that $M$ has Property F.
status_search_result: No subsequent literature was located that resolves the question of intrinsic structural criteria characterizing $\Lambda$-modules with Property F or that provides general hypotheses ensuring a submodule of a free $\Lambda$-module has Property F. The problem is posed as an open axiomatic-classification question and no published resolution was found in the available search results.

original_question: For an arbitrary number field K and a fixed prime p, does the Leopoldt defect D(K) vanish? In concrete terms, is the p-adic closure of the global unit group always as large as Leopoldt predicted, so that no unexpected p-adic rank defect occurs in the unit embedding?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ denote the group of units of the ring of integers of $K$, and let $E := \mathcal{O}_K^\times / (\text{torsion})$, a free abelian group of rank $r := r_1(K) + r_2(K) - 1$, where $r_1$ and $r_2$ are the numbers of real and complex places of $K$.

For each prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $K$ above $p$, let $K_\mathfrak{p}$ denote the completion of $K$ at $\mathfrak{p}$ and let $U_\mathfrak{p} \subset K_\mathfrak{p}^\times$ be its group of local units. Set
$$U_p := \prod_{\mathfrak{p} \mid p} U_\mathfrak{p},$$
endowed with the product of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic topologies. The diagonal embedding $\mathcal{O}_K^\times \hookrightarrow U_p$ induces a map $E \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Z}_p \to U_p$; let $\overline{E}$ denote the closure of the image of $E$ in $U_p$. Define the Leopoldt defect of $K$ at $p$ by
$$D_p(K) := \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}}(E) - \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(\overline{E}) = r - \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(\overline{E}).$$

Prove or disprove: for every number field $K$ and every prime $p$, one has $D_p(K) = 0$.
status_search_result: Leopoldt's conjecture is known for abelian number fields over $\mathbb{Q}$ (Brumer 1967, using Baker's theorem) and for certain other special cases, and there are partial results (e.g. for some CM fields and specific families of totally real $S_3$-extensions). However, the general statement, that the Leopoldt defect $D_p(K)$ vanishes for every number field $K$ and every prime $p$, remains an open problem as of 2026.

paper_title: Seminar Notes on Open Questions in Iwasawa Theory - SNOQIT I: The Λ[G]-modules of Iwasawa theory II: Units and Kummer theory in Iwasawa extensions
original_question: For a CM Galois extension K containing the p-th roots of unity, is the minus-part T-torsion in the p-unit class-group module trivial; that is, does (A′)^−[T] = {1} hold? This is the classical Gross conjecture in the paper's formulation, expressing that the minus-part p-unit class module has no nontrivial T-torsion.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a CM number field containing the $p$-th roots of unity, with maximal totally real subfield $K^+$. Let $T$ be the (finite, non-empty) set of places of $K$ above $p$. Consider the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $K_\infty/K$, write $K_n$ for its $n$-th layer, and let $\Gamma=\mathrm{Gal}(K_\infty/K)$.

For each $n$, let $A'_n$ denote the $p$-part of the $T$-class group of $K_n$, i.e. the $p$-Sylow subgroup of the ideal class group of the ring of $T$-integers $\mathcal{O}_{K_n,T}$ (equivalently, the quotient of the $p$-part of the full ideal class group by the classes generated by primes of $K_n$ above $p$). Let
$$A' \;=\; \varprojlim_n A'_n,$$
the projective limit taken with respect to the norm maps; this is a finitely generated module over the Iwasawa algebra $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}_p[\![\Gamma]\!]$.

Complex conjugation $j\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/K^+)$ acts on $A'$, and since $p$ is odd one has the eigenspace decomposition $A' = (A')^+ \oplus (A')^-$, where $(A')^- = \{x\in A' : j(x) = -x\}$.

Let $T$ also denote, by abuse of notation, the closed subgroup of $A'$ generated topologically by classes coming from the decomposition groups of the primes above $p$ in $K_\infty/K$, and write $(A')^-[T]$ for the $T$-torsion submodule of the minus part $(A')^-$.

Prove or disprove: 
$$(A')^-[T] = \{1\}.$$
status_search_result: The statement is known as the Gross (or Gross–Kuz'min) conjecture. It is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the $p$-adic regulator of $p$-units (Federer–Gross, 1981) and was proved by Greenberg (1973) for abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. In full generality for CM fields it is widely regarded as still open, though several partial and conditional results (e.g., Kolster, and conditional proofs assuming Leopoldt) and proposed proofs (e.g., the 2011 preprint "The Gross–Kuz'min conjecture for CM fields") exist; the conjecture in full generality has not been universally accepted as solved.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
original_question: For the copolymer model with α = 1/2, prove that the weak-coupling critical slope m_{1/2} is strictly larger than 2/3.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the disordered copolymer model defined as follows. Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, with law $\mathbf{P}$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, with law $\mathbb{P}$. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ (coupling intensity) and $h\ge 0$ (asymmetry bias), and for $N\in\mathbb{N}$, define the polymer measure of length $N$ by
$$\frac{d\mathbf{P}_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}{d\mathbf{P}}(S) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}\,\exp\!\Big(\lambda \sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\Big),$$
with the convention $\mathrm{sign}(0)=\mathrm{sign}(S_{n-1})$, and where $Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}$ is the normalizing partition function. The quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h) \;=\; \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}$$
exists and is non-negative; the localized phase is $\{\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)>0\}$ and the delocalized phase is $\{\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)=0\}$. There is a critical curve $h_c:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ separating these phases, and it is known that the limit
$$m \;=\; \lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0} \frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}$$
exists in $(0,1]$. (More generally, when the underlying random-walk return-time distribution has tails of index $1+\alpha$ with $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the corresponding weak-coupling slope is denoted $m_\alpha$, and the simple random walk corresponds to $\alpha=1/2$.)

It is known that $m_\alpha\ge 1/(1+\alpha)$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$; in particular $m_{1/2}\ge 2/3$.

Prove that
$$m_{1/2} \;>\; \tfrac{2}{3}.$$
status_search_result: The strict inequality $m_\alpha > 1/(1+\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ was established by Bolthausen, den Hollander, and Opoku, ruling out Monthus' conjecture $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$. In particular this gives $m_{1/2}>2/3$, resolving the problem (although the exact value of $m_{1/2}$ remains unknown).

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
original_question: For the general copolymer model, the free energy near criticality is known to satisfy F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0 under the stated disorder assumptions. Can this smoothing bound be improved by replacing the exponent 2 with a larger exponent?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\omega = (\omega_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables under a probability measure $\mathbb{P}$, satisfying $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1] = 0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2] = 1$, and $M(t) := \mathbb{E}[\exp(t\omega_1)] < \infty$ for all $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$. Let $S = (S_n)_{n \geq 0}$ be a simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, with law $\mathbf{P}$, and define $\Delta_n = \mathrm{sign}(S_n) \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ (with the convention that $\mathrm{sign}(0)$ is determined by an arbitrary fixed rule, e.g., $\mathrm{sign}(0) = +1$).

For parameters $\lambda \geq 0$ and $h \in \mathbb{R}$, and an integer $N \geq 1$, define the copolymer Hamiltonian
$$H_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)(S) = \lambda \sum_{n=1}^{N} (\omega_n + h)\, \Delta_n,$$
the partition function $Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h) = \mathbf{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(H_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)(S)\right)\right]$, and the quenched free energy
$$\textsf{F}(\lambda,h) = \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N}\, \mathbb{E}\!\left[\log Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)\right] - \lambda h,$$
which exists, is non-negative, and is non-increasing in $h$. The quenched critical point is
$$h_c(\lambda) = \inf\{h \in \mathbb{R} : \textsf{F}(\lambda,h) = 0\}.$$
The simple random walk return time satisfies $\mathbf{P}(\tau_1 = 2n) \sim C n^{-3/2}$ as $n \to \infty$, so the underlying renewal exponent is $\alpha = 1/2$.

Known smoothing bound. For every $\lambda > 0$ there exists $c(\lambda) < \infty$ such that
$$0 \leq \textsf{F}(\lambda, h_c(\lambda) + \delta) \leq (1+\alpha)\, c(\lambda)\, \delta^{2} \qquad \text{for every } \delta > 0.$$

Question. Can the exponent $2$ in this upper bound be improved? That is, do there exist $\lambda_0 > 0$, $\gamma > 2$, $\delta_0 > 0$, and a finite constant $C(\lambda_0)$ such that
$$\textsf{F}(\lambda_0, h_c(\lambda_0) + \delta) \leq C(\lambda_0)\, \delta^{\gamma} \qquad \text{for all } 0 < \delta < \delta_0,$$
or, alternatively, prove that no such improvement is possible (e.g., establish a matching lower bound $\textsf{F}(\lambda, h_c(\lambda) + \delta) \geq c'(\lambda)\, \delta^{2}$ for small $\delta > 0$)?
status_search_result: Subsequent work has refined the smoothing inequality of Giacomin–Toninelli (sharper constants, weaker disorder assumptions, extension to correlated disorder), but the quadratic exponent $\gamma = 2$ has not been improved. No source found that establishes a smoothing exponent strictly greater than $2$ at criticality for the copolymer model, so the question of whether $\delta^2$ can be replaced by $\delta^{\gamma}$ with $\gamma > 2$ appears to remain open.

paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
context_brief: Inverse correlation length versus free energy
original_question: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) denote the inverse correlation length defined through the exponential decay rate appearing in the model's excursion and correlation estimates. As h approaches the critical point h_c(λ) from below, is log μ(λ,h) asymptotic to log F(λ,h), where F(λ,h) is the free energy?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the copolymer model at a selective interface defined as follows. Let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables with mean zero, unit variance, and finite exponential moments, defined on a probability space with expectation E. Let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} be a simple symmetric random walk on Z, independent of ω, with law P and expectation E. For parameters λ > 0 and h ≥ 0, define the quenched partition function
   Z_{N,ω} = E[ exp( -2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N} (ω_n + h) Δ_n ) ],
where Δ_n = (1 - sign(S_n))/2 (taken to be (1 - sign(S_{n-1}))/2 when S_n = 0, by convention), so the polymer is penalized for monomers in the lower half-plane.

The quenched free energy is
   F(λ,h) = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) E[ log Z_{N,ω} ],
which exists and is non-negative. The critical curve is h_c(λ) = inf{h ≥ 0 : F(λ,h) = 0}, separating the localized phase {F > 0} from the delocalized phase {F = 0}.

For (λ,h) in the localized phase, define the inverse correlation length
   μ(λ,h) = - lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[ (1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N}(ω_n + h))) / Z_{N,ω} ],
which governs the exponential decay rate of excursion and correlation estimates for the model.

Question: Is it true that
   log μ(λ,h)  ∼  log F(λ,h)   as  h ↗ h_c(λ),
in the sense that the ratio log μ(λ,h) / log F(λ,h) tends to 1?
status_search_result: The question of whether log μ(λ,h) is asymptotically equivalent to log F(λ,h) as h approaches the critical curve from the localized side is posed as a problem expected (in connection with disorder relevance) to fail, but no proof or disproof appears in the literature on copolymer models at selective interfaces. Subsequent work (e.g., Bolthausen–den Hollander–Opoku 2015) addresses variational characterizations of the free energy but does not resolve this asymptotic comparison.

paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
original_question: Can more precise measurements of the branching ratio for the purely leptonic decay B+ → τ+ντ resolve the tension between the experimental average (1.64 ± 0.34) × 10−4 and indirect CKM global-fit determinations, where CKMfitter places the indirect determination 2.6 standard deviations from the experimental value and UTfit places it 3.2 standard deviations away?
self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the purely leptonic decay $B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau$ has a branching ratio that can be predicted indirectly from a global fit to the parameters of the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) quark-mixing matrix (using inputs such as $|V_{ub}|$, the $B$-meson decay constant $f_B$, the $B$-meson lifetime, and the unitarity-triangle constraints), and can also be measured directly in $B$-factory experiments. The current world-average direct experimental measurement is
$$\mathcal{B}(B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau)_{\text{exp}} = (1.64 \pm 0.34) \times 10^{-4},$$
while the indirect global-fit determinations disagree with this value at the level of $2.6\sigma$ (CKMfitter-style fit) and $3.2\sigma$ (UTfit-style fit).

Question: Will future, more precise experimental measurements of $\mathcal{B}(B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau)$ resolve this tension between the direct measurement and the indirect CKM global-fit determination — that is, will the discrepancy converge toward zero (consistent with the Standard Model fit) or persist/grow into a significant deviation indicative of physics beyond the Standard Model?
category_tag: CKM unitarity and rare B-meson decays
status_search_result: Subsequent measurements (notably the 2015 Belle semileptonic-tag analysis with the full Belle dataset) brought the experimental branching ratio closer to the Standard Model CKM-fit prediction, substantially reducing the previously reported 2.6–3.2σ tension. However, the precision is still limited and the program of improving this measurement (e.g., Belle II and proposed FCC-ee studies) remains active, so the question of definitively resolving the tension is not fully closed.

paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
original_question: Can SuperB-era analyses reduce the dominant irreducible systematic uncertainty in BR(B+ → τ+ντ), mainly from Btag and Bsig reconstruction efficiencies and B Bbar counting, enough to avoid a systematics-dominated measurement and reach the assumed factor-of-two improvement that would give about 4.5% uncertainty at 75 ab−1?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the leptonic decay $B^+ 	o 	au^+ 
u_	au$ measured at a future high-luminosity asymmetric $e^+e^-$ B-factory operating at the $\Upsilon(4S)$ resonance, in which one $B$ meson of the produced $B ar{B}$ pair is fully reconstructed in a hadronic or semileptonic mode (the "tag side", $B_{m tag}$) and the signal $B$ ($B_{m sig}$) is searched for through its leptonic decay. Suppose that, with current analysis techniques, the irreducible systematic uncertainty on the measured branching ratio $\mathrm{BR}(B^+ 	o 	au^+ 
u_	au)$ is $\sigma_{m syst} = 8.7\%$, dominated by three contributions: (i) the $B_{m tag}$ reconstruction efficiency, (ii) the $B_{m sig}$ reconstruction efficiency, and (iii) the $B ar{B}$ counting uncertainty. The statistical uncertainty scales as $1/\sqrt{\mathcal{L}}$ with integrated luminosity $\mathcal{L}$. Under the hypothesis that improved analysis techniques, control samples, and detector understanding allow each of these systematic components to be reduced so that the total irreducible systematic uncertainty on $\mathrm{BR}(B^+	o	au^+
u_	au)$ is reduced by a factor of two (to roughly $4.35\%$), determine whether the combined statistical-plus-systematic uncertainty on $\mathrm{BR}(B^+	o	au^+
u_	au)$ at an integrated luminosity of $\mathcal{L} = 75\ \mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ can be brought down to approximately $4.5\%$ without becoming systematics-dominated, and identify which improvements in the calibration and modeling of $B_{m tag}$ efficiency, $B_{m sig}$ efficiency, and $B ar{B}$ counting are required to realize this scenario.

paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.
self_contained_problem: Let G be a finite simple graph given by its adjacency matrix. A finite set P of points in the Euclidean plane realizes G as its point visibility graph if there is a bijection between the vertices of G and the points of P such that two distinct points p, q ∈ P are adjacent in G if and only if the open line segment joining p and q contains no other point of P (equivalently, no third point of P lies on the segment between them). The decision problem is: given the adjacency matrix of G, determine whether such a finite point set P exists. Provide an algorithm that decides this problem, or characterize its computational complexity.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has shown the recognition of point visibility graphs is NP-hard (Roy, 2014/2016) and, more strongly, complete for the existential theory of the reals ∃R (Cardinal & Hoffmann, SoCG 2015 / DCG 2017), which places it in PSPACE and hence makes it decidable. However, no efficient (polynomial-time) recognition algorithm is known, and an exact characterization of point visibility graphs remains open. Thus the problem is partially resolved: complexity-classified but no tractable algorithm or combinatorial characterization exists.

paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
original_question: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.
self_contained_problem:
Let P = {p_1, ..., p_n} be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (no three collinear is not assumed; collinearity may block visibility). Two points p_i, p_j ∈ P are mutually visible if the open line segment connecting them contains no other point of P. The visibility graph of P is the simple undirected graph V(P) on vertex set {1, ..., n} in which {i, j} is an edge if and only if p_i and p_j are mutually visible.

Suppose a finite simple graph G is given together with the promise that there exists some finite point set P in the plane with V(P) ≅ G. Provide an algorithm (or constructive procedure) that, on input G, outputs explicit coordinates for a point set P' ⊂ ℝ² such that V(P') ≅ G.
status_search_result: The reconstruction problem for point visibility graphs remains open. Recognition of point visibility graphs is known to be complete for the existential theory of the reals (Cardinal–Hoffmann, 2015), and there exist point visibility graphs that admit no realization with rational/integer coordinates, indicating fundamental obstacles to constructive reconstruction. No general polynomial-time or constructive algorithm to produce coordinates from a given (promised) point visibility graph is known.

self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear). The point visibility graph $G=G(P)$ has vertex set $P$, with two points $p,q\in P$ joined by an edge if and only if the open line segment $pq$ contains no other point of $P$. Denote by $\chi(G)$ the chromatic number and by $\omega(G)$ the clique number of $G$.

Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c$ such that every point visibility graph $G$ with $\omega(G)=5$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le c$.

No source located resolves the ω(G) = 5 case, so its status appears to remain open, but this could not be definitively confirmed from the searched material.

original_question: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane in general position, meaning that no three points of P are collinear. A blocking set for P is a finite set Q of points in the plane, disjoint from P, such that for every pair of distinct points p, p' ∈ P, the open line segment pp' contains at least one point of Q. (Equivalently, Q "blocks" all visibilities between points of P.) Define
   b(P) = min{ |Q| : Q is a blocking set for P },
and, for each integer n ≥ 3,
   b(n) = min{ b(P) : P ⊂ ℝ² has |P| = n and no three points of P are collinear }.

It is known that b(n) ≥ n − 1 for all n ≥ 3. Prove (or disprove) that
   b(n) / n → ∞   as n → ∞.
category_tag: Discrete and combinatorial geometry — blocking/visibility sets
status_search_result: The conjecture that b(n)/n → ∞ for blocking sets of n points in general position is attributed to Pór and Wood (2010, "Blocking Visibility for Points in General Position"). Subsequent literature (e.g., surveys on visibility/obstacle problems and follow-up work by Pór–Wood and others) continues to list it as an open problem; the best known general lower bound remains linear in n, while the conjectured upper bound O(n log n) and the lower bound b(n) = ω(n) have not been established. No published resolution was found.

paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
original_question: Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.
self_contained_problem:
An obstacle representation of a simple graph $G=(V,E)$ in the Euclidean plane consists of an injective placement of the vertices $V$ as points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ together with a finite collection of pairwise disjoint connected closed sets ("obstacles") in $\mathbb{R}^2$, disjoint from the vertex points, such that for any two distinct vertices $u,v \in V$, the open straight-line segment $uv$ avoids every obstacle if and only if $uv \in E$. The obstacle number $\mathrm{obs}(G)$ is the minimum number of obstacles in any obstacle representation of $G$. Let
$$f(n) := \max\{\mathrm{obs}(G) : G \text{ is a graph on } n \text{ vertices}\}.$$
It is known that $f(n) = \Omega(n / \log^2 n)$. Improve this lower bound: that is, exhibit an explicit superlinear-in-the-denominator improvement, ideally proving $f(n) = \Omega(n/\log n)$, $f(n) = \Omega(n)$, or even a stronger lower bound, by constructing $n$-vertex graphs whose obstacle number grows faster than $n/\log^2 n$.
status_search_result: The lower bound has been improved several times since the problem was posed. No matching Ω(n) bound is known for general or simple-polygon obstacles, so the question of the exact growth rate remains open.

original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, find a Hamiltonian cycle of G in polynomial time.
self_contained_problem:

A clique of G is a subset C ⊆ V such that every two distinct vertices of C are adjacent. A maximum clique is a clique of largest cardinality.

Problem. Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G on n vertices as input, design an algorithm that computes a maximum clique of G, and determine the computational complexity of this task. original_question: Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph. A geometric realization of G as a point visibility graph is an injective map f : V → R^2 such that (i) the points {f(v) : v ∈ V} are in general position (no three collinear, or, depending on the convention, with collinearities respected by the visibility relation), and (ii) for every pair of distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, {u,v} ∈ E if and only if the open segment between f(u) and f(v) contains no point f(w) with w ∈ V \ {u,v}. A graph G is called a visibility graph if such a realization exists.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial p(n) such that every visibility graph G on n vertices admits a realization f in which every coordinate of every point f(v) is an integer that can be written using at most p(n) bits?

Equivalently, can every visibility graph be realized with integer endpoint coordinates whose bit-length is polynomial in the number of vertices?
status_search_result: For point visibility graphs, Cardinal and Hoffmann (SoCG 2015 / DCG 2017) proved that some point visibility graphs admit no realization with all integer coordinates, and that some require doubly-exponential coordinates in any realization, ruling out polynomial bit-length in general. They also showed point-visibility-graph recognition is complete for the existential theory of the reals, and that recognizing those realizable on an integer grid is equivalent to decidability of the existential theory of the rationals. Thus for point visibility graphs the answer is negative; the broader question for visibility graphs of segments/polygons appears to remain open.

original_question: Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon with n vertices, and let G be its vertex visibility graph: the graph on the vertex set of P in which two vertices are adjacent if and only if the open line segment joining them lies in the closure of the interior of P (so adjacencies include polygon edges as well as interior diagonals).

A Hamiltonian cycle C of G that traverses the vertices of P in their cyclic order along the boundary is called the boundary cycle. An ordered chord of C is a chord (u,v) of C together with a chosen direction. A covering set for G (with respect to C) is a collection S of ordered chords of C such that every chord of C lies in the convex hull, in the appropriate combinatorial sense induced by the boundary cycle, of some ordered chord in S; equivalently, S certifies one of the standard necessary conditions of Ghosh for a graph to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon, namely that every chord of the Hamiltonian boundary cycle is "covered" by some member of S.

It is known that there exist covering sets whose total descriptive size, measured in bits, matches a certain optimal asymptotic upper bound f(n) (the best presently established information-theoretic bound on the size of a smallest covering set for an n-vertex visibility graph).

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given as input the visibility graph G on n vertices together with its boundary Hamiltonian cycle C, runs in time polynomial in n and outputs a covering set for G whose total bit-size is O(f(n)), thereby matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound in polynomial time.
status_search_result: A targeted web search for a polynomial-time construction of an optimal-size covering set for visibility graphs of simple polygons did not return any publication that resolves this question. Surveys and follow-up work on visibility-graph recognition continue to list polynomial-time testability of Ghosh's higher necessary conditions (which involve covering sets) as unresolved, but no source explicitly confirms that this specific covering-set construction problem has been settled. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

context_brief: Quadratic bound for k-blocked point sets
original_question: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. Given a finite set $P$ of points, say that a point $x \in P$ blocks two other points $v, w \in P$ if $x$ lies in the interior of the line segment $vw$. For an integer $k \ge 1$, call $P$ a $k$-blocked set if there exists a coloring $c : P \to \{1,2,\dots,k\}$ using exactly $k$ colors such that, for every pair of distinct points $v, w \in P$, one has $c(v) = c(w)$ if and only if some point of $P \setminus \{v,w\}$ blocks $v$ and $w$ (equivalently, lies on the open segment $vw$).

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$, every $k$-blocked set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies $|P| \le C k^2$.

No proof or counterexample of the general quadratic bound appears in the literature; the conjecture remains open.

Two points $p,q\in P$ are said to be mutually visible (with respect to $P$) if the open line segment between $p$ and $q$ contains no point of $P$. A subset $C\subseteq P$ is called a visibility clique if every two points of $C$ are mutually visible. A subset $L\subseteq P$ is called collinear if all its points lie on a common straight line.
