paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: Why do technically demanding AC-susceptibility and specific-heat experiments on high-dilution LiHoxY1−xF4 disagree about whether the system shows conventional spin-glass freezing or unusual antiglass behavior, particularly between the earlier measurements of Reich, Ghosh, and collaborators and the later measurements of Quilliam and collaborators?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the dilute dipolar-coupled Ising magnet LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ in the high-dilution regime (e.g. $x \approx 0.045$), where Ho$^{3+}$ ions occupy a small fraction of the rare-earth sites and interact predominantly through long-ranged magnetic dipolar interactions with a small transverse off-diagonal exchange that introduces effective quantum fluctuations. The low-temperature, low-frequency magnetic response of this system has been probed by AC magnetic susceptibility (real and imaginary parts $\chi'(\omega,T)$ and $\chi''(\omega,T)$) and by specific heat $C(T)$ measurements down to millikelvin temperatures.

One set of careful experiments reports: (a) a quasi-static susceptibility $\chi_0(T)$ that diverges with an anomalous power law $\chi_0 \sim T^{-0.75}$, (b) a frequency distribution of $\chi''$ that narrows as the temperature is lowered, and (c) specific-heat features interpreted as signatures of a quantum-disordered "antiglass" state with entangled magnetic moments rather than a conventional spin glass. Another set of equally careful experiments on nominally identical samples reports: (a$'$) no such anomalous divergence of $\chi_0$, (b$'$) a frequency distribution of $\chi''$ that broadens upon cooling (as expected for canonical spin-glass freezing), and (c$'$) a specific heat lacking the unusual features attributed to the antiglass phase.

Problem. Identify and justify a quantitative physical mechanism — taking into account ingredients such as nuclear hyperfine couplings to the Ho$^{3+}$ electronic moments, off-diagonal dipolar terms generating an effective random transverse field, sample-dependent demagnetization and shape effects, thermal contact and equilibration on extremely long relaxation timescales, and possible non-equilibrium / aging dynamics — that explains the discrepancy between the two sets of AC-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements on highly diluted LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$, and determine which (if either) of the two scenarios (conventional spin-glass freezing versus antiglass quantum-disordered behavior) describes the true equilibrium low-temperature phase of the system in the high-dilution limit.
category_tag: dilute dipolar Ising magnets / spin glasses
status_search_result: The discrepancy between the earlier antiglass-supporting AC-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements (Reich, Ghosh and collaborators) and the later spin-glass-consistent measurements (Quilliam et al.) on highly diluted LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ remains unresolved in the literature. Subsequent works (e.g. μSR studies and perturbative quantum Monte Carlo analyses) have continued to debate the existence of an antiglass phase versus conventional spin-glass freezing without converging on an accepted explanation for the experimental disagreement.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: Do sample shape and demagnetization effects influence whether a spin-glass phase exists in highly diluted LiHoxY1−xF4, even though such effects are expected not to determine the existence of the spin-glass phase?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the dipolar Ising magnet LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$, in which magnetic Ho$^{3+}$ ions are randomly substituted by non-magnetic Y$^{3+}$ ions at concentration $1-x$, and the remaining Ho$^{3+}$ ions carry effective Ising moments coupled predominantly through long-range, anisotropic magnetic dipole-dipole interactions. In the highly diluted regime (small $x$), the question of whether a thermodynamic spin-glass phase exists at low temperature is of central interest. Because dipolar interactions are long ranged, the magnetostatic energy of a finite sample depends on its shape, leading to demagnetization corrections that depend on the sample geometry.

Determine whether sample shape and the associated demagnetization effects can influence the existence (as opposed to merely the location or sharpness) of an equilibrium spin-glass phase transition in highly diluted LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$. Specifically, decide whether two macroscopic samples with the same Ho concentration $x \ll 1$ but different shapes (e.g. needle-like versus oblate) must exhibit the same answer to the question "is there a finite-temperature spin-glass phase?", or whether shape/demagnetization can change this answer.
status_search_result: Studies of dilute LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ continue to debate whether a true spin-glass phase exists at small $x$ (with conflicting reports of glassy dynamics versus antiglass behavior at $x=0.045$, and reported transitions at other dilutions). No work appears to have decisively settled whether sample shape/demagnetization corrections can change the existence of the spin-glass phase; the issue remains an open experimental and theoretical question.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: For diluted dipolar Ising models intended to describe LiHoxY1−xF4, can larger classical Monte Carlo simulations bring finite-size corrections under control, reconcile the different spin-glass correlation-length crossings along the a and c axes, and thereby determine the finite-temperature spin-glass transition more reliably?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a site-diluted dipolar Ising model on a tetragonal lattice intended as a microscopic description of LiHo_xY_{1−x}F_4: place classical Ising spins σ_i = ±1 on a fraction x of the rare-earth sites of a tetragonal lattice (with distinct a and c crystallographic axes) and let them interact via the long-range, anisotropic magnetic dipole-dipole interaction (with appropriate Ewald summation under periodic boundary conditions), with the Ising axis aligned along the c axis. For a finite system of linear size L, define the wavevector-dependent spin-glass susceptibility from the disorder- and thermal-averaged squared overlap, and from it define the second-moment spin-glass correlation length ξ_sg(L,T) separately for wavevectors along the a and c axes, yielding ξ_sg^a(L,T) and ξ_sg^c(L,T).

It is known that, for accessible system sizes, the curves ξ_sg^a(L,T)/L for different L cross at one apparent temperature, while the curves ξ_sg^c(L,T)/L cross at a slightly different apparent temperature, suggesting that finite-size corrections to scaling are not yet under control.

Question: by performing classical Monte Carlo simulations on substantially larger system sizes L, can one bring the leading finite-size scaling corrections under control, force the crossing temperatures of ξ_sg^a/L and ξ_sg^c/L to coincide in the L → ∞ limit, and thereby reliably determine the finite-temperature spin-glass transition temperature T_sg(x) of this site-diluted dipolar Ising model?
status_search_result: Subsequent Monte Carlo studies (e.g., Tam–Gingras and Alonso–Fernández type works on site-diluted dipolar Ising models, and later large-scale simulations of dipolar spin glasses in 3D published in Phys. Rev. B 100, 064425 (2019)) provide stronger evidence for a finite-temperature spin-glass transition and give critical exponents, but I did not find a clear, definitive resolution of the specific axis-dependent discrepancy between the ξ_sg^a/L and ξ_sg^c/L crossings for the realistic LiHo_xY_{1−x}F_4 model. Status appears unresolved/unclear from available sources.

paper_title: Some open questions in TDDFT: Clues from Lattice Models and Kadanoff-Baym Dynamics
original_question: Can a practical exchange-correlation kernel fxc for linear-response TDDFT be constructed that is nonlocal and frequency dependent, improves systematically on ALDA, and avoids the unphysical poles caused by the linearized Sham-Schlueter or Klein-functional route, where double inversion of the non-interacting Kohn-Sham response function chi0 turns zeros of chi0 into double poles in fxc? One proposed direction is to start from the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than the Klein functional, but it remains open whether that avoids the known pathology without creating new ones.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. In linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) the density–density response function χ(r,r';ω) of an interacting electronic system is related to the Kohn–Sham non-interacting response function χ₀(r,r';ω) by the Dyson-like equation

  χ = χ₀ + χ₀ ⋆ ( v_C + f_xc ) ⋆ χ ,

where v_C(r,r') = 1/|r−r'| is the Coulomb interaction and f_xc(r,r';ω) is the (in general nonlocal and frequency-dependent) exchange-correlation kernel, defined as the second functional derivative of the exchange-correlation action with respect to the density. Solving for f_xc requires inverting χ₀ twice:

  f_xc = χ₀⁻¹ − χ⁻¹ − v_C .

Consequently any zero of χ₀(ω) on the real axis becomes a double pole of f_xc, and these spurious poles propagate to χ, generating unphysical poles of χ in the upper half complex frequency plane. This pathology is known to afflict every kernel obtained from the linearized Sham–Schlüter equation, equivalently from the variational principle based on the Klein functional Φ_K[G].

Adiabatic local density approximation (ALDA) sets f_xc^ALDA(r,r';ω) = δ(r−r') d²(n e_xc(n))/dn²|_{n=n(r)}; it is local, frequency-independent, and free of the above pathology, but lacks systematic improvability and misses important particle-hole effects beyond RPA.

Question. Does there exist a practical, systematically improvable construction of an exchange-correlation kernel f_xc(r,r';ω) that

(a) is genuinely nonlocal in space and frequency dependent,
(b) improves upon ALDA in a controlled, systematic manner (e.g. captures particle-hole interactions beyond RPA),
(c) does not suffer from the double-inversion pathology, i.e. yields a response function χ(ω) whose poles all lie on the real axis with physically correct residues?

In particular, if one starts from the Luttinger–Ward functional Φ_LW[G] in place of the Klein functional Φ_K[G] when deriving f_xc, does the resulting variational kernel avoid the spurious upper-half-plane poles of χ without introducing new pathologies (such as causality violations, additional spurious poles, sum-rule violations, or lack of positivity of Im χ)?
status_search_result: No publication was found that derives a nonlocal, frequency-dependent exchange-correlation kernel from the Luttinger–Ward functional and demonstrates absence of the double-inversion pathology together with systematic improvability over ALDA. Existing approaches that avoid the pathology (e.g. nonlocal kernels imported from time-dependent current DFT, Bethe–Salpeter–derived kernels, or recent machine-learned kernels) do not provide the variational Luttinger–Ward construction asked about, and current literature still characterizes systematic, pathology-free f_xc beyond ALDA as an open challenge.

paper_title: Some open questions in TDDFT: Clues from Lattice Models and Kadanoff-Baym Dynamics
original_question: What are the physical regimes and corrective principles for Kadanoff-Baym dynamics combined with many-body perturbation theory when conserving approximations still show fundamental failures, such as breakdown at strong interaction, artificial correlation-induced damping, questionable steady states in extended systems, and violations of positivity in two-particle correlation functions? The setting is the nonequilibrium Green's-function approach, where the Kadanoff-Baym equations use a self-energy from approximations such as second Born, GW, or T-matrix, which conserve macroscopic quantities but do not guarantee all physically required properties.
category_tag: Kadanoff-Baym equations and conserving many-body approximations
status_search_result: No comprehensive resolution is available. Recent works (e.g., 2023 results on the failure of the Baym-Kadanoff construction to match quantum dynamics with thermodynamic critical behavior, and ongoing studies of KBE for open quantum systems) confirm that the listed pathologies of conserving MBA-based KBE remain active research issues, with only partial remedies known in specific regimes. The general problem of jointly curing strong-coupling breakdown, artificial damping, spurious steady states, and positivity violations appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open questions in TDDFT: Clues from Lattice Models and Kadanoff-Baym Dynamics
original_question: How should exchange-correlation kernels for Hubbard lattice TDDFT account for qualitative features of the ALDA kernel that have no known continuum analogue, including a sign that changes with density and interaction strength, and a singularity at half filling for sufficiently large interaction U caused by the discontinuity of vxc at the Mott-Hubbard metal-insulator transition? The paper expects these features to persist when nonlocal and nonadiabatic effects are added, so a complete theory must explain how they affect density response beyond the local adiabatic limit.
category_tag: TDDFT exchange-correlation kernels for Hubbard models
status_search_result: The construction of nonlocal, nonadiabatic xc kernels for Hubbard-model TDDFT that retain the sign-changing and Mott-singularity features of the ALDA kernel remains an active research direction. No published work appears to provide a complete such kernel; subsequent literature on lattice TDDFT (Verdozzi, Stefanucci, Capelle and collaborators) continues to investigate these issues without offering a definitive resolution.

original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g, h ∈ L∞(µ). If C(n) := ∫ f · T^n g · T^(2n) h dµ, is the sequence (C(n)) an approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measure-preserving transformation of the probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$. For $f,g,h\in L^\infty(\mu)$, define the 3-term correlation sequence
$$C(n) \;=\; \int_X f\cdot (T^n g)\cdot (T^{2n} h)\,d\mu, \qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.$$

A basic 2-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $(F(a^n\Gamma))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, where $G/\Gamma$ is a 2-step nilmanifold (i.e., $G$ is a 2-step nilpotent Lie group and $\Gamma\le G$ is a discrete cocompact subgroup), $a\in G$, and $F:G/\Gamma\to\mathbb{C}$ is continuous. A generalized 2-step nilsequence is a uniform limit of basic 2-step nilsequences.

Determine whether the following holds: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist finitely many generalized 2-step nilsequences $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_k$ and integers $c_1,\dots,c_k\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$\limsup_{N\to\infty}\;\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\Bigl|\,C(n)\;-\;\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j\,\psi_j(n)\Bigr| \;<\;\varepsilon.$$

That is, is $(C(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ an approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences?
category_tag: Ergodic multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences
status_search_result: For a single measure-preserving transformation, decomposition results (Bergelson–Host–Kra; Frantzikinakis) show that the 3-term correlation sequence $C(n)$ can be written as a 2-step nilsequence plus an error term small in uniform density, which is closely related to but slightly weaker than an "approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences." Generalizations to commuting transformations and along primes have appeared (Frantzikinakis 2015 Inventiones; Frantzikinakis–Host; Koutsogiannis–Le–Moreira–Richter 2020), and recent work (e.g., 2504.07038, 2026) further refines such decompositions. The exact integral-combination formulation does not appear to have a definitive published affirmative resolution in full generality; the problem is partially solved.

original_question: For integer sequences a1(n), ..., aℓ(n), are the following conditions equivalent: (i) the sequences are good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations; (ii) they are good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer ℓ ≥ 1. Throughout, "system" means an invertible measure-preserving system (X, ℬ, μ, T₁, …, T_ℓ) consisting of a probability space and ℓ commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations.

An ℓ-step nilsystem is a system of the form (G/Γ, T_{b_1}, …, T_{b_ℓ}), where G is an ℓ-step nilpotent Lie group, Γ ⊂ G is a discrete cocompact subgroup, b_1, …, b_ℓ ∈ G commute, and T_{b_i}(xΓ) = b_i x Γ; the measure is the Haar measure on G/Γ.

A basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence in ℓ variables is a sequence of the form ψ(n_1, …, n_ℓ) = F(b_1^{n_1} ⋯ b_ℓ^{n_ℓ} Γ), where G/Γ is an ℓ-step nilmanifold, b_1, …, b_ℓ ∈ G commute, and F : G/Γ → ℂ is continuous.

Let a_1(n), …, a_ℓ(n) be sequences of integers. Say that (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations if for every system (X, ℬ, μ, T_1, …, T_ℓ) with T_1, …, T_ℓ commuting and every f_1, …, f_ℓ ∈ L^∞(μ), the averages
   (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N (T_1^{a_1(n)} f_1) ⋯ (T_ℓ^{a_ℓ(n)} f_ℓ)
converge in L²(μ) as N → ∞.

Say that (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems if the same convergence holds whenever (X, ℬ, μ, T_1, …, T_ℓ) is an ℓ-step nilsystem and f_1, …, f_ℓ are continuous.

Prove or disprove that the following three statements are equivalent:
(i) (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations;
(ii) (a_1, …, a_ℓ) is good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems;
(iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a_1(n), …, a_ℓ(n)) converge as N → ∞.
status_search_result: The problem concerns equivalence of three notions of being "good for ℓ-convergence" for integer sequences in the setting of commuting transformations and ℓ-step nilsystems. Subsequent work by Frantzikinakis and collaborators (e.g., on multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences, arXiv:1407.0631) addresses related decompositions and weighted convergence questions, but I could not locate a definitive resolution of the three-way equivalence as stated. Status appears unresolved in the literature I was able to verify.

original_question: Let (wn) be a complex sequence such that the weighted averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N wn ψ(n) converge for every generalized 2-step nilsequence ψ. Must it follow that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and f, g ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N wn T^n f · S^n g converge weakly in L2(µ)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A measure-preserving system is a quadruple $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ where $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a standard probability space and $T\colon X	o X$ is an invertible measurable transformation that preserves $\mu$. By a system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ we mean such a probability space equipped with two commuting invertible $\mu$-preserving transformations $T$ and $S$.

A $k$-step nilmanifold is a quotient $G/\Gamma$ where $G$ is a connected, simply connected $k$-step nilpotent Lie group and $\Gamma\subset G$ is a discrete cocompact subgroup. A basic $k$-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $(F(a^n\cdot e\Gamma))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, where $a\in G$, $e\Gamma\in G/\Gamma$, and $F\colon G/\Gamma	o\mathbb{C}$ is continuous. A $k$-step nilsequence is a uniform limit of basic $k$-step nilsequences. A generalized $k$-step nilsequence is a sequence $\psi\colon\mathbb{N}	o\mathbb{C}$ that arises as a bounded measurable function of a $k$-step nilsequence (equivalently, $\psi(n)=	ilde F(a^n\cdot e\Gamma)$ for some bounded Borel function $	ilde F$ on a $k$-step nilmanifold $G/\Gamma$ and some $a\in G$).

Problem. Let $(w_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of complex numbers with the property that the weighted averages
$$ rac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} w_n\,\psi(n)$$
converge as $N	o\infty$ for every generalized $2$-step nilsequence $\psi$. Prove or disprove: for every system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ with two commuting measure-preserving transformations and for all $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the weighted ergodic averages
$$ rac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} w_n\,(T^n f)\cdot(S^n g)$$
converge weakly in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N	o\infty$.

However, I could not find an explicit verification that the specific 2-step variant for two commuting transformations $T,S$ has been settled in full generality, so the precise status remains unclear from the available search evidence.

original_question: If an integer sequence a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, must each power sequence a(n)^k be good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, ..., ℓ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of integers and let $\ell\geq 1$ be an integer. Call $(a(n))$ **good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers** if for every invertible probability measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, one has
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-a(n)}A\cap T^{-a(n)^2}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-a(n)^\ell}A\right)>0.$$
Call an integer sequence $(b(n))$ **good for $1$-recurrence** if for every invertible probability measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$,
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-b(n)}A\right)>0.$$

Question: Suppose $(a(n))$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers. Must the power sequence $(a(n)^k)$ be good for $1$-recurrence for every $k=1,2,\ldots,\ell$?
status_search_result: The problem appears as an open problem in Frantzikinakis's survey of open problems on multiple ergodic averages. Related work by Frantzikinakis, Johnson, Lesigne, and Wierdl on "Powers of sequences and convergence of ergodic averages" addresses analogous questions for the mean ergodic theorem rather than recurrence, and recent surveys (e.g., "A view on multiple recurrence") still list questions of this type. No published resolution of this specific recurrence question was located.

original_question: Does there exist an integer sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. By a measure-preserving system we mean a quadruple $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ where $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T\colon X\to X$ is an invertible measurable transformation that preserves $\mu$. More generally, a system with two commuting transformations is $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,T_2)$ where $T_1,T_2$ are invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ satisfying $T_1T_2=T_2T_1$.

Given a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $S=(s_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, we say that $S$ is:

(a) good for 2-recurrence of powers (of a single transformation) if for every measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{-s_n}A\cap T^{-2s_n}A\bigr)>0;$$

(b) good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations if for every system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,T_2)$ with $T_1,T_2$ commuting measure-preserving transformations and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-s_n}A\cap T_2^{-s_n}A\bigr)>0.$$

Question. Does there exist a strictly increasing sequence $S=(s_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive integers that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?
status_search_result: A direct web search did not turn up a published resolution of this specific question. Related problems on multiple recurrence with commuting transformations and on recurrence along powers of sequences have continued to attract attention (e.g., works by Frantzikinakis–Host, Frantzikinakis–Lesigne–Wierdl, Chu, Assani–Moore, and recent counterexamples of 2025 in the non-commuting setting), but no source consulted reports a sequence good for 2-recurrence of powers yet not for commuting transformations, nor a proof that none exists. Status appears to remain unresolved, but this could not be confirmed with full certainty.

original_question: Let P be a family of at least two essentially distinct integer polynomials, and let dmin(P) be the least d such that the Host–Kra factor Zd,T is characteristic for mean convergence of the averages (1/N) Σ T^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)} fℓ. Must one always have dmin(P) ≤ |P| - 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving system on a probability space, and for each integer $k\ge 0$ let $Z_{k,T}$ denote the $k$-th Host–Kra factor of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ (so $Z_{0,T}$ is the trivial factor, $Z_{1,T}$ is the Kronecker factor, and in general $Z_{k,T}$ is the inverse limit of $k$-step nilfactors of $T$).

Given a finite family $P=\{p_1,\dots,p_\ell\}$ of integer-valued polynomials in one variable, say that the factor $Z_{d,T}$ is characteristic for $P$ if for every system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N}\Big(\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}T^{p_i(n)}f_i-\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}T^{p_i(n)}\mathbb{E}(f_i\mid Z_{d,T})\Big)=0$$
in $L^2(\mu)$, and in particular the limit on the left of (i.e. of $\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_i T^{p_i(n)}f_i$) exists in $L^2(\mu)$.

Two integer polynomials are called essentially distinct if their difference is not a constant. Assume $P$ contains at least two essentially distinct polynomials, and let
$$d_{\min}(P)=\min\{d\ge 0: Z_{d,T}\text{ is characteristic for }P\}.$$
Set $|P|=\ell$.

Prove or disprove: for every such family $P$ with $|P|\ge 2$,
$$d_{\min}(P)\le |P|-1.$$
status_search_result: The problem appears in Frantzikinakis' survey of open problems on multiple ergodic averages (2011) and is consistent with subsequent literature treating sharp characteristic factor degrees as an open question. Recent work (e.g., joint ergodicity results of Frantzikinakis–Kuca and others, 2021–2024) has clarified characteristic factors for many polynomial families but does not establish the universal bound $d_{\min}(P)\le |P|-1$. No source found establishing or refuting the bound in full generality.

original_question: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials, meaning every nontrivial linear combination of the sequences p1,N, ..., pℓ,N is good in the sense that its exponential sums against every nonzero frequency tend to zero. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ T^[p1,N(n)] f1 · ... · T^[pℓ,N(n)] fℓ converge in L2(µ) to ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\ge 1$. For each $N\in\mathbb N$ let $p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N}\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be real polynomials. For a sequence $a\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ define its exponential sums by $E_N(a,t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}e^{2\pi i\,t\,a(n)}$. Call a sequence $(a_N(n))_{N,n}$ (with $a_N$ depending on $N$ and $n$ ranging over $1,\dots,N$) "good" if for every $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ one has $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}e^{2\pi i t\,a_N(n)}\to 0$ as $N\to\infty$. Call the family of $\ell$-tuples $(p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N})_{N\in\mathbb N}$ good if every nontrivial integer (equivalently real) linear combination $c_1 p_{1,N}+\cdots+c_\ell p_{\ell,N}$, $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell)\ne 0$, gives a good sequence in the above sense.

Prove or disprove: whenever $(p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N})_{N\in\mathbb N}$ is good in this sense, then for every ergodic invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T)$ and all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the multiple ergodic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \big(T^{\lfloor p_{1,N}(n)\rfloor}f_1\big)\cdots\big(T^{\lfloor p_{\ell,N}(n)\rfloor}f_\ell\big)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$, as $N\to\infty$, to $\int f_1\,d\mu\,\cdots\int f_\ell\,d\mu$.
category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along variable polynomials
status_search_result: The problem appears in Frantzikinakis's list of open problems on multiple ergodic averages and is referenced in recent surveys (e.g., a 2026 survey on joint ergodicity) which note that the area remains full of open problems and direct readers to the maintained problem list for updates. No source located reports a full resolution of the variable-polynomial good-implies-joint-ergodicity question; partial results exist for fixed polynomials and specific Hardy-field families.

original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ). If Λ is the von Mangoldt function and φ is a multiplicative function with values in the closed unit disk that has convergent means, do the weighted averages (1/N) Σ Λ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) and (1/N) Σ φ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measurable transformation preserving the probability measure $\mu$, and let $f,g\in L^{\infty}(\mu)$.

Recall the von Mangoldt function $\Lambda:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $\Lambda(n)=\log p$ if $n=p^k$ for some prime $p$ and integer $k\ge 1$, and $\Lambda(n)=0$ otherwise. Let $\varphi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a multiplicative function (i.e. $\varphi(mn)=\varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ whenever $\gcd(m,n)=1$) taking values in the closed unit disc $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\le 1\}$, and assume that $\varphi$ has convergent means, i.e. the limit
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)$$
exists in $\mathbb{C}$.

Prove or disprove: for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$, both of the weighted bilinear averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\Lambda(n)\,f(T^{n}x)\,g(T^{2n}x)\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)\,f(T^{n}x)\,g(T^{2n}x)$$
converge as $N\to\infty$.
status_search_result: Recent work (notably a 2025 preprint on pointwise convergence of polynomial multiple ergodic averages along the primes) establishes pointwise a.e. convergence of von Mangoldt-weighted multilinear averages along polynomials of pairwise distinct degrees. The bilinear case with iterates $T^n$ and $T^{2n}$ (both linear, hence of the same degree) is not covered by these results, and no result for general multiplicative weights with convergent means in this bilinear setting appears to be available. The problem therefore appears to remain open.

original_question: If p1, ..., pℓ are integer-valued generalized polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure preserving transformations on a common system, must the averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ always converge in L2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations. A generalized polynomial $p\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is any integer-valued function obtained from the identity function and integer constants by finitely many applications of addition, multiplication, and the floor function $\lfloor\,\cdot\,\rfloor$ (so e.g. $p(n)=\lfloor\alpha n^2\rfloor\lfloor\beta n\rfloor + \lfloor\gamma n\rfloor^3$ is allowed). 

Given integer-valued generalized polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell$ and bounded measurable functions $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(X,\mu)$, prove or disprove that the multiple ergodic averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T_1^{p_1(n)}f_1)(x)\cdots (T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell)(x)$$
converge in $L^2(X,\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.
category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along generalized polynomials
status_search_result: For ordinary integer polynomial iterates, Walsh (Annals 2012) proved L^2 convergence of multiple ergodic averages even for nilpotent groups of transformations, which subsumes the commuting polynomial case. However, generalized polynomials involve the floor function and are not polynomial maps, so Walsh's theorem does not apply. Recent results (Frantzikinakis–Kuca, and work on Hardy field functions) handle special subclasses, but no general L^2 convergence theorem for arbitrary generalized polynomial iterates with several commuting transformations appears in the literature; the question seems to remain open in full generality.

original_question: In the special case where T1, ..., Tℓ are weak mixing and p1, ..., pℓ are pairwise independent integer polynomials, must the averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ converge in L2(µ) to the product of the integrals ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\ldots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations. Recall that a measure-preserving transformation $T$ on $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ is called weakly mixing if for every $f,g\in L^2(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Big|\int (f\circ T^n)\,g\,d\mu-\int f\,d\mu\int g\,d\mu\Big|=0.$$
A family of polynomials $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ is called pairwise independent if $p_i$ and $p_i-p_j$ are non-constant for all $i\neq j$.

Assume that each $T_i$ is weakly mixing and that $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ are pairwise independent. Prove or disprove: for all $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\big(T_1^{p_1(n)}f_1\big)\cdots\big(T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell\big)=\int f_1\,d\mu\,\cdots\,\int f_\ell\,d\mu$$
in $L^2(\mu)$.
status_search_result: Recent work of Frantzikinakis and Kuca (Inventiones Math., 2024; arXiv:2207.12288) on joint ergodicity for commuting transformations gives necessary and sufficient conditions for joint ergodicity along pairwise independent polynomial iterates and, combined with seminorm-control results, settles this case: for commuting weakly mixing transformations and pairwise independent integer polynomials, the multiple polynomial average converges in $L^2$ to the product of the integrals.

context_brief: optimal lower bounds for polynomial recurrence
original_question: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ ∈ Z[t] are rationally independent and have zero constant term. For every measurable set A and every ε > 0, must there exist n ∈ N such that µ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} A) ≥ µ(A)^{ℓ+1} - ε?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ be a probability space equipped with $\ell$ commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$. Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$ be polynomials with zero constant term that are rationally independent (meaning that no nontrivial linear combination $\sum_{i=1}^\ell c_i p_i$ with $c_i\in\mathbb{Q}$, not all zero, is the zero polynomial; equivalently, the $p_i$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$).

Prove or disprove: for every measurable set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap T_2^{p_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A\bigr)\;\ge\;\mu(A)^{\ell+1}-\varepsilon.$$
status_search_result: Optimal lower bounds of the form $\mu(A)^{\ell+1}-\varepsilon$ are known in several special cases (e.g., for a single polynomial by Frantzikinakis–Kra and for certain independent families by Frantzikinakis), and Frantzikinakis established related results for non-commuting transformations along rationally independent polynomials. However, the full conjecture for $\ell$ commuting transformations along arbitrary rationally independent integer polynomials with zero constant term does not appear to have been resolved in general.

original_question: For every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and bounded functions f, g, do the commuting-transformation averages (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(S^n x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a standard probability space, and let $T,S:X\to X$ be two measure-preserving transformations that commute, i.e. $T\circ S = S\circ T$. For any pair of bounded measurable functions $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the double ergodic averages
$$A_N(f,g)(x) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^n x)\,g(S^n x), \qquad x\in X,\ N\ge 1.$$
Prove or disprove: for every such system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ and every $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the sequence $A_N(f,g)(x)$ converges as $N\to\infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.
status_search_result: The pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the double ergodic averages (1/N)Σ f(T^n x) g(S^n x) for commuting measure-preserving transformations T, S is a well-known long-standing open problem in ergodic theory. Norm (L^2) convergence was established by Conze–Lesigne, and pointwise convergence has been proved in special cases (e.g., randomized exponents, distal systems, strictly ergodic models, certain nilpotent settings), but the general deterministic pointwise problem remains unresolved as of recent literature.

context_brief: noncommuting polynomial recurrence with extra variable
original_question: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure preserving transformations, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Must every measurable set A of positive measure contain a pattern of the form A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)} A with positive measure for some m, n ∈ N?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell:X\to X$ be (not necessarily commuting) invertible measure-preserving transformations. Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[n]$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Prove or disprove: for every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$ there exist $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{\,m+p_1(n)}A\cap T_2^{\,m+p_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{\,m+p_\ell(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$
status_search_result: Frantzikinakis (2013, published 2023) established the desired multiple recurrence (in fact a positive lower bound on the averages) when the polynomials p_1,...,p_ℓ are rationally independent and have zero constant term, for arbitrary invertible measure-preserving T_i. However, in 2025 counterexamples were produced showing that double recurrence (ℓ=2) can fail for non-commuting transformations when the p_i are injective polynomials of equal degree (degree 1, or both degree ≥2), so the general problem as stated does not always hold. Thus the question is partially resolved: positive results exist under rational independence, while the unrestricted problem has been disproved in certain cases.

original_question: Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth. Is the family of integer sequences {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation exactly when every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) either stays farther than logarithmic scale from every real multiple of an integer polynomial, or differs from some real multiple of an integer polynomial by a finite limit, or stays within O(log t) of t/m for some nonzero integer m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Hardy field, i.e. a field (under pointwise operations) of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on half-lines $[t_0,\infty)$, closed under differentiation. A function $a\in\mathcal{H}$ is said to have polynomial growth if there exists an integer $k\ge 0$ with $|a(t)|/t^k\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. Fix $\ell\ge 1$ and let $F=\{a_1,\dots,a_\ell\}\subset\mathcal{H}$ consist of functions of polynomial growth. Write $\operatorname{span}^*(F)$ for the set of nonzero real linear combinations $c_1 a_1+\cdots+c_\ell a_\ell$.

For a measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ on a probability space and $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell):=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} T^{\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor}f_1\cdot T^{\lfloor a_2(n)\rfloor}f_2\cdots T^{\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor}f_\ell.$$
Call the family $\{(\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor),\dots,(\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor)\}$ \emph{good for $\ell$-convergence of a single transformation} if for every such system and every choice of $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages $A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$ converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

Prove or disprove: $\{(\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor),\dots,(\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor)\}$ is good for $\ell$-convergence of a single transformation if and only if every $a\in\operatorname{span}^*(F)$ satisfies at least one of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item $|a(t)-c\,p(t)|/\log t\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$ for every $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and every $p\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$; or
\item $a(t)-c\,p(t)\to d$ as $t\to\infty$ for some $c,d\in\mathbb{R}$ and some $p\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$; or
\item $|a(t)-t/m|\le C\log t$ for all sufficiently large $t$, for some nonzero $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and some $C>0$.
\end{itemize}

status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Tsinas (arXiv:2109.07941) and Frantzikinakis–Tsinas (arXiv:2006.03558) established mean convergence of such multiple ergodic averages for Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth under the "logarithmic independence" condition (the first bullet), confirming several conjectures of Frantzikinakis. The full equivalence with the three-case characterization has not been fully verified in the surveyed literature, so the problem appears partially solved.

original_question: If a and b are distinct positive nonintegers, then for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, must the averages (1/N) Σ f(T^[n^a] x) g(T^[n^b] x) converge almost everywhere to ∫f dµ · ∫g dµ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct positive non-integers. Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be an ergodic measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measurable transformation preserving the probability measure $\mu$, and ergodicity means every $T$-invariant measurable set has measure $0$ or $1$. For real $t$, let $[t]$ denote the integer part of $t$. Determine whether, for every such system and every pair of bounded measurable functions $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^{[n^a]}x)\, g(T^{[n^b]}x)$$
converge, as $N\to\infty$, to $\left(\int f\,d\mu\right)\left(\int g\,d\mu\right)$ for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.

status_search_result: The deterministic pointwise convergence problem for bilinear ergodic averages along fractional power sequences $[n^a],[n^b]$ is listed among Frantzikinakis' open problems. Although random and polynomial bilinear analogues (e.g., Krause–Mirek–Tao for $n,n^2$) and related joint ergodicity results have been established, the deterministic Hardy-power case with distinct positive non-integers $a,b$ remains open as of recent surveys and 2024–2025 work.

original_question: Can one find a Hardy-field function a(t) with super-polynomial growth, meaning a(t)/t^k → ∞ for every k, such that the integer sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote a Hardy field, that is, a field (under pointwise addition and multiplication) of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on half-lines $[c,\infty)$, closed under differentiation. For $a\in\mathcal{H}$, write $[a(n)]$ for the sequence of integer parts $\lfloor a(n)\rfloor$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

A sequence of integers $(b_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is said to be good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers if, for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, one has
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-b_n}A\cap T^{-2b_n}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-kb_n}A\right)>0,$$
and, moreover, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{b_n}x)\,f_2(T^{2b_n}x)\cdots f_k(T^{kb_n}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

The function $a\in\mathcal{H}$ is said to have super-polynomial growth if $a(t)/t^k\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$ for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$.

Question: Does there exist a function $a\in\mathcal{H}$ of super-polynomial growth such that the integer sequence $([a(n)])_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers in the sense above?
category_tag: Hardy field sequences and multiple recurrence
status_search_result: Recent works on multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy field sequences (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Host 2020, and follow-ups on Furstenberg systems of Hardy sequences) treat the polynomial-growth regime; results allowing super-polynomial growth have been pursued (notably a 2025 preprint on Furstenberg systems of certain super-polynomial Hardy sequences), but no published result is found explicitly producing a super-polynomial Hardy function whose integer parts are good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers in full generality. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Is the oscillatory sequence [n sin n] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denote the integer part of a real number $x$, and consider the integer-valued sequence $a(n) = \lfloor n \sin n\rfloor$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

A sequence $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset\mathbb{Z}$ is called good for multiple recurrence of powers if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every integer $k\geq 1$, and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{a(n)}A\cap T^{2a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{k\,a(n)}A\bigr) > 0.$$

It is called good for multiple convergence of powers if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every integer $k\geq 1$, and all $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{a(n)}x)\,f_2(T^{2a(n)}x)\cdots f_k(T^{k\,a(n)}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

Prove or disprove: the sequence $(\lfloor n\sin n\rfloor)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is good for multiple recurrence of powers and good for multiple convergence of powers.
status_search_result: Searches for results on whether $\lfloor n\sin n\rfloor$ is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers did not turn up any resolution. Recent work by Bergelson, Moreira, Richter and others on single and multiple recurrence along non-polynomial sequences treats classes such as $\lfloor n^a\rfloor$ and slowly varying functions but does not cover $\lfloor n\sin n\rfloor$, which is non-monotone and not equidistributed in a standard way. No paper claiming a proof or disproof was located, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Do the prime numbers contain infinitely many patterns of the forms {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], ..., m + ℓ[n^c]} and {m, m + [n^c1], ..., m + [n^cℓ]} for given positive real exponents c, c1, ..., cℓ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell$ be a positive integer and let $c, c_1, c_2, \dots, c_\ell$ be positive real numbers. For a real number $x$, denote by $[x]$ its integer part (floor). Prove or disprove each of the following statements:

(a) There exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which there is a positive integer $m$ such that all of
$$m,\; m + [n^c],\; m + 2[n^c],\; \dots,\; m + \ell\,[n^c]$$
are prime numbers.

(b) There exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which there is a positive integer $m$ such that all of
$$m,\; m + [n^{c_1}],\; m + [n^{c_2}],\; \dots,\; m + [n^{c_\ell}]$$
are prime numbers.

In other words, decide whether the primes contain infinitely many "Hardy-type" arithmetic progressions with common difference $[n^c]$ of length $\ell+1$, and infinitely many configurations whose gaps from a base point $m$ are prescribed by floors of arbitrary positive real powers of $n$.
status_search_result: The general problem appears to be open. The literature establishes that Piatetski-Shapiro primes (primes of the form $[n^c]$) exist infinitely often only in restricted ranges of $c$ (currently roughly $1 < c < 243/205$), and analogous results for primes in arithmetic progressions with Piatetski-Shapiro common difference are known only under similar restrictions. No result is known that handles arbitrary positive real exponents $c, c_1, \dots, c_\ell$ and arbitrary length $\ell$, so the full conjecture remains unresolved.

original_question: For a random sequence (a_n(ω)) selected with nσ_n → ∞, is it almost surely true that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and bounded functions f, g, the averages (1/N) Σ T^n f · S^{a_n(ω)} g converge in L2 to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)? If σ_n = n^{-a} with a ∈ (0,1), does the convergence also hold almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\sigma_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of numbers in $[0,1]$ with $n\sigma_n \to \infty$. Construct a random sequence $(a_n(\omega))_{n\ge 1}$ of positive integers as follows: on some probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$, let $(\xi_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be independent $\{0,1\}$-valued random variables with $\mathbb P(\xi_n=1)=\sigma_n$, and let $a_1(\omega)<a_2(\omega)<\cdots$ be the enumeration in increasing order of $\{n\ge 1:\xi_n(\omega)=1\}$.

Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T,S)$ be any measure-preserving system in which $T,S:X\to X$ are (not necessarily commuting) invertible measure-preserving transformations of a probability space. $$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T^n f)(x)\,(S^{a_n(\omega)} g)(x) \;=\; \mathbb E(f\mid\mathcal I_T)(x)\cdot\mathbb E(g\mid\mathcal I_S)(x),$$
with the limit taken in $L^2(\mu)$.

(b) If in addition $\sigma_n=n^{-a}$ for some $a\in(0,1)$, show that the convergence in (a) also holds pointwise $\mu$-almost everywhere.

original_question: A system with multiplicative structure is a quadruple (X, X, µ, T_n) where T_0 = T_1 = id and T_m ◦ T_n = T_{mn}. In every such system and for every measurable set A of positive measure, do there exist integers m > n ≥ 1 such that µ(T_{2mn} A ∩ T_{(m-n)(m+n)} A) > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a probability space. Suppose $\{T_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is a family of invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ satisfying
$$T_0 = T_1 = \mathrm{id}, \qquad T_m \circ T_n = T_{mn} \quad \text{for all } m,n\in\mathbb{N}.$$
We call $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,\{T_n\})$ a measure-preserving system with multiplicative structure.

Prove or disprove: for every such system and for every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exist integers $m>n\geq 1$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(T_{2mn}\,A \;\cap\; T_{(m-n)(m+n)}\,A\bigr) > 0.$$

(The pair $(2mn,\,(m-n)(m+n))$ is the standard parametrization of the legs of a Pythagorean triple.)
status_search_result: Recent work by Frantzikinakis and collaborators (2023–2025) establishes recurrence along generalized Pythagorean triples for restricted classes of multiplicative measure-preserving actions (notably pretentious systems), and proves partition regularity of Pythagorean pairs, but the general multiplicative recurrence question for arbitrary multiplicative systems on Pythagorean configurations $(2mn,(m-n)(m+n))$ does not appear to be resolved. Surveys note that whether sets arising from Pythagorean triples are sets of multiplicative recurrence remains unknown.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: In non-commutative, group-based cryptography, what class of group is the most appropriate platform group for building cryptographic schemes?
status_search_result: This is a broad foundational open question in non-commutative cryptography. Various platforms have been proposed (braid groups, Thompson's group F, polycyclic groups, free metabelian groups, small cancellation groups, hyperbolic groups, matrix groups over rings), and many have been subjected to successful cryptanalyses (e.g. length-based attacks on braid groups, linear attacks via Lawrence–Krammer representations). No consensus or proof identifies a single optimal platform class, and the problem remains open as a guiding research question in the field.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: How can one prove that a chosen group platform is secure for non-commutative cryptographic constructions such as public-key exchange protocols, digital-signature schemes, and authentication schemes?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a non-abelian (in general, infinite or finite) group, called a platform group, on which one builds non-commutative cryptographic constructions such as a public-key exchange protocol, a digital signature scheme, or an authentication scheme. The security of such constructions typically relies on the conjectured computational hardness of certain group-theoretic problems in G (for example, the conjugacy search problem, the word problem, the simultaneous conjugacy problem, the decomposition problem, or related problems).

Develop a general framework, together with explicit criteria on the platform group G, that allows one to prove (in a rigorous reductionist sense, e.g. by reducing the security of the protocol against a specified adversarial model to a precisely formulated, average-case hard computational problem in G) that the chosen platform G yields provably secure non-commutative public-key exchange protocols, digital signature schemes, and authentication schemes.

Concretely: identify a class of platform groups G and an associated family of group-theoretic problems P(G) such that
(i) P(G) is hard in the average case under a natural distribution on instances,
(ii) the security of the proposed key exchange / signature / authentication scheme based on G can be reduced to P(G) in a standard cryptographic security model (e.g. IND-CPA, EUF-CMA, or analogous notions), and
(iii) the reduction yields concrete, quantifiable security parameters.
status_search_result: The question of providing fully reductionist provable security for non-commutative group-based cryptographic schemes (key exchange, signatures, authentication) over a chosen platform group remains an active research problem. Recent works (e.g., the 2018 "Provably Secure Integration Cryptosystem on Non-Commutative Group", the generalization of LWE/LPN to "learning homomorphisms with noise" on non-abelian groups, and survey/status papers on polycyclic and quantum-era group-based cryptography from 2016–2022) propose partial frameworks and specific platform candidates but do not deliver a general solution. No comprehensive provable-security framework comparable to that available in the abelian/lattice setting has been established.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Can the security of the non-commutative cryptographic protocols surveyed in the paper be analyzed rigorously?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of public-key cryptographic protocols whose security is based on algorithmic problems in finitely generated non-abelian groups. Representative examples include:

(a) The Anshel–Anshel–Goldfeld key-exchange protocol, whose security rests on variants of the simultaneous conjugacy search problem in a non-abelian group G: given tuples (a_1,...,a_n) and (b a_1 b^{-1},...,b a_n b^{-1}) of elements of G, recover an element b' such that b' a_i b'^{-1} = b a_i b^{-1} for all i.

(b) The Ko–Lee–Cheon–Han–Kang–Park protocol and related Diffie–Hellman-type schemes in braid groups B_n and other non-abelian platform groups, whose security rests on the conjugacy search problem (given x and y = g x g^{-1} in G, find g) and the decomposition / generalized conjugacy search problems in distinguished subgroups.

(c) Protocols based on the word problem, the membership problem, or the twisted conjugacy problem in platform groups such as braid groups, Thompson's group F, polycyclic groups, Grigorchuk groups, and finitely generated linear (matrix) groups.

Provide a rigorous security analysis of these non-abelian group-based cryptographic protocols. Specifically:

1. For each protocol, identify the precise computational problem P (in a specified platform group G with a specified distribution on instances) whose hardness is necessary and sufficient for the protocol's security under a stated adversarial model (passive eavesdropper, chosen-plaintext, chosen-ciphertext).

2. Establish, with proof, either (i) a polynomial-time reduction from a well-studied hard problem to P, thereby giving a provable security guarantee, or (ii) a polynomial-time algorithm (deterministic, randomized, or generic-case / heuristic with rigorous success-probability bounds) that breaks P on the instance distribution used by the protocol.

3. In particular, determine the worst-case and generic-case computational complexity of the conjugacy search problem, the simultaneous conjugacy search problem, and the decomposition problem in the platform groups listed in (a)–(c), and decide whether each protocol admits a rigorous proof of security or a rigorous polynomial-time attack.
status_search_result: Surveys and monographs from 2011 onward (e.g., Myasnikov–Shpilrain–Ushakov's AMS volume on non-commutative cryptography, the 2016 polycyclic-group survey on arXiv, and later surveys of public-key cryptography over non-abelian groups) consistently note that rigorous security proofs for the main non-abelian group-based protocols are lacking, and that the precise complexity (in particular generic-case complexity) of the underlying conjugacy-type search problems in platform groups such as braid groups and polycyclic groups remains unresolved. Specific schemes (e.g., the original Ko–Lee braid-group protocol) have been broken by length-based and linear-representation attacks, but a unified rigorous security analysis of the surveyed family of protocols is still considered an open problem.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: For polycyclic-group cryptographic constructions that rely on commuting subgroups, which choice of commuting subgroups makes the schemes secure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a polycyclic group (a group admitting a subnormal series $1 = G_0 \triangleleft G_1 \triangleleft \cdots \triangleleft G_n = G$ with each quotient $G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic). Two subgroups $A, B \le G$ are called commuting if $ab = ba$ for every $a \in A$ and $b \in B$ (equivalently, $[A,B] = 1$).

Several non-abelian key-exchange and cryptographic protocols use such a pair $(A,B)$ in $G$ as public data: a public element $g \in G$ is fixed, Alice picks a secret $a \in A$ and publishes $a^{-1} g a$ (or $g^a$), Bob picks a secret $b \in B$ and publishes $b^{-1} g b$, and the shared key $b^{-1} a^{-1} g a b = a^{-1} b^{-1} g b a$ is recoverable by both parties because $A$ and $B$ commute elementwise. The security of such schemes rests on the computational hardness, in $G$, of recovering the secrets from the public transcript (variants of the conjugacy search and commutator key-exchange problems restricted to $A$ and $B$).

Problem: Determine an explicit construction of a polycyclic group $G$ together with a pair of elementwise-commuting subgroups $A, B \le G$ such that the associated key-exchange/commutator protocols above are provably (or at least heuristically) secure against all known attacks — i.e., characterize which choices of commuting subgroup pairs $(A,B)$ in polycyclic platform groups yield secure instances of these schemes.
status_search_result: A 2016 follow-up survey on the status of polycyclic group-based cryptography (Gryak–Kahrobaei) and a 2022 survey on group-based cryptography in the quantum era (Kahrobaei–Flores) both continue to discuss the choice of commuting subgroups in polycyclic platforms as an unresolved design issue, with no general characterization of secure choices established. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: What is the computational complexity of the decision conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups, for example for the Eick-Ostheimer algorithm?
self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series
$$G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_n = \{1\}$$
in which every quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. Every polycyclic group is finitely presented and admits a polycyclic presentation, with respect to which group elements have a unique normal form. The decision conjugacy problem in $G$ asks: given two elements $u, v \in G$ (encoded by their normal forms), decide whether there exists $g \in G$ such that $g^{-1} u g = v$.

It is known that the decision conjugacy problem is solvable for every polycyclic group, and concrete algorithms (such as the one of Eick and Ostheimer, which reduces the problem to computations involving unit groups and orbit-stabilizer problems in algebraic number fields and matrix groups) realize such a decision procedure.

Determine the computational complexity of the decision conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups. In particular, give a rigorous worst-case complexity analysis (as a function of the input size, e.g.\ the bit-length of the polycyclic presentation together with the input elements) of the Eick–Ostheimer conjugacy algorithm.
status_search_result: A complete worst-case complexity analysis of the Eick–Ostheimer algorithm itself does not appear to have been carried out; experimental studies (Eick–Kahrobaei) showed the running time grows rapidly with Hirsch length. On the structural side, partial progress is available: Cavallo and Kahrobaei (2014, arXiv:1403.4153) exhibit a family of polycyclic groups for which the (uniform) conjugacy problem is NP-complete, showing that no polynomial-time algorithm is possible in general unless P = NP. The general status of the precise complexity of the decision conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups remains an open problem in the polycyclic-group cryptography literature.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: What is the computational complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a polycyclic group, given by a finite polycyclic presentation (so that elements are represented by collected normal words). For an endomorphism φ : G → G, two elements u, v ∈ G are said to be φ-twisted conjugate if there exists x ∈ G such that v = x^{-1} u φ(x). The twisted search conjugacy problem is: given as input a polycyclic presentation of G, an endomorphism φ : G → G (specified by the images of the generators), and two elements u, v ∈ G that are known (or promised) to be φ-twisted conjugate, compute an element x ∈ G such that v = x^{-1} u φ(x).

Determine the computational complexity of this problem as a function of the input size (the lengths of the words representing u, v, the images φ(g_i), and the size of the presentation). In particular, decide whether it admits a polynomial-time algorithm, or establish hardness (e.g., NP-hardness) for some family of polycyclic groups.
status_search_result: Recent work provides decidability results and practical algorithms for the twisted conjugacy problem in polycyclic and virtually polycyclic groups (e.g., Tertooy 2020, 2025), and shows the (uniform) ordinary conjugacy problem can be NP-complete on certain polycyclic families. However, a precise complexity classification of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups does not appear to have been established; subsequent surveys (e.g., the 2016 polycyclic-cryptography status survey) continue to list it among open questions.

paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
original_question: What is the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a polycyclic group, given by a finite polycyclic presentation, so that every element of G has a unique normal form as a word in the polycyclic generators. The search conjugacy problem in G is the following algorithmic task: given as input a pair (u, v) of elements of G that are known to be conjugate in G, find an element x of G such that x^{-1} u x = v.

Recall the framework of generic-case complexity. For each n, let I_n denote the set of valid inputs (pairs of conjugate elements) whose total size (sum of normal-form lengths) is at most n, equipped with the uniform probability measure. A subset S of inputs is called generic if the fraction |S ∩ I_n| / |I_n| tends to 1 as n → ∞, and strongly generic if this convergence is exponentially fast. An algorithm A is said to solve the search conjugacy problem with generic-case complexity in a class C (e.g. polynomial time, linear time) if there exists a generic subset S of inputs such that A halts on every input in S within the resource bounds of C and outputs a correct conjugator, while on inputs outside S the algorithm may fail to terminate or output "don't know."

Determine the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups: namely, identify the smallest natural complexity class C such that for every (or for a suitable broad family of) finitely presented polycyclic group G, there is an algorithm solving the search conjugacy problem in G with generic-case complexity in C, and prove a matching generic-case lower bound.
status_search_result: Related results exist: the uniform conjugacy problem over a family of polycyclic groups is known to be NP-complete (Cavallo–Kahrobaei, 2014), and generic-case polynomial-time algorithms have been established for related classes (e.g., Baumslag's group, free-by-cyclic groups). However, no source clearly settles the generic-case complexity of the search conjugacy problem in general polycyclic groups, so the status appears to remain unresolved.

original_question: Can the computer algebra system GAP be used as a practical and secure implementation platform for these non-commutative cryptographic schemes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider non-commutative group-based cryptographic schemes (such as key exchange, encryption, and authentication protocols whose security relies on algorithmic problems in non-abelian groups, e.g., the conjugacy search problem, the simultaneous conjugacy search problem, the word problem, or the decomposition problem in platform groups like braid groups, polycyclic groups, Thompson's group, or matrix groups over finite rings). Let GAP denote the open-source computer algebra system "Groups, Algorithms, Programming," which provides a programming language and libraries for computational discrete algebra and computational group theory.

paper_title: Open Questions in GRB Physics
original_question: What progenitor systems actually produce the main classes of gamma-ray bursts? More specifically, which stellar or compact-object channels generate massive-star GRBs and compact-star GRBs, given that current evidence is indirect, only a small and biased subset of long GRBs have secure supernova associations, and some short-duration or high-redshift events do not fit a simple neutron-star-merger picture?
self_contained_problem:
Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are intense, transient flashes of cosmic gamma radiation, conventionally divided by their prompt-emission duration into two main classes: long-duration GRBs (T90 ≳ 2 s), often called massive-star or Type II GRBs, and short-duration GRBs (T90 ≲ 2 s), often called compact-star or Type I GRBs. The prevailing hypothesis associates long GRBs with the gravitational collapse of rapidly rotating, massive stars (the "collapsar" channel, which can produce Type Ic broad-line supernovae), and short GRBs with the coalescence of compact-object binaries (double neutron stars or neutron-star–black-hole systems).

However, only a small, observationally biased subset of long GRBs have secure supernova associations, several short-duration and high-redshift bursts do not fit a simple neutron-star-merger picture, and some long-duration events show kilonova-like signatures expected from compact mergers rather than hypernova signatures.

Problem. Identify, from first principles and observational diagnostics, the actual progenitor systems that produce each main class of GRB. Concretely:

(a) Determine the full set of stellar or compact-object channels that give rise to massive-star (long-duration) GRBs, including conditions on stellar mass, metallicity, rotation, and binarity required to launch a successful relativistic jet, and explain the apparent paucity of secure supernova associations.

(b) Determine the full set of compact-object channels (e.g., NS–NS, NS–BH, WD–NS, WD–BH, accretion-induced collapse) that give rise to compact-star (short-duration or merger-driven) GRBs, and account for short or high-redshift events that are inconsistent with a standard neutron-star-merger origin.

(c) Provide observational discriminants — using prompt light curves, afterglow spectra, host-galaxy properties, offsets, and multi-messenger (gravitational-wave, kilonova) signatures — that uniquely map an individual burst to its progenitor channel, replacing duration-based classification with progenitor-based classification.
status_search_result: The progenitor question has been partially resolved since the original posing. The 2017 multi-messenger event GW170817/GRB 170817A confirmed binary neutron-star mergers as one channel for short GRBs, and several long GRBs have secure broad-line Type Ic supernova associations supporting the collapsar channel. However, anomalous events such as GRB 211211A and GRB 191019A (long-duration bursts with kilonova-like signatures suggesting merger origins) and GRB 200826A (a short burst with a supernova association) demonstrate that a complete, progenitor-based classification mapping all GRBs to specific stellar/compact-object channels remains open as of 2026.

paper_title: Open Questions in GRB Physics
original_question: What is the composition of gamma-ray-burst ejecta at the prompt-emission radius: are the outflows primarily matter-dominated fireballs or magnetically dominated jets, and what are the baryon, lepton-pair, and neutron contents of the flow? Here the key quantity is the magnetization sigma, the ratio of Poynting flux to matter flux, and the problem is to determine whether sigma is much less than 1, of order 1, or much greater than 1 in the emitting region.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a gamma-ray burst (GRB) relativistic outflow at the radius where the prompt gamma-ray emission is produced. Define the magnetization parameter

σ = F_P / F_M,

where F_P is the Poynting (electromagnetic) energy flux and F_M is the matter (kinetic plus rest-mass) energy flux carried by the outflow through a surface at the prompt-emission radius. The outflow may contain baryons, electron–positron pairs, and free neutrons.

Determine the composition of the GRB ejecta at the prompt-emission radius. Specifically:

1. Decide whether the outflow there is matter-dominated (a "fireball" regime, σ ≪ 1), roughly equipartitioned (σ ~ 1), or magnetically dominated (a Poynting-flux-dominated jet, σ ≫ 1).
2. Quantify the baryon loading, the relative content of electron–positron pairs, and the neutron component of the flow.

Provide the diagnostic observational and theoretical criteria that fix σ and the particle content in the emitting region, and characterize the answer either universally across GRBs or as a distribution over the GRB population.
status_search_result: The composition of GRB outflows at the prompt-emission radius remains an open and actively debated question. Recent studies (e.g., analyses of GRB 230307A in 2024 and GRB 221009A) provide evidence that some bursts are Poynting-flux-dominated (σ ≫ 1, consistent with the ICMART model), while others (e.g., GRB 090902B) show a quasi-thermal component pointing to matter-dominated fireballs. No universal value of σ is established across the GRB population, and the baryon/pair/neutron content remains poorly constrained from data.

paper_title: Open Questions in GRB Physics
original_question: What radiation mechanism produces the prompt gamma-ray-burst spectrum that is usually fit by the empirical Band function? The unresolved possibilities include synchrotron or jitter emission from accelerated leptons, synchrotron self-Compton emission, Comptonization of thermal or photospheric photons, and hadronic emission, and the explanation must account for observed low-energy spectral slopes, cooling behavior, and peak energies.
status_search_result: Recent literature through 2024 confirms that the dominant radiation mechanism producing the prompt GRB spectrum fit by the Band function remains an open and actively debated question. Reviews and recent papers describe it as "an unsolved puzzle," and no single model (synchrotron, SSC, photospheric Comptonization, or hadronic) has been shown to fit the broadband spectrum and explain low-energy slopes, cooling, and peak energies for the GRB population.

paper_title: Open Questions in GRB Physics
original_question: Which components of observed post-burst gamma-ray-burst light curves are genuinely produced by the external forward or reverse shock, and how should jet breaks, chromatic behavior, and reverse-shock signatures be interpreted once internal central-engine contributions are removed? This is especially important in the Swift era, where X-ray afterglows commonly contain multiple components that complicate standard external-shock parameter inference.
self_contained_problem:
Consider observed multi-wavelength light curves of gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows obtained in the Swift era, where the X-ray and optical emission following the prompt gamma-ray phase is typically modeled as synchrotron emission from a relativistic blast wave decelerating in the circumburst medium (the external forward shock) and, at early times, from a short-lived reverse shock crossing the ejecta, with possible additional contributions from a long-lived central engine (e.g., late prompt emission, plateau, flares).

Define the following:
- An "external forward shock" component is emission whose temporal decay indices α and spectral indices β across bands satisfy the standard closure relations of synchrotron blast-wave theory for a given jet/medium configuration.
- A "reverse shock" component is the short-lived, typically optical/radio early-time emission from the shocked ejecta predicted by Sari–Piran-type models.
- A "jet break" is a steepening of the light curve due to the bulk Lorentz factor dropping below the inverse jet opening angle; it is "achromatic" if the break time and post-break decay slope agree across all observing bands (X-ray, optical, radio), and "chromatic" otherwise. Call a jet break "platinum" if it is verified achromatic across all available bands simultaneously.

The problem: Provide a method, supported by quantitative criteria, to decompose observed Swift-era GRB afterglow light curves into (a) the genuine external forward-shock component, (b) the genuine reverse-shock component, and (c) contributions of internal/central-engine origin, so that:

1. The external-shock parameters (isotropic kinetic energy E, circumburst density n, electron and magnetic energy fractions ε_e and ε_B, electron index p, jet opening angle θ_j) can be reliably inferred only from (a) and (b).
2. One can determine whether any observed light-curve break is a platinum (achromatic across all wavelengths) jet break, and explain the prevalence of chromatic breaks under the proposed decomposition.
3. The reverse-shock signatures (e.g., early optical flash, radio flare) predicted under thin-shell vs. thick-shell regimes can be unambiguously identified or ruled out in each event.

Decide, on the basis of currently available multi-wavelength GRB afterglow data, whether such a decomposition exists in general, and in particular whether any observed jet break to date qualifies as platinum.
status_search_result: Subsequent systematic studies (e.g., a 2015 analysis of 85 Swift-era GRBs with well-monitored X-ray and optical light curves) graded events by consistency with external forward-shock predictions and found that simple forward-shock models account for roughly half of GRBs, while up to ~90% can be fit when extended models (long-lasting reverse shock, structured jets, varying medium profiles) are invoked. A small fraction show clearly chromatic behavior incompatible with single-component external-shock models. No truly achromatic ("platinum") jet break across all wavelengths has been unambiguously identified, so the interpretive question remains partially open.

paper_title: Open Questions in GRB Physics
original_question: Are massive-star gamma-ray bursts reliable tracers of the star-formation history of the universe across cosmic time, especially at high redshift?
self_contained_problem:
Long-duration gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) are believed to originate from the core collapse of certain massive stars. Under the hypothesis that the comoving rate density of such bursts is proportional to the cosmic star-formation rate density (SFRD), one may attempt to use the observed LGRB redshift distribution (corrected for instrumental detection thresholds, beaming, and luminosity function) as a direct tracer of the SFRD ψ(z) of the universe.

Determine whether massive-star (long-duration) gamma-ray bursts are reliable, unbiased tracers of the cosmic star-formation history across all redshifts, and in particular at high redshift (z ≳ 3–4). Specifically: does the comoving LGRB rate density R_GRB(z), inferred from observed samples, satisfy R_GRB(z) ∝ ψ(z) over the full observable redshift range, or is there a systematic, redshift-dependent bias (for example arising from metallicity dependence of the progenitor channel, evolution of the initial mass function, or evolution of LGRB luminosity/beaming properties) that prevents such a proportionality? Quantify any such bias and characterize the redshift regime, if any, in which LGRBs may be used as unbiased tracers of star formation.
category_tag: Gamma-ray bursts and cosmic star formation
status_search_result: Multiple studies (2014–2025) have established that long GRBs are biased tracers of star formation, with the bias well explained by a metallicity threshold on progenitors (logOH ≲ 8.55) and possible evolution in LGRB properties (luminosity function, beaming). Under the metallicity-threshold model, LGRBs are expected to become approximately unbiased tracers of the SFRD at z ≳ 3, when most star formation occurs below the metallicity ceiling. However, recent work (2024–2025) indicates additional evolving properties beyond a simple metallicity cut are needed for full reconciliation, so the question is partially resolved rather than fully closed.
