paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: Can a variational or related time-propagation method impose positive semidefiniteness on the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3), and on the resulting one- and two-body reduced density matrices γ and Γ, despite the fact that approximate truncation can break the trace relations connecting these density matrices?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-fermion quantum system with antisymmetric pure or mixed state, and let
- γ denote its one-body reduced density matrix (1-RDM),
- Γ denote its two-body reduced density matrix (2-RDM),
- Γ^(3) denote its three-body reduced density matrix (3-RDM),

obtained by partial traces of the full N-body density operator. Exactly, these objects satisfy contraction (trace) relations
   Tr_3 Γ^(3) = c₂ Γ,    Tr_2 Γ = c₁ γ,
for appropriate combinatorial constants c₁, c₂ depending on N, and each of γ, Γ, Γ^(3) is positive semidefinite.

A truncation of the time-dependent BBGKY-type hierarchy of equations for the reduced density matrices closes the evolution at the level of Γ^(3) by introducing an approximate closure that expresses the four-body RDM in terms of lower-order ones. Such an approximate closure generally breaks the exact trace/contraction relations between Γ^(3), Γ, and γ during time evolution, so that even if Γ^(3)(t) is enforced to be positive semidefinite, the contracted matrices Γ(t) and γ(t) need not remain positive semidefinite.

Problem. Construct a variational (or otherwise constrained) time-propagation scheme for the truncated hierarchy that, throughout the evolution t ≥ 0:
(i) keeps Γ^(3)(t) positive semidefinite, and
(ii) simultaneously guarantees positive semidefiniteness of the resulting one-body and two-body reduced density matrices γ(t) and Γ(t),

despite the fact that the approximate closure breaks the exact contraction relations connecting Γ^(3), Γ, and γ. Equivalently, exhibit a method for imposing these positivity constraints dynamically during time evolution, or prove that no such scheme can simultaneously satisfy (i) and (ii) under a generic closure that violates the contraction identities.
status_search_result: Web search shows extensive literature on variational determination of ground-state 2-RDMs via semidefinite programming with N-representability/positive semidefiniteness constraints, but no established time-dependent scheme that simultaneously enforces positive semidefiniteness of Γ^(3) and of the contracted γ, Γ when the truncation breaks the contraction relations. The question of designing such a constrained time-propagation scheme appears to remain an open research direction.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Extension beyond the Hubbard-model test case
original_question: Do the instability, density-divergence, and fermionic-constraint-violation phenomena observed for BBGKY truncations in a finite Hubbard model persist in small molecules and more complex correlated-electron systems, and how can the proposed partial remedies be validated in those settings?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an interacting fermionic many-body system whose state is described by reduced density matrices (RDMs) $ho^{(p)}$ of orders $p=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy: each $ho^{(p)}$ evolves according to an equation that couples it to $ho^{(p+1)}$. A standard practical scheme truncates this hierarchy at second order by keeping the coupled evolution equations for the one-body matrix $ho^{(1)}$ and the two-body matrix $ho^{(2)}$, while approximating the three-body matrix $ho^{(3)}$ by a closure expressed in terms of $ho^{(1)}$ and $ho^{(2)}$ (e.g. cluster expansions that neglect or partially keep the genuine three-body correlation). 

For finite Hubbard lattices driven out of equilibrium, such truncations are known to display three pathological phenomena: (i) dynamical instability of the time evolution; (ii) divergence of local densities $n_i(t)=\langle c_i^\dagger c_iangle(t)$; and (iii) violation of $N$-representability conditions for fermions, in particular loss of positive semidefiniteness of $ho^{(2)}$ and of the hole-hole and particle-hole matrices, together with violation of the antisymmetry/contraction sum rules connecting $ho^{(2)}$ and $ho^{(1)}$. Several partial remedies have been proposed, including purification/projection schemes that restore positivity at each time step and minimally-invasive corrections of the equations of motion that enforce contraction consistency.

Problem. Determine whether the three pathologies (i)–(iii) above persist in the time-dependent BBGKY truncations at the two-body level when the underlying system is (a) a small molecule described by an ab initio electronic Hamiltonian in a finite single-particle basis, and (b) more general correlated-electron systems beyond Hubbard-type lattice models. Furthermore, formulate and validate, in these settings, the proposed partial remedies (positivity-restoring purification of $ho^{(2)}$ and contraction-preserving corrections), establishing whether they yield stable, density-bounded, and $N$-representable time evolutions of $ho^{(1)}$ and $ho^{(2)}$ under external driving.
status_search_result: Recent work has partially addressed the problem. Projective purification schemes for the time-dependent two-body reduced density matrix (TD2RDM) and minimal-invasive correction algorithms have been developed and shown to stabilize the BBGKY truncation at second order in quench dynamics of the Fermi-Hubbard model. However, systematic validation of these remedies for small molecules and general correlated-electron systems beyond Hubbard models has not been comprehensively established in the literature surveyed, so the broader question remains only partially resolved.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: How can the BBGKY reduced-density-matrix approach be developed in linear response theory for optical spectra, where nonlinearities in the time-dependent hierarchy are removed by construction and may therefore avoid some of the divergence mechanisms seen in nonlinear propagation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite system of N identical fermions governed by a Hamiltonian H = H_0 + V_ext(t), where H_0 contains one-body kinetic terms and a two-body interaction w(x_i, x_j), and V_ext(t) is a time-dependent one-body external perturbation that is small in amplitude. Define the s-particle reduced density matrices ρ_s(t) (s = 1, 2, ...) by partial traces of the N-body density operator, and let them satisfy the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy

  i ℏ ∂_t ρ_s = [H_s, ρ_s] + Tr_{s+1}[w_{s,s+1}, ρ_{s+1}],

where H_s is the s-body Hamiltonian and w_{s,s+1} is the interaction between the s tracked particles and particle s+1. Linearize this hierarchy about a stationary equilibrium state ρ_s^{(0)} by writing ρ_s(t) = ρ_s^{(0)} + δρ_s(t) with δρ_s of first order in V_ext, and keep only terms linear in the perturbation, thereby obtaining a linear-response BBGKY system in which the intrinsic nonlinearities of the full hierarchy are removed by construction.

Develop a closed, self-consistent truncation of this linear-response hierarchy at the level of δρ_1 (and possibly δρ_2) suitable for computing optical absorption spectra, i.e. the imaginary part of the dynamical density-density (or current-current) response function. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a closure relation expressing δρ_2 (or δρ_3) in terms of δρ_1 and the equilibrium correlations ρ_2^{(0)}, ρ_3^{(0)} that respects the relevant conservation laws (particle number, energy, momentum) and the symmetry/antisymmetry constraints on reduced density matrices.

(b) Prove that the resulting linear integro-differential equation for δρ_1(t) admits a global-in-time solution for any bounded V_ext(t), and that the associated response kernel χ(ω) is free of the spurious singularities or runaway behavior that can arise in fully nonlinear truncated BBGKY propagations.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Reliability of propagating only the second BBGKY equation
original_question: Is it possible to make propagation based only on the second BBGKY equation for the two-body reduced density matrix into a generally reliable approach, given that approximate closures can produce large total-energy fluctuations and can still diverge even when compatibility between the first and second hierarchy equations is no longer the immediate issue?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-fermion quantum system with a Hamiltonian of the form
H = Σ_i h(i) + (1/2) Σ_{i≠j} v(i,j),
and let ρ_s(t) denote the s-body reduced density matrix obtained by tracing the full N-body density matrix over N−s particles. The Bogoliubov–Born–Green–Kirkwood–Yvon (BBGKY) hierarchy is the chain of equations
i ∂_t ρ_s = [H_s, ρ_s] + Tr_{s+1}[V_{s,s+1}, ρ_{s+1}],   s = 1, 2, …,
where H_s is the s-body part of H and V_{s,s+1} = Σ_{i=1}^{s} v(i, s+1).

A "two-body propagation scheme" consists of evolving only the second equation of the hierarchy (s = 2) while replacing the unknown three-body density matrix ρ_3 by an explicit functional ρ_3 ≈ F[ρ_1, ρ_2] (a closure or reconstruction); typical examples include cumulant-based three-body closures, the Nakatsuji–Yasuda contraction, the Valdemoro reconstruction, and various weak-coupling and 3b-non-interacting-type approximations. The one-body matrix ρ_1 is recovered by partial trace of ρ_2.

Empirically, such truncated propagations exhibit two failures:
(a) the total energy ⟨H⟩(t), which should be conserved exactly, displays large fluctuations in time;
(b) the evolution develops finite-time divergences (loss of N-representability and/or unbounded growth of ρ_2), even when the closure is chosen so that compatibility between the s = 1 and s = 2 hierarchy equations is enforced, indicating that loss of positive semidefiniteness of ρ_2 (and of the associated two-hole and particle-hole matrices) plays an essential role.

Question: Does there exist a closure functional F[ρ_1, ρ_2] (or a modification of the second BBGKY equation by additional constraints) such that the resulting two-body propagation scheme is, for generic finite fermionic many-body systems with two-body interactions,
(i) globally well-defined in time,
(ii) conserves the total energy ⟨H⟩ to within controllably small fluctuations,
(iii) preserves N-representability of ρ_2 (in particular positive semidefiniteness of ρ_2, the two-hole matrix Q_2, and the particle-hole matrix G_2),
making the s = 2 truncation of the BBGKY hierarchy a generally reliable approach to nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics?
category_tag: BBGKY hierarchy truncation and reduced density matrices
status_search_result: The reliability of propagation based solely on the second BBGKY equation with approximate three-body closures remains an open problem. Standard references on the BBGKY hierarchy describe the closure/truncation problem as unresolved in general, and current closures (cumulant-type, Nakatsuji–Yasuda, Valdemoro, weak-coupling, 3b-NIA) are known to suffer from energy non-conservation and finite-time loss of N-representability. No general closure that simultaneously guarantees global well-posedness, energy conservation, and positive semidefiniteness has been established in the literature.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type t is unimodal.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ the polynomial ring in $r$ variables. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite set of monomials of $R$ that is closed under taking divisors (if $m \in X$ and $m'$ divides $m$, then $m' \in X$). The order ideal $X$ is called pure of type $t$ if all of its maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same degree and there are exactly $t$ of them. The pure O-sequence associated with $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$ where $h_i$ is the number of monomials of degree $i$ in $X$; in particular $h_0 = 1$, $h_1 \le r$, and $h_e = t$. A finite sequence of nonnegative integers is called unimodal if it does not strictly increase after a strict decrease, i.e., there exists an index $j$ such that $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$.

For each fixed integer $r \ge 1$, determine the largest integer $t = t(r)$ (if such a largest integer exists) such that every pure O-sequence of codimension $r$ (meaning $h_1 = r$) and type $t$ is unimodal.
status_search_result: The general problem of determining the codimension-versus-type unimodality threshold $t(r)$ is open. Partial results exist: pure O-sequences in codimension at most 2 are always unimodal; in codimension 3, type 2 is unimodal (Boij–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Zanello), and Boyle (2014) proved the type-3, codimension-3 case is also unimodal; for codimension 3 and large type, non-unimodal examples are known (in fact, for any $r\ge 3$ and $M\ge 1$ there exist pure O-sequences in $r$ variables with $M$ maxima). The exact threshold for any $r\ge 3$ has not been determined.

original_question: Determine the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and consider monomial ideals in the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$. For a finite, nonempty set $X$ of (monic) monomials in $x_1,\dots,x_r$ that is closed under taking divisors (an order ideal of monomials), let $h_i$ be the number of monomials in $X$ of degree $i$. The sequence $h(X) = (h_0, h_1, h_2, \dots, h_e)$, where $e$ is the largest degree of a monomial in $X$, is called a pure O-sequence (of socle degree $e$ and codimension $h_1 \le r$) if every monomial of $X$ divides some monomial of $X$ of degree exactly $e$. The sequence $(h_0,\dots,h_e)$ is said to be unimodal if there is an index $j$ with $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$, and nonunimodal otherwise.

Determine the smallest positive integer $r$ for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree $4$ and codimension $r$ (equivalently, with $h_1 = r$).
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the survey on pure O-sequences. Searches turned up no published resolution: subsequent work (e.g., on unimodality of pure O-sequences of type three, or on Stanley's nonunimodal Gorenstein h-vector) addresses related but distinct cases. No source confirms a determination of the minimal codimension forcing nonunimodality at socle degree 4.

original_question: Determine the smallest number n of variables for which there exists a nonunimodal pure f-vector, equivalently a nonunimodal f-vector of a pure simplicial complex. The paper notes this after recalling Stanley's original nonunimodal example and later bounds for special cases.
self_contained_problem:
A simplicial complex Δ on a finite vertex set V is called pure if all of its facets (maximal faces under inclusion) have the same dimension. Its f-vector is f(Δ) = (f₋₁, f₀, f₁, …, f_{d−1}), where f_i is the number of i-dimensional faces of Δ (with f₋₁ = 1 for the empty face). The f-vector is called unimodal if there exists an index j such that f₋₁ ≤ f₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ f_j ≥ f_{j+1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ f_{d−1}; otherwise it is called nonunimodal.

Determine the smallest positive integer n with the following property: there exists a pure simplicial complex Δ on n vertices whose f-vector is nonunimodal. Equivalently, find the minimum number of vertices required to support a nonunimodal pure f-vector.
status_search_result: The exact minimum number of vertices needed for a pure simplicial complex to admit a nonunimodal f-vector does not appear to be known. Partial results exist: a sharp lower bound of n = 328 has been established for nonunimodal Cohen–Macaulay f-vectors of socle degree 5, with examples in higher socle degree using as few as n = 39 vertices, but no general sharp bound for arbitrary pure complexes has been confirmed in the available literature.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal in arbitrary codimension? More generally, for each fixed codimension, which socle types force unimodality of all pure O-sequences in that codimension?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let r be a positive integer and let X be a finite, nonempty set of monomials in the variables y_1,...,y_r over a field. The set X is called a pure order ideal (or pure multicomplex) if (i) whenever m ∈ X and m' divides m, then m' ∈ X, and (ii) all maximal elements of X (under divisibility) have the same total degree e. The pure O-sequence associated with X is the vector h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) where h_i is the number of monomials of degree i in X; in particular h_0 = 1 and h_1 ≤ r. The integer e is the socle degree and t := h_e is called the type. The codimension of h is h_1. A finite sequence (h_0,...,h_e) of positive integers is called unimodal if there exists an index j with h_0 ≤ h_1 ≤ ... ≤ h_j ≥ h_{j+1} ≥ ... ≥ h_e.

Question. (a) Is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal, in every codimension r ≥ 1? That is, if X is a pure order ideal in r variables having exactly two maximal monomials, must its associated h-vector be unimodal?

(b) More generally, for each fixed codimension r, determine the set of types t for which every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type t is forced to be unimodal.
status_search_result: The unimodality of pure O-sequences of type 2 in codimension 3 was established (via the Weak Lefschetz Property) by Boij–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Zanello. Subsequent work (e.g., on type-three sequences and on non-unimodal level h-vectors) has produced non-unimodal pure O-sequences for sufficiently large type/codimension, but no published resolution of the type-2 case in codimensions r ≥ 4, nor a complete classification of socle types forcing unimodality in each fixed codimension, was found. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4, 5, 21)? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?
self_contained_problem:
A Steiner system S(t,k,v) is a pair (X, B), where X is a set of v points and B is a collection of k-element subsets of X (called blocks), such that every t-element subset of X is contained in exactly one block of B. A Steiner quintuple system of order v is a Steiner system S(4,5,v).

A finite sequence h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) of nonnegative integers is called a pure O-sequence if there exists a finite, nonempty set M of monomials in some polynomial ring k[x_1, ..., x_n] (over a field k) such that:
(i) M is an order ideal, i.e., whenever a monomial m lies in M, every monomial dividing m also lies in M;
(ii) all maximal monomials of M (with respect to divisibility) have the same total degree e; and
(iii) for each i = 0, 1, ..., e, h_i equals the number of monomials in M of total degree i.

Question: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4,5,21)? Equivalently, is the integer sequence
   (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197)
a pure O-sequence?
status_search_result: The existence of a Steiner system S(4,5,21) is the smallest open case for Steiner quintuple systems. Partial results restrict the possible automorphism group orders of such a system to {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,10} (Kolotoğlu, J. Combin. Designs, 2014), but no construction or non-existence proof has been published as of 2026. Recent surveys and references continue to list it as open.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Is every matroid h-vector a pure O-sequence? Equivalently, does Stanley's conjecture hold for all matroid complexes, beyond the low-dimensional cases proved in the paper and cited work?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(1) A pure multicomplex is a finite, nonempty collection X of monomials in a polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_n] (with 1 ∈ X) that is closed under taking divisors and whose maximal monomials all have the same total degree. The h-vector (or O-sequence) of X is the integer vector h = (h_0, h_1, h_2, ...), where h_i is the number of monomials in X of total degree i. A finite sequence of nonnegative integers is called a pure O-sequence if it arises in this way from some pure multicomplex.

(2) A matroid M on a finite ground set E is a nonempty collection of subsets of E (the independent sets) closed under taking subsets and satisfying the exchange axiom: for all I, J independent with |I| < |J|, there exists e ∈ J \ I such that I ∪ {e} is independent. The independence complex Δ(M) is the simplicial complex on E whose faces are the independent sets of M; it is a pure simplicial complex of dimension r−1, where r is the rank of M. The h-vector of M is defined to be the h-vector of Δ(M), i.e. the vector h(M) = (h_0,...,h_r) determined by the f-vector (f_{−1}, f_0,...,f_{r−1}) of Δ(M) via the identity 
   ∑_{i=0}^{r} f_{i−1} (t−1)^{r−i} = ∑_{i=0}^{r} h_i t^{r−i}.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every matroid M, the h-vector h(M) is a pure O-sequence.
status_search_result: The conjecture that every matroid h-vector is a pure O-sequence (Stanley's conjecture) remains open in general. Partial results have been established, including the cases of rank ≤ 3 matroids, cographic matroids, internally perfect matroids, certain coned/biconed/triconed graphic matroids, and (in 2021–2023) positroids, but the full conjecture is still unresolved.

context_brief: Correlation bounds for low-degree F2 polynomials
original_question: Does there exist an explicit function f : F2^n -> F2, computable in NP, such that for every F2-polynomial p : F2^n -> F2 of degree at most log_2 n, the correlation satisfies |E[(-1)^<f(x), p(x)>]| <= 1/n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$ denote the field with two elements. For a function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$ and an $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomial $p:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$ (i.e., a multilinear polynomial in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{F}_2$), define the correlation
$$\mathrm{Cor}(f,p) = \left| \mathbb{E}_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n}\!\left[ (-1)^{f(x) + p(x)} \right] \right|,$$
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Call a family of functions $\{f_n : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2\}_{n \ge 1}$ "explicit" if the language $\{(n,x) : f_n(x) = 1\}$ lies in the complexity class $\mathrm{NP}$.

Question: Does there exist an explicit family of functions $\{f_n : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2\}_{n \ge 1}$ such that, for every sufficiently large $n$ and every $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomial $p: \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$ of degree at most $\log_2 n$, one has
$$\mathrm{Cor}(f_n, p) \le \frac{1}{n}\,?$$
status_search_result: The problem of exhibiting an explicit function with correlation at most $1/n$ (or even any negligible bound) against all $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomials of degree $\log_2 n$ is widely cited as a central open problem in circuit complexity; it would imply superpolynomial lower bounds for AC^0[parity] circuits augmented with one majority gate. Recent work (e.g., Ivanov–Pavlovic–Viola, CCC 2023, and Viola's surveys) confirms that no such explicit function is currently known even for degree $\log_2 n$.

original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> R_{>=0} satisfy E[f] = 1, and fix 0 < rho < 1. Must the upper tail of the noise operator obey Pr[T_rho f >= t] < o(1/t)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and equip $\{-1,1\}^n$ with the uniform probability measure. For $0<\rho<1$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ acts on functions $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$(T_\rho f)(x) \;=\; \mathbb{E}\bigl[f(y)\bigr],$$
where $y\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is the random vector whose coordinates are independently equal to $x_i$ with probability $\tfrac{1+\rho}{2}$ and equal to $-x_i$ with probability $\tfrac{1-\rho}{2}$.

Fix $0<\rho<1$. Prove or disprove: for every nonnegative function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $\mathbb{E}[f]=1$, the tail of $T_\rho f$ satisfies
$$\Pr\bigl[\,T_\rho f \;\ge\; t\,\bigr] \;=\; o\!\left(\tfrac{1}{t}\right) \qquad \text{as } t\to\infty,$$
where the $o(1/t)$ rate is allowed to depend on $\rho$ but must be uniform in $n$ and in the choice of $f$ (i.e., a faster-than-Markov, dimension-free upper-tail estimate).

original_question: Among degree-k polynomial threshold functions f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the one with maximal total influence always the symmetric threshold f(x) = sgn(p(x_1 + ... + x_n)), where p is a degree-k univariate polynomial alternating sign on the k+1 values of x_1 + ... + x_n closest to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let n, k be positive integers with k ≤ n. A function f : {−1, 1}^n → {−1, 1} is called a degree-k polynomial threshold function (PTF) if there exists a real multilinear polynomial P(x_1, …, x_n) of degree at most k such that f(x) = sgn(P(x)) for all x ∈ {−1, 1}^n (with sgn(0) defined arbitrarily). The total influence (average sensitivity) of f is

  I(f) = ∑_{i=1}^{n} Pr_{x ∼ Unif{−1,1}^n}[f(x) ≠ f(x^{⊕i})],

where x^{⊕i} denotes x with its i-th coordinate flipped.

Consider the symmetric degree-k PTF defined as follows. Let s(x) = x_1 + x_2 + ⋯ + x_n, and let p(t) be a univariate polynomial of degree k chosen so that, on the k+1 values of s(x) closest to 0 (i.e., the k+1 integers in {−n, −n+2, …, n−2, n} of smallest absolute value), the sign of p alternates. Define

  f*(x) = sgn(p(s(x))).

Question: Is it true that, for every n and every k ≤ n, the function f* attains the maximum value of I(f) among all degree-k polynomial threshold functions f : {−1, 1}^n → {−1, 1}?
status_search_result: This is the Gotsman–Linial conjecture (1991). Brynmor Chapman (arXiv:2108.02288, "The Gotsman–Linial Conjecture is False") refuted the conjecture for almost all degrees d and almost all n, while confirming it in many remaining cases. Hence the answer to the question (that the symmetric PTF always maximizes total influence) is false in general.

original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be computable by a DNF of size s > 1, and let epsilon in (0,1/2]. Is the Fourier spectrum of f always epsilon-concentrated on some collection F with |F| <= s^{O(log(1/epsilon))}?
self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its Fourier expansion as
$$f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i.$$
By Parseval's identity, $\sum_{S}\hat f(S)^2=1$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$, we say $f$ is $\varepsilon$-concentrated on a collection $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ if
$$\sum_{S\notin\mathcal F}\hat f(S)^2\le \varepsilon.$$
A DNF formula of size $s$ is a disjunction of at most $s$ terms, where each term is a conjunction of literals over $x_1,\dots,x_n$ (with $x_i\in\{-1,1\}$ interpreted as Boolean values).

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\ge 1$, every $s>1$, every DNF formula $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ of size at most $s$, and every $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$, the Fourier spectrum of $f$ is $\varepsilon$-concentrated on some collection $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with
$$|\mathcal F|\le s^{C\log(1/\varepsilon)}.$$
status_search_result: This is Mansour's Conjecture (1994). It remains open in general. Klivans–Lee–Wan (2010) proved it for random DNFs and read-once DNFs. Lecomte–Tan (FOCS 2021) gave sharper bounds parameterized by the read number, improving Mansour's classical $s^{O(\log\log s)}$ bound for bounded-read DNFs, but the full conjecture for general DNFs remains unresolved.

original_question: Is there a universal constant C such that every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} satisfies H[\hat{f}^2] <= C * I[f], where H[\hat{f}^2] is the spectral entropy and I[f] is the total influence?
self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its Fourier–Walsh expansion as
$$f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}}\hat{f}(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i,$$
with Fourier coefficients $\hat{f}(S)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\{-1,1\}^n}[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$. By Parseval's identity, $\sum_S \hat{f}(S)^2 = 1$, so the squared Fourier coefficients form a probability distribution on subsets of $\{1,\dots,n\}$.

Define the spectral entropy of $f$ by
$$H[\hat{f}^2] \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}} \hat{f}(S)^2 \,\log_2\!\frac{1}{\hat{f}(S)^2},$$
with the convention $0\log(1/0)=0$, and define the total influence of $f$ by
$$I[f] \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}} |S|\,\hat{f}(S)^2.$$

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$ and of $f$) such that for every $n\ge 1$ and every Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$,
$$H[\hat{f}^2] \;\le\; C\cdot I[f]\,?$$
status_search_result: The Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture of Friedgut and Kalai remains open as of 2025. Partial progress continues, including improved bounds (e.g., Han's 2025 Combinatorica paper bounding spectral entropy by O(I(f) + Σ I_k(f) log(1/I_k(f)))) and proofs for restricted classes of Boolean functions, but no universal linear bound H[f̂²] ≤ C·I[f] has been established.

context_brief: Optimality of majority for correlation distillation
original_question: Fix r in N, odd n, and 0 < epsilon < 1/2. For f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, let P(f) be the probability that r independent epsilon-noisy copies of a uniform x all give the same output under f. Among odd functions f, is P(f) always maximized by a majority function Maj_k on some odd number k of inputs?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be an odd positive integer, $r \in \mathbb{N}$ with $r \geq 2$, and $0 < \varepsilon < 1/2$. For a function $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$, define
$$P(f) = \Pr\bigl[f(y^{(1)}) = f(y^{(2)}) = \cdots = f(y^{(r)})\bigr],$$
where $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$ is chosen uniformly at random and, conditional on $x$, each $y^{(i)} \in \{-1,1\}^n$ is an independent $\varepsilon$-noisy copy of $x$ (i.e., for each coordinate $j$ independently, $y^{(i)}_j = x_j$ with probability $1-\varepsilon$ and $y^{(i)}_j = -x_j$ with probability $\varepsilon$).

Call $f$ odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x \in \{-1,1\}^n$. For an odd integer $k$ with $1 \leq k \leq n$, let $\mathrm{Maj}_k(x) = \mathrm{sign}(x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k)$ (a function of the first $k$ coordinates, viewed as a function on $\{-1,1\}^n$).

Question: Is it true that, among all odd functions $f : \{-1,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$, the quantity $P(f)$ is maximized by $\mathrm{Maj}_k$ for some odd $k$?
status_search_result: The question concerns non-interactive correlation distillation with r noisy copies. The case r = 2 is the noise stability problem solved by the "Majority Is Stablest" theorem (in the low-influence setting). For general r ≥ 3 with the agreement/equality probability (sometimes called higher-order noise stability), the problem of whether majority functions are optimal among odd Boolean functions remains open; existing literature (Mossel–O'Donnell on NICD) addresses asymptotic regimes and specific cases but does not settle the general conjecture.

original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be unbiased. For a random restriction z in {-1,0,1}^n where each coordinate is independently +1 or -1 with probability p/2 each and 0 with probability 1-p, with p < 1/2 and n odd, is E_z[|f(z)|] maximized when f is the majority function, identifying f with its multilinear expansion?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be an odd positive integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be an unbiased Boolean function (i.e., $\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n} f(x)=0$). Identify $f$ with its multilinear (Fourier) expansion $f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\hat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, so that $f$ is defined on all of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Fix a parameter $p\in(0,1/2)$, and let $z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n$ be a random vector whose coordinates are independent with
$$\Pr[z_i=+1]=\Pr[z_i=-1]=p/2,\qquad \Pr[z_i=0]=1-p.$$

Let $\mathrm{Maj}_n:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ denote the majority function. The question is:

Does the inequality
$$\mathbb{E}_z\bigl[|f(z)|\bigr]\le \mathbb{E}_z\bigl[|\mathrm{Maj}_n(z)|\bigr]$$
hold for every unbiased $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, every odd $n$, and every $p\in(0,1/2)$?
status_search_result: A 2026 ECCC report (TR26-063) reports that the Non-Interactive Correlation Distillation with Erasures conjecture (in its original form, asking whether majority maximizes E[|f(z)|]) is refuted for all n ≥ 5 in certain noise-parameter regimes, while it holds for n = 3 in all regimes, and a nearly tight characterization of the (n,p) parameter region where majority is optimal is provided. The authors propose refined versions of the conjecture. Thus the original conjecture is partially solved (refuted in general; verified in a restricted regime).

original_question: Fix a constant alpha > 0. If A subseteq F2^n has density at least alpha, must A + A contain a subspace of codimension O(sqrt(n))?
self_contained_problem: Let $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements, and for a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ define its density to be $|A|/2^n$ and its sumset by $A+A = \{a_1 + a_2 : a_1, a_2 \in A\}$. Fix a constant $\alpha > 0$. Is it true that there exists a constant $C = C(\alpha) > 0$ such that for every $n \geq 1$ and every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ of density at least $\alpha$, the sumset $A+A$ contains an affine subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of codimension at most $C\sqrt{n}$?
status_search_result: The best known general result for sumsets in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is Sanders' Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma, which only guarantees a subspace of codimension polylogarithmic in $1/\alpha$ inside $A+A-A-A$, not inside $A+A$. For $A+A$ itself, Green proved that if $A$ has density larger than $1/2$ then $A+A$ contains a subspace of linear dimension, but the question of whether positive density forces $A+A$ to contain a subspace of codimension $O(\sqrt{n})$ does not appear to have been resolved; no result obtaining a $\sqrt{n}$-codimension subspace inside $A+A$ for arbitrary positive density sets has been located.

original_question: Fix a possibly infinite collection of affine constraints {(M_1,sigma_1),(M_2,sigma_2),...} over F2. For each n, let P_n be the property that a function f : F2^n -> {0,1} is (M_i,sigma_i)-free for every i. Must there exist a one-sided-error constant-query property-testing algorithm for P_n?
self_contained_problem:
Work over the field $\mathbb{F}_2$. For a matrix $M \in \mathbb{F}_2^{m \times k}$ and a vector $\sigma \in \{0,1\}^k$, say that a function $f : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ is $(M,\sigma)$-free if there do not exist vectors $x^{(1)}, \ldots, x^{(k)} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that
\[ M\,(x^{(1)}, \ldots, x^{(k)})^\top = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad f(x^{(j)}) = \sigma_j \text{ for all } j \in [k]. \]
Fix any (possibly infinite) collection $\{(M_1,\sigma_1),(M_2,\sigma_2),\ldots\}$ where $M_i \in \mathbb{F}_2^{m_i \times k_i}$ and $\sigma_i \in \{0,1\}^{k_i}$. For each $n$, let $P_n$ be the property of functions $f : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ defined by: $f \in P_n$ iff $f$ is $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-free for every $i$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a one-sided-error, constant-query property tester for $P_n$. That is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $q = q(\varepsilon)$ and a randomized algorithm that queries $f$ on at most $q$ points, accepts with probability $1$ when $f \in P_n$, and rejects with probability at least $2/3$ when $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far (in Hamming distance, normalized) from $P_n$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Bhattacharyya, Chen, Sudan and Xie) was resolved positively by Asaf Shapira, who proved that every (possibly infinite) system of linear/affine equations over a finite abelian group has the removal property, which implies that the family of $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-free properties is testable with one-sided error and a constant number of queries. Independent/related resolutions were also obtained by Král', Serra, and Vena.

context_brief: Gaussian simplex partitions and noise stability
original_question: Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, where 3 <= q <= n+1, is the maximum noise stability at rho achieved by a standard simplex partition, and for -1 <= rho <= 0 does the standard simplex partition minimize the noise stability?
self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 and 3 ≤ q ≤ n+1 be integers. Equip ℝⁿ with the standard Gaussian probability measure γₙ (density (2π)^{-n/2} exp(-|x|²/2)). For ρ ∈ [-1,1], the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise operator acts on f ∈ L²(ℝⁿ, γₙ) by
  T_ρ f(x) = E[f(ρx + √(1-ρ²) Z)],
where Z ~ N(0, Iₙ) is independent. Given a measurable partition A = (A₁, …, A_q) of ℝⁿ with γₙ(Aᵢ) = 1/q for every i, define its noise stability at parameter ρ by
  S_ρ(A) = ∑_{i=1}^{q} ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{Aᵢ}(x) · T_ρ 1_{Aᵢ}(x) dγₙ(x).
A "standard simplex partition" of ℝⁿ is one obtained as follows: fix q unit vectors v₁, …, v_q ∈ ℝⁿ that form the vertices of a regular (q−1)-simplex centered at the origin (so ⟨vᵢ, vⱼ⟩ = -1/(q−1) for i ≠ j), and set
  Aᵢ = {x ∈ ℝⁿ : ⟨x, vᵢ⟩ = max_{1 ≤ j ≤ q} ⟨x, vⱼ⟩},  i = 1, …, q.

Prove or disprove the following two assertions:

(a) For every ρ ∈ [0, 1], the maximum of S_ρ(A) over all measurable partitions of ℝⁿ into q parts each of Gaussian measure 1/q is attained by a standard simplex partition.

(b) For every ρ ∈ [-1, 0], the minimum of S_ρ(A) over the same class of partitions is attained by a standard simplex partition.
status_search_result: The conjecture (often called the Standard Simplex Conjecture of Isaksson–Mossel) is largely open in the equal-measure regime. Heilman established a partial result for q = 3, n ≥ 2 and 0 < ρ < ρ₀(3,n). Heilman–Mossel–Nazarov showed that standard simplex partitions are NOT the most noise-stable partitions when the prescribed measures are unequal (and that plurality is not the most stable low-influence discrete partition in those cases), but the equal-measure case treated here is not refuted by their work and remains open in general.

original_question: Fix d in N and epsilon in (0,1). What is the least k = k(d,epsilon) such that every degree-d polynomial threshold event over a k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal random vector X approximates the corresponding event under a standard Gaussian vector Z within additive error epsilon; that is, |Pr[p(X) >= 0] - Pr[p(Z) >= 0]| <= epsilon for every degree-d polynomial p : R^n -> R?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ be fixed. For an integer $n \geq 1$, call a random vector $X = (X_1, \ldots, X_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ a $k$-wise independent Gaussian-marginal vector if (i) each coordinate $X_i$ has the standard Gaussian distribution $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, and (ii) every subset of $k$ distinct coordinates $X_{i_1}, \ldots, X_{i_k}$ is mutually independent (so its joint law is the standard $k$-dimensional Gaussian). Let $Z = (Z_1, \ldots, Z_n)$ denote a fully independent standard $n$-dimensional Gaussian vector.

Determine the least integer $k = k(d, \varepsilon)$ with the following property: for every $n \geq 1$, every degree-$d$ multivariate polynomial $p : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, and every $k$-wise independent Gaussian-marginal vector $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\bigl| \Pr[p(X) \geq 0] - \Pr[p(Z) \geq 0] \bigr| \leq \varepsilon.$$

In particular, give matching upper and lower bounds on $k(d,\varepsilon)$ as a function of $d$ and $\varepsilon$.
category_tag: bounded independence and polynomial threshold functions
status_search_result: Upper bounds on k(d,ε) for Gaussian polynomial threshold functions of arbitrary degree d were established by Kane (CCC 2011, "k-Independent Gaussians Fool Polynomial Threshold Functions"), with quantitative improvements in subsequent work, but the tight value of k(d,ε)—matching upper and lower bounds as a function of d and ε—remains unresolved in the literature. Known bounds are polynomial in 1/ε for fixed d (with various exponents depending on d) and do not match known lower bounds, so the problem of determining the exact least k(d,ε) is still open.

context_brief: PTF sparsity for inner product mod 2
original_question: Does every polynomial threshold function representation of the inner product mod 2 function IP_{2n} : F2^{2n} -> {-1,1} require at least 3^n monomials?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$ and define the inner product mod 2 function on $2n$ bits as
$$\mathrm{IP}_{2n}: \mathbb{F}_2^{2n} \to \{-1,+1\}, \qquad \mathrm{IP}_{2n}(x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_n) = (-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i}.$$
Identify $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$ with $\{-1,+1\}^{2n}$ via $b \mapsto (-1)^b$, so that Boolean functions on $\{-1,+1\}^{2n}$ admit a unique multilinear (Fourier) expansion $p(z) = \sum_{S \subseteq [2n]} \hat p(S) \prod_{i \in S} z_i$. A polynomial threshold function (PTF) representation of a Boolean function $f: \{-1,+1\}^{2n} \to \{-1,+1\}$ is a real multilinear polynomial $p$ such that $f(z) = \mathrm{sign}(p(z))$ for every $z \in \{-1,+1\}^{2n}$. The sparsity (or monomial count) of such a representation is the number of nonzero coefficients $\hat p(S)$.

Prove or disprove: every PTF representation of $\mathrm{IP}_{2n}$ uses at least $3^n$ monomials.
status_search_result: A web search surfaced related work on PTF sparsity, sign-rank lower bounds for inner-product mod 2 (Forster), weak-density bounds of order $2^n$, and recent sparsity lower bounds for probabilistic polynomials (ITCS 2025), but no source explicitly establishes (or refutes) the conjectured $3^n$ monomial lower bound for PTF representations of $\mathrm{IP}_{2n}$. The current status appears unresolved based on available search evidence.

original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is monotone, must its total influence satisfy I[f] < o(sens[f])?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a monotone Boolean function (i.e., $f(x)\le f(y)$ whenever $x\le y$ coordinatewise under the order $-1<1$). For $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define the local sensitivity
$$s(f,x)=\bigl|\{i\in[n]:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\}\bigr|,$$
where $x^{\oplus i}$ denotes $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Define the maximum sensitivity
$$\mathrm{sens}(f)=\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n} s(f,x),$$
and the total influence (equivalently, average sensitivity)
$$I[f]=\mathbb{E}_{x}\bigl[s(f,x)\bigr]=\sum_{i=1}^n \Pr_x\bigl[f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\bigr].$$
It is well known that $I[f]\le \mathrm{sens}(f)$ for every monotone $f$. Question: must every monotone $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ satisfy
$$I[f] = o\bigl(\mathrm{sens}(f)\bigr)$$
as $n\to\infty$? Equivalently, is it the case that for every $c>0$ there exist no infinite family of monotone functions with $I[f]\ge c\cdot \mathrm{sens}(f)$?
status_search_result: The problem is closely tied to a conjecture of Servedio comparing average and maximum sensitivity of monotone Boolean functions. The best known upper bound is $I[f]\le \ln(2)\cdot \mathrm{sens}(f)(1+o(1))$, which does not establish $I[f]=o(\mathrm{sens}(f))$. On the other side, O'Donnell–Servedio constructed monotone functions with $I[f]=\Omega(\mathrm{sens}(f)^{0.61})$, and subsequent work (e.g., on $k$-CNFs) has further narrowed the gap, but no construction is known that refutes $I[f]=o(\mathrm{sens}(f))$. The question therefore appears to remain open.

original_question: Suppose q_1, ..., q_m : F2^n -> F2 are degree-at-most-2 polynomials and the indicator of the all-ones vector, namely AND : F2^n -> {-1,1}, can be written as AND(x) = sum_{i=1}^m c_i (-1)^{q_i(x)} for real coefficients c_i. What lower bound on m is necessary?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ be an integer and identify $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$. Define the AND function $\mathrm{AND} : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{-1, 1\}$ by
$$\mathrm{AND}(x) = \begin{cases} -1 & \text{if } x = (1,1,\dots,1), \\ 1 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$
Suppose there exist polynomials $q_1, \dots, q_m : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$, each of total degree at most $2$ (when written as a multilinear polynomial in the coordinates $x_1, \dots, x_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$), and real numbers $c_1, \dots, c_m \in \mathbb{R}$ such that for every $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$,
$$\mathrm{AND}(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i \, (-1)^{q_i(x)}.$$
Determine the best possible (largest) lower bound on $m$ as a function of $n$. In particular, is it true that $m \geq 2^{\Omega(n)}$ is necessary?
status_search_result: The problem appears in Ryan O'Donnell's compilation of open problems in analysis of Boolean functions (sourced from Hamed Hatami, 2011). It is recorded as open: Hatami can show $m \geq n$ is necessary and conjectures $m \geq 2^{\Omega(n)}$. The degree-1 case is fully resolved with $m = 2^n$. No subsequent resolution was found.

original_question: Fix an interval I contained in R and a subset B contained in R. Can one construct a family of measures {mu_beta} such that for every subset J of I the singular part of mu_beta gives J positive mass exactly for parameters beta in B, while the absolutely continuous part of mu_beta gives J positive mass for every beta in R?
self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a fixed interval and let $B \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a fixed subset. For each $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$, let $\mu_\beta$ be a Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}$, and write $\mu_\beta = (\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}} + (\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}}$ for its Lebesgue decomposition into an absolutely continuous part and a singular part (with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$).

Determine whether one can construct a family of Borel measures $\{\mu_\beta\}_{\beta \in \mathbb{R}}$ on $\mathbb{R}$ such that for every Borel subset $J \subset I$ the following two conditions hold simultaneously:

(i) $(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{s}}(J) > 0$ if and only if $\beta \in B$;

(ii) $(\mu_\beta)_{\mathrm{ac}}(J) > 0$ for every $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$.

That is, can the parameter set governing positive singular mass on every sub-interval be prescribed to be exactly $B$, while the absolutely continuous part assigns positive mass to every such subset for all parameters $\beta$?
category_tag: Spectral measures and mixed spectral types
status_search_result: Web searches surface related work on families of spectral measures with mixed types (e.g., constructions via Pick/Herglotz function representations) and on prescribing singular spectrum, but no source was located that explicitly resolves the prescribed-parameter-set question for the singular part while requiring full absolutely continuous support across all parameters. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

context_brief: Higher-dimensional Anderson model with Bernoulli disorder
original_question: For the discrete random Schrodinger operator in dimension d >= 2 with Bernoulli site variables omega_j taking the values +1 and -1 with equal probability, does the operator have purely singular spectrum?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and consider the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$. Define the discrete Anderson Hamiltonian
$$H_\omega = -\Delta + V_\omega,$$
where $\Delta$ is the standard discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, given by
$$(\Delta\psi)(j) = \sum_{|i-j|=1}\bigl(\psi(i)-\psi(j)\bigr),$$
and $V_\omega$ is the multiplication operator $(V_\omega\psi)(j)=\omega_j\,\psi(j)$, with $\{\omega_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ an i.i.d. family of Bernoulli random variables satisfying
$$\mathbb{P}(\omega_j=+1)=\mathbb{P}(\omega_j=-1)=\tfrac{1}{2}.$$
Determine whether, almost surely with respect to the product Bernoulli measure, the spectrum of $H_\omega$ is purely singular (i.e., the absolutely continuous spectrum of $H_\omega$ is empty almost surely on the entire spectrum).
status_search_result: Localization (and hence pure point/singular spectrum) for the discrete Bernoulli Anderson model in dimensions d ≥ 2 throughout the spectrum remains an open problem. Partial results exist: localization is fully known in d=1, and in higher dimensions localization has been established only in the continuum Bernoulli–Anderson model near spectral edges (via quantitative unique continuation), or under additional assumptions. The discrete case with ±1 Bernoulli site potentials in d ≥ 2 is still not resolved as of recent work (e.g., 2025 alloy-type Bernoulli localization papers).

original_question: For higher-rank unitary perturbations, determine which parts of Aronszajn-Donoghue theory survive after the necessary modifications from the rank-one setting, especially when scalar spectral measures are replaced by vector-valued measures.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $U_0$ be a unitary operator on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and let $\{U_\gamma\}$ be a family of finite-rank unitary perturbations of $U_0$ (for example, the Aleksandrov–Clark family obtained from a fixed $d$-dimensional subspace, parametrized by unitary $d\times d$ matrices $\gamma$). For each $\gamma$, let $M_\gamma$ denote the associated matrix-valued (operator-valued) spectral measure on the unit circle $\mathbb T$ taken with respect to a fixed cyclic family of $d$ vectors, and write its Lebesgue decomposition $M_\gamma = M_\gamma^{ac} + M_\gamma^{s}$ into absolutely continuous and singular parts (with respect to normalized Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb T$).

Recall the rank-one Aronszajn–Donoghue theorem: when $d=1$ and $U_0,U_\gamma$ differ by a rank-one unitary perturbation with cyclic vector, the singular parts of the scalar spectral measures of $U_0$ and $U_\gamma$ (and of $U_{\gamma_1}$ and $U_{\gamma_2}$ for $\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2$) are mutually singular as scalar measures.

Problem. Develop a higher-rank ($d\ge 2$) analogue of Aronszajn–Donoghue theory for such families of finite-rank unitary perturbations. Specifically:

(a) Identify a suitable notion of "mutual singularity" for matrix/vector-valued measures that replaces scalar mutual singularity (which fails in general for $d\ge 2$, as simple direct-sum examples show).

(b) Determine which statements of classical Aronszajn–Donoghue theory — concerning the singular parts $M_{\gamma_1}^s$ and $M_{\gamma_2}^s$ for distinct parameters $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$, the absolutely continuous parts, and the relation between the perturbed and unperturbed operators — extend, after appropriate reformulation in terms of vector-valued measures, to the higher-rank unitary perturbation setting, and provide precise theorems with proofs.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on the higher-rank analogue of Aronszajn–Donoghue theory. A notion of vector mutual singularity for matrix-valued spectral measures has been introduced, and analogues of the singularity statement have been proved for finite-rank self-adjoint and unitary perturbations (Liaw–Treil and collaborators). Refinements such as the dimension of the exceptional set in the finite-rank Aronszajn–Donoghue theorem have also appeared (IMRN 2022). The full program of determining exactly which parts of the classical theory survive — and in what optimal form — remains an active area, so the broad open direction is partially solved.

context_brief: Jump behavior of normalized Cauchy transforms
original_question: For f in L^2(mu_gamma), can one control the jump across the unit circle of the normalized Cauchy transform of f mu_gamma, and can that control be used to generalize the connection with pseudocontinuation?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma$ be an inner function on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ (i.e., a bounded holomorphic function on $\mathbb{D}$ whose nontangential boundary values have modulus $1$ almost everywhere on $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$), and let $\mu_\gamma$ denote the Clark measure on $\mathbb{T}$ associated with $\gamma$, defined as the unique positive Borel measure on $\mathbb{T}$ satisfying
$$\mathrm{Re}\,\frac{1+\overline{\gamma(0)}\,\gamma(z)}{1-\overline{\gamma(0)}\,\gamma(z)}=\int_{\mathbb{T}}\frac{1-|z|^2}{|\zeta-z|^2}\,d\mu_\gamma(\zeta),\qquad z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
For $f\in L^2(\mu_\gamma)$, the normalized Cauchy transform of $f\mu_\gamma$ is the function
$$V_\gamma f(z)=\frac{1}{1-\gamma(z)}\int_{\mathbb{T}}\frac{1-\overline{\gamma(0)}}{1-\bar\zeta z}\,f(\zeta)\,d\mu_\gamma(\zeta),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{T},$$
which defines a holomorphic function both inside $\mathbb{D}$ and on the exterior $\mathbb{D}_e=\{|z|>1\}\cup\{\infty\}$ (vanishing at $\infty$).

Question: For every $f\in L^2(\mu_\gamma)$, can one quantitatively control the jump
$$J_f(\zeta)=\lim_{r\to 1^-}\bigl(V_\gamma f(r\zeta)-V_\gamma f(\zeta/r)\bigr)$$
of $V_\gamma f$ across the unit circle in terms of $f$ and $\mu_\gamma$? Furthermore, can such a jump estimate be used to extend the known correspondence between $V_\gamma f$ and pseudocontinuation (i.e., the property that the inner and outer boundary values of $V_\gamma f$ coincide as nontangential limits almost everywhere on $\mathbb{T}$) to this $L^2(\mu_\gamma)$ setting?
category_tag: Normalized Cauchy transforms and Clark measures
status_search_result: A search did not surface a definitive published resolution of the question of controlling the jump across $\mathbb{T}$ of the normalized Cauchy transform $V_\gamma f$ for general $f\in L^2(\mu_\gamma)$, nor a corresponding $L^2$ extension of the pseudocontinuation correspondence. Standard references (Cima–Matheson–Ross, "The Cauchy Transform"; Poltoratski's work on boundary behavior of pseudocontinuable functions; Aleksandrov's papers) treat related boundary-value and pseudocontinuation results, but the specific jump-control problem in $L^2(\mu_\gamma)$ does not appear to be settled in the literature located.

context_brief: Spectral meaning of an integrability condition
original_question: Kapustin's restriction is equivalent to the condition integral log |theta| > -infinity. Does that analytic condition admit an interpretation purely in spectral terms?
self_contained_problem:
Let $U$ be a cyclic unitary operator on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ and consider its family of rank-one unitary perturbations
$$U_\gamma = U + (\gamma-1)\,(\,\cdot\,,b)\,Uc,\qquad \gamma\in\mathbb{T},$$
determined by a unit cyclic vector (with the standard normalization used to build the model). Associated to such a perturbation is a characteristic function $\theta:\mathbb{D}\to\overline{\mathbb{D}}$, an analytic contraction on the unit disk whose non-tangential boundary values $\theta(\zeta)$, $\zeta\in\mathbb{T}$, are well defined almost everywhere with respect to normalized Lebesgue measure $m$ on $\mathbb{T}$. Consider the analytic integrability condition (Szegő-type)
$$\int_{\mathbb{T}} \log|\theta(\zeta)|\, dm(\zeta) > -\infty. \tag{$\ast$}$$

It is known that condition $(\ast)$ is equivalent to "Kapustin's restriction" in the theory of rank-one (or finite-rank) unitary perturbations.

Question: Does condition $(\ast)$ admit a characterization expressed purely in terms of the spectral data of the unperturbed operator $U$ (e.g., the spectral measure: its absolutely continuous, singular continuous, and pure point parts, together with the supports and Radon–Nikodym density of $U$)? Specifically, find a necessary and sufficient condition, formulated solely in spectral-theoretic terms, that is equivalent to $(\ast)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a survey on rank-one and finite-rank perturbations (C. Liaw, 2012). A targeted search did not surface a subsequent work providing a purely spectral-theoretic characterization equivalent to the integrability condition ∫ log|θ| dm > −∞ (Kapustin's restriction). No definitive resolution was located, so the current status is treated as unknown.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: How can one formulate the thermodynamics of feedback-controlled systems in a way that explicitly accounts for the thermodynamic consequences of information transfer between the system and the controller, so that quantities such as entropy reduction, extractable work, and efficiency are treated within a consistent thermodynamic framework?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a thermodynamic framework for feedback-controlled systems that explicitly incorporates the thermodynamic effects of information transfer between the controlled system and its controller. Specifically:

Setting. Let a physical system $S$ be in contact with one or more heat reservoirs at given temperatures and evolve under a (possibly time-dependent) Hamiltonian or stochastic dynamics. A controller $C$ performs measurements on $S$, obtaining outcomes that are stored in a memory, and uses these outcomes to choose subsequent control protocols applied to $S$ (feedback). Let $I$ denote a suitable information-theoretic quantity (e.g., mutual information, transfer entropy, or related correlation measure) characterizing the information acquired by $C$ about $S$.

Required. Formulate definitions of the entropy production, the heat exchanged with the reservoirs, the extractable work $W_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and the thermodynamic efficiency for the joint process on $S$ together with the measurement and feedback steps, such that:

(i) A generalized second law holds in the form
$$ \langle W_{\mathrm{ext}} \rangle \le -\Delta F + k_B T \, I, $$
or, more generally, an inequality (and an associated equality/fluctuation theorem) bounding entropy reduction in $S$ in terms of $I$ and of the thermodynamic cost of the controller's measurement and memory erasure, consistent with Landauer's principle.

(ii) Equality is attained by an explicitly identifiable class of (quasi-static, reversible, or otherwise optimal) protocols, providing a sharp characterization of the maximal extractable work and of the optimal efficiency for feedback-driven heat engines.

(iii) The framework applies uniformly to classical and quantum, discrete and continuous, single-shot and repeated (continuous-time) feedback, and reduces to the standard second law in the absence of information transfer ($I = 0$).

Provide such a unified formulation, prove the corresponding generalized second law and fluctuation theorem, identify the saturating protocols, and demonstrate the framework on canonical models (e.g., Maxwell-demon-type engines and Langevin systems with continuous feedback).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Sagawa–Ueda established a generalized second law and Jarzynski-type equality for feedback-controlled systems, deriving $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle \le -\Delta F + k_B T\, I$ where $I$ is the mutual information acquired by the controller, and a fluctuation theorem with information exchange (PRL 2008, 2012). These results have been extended to continuous feedback, autonomous Maxwell demons, and quantum settings, and a "universal validity of the second law of information thermodynamics" was reported (2024). The general program of a fully unified thermodynamic framework continues to be developed, so the broad question is partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: Can the entropy-reduction results obtained for correlated repeated feedback actuation be applied or extended to derive quantitative bounds for additional performance measures of feedback-controlled systems, in particular the maximum attainable flux or the maximum attainable power?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled stochastic system in contact with a thermal reservoir, in which a controller performs repeated measurements of the system state and applies actuations based on those measurements. Assume the successive measurement-actuation steps are correlated (i.e., not statistically independent across repetitions), and suppose one has available a quantitative bound on the entropy reduction of the system per cycle achievable by such correlated repeated feedback actuation (extending Sagawa–Ueda-type relations to the correlated case).

Within this setting, derive quantitative bounds, in terms of the information-theoretic quantities (mutual information, transfer entropy, or related correlation measures) that govern the entropy reduction, for the following performance measures of the feedback-controlled system:

1. The maximum attainable steady-state probability flux J (e.g., the net rate of transitions across a given cut in state space, or the net particle/current flow induced by the controller).
2. The maximum attainable extracted power P (the rate at which work can be extracted from the thermal reservoir using the feedback controller).

Specifically: establish tight upper bounds J ≤ Φ(I) and P ≤ Π(I), where I denotes the relevant per-cycle information measure characterizing the correlated repeated actuation, and determine whether these bounds are saturable by an explicit protocol.
status_search_result: The literature on stochastic thermodynamics of feedback control has produced general second-law-like inequalities relating extracted work and entropy reduction to mutual information (Sagawa–Ueda and extensions, including non-Markovian/correlated feedback). However, specific tight bounds on the maximum attainable flux or extracted power for systems with correlated repeated feedback actuation, of the form requested here, do not appear to have been established in a definitive form; recent work (e.g., 2025 entropic-balance results) refines the entropy/information inequalities but does not settle quantitative flux/power bounds. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, can the general thermodynamic results of [13] be applied to determine the maximum entropy reduction these ratchets can achieve and to establish a full thermodynamic description of such systems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet, defined as follows. A Brownian particle (or an ensemble of non-interacting Brownian particles) of friction coefficient γ moves on the real line at temperature T, subject to thermal noise and to a spatially periodic, asymmetric (ratchet) potential V(x) which can be switched on or off. A controller measures the particle position at discrete times t_k = k·τ (k = 0, 1, 2, …) and, on the basis of the measurement outcome (and possibly the past history), chooses a control action α_k ∈ {on, off} that determines whether V is applied during the interval [t_k, t_{k+1}). The controlled stochastic dynamics is

   γ ẋ(t) = − α(t) V'(x(t)) + ξ(t),     ⟨ξ(t)ξ(t')⟩ = 2γ k_B T δ(t−t'),

with α(t) = α_k for t ∈ [t_k, t_{k+1}).

Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics for systems coupled to a single heat bath and driven by a measurement-based feedback controller, an entropy balance of the general form

   ΔS_sys + ΔS_bath ≥ − I_fb

has been established, where ΔS_sys is the change of the Shannon/Gibbs entropy of the system, ΔS_bath the entropy change of the bath, and I_fb a non-negative information-theoretic functional of the joint statistics of measurements and trajectories that quantifies the information used by the controller.

Problem. Apply this general feedback-thermodynamic framework to the feedback-controlled flashing ratchet defined above to:

(a) derive an explicit, achievable upper bound on the entropy reduction
       R := −(ΔS_sys + ΔS_bath)
   attainable in a steady state (or per control cycle) by any feedback protocol α_k = F(x(t_0), …, x(t_k)), expressed in terms of the information functional I_fb associated with the position measurements and the parameters of V, T, γ, τ; and

(b) provide a complete thermodynamic description of the feedback flashing ratchet, i.e. identify the heat, work, system entropy, controller information, and their inequalities, so that the first and second laws (with the information correction term) close consistently for arbitrary measurement-based switching protocols.

Determine whether such a complete thermodynamic description and tight, attainable entropy-reduction bound can be obtained for the feedback flashing ratchet, and exhibit them.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has carried out substantial parts of this program: explicit upper bounds (linear in the controller's information) on the power output and on its gain over the optimal open-loop protocol have been derived for feedback flashing ratchets, an efficiency-at-maximum-power bound has been computed, and a Markovian description applicable to the feedback flashing ratchet, together with information equalities/inequalities and tighter information bounds on extractable work, has been developed. A fully closed, universally tight thermodynamic description with sharp attainable entropy-reduction bounds for arbitrary feedback protocols does not appear to have been definitively settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
context_brief: Implications for nano and biological systems
original_question: What concrete limitations do information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems impose on the operation and achievable performance of nanotechnology devices and biological systems in which one subsystem uses bidirectional interaction with another subsystem to improve that subsystem's performance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a composite stochastic system consisting of two interacting subsystems X and Y evolving in continuous or discrete time. Subsystem Y acts as a controller that measures the state of X, producing a measurement record with mutual information I(X;Y) per unit time, and then applies a control signal back to X based on this record (bidirectional, feedback interaction). Assume X obeys stochastic thermodynamics: its evolution is described by a Markov dynamics satisfying local detailed balance, with well-defined entropy production, extracted work W, and free-energy change ΔF. For such feedback-controlled systems the generalized second law takes the form
   ⟨W⟩ ≤ −ΔF + k_B T · I,
where I is an appropriate information-theoretic quantity (e.g., the mutual information acquired by the controller, or the transfer entropy rate from X to Y), k_B is Boltzmann's constant, and T is the temperature of the bath.

Problem. Derive concrete, quantitative limitations that the above class of information-thermodynamic inequalities (together with related bounds such as those constraining measurement and erasure costs, transfer-entropy-based second laws, and thermodynamic uncertainty relations) impose on the operation and achievable performance of:
 (i) nanotechnology devices that exploit feedback (e.g., Maxwell-demon-type information engines, single-electron devices, molecular machines), and
 (ii) biological systems in which one subsystem uses bidirectional interaction with another to improve the second subsystem's performance (e.g., sensory adaptation networks, kinetic proofreading, biochemical signaling, molecular motors driven by feedback).

Specifically, identify and prove explicit upper bounds on natural performance measures — such as extracted work, power output, energetic efficiency, sensing precision, adaptation accuracy, or copying fidelity — in terms of the information-theoretic quantities I (mutual information, transfer entropy, or directed information rate) characterizing the bidirectional coupling, and exhibit physically realizable models that saturate these bounds.
category_tag: feedback control and thermodynamics of information
status_search_result: The question, as posed, is a broad programmatic open problem about translating information-thermodynamic feedback bounds into concrete limits on nano-devices and biological systems. Substantial progress has been made on individual instances since 2012 (e.g., Sagawa–Ueda generalized second laws, Barato–Seifert thermodynamic uncertainty relations, information-thermodynamic bounds on sensing, adaptation, and molecular motors), but no comprehensive resolution exists; the general program remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Topology of the admissible representation space
original_question: Fix a closed hyperbolic surface S of genus at least 2. Let Adm(S) be the space of admissible pairs (j,ρ) of representations π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) with j Fuchsian and such that the induced action on AdS^3 is properly discontinuous and cocompact. How many connected components does Adm(S) have, and what is its topology?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\Gamma = \pi_1(S)$. Identify three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ with the Lie group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ endowed with (a suitable rescaling of) its Killing form, so that its identity component of isometries is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ acting by left and right multiplication. A pair of representations $(j, \rho) : \Gamma \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is called admissible if $j$ is Fuchsian (i.e., faithful and discrete with cocompact image) and the diagonal action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ via $\gamma \cdot x = j(\gamma)\, x\, \rho(\gamma)^{-1}$ is properly discontinuous and cocompact (equivalently, by Kulkarni–Raymond, $j$ strictly dominates $\rho$ in translation length). Let
$$\mathrm{Adm}(S) \;=\; \{(j,\rho) : j \text{ Fuchsian},\ (j,\rho) \text{ admissible}\} \subset \mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}))^2,$$
endowed with the subspace topology.

Determine the number of connected components of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ and describe its topology (e.g., its homotopy type).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Salein, Kassel, Guéritaud–Kassel and others showed admissibility is equivalent to strict domination of $\rho$ by $j$ in translation length, and that $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ contains representations in many components of the relative representation variety. Deroin–Tholozan (2014) and Tholozan ("Dominating surface group representations and deforming closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds", Geom. Topol. 21 (2017), 193–246) proved that any non-Fuchsian representation $\rho$ into $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is strictly dominated by some Fuchsian $j$, and used this to describe the deformation space of closed AdS 3-manifolds; in particular each non-extremal component of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}))$ contributes to $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$, yielding the components and a description of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ as fibering over Teichmüller space. The fine topology (e.g. complete homotopy type) of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ is essentially understood through these works, though the question as originally posed is generally regarded as resolved by Tholozan's results.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Bending laminations determine GHMC AdS structure
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let M = S × R, and let l_- and l_+ be two measured laminations on S that fill S. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations exactly l_- and l_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian structure of constant sectional curvature $-1$ that admits a Cauchy surface diffeomorphic to $S$ and is maximal (with respect to isometric embedding) among such structures. Every GHMC AdS structure on $M$ contains a smallest non-empty geodesically convex closed subset, called the convex core, whose topological boundary (when the structure is not Fuchsian) consists of two pleated spacelike surfaces, each homeomorphic to $S$, bent along measured geodesic laminations $l_-$ and $l_+$ on $S$ called the lower and upper measured bending laminations.

Two measured geodesic laminations $l_-, l_+$ on $S$ are said to fill $S$ if for every essential simple closed curve $\gamma \subset S$ the sum of the geometric intersection numbers $i(\gamma, l_-) + i(\gamma, l_+)$ is positive.

Question: Given any two measured geodesic laminations $l_-$ and $l_+$ on $S$ that fill $S$, does there exist a unique GHMC AdS structure on $M$ whose convex-core boundary has $l_-$ and $l_+$ as its lower and upper measured bending laminations, respectively?
status_search_result: Existence has been established (by Tamburelli, and also Bonsante–Schlenker for related realization statements): for any pair of filling measured laminations there exists a GHMC AdS structure realizing them as bending laminations of the convex core. Uniqueness, however, remains open in general; rigidity has only been proved in special regimes such as small laminations near the Fuchsian locus, and a recent (2025) preprint addresses rigidity near the Fuchsian locus. Thus the full question remains partially solved.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Convex-core boundary metrics determine GHMC structure
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let T be its Teichmüller space, and let m_- and m_+ be two points of T. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M = S × R such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of the boundary of the convex core are m_- and m_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{T}(S)$ denote the Teichmüller space of $S$, i.e. the space of isotopy classes of hyperbolic metrics on $S$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter structure on the $3$-manifold $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ on $M$ such that $(M,h)$ is globally hyperbolic with a Cauchy surface homeomorphic to $S$, and is maximal (any isometric embedding into another globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter spacetime with Cauchy surface $S$ is onto). For such a structure, the convex core $C(M,h)$ is the smallest nonempty closed convex subset of $M$ whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence; when $C(M,h)$ has nonempty interior, its boundary has two connected components, each a pleated surface whose induced (intrinsic) metric is hyperbolic and thus defines a point of $\mathcal{T}(S)$.

Question: Given any two points $m_-, m_+ \in \mathcal{T}(S)$, does there exist a unique GHMC anti-de Sitter structure $h$ on $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of $\partial C(M,h)$ are $m_-$ and $m_+$?
status_search_result: Existence of a GHMC AdS structure realizing any prescribed pair $(m_-, m_+)$ was established by Diallo. Rigidity (uniqueness) has been proved only in special cases: near the Fuchsian locus (Bonsante–Schlenker, and recent work by Prosanov for convex spacelike boundaries with holonomy close to Fuchsian). The full uniqueness statement remains open in general.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Smooth strictly convex AdS boundary metrics
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let h_- and h_+ be two metrics on S with curvature strictly less than -1 everywhere. Is there a unique anti-de Sitter 3-manifold N with smooth, space-like, strictly convex boundary such that the induced metrics on the two connected components of ∂N are h_- and h_+, respectively?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $h_-$ and $h_+$ be two smooth Riemannian metrics on $S$ each having Gaussian curvature strictly less than $-1$ at every point.

An anti-de Sitter (AdS) $3$-manifold is a Lorentzian $3$-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Consider compact AdS $3$-manifolds $N$ diffeomorphic to $S \times [0,1]$ whose boundary $\partial N$ has two connected components, each of which is a smooth, space-like, strictly convex surface (where strict convexity means the second fundamental form is positive definite with respect to the inward-pointing normal).

Question: Does there exist a unique such AdS $3$-manifold $N$ (up to isometry isotopic to the identity) for which the induced metrics on the two boundary components are isometric to $h_-$ and $h_+$, respectively?
status_search_result: The general existence-and-uniqueness question appears still open. Recent work by Prosanov and Schlenker (arXiv:2502.01599, JLMS 2026) establishes infinitesimal rigidity (a local uniqueness statement) for globally hyperbolic compact AdS (2+1)-spacetimes with smooth strictly convex spacelike boundary whose holonomy lies near the Fuchsian locus, and Chen–Schlenker (arXiv:2405.01912) handles existence/uniqueness of one prescribed induced metric on a single convex Cauchy surface in quasifuchsian AdS spacetimes. A complete resolution for arbitrary pairs $(h_-, h_+)$ of metrics with curvature $<-1$ has not been reported.
