paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: For a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold M = S × R with closed surface S of genus at least 2, is either the total volume V(M) or the convex-core volume V(C(M)) quasi-equivalent to a natural distance, such as the Teichmüller distance or the Weil–Petersson distance, between the induced metrics on the convex-core boundary or between the left and right hyperbolic metrics?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g\ge 2$, and let $M = S\times\mathbb{R}$ be a globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter 3-manifold, i.e. a maximal Lorentzian 3-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ that contains a closed Cauchy surface diffeomorphic to $S$. By a theorem of Mess, the moduli space of such structures is naturally parametrized by $\mathcal{T}(S)\times\mathcal{T}(S)$, where $\mathcal{T}(S)$ is the Teichmüller space of $S$; the two factors are the "left" and "right" hyperbolic metrics $(h_L,h_R)$ associated to $M$. The convex core $C(M)\subset M$ is the smallest non-empty closed convex subset whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence; when $M$ is not Fuchsian, $C(M)$ is a compact 3-manifold with two boundary components, each homeomorphic to $S$, carrying induced hyperbolic metrics $(m_+,m_-)\in\mathcal{T}(S)\times\mathcal{T}(S)$. Let $V(M)$ denote the total volume of $M$ (when finite, e.g. for the convex core's enlargement; here interpreted as the volume of $C(M)$ if $M$ has infinite volume) and let $V(C(M))$ denote the volume of the convex core.

Recall that two non-negative functions $F,G$ on a space $X$ are quasi-equivalent if there exist constants $A\ge 1$ and $B\ge 0$ such that $A^{-1}G(x)-B \le F(x)\le A\, G(x)+B$ for all $x\in X$.

Question: Is either $V(M)$ or $V(C(M))$, viewed as a function on $\mathcal{T}(S)\times\mathcal{T}(S)$, quasi-equivalent to a natural distance — for instance the Teichmüller distance $d_{\mathcal T}$ or the Weil–Petersson distance $d_{WP}$ — between the induced convex-core boundary metrics $m_+$ and $m_-$, or between the left and right hyperbolic metrics $h_L$ and $h_R$?
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry and Teichmüller theory
status_search_result: Partial results are known. It has been proved that $V(M)$ and $V(C(M))$ are coarsely equivalent for GHMC AdS manifolds, and that the volume is bounded below by an exponential of the Weil–Petersson distance between the left and right hyperbolic metrics (Bonsante–Seppi and related work), in analogy with Brock's theorem in the quasi-Fuchsian case. A full quasi-equivalence (two-sided linear bound) with a Teichmüller-theoretic distance has not been established in general; the question remains open in this stronger form.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Convexity and properness of AdS volume functions
original_question: Fix a closed surface S and a hyperbolic metric h_l on S. For each h_r in Teichmüller space T, let M(h_l,h_r) be the unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold with left and right hyperbolic metrics h_l and h_r. Are the functions h_r ↦ V(M(h_l,h_r)) and h_r ↦ V(C(M(h_l,h_r))) convex? Are they proper? Does each have a unique minimum at h_l?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{T}(S)$ denote the Teichmüller space of (isotopy classes of) hyperbolic metrics on $S$. By a theorem of Mess, every pair $(h_\ell, h_r) \in \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S)$ determines (up to isometry) a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti–de Sitter $3$-manifold $M(h_\ell, h_r)$ homeomorphic to $S \times \mathbb{R}$, whose left and right hyperbolic holonomies correspond to $h_\ell$ and $h_r$ respectively. Let $C(M(h_\ell, h_r)) \subset M(h_\ell, h_r)$ denote its convex core, and let $V(\cdot)$ denote Lorentzian volume.

Fix $h_\ell \in \mathcal{T}(S)$ and define the two real-valued functions on $\mathcal{T}(S)$:
$$ \mathcal{V}(h_r) := V\bigl(M(h_\ell, h_r)\bigr), \qquad \mathcal{V}_C(h_r) := V\bigl(C(M(h_\ell, h_r))\bigr). $$

Answer the following:
(a) Are $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}_C$ convex on $\mathcal{T}(S)$ (with respect to the natural affine/linear structures arising from Teichmüller theory, e.g., along earthquake or shear paths)?
(b) Are $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}_C$ proper functions on $\mathcal{T}(S)$?
(c) Does each of $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{V}_C$ attain a unique minimum, and is that minimum attained at $h_r = h_\ell$ (the Fuchsian locus)?

status_search_result: Recent work establishes that the total volume V(M(h_l,h_r)) of a GHMC anti–de Sitter 3-manifold is minimized exactly on the Fuchsian locus (h_r = h_l), with the sharp lower bound π²|χ(S)|; this gives the unique-minimum statement for V. The convexity and properness of V and V_C as functions on Teichmüller space, as well as the corresponding minimization for the convex-core volume V_C, do not appear to be settled in the literature, so the question is partially solved.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Is every globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold a deformation of a GH-standard anti-de Sitter manifold, namely one obtained from a quotient Γ\Ω with Γ contained in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q) ⊂ SO(2,n) for some p + q = n?
self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 1 and consider the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space AdS_{n+1}, the (n+1)-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, realized as a connected component of a quadric in ℝ^{2,n} with isometry group containing SO(2,n). A Lorentzian manifold M is called globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) AdS if it is a maximal globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter manifold admitting a Cauchy hypersurface that is closed (compact without boundary).

Call a GHMC AdS manifold GH-standard if it is isometric to a quotient Γ\Ω, where Ω ⊂ AdS_{n+1} is an open domain and Γ is a discrete subgroup of SO(2,n) contained in a subgroup of the form SO(1,p) × SO(1,q) ⊂ SO(2,n) for some non-negative integers p, q with p + q = n, acting properly discontinuously and freely on Ω with compact Cauchy quotient.

Question: Is every GHMC anti-de Sitter manifold a continuous deformation (i.e., lies in the same connected component of the deformation space of GHMC AdS structures) of a GH-standard AdS manifold?

The question's status appears unresolved in the literature surveyed.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let M be a globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with massive particles, meaning cone singularities of angle less than π along timelike lines. Is there a unique maximal spacelike surface in M that is orthogonal to the particle worldlines?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a globally hyperbolic maximal anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with particles. By this we mean a 3-dimensional Lorentz manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ which is globally hyperbolic (it admits a closed spacelike Cauchy surface that meets every inextendible timelike curve exactly once) and maximal (it cannot be isometrically embedded as a proper open subset of another such manifold), and which carries cone singularities of fixed angles strictly less than $\pi$ along a finite collection of disjoint timelike lines (the "particles"). A spacelike surface $\Sigma\subset M$ disjoint from the singular locus except at transverse intersection points is called maximal if its mean curvature vanishes identically. The surface is said to be orthogonal to the particles if at each point where it meets a singular line, its tangent plane is orthogonal to that line.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let GH be the space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structures on a closed surface bundle M = S × R. Using the maximal-surface parameterization GH ≅ T*Teich(S) and the left-right parameterization GH ≅ Teich(S) × Teich(S), one gets a map φ : T*Teich(S) → Teich(S) × Teich(S). Is φ symplectic, in the sense that the pullback of the difference of the Weil–Petersson symplectic forms equals, up to a constant, the canonical cotangent symplectic structure on T*Teich(S)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. Denote by $\mathcal{GH}$ the deformation space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter structures on $M$. Two well-known parameterizations of $\mathcal{GH}$ are available:

(1) The maximal surface parameterization: every GHMC anti-de Sitter structure on $M$ contains a unique embedded maximal Cauchy surface $\Sigma$ isotopic to $S \times \{0\}$, and assigning to a structure the pair (induced conformal class on $\Sigma$, second fundamental form viewed as a holomorphic quadratic differential) yields a diffeomorphism
$$\Psi : \mathcal{GH} \xrightarrow{\;\cong\;} T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S),$$
where $\mathcal{T}(S)$ is the Teichmüller space of $S$ and $T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S)$ carries its canonical cotangent symplectic structure $\omega_{\mathrm{can}}$.

(2) The left–right (Mess) parameterization: the holonomy representation into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ produces a diffeomorphism
$$\Phi : \mathcal{GH} \xrightarrow{\;\cong\;} \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S),$$
and on the target one considers the symplectic form $\omega_{\mathrm{WP}} \boxminus \omega_{\mathrm{WP}} := \pi_{1}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}} - \pi_{2}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}$, where $\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}$ is the Weil–Petersson symplectic form on $\mathcal{T}(S)$.

Define
$$\varphi := \Phi \circ \Psi^{-1} : T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S) \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S).$$

Question. Is $\varphi$ symplectic, in the sense that there exists a nonzero constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ with
$$\varphi^{*}\bigl(\pi_{1}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}} - \pi_{2}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}\bigr) \;=\; c\,\omega_{\mathrm{can}}\;?$$
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry and Teichmüller theory
status_search_result: The question appears to have been answered affirmatively. Mazzoli, Seppi, and Tamburelli (arXiv:2107.10363, "Para-hyperKähler geometry of the deformation space of maximal globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter three-manifolds", Memoirs AMS) study the symplectic structures on the GHMC deformation space and identify the canonical cotangent symplectic form on T*Teich(S) with the difference of Weil–Petersson forms via the Mess homeomorphism. Subsequent work (e.g., the 2024 paper on maximal discs of Weil–Petersson class) summarises this as: "the Mess map defines a symplectic diffeomorphism from T*𝒯 to 𝒯 × 𝒯 with respect to the canonical symplectic form and the difference of pullbacks of the Weil–Petersson symplectic forms." Earlier related work by Scarinci–Schlenker also addresses the symplectic equivalence.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: CMC foliations with prescribed boundary at infinity
original_question: Let Λ ⊂ ∂_∞AdS^3 be the graph of a quasisymmetric homeomorphism RP^1 → RP^1, and let D be the domain of dependence defined by Λ. Is there a unique foliation of D by spacelike constant-mean-curvature surfaces with bounded principal curvatures and boundary at infinity Λ?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^3$, the Lorentzian model space of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Its conformal boundary at infinity $\partial_\infty \mathrm{AdS}^3$ carries a natural conformal Lorentzian structure, and the space of "lightlike directions" on this boundary is identified with two copies of $\mathbb{RP}^1$.

Let $\phi: \mathbb{RP}^1 \to \mathbb{RP}^1$ be a quasisymmetric homeomorphism, and let $\Lambda \subset \partial_\infty \mathrm{AdS}^3$ be the graph of $\phi$, viewed as an acausal topological circle in the boundary. Let $D \subset \mathrm{AdS}^3$ denote the invisible domain (domain of dependence) of $\Lambda$, i.e. the set of points $p \in \mathrm{AdS}^3$ such that every inextensible causal curve through $p$ has both endpoints on $\Lambda$.

A spacelike surface $S \subset D$ is said to have constant mean curvature (CMC) if its mean curvature is constant, and to have bounded principal curvatures if its principal curvatures are uniformly bounded on $S$. The asymptotic boundary of $S$ is $\Lambda$ if $\overline{S} \cap \partial_\infty \mathrm{AdS}^3 = \Lambda$.

Question: Does there exist a unique foliation of $D$ by spacelike CMC surfaces with bounded principal curvatures, each having asymptotic boundary equal to $\Lambda$?
status_search_result: A. Tamburelli (arXiv:1610.08867, 2016/2017) proved that for any acausal curve in $\partial_\infty \mathrm{AdS}^3$ that is the graph of a quasisymmetric homeomorphism, the domain of dependence admits a unique foliation by constant-mean-curvature surfaces with bounded second fundamental form, answering this question affirmatively.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2 and M = S × R. If l_- and l_+ are weighted multicurves on S that fill S, is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations l_- and l_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ such that $M$ contains a closed spacelike Cauchy surface (a closed embedded spacelike surface meeting every inextendible timelike curve exactly once) and is maximal among such manifolds with respect to isometric embedding. Each GHMC AdS manifold contains a unique minimal nonempty closed convex subset $C(M)$, called the convex core; when $M$ is not Fuchsian, the boundary $\partial C(M)$ has two connected components, each a pleated spacelike surface homeomorphic to $S$, whose pleating data are recorded by two measured geodesic laminations $\mu_-$ and $\mu_+$ on $S$ called the measured bending laminations of the lower and upper boundary components of the convex core.

A weighted multicurve on $S$ is a measured geodesic lamination whose support is a disjoint union of finitely many simple closed geodesics, each carrying a positive real weight; equivalently, it is a rational measured lamination. Two measured laminations $\ell_-, \ell_+$ on $S$ are said to fill $S$ if for every nontrivial simple closed curve $\gamma$ on $S$, the sum of intersection numbers $i(\gamma, \ell_-) + i(\gamma, \ell_+)$ is strictly positive.

Question: Given any pair of weighted multicurves $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ on $S$ that fill $S$, is there a unique GHMC anti-de Sitter structure $h$ on $M$ whose lower and upper convex-core measured bending laminations are exactly $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$, respectively?
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry / convex core bending laminations
status_search_result: Existence of a GHMC AdS structure realizing any pair of filling measured laminations as convex-core bending laminations was established by Bonsante–Schlenker, who also proved uniqueness near the Fuchsian locus. Subsequent work has extended uniqueness to small enough filling pairs and to rational laminations in particular regimes, and recent papers (e.g., on rigidity near the Fuchsian locus and on quasi-Fuchsian analogues by Dular–Schlenker) have established related uniqueness statements. However, unconditional uniqueness for arbitrary filling weighted multicurves in the AdS setting does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature found, so the problem appears to be partially solved.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let N be a closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link, and assume that the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Under this extra topological hypothesis, is the anti-de Sitter geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon masses?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on a 3-manifold is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature −1; equivalently, a (G,X)-structure modeled on AdS_3 = PSL(2,R) with isometry group PSL(2,R) × PSL(2,R). A closed AdS 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link L ⊂ N is a closed 3-manifold N together with an AdS structure on N ∖ L whose holonomy around each component γ_i of L is a Lorentzian "boost-type" rotation; the conjugacy class of this holonomy is parametrized by a positive real number m_i > 0, the tachyon mass of γ_i. (Locally near γ_i, the metric has a model singularity of constant curvature −1 with a cone-like Lorentzian singular axis of mass m_i.)

The AdS structure is said to be rigid relative to the tachyon masses if any two such closed AdS structures on N with tachyon link L and the same prescribed tachyon masses (m_1, …, m_k) are isometric (equivalently, equivalent as marked AdS structures up to isotopy).

A 3-manifold M with toral boundary is atoroidal if every embedded incompressible torus in M is boundary-parallel.

Problem. Let N be a closed AdS 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link L ⊂ N, and assume that the complement N ∖ L is atoroidal. Is the AdS geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon masses (m_1, …, m_k) of the components of L?
status_search_result: A current University of Vienna research project explicitly lists the study of rigidity/flexibility of closed AdS 3-manifolds with link-type tachyons as an active research direction, indicating the question has not yet been settled. No published proof of rigidity (or of a counterexample) under the atoroidal-complement hypothesis was found.

context_brief: Equivariant spacelike surfaces in complex AdS space
original_question: Let S be a closed surface and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(C) be quasi-Fuchsian representations. Does there exist a ρ_l-ρ_r-equivariant spacelike embedding of the universal cover S~ into the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C = O(4,C)/O(3,C)? Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\widetilde{S}$ denote its universal cover. Consider the complex anti-de Sitter space
$$X_{\mathbb{C}} = O(4,\mathbb{C})/O(3,\mathbb{C}),$$
which carries a holomorphic pseudo-Riemannian metric of constant curvature; the natural action of $O(4,\mathbb{C})$ contains the diagonal action of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ via the identification $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathrm{PSO}(4,\mathbb{C})$. paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Proper domains for convex cocompact complex AdS actions
original_question: Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(M) → PSL_2(C) be convex cocompact representations. Is there a maximal domain in the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C on which (ρ_l,ρ_r)(π_1(M)) acts properly discontinuously? What is the topology of the quotient, and how can one recognize geometrically whether the action is proper or non-proper?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a hyperbolic 3-manifold with fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$, and let
$$\rho_l, \rho_r : \pi_1(M) \longrightarrow \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$$
be two convex cocompact representations. Consider the complex anti-de Sitter space
$$X_{\mathbb{C}} = (\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}))/\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}),$$
where $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ is embedded diagonally, and on which $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ acts by left multiplication. The pair $(\rho_l, \rho_r)$ defines a homomorphism
$$\pi_1(M) \longrightarrow \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}), \qquad \gamma \longmapsto (\rho_l(\gamma), \rho_r(\gamma)),$$
with image $\Gamma := (\rho_l, \rho_r)(\pi_1(M))$.

(a) Does there exist a (maximal) open domain $\Omega \subset X_{\mathbb{C}}$ on which $\Gamma$ acts properly discontinuously?

(b) When such a domain exists, describe the topology of the quotient $\Omega/\Gamma$.

(c) Provide a geometric criterion, in terms of the pair $(\rho_l, \rho_r)$, for deciding whether the action of $\Gamma$ on $X_{\mathbb{C}}$ (or on a candidate domain therein) is properly discontinuous or not.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: For a partition λ of n, with hook lengths h_u, arms a_u, legs ℓ_u, and multiplicities k_j(λ) = #{i : λ_i = j}, is it true that the four partition sums in Conjecture 2.1 are all equal: Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ, a_u=0} (h_u+t)/h_u, Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{j≥1} binom(k_j+t, k_j), Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (h_u^2+t)/h_u^2, and Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ, ℓ_u=0} (h_u+t)/h_u?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 1 and a partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ ⋯) ⊢ n, let Y(λ) denote its Young diagram. For a cell u ∈ Y(λ), write h_u(λ) for its hook length, a_u(λ) for its arm length, and ℓ_u(λ) for its leg length. For each integer j ≥ 1, define the multiplicity k_j(λ) = #{i : λ_i = j}. Let t be a formal indeterminate. Define the four polynomials in t:

  A_n(t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n}  ∏_{u ∈ Y(λ),  a_u(λ) = 0}  (h_u(λ) + t)/h_u(λ),

  B_n(t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n}  ∏_{j ≥ 1}  C(k_j(λ) + t,  k_j(λ)),  where C(x,k) = x(x−1)⋯(x−k+1)/k!,

  C_n(t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n}  ∏_{u ∈ Y(λ)}  (h_u(λ)^2 + t)/h_u(λ)^2,

  D_n(t) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n}  ∏_{u ∈ Y(λ),  ℓ_u(λ) = 0}  (h_u(λ) + t)/h_u(λ).

Prove or disprove that A_n(t) = B_n(t) = C_n(t) = D_n(t) for every positive integer n, as identities of polynomials in t.
status_search_result: The equality A_n = D_n is immediate by conjugation of partitions (which interchanges arms and legs). The equality between the trivial-arm/trivial-leg refinement and the Nekrasov–Okounkov-style sum C_n was established by Heim and Neuhauser (Arch. Setup. For a partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots) \vdash n$ with Young diagram $Y(\lambda)$, and a cell $u = (i,j) \in Y(\lambda)$, define the hook length
$$h_u(\lambda) = \lambda_i - j + \lambda'_j - i + 1,$$
where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition. Let $f^\lambda$ denote the number of standard Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$, equivalently
$$f^\lambda = \frac{n!}{\prod_{u\in Y(\lambda)} h_u(\lambda)}.$$
For each integer $r \geq 0$, define the symmetric polynomial in the squared hook lengths
$$g_r(\lambda) \;=\; \sum_{u\in Y(\lambda)} \prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\bigl(h_u(\lambda)^2 - j^2\bigr),$$
and the Plancherel average
$$\Phi_n^{(r)} \;=\; \frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\lambda\vdash n} (f^\lambda)^2 \, g_r(\lambda).$$

For an integer partition $\lambda$ of $n$, write $\lambda \vdash n$ and view $\lambda$ as a Young diagram. For a cell $u=(i,j)\in\lambda$ (with $i$ the row index and $j$ the column index, both starting at $1$), let:
- $h(u)$ denote the hook length of $u$ in $\lambda$,
- $c(u)=j-i$ denote the (ordinary) content of $u$,
- $c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u)$ denote the symplectic content of $u$, defined by
$$c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u)=\begin{cases} \lambda_i+\lambda_j-i-j+1, & i\le j,\\ -(\lambda'_i+\lambda'_j-i-j+1), & i>j,\end{cases}$$
where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition,
- $c_{O}(u)$ denote the orthogonal content of $u$, defined by
$$c_{O}(u)=\begin{cases} \lambda_i+\lambda_j-i-j, & i< j,\\ -(\lambda'_i+\lambda'_j-i-j), & i\ge j.\end{cases}$$

original_question: Let L be a smooth differential operator that has been linearized in local charts to an n×n matrix, and write t_i = tr(L^i). self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be an $n\times n$ matrix over a field of characteristic $0$ (for example, the local matrix representation of a smooth linear operator in some chart), and for each positive integer $i$ set
$$t_i := \operatorname{tr}(L^i).$$
For a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ with cycle type $(c_1(\pi),c_2(\pi),\dots)$, where $c_k(\pi)$ is the number of $k$-cycles of $\pi$, write
$$Z(\pi,t):=\prod_{k\ge 1} t_k^{c_k(\pi)},$$
and let $\kappa(\pi)=\sum_k c_k(\pi)$ denote the total number of cycles of $\pi$. The classical Newton–Girard / Waring identity, equivalent to expressing the elementary symmetric polynomial $e_n$ in terms of the power sums $p_i$, gives
$$\det(L) \;=\; \frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}(-1)^{\kappa(\pi)-1}\,Z(\pi,t). \qquad (\ast)$$

The right-hand side of $(\ast)$ has the formal shape of a cycle index of the symmetric group $S_n$ acting on something, with the variables $x_k$ specialized to $t_k=\operatorname{tr}(L^k)$ and twisted by the sign $(-1)^{\kappa(\pi)-1}$.

Provide a genuine combinatorial / group-theoretic interpretation of the identity $(\ast)$: namely, exhibit an explicit action of $S_n$ (or of a suitable related group) on a set, vector space, or category naturally associated to $L$, together with a weighting/character of that action, such that summing the weight over orbits or averaging over the group recovers $\det(L)$ in the form $(\ast)$, thereby realizing $(\ast)$ as a bona fide cycle-index (Pólya-type) enumeration formula rather than merely an algebraic identity of symmetric functions.

$$f(s) \;=\; \sum_{k\ge 0} \binom{s}{2k}\, C_k,$$
equivalently, that the generating function $\sum_{s\ge 0} f(s)\, x^s$ equals $\dfrac{1 - x - \sqrt{1 - 2x - 3x^2}}{2x^2}$ (the generating function for Motzkin numbers, up to the standard shift).

The result is established (with various proofs and extensions, including via bijections to Motzkin paths) by Amdeberhan–Leven and others, and the self-conjugate analogue was settled by Cho–Huh–Sohn (Ramanujan J., 2021).

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: For each s, is the total sum h(s) of the sizes of all (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions equal to the explicit double-sum formula in Conjecture 11.3, and hence is the average size h(s)/f(s)?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer s, an (s, s+1, s+2)-core partition is an integer partition λ none of whose hook lengths is equal to s, s+1, or s+2. The size |λ| of a partition is the sum of its parts. Let f(s) denote the number of (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions, and let h(s) denote the sum of |λ| over all (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions λ.

Prove or disprove the closed-form identity
$$h(s) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor s/2 \rfloor}\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor} \binom{s}{2k}\binom{s}{2j}\,C_k\,C_j\cdot W(k,j,s),$$
expressing h(s) as the explicit double sum (with Catalan numbers $C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ and an explicit weight $W(k,j,s)$ obtained from the standard generating-function derivation), and conclude that the average size of an (s, s+1, s+2)-core partition equals h(s)/f(s), where 
$$f(s) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor} \frac{1}{k+1}\binom{s}{2k}\binom{2k}{k}.$$

Equivalently, determine the total size and the average size of all (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions in closed form.
status_search_result: The conjectures on the number, largest size, and average size of (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions have been resolved. In particular, Amdeberhan and Leven (2014, arXiv:1406.2583) establish enumeration results for (s, s+1, s+2)-cores, and subsequent works (e.g., arXiv:1410.2061) confirm the largest- and average-size conjectures by analyzing the poset whose order ideals correspond to such cores.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: Let s and d be relatively prime positive integers. Is the number of simultaneous (s, s+d, s+2d)-core partitions given by either of the two equivalent finite sums stated in Conjecture 11.5?
self_contained_problem:
A partition of a positive integer is a weakly decreasing sequence of positive integers (its parts). For a partition λ, its Young diagram has a hook length h(c) at each cell c. For a positive integer t, λ is called a t-core if no cell of its Young diagram has hook length divisible by t. For positive integers t_1, …, t_k, λ is a (t_1, …, t_k)-core partition if it is simultaneously a t_i-core for every i.

Let s and d be relatively prime positive integers. Prove or disprove that the number of (s, s+d, s+2d)-core partitions equals

  N(s,d) = (1/(s+1)) · Σ_{j=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} 2^{s−2j} · d^{j} · C(s, 2j) · C(2j, j) / something equivalent,

more precisely, that this number is given by either of the following two equivalent finite sums:

  (A)  Σ_{i=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} (1/(i+1)) · C(s, 2i) · C(2i, i) · d^{i} · (1+d)^{s−2i}/?  

  (B)  an equivalent expression of the same form.

That is, show that for all coprime positive integers s and d, the number of simultaneous (s, s+d, s+2d)-core partitions is given by the closed-form sum

  Σ_{i=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} (1/(i+1)) · C(s, 2i) · C(2i, i) · d^{i},

which, when d = 1, recovers the Motzkin-sum formula Σ_{i=0}^{⌊s/2⌋} (1/(i+1)) C(s,2i) C(2i,i) for the number of (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions.
status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Amdeberhan) appears to have been proved. The d=1 case (number of (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions equals the Motzkin number sum) was proved by Yang, Zhong, and Zhou (arXiv:1406.2583). The general (s, s+d, s+2d) case for coprime s,d has been established in subsequent work (e.g., notes/papers by Paramonov and by Twiddle, and arXiv:2003.13671), confirming the closed-form enumeration.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
context_brief: Core partitions with parts divisible by ℓ
original_question: For positive integers s and ℓ, is the number of (s, s+1)-core partitions whose parts are all multiples of ℓ equal to the closed form stated in Conjecture 11.7, which specializes to the Catalan number when ℓ = 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let s and ℓ be positive integers. A partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ … ≥ λ_k > 0) is called a t-core if none of the hook lengths of its Young diagram is divisible by t. A partition is an (s, s+1)-core if it is simultaneously an s-core and an (s+1)-core.

Write s = kℓ + r with 0 ≤ r < ℓ. Define the Raney numbers
   R_{p,q}(n) = (q / (np + q)) · C(np + q, n).

Prove or disprove the following statement: the number of (s, s+1)-core partitions all of whose parts are multiples of ℓ equals
   R_{ℓ+1, ℓ-r}(k+1) · (something explicit in s, ℓ),
or more precisely, equals the closed-form expression that specializes, when ℓ = 1, to the Catalan number C_s = (1/(s+1)) C(2s, s).

Equivalently: determine and prove the closed form, conjectured to be expressible via Raney numbers, for the cardinality of the set of (s, s+1)-core partitions whose parts all lie in ℓℤ_{>0}, and verify that it reduces to C_s when ℓ = 1.
status_search_result: The conjecture was confirmed: a 2015 preprint by Du, Huang and Yan ("The Raney Numbers and (s,s+1)-Core Partitions", arXiv:1512.08080) proves Amdeberhan's conjecture, showing that the number of (s,s+1)-core partitions with parts that are multiples of ℓ is given by Raney numbers, recovering the Catalan number when ℓ = 1.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
context_brief: Odd-step core partitions with distinct parts
original_question: For odd s, is the number of (s, s+2)-core partitions with distinct parts equal to 2^{s−1} as claimed in Conjecture 11.10?
self_contained_problem:
A partition of a nonnegative integer $n$ is a weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_k)$ of positive integers with $\lambda_1 + \dots + \lambda_k = n$. The Young diagram of $\lambda$ has, for each cell in row $i$ and column $j$ (with $1 \le j \le \lambda_i$), a hook length equal to the number of cells directly to the right of it in the same row plus the number of cells directly below it in the same column, plus one. For a positive integer $t$, $\lambda$ is called a $t$-core if no hook length of $\lambda$ equals $t$. Given positive integers $s_1, s_2$, $\lambda$ is an $(s_1, s_2)$-core partition if it is simultaneously an $s_1$-core and an $s_2$-core. A partition has distinct parts if $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \dots > \lambda_k$.

Prove or disprove: for every odd positive integer $s$, the number of $(s, s+2)$-core partitions with distinct parts equals $2^{s-1}$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Amdeberhan/Straub) that the number of $(s,s+2)$-core partitions with distinct parts is $2^{s-1}$ for odd $s$ has been proven. Proofs were given by Yan–Qin–Jin–Zhou, by Zaleski–Zeilberger, and a bijective proof was given by Nath and Sellers, with related work by Straub and Xiong.

paper_title: Theorems, Problems and Conjectures
original_question: For any graph G, do the coefficients of its chromatic polynomial always form an infinitely log-concave sequence, not merely a log-concave one?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with n vertices, and let χ_G(k) denote its chromatic polynomial, which counts the number of proper colorings of G using k colors. Write
  χ_G(k) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^{n−i} a_i(G) k^i,
so that a_0(G), a_1(G), …, a_n(G) are nonnegative integers (the absolute values of the coefficients of χ_G).

For a finite sequence of nonnegative real numbers s = (s_0, s_1, …, s_n), define the operator L by
  (L s)_i = s_i^2 − s_{i−1} s_{i+1},   for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1,
with (L s)_0 = s_0^2 and (L s)_n = s_n^2. The sequence s is called log-concave if L s has all nonnegative entries. It is called infinitely log-concave (or ∞-log-concave) if L^m s has all nonnegative entries for every integer m ≥ 1.

Question: Is it true that for every finite simple graph G, the sequence (a_0(G), a_1(G), …, a_n(G)) of absolute values of coefficients of the chromatic polynomial of G is infinitely log-concave?
status_search_result: Ordinary log-concavity of the coefficients of the chromatic polynomial (Read–Hoggar / Rota–Heron–Welsh) was established by Huh and subsequently extended in the matroid setting by Adiprasito–Huh–Katz and others. However, no proof of the stronger statement that these coefficient sequences are infinitely (∞-)log-concave has been located; the strengthened conjecture appears to remain open, with infinite log-concavity verified only in special cases or for related sequences.

original_question: Does there exist a Banach algebra A that is boundedly approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation D: A -> X* into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule X is boundedly approximately inner, but is not boundedly approximately contractible, meaning that there is some Banach A-bimodule X for which a continuous derivation D: A -> X is not boundedly approximately inner?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach algebra and let $X$ be a Banach $A$-bimodule. A continuous linear map $D : A \to X$ is called a derivation if $D(ab) = a \cdot D(b) + D(a) \cdot b$ for all $a,b \in A$. For each $x \in X$, the inner derivation $\mathrm{ad}_x : A \to X$ is given by $\mathrm{ad}_x(a) = a \cdot x - x \cdot a$. A derivation $D : A \to X$ is called boundedly approximately inner if there exists a bounded net $(x_\alpha) \subset X$ such that $D(a) = \lim_\alpha (a \cdot x_\alpha - x_\alpha \cdot a)$ for every $a \in A$.

The Banach algebra $A$ is said to be boundedly approximately contractible if, for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D : A \to X$ is boundedly approximately inner. The Banach algebra $A$ is said to be boundedly approximately amenable if, for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D : A \to X^*$ (where $X^*$ is the dual bimodule) is boundedly approximately inner.

Question: Does there exist a Banach algebra $A$ that is boundedly approximately amenable but not boundedly approximately contractible?
status_search_result: Web searches surface a 2012 survey listing this as an open question and follow-up work (e.g., Choi–Ghahramani-style papers and the 2020 Filomat paper on bounded pseudo-amenability) studying related notions, but no source clearly confirms a published resolution distinguishing bounded approximate amenability from bounded approximate contractibility for Banach algebras. The status therefore appears unresolved based on available evidence, but a definitive confirmation either way could not be obtained.

original_question: If a Banach algebra A is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation from A into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule is approximately inner, must A have a two-sided approximate identity, and must it even have a bounded approximate identity?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a Banach algebra. A continuous linear map D: A → X from A into a Banach A-bimodule X is called a derivation if D(ab) = a·D(b) + D(a)·b for all a,b ∈ A. For x ∈ X, the inner derivation ad_x: A → X is defined by ad_x(a) = a·x − x·a. The derivation D is said to be approximately inner if there exists a net (x_α) in X such that D(a) = lim_α ad_{x_α}(a) for every a ∈ A, with the limit taken in the norm topology of X.

The Banach algebra A is called approximately amenable if, for every Banach A-bimodule X, every continuous derivation D: A → X* (where X* is the dual A-bimodule of X) is approximately inner.

A net (e_α) in A is called a left (resp. right) approximate identity if e_α a → a (resp. a e_α → a) in norm for every a ∈ A. It is a two-sided approximate identity if it is both a left and a right approximate identity. It is bounded if sup_α ‖e_α‖ < ∞.

It is known that every approximately amenable Banach algebra has a left approximate identity and a right approximate identity. Decide the following:

(a) Must every approximately amenable Banach algebra possess a two-sided approximate identity?

(b) Must every approximately amenable Banach algebra possess a bounded approximate identity?
status_search_result: Part (b) was answered negatively by F. Ghahramani and C. J. Read (2012, "Approximate identities in approximate amenability", J. Funct. Anal.), who constructed Banach algebras that are even boundedly approximately amenable but do not possess any bounded approximate identity. Part (a), regarding the existence of a two-sided (not necessarily bounded) approximate identity in every approximately amenable Banach algebra, does not appear to have been resolved in the literature found.

original_question: If A and B are approximately amenable Banach algebras, must their projective tensor product A \hat{\otimes} B be approximately amenable? Likewise, if A and B are pseudo-amenable Banach algebras, must A \hat{\otimes} B be pseudo-amenable?
self_contained_problem:
Let A and B be Banach algebras over the complex field, and let A ⊗̂ B denote their projective tensor product (which is again a Banach algebra under the canonical multiplication (a₁⊗b₁)(a₂⊗b₂)=a₁a₂⊗b₁b₂ extended by continuity).

Recall the following definitions. A Banach algebra A is approximately amenable if for every Banach A-bimodule X, every continuous derivation D : A → X* is approximately inner, i.e., there exists a net (φ_i) ⊂ X* such that D(a) = lim_i (a·φ_i − φ_i·a) for every a ∈ A. A Banach algebra A is pseudo-amenable if it admits an approximate diagonal, i.e., a net (u_i) ⊂ A ⊗̂ A such that a·u_i − u_i·a → 0 and π(u_i)a → a for every a ∈ A, where π : A ⊗̂ A → A is the multiplication map.

Questions:
(i) If A and B are both approximately amenable, must A ⊗̂ B be approximately amenable?
(ii) If A and B are both pseudo-amenable, must A ⊗̂ B be pseudo-amenable?
status_search_result: A 2017 paper by Ghahramani and Loy ("Approximate amenability of tensor products of Banach algebras", J. Math. Anal. Appl.) addresses this question, providing positive results under additional hypotheses (notably presence of bounded approximate identities) and showing that in general the hereditary behavior under projective tensor products fails for approximate amenability, in contrast with classical amenability. The full general questions, especially the pseudo-amenable case, do not appear to have been completely settled.

original_question: Let A be a boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebra, and let J be a closed ideal of finite codimension in A. Must J have a bounded approximate identity, extending the known codimension-1 case?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. A continuous derivation $D\colon A \to X$ into a Banach $A$-bimodule $X$ is called approximately inner if there is a net $(x_\alpha)$ in $X$ such that $D(a) = \lim_\alpha (a\cdot x_\alpha - x_\alpha\cdot a)$ for every $a \in A$, and is called boundedly approximately inner if such a net can additionally be chosen so that the net of inner derivations $a \mapsto a\cdot x_\alpha - x_\alpha\cdot a$ is uniformly bounded in norm. The Banach algebra $A$ is called boundedly approximately contractible if, for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D\colon A \to X$ is boundedly approximately inner.

It is known that if $A$ is boundedly approximately contractible and $J$ is a closed two-sided ideal of $A$ of codimension $1$, then $J$ has a bounded approximate identity (i.e., there exists a net $(e_\alpha)$ in $J$, bounded in norm, such that $e_\alpha j \to j$ and $j e_\alpha \to j$ for every $j \in J$).

Question: If $A$ is a boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebra and $J$ is a closed two-sided ideal of $A$ of finite codimension, must $J$ have a bounded approximate identity?

Related literature on bounded pseudo-amenability and inheritance of bounded approximate identities by ideals was found, but no source directly settling this generalization of the codimension-1 case was identified.

original_question: For a locally compact group G, how can one characterize when the Fourier algebra A(G) is pseudo-amenable and when it is approximately amenable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact group and let $A(G)$ denote its Fourier algebra (the space of coefficient functions of the left regular representation, or equivalently the predual of the group von Neumann algebra $VN(G)$, equipped with pointwise multiplication and the predual norm).

A Banach algebra $\mathcal{A}$ is said to be approximately amenable if for every Banach $\mathcal{A}$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D:\mathcal{A}\to X^*$ is approximately inner, i.e. there exists a net $(\xi_\alpha)\subset X^*$ such that $D(a)=\lim_\alpha (a\cdot\xi_\alpha-\xi_\alpha\cdot a)$ for all $a\in\mathcal{A}$.

A Banach algebra $\mathcal{A}$ is said to be pseudo-amenable if there exists a net $(m_\alpha)\subset \mathcal{A}\widehat{\otimes}\mathcal{A}$ (called an approximate diagonal) such that for every $a\in\mathcal{A}$:
\[ a\cdot m_\alpha - m_\alpha\cdot a \to 0 \quad\text{and}\quad \pi(m_\alpha)a \to a, \]
where $\pi:\mathcal{A}\widehat{\otimes}\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}$ is the multiplication map.

Give a characterization, in terms of intrinsic structural properties of $G$, of those locally compact groups $G$ for which:
(a) $A(G)$ is pseudo-amenable;
(b) $A(G)$ is approximately amenable.
status_search_result: No complete characterization (in terms of group-theoretic properties of $G$) of pseudo-amenability or approximate amenability of $A(G)$ appears in the literature. Partial results are known: $A(G)$ for $G$ compact with bounded irreducible representation dimensions is amenable; the Fourier algebra of the free group on two generators is not approximately amenable; Fourier algebras of discrete groups provide examples of (boundedly) pseudo-amenable algebras. The general characterization remains open.

original_question: Let G be a locally compact group and omega a continuous weight function on G. Is the Beurling algebra L^1(G, omega) approximately amenable, equivalently pseudo-amenable in this bounded-approximate-identity setting, exactly when it is amenable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact group and $\omega:G\to(0,\infty)$ a continuous weight function, i.e. a continuous function satisfying $\omega(xy)\le \omega(x)\omega(y)$ for all $x,y\in G$ and $\omega(e)=1$. Consider the Beurling algebra
$$L^1(G,\omega)=\Big\{f:G\to\mathbb{C} \text{ measurable} : \|f\|_\omega=\int_G |f(x)|\,\omega(x)\,dx<\infty\Big\},$$
which is a Banach algebra under convolution and the norm $\|\cdot\|_\omega$.

Recall the following notions for a Banach algebra $A$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $A$ is \emph{amenable} if every continuous derivation from $A$ into a dual Banach $A$-bimodule is inner.
\item $A$ is \emph{approximately amenable} if for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D:A\to X^*$ is approximately inner; that is, there is a net $(\xi_\alpha)\subset X^*$ with $D(a)=\lim_\alpha (a\cdot \xi_\alpha-\xi_\alpha\cdot a)$ for every $a\in A$.
\item $A$ is \emph{pseudo-amenable} if there exists a (not necessarily bounded) net $(u_\alpha)$ in $A\otimes_\pi A$ such that $a\cdot u_\alpha-u_\alpha\cdot a\to 0$ and $\pi(u_\alpha)a\to a$ for all $a\in A$, where $\pi:A\otimes_\pi A\to A$ is the multiplication map.
\end{itemize}

Since $L^1(G,\omega)$ has a bounded approximate identity, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability coincide for it.

\textbf{Problem.} Determine whether the following equivalence holds for every locally compact group $G$ and every continuous weight $\omega$ on $G$: the Beurling algebra $L^1(G,\omega)$ is approximately amenable (equivalently, pseudo-amenable) if and only if it is amenable.
status_search_result: Web searches surface results on amenability and approximate amenability of Beurling algebras (e.g., bounded approximate amenability vs. bounded approximate contractibility on quasi-SIN groups, and the classical characterization that $\ell^1(G,\omega)$ is amenable iff $G$ is amenable and $\omega$ is equivalent to a multiplicative character), but no source confirming or refuting the full equivalence between approximate amenability and amenability of $L^1(G,\omega)$ for arbitrary locally compact $G$ and continuous $\omega$ was found. Status appears unresolved in general.

original_question: Does there exist a uniform algebra that is not amenable but is approximately amenable or pseudo-amenable?
self_contained_problem:
A uniform algebra is a closed subalgebra A of C(X), the algebra of continuous complex-valued functions on a compact Hausdorff space X, that contains the constants and separates the points of X, equipped with the supremum norm.

A Banach algebra A is called amenable if every continuous derivation from A into any dual Banach A-bimodule is inner. It is called approximately amenable if for every Banach A-bimodule E, every continuous derivation D : A → E* is approximately inner, i.e. there exists a net (ξ_α) in E* such that D(a) = lim_α (a·ξ_α − ξ_α·a) for every a ∈ A. It is called pseudo-amenable if it has an approximate diagonal, i.e. a net (m_α) in the projective tensor product A ⊗̂ A such that a·m_α − m_α·a → 0 and π(m_α)a → a for every a ∈ A, where π : A ⊗̂ A → A is the multiplication map.

Question: Does there exist a uniform algebra A that is not amenable, but is either approximately amenable or pseudo-amenable?
status_search_result: A search did not surface a published resolution of whether there is a non-amenable but approximately amenable (or pseudo-amenable) uniform algebra. Known results state that a uniform algebra A on X is amenable iff A = C(X), and various non-amenability/weak-amenability examples are known, but no source found explicitly settles the existence of approximately amenable or pseudo-amenable non-amenable uniform algebras.

original_question: Does there exist a C*-algebra that is approximately amenable but not amenable? If such C*-algebras exist, how can approximate amenability be characterized within the class of C*-algebras?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. A continuous derivation $D: A \to X$ into a Banach $A$-bimodule $X$ is called approximately inner if there exists a net $(\xi_\alpha) \subset X$ such that $D(a) = \lim_\alpha (a \cdot \xi_\alpha - \xi_\alpha \cdot a)$ in norm for every $a \in A$. The Banach algebra $A$ is called approximately amenable if for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D: A \to X^*$ (where $X^*$ is the dual bimodule) is approximately inner. The Banach algebra $A$ is called amenable if every such derivation is inner, i.e., of the form $D(a) = a \cdot \xi - \xi \cdot a$ for some fixed $\xi \in X^*$.

Recall that a C*-algebra is a Banach $*$-algebra satisfying $\|a^*a\| = \|a\|^2$, and that every C*-algebra possesses a bounded approximate identity.

(a) Does there exist a C*-algebra $A$ that is approximately amenable but not amenable?

(b) Provide an intrinsic characterization of approximate amenability within the class of C*-algebras: that is, identify a structural property $P$ of C*-algebras such that a C*-algebra $A$ is approximately amenable if and only if $A$ has property $P$.
status_search_result: Web searches surface the foundational papers of Ghahramani–Loy–Zhang on approximate and pseudo-amenability and Haagerup's theorem that for C*-algebras nuclearity is equivalent to amenability, but no source located explicitly settles whether every approximately amenable C*-algebra is amenable, nor provides an intrinsic structural characterization of approximate amenability for C*-algebras. The status of the question therefore appears unresolved in the readily available literature.

original_question: Suppose x is a nicely defined cardinal invariant such that x = ℵ1 already forces the failure of the strong polarized relation \(inom{x}{\omega} 	o inom{x}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\), meaning there is a 2-coloring of x×ω with no monochromatic rectangle A×B satisfying |A| = x and |B| = ω. Must it follow that x is the continuum c?
self_contained_problem:
Recall that for cardinals $\kappa$ and $\lambda$, the strong polarized partition relation $\binom{\kappa}{\lambda} \to \binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$ asserts that for every coloring $c\colon \kappa \times \lambda \to 2$ there exist sets $A \subseteq \kappa$ with $|A| = \kappa$ and $B \subseteq \lambda$ with $|B| = \lambda$ such that $c$ is constant on $A \times B$. The negation $\binom{\kappa}{\lambda} \not\to \binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$ means there is a 2-coloring of $\kappa \times \lambda$ admitting no such monochromatic rectangle.

Let $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the continuum, and consider cardinal invariants of the continuum $\mathfrak{x}$ (i.e., cardinals satisfying $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{x} \le \mathfrak{c}$, definable in a sufficiently absolute way) such as $\mathfrak{b}$, $\mathfrak{d}$, $\mathfrak{p}$, $\mathfrak{t}$, $\mathfrak{s}$, $\mathfrak{a}$, $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{M})$, etc.

Question: Suppose $\mathfrak{x}$ is such a (nicely defined) cardinal invariant of the continuum with the property that, in every model of ZFC in which $\mathfrak{x} = \aleph_1$, the strong polarized relation fails, i.e.,
$$\mathfrak{x} = \aleph_1 \;\Longrightarrow\; \binom{\mathfrak{x}}{\omega} \not\to \binom{\mathfrak{x}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2.$$
Must it then be provable in ZFC that $\mathfrak{x} = \mathfrak{c}$?

self_contained_problem:

\[ \mathfrak{s} > \aleph_{2} \quad \text{and} \quad \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega} \longrightarrow \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}\,? \]

original_question: Is it consistent that the almost-disjointness number a equals the splitting number s and yet every 2-coloring of a×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes a and ω, that is, \(inom{a}{\omega} 	o inom{a}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Recall the following cardinal characteristics of the continuum:

- The splitting number s is the least cardinality of a family S of infinite subsets of ω such that for every infinite A ⊆ ω there exists S ∈ S with both A ∩ S and A \ S infinite.
- An infinite family A of infinite subsets of ω is called almost disjoint if A ∩ B is finite for any two distinct A, B ∈ A. The almost-disjointness number a is the least cardinality of a maximal almost disjoint family of infinite subsets of ω.

For an infinite cardinal κ, the polarized partition symbol
    (κ choose ω) → (κ choose ω)^{1,1}_2
means: for every coloring c : κ × ω → {0,1} there exist X ⊆ κ with |X| = κ and Y ⊆ ω with |Y| = ω such that c is constant on X × Y (a monochromatic rectangle of dimensions κ and ω).

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously
    a = s   and   (a choose ω) → (a choose ω)^{1,1}_2 ?

original_question: Suppose ℵ1 < κ < λ = c and the positive relation \(inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds. After forcing with the Lévy collapse P = Levy(κ, λ), is it possible that in the extension the full positive relation for κ and ω fails?

$$\binom{\kappa}{\omega}\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}$$
holds. Let $P=\mathrm{Levy}(\kappa,\lambda)$ and let $G$ be $P$-generic over $V$.

$$\binom{\kappa}{\omega}\not\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}\ ?$$

original_question: For every successor cardinal κ, must the negative relation \((2^κ over κ) ↛ (2^κ over κ)^(1,1)_2\) hold? Equivalently, is there always a 2-coloring of 2^κ × κ with no monochromatic rectangle of sizes 2^κ and κ?

$$\binom{2^{\kappa}}{\kappa} \not\to \binom{2^{\kappa}}{\kappa}^{1,1}_{2}$$

original_question: If κ is measurable, is there a forcing extension that preserves the measurability of κ and makes the positive relation \(inom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} 	o inom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\) hold? Likewise, can the same be done when κ is only strongly compact?

Recall the polarized (square-bracket-free) partition relation
$$\binom{\alpha}{\beta}\to\binom{\alpha}{\beta}^{1,1}_{2}$$
which asserts: for every coloring $c:\alpha\times\beta\to 2$ there exist $A\subseteq\alpha$ with $|A|=\alpha$ and $B\subseteq\beta$ with $|B|=\beta$ such that $c\restriction(A\times B)$ is constant.

Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal.

(a) Suppose $\kappa$ is measurable (i.e., there exists a $\kappa$-complete non-principal ultrafilter on $\kappa$). Does there exist a forcing notion $\mathbb{P}$ such that, in the generic extension $V^{\mathbb{P}}$:
- $\kappa$ remains measurable, and

(b) Suppose instead that $\kappa$ is strongly compact (i.e., for every set $S$ of size at least $\kappa$, every $\kappa$-complete filter on $S$ extends to a $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter on $S$). Does there exist a forcing notion $\mathbb{P}$ such that, in $V^{\mathbb{P}}$, $\kappa$ remains strongly compact and $\binom{2^{\kappa}}{\kappa}\to\binom{2^{\kappa}}{\kappa}^{1,1}_{2}$ holds?

paper_title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions
context_brief: Admissible walks with bounded even step sizes
original_question: For a fixed positive integer m, let F_m be the set of all nonzero even integers j with |j| <= m. A walk x from -n to n is a finite sequence of nonzero even steps x(t) whose total sum is 2n; writing the intermediate vertices as j(0) = -n and j(t) = -n + sum_{i=1}^t x(i), the walk is admissible when j(t) is never equal to ±n for 1 <= t <= ν, where ν + 1 is the number of steps. Let X_n^+(F_m) be the set of admissible walks from -n to n that use only positive steps from F_m, and for each such walk define h(x) = (∏_{t=1}^ν [n^2 - j(t)^2]^{-1})(∏_{t=1}^{ν+1} V(x(t))). For z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) ∈ C^m, define P_{m,n}(z) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x). Determine these polynomials P_{m,n}(z), and/or determine their asymptotic behavior for fixed m as n → ∞.
self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer m and a positive integer n. Let F_m = { j ∈ 2ℤ \ {0} : |j| ≤ m } be the set of nonzero even integers of absolute value at most m.

A walk from −n to n is a finite sequence x = (x(1), x(2), …, x(ν+1)) of nonzero even integers (the "steps") whose sum equals 2n. Define the vertices of the walk by
  j(0) = −n,  j(t) = −n + Σ_{i=1}^{t} x(i)  for 1 ≤ t ≤ ν+1,
so that j(ν+1) = n. The walk is called admissible if j(t) ≠ ±n for every 1 ≤ t ≤ ν.

Let X_n^+(F_m) denote the set of admissible walks from −n to n in which every step x(t) lies in F_m and is positive (so x(t) ∈ {2, 4, …, m} when m is even, or x(t) ∈ {2, 4, …, m−1} when m is odd).

To each formal symbol V(2k) (k = 1, …, m/2 rounded down) associate a complex variable, and write z = (V(2), V(4), …, V(2⌊m/2⌋)) ∈ ℂ^{⌊m/2⌋}. For each walk x ∈ X_n^+(F_m) define the weight
  h(x) = ( Π_{t=1}^{ν} [n² − j(t)²]^{-1} ) · ( Π_{t=1}^{ν+1} V(x(t)) ).

Define the polynomial
  P_{m,n}(z) = Σ_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x).

Problem: Determine an explicit closed form for the polynomials P_{m,n}(z), and/or determine their asymptotic behavior as n → ∞ with m fixed.
category_tag: Admissible walks and Hill operator identities
status_search_result: A combinatorial identity of Djakov–Mityagin associated with the simplest two-term case (essentially m = 4) has been given a direct combinatorial proof (Zagier, and subsequent work). However, no published source found explicitly resolves the general problem of finding closed forms or asymptotics of P_{m,n}(z) for arbitrary m, so the general question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions
original_question: Let W = { z : C(z) = ∞ } be the exceptional set associated with the comparison inequality ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| <= C(z) * |∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)| from the preceding question. Determine the structure of this exceptional set W inside C^m.
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $m \geq 1$ and $n \geq 1$. For a vector $z = (V_1, \dots, V_m) \in \mathbb{C}^m$ regarded as parameters of a trigonometric polynomial potential, let $F_m$ denote the associated combinatorial datum and let $X_n^+(F_m)$ denote the finite set of admissible configurations of size $n$ arising from the eigenfunction-decomposition combinatorics of the corresponding Hill operator (so that each $x \in X_n^+(F_m)$ contributes a complex weight $h(x) = h(x; z)$ depending polynomially on the coordinates of $z$).

For $z \in \mathbb{C}^m$, define
$$C(z) := \sup_{n \geq 1} \sup_{h} \frac{\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)|}{\bigl|\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)\bigr|},$$
where the inner supremum is taken over the admissible weight functions $h$ from the spectral problem (with the convention that the ratio is $0$ when both numerator and denominator vanish, and $\infty$ when only the denominator vanishes). Define the exceptional set
$$W := \{ z \in \mathbb{C}^m : C(z) = \infty \}.$$

Determine the structure of $W$ as a subset of $\mathbb{C}^m$: in particular, decide whether $W$ has Lebesgue measure zero (so the comparison inequality $\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| \leq C(z) \bigl|\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)\bigr|$ holds for almost every $z \in \mathbb{C}^m$), and describe $W$ geometrically (e.g., as a countable union of analytic subvarieties, or otherwise).
status_search_result: A web search returned the original problem source and related works by Djakov–Mityagin on convergence/divergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials, plus a follow-up paper "On a Combinatorial Identity of Djakov and Mityagin." None of the visible results explicitly resolves the structural description of the exceptional set $W = \{z : C(z) = \infty\}$ in $\mathbb{C}^m$. Status could not be conclusively verified.

paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
original_question: For the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB, which gradings by small finite abelian groups preserve the algebraic or coalgebraic structure? More concretely, for groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z2 × Z2, classify the group actions or coactions that turn these paraparticle algebras into graded module algebras or graded module coalgebras.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathbb{C}$ be the ground field. The relative parabose-fermi algebra $P_{BF}$ and the relative parafermi-bose algebra $P_{FB}$ are the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebras defined as follows.

Fix positive integers $m,n$ and generators $\{b_i^+, b_i^- : i=1,\dots,m\}$ ("para-bose") and $\{f_j^+, f_j^- : j=1,\dots,n\}$ ("para-fermi"). For $\xi,\eta,\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}$ write $[x,y]=xy-yx$ and $\{x,y\}=xy+yx$.

The algebra $P_{BF}$ is generated by these symbols subject to the (Greenberg–Messiah) trilinear relations
\[
[\{b_i^\xi,b_j^\eta\},b_k^\varepsilon]=2\delta_{jk}(\varepsilon-\eta)\,b_i^\xi\delta_{\xi\varepsilon}\cdots
\]
(the standard parabose triple relations among the $b$'s), the standard parafermi triple relations
\[
[[f_i^\xi,f_j^\eta],f_k^\varepsilon]=2\delta_{jk}\delta_{\eta,-\varepsilon}\eta\,f_i^\xi-2\delta_{ik}\delta_{\xi,-\varepsilon}\xi\,f_j^\eta
\]
among the $f$'s, together with the mixed "relative" commutation relations
\[
[b_i^\xi,f_j^\eta]=0\qquad\text{for all }i,j,\xi,\eta,
\]
i.e. paraboson and parafermion sectors mutually commute. The algebra $P_{FB}$ is defined identically except that the mixed sector relations are replaced by the anticommuting relations
\[
\{b_i^\xi,f_j^\eta\}-\text{appropriate trilinear corrections}=0,
\]
so that the two sectors anticommute (the "relative" parafermi-bose case). Both algebras carry natural Hopf-algebra-like (super)bialgebra structures: a coproduct, counit and antipode making them braided graded module bialgebras in suitable braided categories.

Problem.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and write $\mathbb{C}G$ for its group algebra and $(\mathbb{C}G)^*$ for its dual Hopf algebra. A $G$-grading of an associative algebra $A$ that respects its (co)algebra structure means a $\mathbb{C}G$-module algebra structure (equivalently a $G$-action by algebra automorphisms) on $A$, or dually a $\mathbb{C}G$-comodule coalgebra structure (a $G$-grading of the underlying coalgebra) such that the coproduct, counit and antipode become $G$-graded maps.

Classify, up to equivalence, all $G$-actions and all $G$-coactions on $P_{BF}$ and on $P_{FB}$ that turn these algebras into $\mathbb{C}G$-module algebras and $\mathbb{C}G$-comodule coalgebras, respectively, for each of the small finite abelian groups
\[
G\in\{\mathbb{Z}_2,\;\mathbb{Z}_3,\;\mathbb{Z}_4,\;\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2\}.
\]
Equivalently, classify all gradings $P_{BF}=\bigoplus_{g\in G}(P_{BF})_g$ and $P_{FB}=\bigoplus_{g\in G}(P_{FB})_g$ that are compatible simultaneously with the algebra and coalgebra structures of these paraparticle (co)algebras.

The problem is stated as a research objective and subsequent literature on these specific algebras does not appear to provide a full classification, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
original_question: Can one apply or develop bosonization, or bosonization-like constructions, that convert the graded and braided paraparticle Hopf structures into ordinary Hopf structures with trivial braiding while preserving equivalent representation theory?
self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $G$ be an abelian group equipped with a bicharacter $\beta: G\times G \to k^\times$ (over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$), and let $\mathcal{H}_\beta$ denote the braided monoidal category of $G$-graded vector spaces with the symmetric/quasi-symmetric braiding $\tau_\beta(x\otimes y)=\beta(|x|,|y|)\,y\otimes x$ on homogeneous elements. A paraparticle Hopf algebra is a Hopf algebra object $H$ in $\mathcal{H}_\beta$: that is, a $G$-graded associative unital algebra equipped with a coproduct $\Delta:H\to H\underline{\otimes}H$, counit, and antipode that are morphisms in $\mathcal{H}_\beta$, where the tensor product $\underline{\otimes}$ uses the braiding $\tau_\beta$. Standard examples include the parabosonic algebra $P_B$, the parafermionic algebra $P_F$, and the relative parabose/parafermi set $P_{BF}$, each carrying such a graded braided Hopf structure.
        
Recall Majid–Radford bosonization: given a braided Hopf algebra $B$ in the category of (Yetter–Drinfeld or comodule) modules over a quasitriangular Hopf algebra $K$, one forms the smash biproduct $B \rtimes K$, an ordinary (ungraded, unbraided) Hopf algebra whose category of (suitable) modules is monoidally equivalent to that of $B$ in the braided category.

Problem. Develop or apply a bosonization (or bosonization-like) construction that, for each paraparticle Hopf algebra $H$ in $\mathcal{H}_\beta$ (in particular for $H = P_B$, $P_F$, and $P_{BF}$), produces an ordinary Hopf algebra $\widehat{H}$ over $k$ (no grading, trivial braiding) such that the representation theory of $H$ as a braided Hopf algebra in $\mathcal{H}_\beta$ is equivalent—as a monoidal category of representations—to the representation theory of $\widehat{H}$ as an ordinary Hopf algebra. Specifically, exhibit such a $\widehat{H}$ explicitly for the parabosonic, parafermionic, and relative parabose–parafermi algebras, and prove the equivalence of their (module or comodule) representation categories.
status_search_result: General Majid–Radford bosonization theory converts braided Hopf algebras (in suitable categories, including super-Hopf algebras and graded/braided ones over abelian group bicharacters) into ordinary Hopf algebras with equivalent representation theory. However, no source located explicitly carries out and verifies this program for the specific paraparticle Hopf algebras (parabosonic, parafermionic, relative parabose–parafermi set) with a published proof of representation-theoretic equivalence; the status of this concrete objective therefore appears unresolved in the literature surveyed.

paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
original_question: When one decomposes the graded tensor-product representations built for PB and PF, do irreducible components appear beyond the known p-Fock-like modules? In other words, can these decompositions produce direct summands or more general submodules that are not equivalent to the standard p-Fock-like representations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P_B$ denote the parabosonic algebra and $P_F$ the parafermionic algebra (the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebras generated, respectively, by parabosonic creation/annihilation generators $b_i^\pm$ and parafermionic creation/annihilation generators $f_i^\pm$ subject to the Green trilinear relations). Each of $P_B$ and $P_F$ carries a natural $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading (with the $+$ and $-$ generators of opposite parity), and for each positive integer $p$ each algebra has a distinguished family of infinite-dimensional irreducible representations, the so-called $p$-Fock-like modules $F_p(P_B)$ and $F_p(P_F)$, on which the $\pm$ generators act as ladder operators on a Fock-type space with vacuum vector annihilated by the $-$ generators and labeled by the order of paraquantization $p$.

Using the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded (super) tensor product structure, form the graded tensor product representations $F_{p_1}(P_B) \otimes F_{p_2}(P_B)$ on $P_B$ (where the action is defined via the graded coproduct $\Delta(x) = x \otimes 1 + (-1)^{|\cdot|} 1 \otimes x$ on homogeneous generators), and similarly $F_{p_1}(P_F) \otimes F_{p_2}(P_F)$ on $P_F$. It is known that each $p$-Fock-like module $F_p(P_B)$ (respectively $F_p(P_F)$) appears as an irreducible factor in the decomposition of these graded tensor products.

Question: In the decomposition of the graded tensor product representations $F_{p_1}(P_B) \otimes F_{p_2}(P_B)$ and $F_{p_1}(P_F) \otimes F_{p_2}(P_F)$, do there occur irreducible direct summands, or more generally submodules, that are not isomorphic to any of the standard $p$-Fock-like representations? Equivalently, is the family of $p$-Fock-like modules closed under taking irreducible constituents of graded tensor products, or do genuinely new irreducible representations of $P_B$ and $P_F$ arise this way?
status_search_result: Searches turned up the original problem listing and related work on Fock-like representations of parabosonic, parafermionic, and Relative Parabose Set algebras, but no published resolution showing whether non-Fock-like irreducible summands or submodules occur in the graded tensor-product decompositions for $P_B$ and $P_F$. The status appears to remain undetermined in the available literature.

paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
original_question: Do the proposed paraparticle Hamiltonians built from a monochromatic parabosonic field and a (p + 1)-level system yield exactly solvable generalizations of the Jaynes-Cummings model? If so, can one compute their energy levels, eigenfunctions, and transition rates and compare those predictions directly with theoretical and experimental results?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-mode parabosonic field of order $p$, generated by creation/annihilation operators $b^+, b^-$ satisfying the trilinear Green relations
$$[\{b^-,b^+\},b^\pm]=\pm 2 b^\pm,\qquad [\{b^\pm,b^\pm\},b^\pm]=0,$$
acting on the parabosonic Fock-like module $F(p)$ uniquely determined by a vacuum vector $|0\rangle$ with $b^-|0\rangle=0$ and $b^- b^+|0\rangle=p|0\rangle$ (so that for $p=1$ one recovers the ordinary bosonic Fock space). Couple this field to a $(p+1)$-level atomic system whose internal degrees of freedom are described by a finite-dimensional Fock-like module of an associated parafermionic algebra of order $p$, with raising/lowering operators $f^+, f^-$ obeying the analogous parafermionic trilinear relations.

Construct a family of paraparticle Hamiltonians of Jaynes–Cummings type, of the schematic form
$$H = \tfrac{\omega}{2}\{b^+,b^-\} + \tfrac{\Omega}{2}\{f^+,f^-\} + g\bigl(b^+ f^- + f^+ b^-\bigr),$$
on the tensor product module $F(p)\otimes V(p)$, together with reasonable variants involving the natural quadratic Casimir terms of the underlying paraparticle algebras.

Questions:
(a) Is every such Hamiltonian exactly solvable, in the sense that the full Hilbert space decomposes into finite-dimensional invariant subspaces on which $H$ can be diagonalized in closed form?
(b) For each such model, determine the energy spectrum and eigenfunctions explicitly as functions of $p$, $\omega$, $\Omega$, $g$, and compute the transition rates (Rabi-type oscillations, atomic inversion, photon statistics) between Fock-like basis states.
(c) Compare the resulting predictions with the standard ($p=1$) Jaynes–Cummings model and with available experimental data on cavity QED and trapped-ion systems.
status_search_result: The simplest case—a two-level atom in a single-mode para-Bose cavity field—has been treated as an exactly solvable deformed Jaynes–Cummings model, with explicit energy spectrum, eigenstates and Rabi-type dynamics computed (e.g., Dehghani et al., Sci. Rep. 2021; parity-deformed JCM, Sci. Rep. 2016). However, the full proposed program for arbitrary order $p$ with a $(p+1)$-level (parafermionic) system, including direct comparison with experiment, does not appear to have been carried out completely; thus the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Prove or refute the conjectured upper bound SW(1324) < e*pi*sqrt(2/3) for the Stanley-Wilf limit of the classical pattern 1324.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, viewed as the set of permutations written in one-line notation. A permutation $\pi\in S_n$ is said to contain the pattern $1324$ if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<i_3<i_4\le n$ such that
$$\pi(i_1)<\pi(i_3)<\pi(i_2)<\pi(i_4).$$
Otherwise $\pi$ is said to avoid $1324$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_n(1324)$ denote the set of permutations in $S_n$ that avoid the pattern $1324$, and let $a_n=|\mathrm{Av}_n(1324)|$.

By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, the limit
$$\mathrm{SW}(1324)\;=\;\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n^{1/n}$$
exists and is finite. Prove or disprove the inequality
$$\mathrm{SW}(1324)\;<\;e^{\pi\sqrt{2/3}}\;\approx\;13.001954.$$
status_search_result: The exact value of the Stanley–Wilf limit of 1324 remains unknown. The best rigorous upper bound currently in the literature is approximately 13.5 (Bevan, Brignall, Elvey Price, Pantone, 2020), while the best lower bound is around 10.271. Since the conjectured bound $e^{\pi\sqrt{2/3}}\approx 13.0019$ lies strictly between these, the conjecture has neither been proved nor refuted.

original_question: For each pattern length k, determine whether the largest Stanley-Wilf limit among all classical patterns of length k is always attained by a layered pattern.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation $\pi \in S_n$ is said to *contain* a pattern $\tau \in S_k$ if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ such that the subsequence $\pi(i_1), \pi(i_2), \ldots, \pi(i_k)$ is order-isomorphic to $\tau(1), \tau(2), \ldots, \tau(k)$; otherwise $\pi$ *avoids* $\tau$. Let $S_n(\tau)$ denote the number of permutations of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ that avoid $\tau$. The Marcus–Tardos theorem (resolving the Stanley–Wilf conjecture) implies that the limit
$$L(\tau) := \lim_{n\to\infty} S_n(\tau)^{1/n}$$
exists and is finite for every pattern $\tau$.

A permutation $\tau \in S_k$ is called *layered* if it is a concatenation of contiguous blocks (layers) such that within each block the entries are decreasing, and the blocks themselves are arranged so that all entries of an earlier block are smaller than all entries of any later block. Equivalently, $\tau$ is layered if it can be written as a direct sum of decreasing permutations.

Question: Is it true that for every integer $k \ge 1$,
$$\max_{\tau \in S_k} L(\tau)$$
is attained by some layered permutation $\tau \in S_k$?
status_search_result: The conjecture that, among all classical patterns of a given length, the maximum Stanley–Wilf limit is attained by a layered pattern remains open. It is supported by computational enumeration for small lengths and is discussed as a still-believed open conjecture in the recent literature on Stanley–Wilf limits and pattern 1324; partial results give upper bounds (e.g., $L(\tau) \le 4\ell^2$ for layered $\tau$ of length $\ell$), but no general proof or disproof is known.

original_question: For every even integer k, prove or refute that the layered pattern of length k with layers (1, 2, 2, ..., 2, 2, 1) is the most avoided pattern among all patterns of length k.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Given a permutation $\sigma \in S_n$ and a permutation (pattern) $\tau \in S_k$ with $k\le n$, an occurrence of $\tau$ in $\sigma$ is a $k$-tuple of indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ such that the values $\sigma(i_1),\sigma(i_2),\dots,\sigma(i_k)$ appear in the same relative order as $\tau(1),\tau(2),\dots,\tau(k)$. Let $c(\tau,\sigma)$ denote the number of occurrences of $\tau$ in $\sigma$, and define
$$\delta(\tau,\sigma)=\frac{c(\tau,\sigma)}{\binom{n}{k}}.$$
The packing density of $\tau$ is
$$\mathrm{pd}(\tau)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{\sigma\in S_n}\delta(\tau,\sigma).$$

A layered permutation with layer sequence $(\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_r)$ (positive integers with $\ell_1+\cdots+\ell_r=k$) is the permutation in $S_k$ obtained by concatenating $r$ consecutive blocks, where the $i$-th block consists of $\ell_i$ entries arranged in decreasing order, and the blocks are placed so that all entries of block $i$ are smaller than all entries of block $i+1$. Equivalently it is a permutation that avoids both $231$ and $312$.

Call a pattern $\tau\in S_k$ "most avoided of length $k$" if $\mathrm{pd}(\tau)$ attains the minimum value of $\mathrm{pd}$ over all $\tau'\in S_k$.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every even integer $k\ge 2$, the layered pattern of length $k$ with layer sequence $(1,\underbrace{2,2,\dots,2}_{(k-2)/2\ \text{twos}},1)$ is a most avoided pattern of length $k$, i.e. it minimizes $\mathrm{pd}(\tau)$ over $\tau\in S_k$.
status_search_result: No source located that proves or refutes the conjecture that, for even $k$, the layered pattern with layer sequence $(1,2,2,\dots,2,1)$ minimizes packing density among length-$k$ patterns. Recent works on packing densities and density maximizers of layered permutations do not report a resolution, so the conjecture appears to remain open.

original_question: Determine whether there exist two permutation patterns whose avoidance counts switch relative order more than once, and in particular whether two patterns can switch places infinitely often as n grows.
self_contained_problem:
For permutations, given a pattern $\sigma$ (a permutation of $\{1,2,\dots,k\}$), say that a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ avoids $\sigma$ if there is no subsequence $\pi(i_1),\pi(i_2),\dots,\pi(i_k)$ with $i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k$ whose entries are in the same relative order as $\sigma(1),\sigma(2),\dots,\sigma(k)$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)$ denote the number of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ that avoid $\sigma$.

For a pair of patterns $\sigma,\tau$, say that a "switch" occurs at $n$ if the strict inequality between $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)$ and $\mathrm{Av}_\tau(n)$ at $n$ is the opposite of the strict inequality at $n-1$ (with both inequalities strict).

Determine whether the following holds:

(a) (Strong form.) For every pair of patterns $\sigma,\tau$, at most one switch occurs as $n$ ranges over the positive integers.

(b) (Weak form.) For every pair of patterns $\sigma,\tau$, there exists $N$ such that either $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)<\mathrm{Av}_\tau(n)$ for all $n>N$ or $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)>\mathrm{Av}_\tau(n)$ for all $n>N$ (equivalently, only finitely many switches occur).

In particular, can two patterns switch places infinitely often as $n\to\infty$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any resolution of the Stankova–West conjectures on whether avoidance counts of two patterns can switch order more than once or infinitely often. Surveys and follow-up literature on pattern avoidance still refer to this as a conjecture, with no announced proof or counterexample found.

original_question: Characterize completely the intervals [σ, τ] in the permutation pattern poset whose Möbius function satisfies μ(σ, τ) = 0.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the permutation pattern poset P, whose elements are all finite permutations (one for each length n ≥ 1, viewed as sequences σ = σ(1)σ(2)…σ(n) of distinct positive integers, considered up to order-isomorphism so that we may take σ to be a permutation of {1,2,…,n}). The order is pattern containment: for σ of length k and τ of length n, write σ ≤ τ if there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < … < i_k ≤ n such that the subsequence τ(i_1)τ(i_2)…τ(i_k) is order-isomorphic to σ (i.e., τ(i_a) < τ(i_b) iff σ(a) < σ(b)). For σ ≤ τ the closed interval is [σ,τ] = {π : σ ≤ π ≤ τ}, and the Möbius function μ on P is defined recursively by μ(σ,σ) = 1 and, for σ < τ,
   μ(σ,τ) = − ∑_{σ ≤ π < τ} μ(σ,π).

Problem. Give a complete characterization of all intervals [σ,τ] in this poset for which μ(σ,τ) = 0. That is, determine necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions on the pair (σ,τ) for the Möbius function of the interval [σ,τ] to vanish.
category_tag: Möbius function of permutation pattern poset
status_search_result: The problem of completely characterizing intervals [σ,τ] in the permutation pattern poset with μ(σ,τ) = 0 remains open. Substantial partial progress exists: many sufficient conditions for vanishing have been identified (e.g., presence of consecutive monotone triples; two non-order-isomorphic length-2 intervals; mixed ascent/descent intervals), and a two-term formula whose second term often vanishes has been developed. Asymptotic lower bounds (e.g., proportion ≥ (1−1/e)² for principal intervals) have been proven, but no complete characterization has appeared.
