original_question: Construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual-knot diagrams over the integers, understand the existing constructions that work for large classes of virtual links, and determine structural consequences such as which knots are K-full or Kho-full, whether optimal diagrams are minimal in classical crossing number, and which diagram moves preserve that optimality.
self_contained_problem:
A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated either as classical crossings (with over/under information) or as virtual crossings (drawn with a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves (the classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3 together with the virtual moves V1, V2, V3 and the mixed move M). Khovanov homology, originally defined for classical link diagrams over the ring of integers Z by taking the cube of resolutions of the crossings and applying a (1+1)-dimensional TQFT-like Frobenius structure with appropriately chosen edge signs, gives a bigraded link invariant whose graded Euler characteristic is the Jones polynomial.

Several partial extensions of Khovanov homology to virtual links exist: a Z/2-coefficient theory valid for all virtual diagrams, and Z-coefficient theories defined only for certain classes (e.g. "atomic", orientable, or alternating virtual diagrams) where a coherent sign assignment on the cube of resolutions can be made.

Call a virtual knot K-full (respectively Kho-full) if it admits a diagram on which the Kauffman-bracket-style cube (respectively the Khovanov complex) can be defined over Z in the standard way. Call a virtual diagram optimal if it realizes the minimum number of classical crossings among all diagrams of its virtual knot type.

Solve the following:

(a) Construct a Khovanov chain complex, defined over Z and invariant under the generalized Reidemeister moves, for an arbitrary virtual link diagram, reducing to the classical Khovanov complex on classical diagrams.

(b) Classify all virtual knots that are K-full and all virtual knots that are Kho-full.

(c) Determine whether every optimal virtual diagram of a virtual knot is minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings, and identify which diagrammatic moves preserve optimality.
status_search_result: Manturov constructed a Khovanov-type complex for virtual knots over arbitrary coefficient rings, and Dye–Kaestner–Kauffman reformulated this to extend Lee homology and a Rasmussen invariant to virtual knots; further work treats alternating virtual links. Thus part (a) has substantial progress, with constructions valid for broad classes of virtual diagrams, but a fully canonical, universally accepted Z-Khovanov theory for all virtual diagrams together with the structural classifications (K-full/Kho-full knots, optimality of diagrams) appears not to be completely settled.

original_question: Define a notion of alternating virtual knot, classify alternating virtual knots and alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization, and formulate and prove the virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture.
self_contained_problem:
A virtual link diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated either as classical crossings (with over/under information) or as virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves. Equivalently, virtual links may be represented as links in thickened orientable surfaces Σ × [0,1], up to ambient isotopy and stabilization/destabilization of Σ. A diagram on a surface is called alternating if, traveling along each component, classical over- and under-crossings alternate; it is called reduced if it contains no nugatory classical crossing. A flype is a local move on a diagram that rotates a tangle by 180° while moving a single crossing from one side of the tangle to the other.

Carry out the following:

(a) Give a precise definition of an alternating virtual knot (equivalently, an alternating link in a thickened surface considered without stabilization).

(b) Classify alternating virtual knots, and classify all alternating weaves (alternating link diagrams) on closed orientable surfaces, in both cases without allowing stabilization of the surface.

(c) Formulate a virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture: namely, identify the set of local moves (the natural candidate being flypes) such that any two reduced alternating diagrams of the same alternating virtual link, on possibly different surfaces (without stabilization), are related by a finite sequence of these moves. Prove this analogue.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Boden–Karimi and Karimi's PhD thesis develop the theory of alternating virtual knots and prove a Kauffman–Murasugi–Thistlethwaite-type theorem for alternating links in thickened surfaces (minimal crossings, common writhe). A virtual flyping theorem has been announced and posted (arXiv:2210.03720), adapting Menasco–Thistlethwaite's geometric proof to the virtual / thickened-surface setting for alternating virtual links. However, version history of that preprint indicates substantive revisions, and a complete classification of all alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization is not fully resolved, so the program is partially solved rather than completely settled.

original_question: For a virtual link with minimal classical crossing number C, minimal virtual crossing number V, and minimal total crossing number T, determine how C, V, and T are related, whether T = V + L in the notation of the paper, how the virtual unknotting number behaves, how V relates to minimal genus in a surface representation, and what effective algorithms or polynomial bounds exist for computing or estimating these quantities.
self_contained_problem:
A virtual link is an equivalence class of decorated 4-valent plane diagrams whose crossings are of two kinds — classical (over/under) and virtual (a small circled transverse intersection) — taken modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves (the three classical Reidemeister moves, the four purely virtual Reidemeister moves, and the mixed "detour" move). Equivalently, a virtual link can be represented as an embedded link in a thickened orientable closed surface Σ × [0,1], taken up to ambient isotopy and stabilization/destabilization of Σ.

For a virtual link L, define three crossing-number invariants:
 • C(L) = the minimum number of classical crossings over all diagrams of L;
 • V(L) = the minimum number of virtual crossings over all diagrams of L;
 • T(L) = the minimum total number of crossings (classical plus virtual) over all diagrams of L.
Define also the virtual unknotting number u_v(L) of a virtual knot L as the minimum, over all diagrams D of L, of the number of classical crossing changes needed to convert D into a diagram of the trivial knot (where virtual moves are allowed freely between changes). Finally, let g(L) denote the minimal genus of an orientable closed surface Σ such that L admits a representative as a link in Σ × [0,1] that is non-trivial in the sense of stabilization (the virtual genus).

Investigate the following:

(a) Determine the precise relationships among C(L), V(L), and T(L). In particular, decide whether the equality
  T(L) = C(L) + V(L)
holds for every virtual link L.

(b) Establish nontrivial lower and upper bounds on u_v(L) and describe its qualitative behavior (e.g., additivity under connected sum, comparison with the classical unknotting number when L is classical, realizability of arbitrary positive integers).

(c) Determine the relationship between V(L) and g(L); in particular, find sharp inequalities relating these two invariants.

(d) Exhibit effective algorithms or polynomial-time computable bounds (in the size of a given diagram) for estimating C(L), V(L), T(L), and u_v(L).
status_search_result: A web search returned foundational and recent works on virtual knot theory (Kauffman; Manturov; results on virtual crossing number estimates and on unknotting operations for virtual/welded knots), but none establishes the equality T = C + V in general, gives a complete description of the virtual unknotting number, or provides a sharp relation between V and the virtual genus. Partial bounds (e.g., polynomial-invariant lower bounds on V) and special cases exist, so the package of questions is best classified as open with partial progress.

original_question: Understand how virtual-knot polynomials relate to Vassiliev invariants for virtual knots, and determine whether every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots extends to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots in the sense described by the paper, while also clarifying the alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots mentioned there.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle). Virtual knots are equivalence classes of virtual knot diagrams modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves: the three classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3, the three purely virtual moves V1, V2, V3, and the mixed move M (a classical strand passing across a virtual crossing). A long virtual knot is the analogous equivalence class of virtual diagrams of a 1–1 tangle (with two fixed endpoints at infinity).

(b) Following Kauffman, a singular virtual knot is a virtual diagram that, in addition to classical and virtual crossings, has finitely many rigid 4-valent transverse double points ("singular crossings"). Any invariant v of virtual knots taking values in an abelian group is extended to singular virtual knots by the Vassiliev skein relation
   v(D_×) = v(D_+) − v(D_−),
where D_+, D_− are the two classical resolutions of a singular crossing. The invariant v is called a Vassiliev (finite-type) invariant of degree ≤ n (in Kauffman's sense) if its extension vanishes on every singular virtual knot with more than n singular crossings. The same definition is made for long virtual knots.

(c) There is also an alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots in which the role of singular crossings is played by an additional "semi-virtual" resolution, defined by the relation
   v(D_×) = v(D_+) − v(D_v),
where D_v denotes the diagram obtained by replacing the classical crossing by a virtual crossing.

Problems.

1. Establish the precise relationship between the standard polynomial invariants of virtual knots (such as the Jones polynomial, the bracket polynomial, and their virtual generalizations) and the Vassiliev finite-type invariants of virtual knots in Kauffman's sense (b): determine, for each such polynomial, the filtration by finite-type degree of its coefficients (after a suitable substitution like x = e^h).

2. Decide whether every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots (of degree ≤ n) extends to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots of the same degree, in Kauffman's sense.

3. Compare the Kauffman finite-type theory (b) with the alternate finite-type theory (c) for virtual knots, and determine the precise relationship between the resulting filtered algebras of invariants.
status_search_result: There has been substantial progress on connections between virtual knot polynomials and Vassiliev-type invariants in Kauffman's sense, and on the alternate "GPV" finite-type theory due to Goussarov–Polyak–Viro, including weight-system results from the Jones polynomial. However, the literature continues to treat the full classification problem and the question of whether every classical finite-type invariant extends to a long virtual finite-type invariant of the same degree as not fully resolved, and recent work (e.g., on V₁/V₂ polynomials of long virtual knots and on knotoid finite-type invariants from 2020–2025) builds on rather than closes these questions. The status is therefore best described as partially solved / still under active investigation.

original_question: For the virtual braid group V B_n, determine whether it is linear for all n greater than 3, whether the representation rho: V B_n -> Aut(F_{n+1}) described in the paper is faithful for all n greater than 2, and whether there exist non-equivalent virtual links whose braid closures become equivalent after applying the welded-braid representation rho_A.
self_contained_problem:
Let $VB_n$ denote the virtual braid group on $n$ strands, defined as the group with generators $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ (classical braid generators) and $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ (virtual generators) subject to:
- (Braid relations) $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$ for $1\le i\le n-2$, and $\sigma_i\sigma_j = \sigma_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge 2$;
- (Symmetric group relations) $\tau_i^2 = 1$, $\tau_i\tau_{i+1}\tau_i = \tau_{i+1}\tau_i\tau_{i+1}$, and $\tau_i\tau_j = \tau_j\tau_i$ for $|i-j|\ge 2$;
- (Mixed relations) $\sigma_i\tau_j = \tau_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge 2$, and $\tau_i\tau_{i+1}\sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1}\tau_i\tau_{i+1}$.

Let $F_{n+1}=\langle x_1,\dots,x_n,y\rangle$ be the free group of rank $n+1$. Define a homomorphism $\rho: VB_n\to \mathrm{Aut}(F_{n+1})$ by
$$\rho(\sigma_i):\ x_i\mapsto x_ix_{i+1}x_i^{-1},\ x_{i+1}\mapsto x_i,\ x_k\mapsto x_k\ (k\ne i,i+1),\ y\mapsto y,$$
$$\rho(\tau_i):\ x_i\mapsto y\,x_{i+1}\,y^{-1},\ x_{i+1}\mapsto y^{-1}x_i y,\ x_k\mapsto x_k\ (k\ne i,i+1),\ y\mapsto y.$$

Let $\rho_A: WB_n\to \mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ denote the standard faithful Artin-type representation of the welded braid group $WB_n$ (the quotient of $VB_n$ by the "forbidden" relation $\tau_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\tau_{i+1}$), sending $\sigma_i$ to the usual Artin automorphism and $\tau_i$ to the transposition $x_i\leftrightarrow x_{i+1}$ of $F_n=\langle x_1,\dots,x_n\rangle$. For a virtual braid $\beta\in VB_n$, let $\hat\beta$ denote its braid closure as a virtual link, and let $\hat\beta_w$ denote its closure regarded as a welded link.

Resolve the following three questions:
(a) Is $VB_n$ a linear group (i.e., admits a faithful finite-dimensional linear representation over a field) for every $n>3$?
(b) Is the representation $\rho:VB_n\to \mathrm{Aut}(F_{n+1})$ defined above faithful for every $n>2$?
(c) Do there exist virtual braids $\beta,\beta'\in VB_n$ (for some $n$) whose closures $\hat\beta$ and $\hat\beta'$ are inequivalent as virtual links, while $\hat\beta_w$ and $\hat\beta'_w$ are equivalent as welded links?
status_search_result: Recent literature (2021–2025) continues to investigate linearity of $VB_n$ and faithfulness of representations into $\mathrm{Aut}$ of free groups. While $VB_3$ is known to be linear and faithful linear representations of certain crystallographic quotients have been built, linearity of $VB_n$ for $n>3$ is still treated as an open problem. The Bardakov-style representation $\rho$ into $\mathrm{Aut}(F_{n+1})$ is known to be non-faithful in some forms for $n\ge 4$, but the specific faithfulness question and the welded-vs-virtual closure distinction remain unresolved in general.

original_question: Extend the theory of virtual covers so that it applies effectively to classical knots in S^3, relate virtual-cover invariants to Milnor mu-invariants and possibly to one-component links, understand how virtual covers behave under local moves such as crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves, determine whether virtual covers can detect mutations, and characterize exactly which moves on two-component links preserve the associated virtual-knot type.
self_contained_problem:
Background. A two-component link L = J ∪ K in S^3 with J an unknot determines, via the standard "virtual cover" construction, a virtual knot v(L): one removes a tubular neighborhood of J, identifies its complement with a thickened surface Σ × I (where Σ is a genus-one surface arising from the unknotted component), and represents K inside Σ × I; the resulting virtual knot type v(L) ∈ V is the virtual cover of L associated to J. More generally, given a classical link in S^3 and an unknotted sublink U whose complement is homeomorphic to Σ × I for some surface Σ, the virtual cover construction associates a virtual knot (or virtual link) to the remaining components.

Address the following collection of questions about the theory of virtual covers.

(1) Extend the construction so that it produces effective invariants for one-component classical links, i.e. classical knots in S^3, rather than requiring a multi-component setting.

(2) For an n-component classical link L (n ≥ 2) with vanishing Milnor μ̄-invariants of length ≤ k, establish a precise relationship between the higher Milnor μ̄-invariants of L and invariants of the virtual knot v(L) obtained as a virtual cover. In particular, exhibit virtual-knot invariants whose values recover or are determined by specified Milnor μ̄-invariants of L.

(3) Determine the behavior of v(L) under local moves on the classical link L, including: (a) crossing changes between two components; (b) self-Δ moves (Δ-moves involving three strands of the same component); and (c) Z-moves. For each move, identify which classical moves on L correspond to which moves on v(L) in the virtual category, and which leave the virtual isotopy type of v(L) unchanged.

(4) Decide whether the virtual cover v(L) detects mutation, i.e. whether there exist mutant classical links L and L' with v(L) ≠ v(L') as virtual knots, or prove that v is invariant under all classical mutations.

(5) For two-component classical links L = J ∪ K with J an unknot, find a complete set of local moves on L (a finite list of moves such that any two such links L, L' with v(L) = v(L') as virtual knots are connected by a finite sequence of these moves) that exactly characterizes the equivalence relation L ∼ L' ⇔ v(L) = v(L').
status_search_result: Related work has appeared on Milnor-type concordance invariants for virtual knots in thickened surfaces and on welded Milnor invariants of string links, which provides partial progress related to (2). However, no source clearly resolves the full program of questions (extension to one-component links, behavior under crossing changes/self-Δ/Z-moves, mutation detection, and a complete set of moves preserving v(L) for two-component links). The status of the overall problem appears to remain open or only partially addressed.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN GRAVITATIONAL PHYSICS
context_brief: Equivalence Principle as discriminator of gravity formulations
original_question: Can increasingly precise tests of the Equivalence Principle determine whether gravity should be formulated in a purely metric way or in a Palatini-type way with metric g and connection Γ treated as independent variables? More specifically, can Equivalence Principle measurements decide whether Γ is only the Levi-Civita connection of g or whether it may be a more general connection that is, in principle, disentangled from the metric?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a spacetime described by a 4-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with a Lorentzian metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and an affine connection $\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$. Two standard formulations of a gravitational theory are:

(i) the purely metric formulation, in which $\Gamma$ is postulated a priori to be the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, i.e. the unique torsion-free connection satisfying $\nabla_\lambda g_{\mu\nu}=0$, so that the metric is the only independent dynamical field; and

(ii) the Palatini (metric-affine) formulation, in which $g_{\mu\nu}$ and $\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ are treated as independent dynamical variables, with the relation between $\Gamma$ and $g$ (if any) determined by the field equations rather than imposed a priori.

The Equivalence Principle (EP), in its various formulations (weak, Einstein, strong), constrains the universality of free fall and the local validity of special-relativistic physics for test bodies. EP tests measure, for example, the Eötvös parameter $\eta=2|a_1-a_2|/|a_1+a_2|$ comparing the accelerations of bodies of differing composition in an external gravitational field.

Question: Can experimental tests of the Equivalence Principle, of arbitrarily increasing precision, in principle distinguish between the metric and Palatini formulations of gravity? More precisely, does there exist a class of EP-type observables whose outcomes determine whether the connection $\Gamma$ governing the motion of test bodies is necessarily the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, or whether $\Gamma$ may instead be a more general independent connection disentangled from $g$?
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. a 2025 work on "Equivalent Gravities and the Equivalence Principle") continues to discuss how EP tests could in principle discriminate metric vs. Palatini/metric-affine formulations, and earlier results show that Palatini f(R) theories can induce EP violations. However, no consensus experimental or theoretical resolution has been reached, and current EP tests have not been shown to be sufficient on their own to discriminate the two formulations. The problem remains an active open research direction.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN GRAVITATIONAL PHYSICS
context_brief: Physical meaning of Jordan and Einstein frames
original_question: When modified gravitational dynamics are written in the Jordan frame, where Einstein field equations are modified and matter fields are minimally coupled to gravity, or in the Einstein frame, where Einstein field equations are preserved and matter fields are non-minimally coupled, does passing from one conformal frame to the other have genuine physical significance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a scalar–tensor theory of gravity formulated on a 4-dimensional spacetime manifold with Lorentzian metric g and a scalar field φ. Two equivalent mathematical descriptions of such theories are commonly used:

(1) The Jordan frame: the metric g_J satisfies modified Einstein field equations (with φ entering non-trivially as a multiplicative factor of the Ricci scalar in the gravitational action), while matter fields ψ_m are minimally coupled to g_J, so that test particles follow geodesics of g_J.

(2) The Einstein frame: after a conformal transformation g_E = Ω(φ)^2 g_J (with Ω a strictly positive smooth function of φ), together with a corresponding redefinition of the scalar field, the gravitational action takes the standard Einstein–Hilbert form, but matter fields couple non-minimally to g_E through Ω(φ).

The two descriptions are related by a conformal rescaling of the metric and field redefinitions, and are mathematically equivalent at the level of the classical action.

Question: Determine whether the passage from the Jordan frame to the Einstein frame (and back) carries genuine physical significance — that is, whether the two frames describe the same physical theory, or whether observable predictions (for example involving matter trajectories, energy conditions, singularity structure, or quantum effects such as entanglement and vacuum states) can in principle distinguish them. Provide a precise criterion under which the two frames are physically equivalent, and conditions under which they are not.
status_search_result: The question of whether Jordan and Einstein frames are physically equivalent remains actively debated. At the classical level, recent work (e.g., 2024 results in Eur. Phys. J. C) supports a canonical/Hamiltonian equivalence on a reduced phase space, and many authors argue equivalence since conformal rescalings cannot be measured absolutely. At the quantum level, however, multiple recent studies (2023–2025) show inequivalence: loop quantization, entanglement-based probes, and inflationary magnetogenesis distinguish the frames. The physical equivalence is therefore considered open, with partial classical results but unresolved quantum-level status.

paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
context_brief: laboratory access to QCD matter states
original_question: To what extent can strongly interacting QCD matter states resembling (i) high-temperature matter with negligible baryon chemical potential, as in the early universe, or (ii) low-temperature QCD matter, as may exist in neutron-star cores, be produced and studied in terrestrial laboratories through relativistic or ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions?
self_contained_problem:
Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) predicts that strongly interacting matter composed of quarks and gluons can exist in qualitatively different thermodynamic phases, parametrized by temperature T and baryon chemical potential μ_B. Two physically distinguished regimes are:

(i) the high-temperature, nearly baryon-symmetric regime (T large, μ_B ≈ 0), believed to describe the state of the universe a few microseconds after the Big Bang;

(ii) the low-temperature, high-baryon-density regime (T small, μ_B large), expected to be relevant for the interior (cores) of neutron stars.

In terrestrial experiments, transient regions of hot and/or dense strongly interacting matter can be created by colliding heavy atomic nuclei at relativistic or ultra-relativistic center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair. By varying the collision energy, the colliding species, and the collision centrality, different trajectories in the (T, μ_B) plane can in principle be probed.

Question: To what extent can the QCD matter states described in regimes (i) and (ii) above actually be produced in such heavy-ion collisions, and to what extent can their bulk and microscopic properties (e.g. equation of state, transport coefficients, degree of thermalization, phase structure including any deconfinement and chiral transitions, and signatures of collective behavior) be quantitatively reconstructed from the observable final-state hadrons, leptons, and photons? Provide a characterization of which features of regimes (i) and (ii) are accessible to laboratory study via such collisions and which are not, together with the theoretical and experimental criteria justifying that characterization.
status_search_result: The question is a long-standing programmatic open question in heavy-ion physics. While substantial progress has been made (e.g., evidence at RHIC and LHC for a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma at small μ_B, and ongoing beam-energy-scan programs at RHIC, NA61/SHINE, and future FAIR/NICA targeting the high-μ_B regime relevant to neutron-star matter), no complete answer has been reached. Reviews and white papers as recent as 2024–2025 continue to frame the access to early-universe-like and neutron-star-core-like QCD matter via heavy-ion collisions as an active, partially answered research program.

paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
context_brief: deconfinement and hydrodynamic expansion in high-multiplicity pp
original_question: In very high-energy proton-proton collisions with low impact parameter and high charged-particle multiplicity, do multiparton interactions and rescatterings transfer enough energy into a proton-sized volume to create a close-to-equilibrium deconfined initial state, allow thermalization despite the small system size, and produce a proton-sized fireball that expands hydrodynamically or collectively?
self_contained_problem:
Consider proton-proton (pp) collisions at very high center-of-mass energies (of order several TeV), restricted to events with low impact parameter and unusually high charged-particle multiplicity. Model the collision as producing, within a region of roughly proton size (radius R of order 1 fm), a system of partonic constituents whose multiparton interactions and subsequent rescatterings deposit energy into this volume. Assume that in a deconfined QCD medium the mean free path of the constituents is λ ≈ 0.2–0.3 fm, so that R/λ is of order a few.

Address the following physics question precisely: do the multiparton interactions and rescatterings in such high-multiplicity, low-impact-parameter pp events transfer enough energy density into the proton-sized volume to (i) exceed the QCD deconfinement threshold and produce a close-to-equilibrium deconfined initial state, (ii) allow approximate local thermalization despite the smallness of the system relative to typical heavy-ion fireballs, and (iii) produce a proton-sized fireball that subsequently undergoes hydrodynamic or otherwise collective expansion, observable through the same flow-type observables (e.g. long-range azimuthal correlations, radial and anisotropic flow harmonics, mass-ordering of mean transverse momenta, identified-hadron spectra) used to characterize collectivity in nucleus-nucleus collisions?

Provide a quantitative theoretical and/or experimental determination of whether each of (i), (ii), and (iii) holds for high-multiplicity pp collisions at LHC-class energies.
category_tag: QGP and collectivity in small systems
status_search_result: Experimental observations at the LHC (long-range "ridge" correlations, mass-ordered radial flow, strangeness enhancement, nonzero v_n in high-multiplicity pp) have established clear collectivity-like signatures in high-multiplicity pp events, and hydrodynamic models reproduce many features, suggesting QGP-like behavior. However, whether a true close-to-equilibrium deconfined and thermalized state is formed in pp—as opposed to initial-state (e.g. CGC/color-domain) origins of collectivity—remains under active debate as of 2024–2025 reviews. The question is therefore partially resolved on the phenomenological side but not fully settled theoretically.

paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
original_question: What experimental and theoretical mechanism explains the multiplicity-dependent collective-type trends observed in proton-proton collisions at √s = 7 TeV, including the decrease of kinetic freeze-out temperature, the increase of average transverse expansion velocity, and identified-hadron transverse-momentum spectral changes that resemble trends seen in heavy-ion collisions?
self_contained_problem:
In high-energy proton–proton collisions at center-of-mass energy √s = 7 TeV, transverse-momentum spectra of identified hadrons (π, K, p, …) measured in classes of increasing charged-particle multiplicity, when fitted with blast-wave-type (hydrodynamically inspired) parametrizations, exhibit the following trends as multiplicity grows: (i) the extracted kinetic freeze-out temperature T_kin decreases; (ii) the average transverse expansion (radial flow) velocity ⟨β_T⟩ increases; (iii) the identified-hadron p_T spectra harden in a mass-ordered way. These trends qualitatively mirror the centrality dependence observed in heavy-ion (A–A) collisions, where they are attributed to the formation of a thermalized, collectively expanding partonic medium (quark–gluon plasma).

Problem: Identify and characterize the underlying physical mechanism — experimentally testable and theoretically formulated — that produces these multiplicity-dependent collective-type signatures in pp collisions at √s = 7 TeV. Specifically:
(a) Provide a dynamical model (e.g., hydrodynamic evolution of a small thermalized droplet, color reconnection between multi-parton interactions, string/color-rope formation, parton percolation, initial-state color-glass-condensate correlations, or hadronic rescattering) that quantitatively reproduces the joint evolution of (T_kin, ⟨β_T⟩) and the identified-hadron p_T spectra as functions of charged-particle multiplicity.
(b) Determine whether the observed collectivity in high-multiplicity pp events arises from genuine final-state collective expansion of a thermalized system, from initial-state momentum correlations, or from non-collective hadronization mechanisms, and propose experimental observables that discriminate among these scenarios.
category_tag: High-energy heavy-ion and pp collision phenomenology
status_search_result: Recent literature (2019–2025) confirms that collective-type signatures in high-multiplicity pp collisions at 7 TeV — decreasing T_kin, increasing ⟨β_T⟩, mass-ordered spectral hardening, long-range ridge, strangeness enhancement — are now well established experimentally, but the underlying mechanism remains debated. Candidate explanations include hydrodynamic flow in a small QGP droplet, color reconnection among multi-parton interactions, string/color-rope and percolation models, initial-state CGC correlations, and hadronic rescattering. No single mechanism has been shown to reproduce all observables, so the problem is still open.

paper_title: Recent results and open questions on collective type phenomena from A-A to pp collisions
original_question: Can a two-dimensional event-selection condition that combines charged-particle multiplicity with global event-shape observables such as Directivity, Sphericity, Thrust, or Fox-Wolfram moments reliably isolate soft, nearly azimuthally isotropic proton-proton events with specific azimuthal distributions at a given multiplicity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider proton–proton collision events at LHC energies. For each event, let the charged-particle multiplicity be N, and define the following global event-shape observables computed from the transverse momenta p⃗_T,i of the N charged particles in a chosen pseudorapidity acceptance:

- Transverse Sphericity S_T, defined via the smaller eigenvalue λ_2 of the 2×2 transverse momentum tensor
  M = (1/Σ|p⃗_T,i|) Σ_i (1/|p⃗_T,i|) (p_{x,i}^2, p_{x,i}p_{y,i}; p_{y,i}p_{x,i}, p_{y,i}^2),
  by S_T = 2λ_2/(λ_1+λ_2), so that S_T ∈ [0,1] with S_T → 0 for pencil-like and S_T → 1 for azimuthally isotropic events.
- Thrust T = max_{n̂} Σ_i |p⃗_T,i · n̂| / Σ_i |p⃗_T,i|.
- Directivity D, defined analogously as a normalized sum of projections onto a chosen reference direction.
- The Fox–Wolfram moments H_ℓ, ℓ = 0,1,2,…, computed from the angular distribution of final-state particles.

A "soft, azimuthally isotropic" event is one whose azimuthal distribution dN/dφ is consistent with rotational invariance up to statistical fluctuations and which contains no hard jet structure.

Question. Does there exist a two-dimensional event-selection criterion of the form (N, X) ∈ R, where X ∈ {S_T, T, D, H_ℓ} is one of the above event-shape variables and R is a region in the (multiplicity, event-shape) plane, such that the selected sub-sample at any fixed multiplicity N reliably consists of soft, nearly azimuthally isotropic events with prescribed azimuthal distributions, in the sense that residual contamination by hard, jetty events vanishes in a controlled way as the selection is tightened? paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: Let n be a positive integer and let M_n(μ) denote the set of distributions on ℝ that are n-completely mixable with center μ. If a distribution F on ℝ or on ℝ^d is n-completely mixable, must its center be unique? Equivalently, for distinct μ, ν ∈ ℝ, is M_n(μ) ∩ M_n(ν) empty?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. A probability distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (respectively on $\mathbb{R}^d$) is called $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ (respectively $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$) if there exist random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$, each having distribution $F$, such that
$$X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = n\mu \quad \text{almost surely}.$$
For each $\mu$, let $M_n(\mu)$ denote the set of all distributions on $\mathbb{R}$ (respectively on $\mathbb{R}^d$) that are $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu$.

Question: Is the center of complete mixability necessarily unique? Equivalently, for any two distinct points $\mu \neq \nu$, is it true that
$$M_n(\mu) \cap M_n(\nu) = \emptyset \, ?$$
status_search_result: The problem has been resolved negatively. Puccetti, Rigo, Wang and Wang (J. Theor. Probab., 2019, "Centers of probability measures without the mean") show that for each $n\ge 2$, $n$ standard Cauchy random variables can be coupled to sum to any constant $C$ with $|C|\le n\log(n-1)/\pi$. This gives an explicit distribution (Cauchy) that is $n$-completely mixable with infinitely many distinct centers, so the center is not unique in general; however, uniqueness does hold whenever at least $n-2$ of the marginals have finite mean.

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: Theorem 3 states that a ℤ_+-valued random vector X is a joint mix with joint center N if and only if it can be written as X = ∑_{k=1}^N X_k, where each X_k is a binary multinomial random vector. Can this decomposition be used in a nontrivial way to characterize additional classes of completely mixable or jointly mixable distributions, and if so how?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A random vector $\mathbf{X}=(X^{(1)},\dots,X^{(d)})$ taking values in $\mathbb{Z}_+^d$ is called a joint mix with joint center $N\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ if its components are (in general) non-degenerate and $X^{(1)}+X^{(2)}+\cdots+X^{(d)}=N$ almost surely. A binary multinomial random vector is a random vector taking values in $\{0,1\}^d$ whose entries sum to $1$ almost surely (equivalently, a one-trial multinomial vector that puts a single $1$ uniformly or non-uniformly among the $d$ coordinates). A tuple of univariate distributions $(F_1,\dots,F_d)$ is called jointly mixable (JM) if there exist random variables $Y_1\sim F_1,\dots,Y_d\sim F_d$ on a common probability space such that $Y_1+\cdots+Y_d$ is almost surely constant; a single distribution $F$ is called $d$-completely mixable ($d$-CM) if $(F,F,\dots,F)$ ($d$ copies) is jointly mixable.

Known representation. A $\mathbb{Z}_+^d$-valued random vector $\mathbf{X}$ is a joint mix with joint center $N$ if and only if it admits the representation
$$\mathbf{X}=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\mathbf{X}_k,$$
where $\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_N$ are (not necessarily independent and not necessarily identically distributed) binary multinomial random vectors on $\{0,1\}^d$.

Problem. Determine whether the above binary-multinomial decomposition can be used in a nontrivial way to characterize further classes of completely mixable or jointly mixable distributions beyond those currently known. Specifically, exhibit (or rule out) new families of univariate distributions $F$ (or tuples $(F_1,\dots,F_d)$) for which complete mixability (respectively joint mixability) can be established or excluded by means of constructing or obstructing an appropriate decomposition into binary multinomial summands, and provide an explicit characterization of such new families together with the constructive coupling implied by the decomposition.
status_search_result: A full characterization of completely mixable and jointly mixable distributions is known only for $n\le 2$; for $n\ge 3$ the problem remains open, and no published work appears to have leveraged the binary-multinomial decomposition theorem to characterize new classes of CM/JM distributions. Subsequent work on detecting and on elliptical/related families of joint mixability does not address this specific question.

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: If C is a convex subset of ℝ^d, is the uniform distribution on C necessarily n-completely mixable for every n ≥ d + 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 1$ be an integer and let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex set of finite, positive Lebesgue measure. Let $X$ be a random vector uniformly distributed on $C$, with mean $\mu = \mathbb{E}[X] \in \mathbb{R}^d$. For an integer $n \geq 2$, the distribution of $X$ is said to be $n$-completely mixable ($n$-CM) if there exist random vectors $X_1, \dots, X_n$, each having the same distribution as $X$ (i.e., uniform on $C$), defined on a common probability space, such that
$$X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = n\mu \quad \text{almost surely.}$$

Question: Is it true that for every convex set $C \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite positive volume, the uniform distribution on $C$ is $n$-completely mixable for every integer $n \geq d+1$?
status_search_result: Web searches on complete mixability literature (Puccetti–Wang and successors) surface general results — e.g. continuous distributions with concave densities are $n$-CM for all $n\geq 2$, and $n$-radially symmetric distributions are $m$-CM for $m\geq n+1$ — but no source verifying or refuting the specific claim that the uniform law on an arbitrary convex body in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is $n$-CM for all $n \geq d+1$ was found. The current status appears unresolved in the publicly available literature.

original_question: Is every absolutely continuous distribution supported on a bounded interval n-completely mixable once n is large enough?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. A probability distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is called $n$-completely mixable ($n$-CM) if there exist random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$, each with marginal distribution $F$, and a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$ \mathbb{P}(X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = c) = 1. $$
(The joint distribution of $(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ is not required to be the product distribution; only the marginals are fixed to be $F$.)

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: Suppose a distribution F satisfies a known sufficient condition for n-complete mixability, such as one of the conditions listed earlier in Section 2.2. Is there a way to simulate samples from an n-complete mix with margins F?
self_contained_problem:
A distribution function $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is called $n$-completely mixable ($n$-CM) if there exist random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$, each with marginal distribution $F$, such that
$$X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = n\,\mu_F \quad \text{almost surely},$$
for some constant $\mu_F \in \mathbb{R}$ (necessarily equal to the mean of $F$ when it exists). A random vector $(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ realizing this property is called an $n$-complete mix with margins $F$.

Several sufficient conditions for $n$-complete mixability are known. For example, if $F$ has a monotone density on its (bounded) support and the mean satisfies an appropriate moderate-mean condition, then $F$ is $n$-CM; other sufficient conditions involve symmetry/unimodality assumptions.

Problem: Suppose $F$ is known to satisfy such a sufficient condition guaranteeing that $F$ is $n$-CM. Provide an explicit, implementable algorithm that produces samples from a joint distribution $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ whose marginals are all equal to $F$ and whose coordinates sum almost surely to the constant $n\,\mu_F$ — that is, design a simulation procedure for an $n$-complete mix with margins $F$.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive algorithm or published solution for general simulation of an n-complete mix with arbitrary margins F satisfying standard sufficient conditions for n-complete mixability. Existing literature on complete mixability focuses on existence results, detection, and convex minimization, rather than constructive simulation. The status appears unresolved in general, though partial constructions may exist for specific subclasses (e.g., monotone densities); evidence is inconclusive.

original_question: Let D_n be the aggregation set of sums X_1 + ⋯ + X_n formed from random variables with prescribed marginal distributions F_1, …, F_n. What are necessary and sufficient conditions for D_n to contain a smallest element with respect to convex order?

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and let $F_1, \dots, F_n$ be prescribed (one-dimensional) cumulative distribution functions on $\mathbb{R}$, each with finite mean. Define the aggregation set
$$D_n(F_1, \dots, F_n) = \{X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n : X_i \text{ is a random variable with distribution } F_i,\ i=1,\dots,n\},$$
where the joint distribution of $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ is allowed to be any coupling of the marginals $F_1, \dots, F_n$ (so $D_n$ is a set of distributions of sums, identified with the laws of $X_1+\cdots+X_n$).

Recall that for two integrable real random variables $Y$ and $Z$, $Y$ is said to precede $Z$ in convex order, written $Y \le_{cx} Z$, if $\mathbb{E}[\phi(Y)] \le \mathbb{E}[\phi(Z)]$ for every convex function $\phi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ for which both expectations exist. An element $S^* \in D_n$ is called a smallest element of $D_n$ with respect to convex order if $S^* \le_{cx} S$ for every $S \in D_n$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the marginals $F_1, \dots, F_n$ for the aggregation set $D_n(F_1, \dots, F_n)$ to contain a smallest element with respect to convex order.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in the survey on complete mixability and is repeatedly cited as such in subsequent literature. Sufficient conditions are known (e.g., when each F_i has a decreasing density on its support, or in other special cases studied by Bernard–Jiang–Wang and Zhu), but a full characterization of necessary and sufficient conditions for D_n to admit a convex-order smallest element does not appear to have been established.

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: Given positive numbers a_{i,j} representing the time taken by worker (i, j) to complete production step j, and using permutations σ_1, …, σ_n ∈ S_m to assign one worker from each step to each of m equipments, minimize max_{i=1,…,m} ∑_{j=1}^n a_{σ_j(i),j}. What assignment of workers is optimal, and how can an optimal assignment be computed?
self_contained_problem:
Let m, n be positive integers, and let A = (a_{i,j}) be an m × n matrix with strictly positive real entries; the entry a_{i,j} represents the time required by worker i to perform production step j. There are m identical pieces of equipment, and for each step j ∈ {1, …, n} an assignment σ_j ∈ S_m (the symmetric group on {1, …, m}) is chosen, which assigns the worker σ_j(i) to equipment i for step j. The total processing time on equipment i is

  T_i(σ_1, …, σ_n) = Σ_{j=1}^n a_{σ_j(i), j},

and the makespan is M(σ_1, …, σ_n) = max_{1 ≤ i ≤ m} T_i(σ_1, …, σ_n).

(a) Characterize the tuples (σ_1, …, σ_n) ∈ (S_m)^n that minimize M(σ_1, …, σ_n).

(b) Provide an algorithm that computes such an optimal tuple, and analyze its computational complexity (in particular, determine whether the problem can be solved in time polynomial in m and n, or whether it is NP-hard).
status_search_result: No direct resolution of this minimax permutation-assignment formulation (as posed in the context of complete mixability) was located. The problem is closely related to multiprocessor scheduling makespan minimization with column-permutation structure, which in general is NP-hard, but a dedicated optimal-arrangement characterization for this exact formulation does not appear to have been published. Status remains best described as open.

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: For given distributions, can one design effective algorithms to decide whether they are jointly mixable or to solve the minimax assignment problem from Section 1? In particular, under what conditions do the swapping algorithms discussed in the paper converge?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $F_1,\dots,F_d$ be one-dimensional probability distribution functions on $\mathbb{R}$ with finite means. The tuple $(F_1,\dots,F_d)$ is called jointly mixable if there exist random variables $X_1,\dots,X_d$ on a common probability space, with $X_i\sim F_i$ for each $i$, such that
$$ X_1+X_2+\cdots+X_d = c \quad \text{almost surely} $$
for some constant $c\in\mathbb{R}$ (necessarily $c=\sum_i \mathbb{E}[X_i]$). When $d=1$ and a single distribution $F$ admits such a representation with $d$ i.i.d. copies summing to a constant, $F$ is called $d$-completely mixable.

Discrete approximation. Given $F_1,\dots,F_d$, fix a large integer $N$ and form a $d\times N$ matrix $M$ whose $i$-th row consists of $N$ quantiles $F_i^{-1}((j-1/2)/N)$, $j=1,\dots,N$. A swapping (rearrangement) algorithm iteratively rearranges entries within each row of $M$ to minimize the variance of the column sums; convergence here means that the column-sum variance tends to $0$ as $N\to\infty$ and the iteration count grows.

Problem. 
(a) Design an effective algorithm that, given $F_1,\dots,F_d$ (specified e.g. by their quantile functions to arbitrary precision), decides whether $(F_1,\dots,F_d)$ is jointly mixable.
(b) Design an effective algorithm to solve the minimax assignment problem
$$ \min_{\sigma_2,\dots,\sigma_d \in S_N} \;\max_{1\le j\le N}\; \Big( x_{1,j}+\sum_{i=2}^{d} x_{i,\sigma_i(j)} \Big) - \min_{1\le j\le N}\Big(x_{1,j}+\sum_{i=2}^{d} x_{i,\sigma_i(j)}\Big), $$
where $(x_{i,j})$ is the matrix $M$ above and $S_N$ is the symmetric group on $N$ elements; equivalently, find permutations of the rows that minimize the range of the column sums.
(c) Identify explicit, sharp sufficient conditions on $F_1,\dots,F_d$ under which the swapping (rearrangement) algorithm — which at each step replaces the entries of one row by a permutation that makes that row oppositely ordered to the sum of the remaining rows — converges to an arrangement whose column sums have variance $0$ (in the limit $N\to\infty$).
status_search_result: Detection of joint/complete mixability and the worst-VaR rearrangement problem have been studied by Puccetti–Wang ("Detecting complete and joint mixability", 2015) and refined by Block Rearrangement Algorithm variants (Bernard–McLeish, Boudt et al., 2017+). Convergence rate results for the minimal-variance problem and partial guarantees for BRA exist, but general necessary-and-sufficient convergence conditions for the original swapping/rearrangement algorithm remain not fully characterized; thus the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: What happens if the definition of mixability uses a multivariate function other than the sum x_1 + ⋯ + x_n? Which alternative multivariate functions lead to useful notions of mixability, and how should those notions be characterized?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A tuple of univariate distributions $F_1,\dots,F_n$ is called jointly mixable if there exist random variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ defined on a common probability space such that $X_i\sim F_i$ for each $i$ and the sum $X_1+\cdots+X_n$ is almost surely equal to a constant. When $F_1=\cdots=F_n=F$, the distribution $F$ is called $n$-completely mixable.

Problem. Replace the additive aggregation function $S(x_1,\dots,x_n)=x_1+\cdots+x_n$ by a general measurable function $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ (or more generally $\Phi:\mathcal{X}^n\to\mathcal{Y}$ for a suitable measurable space). Say that distributions $F_1,\dots,F_n$ are $\Phi$-mixable if there exist random variables $X_i\sim F_i$ on a common probability space with $\Phi(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ almost surely constant.

(a) Identify the classes of functions $\Phi$ for which $\Phi$-mixability yields a non-trivial and useful theory (e.g., functions invariant under permutations of coordinates, continuous, monotone in each argument, or Schur-concave/convex aggregations such as $\max$, $\min$, products, $L^p$-norms, or quasi-arithmetic means $\phi^{-1}\!\big(\tfrac{1}{n}\sum\phi(x_i)\big)$).

(b) For such classes, give a characterization (necessary and sufficient conditions on $F_1,\dots,F_n$) for $\Phi$-mixability, generalizing known characterizations available for $\Phi=S$ (e.g., the mean condition and the variance/length conditions for monotone marginal densities).

(c) Determine the analogue of the "center" (the almost-sure constant value of $\Phi(X_1,\dots,X_n)$) and the set of admissible centers.
status_search_result: No general theory characterizing $\Phi$-mixability for arbitrary aggregation functions $\Phi$ replacing the sum appears in the literature. Some related generalizations exist (e.g., joint mixability with center, and unrelated "Φ-mixability" in online learning by Reid et al., 2015), but a systematic answer to which alternative multivariate aggregation functions yield a useful mixability theory and how to characterize them remains, to current knowledge, open.

paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
original_question: For n > 3, can one fully characterize the set J_n(K) of n-tuples of distributions that are jointly mixable with joint center K, or equivalently the set M_n(μ) of distributions on ℝ that are n-completely mixable with center μ?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $F_1,\dots,F_n$ be univariate cumulative distribution functions on $\mathbb{R}$. The tuple $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ is called jointly mixable with center $K\in\mathbb{R}$ if there exist random variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ defined on a common probability space, with $X_i\sim F_i$ for each $i$, such that
$$P(X_1+X_2+\cdots+X_n=K)=1.$$
Define
$$J_n(K)=\{(F_1,\dots,F_n): (F_1,\dots,F_n)\text{ is jointly mixable with center }K\}.$$
A distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is called $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu$ if $(F,F,\dots,F)\in J_n(n\mu)$, and we set
$$M_n(\mu)=\{F: F\text{ is }n\text{-completely mixable with center }\mu\}.$$

Problem. For each integer $n>3$, give a full (necessary and sufficient) characterization of the set $J_n(K)$ of $n$-tuples of one-dimensional distributions that are jointly mixable with center $K$, or equivalently of the set $M_n(\mu)$ of distributions on $\mathbb{R}$ that are $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu$.

paper_title: Settling Some Open Problems on 2-Player Symmetric Nash Equilibria
original_question: For a two-player bimatrix game (A, B), where the rank of the game is defined to be rank(A + B), can a Nash equilibrium always be computed in polynomial time when rank(A + B) = 2, or is the rank-2 case computationally intractable?
self_contained_problem:
Let (A, B) be a two-player bimatrix game, where A, B ∈ ℚ^{m×n} are the payoff matrices for the row player and the column player respectively. A Nash equilibrium of (A, B) is a pair of mixed strategies (x, y), with x ∈ Δ_m and y ∈ Δ_n (probability simplices), such that

  x^T A y ≥ (x')^T A y for all x' ∈ Δ_m, and
  x^T B y ≥ x^T B y' for all y' ∈ Δ_n.

Define the rank of the bimatrix game (A, B) to be rank(A + B). 

Determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given a bimatrix game (A, B) with rank(A + B) = 2, compute a Nash equilibrium of (A, B). Specifically, decide whether there exists an algorithm that, on input (A, B) with rank(A + B) = 2, outputs a Nash equilibrium in time polynomial in the bit-length of the input, or whether the problem is computationally intractable (e.g., PPAD-hard).
category_tag: algorithmic game theory / bimatrix Nash equilibria
status_search_result: The complexity of computing a Nash equilibrium in rank-2 bimatrix games (where rank is defined as rank(A+B)) appears to remain open. Rank-1 was solved in polynomial time by Adsul, Garg, Mehta, Sohoni (2011). Mehta (2014/STOC) showed that bimatrix games of any constant rank ≥ 3 are PPAD-hard. The rank-2 case sits between these results and is, to current knowledge, unresolved.

paper_title: Settling Some Open Problems on 2-Player Symmetric Nash Equilibria
context_brief: symmetric fixed-rank games of rank 2 through 5
original_question: For each k in {2, 3, 4, 5}, what is the computational complexity of finding a symmetric Nash equilibrium in a two-player symmetric bimatrix game (A, A^T) whose rank is k, that is, for which rank(A + A^T) = k?
self_contained_problem:
A two-player bimatrix game is given by a pair of real n×n payoff matrices (A, B), where the row player chooses a probability distribution x ∈ Δ_n = {x ∈ ℝ^n_{≥0} : Σ x_i = 1} and the column player chooses y ∈ Δ_n; the row player's expected payoff is x^T A y and the column player's is x^T B y. A Nash equilibrium (NE) is a pair (x, y) ∈ Δ_n × Δ_n such that x^T A y ≥ x'^T A y for every x' ∈ Δ_n and x^T B y ≥ x^T B y' for every y' ∈ Δ_n. The game is called symmetric if B = A^T; in that case a symmetric Nash equilibrium is a NE of the form (x, x) with x ∈ Δ_n. The rank of a symmetric game (A, A^T) is defined as rank(A + A^T).

For each fixed integer k ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5}, determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given a symmetric bimatrix game (A, A^T) with rational entries satisfying rank(A + A^T) = k, compute a symmetric Nash equilibrium of the game. In particular, for each such k decide whether this problem admits a polynomial-time algorithm, is PPAD-hard, or is complete for some natural intermediate class.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has established that computing a symmetric Nash equilibrium in symmetric games of rank ≥ 6 is PPAD-hard, while the rank-1 symmetric case admits a polynomial-time algorithm. The complexity of the symmetric NE problem for symmetric games of rank exactly 2, 3, 4, or 5 has not been resolved in the literature found, and these cases are still reported as open.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
context_brief: Hadronic final states in CCQE-like models
original_question: How can neutrino-nucleus CCQE-like interaction models that reproduce outgoing charged-lepton kinematics also assign a hadronic final state consistently, including outgoing proton multiplicities and kinematics, for fine-grained tracking detectors and liquid-argon time projection chambers?
self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasi-elastic-like (CCQE-like) neutrino–nucleus scattering, in which an incoming neutrino interacts with a nucleus (e.g. carbon or argon) producing an outgoing charged lepton together with one or more knocked-out nucleons, in the kinematic regime relevant to accelerator-based neutrino experiments (incoming neutrino energies of order 0.5–5 GeV). Theoretical descriptions of this process commonly include single-nucleon quasi-elastic scattering supplemented by random-phase-approximation (RPA) corrections, multi-nucleon (2p2h/np-nh) contributions, and final-state interactions of the outgoing hadrons in the nuclear medium.

Such inclusive descriptions, which integrate over hadronic final states, can reproduce the measured outgoing charged-lepton kinematics (for example double-differential cross sections in the muon momentum and angle). However, fine-grained tracking detectors and liquid-argon time projection chambers are able to resolve the exclusive hadronic final state, including the multiplicity of outgoing protons above detection threshold and their individual momenta and angles.

Problem: Construct a theoretical and computational framework for CCQE-like neutrino–nucleus interactions that simultaneously
(i) reproduces the inclusive outgoing charged-lepton double-differential kinematics with the same accuracy as current RPA + multi-nucleon inclusive calculations, and
(ii) consistently assigns, on an event-by-event basis, an exclusive hadronic final state — specifying the number of outgoing protons above a given kinematic threshold and their full momentum distributions — that is correlated with the lepton kinematics in a manner derived from the underlying nuclear dynamics (rather than imposed by an ad hoc cascade) and that agrees with exclusive proton-multiplicity and proton-kinematics measurements from fine-grained tracking detectors and liquid-argon time projection chambers.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. relativistic distorted-wave impulse approximation implementations in NEUT, 2025; MicroBooNE final-state-interaction studies on argon, 2024) continues to develop and benchmark exclusive CCQE-like models with proton multiplicities and kinematics, but no single framework has been established that simultaneously reproduces inclusive lepton kinematics and exclusive hadronic final states across carbon and argon targets. The problem of consistently assigning the hadronic final state with the lepton kinematics remains an active area of investigation.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
original_question: How can the scaling analyses and short-range correlation information obtained from inclusive electron quasielastic scattering be made usable in neutrino-nucleus CCQE analyses, given that neutrino experiments generally do not know the incident neutrino energy event by event and therefore cannot directly establish the transferred momentum q and transferred energy ω?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. In inclusive quasielastic (QE) lepton–nucleus scattering, the kinematic variables of the reaction are the three-momentum transfer q and the energy transfer ω from the probe to the nuclear target. For inclusive electron QE scattering, both q and ω are determined event by event from the measured incident and scattered electron momenta, and the inclusive double-differential cross section, divided by an appropriate single-nucleon factor and expressed in a suitable scaling variable ψ(q,ω), exhibits "superscaling": the resulting scaling function f(ψ) becomes (to good approximation) independent of q and of the target nucleus. From these analyses one also extracts information about short-range correlated nucleon pairs (a high-momentum component carrying roughly 20% of the nucleons) that produce an enhancement in the transverse nuclear response.

For charged-current quasielastic (CCQE) neutrino–nucleus scattering νℓ + A → ℓ⁻ + X, the incoming neutrino energy Eν is not measured event by event; it is drawn from a broad flux Φ(Eν), and only the outgoing charged-lepton kinematics (and possibly hadronic observables) are recorded. Consequently q and ω cannot be reconstructed directly from the lepton kinematics alone, so the electron-scattering scaling function f(ψ) and the short-range-correlation information cannot be applied event by event in the standard way.

Problem. Devise a quantitative procedure that takes as input

  (i) the superscaling function f(ψ) and the associated transverse-enhancement contribution from short-range correlated pairs, as extracted from inclusive electron QE scattering data, and
  (ii) a known neutrino flux Φ(Eν) together with the measured outgoing charged-lepton (and, where available, hadronic) kinematics,

and produces predictions for flux-integrated CCQE neutrino–nucleus differential cross sections that consistently incorporate the electron-scattering scaling and short-range-correlation information despite the event-by-event ignorance of Eν, q, and ω. Specify how to fold the unknown Eν over Φ(Eν), how to treat the axial-vector response and the meson-exchange/2p2h contributions tied to short-range correlations, and quantify the residual theoretical uncertainty introduced by the unknown incident neutrino energy.
status_search_result: The SuSA and SuSAv2 programs (Amaro, Barbaro, Caballero, Donnelly, et al.) have extended electron-scattering superscaling to neutrino CCQE by folding the extracted scaling function over the neutrino flux and adding a 2p2h/meson-exchange-current contribution tied to short-range correlations. These approaches give working predictions for MiniBooNE, T2K, MINERvA and NOvA CCQE data, but residual flux-folding uncertainties and tensions in some kinematic regions remain, so the underlying question is partially addressed rather than fully closed.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
original_question: Why do the Martini and IFIC/Nieves RPA-based calculations for carbon neutrino CCQE-like scattering integrated over the MiniBooNE flux give a two-particle–two-hole (2p–2h) contribution that differs by about a factor of two, and is the unresolved axial-response enhancement responsible for this difference?
self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasi-elastic-like (CCQE-like) scattering of muon neutrinos on a carbon-12 target, integrated over the MiniBooNE muon-neutrino flux. Two microscopic many-body calculations of this process, both based on a local Fermi gas description of the nucleus together with Random Phase Approximation (RPA) long-range correlations and an explicit two-particle–two-hole (2p–2h) multinucleon excitation channel — namely (i) the model of Martini and collaborators and (ii) the IFIC/Valencia model of Nieves and collaborators — produce flux-integrated total CCQE-like cross sections that are in reasonable mutual agreement, but their separate 2p–2h contributions differ by approximately a factor of two, with the Martini 2p–2h piece being the larger.

(a) Identify the physical and formal origins of this factor-of-two discrepancy in the 2p–2h contribution. In particular, account for differences in (i) the set of diagrams included (pionic, Δ-mediated, exchange, and interference terms), (ii) the treatment of in-medium pion and Δ propagators and short-range correlations (e.g., Landau–Migdal g′ parameters), (iii) the kinematic phase space and energy–momentum-transfer regions actually integrated, and (iv) the precise definition of what is labelled "n-particle n-hole" in each formalism versus n-body currents used elsewhere.

(b) Determine whether an enhancement of the isovector axial nuclear response (beyond the standard RPA quenching that is well established for the isovector spin-longitudinal channel) is present in one calculation but not the other, and decide whether such an axial-response enhancement is the dominant cause of the factor-of-two difference in the 2p–2h contribution.
status_search_result: The discrepancy between the Martini et al. and Nieves et al. RPA-based 2p–2h predictions for MiniBooNE CCQE-like scattering on carbon remains an active and unresolved topic. Subsequent generator-implementation studies (e.g., NEUT and GENIE comparisons) and recent reviews still report the factor-of-two gap and treat the underlying axial-response enhancement as an open issue under investigation; no community-accepted resolution has appeared.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
context_brief: Relativistic extension of ab initio calculations
original_question: How can nonrelativistic ab initio nuclear approaches such as Green’s Function Monte Carlo calculations, which are currently limited to light nuclei, be extended or connected to the relativistic momentum and energy transfers encountered in accelerator neutrino beams so that they contribute to a complete CCQE description?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an ab initio many-body description of a nucleus with mass number A, in which the ground state and low-lying excited states are obtained from a realistic two-nucleon interaction (e.g., Argonne v18) supplemented by a three-nucleon interaction, with eigenstates and electroweak response functions computed via Green's Function Monte Carlo (GFMC). Such a treatment is intrinsically nonrelativistic and, due to its computational complexity, is currently feasible only for light nuclei (A ≤ 12).

In charged-current quasi-elastic (CCQE) neutrino–nucleus scattering at accelerator energies, the leptonic vertex transfers four-momentum (q, ω) whose magnitude routinely lies in the relativistic regime, where the struck nucleon's final momentum is comparable to or exceeds its rest mass.

Problem: Formulate a systematic framework that extends or connects nonrelativistic GFMC-type ab initio calculations of nuclear electroweak response functions to the relativistic kinematic regime characteristic of accelerator neutrino beams. Specifically:

(a) Construct a Lorentz-covariant (or appropriately boosted) prescription for the hadronic tensor W^{μν}(q,ω) that reduces, in the limit |q|/M_N → 0, to the GFMC nonrelativistic response functions, while incorporating the correct relativistic single-nucleon current and kinematics at large |q|.

(b) Specify how two-body meson-exchange currents and final-state interactions, presently treated nonrelativistically in GFMC, are to be promoted to the relativistic setting in a manner consistent with current conservation and gauge invariance.

(c) Provide quantitative criteria, in terms of |q| and ω, delimiting the kinematic domain in which the proposed extension reproduces nonrelativistic GFMC results and the domain in which relativistic corrections dominate, and demonstrate convergence to known relativistic limits (e.g., the relativistic Fermi gas or relativistic mean-field response) at high |q|.
category_tag: Ab initio nuclear response functions for neutrino scattering
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Rocco et al. (Phys. Rev. C 97, 055501, 2018) developed a relativistic treatment of ab initio electron-nucleus scattering using a factorization (spectral function) approach informed by GFMC, and Nikolakopoulos et al. (Phys. Rev. C 109, 014623, 2024; arXiv:2304.11772) introduced a two-fragment-model boost to a frame minimizing nucleon momenta, extending GFMC neutrino-nucleus calculations to higher |q|. These are partial solutions: a fully relativistic, gauge-consistent ab initio framework valid throughout the accelerator-neutrino kinematic range, including two-body currents and final-state interactions, is still under active development.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
original_question: How should oscillation analyses reconstruct the incident neutrino energy in CCQE-like events when only the outgoing lepton or an incomplete hadronic final state is measured, given Fermi motion, scattering from correlated nucleon pairs, finite detection thresholds, limited neutron detection, flux uncertainties, and model-dependent multinucleon effects that can bias the mapping between true and reconstructed energy?
self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasi-elastic-like (CCQE-like) neutrino–nucleus scattering events of the form ν_ℓ + A → ℓ^- + X, where the incoming neutrino has unknown energy E_ν drawn from a flux distribution Φ(E_ν) with significant uncertainty, and the target nucleus contains nucleons subject to Fermi motion as well as short-range correlated nucleon pairs whose constituents are appreciably off the mass shell. Assume that detectors observe the outgoing lepton four-momentum p_ℓ exactly, but observe the hadronic final state only partially: each final-state hadron of species s is detected with probability depending on its kinetic energy through a threshold function (in particular, final-state neutrons are largely undetected), and additional final-state interactions and multinucleon (2p2h) processes — described by a family of competing nuclear models {M_α} — can produce additional unobserved nucleons.

Under these conditions, design a procedure (a deterministic estimator or a posterior reconstruction) that maps the observed event data to a reconstructed neutrino energy Ê_ν such that the bias and variance of Ê_ν − E_ν are controlled uniformly over (i) the flux uncertainty in Φ, (ii) the Fermi-motion distribution of the struck nucleon, (iii) the contribution of scattering off correlated nucleon pairs (which, when treated as single-nucleon CCQE using only the lepton kinematics, systematically underestimates E_ν because both nucleons of the pair must be put on-shell), (iv) finite detection thresholds and missing neutron information, and (v) the choice of multinucleon model M_α.

Specifically: give an explicit reconstruction prescription, together with quantitative bounds on its model-dependence, that an oscillation analysis (which infers oscillation parameters from the reconstructed-energy spectrum) can use without introducing biases larger than its statistical precision; or prove that no such prescription exists, identifying the minimal additional measurement (e.g., specified hadronic observables above specified thresholds) required to make the mapping from true to reconstructed neutrino energy unambiguous.
status_search_result: Neutrino energy reconstruction in CCQE-like events remains an active and unresolved problem in neutrino physics. Recent literature (T2K, NOvA, MicroBooNE, DUNE generator and theory studies through 2024–2025) continues to report model-dependent biases from 2p2h/multinucleon effects, Fermi motion, and missing neutrons, with no universally accepted unbiased estimator; mitigation via transverse-kinematic-imbalance variables and improved nuclear models is partial.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
original_question: What remaining neutral-current single-photon production mechanisms, especially anomalous ωZγ contributions with large theoretical uncertainties, and what direct measurements by MicroBooNE, MINERvA, ND280/T2K, or similar detectors are needed to make this background sufficiently controlled for electron-neutrino appearance studies?
self_contained_problem:
Consider neutral-current (NC) single-photon production in neutrino–nucleus scattering, i.e. processes of the form ν + N → ν + γ + X, which constitute an irreducible background to electron-neutrino appearance searches in accelerator-based oscillation experiments. Standard contributions include NC Δ(1232) radiative decay, non-resonant nucleon-pole and meson-exchange amplitudes, and NC coherent photon production on nuclei. In addition, the chiral anomaly induces an "anomalous" ωZγ vertex (analogous to the ωγγ Wess–Zumino–Witten term), giving an ω-meson-exchange contribution to NC γ production whose normalization, off-shell behavior, and nuclear modification carry large theoretical uncertainties.

Identify and quantify:
(a) the remaining NC single-photon production mechanisms—most importantly the anomalous ωZγ contribution—that are not yet under firm theoretical control, providing a robust calculation of their cross sections (flux-averaged differential and total) on nucleon and nuclear targets in the sub-GeV to few-GeV neutrino energy range, with quantified theoretical uncertainties; and
(b) the direct experimental measurements of NC γ production (exclusive single-photon final states, separated into resonant, non-resonant/anomalous, and coherent components) achievable with detectors such as MicroBooNE (liquid argon TPC at the Booster Neutrino Beam), MINERvA, and ND280/T2K, that are required to constrain these mechanisms at a level sufficient (typically ≲10–20% on the total NC γ rate in the relevant kinematic region) for this background to no longer limit νe appearance / sterile-neutrino searches.

The problem is to determine what theoretical refinements and experimental measurements are needed, and at what precision, so that the NC single-photon background — including the anomalous ωZγ piece — is rendered "sufficiently controlled" for current and next-generation electron-neutrino appearance studies.
status_search_result: MicroBooNE has since published several direct measurements of NC single-photon production: a search for NC Δ radiative decay placing a 90% CL bound of <2.3× the nominal rate (PRL 128, 111801, 2022), a first search for NC coherent single-photon production (arXiv:2502.06091, 2025), and an inclusive anomalous single-photon search (arXiv:2502.06064, 2025). These directly address the experimental program called for, but a definitive measurement isolating the anomalous ωZγ contribution and reducing its theoretical uncertainty has not yet been achieved; work on MINERvA and ND280/T2K is ongoing. Hence the question is partially solved.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
original_question: How should neutrino experiments report CCQE measurements with precise definitions of the event selection, observables, and the meaning of “CCQE,” while providing model-independent quantities and flux information that theorists can calculate directly, so that comparisons with neutrino and electron-scattering theory are unambiguous?
self_contained_problem:
In neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments, charged-current quasi-elastic (CCQE) interactions are conventionally identified by an event selection that targets a charged lepton plus one (or zero) outgoing nucleons with no detected mesons in the final state. Because nuclear effects, final-state interactions, and detector thresholds blur the distinction between the underlying elementary process and what is actually observed, the operational meaning of "CCQE" varies between experiments and differs from the usage in the electron-scattering community.

Devise a reporting framework for CCQE measurements that makes experiment–theory comparison unambiguous. Specifically, formulate:

1. A precise definition of the event-selection topology in terms of observable final-state particles (lepton kinematics, nucleon multiplicity and momentum thresholds, photon and meson vetoes), independent of any underlying interaction model.

2. A set of model-independent observables (e.g., differential cross sections in directly measured kinematic variables of the outgoing lepton and hadrons) that a theorist can compute from first principles without needing to replicate the experiment's neutrino-generator assumptions.

3. A specification of the incoming neutrino flux Φ(E_ν), including its uncertainties and correlations, in a form that can be convolved with any theoretical cross-section model dσ/dΩ(E_ν, …) to yield a prediction directly comparable to the reported observables.

4. A clear statement distinguishing the experimental "CCQE-like" topology from the theoretical notion of quasi-elastic scattering (one-body current on a single nucleon) and from the electron-scattering usage of "quasi-elastic" and "final-state interactions."

The problem is to produce such a reporting protocol—definitions, observables, flux deliverables, and unfolding/acceptance conventions—so that comparisons of CCQE measurements with both neutrino- and electron-scattering theoretical predictions become unambiguous and reproducible.

original_question: Take p ∈ {2, 3} and let L be a finite field of characteristic p and order q. For the exponent s = q − 2, which satisfies s ≡ 1 (mod p − 1) exactly in these two characteristics, can one prove the Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture for this case without using the theory of elliptic curves? In other words, can one show by a different method that there exists a nonzero a ∈ L such that W_{L,q−2}(a) = 0?

Let $p\in\{2,3\}$ be a prime and let $L=\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$ with $q=p^m$ elements. For an integer $s$ coprime to $q-1$ and $a\in L$, define the Walsh (cross-correlation) transform
$$W_{L,s}(a)\;=\;\sum_{x\in L}\chi\!\left(x^{s}-a x\right).$$
Take the exponent $s=q-2$ (note $q-2\equiv 1\pmod{p-1}$ exactly when $p\in\{2,3\}$). The Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture asserts that there exists a nonzero $a\in L$ with $W_{L,s}(a)=0$.
