context_brief: Topology dependence of the McShane integral
original_question: Let f: Ω → X be a function on a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) with values in a Banach space X. If T_1 and T_2 are two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon, and f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T_2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a complete probability space and let $X$ be a Banach space. Recall that a topology $\mathcal{T}$ on $\Omega$ is said to make $\mu$ quasi-Radon if $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu, \mathcal{T})$ is a quasi-Radon measure space, i.e., $\mathcal{T} \subseteq \Sigma$, $\mu$ is inner regular with respect to closed sets, $\mu$ is $\tau$-additive (the measure of the union of any upward-directed family of open sets equals the supremum of their measures), and the measure is complete and locally determined.

For such a quasi-Radon structure, a function $f: \Omega \to X$ is called McShane integrable (with respect to $\mathcal{T}$) with integral $w \in X$ if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a "gauge" $\Delta: \Omega \to \mathcal{T}$ with $x \in \Delta(x)$ for all $x \in \Omega$, such that for every finite collection $\{(E_1, x_1), \ldots, (E_n, x_n)\}$ with the $E_i \in \Sigma$ pairwise disjoint, $x_i \in \Omega$, $E_i \subseteq \Delta(x_i)$, and $\sum_{i=1}^n \mu(E_i) \geq 1 - \varepsilon$, one has
$$\Big\| \sum_{i=1}^n \mu(E_i)\, f(x_i) - w \Big\| \leq \varepsilon.$$

Suppose $\mathcal{T}_1$ and $\mathcal{T}_2$ are two topologies on $\Omega$ each making $\mu$ quasi-Radon, and suppose $f: \Omega \to X$ is McShane integrable with respect to $\mathcal{T}_1$. Must $f$ also be McShane integrable with respect to $\mathcal{T}_2$?
status_search_result: The problem, posed by Fremlin, appears to remain open in general. A partial affirmative answer is known: if one of the topologies has a countable base, then McShane integrability transfers between the two topologies and the integrals agree. No full resolution was located in the search results.

context_brief: Weakly compact subsets of c_0 as vector-measure ranges
original_question: Let K be a weakly compact subset of c_0. Must there exist a c_0-valued countably additive vector measure whose range contains K?
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real sequences converging to $0$, equipped with the supremum norm. A function $\mu : \Sigma \to c_0$ defined on a $\sigma$-algebra $\Sigma$ of subsets of some set $\Omega$ is called a countably additive vector measure if $\mu\left(\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} E_n\right) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \mu(E_n)$ in the norm topology of $c_0$ for every sequence $(E_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of pairwise disjoint members of $\Sigma$. The range of $\mu$ is the set $\{\mu(E) : E \in \Sigma\} \subseteq c_0$.

Suppose $K \subseteq c_0$ is weakly compact (i.e., compact in the weak topology of $c_0$). Must there exist a measurable space $(\Omega,\Sigma)$ and a countably additive vector measure $\mu : \Sigma \to c_0$ such that $K$ is contained in the range of $\mu$?
status_search_result: The question is a long-standing problem attributed to Anantharaman and Diestel concerning whether every weakly compact subset of $c_0$ lies in the range of a $c_0$-valued countably additive vector measure. Web searches turn up surveys of open problems in Banach spaces and vector-measure theory that still list related questions, and no resolution (positive or negative) was located. The status appears to remain open.

original_question: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly compactly generated, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X) also be strongly weakly compactly generated?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a real Banach space. We say that X is strongly weakly compactly generated (SWCG) if there exists a weakly compact set G ⊂ X such that for every weakly compact set K ⊂ X and every ε > 0 there exists n ∈ ℕ with K ⊂ nG + εB_X, where B_X denotes the closed unit ball of X. Equivalently, the family of all weakly compact subsets of X is strongly generated by a single weakly compact set.

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a finite (or σ-finite, non-purely-atomic) positive measure space, and let L^1(μ, X) denote the Lebesgue–Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) Bochner-integrable functions f : Ω → X with norm ‖f‖ = ∫_Ω ‖f(ω)‖ dμ(ω).

Question: If X is SWCG, must L^1(μ, X) also be SWCG?
category_tag: Banach spaces — SWCG and Lebesgue–Bochner spaces
status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Schlüchtermann and Wheeler, appears to remain open. Subsequent work (e.g., Rodríguez, 2015–2017) established partial results — for instance, that L^1(μ, X) is SWCG when X is an SWCG subspace of an L^1-space, and reformulations in terms of strong generation of uniformly bounded weakly compact families — but a full answer in general is not reported in the available literature.

original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the vector-valued Lebesgue space L^p([0, 1], X), with 1 < p < ∞, has an unconditional basis.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a (real or complex) infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $1 < p < \infty$. Let $L^p([0,1], X)$ denote the Bochner space of (equivalence classes of) strongly measurable functions $f : [0,1] \to X$ such that $\|f\|_{L^p(X)} := \left( \int_0^1 \|f(t)\|_X^p \, dt \right)^{1/p} < \infty$, equipped with this norm. A sequence $(e_n)_{n \ge 1}$ in a Banach space $E$ is called a Schauder basis of $E$ if every $x \in E$ admits a unique representation $x = \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n e_n$ converging in norm; the basis is called unconditional if this series converges unconditionally for every $x \in E$. 

Give a characterization, in terms of intrinsic Banach-space properties of $X$, of those Banach spaces $X$ for which $L^p([0,1], X)$ admits an unconditional Schauder basis.

original_question: Does L^1[0, 1] have property (D_∞), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → L^1[0, 1] which is bounded in L^∞([0, 1], L^1[0, 1]) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 admits a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X = L^1[0,1]$ (with Lebesgue measure). A function $f:[0,1] \to X$ is said to be strongly measurable if it is the almost-everywhere limit of a sequence of simple $X$-valued functions. For $g \in X^* = L^\infty[0,1]$, the scalar function $\langle f, g\rangle: t \mapsto \langle f(t), g\rangle$ is then measurable.

A sequence $(f_n)$ of strongly measurable functions $f_n:[0,1] \to X$ is said to:
(i) be bounded in $L^\infty([0,1], X)$ if $\sup_n \operatorname{ess\,sup}_{t \in [0,1]} \|f_n(t)\|_X < \infty$;
(ii) converge scalarly in measure to $0$ if for every $g \in X^*$ the scalar sequence $\langle f_n(\cdot), g\rangle$ converges to $0$ in Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$;
(iii) converge scalarly to $0$ almost everywhere if there is a measurable set $N \subset [0,1]$ of measure zero such that for every $g \in X^*$ and every $t \in [0,1]\setminus N$, $\langle f_n(t), g\rangle \to 0$.

The Banach space $X$ is said to have property $(D_\infty)$ if every sequence $(f_n)$ of strongly measurable functions $f_n:[0,1] \to X$ which is bounded in $L^\infty([0,1], X)$ and converges scalarly in measure to $0$ admits a subsequence that converges scalarly to $0$ almost everywhere.

original_question: Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is a partially ordered set, with elements called faces, that satisfies the standard axioms generalizing the face lattice of a convex polytope: it has a unique minimum face and a unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) has the same length $n+2$, $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on the set of flags of $\mathcal{P}$, and $\mathcal{P}$ is called a $k$-orbit polytope when this action has exactly $k$ orbits.

When $\mathcal{P}$ is regular (1-orbit), fixing a base flag $\Phi$ produces distinguished generators $\rho_0,\dots,\rho_{n-1}$ of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$, where $\rho_i$ maps $\Phi$ to its unique $i$-adjacent flag. In this case $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ is a string C-group: it is generated by involutions satisfying string Coxeter-type relations together with the intersection condition
$$\langle \rho_i : i \in I\rangle \cap \langle \rho_i : i \in J\rangle = \langle \rho_i : i \in I\cap J\rangle$$
for all $I,J \subseteq \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$. Conversely, every string C-group arises this way, giving a bijection between regular abstract polytopes and string C-groups.

For a $k$-orbit polytope ($k \geq 2$) with a prescribed symmetry type graph, choose an analogous distinguished generating set for $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ obtained from a base flag together with selected flag-changing automorphisms or coset representatives encoding the orbit structure.

Problem. Formulate and prove an analogue of the intersection condition for such a distinguished generating set of the automorphism group of a $k$-orbit abstract polytope, characterizing exactly which groups, equipped with these generators and relations, arise as automorphism groups of $k$-orbit polytopes with the given symmetry type graph.
status_search_result: The problem has seen significant progress: a 2023 paper (Hubard–Schulte, "All polytopes are coset geometries") characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes in terms of generators, relations, and intersection conditions tied to the symmetry type graph. Specific cases — two-orbit polytopes and 3-orbit polyhedra — have explicit intersection-property formulations. A general unified analogue for arbitrary k and arbitrary symmetry type graph continues to be developed, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully closed.

original_question: Can one find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for coverings that works beyond the regular and chiral cases?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P (whose elements are called faces) with a unique minimum face and unique maximum face, in which every maximal chain (flag) has the same length n+1, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G are faces with rank(G) = rank(F) + 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. The set of flags F(P) carries, for each i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1}, an involution which sends a flag Φ to the unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i face; these are the flag-adjacency relations.

A surjective rank- and adjacency-preserving map η : P → Q between abstract polytopes of the same rank is called a covering. The polytope P is regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on F(P), and chiral if this group has exactly two orbits on F(P) such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits. More generally, P is a k-orbit polytope if Aut(P) has exactly k orbits on F(P).

For regular polytopes there is a classical quotient criterion: a regular polytope R covers a regular polytope Q if and only if Q ≅ R/N for some subgroup N of Aut(R) satisfying an explicit intersection condition on the distinguished generators. An analogous quotient criterion has been established for chiral polytopes.

Formulate and prove a purely combinatorial quotient criterion for coverings of abstract polytopes that applies to k-orbit polytopes for arbitrary k, and in particular yields a necessary and sufficient combinatorial condition (without restriction to the regular or chiral cases) under which one abstract polytope covers another.

original_question: Does there exist a polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but that still has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or can one prove that no such polytope exists?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a strict rank function taking values in {-1, 0, …, n}, possessing a unique minimum element F_{-1} and unique maximum element F_n, in which every maximal chain (flag) has exactly n+2 elements, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G with rank(G) = rank(F)+2, there are exactly two elements H with F < H < G. The set of flags of P is denoted F(P). For each i ∈ {0,…,n-1} and each flag Φ ∈ F(P), there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i element; this defines an involution r_i on F(P).

The monodromy group Mon(P) is the subgroup of the symmetric group on F(P) generated by r_0, r_1, …, r_{n-1}.

A string C-group of rank n is a group G generated by involutions ρ_0,…,ρ_{n-1} satisfying (i) the string condition (ρ_iρ_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i-j| ≥ 2, and (ii) the intersection condition: ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I ∩ J⟩ for all I, J ⊆ {0,…,n-1}. Abstract regular polytopes correspond bijectively to string C-groups via their automorphism groups acting on a base flag.

A regular cover of P is an abstract regular polytope R together with a rank- and adjacency-preserving surjection R → P (i.e., a covering of flag systems commuting with each r_i). A minimal regular cover of P is a regular cover that does not properly cover any other regular cover of P.

Problem. Determine whether there exists an abstract polytope P such that:
(a) the monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group, and
(b) P nonetheless admits a unique minimal regular polytopal cover;
or, alternatively, prove that no such polytope P exists.
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this specific question. Related work (e.g., on chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is itself a polytope, and on minimal covers of prisms, antiprisms, and Archimedean tilings) addresses adjacent cases but does not appear to settle the existence/non-existence question for polytopes with non-string-C-group monodromy yet a unique minimal regular polytopal cover. Status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

original_question: What is the correct way to generalize the chirality group from two-orbit polytopes to k-orbit polytopes?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope P is a ranked partially ordered set whose maximal chains (called flags) satisfy the diamond condition and a connectedness axiom; its automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on flags. A polytope is called regular if Γ(P) is transitive on flags, and (two-orbit) chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on flags with adjacent flags lying in different orbits. For a chiral polytope P, the chirality group X(P) is defined as the kernel of the natural epimorphism from Γ(P) onto the automorphism group of the maximal regular quotient of P; equivalently, X(P) measures how far P is from being regular and is trivial precisely when P is regular.

More generally, a polytope is called a k-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on the set of flags, and its symmetry type is encoded by a symmetry type graph on k vertices.

Problem. Formulate an appropriate definition of a "chirality group" for an arbitrary k-orbit abstract polytope P (for every k ≥ 2 and for every admissible symmetry type graph) that:
(i) reduces to the classical chirality group when P is a two-orbit chiral polytope,
(ii) is trivial if and only if P is regular,
(iii) measures, in a functorial way, the obstruction for P to cover its maximal regular quotient,
and establish its basic structural properties (such as its relation to the mix of P with its dual/mirror images and to coverings of P by regular polytopes).
status_search_result: Recent literature on k-orbit abstract polytopes (e.g., work on automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra and characterizations of k-orbit polytopes as coset geometries) develops symmetry-type-graph machinery and partial generalizations, but no source found gives a definitive, generally accepted notion of a chirality group for arbitrary k-orbit polytopes. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Which pairs of rooted polytopes have the property that their mix is itself a polytope?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a partially ordered set P with a strictly monotone rank function whose elements (called faces) of ranks -1, 0, ..., n, n+1 satisfy the standard diamond and flag-connectedness conditions of an abstract n-polytope, with a unique minimum face F_{-1} and a unique maximum face F_n. A flag is a maximal totally ordered subset of P. A rooted polytope is a pair (P, Φ) consisting of an abstract polytope P together with a chosen base flag Φ.

For each rank i ∈ {0, 1, ..., n-1}, there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ exactly in its rank-i face; this defines, for any P-preserving structure, distinguished involutions r_0, ..., r_{n-1} acting on the flags. The connection group (monodromy group) Mon(P) of P is the group generated by these flag-changing involutions r_0, ..., r_{n-1}.

Given two rooted polytopes (P, Φ_P) and (Q, Φ_Q) of the same rank n, with connection-group generators r_0^P, ..., r_{n-1}^P and r_0^Q, ..., r_{n-1}^Q, the mix P ◇ Q is defined as the flag system generated by the diagonal involutions s_i := (r_i^P, r_i^Q) acting on Mon(P) × Mon(Q), with base flag (Φ_P, Φ_Q). The resulting structure is always a pre-polytope, but it need not be an abstract polytope (the diamond condition or flag-connectedness can fail).

Problem: Characterize all pairs of rooted polytopes ((P, Φ_P), (Q, Φ_Q)) for which the mix P ◇ Q is itself an abstract polytope.

The mix operation is studied in the abstract polytopes literature (e.g., the mix of a regular polytope with a face), but the general characterization problem appears to remain open, with only special cases (e.g., specific regular polytopes) treated.

original_question: Given a group Gamma, for which integers k >= 1 and n >= 3 is Gamma the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or maniplex of rank n?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) are graded by ranks in {-1, 0, ..., n}, satisfying the standard axioms: it has a unique minimum face and unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 faces, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any face F of rank i-1 and any face H of rank i+1 with F<H, there are exactly two faces G of rank i with F<G<H). More generally, a maniplex of rank n is a connected, n-edge-colored, n-regular graph in which, for any two distinct colors i and j with |i-j|>1, every connected component of the subgraph induced by edges of colors i and j is a 4-cycle; the vertices play the role of flags. The automorphism group Γ(M) of a polytope or maniplex M consists of the color- and incidence-preserving bijections (equivalently, automorphisms of its flag graph), and it acts freely on flags. The number of orbits of Γ(M) on flags is called the number of flag orbits; M is called a k-orbit polytope (resp. maniplex) of rank n if it has rank n and exactly k flag orbits.

Problem. Given an abstract group Γ, determine the set of pairs (k, n) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3 such that there exists a k-orbit abstract polytope (respectively, k-orbit maniplex) of rank n whose automorphism group is isomorphic to Γ.
status_search_result: The general problem appears open. Partial progress exists: characterizations of automorphism groups are known mainly for small k (regular k=1 and chiral k=2), with recent work extending tools for k=3 (e.g., 3-orbit polyhedra) and a general coset-geometry characterization of automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes. Targeted constructions prescribing automorphism groups for polytopes have been given, but a complete answer for arbitrary Γ, all k≥1 and all n≥3 has not been established.

original_question: Are there constructions of (n + 1)-polytopes from n-polytopes whose resulting symmetry type graphs differ from the families produced in Theorem 4.2 and from their duals?
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a graded poset (with elements called faces, ranked from -1 to n) satisfying the standard diamond, flag-connectedness, and strong flag-connectedness conditions of abstract polytope theory. The flag graph of an n-polytope P has the flags of P as vertices, with edges colored 0,1,...,n-1, where two flags are joined by an edge of color i whenever they differ exactly in their rank-i face. The automorphism group Γ(P) acts on flags preserving the edge coloring, and the symmetry type graph T(P) is the quotient of the flag graph by this action: its vertices are the flag-orbits of Γ(P), and edges are colored 0,...,n-1, possibly including semi-edges (loops indicating that an i-adjacent flag lies in the same orbit). The dual of a symmetry type graph is obtained by reversing the order of the colors 0,...,n-1.

Suppose one is given a family of constructions producing, from each n-polytope P, an (n+1)-polytope P′ whose facets or other structure is related to P, and suppose Theorem 4.2 (assume given) describes a fixed finite list F of possible symmetry type graphs (parametrized in n) realized by all known such constructions, together with the duals of the graphs in F.

Question: Does there exist a construction that, from some n-polytope P, produces an (n+1)-polytope P′ whose symmetry type graph T(P′) is not isomorphic (as an edge-colored graph with semi-edges) to any graph in F or to the dual of any graph in F?

original_question: Do there exist polytopes P and Q such that the amalgamation class hP, Qi is nonempty and P has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set of "faces", graded by ranks −1, 0, 1, …, n, satisfying the standard diamond and connectedness axioms of abstract polytope theory. original_question: Describe all chiral polytopes of nearly full rank.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) of ranks $-1, 0, 1, \dots, n$ satisfy the standard combinatorial axioms of an abstract polytope: it has a unique minimum face of rank $-1$ and a unique maximum face of rank $n$, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, the poset is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two faces $F < G$ with $\operatorname{rank}(G) - \operatorname{rank}(F) = 2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$).

Let $\mathcal{P}$ be such a polytope. Its automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on the set of flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on flags. It is called chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on flags such that any two adjacent flags (flags differing in exactly one face) lie in different orbits.

A faithful (geometric) realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in Euclidean $d$-space $\mathbb{E}^d$ assigns to each face of $\mathcal{P}$ a subset of $\mathbb{E}^d$, compatibly with the partial order, in such a way that the symmetry group of the realized figure is isomorphic (via the realization) to $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ and acts in the same way on flags. The realization has full rank if its ambient dimension equals $n$ when $\mathcal{P}$ is finite, or $n-1$ when $\mathcal{P}$ is infinite (an apeirotope). It is said to have nearly full rank if its ambient dimension equals $n+1$ in the finite case, or $n$ in the infinite case.

Problem. Describe (classify up to similarity) all chiral abstract polytopes and apeirotopes admitting a faithful realization of nearly full rank in Euclidean space.
status_search_result: The analogous classification for regular polytopes and apeirotopes of nearly full rank has been completed (work of McMullen and collaborators). For the chiral case, related questions have seen recent progress (e.g., chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5, established by Cunningham–Pellicer and others around 2020–2021), but a full classification of chiral polytopes of nearly full rank does not appear in the literature found, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank.
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set (with a least and a greatest face) satisfying the standard diamond condition and strong flag-connectedness, so that every flag (maximal chain) has exactly n+1 proper faces and, for each flag Φ and each i ∈ {0,1,…,n−1}, there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in its rank-i face. The automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on flags; P is called a two-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on the set of flags.

A geometric realization of an abstract polytope P of rank n is a (faithful) embedding of its faces into Euclidean space E^d (or, in the case of an apeirotope, a discrete one) such that Γ(P) is induced by Euclidean isometries. Such a realization is said to be of full rank when:
 (i) for a finite polytope, the affine hull of the realization has dimension equal to the rank n; 
 (ii) for an infinite polytope (apeirotope), the affine hull has dimension equal to n − 1.

Problem. Give a complete description (classification) of all two-orbit polytopes admitting a faithful geometric realization of full rank, in every rank n ≥ 3, listing for each rank the polytopes that occur, the class (among the 2^n − 1 possible two-orbit classes indexed by proper non-empty subsets I ⊊ {0,…,n−1}) to which each belongs, and their symmetry groups.

context_brief: Dimension bounds for convex k-orbit polytopes
original_question: Determine the number N_k for each k, or improve the known bounds on N_k, where N_k bounds the dimensions in which geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes can exist.
self_contained_problem:
A convex polytope P in Euclidean space is called geometrically k-orbit if the symmetry group G(P) (the group of Euclidean isometries preserving P) acts on the set of flags of P (where a flag is a maximal chain F_0 < F_1 < ... < F_{d-1} of nonempty proper faces of P) with exactly k orbits. For each positive integer k, define

  N_k = the smallest integer N (or +∞ if no such integer exists) such that every geometrically k-orbit convex polytope has dimension at most N,

so that geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes can exist only in dimensions d ≤ N_k (with N_k = ∞ meaning they exist in arbitrarily high dimensions).

Problem: For each integer k ≥ 1, determine the exact value of N_k, or otherwise improve the known upper and lower bounds on N_k.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of a list of open problems on k-orbit polytopes. While progress has been made on related questions about k-orbit abstract polytopes (e.g., characterizations via coset geometries), no source found determines N_k exactly for general k or substantially sharpens the bounds in the geometric (convex) setting.

context_brief: Geometric flag orbits in convex polytopes
original_question: For which values of k and d does there exist a convex d-polytope with exactly k geometric flag orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a convex d-dimensional polytope in Euclidean space, and let G(P) denote its geometric symmetry group (the group of Euclidean isometries of the ambient space that map P to itself). A flag of P is a maximal chain F_{-1} ⊂ F_0 ⊂ F_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_{d-1} ⊂ F_d = P of faces of P, where F_i has dimension i (and F_{-1} = ∅). The group G(P) acts on the set of flags of P; the orbits of this action are called the geometric flag orbits of P, and their number is denoted f(P).

Determine, for which pairs of positive integers (k, d), there exists a convex d-polytope P with exactly k geometric flag orbits, i.e. f(P) = k.
status_search_result: The cases k = 1 (regular polytopes, classified by Schläfli), k = 2 (existing only in dimensions 2 and 3, fully classified), and k = 3 (existing in dimensions 2 through 8, with full classifications in dimensions 5–8) have been resolved. The general question of which (k, d) admit a convex d-polytope with exactly k geometric flag orbits remains open for k ≥ 4.

original_question: Classify all two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space H^3.
self_contained_problem:
A polyhedron in hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ is, in the skeletal sense, a connected geometric realization $P$ of a combinatorial polyhedron (an abstract polytope of rank 3) consisting of vertices (points of $\mathbb{H}^3$), edges (geodesic segments), and faces (finite or infinite skew or planar polygons), in which every edge lies in exactly two faces and the vertex-figure at each vertex is a single (possibly skew) polygon. The symmetry group $G(P)$ is the group of isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$ that map $P$ to itself.

A flag of $P$ is an incident triple (vertex, edge, face). The group $G(P)$ acts on the set of flags of $P$, and $P$ is called a $k$-orbit polyhedron if this action has exactly $k$ orbits. The case $k = 1$ corresponds to regular polyhedra; the case $k = 2$ defines the class of two-orbit polyhedra.

Problem: Classify, up to isometry of $\mathbb{H}^3$, all two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3$.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Cunningham–Pellicer and collaborators) has classified two-orbit skeletal polyhedra in Euclidean 3-space (in classes such as 2₀ and 2₂) and chiral polyhedra in several 3-dimensional geometries, but no complete classification of two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit polytopes.
self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a graded partially ordered set P with a unique minimum and unique maximum element, whose maximal chains (called flags) all have the same length n+1, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition (for any chain missing exactly one element of an intermediate rank, there are exactly two ways to extend it to a flag). The automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the set of flags, and P is called a k-orbit polytope if this action has exactly k orbits; when k=1, P is regular.

A (geometric) realization of an abstract n-polytope P is, roughly, a mapping β from the vertex set of P into a Euclidean space (extended in a compatible way to higher-rank faces by taking convex hulls/affine images) which is compatible with the symmetry structure of P; for regular (1-orbit) polytopes, a well-developed theory of realizations exists in which the moduli space of realizations forms a convex cone, and the symmetric (regular) realizations correspond to the orthogonal representations of the automorphism group, with irreducible realizations corresponding to irreducible representations.

A "matched" or "k-orbit" realization of a k-orbit polytope should be a realization in which the symmetry of the realization (as a configuration in Euclidean space) reflects the k-orbit structure of P, i.e. the realization has exactly k flag orbits under its geometric symmetry group, matching the abstract orbit structure.

Problem. Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit abstract polytopes that extends the classical realization theory of regular abstract polytopes. In particular, define the moduli space of k-orbit (matched) realizations of a given k-orbit abstract polytope P, identify its structure (e.g. as a convex cone), describe a notion of irreducible k-orbit realizations and a decomposition of arbitrary k-orbit realizations into irreducibles, and connect these objects to the representation theory of the automorphism group Γ(P) and of the flag-stabilizer subgroups corresponding to the k flag orbits.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes published in Discrete Mathematics. While realization theory for regular (1-orbit) polytopes is well-developed (notably by McMullen and Schulte) and there has been related work on rooted polytopes and on characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes (e.g. Hubard et al., 2022), no comprehensive theory of k-orbit (matched) realizations for general k-orbit polytopes has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes.
self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) satisfy the standard combinatorial axioms of an abstract polytope: it is ranked, has unique minimum and maximum faces, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition. The automorphism group of an abstract polytope acts freely on the set of flags; the polytope is called an m-orbit polytope if this action has exactly m orbits on flags. A (geometric) realization of an abstract polytope P is a mapping β from the vertex set of P into some Euclidean space such that every automorphism of P is induced by an isometry of the ambient space; the realization extends to all faces, and the symmetry group of the realized figure acts on its flags. The realization is called a k-orbit realization if the symmetry group of the resulting geometric figure has exactly k orbits on the flags of P.

Develop a systematic theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit abstract polytopes. In particular, for given integers k and m, characterize which m-orbit abstract polytopes admit a faithful k-orbit realization in some Euclidean space, describe the structure of the cone (or space) of all such realizations, determine the possible relationships k ↔ m (including necessary divisibility or group-theoretic conditions linking the symmetry groups of realizations to the abstract automorphism group), and provide existence and classification results for the realizations whose flag-orbit count differs from the abstract flag-orbit count.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of 35 open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes published in Discrete Mathematics (Pellicer, 2018). Subsequent literature on k-orbit polytopes and realizations (e.g., work on 2-orbit and 3-orbit polyhedra, characterizations of automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes, and combining realization space models of polytopes) addresses related aspects but no comprehensive theory of k-orbit realizations of m-orbit polytopes has been established. The status appears to remain open.

original_question: Develop a theory of realizations of regular polytopes in hyperbolic spaces.
self_contained_problem:
A regular abstract polytope is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ with a strictly monotone rank function whose elements (called faces) of ranks $-1$ and $n$ are unique, such that every maximal chain (flag) has the same length, $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected, the diamond condition holds, and the automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on the flags. A realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in a metric space $X$ is a mapping $\beta$ from the set of vertices (rank-0 faces) of $\mathcal{P}$ into $X$ such that every automorphism in $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ induces an isometry of $X$ permuting the image vertices in the appropriate way, with the realization extended in the natural recursive manner to higher-rank faces. In Euclidean space, a well-developed theory exists: the cone of realizations decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible (pure) realizations indexed by the irreducible orthogonal representations of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$, and there are explicit Wythoff-style and orthogonality (cosine vector) relations.

Develop an analogous theory of realizations of regular abstract polytopes in hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n$ (and, more generally, in real, complex, or quaternionic hyperbolic spaces). Specifically:

(a) Formulate the correct notion of a (faithful, symmetric) realization of a regular polytope in hyperbolic space, accounting for the noncompact isometry group $\mathrm{O}^+(n,1)$ in place of $\mathrm{O}(n+1)$.

(b) Establish a decomposition or structure theorem for the space of all such realizations analogous to the orthogonal-representation decomposition in the Euclidean/spherical case, using the representation theory of the relevant indefinite-orthogonal or noncompact Lie groups.

(c) Identify which regular polytopes admit faithful hyperbolic realizations, characterize the pure (irreducible) hyperbolic realizations, and derive the corresponding cosine-type orthogonality relations, including criteria for when realizations are discrete.
status_search_result: The Euclidean theory of realizations of regular polytopes (McMullen and Schulte) is well-established, and there are extensive results on regular tessellations and Coxeter polytopes in hyperbolic space. However, no general theory of realizations of regular abstract polytopes in hyperbolic spaces analogous to the Euclidean case appears in the literature; the problem is an open program rather than a settled theorem.

original_question: For a metric space (X, d), it is known that if (X, d) is separable then the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is metrizable and therefore paracompact and normal. Is the converse true? Equivalently, is (2^X, T_W(d)) normal if and only if it is metrizable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let $2^X$ denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of $X$. The Wijsman topology $\tau_W(d)$ on $2^X$ is the weakest topology such that, for every $x \in X$, the distance functional
$$ d_x : 2^X \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad d_x(A) = d(x,A) := \inf_{a \in A} d(x,a), $$
is continuous.

It is known that if $(X,d)$ is separable, then $(2^X, \tau_W(d))$ is metrizable, and hence paracompact and normal.

Question: Is the converse true? That is, for an arbitrary metric space $(X,d)$, is the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \tau_W(d))$ normal if and only if it is metrizable (equivalently, if and only if $(X,d)$ is separable)?
status_search_result: The problem (originally posed by Di Maio and Meccariello, 1998) is partially solved. Cao and Junnila (2012) proved that every hereditarily normal Wijsman hyperspace is metrizable. Special cases are known: e.g., for linear metric spaces, normality of the Wijsman hyperspace is equivalent to metrizability; and if the weight of X is a regular uncountable cardinal and X is locally separable, the Wijsman hyperspace fails to be normal. The full equivalence "normal iff metrizable" for arbitrary metric spaces appears to remain open.

original_question: If (X, d) is completely metrizable, with no separability assumption, is that equivalent to some completeness-type topological property of the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d))?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space (no separability is assumed). Let $2^X$ denote the collection of all nonempty closed subsets of $X$. The Wijsman topology $\tau_W(d)$ on $2^X$ is the weakest topology such that, for every $x\in X$, the distance functional $A\mapsto d(x,A)=\inf\{d(x,a):a\in A\}$ is continuous from $2^X$ to $\mathbb{R}$.

Recall that $(X,d)$ is completely metrizable means that there exists a metric $d'$ on $X$, equivalent to $d$ (i.e., generating the same topology), such that $(X,d')$ is a complete metric space. Standard "completeness-type" topological properties include Čech-completeness, hereditary Baireness, complete metrizability, sieve completeness, partition completeness, and similar properties.

Question: Does there exist a completeness-type topological property $\mathcal{P}$ of topological spaces such that, for every metric space $(X,d)$ (without any separability hypothesis), $(X,d)$ is completely metrizable if and only if the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X,\tau_W(d))$ has property $\mathcal{P}$?
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Search results show that for non-separable complete metric spaces the Wijsman hyperspace can fail standard completeness-type properties (e.g., it need not be Čech-complete), and that the Wijsman hyperspace is metrizable iff X is separable. No source found announcing a characterization of complete metrizability of (X,d) (without separability) via a topological completeness property of (2^X, τ_W(d)).

original_question: Let X be a metrizable space. If, for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable, must X itself be completely metrizable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a metrizable topological space. For a metric $d$ on $X$ compatible with its topology, let $2^X$ denote the collection of all nonempty closed subsets of $X$, and let $\mathcal{T}_W(d)$ denote the Wijsman topology on $2^X$, i.e., the weakest topology on $2^X$ making the distance functional $A \mapsto d(x,A) := \inf\{d(x,a) : a \in A\}$ continuous for every $x \in X$.

Recall the strong Choquet game on a topological space $Y$: players I and II alternate moves; in round $n$, player I picks a pair $(x_n, U_n)$ with $x_n \in U_n$ and $U_n$ open (and $U_n \subseteq V_{n-1}$), and player II responds with an open set $V_n$ with $x_n \in V_n \subseteq U_n$. Player II wins if $\bigcap_n V_n = \bigcap_n U_n \neq \emptyset$. The space $Y$ is called strongly Choquet if II has a winning strategy, and strongly $\alpha$-favorable if II has a stationary winning strategy (depending only on the previous move of I).

Question: Suppose that for every metric $d$ on $X$ compatible with the topology of $X$, the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \mathcal{T}_W(d))$ is strongly Choquet (respectively, strongly $\alpha$-favorable). Must $X$ be completely metrizable?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about converses in the relationship between completeness properties of a metrizable space and game-theoretic completeness of all its Wijsman hyperspaces. The known forward direction (complete metrizability implies strong $\alpha$-favorability of every Wijsman hyperspace) is established in the literature (Zsilinszky and others), but no published resolution of the converse for arbitrary metrizable $X$ was found in the search; results are available only in the locally separable case.

original_question: Given a metric space (X, d), characterize when the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space, using properties of the underlying metric space (X, d).
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $2^X$ denote the collection of all nonempty closed subsets of $X$. The Wijsman topology $\tau_W(d)$ on $2^X$ is the weakest topology for which, for each fixed $x \in X$, the distance functional
$$d_x : 2^X \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad d_x(A) = \inf\{d(x,a) : a \in A\}$$
is continuous. Recall that a topological space is a Baire space if the intersection of every countable family of dense open sets is dense (equivalently, no nonempty open set is of the first category).

Problem: Find a characterization, expressed purely in terms of properties of $(X,d)$, of those metric spaces $(X,d)$ for which the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \tau_W(d))$ is a Baire space.
status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Baireness of the Wijsman hyperspace in terms of properties of the underlying metric space (X,d) appears to remain open. Partial results are known: completeness of (X,d) implies Baireness of the Wijsman hyperspace; Zsilinszky and others gave characterizations under additional assumptions (e.g., metrizable base with a countable-in-itself π-base); and Pol–Zsilinszky exhibited a first-category metric space whose Wijsman hyperspace is Baire. Whether the Wijsman hyperspace of every metric Baire space is Baire is still an open question, and no full characterization has been found.

original_question: If (X, d) is a Baire metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space. The Wijsman topology $\tau_{W(d)}$ on the hyperspace $2^X$ of all nonempty closed subsets of $X$ is the weakest topology for which, for each $x\in X$, the distance functional
$$d_x:2^X\to\mathbb{R},\qquad d_x(A)=d(x,A)=\inf_{a\in A}d(x,a),$$
is continuous. A topological space is called a Baire space if the intersection of any countable family of dense open subsets is dense (equivalently, every nonempty open set is of second category).

Question: Suppose that $(X,d)$ is a metric space such that the underlying topological space is Baire. Must the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X,\tau_{W(d)})$ then also be a Baire space?
status_search_result: The problem of whether the Wijsman hyperspace of an arbitrary Baire metric space must be Baire is reported as open. Partial results are known: the Wijsman hyperspace is Baire when X is completely metrizable, has a dense completely metrizable subspace, is almost locally separable Baire, or is hereditarily Baire (Cao–Tomita). Chaber and Pol showed it may fail to be hereditarily Baire even for complete X. No general resolution has been located.

continuous. Recall that a topological space is a Baire space if the intersection of every countable family of dense open sets is dense.

original_question: Let F be the abelian group of algebraic functions with the Fermat property. Let D be the subgroup generated by logarithmic derivatives U^(partial)(x) = xU'(x) of algebraic functions U(x), let Z[x] be the polynomial subgroup, and let P be the subgroup generated by finite sums of power-substituted algebraic functions U_j(x^{M_j}) with M_j >= 2. For an algebraic function U over Q(x) that is unramified at x = 0, let F_U = F intersect Q(x, U), D_U = D intersect Q(x, U), and P_U = P intersect Q(x, U). Determine the structure of the quotient groups F/(D + Z[x] + P), A_U = F_U/(D_U + Z[x]), and P_U = F_U/(D_U + Z[x] + P_U). In particular, determine the corresponding quotient in the purely rational case Q(x).
self_contained_problem:
Consider algebraic functions over $\mathbb{Q}(x)$ that are unramified at $x=0$ and analytic there, expanded as power series $U(x)=\sum_{n\ge 0} a(n)x^n$. Say that such a $U$ has the "Fermat property" if its coefficient sequence $a(n)$ satisfies a Fermat-type congruence (specifically, $a(p^k) \equiv a(p^{k-1}) \pmod{p^k}$ for every prime $p$ and every integer $k\ge 1$, for almost all primes $p$). Let $F$ denote the abelian group, under addition, of all such algebraic functions with the Fermat property whose power-series coefficients lie in $\mathbb{Z}$.

Inside $F$, define three subgroups:
1. $D$, the subgroup generated by all logarithmic derivatives $U^{\partial}(x) := xU'(x)$ where $U$ ranges over algebraic functions in $F$;
2. $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, the subgroup of polynomials with integer coefficients;
3. $P$, the subgroup generated by finite sums $\sum_{j=1}^{s} U_j(x^{M_j})$ where each $U_j \in F$ and each integer $M_j\ge 2$.

For an algebraic function $U$ over $\mathbb{Q}(x)$ unramified at $0$, set
$$F_U = F\cap \mathbb{Q}(x,U),\quad D_U = D\cap \mathbb{Q}(x,U),\quad P_U = P\cap \mathbb{Q}(x,U).$$

Determine the structure of the abelian quotient groups
$$F/(D+\mathbb{Z}[x]+P),\qquad A_U = F_U/(D_U+\mathbb{Z}[x]),\qquad \mathcal{P}_U = F_U/(D_U+\mathbb{Z}[x]+P_U).$$
In particular, determine $\mathcal{P}_\varnothing$, i.e.\ the quotient corresponding to the purely rational case where the ambient field is $\mathbb{Q}(x)$.
status_search_result: No published resolution of this structural problem on quotients of the group of Fermat-property algebraic functions modulo logarithmic derivatives, integer polynomials, and power-substitution subgroups was located. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Let lambda_n(s) be the canonically indexed eigenvalues of the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator for the Gauss continued-fraction map, indexed so that the labeling by n is canonical and corresponds to ordering by magnitude. For each nontrivial zero rho of the Riemann zeta function, let t(rho) be the integer M such that lambda_M(rho/2) = 1. Given a fixed integer M in N, determine what can be said about the set t^(-1)(M): whether it is infinite, how the conjectural distribution of Riemann zeros changes when restricted to that set, and how one can compute sets such as t^(-1)(1) effectively.
self_contained_problem:
Let T:[0,1]\to[0,1] be the Gauss continued-fraction map T(x)=1/x-\lfloor 1/x\rfloor (with T(0)=0). For a complex parameter s with \mathrm{Re}\,s>1/2, the Mayer–Ruelle transfer operator \mathcal{L}_s is defined on a suitable Banach space of holomorphic functions on a disk containing [0,1] by
\[
(\mathcal{L}_s f)(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(k+z)^{2s}}\, f\!\left(\frac{1}{k+z}\right).
\]
For each such s, \mathcal{L}_s is nuclear and has a discrete spectrum of eigenvalues which can be canonically indexed as a sequence \{\lambda_n(s)\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} (for instance, in non-increasing order of magnitude, with the canonical labeling extended analytically in s).

It is known that for every nontrivial zero \rho of the Riemann zeta function \zeta there exists a unique positive integer M=t(\rho)\in\mathbb{N} such that
\[
\lambda_{M}\!\left(\tfrac{\rho}{2}\right)=1.
\]
This defines a map t from the set of nontrivial zeros of \zeta to \mathbb{N}.

Fix M\in\mathbb{N}. Address the following:

(a) Is the fiber t^{-1}(M)=\{\rho:\zeta(\rho)=0,\ 0<\mathrm{Re}\,\rho<1,\ t(\rho)=M\} infinite?

(b) Assuming the Riemann hypothesis and the standard conjectural distribution of nontrivial zeros (e.g.\ the Montgomery pair-correlation / GUE distribution of normalized spacings), how does the distribution of zeros change when one restricts to the subset t^{-1}(M)?

(c) Provide an effective procedure to compute the set t^{-1}(1) (the nontrivial zeros \rho for which \rho/2 is a parameter at which the largest canonical eigenvalue of \mathcal{L}_s equals 1).
status_search_result: The relationship between zeros of 1-\lambda_n(s) for the Mayer transfer operator and the nontrivial zeros of \zeta is established (Mayer; Lewis–Zagier; recent asymptotic results), but no published work resolves the fiber structure of the index map t, the conditional distribution of zeros within fibers t^{-1}(M), or gives an effective algorithm for t^{-1}(1). The question appears to remain open.

original_question: An uphill lattice path is a doubly infinite monotone path in R^2 made of unit steps from (a, b) to either (a, b + 1) or (a + 1, b), and a downhill lattice path is defined similarly with b - 1 in place of b + 1. For a finite set P of points in Z^2, call such a monotone lattice path friendly if the number of points of P on one side of the path equals the number on the other side, ignoring points that lie on the path itself. Is it true that every odd-sized finite set of lattice points has a friendly path?
self_contained_problem:
Define an uphill lattice path in $\mathbb{R}^2$ to be the union of a doubly infinite sequence of unit directed line segments, each going from some integer point $(a,b)\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ to either $(a,b+1)$ or $(a+1,b)$. Define a downhill lattice path in the same way, but with steps from $(a,b)$ to either $(a,b-1)$ or $(a+1,b)$. A monotone lattice path is an uphill or downhill lattice path. Such a path divides $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus(\text{path})$ into two open connected components ("sides"). 

Given a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$, a monotone lattice path is called friendly for $P$ if the number of points of $P$ lying strictly on one side of the path equals the number of points of $P$ strictly on the other side (points of $P$ that lie on the path are not counted on either side).

Question: Is it true that for every finite set $P\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$ of odd cardinality, there exists a friendly monotone lattice path?
status_search_result: The question is answered in the negative. Alkauskas (arXiv:2302.01137, "Friendly paths for finite subsets of plane integer lattice. I") exhibits inseparable odd-sized configurations: for odd $n\le 41$, the unique inseparable set (up to symmetry) has $n=27$, and further odd inseparable sizes such as $n=43,45$ also occur. Hence not every odd-sized finite set has a friendly monotone lattice path.

context_brief: Moments of the Minkowski question mark function
original_question: Let ?(x) be the Minkowski question mark function on [0, 1], defined by ?([0, a_1, a_2, a_3, ...]) = 2^(1-a_1) - 2^(1-(a_1+a_2)) + 2^(1-(a_1+a_2+a_3)) - ... for the regular continued-fraction expansion x = [0, a_1, a_2, ...]. Define rational functions Q_n(z) = B_n(z)z^(-n-1) by Q_0(z) = -1/(2z) and Q_n(z) = (1/2) sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (1/j!) (d^j/dz^j Q_{n-j-1}(-1)) (z^j - 1/z^(j+2)). Is it true that Lambda(t) = sum_{n>=0} Q_n'(-1)t^n/n! is an entire function and that int_0^infty Lambda(t)e^(-t) dt = int_0^1 x^2 d?(x)?
self_contained_problem:
Let ?(x) denote the Minkowski question mark function on [0,1], defined for x = [0; a_1, a_2, a_3, ...] (regular continued fraction expansion, a_i ∈ ℕ) by

Define a sequence of rational functions Q_n(z), n ≥ 0, recursively by
   Q_0(z) = −1/(2z),
   Q_n(z) = (1/2) ∑_{j=0}^{n−1} (1/j!) · [ (d^j/dz^j Q_{n−j−1})(−1) ] · ( z^j − 1/z^{j+2} ),  n ≥ 1.
Form the formal power series
   Λ(t) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ ( Q_n'(−1) / n! ) · t^n .
Prove or disprove the following statement: Λ(t) extends to an entire function of t ∈ ℂ, and
   ∫_0^∞ Λ(t) e^{−t} dt = ∫_0^1 x^2 d?(x) .

context_brief: Moment representation for Stern sequence growth
original_question: Let a(n) be Stern's diatomic sequence, defined by a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1, a(2n) = a(n), and a(2n + 1) = a(n) + a(n + 1). For L in N_0, define Q^(L)(N) = sum_{n=2^N+1}^{2^(N+1)} a(n)^L. Proposition 1 states that there is a unique algebraic number mu_L and a constant c_L such that Q^(L)(N)/2^N is asymptotic to c_L mu_L^N. Does there exist a function p(x) - analytic, continuous of bounded variation, or more generally a distribution - such that int_0^((1+sqrt(5))/2) x^L dp(x) = mu_L for every L >= 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $a(n)$ denote Stern's diatomic sequence, defined by
$$a(0)=0,\quad a(1)=1,\quad a(2n)=a(n),\quad a(2n+1)=a(n)+a(n+1)\ \text{for } n\ge 1.$$
For each integer $L\ge 0$ and each integer $N\ge 0$, define the moment
$$Q^{(L)}(N)=\sum_{n=2^N+1}^{2^{N+1}} a(n)^L.$$
It is known that for each fixed $L$, the sequence $\{Q^{(L)}(N)\}_{N\ge 0}$ satisfies a linear recurrence of degree $L$, and there exists a unique algebraic number $\mu_L$ (which is half of an algebraic integer) and a constant $c_L>0$ such that
$$\frac{Q^{(L)}(N)}{2^N}\sim c_L\,\mu_L^{N}\quad\text{as } N\to\infty.$$
One has $\mu_L\in[1,\varphi]$ where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt 5)/2$, with $\mu_0=1$ and $\mu_L\to\varphi$ as $L\to\infty$.

Question: Does there exist a function (or distribution) $p$ on the interval $[0,\varphi]$ — for instance analytic, or continuous of bounded variation, or more generally a Schwartz distribution — such that
$$\int_0^{\varphi} x^{L}\,dp(x) = \mu_L \qquad\text{for every integer } L\ge 0\,?$$
If so, identify and characterize such a representing function or distribution.
status_search_result: A direct web search for a moment-representation result for the algebraic numbers $\mu_L$ associated with the Stern sequence on $[0,\varphi]$ did not return any source establishing or refuting the existence of such a representing function or distribution. The general literature on Stern's diatomic sequence discusses its asymptotic order in terms of $\varphi$, but no specific resolution of this moment problem was located.

Consider the tree-level gravi-dilaton effective action in $D = d+1$ spacetime dimensions with NS-NS sector fields, namely the metric $g_{\mu
u}$, the dilaton $\phi$, and the antisymmetric Kalb–Ramond two-form $B_{\mu
u}$ with field strength $H_{\mu
uho}=3\,\partial_{[\mu}B_{
uho]}$:
$$S=-	frac{1}{2\lambda_s^{D-2}}\int d^{D}x\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\Big(R+(
abla\phi)^2-	frac{1}{12}H_{\mu
uho}H^{\mu

ignoring all $\alpha'$ (higher-derivative) and string-loop corrections. Restrict attention to spatially homogeneous cosmologies, in which one may take a Bianchi-type metric
$$ds^{2}=-dt^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}a_{i}(t)^{2}(dx^{i})^{2},$$

• Axion (rolling-axion) solutions where the pseudoscalar $\sigma$ is non-trivial.

Problem. (a) Carry out a complete asymptotic analysis of the autonomous dynamical system arising from the above tree-level NS-NS cosmological equations: classify all possible asymptotic regimes (as $t	o 0^{\pm}$ and $t	o\pm\infty$, including pre-/post-big-bang branches) of homogeneous solutions, identifying the limiting behaviour of $(H_i,\dot\phi,\dot\sigma)$ and of suitable scale-invariant variables.

(b) Determine whether the dilaton–moduli–vacuum solutions and the axion solutions are asymptotically stable as critical points (or invariant sets) of this dynamical system, i.e. decide for each such solution whether nearby trajectories converge to it in the relevant asymptotic limit, and characterise its basin of attraction.
status_search_result: No specific source was found that provides a complete asymptotic classification together with a full asymptotic-stability analysis of the dilaton-moduli-vacuum and axion tree-level NS-NS cosmological solutions in this generality. Partial results on individual exact solutions and pre-/post-big-bang branches are well known, but the comprehensive program described appears not to be fully resolved; status is therefore taken as unknown.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: When anisotropies are added to tree-level string cosmologies with NS-NS fields, RR fields, or both, what asymptotic regimes occur in simple anisotropic models, which asymptotic decompositions and cancellations are possible, and can one identify lower-parameter attractor solutions that organize the full solution space of these string cosmologies?
self_contained_problem:
Consider tree-level low-energy effective string actions in D spacetime dimensions of the form
  S = ∫ d^D x √(-g) e^{-φ} ( R + (∇φ)^2 - (1/12) H_{μνρ} H^{μνρ} ) + S_RR ,
where φ is the dilaton, H = dB is the field strength of the NS-NS two-form B, and S_RR denotes contributions from Ramond-Ramond p-form field strengths F_{(p+1)}, included individually or in combination with H. Restrict to spatially homogeneous, anisotropic cosmologies of Bianchi type I, with metric
  ds^2 = -dt^2 + Σ_{i=1}^{D-1} a_i(t)^2 (dx^i)^2 ,
and with φ = φ(t), and with B and F_{(p+1)} compatible with the homogeneity (so their components depend only on t).

Introduce expansion-normalized variables (Hubble rates H_i = ȧ_i/a_i, the shear σ_{ij}, the dilaton velocity, and the appropriately rescaled NS-NS and RR field strengths) so as to recast the field equations as an autonomous polynomial dynamical system on a finite-dimensional state space, and study its asymptotic behavior as t → ±∞ (or as the system approaches a singular boundary).

Address the following:

1. Classify all asymptotic regimes (equilibrium points, heteroclinic chains, and invariant boundary subsets) of this dynamical system in the cases (a) only NS-NS fields are excited, (b) only RR fields are excited, and (c) both NS-NS and RR fields are excited.

2. Determine all decompositions of the asymptotic vector field into dominant balances, and identify which "asymptotic cancellations" — situations where leading-order terms cancel forcing one to subleading orders — actually occur.

3. Identify lower-parameter attractor solutions: solutions depending on strictly fewer than the maximal number of arbitrary constants that nevertheless attract open families of full-parameter solutions in the asymptotic limit, and describe their basins of attraction.

Provide a complete answer for the simplest nontrivial anisotropic models (e.g. Bianchi I in D = 4 and D = 10 with one or two excited form fields).
status_search_result: A literature search shows partial results for restricted cases: NS-NS-only anisotropic Bianchi-I cosmologies with dilaton and B-field have known attractor and pre-Big-Bang solutions, and some D-brane / RR-driven anisotropic models have been analyzed. However, a complete classification of asymptotic regimes, dominant-balance decompositions, asymptotic cancellations, and lower-parameter attractors covering combined NS-NS + RR anisotropic tree-level string cosmologies has not been established. The full problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: Are the cosmological solutions in M-theory that are associated with a BPS state stable under the inhomogeneous perturbations required by such solutions, and how does that stability affect their possible role in the ambient cosmological construction?
self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory) and its time-dependent (cosmological) solutions of the equations of motion that are associated with a BPS state, i.e. solutions preserving a fraction of the supersymmetry of the underlying theory. Such cosmological backgrounds are generically required to be spatially inhomogeneous in order to be compatible with the BPS condition.

Determine whether these BPS-associated cosmological solutions of M-theory are stable under the inhomogeneous metric and matter perturbations that are intrinsically required by the BPS structure of the solutions. More precisely:

(a) Formulate a precise notion of linear (and, where possible, nonlinear) stability for a BPS cosmological background of eleven-dimensional supergravity under inhomogeneous perturbations consistent with the BPS data.

(b) For each such BPS cosmological solution, decide whether it is stable, marginally stable, or unstable in the sense of (a).

(c) Analyze how the resulting stability or instability constrains the role that such BPS cosmological solutions can play as building blocks of a larger (ambient) cosmological construction, e.g. as asymptotic regimes or as components glued into a global cosmological spacetime.
status_search_result: No specific subsequent work was located that conclusively settles the stability of BPS-associated inhomogeneous cosmological solutions of M-theory in full generality. Partial results exist on stability of particular supersymmetric/BPS backgrounds and of M-theory cosmologies in special limits, but a general resolution does not appear to be in the literature, so the status is taken as unknown.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For flat or curved Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universes governed by the full first-order corrected string action with the dilaton term and its coupling to higher-order curvature terms included, what are the relevant asymptotic regimes and stability properties, especially for the vacuum solutions of this effective string theory?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a $(d+1)$-dimensional gravi-dilaton effective string action including first-order $\alpha'$ corrections,
$$S=\frac{1}{2\kappa^2}\int d^{d+1}x\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\Big[R+(\nabla\phi)^2+\tfrac{\alpha'}{4}\big(R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}+c_1(\nabla\phi)^4+c_2 R(\nabla\phi)^2+\dots\big)\Big],$$
where $\phi$ is the dilaton and the bracketed $\alpha'$ correction includes higher-order curvature terms together with their dilaton couplings (taken in a duality-preserving scheme such as Hohm–Zwiebach). Specialize to a homogeneous, isotropic FRW ansatz
$$ds^2=-dt^2+a(t)^2\,d\Sigma_k^2,\qquad \phi=\phi(t),$$
where $d\Sigma_k^2$ is the spatial metric of constant curvature $k\in\{-1,0,+1\}$, and let $H=\dot a/a$.

Problem. Carry out a complete asymptotic analysis of the resulting autonomous system for $(H,\dot\phi)$ (and its curved-space counterpart for $k\ne0$):
(a) Classify all critical points and asymptotic regimes (early-time and late-time) of the cosmological equations of motion derived from the full $\alpha'$-corrected action including the dilaton terms and their couplings to the higher-curvature terms.
(b) Determine the local and global stability properties of these regimes, in particular establishing the linear and nonlinear stability of the vacuum (trivial flat-space, linear-dilaton) solutions of the effective theory.
(c) Identify whether the inclusion of the $\alpha'$ dilaton couplings alters the attractor structure and the singularity/de Sitter behavior compared to the action without them.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since 2016: works using the Hohm–Zwiebach O(d,d)-covariant formulation construct non-singular gravi-dilaton FRW solutions to all orders in α′ (Hohm–Zwiebach 2019, JHEP 1909.00830) and provide explicit stability analyses of de Sitter and other fixed points (Krishnan et al., "α′-cosmology: solutions and stability analysis," JHEP 2020, arXiv:2002.09856; Bernardo–Chen–Brandenberger 2308.16076). These cover the flat FRW case at first order in α′ with dilaton couplings included, but a complete classification of all asymptotic regimes and full nonlinear vacuum-stability results, especially for curved (k≠0) FRW, is not fully settled in the literature, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
context_brief: Interacting fluids in flat string cosmology
original_question: How do the known single-fluid asymptotic results for flat string cosmologies change when the matter sector is replaced by two interacting, fairly general fluids that exchange energy, and which conclusions about the physical viability of string cosmology survive in that more general interacting setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a spatially flat Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker string cosmology in the string frame, governed by the tree-level (lowest-order in α′) effective equations of motion derived from the dilaton-gravity action

  S = ∫ d^(n+1)x √(-g) e^(-φ) [ R + (∂φ)^2 - 2 Λ ] + S_matter,

with scale factor a(t), shifted dilaton φ̄ = φ - n ln a, and matter sector consisting of two perfect fluids labelled i = 1, 2 with energy densities ρ_i, pressures p_i = w_i ρ_i (with constants w_i, or more generally barotropic equations of state), interacting via an energy-exchange term Q(t):

  ρ̇_1 + n H (ρ_1 + p_1) = -Q,
  ρ̇_2 + n H (ρ_2 + p_2) = +Q,

coupled to the string-frame field equations
  n(n-1) H^2 - 2 n H φ̄˙ + φ̄˙^2 - 2 Λ = 2 e^φ̄ (ρ_1 + ρ_2),
  (other dilaton-gravity equations as derived from S),
where H = ȧ/a.

(a) Determine the asymptotic behaviour (as t → ±∞ or as one approaches a curvature/dilaton singularity) of the solutions (a(t), φ(t), ρ_1(t), ρ_2(t)) in the pre-big-bang and post-big-bang branches, generalising the known single-fluid asymptotic results to this two-fluid interacting setting, for a representative class of interaction terms Q (e.g. Q = α H ρ_1 + β H ρ_2, or Q proportional to ρ̇_total, with α, β real constants).

(b) Identify which qualitative conclusions established in the single-fluid case—such as the existence of a graceful exit from the pre- to post-big-bang phase, avoidance or persistence of curvature/dilaton singularities, scale-factor duality behaviour, and stability of attractor solutions—remain valid when the matter sector is replaced by two interacting fluids exchanging energy.

State precisely the asymptotic regimes (fixed points, scaling solutions, late- and early-time limits) and prove which of the single-fluid viability features survive in the interacting two-fluid generalisation.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this two-interacting-fluid generalisation of flat string cosmology asymptotics could be verified. The question is posed as a research project whose status is not clearly settled in the accessible literature.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: When the M-theory action is deformed by higher-order Lovelock and Weyl corrections, are the resulting exact 11-dimensional supergravity cosmological solutions stable, what asymptotic modes do their fields admit, and can this analysis establish a no-hair theorem for an inflationary stage in M-theory?
self_contained_problem:
Consider 11-dimensional supergravity, whose bosonic field content consists of a Lorentzian metric $g_{MN}$ on an 11-dimensional manifold and a 3-form gauge potential $A_{MNP}$ with 4-form field strength $F=dA$, governed by the leading-order action
$$S_0=\frac{1}{2\kappa^2}\int d^{11}x\sqrt{-g}\Big(R-\tfrac{1}{2\cdot 4!}F_{MNPQ}F^{MNPQ}\Big)-\frac{1}{12\kappa^2}\int A\wedge F\wedge F.$$
Deform this action by adding higher-curvature corrections of Lovelock type (polynomial scalars built from the Riemann tensor with second-order equations of motion, e.g.\ the Gauss--Bonnet density $\mathcal{L}_{GB}=R^2-4R_{MN}R^{MN}+R_{MNPQ}R^{MNPQ}$ and higher Lovelock densities) together with Weyl-tensor corrections (scalars polynomial in the Weyl tensor $C_{MNPQ}$ such as $C_{MNPQ}C^{MNPQ}$ and contractions of higher powers thereof), giving a corrected action
$$S=S_0+\sum_{k\ge 2}\alpha_k\int d^{11}x\sqrt{-g}\,\mathcal{L}_k(\mathrm{Riem},C),$$
with small coupling constants $\alpha_k$.

Let $(g^{(0)},F^{(0)})$ denote an exact cosmological solution of the corrected equations of motion arising from such an action, with a spatially homogeneous (e.g.\ Bianchi-type or FLRW-like) ansatz on an $(1+10)$-dimensional product or warped geometry, possibly with a portion of the spatial directions compactified.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether such a cosmological solution is linearly stable under arbitrary smooth perturbations $(\delta g_{MN},\delta A_{MNP})$ of the metric and gauge field, by analyzing the spectrum of the linearized equations of motion derived from $S$.

(b) Classify all asymptotic modes (in cosmic time and in any compactified spatial directions) that the perturbations $(\delta g_{MN},\delta A_{MNP})$ can admit, distinguishing growing, decaying, and oscillatory behaviors.

(c) Using this analysis, decide whether a no-hair theorem holds for an inflationary stage of these corrected 11-dimensional supergravity cosmologies: namely, whether every sufficiently regular perturbation of an inflating background decays (in appropriate norms) so that the late-time geometry approaches the inflationary attractor independently of initial data.
status_search_result: No definitive resolution was found. The question is posed as an open research project on stability of 11-dimensional supergravity cosmologies under higher-order Lovelock and Weyl corrections, including a possible no-hair theorem for M-theory inflation. While related partial studies exist on higher-curvature corrections to M-theory and on no-hair theorems in higher-dimensional or string cosmology, no source establishes a complete stability analysis or no-hair theorem in this exact setting.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For a three-dimensional Robertson-Walker brane coupled to a scalar field in a five-dimensional bulk, do regular asymptotic solutions exist, and if so can they support the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant while accounting for the role of curvature and the comparison with the Minkowski-brane case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a five-dimensional bulk spacetime containing a three-dimensional Robertson–Walker brane coupled to a bulk scalar field φ. The bulk metric is taken to be of warped form
  ds² = a(Y)² [ -dt² + R(t)² γ_{ij}(k) dx^i dx^j ] + dY²,
where Y is the extra (transverse) coordinate, a(Y) is the warp factor, R(t) is the Robertson–Walker scale factor on the brane, and γ_{ij}(k) is the metric of a maximally symmetric 3-space of spatial curvature k ∈ {-1,0,+1}. The scalar field φ = φ(Y) depends only on the transverse coordinate, with bulk action
  S_bulk = ∫ d⁵x √(-g) [ (1/2κ²) R₅ - (1/2)(∂φ)² - V(φ) ],
together with a brane action localized on the 3-brane and a brane tension/potential.

The resulting Einstein–scalar equations form an autonomous system of ODEs in Y (after substitution of the Robertson–Walker ansatz on the brane). Apply the method of asymptotic splittings: decompose the dominant balances of the system, classify all possible asymptotic behaviors of (a, φ) as Y approaches a finite or infinite value, and determine which dominant balances correspond to formal Puiseux/Fuchsian series solutions that are regular (free of curvature and scalar-field singularities) on the brane.

Question: 
(a) For which choices of bulk potential V(φ), brane potential, and spatial curvature k do globally regular asymptotic solutions (regular bulk warp factor a(Y) and regular scalar profile φ(Y), with finite curvature invariants) exist for the coupled brane–bulk system?
(b) Among such regular asymptotic solutions, do any realize the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant, in the sense that the induced four-dimensional cosmological constant on the brane vanishes (or is dynamically driven to zero) without fine-tuning of the brane tension?
(c) How does the role of the spatial curvature k modify the existence and stability of these regular self-tuning solutions, in comparison with the analogous Minkowski-brane case (k=0 with R(t)=const)?
status_search_result: Self-tuning of the 4D cosmological constant in 5D brane-world setups with bulk scalar fields remains an active area of research. Recent works (e.g., 2017 holographic self-tuning, 2020 bulk-black-hole self-tuning, 2022 P(X,φ) brane-world self-tuning, and 2024 contributions) propose partial mechanisms but a general classification of regular asymptotic Robertson–Walker brane solutions and a fully successful, generic self-tuning resolution of the cosmological constant problem (especially with brane curvature k ≠ 0) has not been established. The problem is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: In string theories with higher-order corrections relevant to ekpyrotic or cyclic cosmology, does the compactified Milne mod Z2 × R3 space that models the reversal phase emerge asymptotically as a stable attractor when the higher-order terms are asymptotically subdominant and the matter content is a fluid with a general equation of state?
self_contained_problem:
Consider higher-order (curvature-corrected) gravitational theories in four spacetime dimensions whose action consists of the Einstein–Hilbert term together with higher-order curvature invariants (for example, terms quadratic or of higher order in the Riemann/Ricci tensors and the Ricci scalar), coupled to a perfect-fluid matter source with a general barotropic equation of state p = wρ, w ∈ ℝ. Assume that the higher-order curvature contributions are asymptotically subdominant relative to the Einstein–Hilbert term in the regime under study.

Within this class of theories, consider the model spacetime "compactified Milne mod ℤ₂ × ℝ³", i.e. the product of three-dimensional flat Euclidean space ℝ³ with the quotient of two-dimensional Milne space (the Lorentzian cone ds² = −dt² + t² dy², t > 0) by a ℤ₂ identification together with a compactification of the y-direction; this geometry is the candidate description of the reversal/bounce phase in ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmological scenarios.

Question: Determine whether the compactified Milne mod ℤ₂ × ℝ³ spacetime emerges as a global asymptotic attractor of the cosmological dynamical system associated with such higher-order gravity theories sourced by a fluid with a general equation of state. That is, prove or disprove that, for generic initial data within an open set of cosmological solutions and for all admissible values of w, the trajectories of the field equations converge asymptotically to this Milne-type state, and characterize the range of w (if any) for which this stability holds.
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published proof or disproof establishing the compactified Milne mod ℤ₂ × ℝ³ state as a global asymptotic attractor of higher-order gravity dynamics with a general-equation-of-state fluid. Related works treat stability of ekpyrotic contracting phases and modified-gravity cyclic models, but the specific global asymptotic stability question for the Milne reversal state with subdominant higher-order corrections appears not to be settled in the literature available.
