paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
context_brief: Routing convergence disruption in UAS networks
original_question: Can adversaries feasibly prevent or slow routing convergence in UAS networks by combining topological perturbation, jamming or adaptive-formation exploitation, and manipulation of node geographical-position knowledge, and what countermeasures can protect convergence in hostile airborne-network environments?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a mobile airborne network modeled as a time-varying graph G(t) = (V, E(t)), where V is a set of unmanned aerial nodes whose positions p_v(t) ∈ R^3 evolve under an adaptive formation-control law, and E(t) is determined by a communication range and channel availability. Each node v maintains an estimate of the geographical positions {p̂_u(t)}_{u∈V} used by a position-based routing protocol R that converges (in the absence of attacks) to a stable forwarding configuration after a finite time T_conv.

Suppose an adversary may, within bounded resources, simultaneously perform any combination of the following actions:
(i) topological perturbation — forcing or removing a bounded number of edges in E(t) per time unit,
(ii) jamming — denying communication on a bounded subset of links or frequencies,
(iii) formation exploitation — injecting control-input perturbations of bounded magnitude that drive the formation-control dynamics so as to alter G(t),
(iv) position manipulation — corrupting the position estimates p̂_u(t) at a bounded number of nodes by bounded offsets.

Address the following:

1. Establish necessary and sufficient conditions on the adversary's resource bounds under which there exists an attack strategy that prevents the routing protocol R from converging, or forces its convergence time to exceed any prescribed threshold T* with high probability.

2. Construct, when feasible, an explicit such adversarial strategy combining (i)–(iv), and characterize its computational complexity.

3. Design a routing/defense mechanism R' (e.g., based on robust position verification, redundant topology maintenance, or anti-jamming coding) and prove quantitative guarantees on the convergence time of R' under the same adversarial model, identifying the largest adversary budget that R' can tolerate.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research problem on convergence attacks against routing in unmanned airborne networks. No published source was found that provides a complete formal feasibility characterization together with provably resilient countermeasures matching the combined adversary model (topology + jamming + formation exploitation + position manipulation). The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
context_brief: Intrinsic meaning of the corrected form-to-section map
original_question: What is the geometric meaning of the construction that sends a smooth differential k-form on a Riemannian manifold, together with the Levi-Civita connection, to two global sections J+ and J− of the chiral de Rham complex using local expressions built from the inverse metric, Christoffel symbols, Bessel-polynomial coefficients, ∂γ terms, and the local generators e_i^±? Equivalently, can the corrected normally ordered formula that glues local expressions into global chiral-de Rham sections be characterized by a more intrinsic geometric construction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold with Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ and Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$, and let $\Omega^{ch}_M$ denote the chiral de Rham complex of $M$ (the sheaf of vertex superalgebras locally generated, on a coordinate chart $U$ with coordinates $x^i$, by even fields $\gamma^i, a_i$ and odd fields $b_i, c^i$ subject to the standard OPE relations of the $bc$–$\beta\gamma$ system). On a chart $U$ introduce the local odd generators
$$e_i^{\pm} \;=\; b_i \;\pm\; g_{ij}\,c^j .$$
For a smooth $k$-form $\omega \in C^\infty(M,\Lambda^k T^*M)$ written locally as $\omega = \sum \omega_{i_1\dots i_k}\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$, define two local sections by the normally ordered expressions
$$J^{\pm}(\omega) \;=\; \sum \omega_{i_1\dots i_k}\bigl(\gamma\bigr)\,:\!e_{i_1}^{\pm}\cdots e_{i_k}^{\pm}\!:\;+\;(\text{correction terms}),$$
where the correction terms are constructed from the inverse metric $g^{ij}$, the Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$, derivatives $\partial\gamma^{l}$, and coefficients given by Bessel polynomials, in such a way that each increase of the form-degree by two requires the insertion of an additional term of the schematic shape $\Gamma^{k}_{\ell m}\,g^{jm}\,\partial\gamma^{\ell}$. Suppose these local expressions glue into two globally well-defined embeddings of sheaves
$$J^{\pm}\colon \Lambda^{\bullet} T^*M \;\hookrightarrow\; \Omega^{ch}_M .$$

Problem. Provide an intrinsic geometric (coordinate-free) characterization of the maps $J^{\pm}$. Equivalently, identify a natural geometric construction—formulated solely in terms of $(M,g,\nabla)$ and standard tensorial/vertex-algebraic operations—that produces the corrected normally ordered local formulas above and explains why the specific Bessel-polynomial coefficients and $\partial\gamma$ corrections are exactly those required for global gluing into $\Omega^{ch}_M$.
status_search_result: A literature search returns the foundational works on the chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds (Ekstrand–Heluani–Källén–Zabzine, Heluani–Zabzine, and the original Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob construction) and follow-ups on twisted/exotic CDR and T-duality, but no source explicitly identifies an intrinsic coordinate-free geometric characterization of the corrected form-to-section maps $J^{\pm}$ involving the Bessel-polynomial corrections and $\partial\gamma$ terms. The status of an intrinsic geometric description appears unresolved in the available literature.

context_brief: N=1 superconformal algebra generated by global G±
original_question: Whenever the local sections G+ and G− given by the curved formula with metric and Christoffel-symbol correction terms glue to global sections of the smooth chiral de Rham complex Ω_ch(M), do they generate two commuting copies of the N=1 superconformal algebra with central charge c = (3/2) dim_R M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of real dimension $d=\dim_{\mathbb R} M$, and let $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$ denote the smooth chiral de Rham complex of $M$, viewed as a sheaf of topological vertex superalgebras on $M$. On a coordinate chart with local coordinates $(x^i)$, bosonic fields $b_i, a^i$ and fermionic fields $\varphi^i,\psi_i$, define the local sections
$$G^{\pm} \;=\; g^{ij}\,\psi_i\,\partial b_j \;\pm\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\Gamma^{i}_{jk}\,\psi_i\,\varphi^{j}\,a^{k} \;+\; (\text{prescribed metric/Christoffel correction terms}),$$
constructed from the Riemannian metric $g$ and its Levi-Civita Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$ in the standard way, such that their sum and difference correspond to the de Rham differential and codifferential on $M$.

Question: Suppose that on a given Riemannian manifold $M$ the locally defined sections $G^{+}$ and $G^{-}$ above patch together to define global sections of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$. Do $G^{+}$ and $G^{-}$ then generate, inside the vertex algebra of global sections, two mutually commuting copies of the $N=1$ Neveu–Schwarz (super-Virasoro) vertex algebra, each of central charge
$$c \;=\; \tfrac{3}{2}\,\dim_{\mathbb R} M\,?$$
category_tag: chiral de Rham complex / vertex superalgebras
status_search_result: The local computation that the curved $G^\pm$ generate two commuting copies of the $N=1$ Neveu–Schwarz algebra of central charge $\tfrac{3}{2}\dim_{\mathbb R} M$ is established in the literature on the chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds (Ekstrand–Heluani–Källén–Zabzine, and Heluani–Zabzine), with extensions to $N=2$ and $N=4$ in Kähler/Calabi–Yau/hyperkähler cases. The remaining global-existence/gluing issue for $G^\pm$ is what makes the question conditional; once globality is assumed the algebraic statement reduces to a verifiable OPE computation, and the relevant pieces appear in the cited works, but a single explicit reference fully asserting the conditional statement on a general Riemannian manifold is not clearly identified, so it is best regarded as partially settled.

original_question: For a G2-holonomy manifold, after constructing a BRST-type cohomology of the smooth chiral de Rham complex with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces, what is the character of that cohomology, does it provide an analog of the elliptic genus for G2 manifolds, and does the resulting series converge and have modular properties?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact 7-dimensional Riemannian manifold with holonomy group contained in the exceptional Lie group $G_2$. Associated to $M$ is the smooth chiral de Rham complex $\Omega^{ch}_M$, a sheaf of topological vertex superalgebras whose space of global sections $H = H^0(M, \Omega^{ch}_M)$ carries an action of the Shatashvili–Vafa $G_2$ superconformal algebra. In particular, $H$ contains two commuting Virasoro fields $T^{+}(z)$ and $X^{+}(z)$ (with zero modes $T^{+}_0$, $X^{+}_0$) and a distinguished odd field whose zero mode $Q^{+}_0$ squares to zero, providing a BRST-type differential on $H$.

Assume that the cohomology $\mathcal{H}(M) := H^*(H, Q^{+}_0)$ has finite-dimensional conformal weight spaces with respect to the residual Virasoro action (so each joint eigenspace of $T^{+}_0$ and $X^{+}_0$ on the cohomology is finite-dimensional).

Define the formal series
$$\chi_M(\tau) = q^{-21/48}\,\mathrm{str}_{\mathcal{H}(M)}\, q^{L^{+}_0}, \qquad q = e^{2\pi i \tau},$$
where $L^{+}_0$ is the zero mode of the residual Virasoro and $\mathrm{str}$ is the supertrace, as well as the two-variable refinement
$$\chi_M(\tau, z) = q^{-21/48}\,\mathrm{str}_{\mathcal{H}(M)}\, q^{T^{+}_0}\, y^{X^{+}_0}, \qquad y = e^{2\pi i z},$$
obtained from the joint $(T^{+}_0, X^{+}_0)$ grading.

Determine:
(i) an explicit formula for $\chi_M(\tau)$ (and for $\chi_M(\tau,z)$) in terms of topological/geometric invariants of $M$, thereby producing a $G_2$-analog of the elliptic genus;
(ii) whether the series $\chi_M(\tau)$ converges in the upper half plane $\{\mathrm{Im}\,\tau > 0\}$;
(iii) whether $\chi_M(\tau)$ (respectively $\chi_M(\tau,z)$) is a modular (respectively Jacobi) form with respect to a suitable congruence subgroup, and identify that group together with the weight and index.
category_tag: Chiral de Rham complex and G2 elliptic genus
status_search_result: A web search for results on a $G_2$ analog of the elliptic genus arising from BRST cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex returned results on the Calabi–Yau (N=2) case (Borisov–Libgober, Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob and follow-ups) and the orbifold/toric case, but no source establishing convergence, an explicit formula, or modular properties of the proposed $G_2$ character. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Are the copies of the Shatashvili-Vafa G2 superconformal algebra SV^G2 embedded in the smooth chiral de Rham complex of a G2-holonomy manifold by Rodriguez's theorem simple vertex algebras, so that the Virasoro subalgebra generated by X is the unitary c=7/10 minimal model and the proposed G2 topological twist can be applied?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let M be a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension 7 with holonomy group equal to the exceptional group G2, and let Ω^{ch}_M denote its smooth chiral de Rham complex, viewed as a sheaf of N=1 superconformal vertex algebras on M. The Shatashvili–Vafa G2 superconformal vertex algebra SV^{G2} is the W-algebra extension of the N=1 superconformal algebra at central charge c = 21/2 generated by fields {L, G, Φ, K, X, M} satisfying the Shatashvili–Vafa OPE relations; in particular it contains a Virasoro field X of central charge c = 7/10 commuting with the remaining N=1 super-Virasoro structure. By a theorem of Rodriguez (here referred to as the "Rodriguez embedding"), the vertex algebra of global sections of Ω^{ch}_M contains two commuting copies of SV^{G2}.

Question. For each of the two copies of SV^{G2} produced by the Rodriguez embedding inside the global sections of Ω^{ch}_M, is the embedded copy a simple vertex algebra? Equivalently, do the embedded copies coincide with the simple quotient of the universal Shatashvili–Vafa vertex algebra at c = 21/2, so that the c = 7/10 Virasoro subalgebra generated by the field X is the unitary tricritical Ising minimal model (a member of the unitary discrete series of Virasoro minimal models)?
status_search_result: Searches surface continuing research on Shatashvili–Vafa G2 algebras, their embeddings into the chiral de Rham complex on G2 manifolds (Rodriguez/Ekstrand–Heluani–Källén–Zabzine), deformations and quantum Hamiltonian reductions, but no source explicitly establishes (or refutes) that the specific copies of SV^{G2} produced by Rodriguez's embedding inside Ω^{ch}_M are simple vertex algebras with the c = 7/10 piece being the unitary tricritical Ising minimal model. The simplicity question and its consequence for performing the proposed G2 topological twist appear to remain unresolved in the publicly available literature.

context_brief: Spin(7) elliptic genus as topological-twist graded dimension
original_question: For a Spin(7)-holonomy manifold M, is its elliptic genus equal to the graded dimension of the BRST/topological-twist cohomology H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) constructed from the conjectural left-moving SV^Spin7 structure, with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension 8 with holonomy group equal to $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$. Let $\Omega^{ch}_M$ denote the chiral de Rham complex of $M$ (the sheaf of vertex superalgebras introduced by Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob), and let $C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M)$ denote its space of global smooth sections, viewed as a vertex superalgebra equipped with the natural conformal grading by $L_0$ and central charge $c=12$.

Assume that $C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M)$ contains two commuting copies of the Shatashvili–Vafa $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ vertex superalgebra $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$, one for each chirality. From the left-moving copy, let $Q^-_0$ denote the BRST/topological-twist differential associated with the topological twist of this $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$ structure, and form the cohomology
$$H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),\,Q^-_0).$$
This cohomology inherits a grading by the conformal weight $L_0$ (and possibly by an additional fermion-number/$U(1)$-type charge needed to define the elliptic genus).

Question: Are the conformal-weight homogeneous components of $H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),Q^-_0)$ all finite-dimensional, and does its graded dimension
$$\mathrm{tr}_{H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),Q^-_0)}\,q^{L_0-c/24}$$
(suitably refined by the available charge to a two-variable trace) coincide with the elliptic genus of the $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-manifold $M$?

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
context_brief: Direct Hamiltonian-reduction construction of CDR supersymmetries
original_question: Can the supersymmetry algebras inside the chiral de Rham complex of special-holonomy manifolds be constructed directly by quantum Hamiltonian reduction: specifically, is there a morphism from the BRST complex C^•(g, f) defining W_k(g, f) to Ω_ch(M), or to a resolution of Ω_ch(M), that induces the N=2, N=4, SV^Spin7, and SV^G2 embeddings described geometrically?
self_contained_problem:
Let M be a smooth Riemannian manifold with special holonomy (in particular, of holonomy type SU(n), Sp(n), Spin(7), or G_2), and let Ω^{ch}_M denote its chiral de Rham complex, the sheaf of vertex superalgebras canonically attached to M. It is known that, depending on the holonomy, the vertex algebra of global sections of Ω^{ch}_M contains a distinguished superconformal subalgebra: an N=2 superconformal algebra (Calabi–Yau case), an N=4 superconformal algebra (hyperkähler case), the Shatashvili–Vafa Spin(7) algebra SV^{Spin(7)}, or the Shatashvili–Vafa G_2 algebra SV^{G_2}.

Each of these superconformal algebras is also known to arise as a quantum W-algebra W_k(g,f) obtained by quantum Hamiltonian (Drinfeld–Sokolov / BRST) reduction of an affine vertex superalgebra associated with a suitable Lie superalgebra g and nilpotent element f, computed as the cohomology of an explicit BRST complex C^•(g,f).

Question: Does there exist a morphism of complexes (compatible with the vertex algebra structure)
   φ : C^•(g,f) ⟶ Ω^{ch}_M
or, more generally, a morphism from C^•(g,f) into a resolution of Ω^{ch}_M, such that the induced map on cohomology realizes the geometric embeddings of the N=2, N=4, SV^{Spin(7)}, and SV^{G_2} algebras into the chiral de Rham complex of M? Equivalently, can the supersymmetry algebras of Ω^{ch}_M for special-holonomy manifolds be constructed directly by quantum Hamiltonian reduction?
status_search_result: A search of the literature on the chiral de Rham complex, Hamiltonian reduction, and Shatashvili–Vafa / Odake algebras (including subsequent work on G_2 manifolds being superconformal) shows that while the relevant superconformal algebras are recognized as W-algebras and the geometric embeddings are constructed by direct vertex-algebraic methods, no morphism from the BRST complex C^•(g,f) into Ω^{ch}_M (or a resolution) inducing these embeddings has been exhibited. The connection between quantum Hamiltonian reduction and the chiral de Rham complex is described as still mysterious, and no later resolution of this question was found.

paper_title: Effective non-linear dynamics of binary condensates and open problems
original_question: For the two-species Bose gas in the Gross-Pitaevskii scaling considered in this paper, can one remove the positivity assumption on the interaction potentials and still rigorously derive persistence of two-component condensation together with the effective coupled Gross-Pitaevskii system? Equivalently, can the theorem proved here under positive, spherically symmetric, compactly supported interaction potentials be extended to allow non-positive interactions at the true Gross-Pitaevskii scaling, rather than only in softer scaling regimes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional dilute gas of $N=N_1+N_2$ identical bosons of two species, evolving under the many-body Hamiltonian
$$H_N = \sum_{j=1}^{N_1}\bigl(-\Delta_{x_j}+U_1(x_j)\bigr) + \sum_{j=1}^{N_2}\bigl(-\Delta_{y_j}+U_2(y_j)\bigr) + \sum_{i<j}^{N_1} N^2 V_{11}(N(x_i-x_j)) + \sum_{i<j}^{N_2} N^2 V_{22}(N(y_i-y_j)) + \sum_{i=1}^{N_1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_2} N^2 V_{12}(N(x_i-y_j)),$$
acting on the bosonic Hilbert space $L^2_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb{R}^{3N_1})\otimes L^2_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb{R}^{3N_2})$, with $N_1/N\to c_1\in(0,1)$ and $N_2/N\to c_2=1-c_1$ as $N\to\infty$. The pair interactions $V_{ab}:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}$ ($a,b\in\{1,2\}$) are assumed spherically symmetric and compactly supported, and $U_1,U_2$ are external trapping potentials.

Suppose that at time $t=0$ the state of the system exhibits complete two-component Bose-Einstein condensation onto one-particle orbitals $\varphi_1^0,\varphi_2^0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$, in the sense that the reduced one-body density matrices of each species converge to $|\varphi_a^0\rangle\langle\varphi_a^0|$.

Question: Without imposing the pointwise positivity condition $V_{ab}\geq 0$ (i.e., allowing partially attractive interactions), can one rigorously prove that the property of two-component condensation is propagated by the Schrödinger evolution generated by $H_N$, with the time-evolved condensate orbitals $\varphi_1(t),\varphi_2(t)$ satisfying the coupled Gross-Pitaevskii system
$$i\partial_t\varphi_1 = -\Delta\varphi_1 + U_1\varphi_1 + 8\pi a_{11} c_1|\varphi_1|^2\varphi_1 + 8\pi a_{12} c_2|\varphi_2|^2\varphi_1,$$
$$i\partial_t\varphi_2 = -\Delta\varphi_2 + U_2\varphi_2 + 8\pi a_{22} c_2|\varphi_2|^2\varphi_2 + 8\pi a_{12} c_1|\varphi_1|^2\varphi_2,$$
where $a_{ab}$ denotes the s-wave scattering length of $V_{ab}$? Equivalently, can the rigorous derivation, which is known under the positivity assumption $V_{ab}\geq 0$ at the true Gross-Pitaevskii scaling and known without positivity only under softer scalings $N^{3\beta-1}V(N^\beta\cdot)$ with $\beta<1$, be extended so as to remove the positivity assumption while keeping $\beta=1$?
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly identified as an open problem in the relevant literature on binary condensates in the Gross-Pitaevskii scaling. Rigorous derivations of the coupled GP system are available either under positivity of all interaction potentials at the true GP scaling (Michelangeli-Olgiati, 2017), or without positivity but only under softer (NLS-type) scalings. A search did not surface a result removing the positivity assumption at the genuine GP scaling for two-component condensates, so the problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

paper_title: Effective non-linear dynamics of binary condensates and open problems
original_question: For a one-component Bose gas, can one rigorously derive the Gross-Pitaevskii equation i∂_t u_t = -∆u_t + 8πa|u_t|^2u_t from the many-body quantum dynamics in the Gross-Pitaevskii scaling?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of $N$ identical spinless bosons in $\mathbb{R}^3$ governed by the Hamiltonian
$$H_N = \sum_{j=1}^N (-\Delta_{x_j}) + \sum_{1\le i<j\le N} N^2 V(N(x_i-x_j)),$$
acting on the symmetric subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{3N})$, where $V\ge 0$ is a smooth, compactly supported, spherically symmetric potential with three-dimensional scattering length $a$. Let $\Psi_{N,t} = e^{-iH_N t}\Psi_{N,0}$ be the solution of the many-body Schrödinger equation, with initial data $\Psi_{N,0}$ exhibiting complete Bose-Einstein condensation in a one-particle state $\varphi\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ (i.e., the one-particle reduced density matrix $\gamma_{N,0}^{(1)}\to |\varphi\rangle\langle\varphi|$ in trace norm as $N\to\infty$).

Prove that for every fixed $t\in\mathbb{R}$, the one-particle reduced density matrix $\gamma_{N,t}^{(1)}$ associated with $\Psi_{N,t}$ converges in trace norm, as $N\to\infty$, to $|u_t\rangle\langle u_t|$, where $u_t$ solves the cubic nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii equation
$$i\partial_t u_t = -\Delta u_t + 8\pi a\, |u_t|^2 u_t,\qquad u_0=\varphi.$$
status_search_result: The derivation of the time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii equation from many-body bosonic quantum dynamics in the GP scaling was solved by Erdős, Schlein and Yau (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 2006; Invent. Math. 2007; Ann. of Math. 2010) using the BBGKY hierarchy. Subsequent works (Pickl; Benedikter–de Oliveira–Schlein; Brennecke–Schlein, etc.) provided alternative proofs and quantitative convergence rates.

original_question: For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?
self_contained_problem:
Let $w = w(n) \le n$ be a bandwidth parameter, and consider the ensemble of random $n \times n$ band matrices $H = (H_{ij})$ defined as follows. The entries satisfy $H_{ij} = 0$ whenever $|i-j| \ge w$, and the entries $\{H_{ij} : |i-j| < w,\ i \le j\}$ are independent random variables (with $H_{ji}$ determined by the symmetry/Hermitian constraint). Two settings are considered:

(a) Real symmetric: $H_{ij} = H_{ji} \in \mathbb{R}$, i.i.d. (up to symmetry) with mean zero and finite variance.

(b) Complex Hermitian: $H_{ij} = \overline{H_{ji}} \in \mathbb{C}$, with independent real and imaginary parts (mean zero, finite variance), again i.i.d. inside the band.

After rescaling so that the empirical spectral measure converges to the semicircle law, consider the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ in the bulk of the spectrum (e.g., the local correlation functions on scale $1/n$, or the gap distribution).

Prove the following Fyodorov–Mirlin transition in both settings (a) and (b):

(i) If $w \gg \sqrt{n}$ (i.e., $w/\sqrt{n} \to \infty$), then the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ converge to those of the corresponding Gaussian invariant ensemble (GOE in case (a), GUE in case (b)).

(ii) If $w \ll \sqrt{n}$ (i.e., $w/\sqrt{n} \to 0$ with $w \to \infty$), then the local eigenvalue statistics converge to those of a Poisson point process (with intensity given by the semicircle density).
status_search_result: The Fyodorov–Mirlin √n conjecture (1991) for one-dimensional random band matrices remains open in general. Substantial partial progress has been made on the GUE/delocalized side: GUE-type local statistics and quantum unique ergodicity of eigenvectors have been established for bandwidths well above √n in Hermitian Gaussian-like models (work of Bourgade, Yau, Yin, and collaborators), and rigorous results have been obtained in special Gaussian or chiral models. The Poisson side for w ≪ √n is essentially still open, and the full conjecture covering both regimes in real symmetric and complex Hermitian band matrices has not been proved.

original_question: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?
self_contained_problem:
Let $W_N$ be a sequence of $N\times N$ random Hermitian (or real symmetric) Wigner-type matrices, i.e. matrices with independent entries (up to the symmetry constraint) whose variances $s_{ij}=\mathbb{E}|W_{ij}|^2$ may depend on $i,j$ in such a way that the empirical spectral distribution of $W_N$ converges, as $N\to\infty$, to a deterministic equilibrium measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ whose support consists of more than one interval.

(a) Prove that the local eigenvalue statistics of $W_N$ are universal in the bulk of every connected component of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$: for any energy $E$ in the interior of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ where $\mu$ has positive density, the rescaled $k$-point correlation functions of the eigenvalues converge to the sine-kernel determinantal (resp. Pfaffian) statistics of the GUE (resp. GOE).

(b) Prove edge universality at every spectral edge of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$, including the internal edges bordering the gaps: at each such edge the rescaled extremal eigenvalue statistics converge to the Tracy–Widom distribution of the appropriate symmetry class.

(c) Consider one-parameter families $\{W_N(t)\}_{t}$ of Wigner-type ensembles whose equilibrium measures $\mu_t$ undergo topological transitions in which two adjacent intervals of the support merge (a gap closes) or a single interval splits (a gap opens). Analyze the local eigenvalue statistics in a neighborhood of the merging point through the transition, and identify the limiting universal local statistics that interpolate between sine-kernel, Tracy–Widom edge, and the cusp (Pearcey) statistics arising at the moment of merging.
status_search_result: The problem has been substantially solved for Wigner-type matrices. Ajanki–Erdős–Krüger established bulk universality for general Wigner-type matrices with multi-interval support; Alt–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder and Cipolloni–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder proved edge universality at all (including internal) edges and cusp universality, completing the Wigner–Dyson–Mehta conjecture in all spectral regimes. The cusp/Pearcey statistics arise precisely at band-merging transitions, addressing the parameter-dependent opening/closing of intervals. The result has been further extended to correlated random matrices (Erdős and collaborators, 2024–2025).

original_question: Can one obtain rigorous explicit formulas for Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles beyond the classical invariant cases beta = 1, 2, and 4, including a rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach for all even beta > 0 and a rigorous verification of the asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general beta > 0?
self_contained_problem:
For each $\beta>0$, the $\beta$-ensemble at the soft edge gives rise to a Tracy–Widom-type limiting distribution $F_\beta$, which for the classical values $\beta\in\{1,2,4\}$ admits explicit Painlevé II representations due to Tracy and Widom. The task is twofold:

(a) (Rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach.) Rumanov proposed Lax-pair representations and explicit formulas for $F_\beta$ for even integer $\beta$, expressing $F_\beta$ in terms of the Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II together with an auxiliary function satisfying a coupled ODE. Rigorously establish such explicit Painlevé/Calogero–Painlevé representations of $F_\beta$ for every even integer $\beta>0$, including a rigorous justification of the corresponding Riemann–Hilbert / isomonodromy framework and of the asymptotic analysis at $\pm\infty$.

(b) (Rigorous verification of the Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal predictions.) For general $\beta>0$, Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal proposed asymptotic formulas for the left and right tails of $F_\beta$ as the argument tends to $-\infty$ and $+\infty$, with explicit leading exponents and constants depending on $\beta$. Rigorously prove these tail asymptotics for all $\beta>0$.

Provide a rigorous derivation of explicit formulas (in (a)) and a rigorous proof of the asymptotic formulas (in (b)) for the Tracy–Widom $\beta$-distributions beyond the classical cases $\beta=1,2,4$.
status_search_result: Rumanov's approach has been substantially developed for the case $\beta=6$: Rumanov (2015) gave a Painlevé representation, and subsequent work by Grava–Its–Kapaev–Mezzadri (2016) and by Bertola–Cafasso–Rubtsov, together with later papers (e.g. arXiv:2010.06733, arXiv:1812.00522), connected $F_6$ to the second Calogero–Painlevé system and provided a Riemann–Hilbert framework enabling rigorous asymptotic analysis. However, a rigorous completion of Rumanov's analysis for all even $\beta>0$ and a rigorous proof of the Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal tail asymptotics for general $\beta>0$ do not appear to have been fully achieved, so the problem remains partially solved.

original_question: Can one analyze solutions of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation simultaneously at more than one space-time point, rather than only through one-point statistics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation
$$\partial_t h(t,x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 h(t,x) + \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x h(t,x))^2 + \xi(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\xi$ is space-time white noise on $\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{R}$, and the equation is interpreted in the Hopf–Cole (or regularity-structures) sense. For an initial condition $h(0,\cdot)=h_0$ (e.g. narrow-wedge, flat, or stationary), let $h(t,x)$ denote the corresponding solution.

Develop a tractable description of the joint law of the random vector
$$\bigl(h(t_1,x_1),\,h(t_2,x_2),\,\dots,\,h(t_n,x_n)\bigr)$$
at an arbitrary finite collection of space-time points $\{(t_i,x_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ with $n\ge 2$ (in particular at distinct times $t_i$), going beyond the well-studied one-point statistics. Concretely, obtain explicit formulas (e.g. Fredholm determinant or integrable-operator representations) for the multi-point distribution function
$$\mathbb{P}\bigl(h(t_1,x_1)\le s_1,\ \dots,\ h(t_n,x_n)\le s_n\bigr),$$
and analyze its properties, for general initial data.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on multi-point space-time statistics of the KPZ universality class. Multi-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point are known explicitly for narrow-wedge and flat initial data, and two-point formulas exist for half-Brownian and Brownian data. A 2025 work derives space-time joint distribution formulas for the KPZ fixed point with general compactly supported initial data via a 1:2:3 scaling limit of TASEP. Corresponding multi-point formulas directly for the KPZ equation (pre-limit) at general initial data remain less complete, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

original_question: For the longest increasing subsequence problem, can one prove KPZ-class fluctuation results when the permutation is sampled from distributions more general than the uniform distribution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and for a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ let $L_n(\pi)$ denote the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $\pi$. When $\pi$ is sampled uniformly at random from $S_n$, it is known (Baik–Deift–Johansson) that
$$\frac{L_n - 2\sqrt{n}}{n^{1/6}} \xrightarrow{d} F_2,$$
where $F_2$ is the GUE Tracy–Widom distribution, placing the model in the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class.

Problem. Identify natural families of probability measures $\{\mu_n\}$ on $S_n$ that differ from the uniform measure, and prove KPZ-class fluctuation theorems for $L_n$ under $\pi\sim\mu_n$: that is, find deterministic centering $a_n$ and scaling $b_n$ (with $b_n$ of KPZ-type order, e.g. a power of $n$ less than $1/2$) such that
$$\frac{L_n - a_n}{b_n} \xrightarrow{d} \mathcal{D}$$
for a KPZ-universality limiting law $\mathcal{D}$ (such as the Tracy–Widom $F_1$, $F_2$, or $F_4$ distribution, or related Airy-type distributions). Determine the broadest class of non-uniform distributions on $S_n$ for which such KPZ-type fluctuation results hold.
category_tag: KPZ universality and longest increasing subsequences
status_search_result: For the uniform distribution, KPZ/Tracy–Widom fluctuations are classical (Baik–Deift–Johansson, 1999), and the scaling limit of the LIS as a path has been identified (Dauvergne, 2021). For non-uniform models, partial results exist: under the Mallows measure with parameter $q\in(0,1)$ regimes, Gaussian (non-KPZ) fluctuations have been established (Bhatnagar–Peled, Mueller–Starr, Basu–Bhatnagar). KPZ-type fluctuations beyond the uniform case remain largely unestablished in general, so the broader question is considered partially solved / still open.

original_question: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-type interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory in integrable dynamical systems, so that persistence of integrability-like structure and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena can be studied beyond exactly solvable models?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a perturbation theory for KPZ-type interacting-particle systems (one-dimensional stochastic growth and interacting-particle models in the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang universality class, such as asymmetric exclusion processes, last-passage percolation, polymer models, and corner growth models) that plays the role analogous to Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser (KAM) theory in classical integrable Hamiltonian dynamics. Specifically, construct a rigorous framework with the following features:

(a) Starting from an exactly solvable ("integrable") KPZ-type model whose one-point distributions, correlation functions, and scaling limits (e.g. Tracy–Widom fluctuations with exponent 1/3 and spatial scale 2/3) are known exactly via determinantal/Bethe-ansatz structures, identify a quantitative notion of "integrable structure" (e.g. determinantal correlation kernels, Markov dualities, intertwiners, or algebraic symmetries) that can be tracked under small perturbations of the model's transition rates or local interactions.

(b) Prove that, for sufficiently small but non-trivial perturbations that destroy exact solvability, a portion of this integrable structure persists in a controlled (possibly asymptotic) sense.

(c) Use this persistence to deduce, rigorously, that the perturbed (non-solvable) model still lies in the KPZ universality class — i.e. that its large-time fluctuations, after appropriate centering and rescaling, converge to the KPZ fixed point (or, on intermediate scales, to the KPZ equation), with the same scaling exponents and limiting distributions as the unperturbed solvable model.

The problem is to either produce such a perturbation theory together with a class of non-solvable models for which universality can be derived from solvable ones, or to establish fundamental obstructions ruling out such a theory.
status_search_result: No KAM-style perturbation theory for KPZ-type non-solvable interacting-particle models is known. Surveys and lecture notes on the KPZ universality class (Corwin, Quastel, Baik, Petrov) continue to emphasize that universality is rigorously established only for special solvable models and certain weak-asymmetry/intermediate disorder limits, with no general framework for perturbing away from integrable models. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the QR algorithm applied to random matrices, can one control, as n tends to infinity, the bulk eigenvalue-ratio statistics |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j| and |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| near the eigenvalue lambda_j closest to zero, together with the associated normalized eigenvectors, so as to prove the analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for QR?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be an $n\times n$ real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) random matrix drawn from a Wigner-type ensemble (with i.i.d. centered entries of unit variance above the diagonal, suitably normalized so that the empirical spectral distribution converges to the semicircle law on $[-2,2]$). The shifted QR eigenvalue algorithm produces a sequence of orthogonally (unitarily) similar tridiagonal matrices $H = H_0, H_1, H_2, \dots$ defined by $H_k - s_k I = Q_k R_k$ (QR factorization) and $H_{k+1} = R_k Q_k + s_k I$, where $\{s_k\}$ is a chosen shift strategy (e.g., the Wilkinson shift). Order the eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ of $H$ and let $j = j(n)$ be an index for which $\lambda_j$ is closest to $0$ (i.e., deep in the bulk).

Prove the following analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for the QR algorithm: as $n\to\infty$, the joint distribution of the bulk ratios
$$\Big(\big|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j\big|,\ \big|\lambda_{j-1}/\lambda_j\big|\Big)$$
together with appropriate functionals of the associated normalized eigenvectors of $\lambda_{j-1},\lambda_j,\lambda_{j+1}$, when properly centered and scaled, converges to a limiting distribution that does not depend on the particular Wigner ensemble (i.e., is universal across the choice of entry distribution), and use this to deduce universality of the halting-time / deflation statistics of the shifted QR algorithm at indices in the bulk of the spectrum.
status_search_result: The problem is described in the literature as a well-known open problem. Universality for the Toda algorithm has been proved (Deift–Trogdon and related works), and analogous empirical universality has been observed numerically for QR, but a rigorous proof of bulk eigenvalue-ratio and eigenvector universality controlling the QR halting time remains unestablished as of the most recent publicly available work. No paper claiming a complete proof was found.

original_question: Can one rigorously prove universality for one of the other numerical algorithms with random data discussed in the paper, especially the conjugate-gradient algorithm for solving a random linear system A x = b with both A and b random?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be a random symmetric positive-definite matrix (for example, a sample covariance / Wishart matrix $A = \frac{1}{m} X X^{T}$ with $X$ an $n \times m$ matrix of i.i.d. entries having mean $0$, variance $1$, and sufficient moment conditions, with $m/n \to \gamma > 1$), and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be an independent random vector with i.i.d. entries (mean $0$, variance $1$). Apply the conjugate gradient algorithm to solve the linear system $A x = b$, starting from $x_{0} = 0$, and define the halting time
$$\tau_{n}(\varepsilon) \;=\; \min\bigl\{ k \geq 1 \;:\; \|r_{k}\| / \|r_{0}\| < \varepsilon \bigr\},$$
where $r_{k} = b - A x_{k}$ is the $k$-th residual and $\varepsilon > 0$ is a fixed tolerance.

Empirically, the fluctuations of $\tau_{n}(\varepsilon)$ — that is, $(\tau_{n}(\varepsilon) - \mathbb{E}\tau_{n}(\varepsilon))/\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}\,\tau_{n}(\varepsilon)}$ — converge as $n \to \infty$ to a limiting distribution that depends only on $\gamma$ and $\varepsilon$, and not on the distribution of the entries of $X$ and $b$ (a universality phenomenon).

Problem: Prove rigorously this universality statement for the conjugate gradient algorithm. More precisely, establish a limit theorem (e.g., a central limit theorem) for $\tau_{n}(\varepsilon)$, or for a closely related observable such as $\|r_{k}\|$, showing that the limiting law is independent of the underlying entry distribution within a broad class.
category_tag: Universality for numerical algorithms on random matrices
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Paquette and Trogdon proved a central limit theorem and a four-moment universality result for the residuals of the conjugate gradient and MINRES algorithms applied to sample covariance matrices, implying an almost-deterministic halting time. Deift–Trogdon and related work show that on well-conditioned Wishart matrices the CG halting time is almost deterministic. However, fully general universality results for the halting-time distribution across broad random-matrix ensembles and data distributions are not yet completely established, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

original_question: For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line, i u_t = u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u for x >= 0 and t >= 0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) and oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one compute the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) for general real driving frequency w?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line,
   i u_t(x,t) = u_{xx}(x,t) + 2 |u(x,t)|^2 u(x,t),   x ≥ 0, t ≥ 0,
with prescribed initial datum
   u(x,0) = f(x),   x ≥ 0,
(decaying sufficiently fast as x → ∞), and with the purely oscillatory Dirichlet boundary condition
   u(0,t) = e^{i ω t},   t ≥ 0,
where ω ∈ ℝ is a given real frequency.

Determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t → ∞ in the various sectors of the (x,t)-quarter-plane (e.g. along rays x/t = ξ held fixed), for arbitrary real ω. That is, give explicit leading-order asymptotic formulas for u(x,t) — including the structure of any emergent modulated elliptic/plane-wave regions, dispersive zones, soliton trains, and transition regions — that are valid for general ω ∈ ℝ.
category_tag: Long-time asymptotics for integrable PDEs (NLS on half-line)
status_search_result: Boutet de Monvel, Its, and Kotlyarov developed a Riemann–Hilbert/Deift–Zhou framework for the focusing NLS equation on the quarter plane with time-periodic Dirichlet data, and obtained long-time asymptotics in certain regimes (e.g., specific ranges of the frequency and decaying initial data). However, a complete description of the long-time behavior valid for arbitrary real ω, with all transition regions and the full structure of the modulated zones rigorously identified, does not appear to have been established; the problem is generally regarded as still open in full generality.

original_question: Can the Bikbaev-Tarasov Backlund-transform method be adapted to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u on the half-line with Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, despite the singularities introduced when the solution is extended from x > 0 to x < 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the half-line,
   i u_t(x,t) = u_{xx}(x,t) - 2 |u(x,t)|^2 u(x,t),  for x > 0, t > 0,
with initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x) (sufficiently smooth and decaying) and homogeneous Robin boundary condition
   u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0,  for t > 0,
where q ∈ ℝ is a fixed coupling constant.

The Bikbaev–Tarasov method, originally developed for the focusing NLS equation, prescribes an explicit Bäcklund transformation that extends a solution defined for x > 0 (subject to a Robin boundary condition at x = 0) to a solution of the same equation on the whole line x ∈ ℝ; the extension is then analyzed by inverse scattering / Riemann–Hilbert techniques applied on the line, and one recovers the half-line solution by restriction. In the focusing case, this extension is regular.

In the defocusing case, the analogous Bäcklund transformation that produces an extension to x < 0 generically introduces singularities of the extended field, and the long-time behavior is expected to differ qualitatively from the focusing case (no decaying solitons on the line, but stationary half-line solitons compatible with the Robin condition).

Question. Can the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transform method be adapted, with control of the singularities introduced when the half-line solution is extended to x < 0, so as to give a complete inverse-scattering / Riemann–Hilbert solution of the initial-boundary value problem above for the defocusing NLS equation with Robin boundary conditions, including a rigorous derivation of the long-time asymptotics of u(x,t)?
category_tag: Integrable IBVPs / inverse scattering on the half-line
status_search_result: The defocusing NLS half-line IBVP with homogeneous Robin boundary conditions has been treated rigorously (Riemann–Hilbert representation, well-posedness in H^{1,1}, t^{-3/4} decay, asymptotic stability of stationary solitons) by Lee et al. (Proc. LMS, 2023), but those authors explicitly state that they adopted a different approach (unified transform method) because the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund extension introduces singularities that are difficult to control in the defocusing case. Thus the IBVP itself is solved by other means, while the specific question of adapting the Bikbaev–Tarasov method appears not to have been carried out and remains open.

original_question: More generally, what smoothness can be proved for solutions of initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and consider a dispersive partial differential equation posed on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$ (for example, a half-space, a smooth bounded domain, or the exterior of a smooth obstacle). Typical model equations include:

- the linear Schrödinger equation $i\partial_t u + \Delta u = 0$,
- the linear or nonlinear Korteweg–de Vries-type and Zakharov–Kuznetsov-type equations,
- and other linear/nonlinear dispersive equations whose symbol $p(\xi)$ satisfies $|\nabla p(\xi)| \to \infty$ as $|\xi| \to \infty$.

The initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) consists of prescribing an initial datum $u(0,x) = u_0(x)$ for $x \in \Omega$ together with appropriate boundary conditions on $(0,T) \times \partial\Omega$ (e.g. Dirichlet, Neumann, or other admissible boundary data) so that the problem is well-posed in a suitable Sobolev space.

Determine, for general dispersive IBVPs in arbitrary spatial dimension $n$, the smoothness (interior and up-to-the-boundary regularity) that solutions $u(t,x)$ must possess. More precisely:

(a) Identify the local and global smoothing effects (gain of regularity in space and/or time) for solutions of such IBVPs as a function of the regularity of the initial data $u_0$ and the boundary data, generalizing the Kato-type local smoothing known for the Cauchy problem on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

(b) Characterize the propagation of regularity from subdomains of $\Omega$ (or from portions of the boundary) into the rest of $\Omega$ for $t > 0$.

(c) Determine sharp Sobolev (or Besov) regularity classes in which the IBVP is well-posed in $n \geq 2$ dimensions, particularly for nonlinear models of KdV, Zakharov–Kuznetsov, and Schrödinger type on domains with boundary.
status_search_result: The general question of smoothness of solutions to initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension remains largely open. Recent work has established partial results: smoothing and propagation-of-regularity results for specific equations (KdV-type, Zakharov–Kuznetsov, two-dimensional Kawahara, Schrödinger) and on bounded intervals or special domains, but no general theory in arbitrary dimension is currently available.

original_question: For the Airy integral operator A_s on L^2(s, infinity), whose Fredholm determinant gives the edge-scaling distribution for the largest GUE eigenvalue, can one analyze the eigenfunctions u_tilde_j(s) asymptotically as s tends to infinity and also compute them accurately for finite s?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Ai}(x)$ denote the Airy function, and define the Airy kernel
$$K_{\mathrm{Ai}}(x,y)=\frac{\mathrm{Ai}(x)\,\mathrm{Ai}'(y)-\mathrm{Ai}'(x)\,\mathrm{Ai}(y)}{x-y},\qquad K_{\mathrm{Ai}}(x,x)=\mathrm{Ai}'(x)^2-x\,\mathrm{Ai}(x)^2.$$
For each real number $s$, let $\mathcal A_s$ be the integral operator on $L^2(s,\infty)$ with kernel $K_{\mathrm{Ai}}(x,y)$. The operator $\mathcal A_s$ is trace class, self-adjoint, and positive with eigenvalues $1>\lambda_0(s)>\lambda_1(s)>\cdots>0$ and corresponding $L^2(s,\infty)$-normalized eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(\,\cdot\,;s)$, $j=0,1,2,\dots$, satisfying
$$\int_s^\infty K_{\mathrm{Ai}}(x,y)\,\tilde u_j(y;s)\,dy=\lambda_j(s)\,\tilde u_j(x;s),\qquad x>s.$$
The Fredholm determinant $\det(I-\mathcal A_s)$ equals the Tracy–Widom distribution $F_2(s)$ governing the edge-scaling limit of the largest eigenvalue of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble.

Problem. (a) Determine the asymptotic behavior of the eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(x;s)$ as $s\to+\infty$, for each fixed $j\ge 0$, including leading-order asymptotics, dependence on $x-s$, and decay properties. (b) Provide a method, with rigorous error bounds, for computing $\tilde u_j(x;s)$ accurately for finite real values of $s$ (including large negative $s$).
status_search_result: Subsequent work (Bremer, Rokhlin, and collaborators) has produced spectral algorithms for the eigendecomposition of the Airy integral operator, exploiting a commuting differential operator due to Tracy–Widom, that compute the eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(\cdot;s)$ to near machine precision for finite $s$. Asymptotic analyses of related Fredholm determinants and tails as $s\to\pm\infty$ exist (e.g., Deift–Its–Krasovsky), but a complete rigorous asymptotic description of the eigenfunctions themselves as $s\to\infty$ is not fully established in the literature found. The problem thus appears partially solved: the numerical computation aspect is largely resolved, while the asymptotic analysis is only partly addressed.

original_question: Can one use Riemann-Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic results obtained by Venakides, Deift, and Oba for the Toda shock problem, where the driven lattice settles into a one-gap periodic state for sufficiently strong driving?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the doubly infinite Toda lattice
\[
\dot a_n(t) = a_n(t)\bigl(b_{n+1}(t)-b_n(t)\bigr),\qquad \dot b_n(t)=2\bigl(a_n(t)^2-a_{n-1}(t)^2\bigr),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,\ t\ge 0,
\]
with step-like initial data
\[
(a_n(0),b_n(0))\to(\tfrac12,c_\pm)\quad\text{as }n\to\pm\infty,
\]
where the asymptotic constant satisfies $c_- > c_+$ (the "shock" condition; equivalently the left background spectrum lies strictly above the right background spectrum, $\inf\sigma(H_-)>\sup\sigma(H_+)$, when the driving is sufficiently strong so that the two background spectra do not overlap).

It has been shown formally that, in the wedge of space-time variables corresponding to the bulk of the shock, the solution $(a_n(t),b_n(t))$ is asymptotically described, as $t\to\infty$ with $n/t$ in a fixed compact subinterval, by a one-gap (genus-one, elliptic) quasi-periodic finite-gap solution of the Toda lattice expressed in terms of Riemann theta functions associated with a hyperelliptic curve determined by the two backgrounds.

Problem. Using the inverse scattering transform reformulation as a matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem on the spectral plane and the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest-descent method (including the construction of appropriate $g$-functions, lens openings, and local parametrices), give a fully rigorous proof, with explicit error estimates, that in the modulation/elliptic region the Toda shock solution converges to the conjectured modulated one-gap finite-gap solution.
status_search_result: A series of works by Egorova, Michor, and Teschl (notably "Long-time asymptotics for Toda shock waves in the modulation region" arXiv:2001.05184, and the companion paper "Toda shock waves: justification of asymptotics", 2020, plus arXiv:2012.12371 on discrete spectrum/resonances) carries out the Riemann–Hilbert / nonlinear steepest-descent analysis with local parametrices and small-norm arguments, providing a rigorous justification of the Venakides–Deift–Oba asymptotics for the Toda shock problem with non-overlapping background spectra.

original_question: Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the diffraction problem for waves passing through two finite slits in the plane, the setting underlying Young's double-slit experiment in optics and the analogous double-slit experiment in quantum mechanics?
status_search_result: Search results indicate that while the single-slit/half-plane diffraction problem has classical rigorous solutions (Sommerfeld), the two-slit case is typically treated via approximations (Kirchhoff, Fraunhofer/Fresnel, Rayleigh–Sommerfeld integrals) rather than an exact closed-form solution. No source found provides a rigorous, explicit closed-form solution to the two-slit Helmholtz diffraction problem with edge conditions, consistent with the problem being still open.

paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
original_question: Does QCD matter, in the region probed by low- and intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions, undergo a first-order phase transition between quark-gluon-plasma matter and hadron-gas matter, and if so is there a critical endpoint associated with that transition?
self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the SU(3) gauge theory of quarks and gluons, at finite temperature T and finite baryon chemical potential μ_B. The grand-canonical partition function on the (T, μ_B) plane defines a thermodynamic phase structure with two known regimes: (i) a high-temperature, deconfined quark–gluon plasma phase, and (ii) a low-temperature, confined hadron-gas phase. At μ_B = 0 lattice QCD establishes that the change between these regimes is a smooth analytic crossover. Determine the following about the phase diagram in the region of moderate to large μ_B accessible to low- and intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions:

(a) Does there exist a curve T_c(μ_B) in the (T, μ_B) plane along which the free energy is non-analytic and across which the system undergoes a genuine first-order phase transition (i.e., a discontinuity in the baryon density and/or energy density) between the quark–gluon plasma phase and the hadron-gas phase?

(b) If such a first-order transition line exists, does it terminate at a critical endpoint (T_E, μ_B^E) with 0 < T_E and 0 < μ_B^E < ∞, at which the transition becomes second order in the 3D Ising universality class, and the crossover region begins?

Provide either a proof of existence together with the location (or rigorous bounds on the location) of the critical endpoint, or a proof that no such first-order line and endpoint exist in this region.
category_tag: QCD phase diagram and critical endpoint
status_search_result: The existence of a first-order deconfinement/chiral transition line at finite baryon chemical potential and an associated QCD critical endpoint remains an open problem. Lattice QCD is hindered by the sign problem at μ_B > 0, and experimental searches (RHIC Beam Energy Scan I and II, NA61/SHINE) have not yet produced conclusive evidence as of 2026. Recent reviews continue to list it as unresolved.

paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
original_question: At intermediate beam energies, how should one construct a dynamical description that consistently interpolates between viscous-hydrodynamic-plus-hadronic-transport hybrid models and purely hadronic transport models? In particular, can the reaction be modeled by surrounding a hydrodynamic core with a transport corona, by embedding hydrodynamic bubbles inside a transport calculation, or by some related framework that also treats the phase transition and the QCD critical point together with their non-equilibrium effects?
status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., 2021–2025) have developed hybrid frameworks pushing toward low beam energies with dynamic initial conditions from hadronic transport (SMASH+MUSIC), corona constructions, and Bayesian analyses. The BEST Collaboration framework explicitly addresses critical-point and non-equilibrium effects with equations of state including a critical end point. While substantial progress has been made on hydro+transport interpolation and on incorporating critical-point physics, a fully consistent unified treatment including all non-equilibrium dynamics near the critical point remains an active research goal rather than a settled result.

paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
original_question: For intermediate-beam-energy heavy-ion collisions, how much explicitly non-equilibrium evolution must be retained before any hydrodynamic description becomes valid, including in transport approaches that incorporate partonic degrees of freedom?
self_contained_problem: Consider relativistic heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies (collision energies in the regime where baryon density is large and the produced matter is far from local thermal equilibrium at early times). A standard modeling strategy is a hybrid description in which an early non-equilibrium stage is followed by a hydrodynamic stage that treats the matter as a fluid satisfying conservation laws supplemented by an equation of state and transport coefficients. Transport approaches with partonic (quark and gluon) degrees of freedom — such as Boltzmann-type kinetic theories with parton scattering, splitting, and hadronization — provide a microscopic alternative or complement to hydrodynamics. \n\nQuantify, within such partonic transport frameworks at intermediate beam energies, the minimal amount of explicitly non-equilibrium evolution (for example, characterized by an effective duration, mean number of partonic interactions per particle, or by quantitative measures of the deviation of the phase-space distribution from local equilibrium such as anisotropy parameters or pressure-anisotropy ratios) that must be retained before a switch to a hydrodynamic description yields physical observables (bulk and flow observables, particle spectra, fluctuations) consistent with those of the full microscopic evolution. Equivalently, determine criteria — expressed in terms of microscopic quantities accessible in partonic transport — that delineate the earliest space-time hypersurface on which a hydrodynamic description becomes valid in this energy regime.
status_search_result: The question of how much non-equilibrium dynamics is required before hydrodynamization at intermediate beam energies, including in partonic-transport-based hybrid approaches, remains an actively investigated open issue. Recent work on hydrodynamization, attractor solutions, and hybrid transport+hydrodynamics modeling for the RHIC Beam Energy Scan continues to address it without a definitive answer.

paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
original_question: Can Color Glass Condensate initial-state modeling for heavy-ion collisions be extended to a fully three-dimensional description, and down to what collision energy do the saturation assumptions used in that framework remain valid?
self_contained_problem:
In the high-energy limit of QCD, the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory describes the wavefunction of a hadron or nucleus in terms of static, large-x color sources sourcing dynamical small-x gluon fields, characterized by a saturation scale Q_s(x) that grows with energy and nuclear thickness. In its standard form, the CGC framework is formulated in the eikonal (boost-invariant) limit and is used to model the initial state of relativistic heavy-ion collisions as essentially two-dimensional in the transverse plane, with the longitudinal (rapidity) direction treated as boost-invariant.

(a) Construct an extension of the CGC initial-state framework for nucleus–nucleus collisions to a fully three-dimensional description that consistently incorporates non-eikonal corrections, finite longitudinal extent of the colliding nuclei, x-dependence (rapidity dependence) of the color sources, and the resulting non-trivial longitudinal structure of the produced gluon fields at proper time τ → 0+, in such a way that the existing 2+1-dimensional boost-invariant CGC results are recovered in the appropriate high-energy limit.

(b) Determine quantitatively the range of center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair √s_NN for which the saturation assumptions underlying the CGC (in particular Q_s ≫ Λ_QCD and the dominance of small-x gluon densities) remain self-consistent, and identify the lower energy threshold below which these assumptions break down for collisions of heavy nuclei.
status_search_result: The problem of extending CGC to a fully 3D (non-boost-invariant) initial-state description, and of delineating the lowest energies at which saturation remains valid, has been actively pursued (e.g., 3D JIMWLK studies, NLO/non-eikonal CGC, work by Schenke, Schlichting, McDonald and collaborators), but no complete, universally accepted 3D CGC framework with an established lower-energy validity bound exists. The question is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
original_question: Can source terms in three-fluid hydrodynamics, where two baryon-rich projectile and target fluids generate a fireball fluid, provide a correct explanation of how baryon deposition occurs in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions?
self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies (of order a few to tens of GeV per nucleon), one observes a redistribution of net baryon number from the colliding nuclei into the central rapidity region — the phenomenon of baryon deposition (or baryon stopping). A standard hydrodynamic framework for modeling such collisions is three-fluid hydrodynamics, in which the matter is described by three coupled relativistic fluids:

(i) a "projectile" fluid carrying baryon number from the forward-going nucleus,
(ii) a "target" fluid carrying baryon number from the backward-going nucleus, and
(iii) a baryon-free "fireball" fluid of newly produced matter.

Each fluid satisfies its own conservation equations
   ∂_μ T^{μν}_α = F^ν_α,   ∂_μ N^μ_α = J_α,   α ∈ {p, t, f},
with phenomenological source/friction terms F^ν_α and J_α coupling the fluids and transferring energy, momentum, and baryon charge from the projectile and target fluids into the fireball fluid, subject to global conservation Σ_α F^ν_α = 0 and Σ_α J_α = 0.

Problem. Determine whether source terms of this form, coupling two baryon-rich projectile and target fluids to a fireball fluid in three-fluid hydrodynamics, can give a quantitatively correct description of baryon deposition (the rapidity distribution of net baryon number, including any double-peak structure and central-rapidity stopping) in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies. Identify functional forms of the friction/source terms F^ν_α, J_α, and an associated equation of state, for which the resulting net-baryon rapidity distributions agree with experimental data over the relevant beam-energy range, or else show that no such choice within the three-fluid framework can do so.
status_search_result: Recent works (2023–2025) continue to develop and refine multi-fluid hydrodynamic descriptions of heavy-ion collisions, including new formulations of friction/source terms and comparisons with baryon-stopping data. While three-fluid hydrodynamics has had partial success reproducing net-baryon rapidity distributions, the question of whether such source terms provide a fully correct, quantitative explanation of baryon deposition at intermediate energies remains an active research topic with no settled answer.

context_brief: bounded operator representation of overcomplete Gabor frames
original_question: Do there exist overcomplete Gabor frames for L^2(R), meaning systems of the form {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} with g in L^2(R) and parameters a,b>0 that form a frame but not a Riesz basis, together with some ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the frame elements, such that the ordered frame can be written as {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded linear operator T and some vector phi?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$. For $a,b>0$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the translation operator $T_a g(x)=g(x-a)$ and the modulation operator $E_b g(x)=e^{2\pi i b x}g(x)$. The associated Gabor system is $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$. A countable family $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R})$ is called a frame if there exist constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ such that
$$A\|f\|^2\le\sum_{k\in I}|\langle f,f_k\rangle|^2\le B\|f\|^2,\qquad \forall f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}),$$
and a Riesz basis if it is the image of an orthonormal basis under a bounded invertible operator. The frame is called overcomplete if it is a frame but not a Riesz basis.

Question: Do there exist parameters $a,b>0$ and a window $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that the Gabor system $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, together with a bijection $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ (for some index set $I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ or $\mathbb{N}$) ordering its elements, a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$, and a vector $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, such that
$$\{f_k\}_{k\in I}=\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}\,?$$
status_search_result: For the index set $I=\mathbb{N}_0$, a complete negative answer has been established: any norm-bounded overcomplete frame, in particular any overcomplete Gabor frame, cannot be represented as the orbit $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\ge 0}$ of a bounded operator. For the two-sided index set $I=\mathbb{Z}$, only partial negative results are known (e.g. for specific classes of overcomplete Gabor frames the representation as an orbit of a bounded invertible operator is impossible), and the general question remains open.

context_brief: characterizing admissible orderings of Gabor frames
original_question: Given an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, which orderings {f_k}_{k in I} of its elements have the property that the ordered frame can be represented as an operator orbit {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for some bounded linear operator T? In other words, can one characterize exactly which permutations or sequential arrangements of the same Gabor frame yield a bounded generating operator?
self_contained_problem:
Let $g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and let $a, b > 0$. For $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, define the modulation and translation operators on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by
$$(E_{mb} h)(x) = e^{2\pi i m b x} h(x), \qquad (T_{na} h)(x) = h(x - na),$$
and consider the Gabor system $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b) = \{E_{mb} T_{na} g\}_{m,n \in \mathbb{Z}}$. Assume that $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, that is, it is a frame but not a Riesz basis.

Given a countable index set $I$ (either $\mathbb{N}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$) and a bijection $\sigma : I \to \mathbb{Z}^2$, set $f_k := E_{\sigma(k)_1 b} T_{\sigma(k)_2 a} g$ for $k \in I$, so that $\{f_k\}_{k \in I}$ is an enumeration (ordering) of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$.

Characterize precisely those orderings $\{f_k\}_{k \in I}$ of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ for which there exists a bounded linear operator $T : L^2(\mathbb{R}) \to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and an element $\varphi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$f_k = T^k \varphi \quad \text{for all } k \in I,$$
i.e., the ordered frame coincides with the orbit $\{T^k \varphi\}_{k \in I}$ of $\varphi$ under iteration of $T$.
status_search_result: The problem has seen significant partial progress but no full characterization. It is known that an overcomplete Gabor frame indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ cannot be represented as $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ with a bounded operator $T$. For the two-sided case ($I=\mathbb{Z}$), a general criterion states that an ordered frame $\{f_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is an orbit of a bounded bijective operator iff $\langle f_i, h_j\rangle = \langle f_{i+1}, h_{j+1}\rangle$ for all $i,j$, where $\{h_k\}$ is the canonical dual. Using this, follow-up work (Christensen–Hasannasab–Stoeva, Cabrelli–Molter–Romero, et al., 2018–2020) showed several negative results, e.g. when $ab \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ no ordering of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ comes from a bounded invertible operator. A complete characterization of admissible orderings remains open in general.

context_brief: universal ordering for bounded Gabor representations
original_question: Is there a single universal ordering rule {f_k}_{k in I} that works for every overcomplete Gabor frame that admits some bounded-operator orbit representation, so that whenever a frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is of a type covered by the previous existence question, arranging its elements according to that one rule always yields {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded operator T?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For $a,b>0$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, the associated Gabor system is
$$\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}},\qquad (T_x f)(t)=f(t-x),\ (E_y f)(t)=e^{2\pi i y t}f(t).$$
Such a system is called a Gabor frame if there exist constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ with
$$A\|f\|^2\le\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}|\langle f,E_{mb}T_{na}g\rangle|^2\le B\|f\|^2\qquad(f\in L^2(\mathbb{R})),$$
and is overcomplete if it remains a frame after removing any one element.

Given a sequence $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ indexed by an ordered set $I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, we say it is represented as an orbit of a bounded operator if there exist $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that $f_k=T^k\varphi$ for all $k\in I$.

Let $\mathcal{G}$ denote the class of overcomplete Gabor frames $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ that, after some bijective relabelling by an index set $I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, can be written as the orbit $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}$ of a bounded operator $T$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.

Question. Does there exist a single universal ordering rule — that is, a fixed scheme assigning to each Gabor frame in $\mathcal{G}$ a bijective enumeration $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ of its elements (depending only on the parameters $a,b$ and the window $g$ via this fixed rule) — such that for every frame in $\mathcal{G}$ the resulting enumeration $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ has the form $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}$ for some bounded operator $T$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and some $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$?
category_tag: Gabor frames and operator orbit representations
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Christensen, Hasannasab, and collaborators (e.g., "Orbits of bounded bijective operators and Gabor frames", 2020; "Frame properties of operator orbits", 2020; and later surveys) establishes strong constraints — for instance, overcomplete Gabor frames cannot be written as orbits $(T^n f_0)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of a bounded operator, and certain classes cannot even be ordered over $\mathbb{Z}$ as orbits of invertible bounded operators. However, no located source explicitly resolves the universal-ordering question for the class of overcomplete Gabor frames that do admit bounded-operator orbit representations; it appears to remain open.

context_brief: norm-bounded-below overcomplete operator orbits in Hilbert space
original_question: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H with an overcomplete frame {f_k}_{k=0}^infty whose vectors are uniformly bounded away from zero in norm and for which there is a bounded linear operator T from H to H such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k>=0? Equivalently, can an overcomplete frame that does not decay in norm still be generated as a one-sided bounded operator orbit?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. A sequence $\{f_k\}_{k=0}^\infty$ of vectors in H is called a frame for H if there exist constants $0 < A \le B < \infty$ such that
$$A\|f\|^2 \;\le\; \sum_{k=0}^\infty |\langle f, f_k\rangle|^2 \;\le\; B\|f\|^2 \qquad \text{for all } f \in H.$$
A frame is called overcomplete if it is not a Riesz basis, equivalently, if there exists at least one index $k_0$ such that $\{f_k\}_{k\ne k_0}$ is still a frame for H. The frame is said to be norm-bounded below if
$$\inf_{k\ge 0} \|f_k\| \;>\; 0.$$
Question: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H, a vector $f_0 \in H$, and a bounded linear operator $T : H \to H$ such that the orbit
$$\{f_k\}_{k=0}^\infty := \{T^k f_0\}_{k=0}^\infty$$
is an overcomplete frame for H that is norm-bounded below?
status_search_result: Subsequent works by Christensen, Hasannasab and collaborators (2018–2020) characterize frames representable as one-sided orbits $\{T^k f_0\}_{k\ge 0}$ of bounded operators, establish strong structural restrictions in the overcomplete case (the image chain of T must have finite length, and finite truncations after the index of stabilization remain frames), and show non-existence for special classes such as Gabor and wavelet frames represented by bounded bijective operators. None of the sources surveyed exhibit an explicit overcomplete, norm-bounded-below example of such an orbit, nor do they prove non-existence in full generality, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
original_question: Can out-of-equilibrium remnants and particle-specific freeze-out hierarchies be identified and measured well enough to reconstruct the dynamics of hadronisation, including how different reaction channels and hadronic cross sections cause different particle species to freeze out at different times and temperatures?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the late stages of an ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collision, in which a hot, dense fireball of strongly-interacting matter expands and cools, producing hadrons that are eventually detected. Two notions of decoupling are usually distinguished:

(i) Chemical freeze-out, the space-time hypersurface on which inelastic (number-changing) reactions cease, fixing the relative abundances (yields) of each hadron species.
(ii) Kinetic (thermal) freeze-out, the hypersurface on which elastic (momentum-changing) reactions cease, fixing the transverse-momentum spectra of each species.

Because different hadron species (e.g. pions, kaons, protons, multistrange baryons such as Ξ and Ω, light nuclei, charm hadrons) couple to the hadronic medium through reaction channels with very different cross sections, each species is expected in principle to freeze out on its own hypersurface, characterised by its own decoupling temperature T_i and time τ_i. Denote by 𝓗 = {(T_i, τ_i)}_i this particle-specific freeze-out hierarchy, and by 𝓡 the set of out-of-equilibrium remnants — deviations of yields, ratios, and momentum distributions from the predictions of a single global equilibrium freeze-out — that encode the underlying hadronisation dynamics.

Problem. Determine whether suitably chosen observables (in particular ratios of identified-particle yields, transverse-momentum spectra, fluctuations, and correlations of the species above) can be measured with sufficient precision and theoretically modelled with sufficient control to:

(a) detect statistically significant species-dependent differences (T_i, τ_i) ≠ (T_j, τ_j), thereby establishing the hierarchy 𝓗;

(b) extract from 𝓡 the dynamical information about reaction channels and hadronic cross sections that drives this hierarchy;

(c) thereby reconstruct the dynamics of hadronisation — that is, the time-ordered sequence of decouplings and the role of specific hadronic interactions — rather than only its time-integrated, equilibrium-averaged outcome.

Provide a quantitative framework (observables, estimators, and uncertainty budget) capable of carrying out (a)–(c), or prove an obstruction showing that hadronisation dynamics cannot be reconstructed in this way from currently accessible observables.
status_search_result: Subsequent literature has established partial evidence for a particle-specific freeze-out hierarchy: mass-dependent kinetic freeze-out and flavor-dependent (strange vs. non-strange) chemical freeze-out have been extracted from yield and pT-spectrum analyses at AGS/SPS/RHIC/LHC energies, and multiple-freeze-out (e.g. separate strange) scenarios are widely discussed. However, fully reconstructing hadronisation dynamics — including disentangling cross-section-driven channel-by-channel decoupling times and out-of-equilibrium remnants in a model-independent way — remains an active, unresolved program.
