original_question: Is there an algorithm that computes a (1+epsilon)-approximation for job-shop makespan minimization J||C_max in time f(m, epsilon) * poly(n), depending on the number of machines m and approximation parameter epsilon but only polynomially on the input size?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the job-shop scheduling problem with makespan objective, denoted J||C_max, defined as follows. We are given m machines M_1,...,M_m and n jobs J_1,...,J_n. Each job J_j consists of an ordered sequence of operations O_{j,1}, O_{j,2}, ..., O_{j,n_j}; each operation O_{j,k} must be processed non-preemptively on a prescribed machine μ(j,k) ∈ {M_1,...,M_m} for a prescribed integer time p_{j,k} > 0. A feasible schedule assigns to each operation O_{j,k} a starting time s_{j,k} ≥ 0 such that (i) for every job J_j and every k, s_{j,k+1} ≥ s_{j,k} + p_{j,k} (operations of a job are processed in the given order, without overlap), and (ii) for every machine M_i, the time intervals [s_{j,k}, s_{j,k}+p_{j,k}) over all operations with μ(j,k) = M_i are pairwise disjoint. The makespan is C_max = max_{j,k}(s_{j,k} + p_{j,k}), and the goal is to minimize C_max.

Let n denote the input size of an instance. Determine whether there exists an algorithm that, given any instance of J||C_max and any ε > 0, outputs a feasible schedule of makespan at most (1+ε)·OPT, where OPT is the optimum makespan, and runs in time f(m, ε) · poly(n) for some computable function f depending only on m and ε (i.e., a fixed-parameter tractable approximation scheme parameterized by the number of machines m, with only polynomial dependence on the rest of the input size).
status_search_result: The question asks whether J||C_max admits an FPT-approximation scheme parameterized by the number of machines m. Existing PTASs for job shop (Jansen–Solis-Oba–Sviridenko, and Feige–Scheideler's linear-time variant) require both the number of machines and the number of operations per job to be constant; no algorithm with running time f(m,ε)·poly(n) depending only on m and ε is known. Surveys on parameterized complexity of scheduling list this as an open problem, and no resolution was found in the literature search.

original_question: For the open-shop throughput problem O|p_ij=1, r_j|sum w_j U_j with unit-time operations and release dates, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following open-shop scheduling problem. There are $m$ machines $M_1,\dots,M_m$ and $n$ jobs $J_1,\dots,J_n$. Each job $J_j$ consists of $m$ operations $O_{1j},\dots,O_{mj}$, where operation $O_{ij}$ must be processed on machine $M_i$ and has unit processing time $p_{ij}=1$. The operations of a single job may be processed on their respective machines in any order, but no two operations of the same job can be processed simultaneously, and each machine processes at most one operation at a time. Each job $J_j$ has a release date $r_j\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ (no operation of $J_j$ may start before time $r_j$), a due date $d_j\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, and a nonnegative integer weight $w_j$. A schedule assigns to every operation $O_{ij}$ an integer start time $s_{ij}\ge r_j$ subject to the machine and job constraints; job $J_j$ is on time if all its operations finish by time $d_j$, in which case $U_j=0$, otherwise $U_j=1$. The objective is to minimize $\sum_{j=1}^n w_j U_j$, the weighted number of tardy jobs.

Question: Is this problem (denoted in standard scheduling notation $O\mid p_{ij}=1, r_j\mid \sum w_j U_j$) fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines $m$? Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm solving every instance in time $f(m)\cdot (n+\max_j(r_j+d_j+w_j))^{O(1)}$ for some computable function $f$?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a paper resolving this specific question (FPT status of the unit-time open-shop problem with release dates minimizing the weighted number of tardy jobs, parameterized by the number of machines). Related results exist (e.g., polynomial-time algorithms for fixed numbers of machines without release dates, and FPT results for parallel-machine variants), but none clearly settle this case in either direction.

paper_title: Revisiting the Arcade Learning Environment: Evaluation Protocols and Open Problems for General Agents
context_brief: Planning and learned models in ALE
original_question: How can one learn and use a model of Atari 2600 games in the Arcade Learning Environment that stays accurate over long rollouts, is fast enough to be useful for planning rather than slower than the emulator itself, and still supports effective planning when the learned model is imperfect and errors compound over time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE), a platform that exposes Atari 2600 games as reinforcement-learning tasks. At every discrete time step t, an agent observes a frame s_t (a 210×160 RGB image, possibly together with the 128 bytes of console RAM), selects an action a_t from the 18-element joystick action set, and receives a scalar reward r_t and next observation s_{t+1} produced by the underlying Stella emulator, which serves as the ground-truth dynamics. A learned forward model is a function f_θ that, given a state representation and an action, predicts the next state representation and the reward; rolling the model out for H steps means iteratively feeding the model's own predictions back as input to produce a length-H simulated trajectory.

Address the following three coupled questions.

(1) Long-horizon accuracy. Construct a learned model f_θ of the ALE dynamics whose H-step open-loop rollout error (measured, for instance, by per-pixel or per-feature prediction error and by predicted cumulative reward error against the true emulator trajectory generated by the same action sequence from the same initial state) remains small as H grows large, so that compounding errors do not render the rollouts unusable for decision making.

(2) Computational efficiency. Ensure that simulating one environment step with f_θ is faster, on standard hardware, than simulating one step with the Stella emulator itself, so that the learned model offers a real planning speedup over direct emulation.

(3) Planning with an imperfect model. Design a planning algorithm that uses such a learned (and necessarily imperfect) model to choose actions and that, despite compounding model errors, attains game-playing performance competitive with planning that has access to the true emulator, across a representative suite of Atari 2600 games.

Provide either a construction achieving (1)–(3) simultaneously together with a quantitative analysis, or a proof of impossibility under stated computational assumptions.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. SimPLe (Kaiser et al., ICLR 2020) demonstrated successful planning/training with a learned video model of Atari, and MuZero (Schrittwieser et al., 2019/2020) achieved state-of-the-art Atari performance by planning with a learned latent model, addressing the imperfect-model planning aspect via value bootstrapping and short rollouts. However, learned pixel-level models typically remain slower than the Stella emulator and still suffer from compounding errors over long open-loop rollouts, so the combined goal of a fast, long-horizon-accurate Atari model usable for general planning is not fully resolved.

paper_title: Revisiting the Arcade Learning Environment: Evaluation Protocols and Open Problems for General Agents
original_question: How can an Arcade Learning Environment agent transfer knowledge across Atari games so as to reduce the number of samples needed to learn new games, including games that are only loosely analogous, while automatically determining when transfer is beneficial versus when it causes negative transfer, and while separating representation transfer from policy transfer instead of conflating both inside a single expert-pretrained neural-network approach?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE), a benchmark consisting of a large collection of Atari 2600 games, each modeled as a Markov decision process whose state is given by raw screen pixels (and optionally the 128 bytes of console RAM), whose action set is the 18 joystick/button combinations, and whose reward is derived from the in-game score. A learning agent interacts with one or more of these MDPs by sampling trajectories and updating its parameters, with sample complexity measured by the number of environment frames consumed before the agent reaches a target level of performance.

Design and analyze a transfer-learning algorithm for ALE agents satisfying all of the following requirements:

1. (Cross-game transfer.) Given experience accumulated on a source set of Atari games G_src = {g_1, ..., g_k}, the algorithm produces an initialization (and/or auxiliary structures) for learning a target Atari game g_target so that the number of target-game samples required to reach a fixed performance threshold is provably or empirically smaller than for an agent trained on g_target from scratch.

2. (Loosely analogous games.) The reduction in sample complexity must hold not only when g_target is mechanically similar to games in G_src but also when g_target shares only loose, abstract structure with the source games (e.g., differing sprites, dynamics, and reward structures).

3. (Automatic detection of useful transfer.) The algorithm must include a procedure that, given (G_src, g_target), automatically decides whether transferring from G_src to g_target is expected to be beneficial or harmful, so as to avoid negative transfer (the case in which using G_src strictly increases target sample complexity compared with learning g_target from scratch).

4. (Decoupling representation and policy transfer.) The algorithm must separate the transferred quantities into (i) a representation component (a state-feature map φ : S → R^d) and (ii) a policy/value component (a mapping from features to actions or action-values), and must allow each component to be transferred independently of the other, rather than transferring a single monolithic neural network jointly encoding both.

Provide such an algorithm together with a theoretical or empirical guarantee on ALE establishing properties (1)–(4).
status_search_result: The problem is a broad open research challenge in deep reinforcement learning. While many partial advances on transfer in Atari/ALE exist (e.g., progressive networks, successor features, PopArt/IMPALA multi-task agents, Agent57, and later foundation-model-style RL agents), no single method is established as solving all four requirements simultaneously—particularly automatic detection of beneficial transfer and a clean separation of representation and policy transfer with guarantees on loosely analogous games. The status is therefore best described as open, with partial progress.

paper_title: Open problem in orthogonal polynomials
context_brief: First polynomial class and its discrete versions
original_question: For the four-parameter orthogonal polynomial H_n(z; μ, ν, α, θ) on the real line, together with the two discrete versions that the source denotes by h_n(k; μ, ν, α, β) and g_n(k; μ, ν, β, N), can one derive a full analytic description from their current definition by three-term recursion relations and initial values alone? In particular, determine their weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, forward/backward shift operator relations, zeros, and a closed-form representation, for example in terms of hypergeometric functions.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following three families of polynomials, each defined solely by a three-term recurrence relation together with the initial value P_0 = 1.

(A) A continuous four-parameter family { H_n(z; μ, ν, α, θ) }_{n=0}^{∞} of polynomials in a real variable z ∈ ℝ, depending on real parameters μ, ν, α, θ (with the parameter ranges that make the recursion produce a positive-definite moment problem on the real line).

(B) A discrete four-parameter family { h_n(k; μ, ν, α, β) }_{n=0}^{∞} of polynomials in the discrete variable k ∈ {0, 1, 2, …}, again specified by a three-term recurrence and h_0 ≡ 1 (countably infinite spectrum case).

(C) A finite discrete four-parameter family { g_n(k; μ, ν, β, N) }_{n=0}^{N} in the variable k ∈ {0, 1, …, N}, specified by a three-term recurrence and g_0 ≡ 1 (finite spectrum case of size N+1).

In each of the three cases, the recurrence coefficients are explicit rational/algebraic functions of n and the parameters (assumed given), and the recursion alone determines the polynomials.

Problem. Starting only from the three-term recurrence relations and initial conditions defining H_n, h_n, and g_n, derive a complete analytic description of these polynomials. In particular:

1. Determine the orthogonality measure / weight function for each family (continuous weight on ℝ for H_n, discrete weights with countably infinite or finite support for h_n and g_n, respectively), and prove the corresponding orthogonality relations.
2. Obtain a generating function for each family.
3. Derive the asymptotic behavior of the polynomials as n → ∞ (and, where relevant, as the variable tends to infinity).
4. Establish a Rodrigues-type formula expressing the n-th polynomial via a finite-difference or differential operator applied to the weight.
5. Find forward and backward shift operator relations linking the polynomials of degree n and n ± 1 with shifted parameters.
6. Describe the location and properties of the zeros.
7. Obtain a closed-form representation, for example as a (possibly terminating) generalized hypergeometric series _pF_q or basic hypergeometric series.

Provide such a complete analytic theory, or prove obstructions explaining why some of these objects cannot be expressed in standard closed form.
status_search_result: No published work was found that supplies a complete analytic theory (weight, generating function, Rodrigues formula, shift operators, closed-form hypergeometric representation) for these polynomials. The families remain primarily defined through their three-term recursions in the available literature, and the call for experts to derive these properties does not appear to have been answered in full. Partial progress on related Alhaidari-type polynomial families exists, but a comprehensive solution for H_n, h_n, and g_n has not been verified.

paper_title: Autonomous Agents Modelling Other Agents: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
original_question: How can an autonomous agent reconstruct models of another agent's behaviour when the interaction is only partially observable, meaning that observations of environment states and other agents' actions may be incomplete, noisy, or missing, especially in settings where observation probabilities cannot be supplied from domain knowledge in advance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a sequential interaction between an autonomous learning agent A and one or more other agents acting in a shared stochastic environment. The environment is modelled as a partially observable stochastic game with state space S, joint action space A = A_1 × ... × A_n, transition kernel T(s' | s, a), and, for the learner A, an observation space O together with an observation kernel O(o | s, a). At each time step t, the learner A executes an action and receives an observation o_t ∈ O that may give incomplete, noisy, or missing information about the true environment state s_t and about the actions taken by the other agents. The learner's goal is to reconstruct, from the observation history (o_1, o_2, ..., o_t), behavioural models of the other agents — i.e. policies π_j : H_j → Δ(A_j) (or any equivalent representation such as finite-state controllers, recursive belief hierarchies, or learned function approximators) that predict each other agent j's action given that agent's interaction history H_j.

Develop a general methodology, with provable guarantees, for solving the following problem:

Given only the learner's observation history under such a partially observable stochastic game, and without being supplied a priori with the observation kernel O (so that observation probabilities cannot be assumed known from domain knowledge), construct estimators π̂_j of the other agents' behavioural models such that, as the interaction length grows, π̂_j converges (in an appropriate metric on policies, e.g. expected KL divergence over reachable histories) to the true π_j. Equivalently: characterize identifiability conditions on (T, O, π_1, ..., π_n) under which behavioural models of the other agents are uniquely recoverable from partial, noisy observations when the observation kernel itself is unknown, and provide constructive learning algorithms that achieve this recovery with finite-sample guarantees.
status_search_result: The problem of reconstructing behavioural models of other agents under partial observability — particularly without prior knowledge of observation probabilities — is identified as an outstanding research direction in the agent-modelling literature. Subsequent work has addressed special cases (e.g. I-POMDPs with known observation models, opponent modelling in POMGs with deep learning), but no general solution with identifiability guarantees and unknown observation kernel appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Autonomous Agents Modelling Other Agents: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
original_question: Given that another agent's decisions may depend on only a small and initially unknown subset of a large interaction history or high-dimensional state description, how can one efficiently discover the factors that are actually relevant to that agent's decision making without assuming they are known beforehand, including every possible factor, or using an exhaustive combinatorial search?
self_contained_problem:
Let A be an agent interacting in an environment whose observable state at time t is described by a high-dimensional feature vector x_t ∈ X ⊆ ℝ^d, and let h_t = (x_1, a_1, …, x_{t-1}, a_{t-1}, x_t) denote the interaction history up to time t, where a_s ∈ A denotes A's action at time s. Suppose that A follows an unknown stationary policy π: H → Δ(A) on histories, but that there exists an unknown subset S* ⊆ {1, …, d} of feature indices, together with an unknown window length k* ≪ t, such that π depends only on the projection π_{S*,k*}(h_t) of the last k* states onto coordinates indexed by S*; that is, π(h_t) = π̃(π_{S*,k*}(h_t)) for some function π̃. An observer can collect i.i.d. samples (h_t, a_t) drawn from A's interaction with the environment, but does not know S*, k*, or π̃, and cannot assume that |S*| or k* is given.

Design an algorithm that, with high probability, recovers S* and k* (or a minimal sufficient set in the sense of conditional independence a_t ⊥ x_t \ S* | x_{t,S*}) using a number of samples and a runtime that scale polynomially in d, in the true |S*|, and in 1/ε for a target predictive accuracy ε, and that strictly avoids exhaustive combinatorial search over subsets of {1, …, d}. Either provide such an algorithm with provable guarantees on sample and computational complexity, or prove a lower bound showing no such algorithm exists under stated assumptions on π̃.
status_search_result: The problem of efficiently discovering the relevant decision factors of another agent—without prior knowledge, without enumerating all factors, and without exhaustive combinatorial search—is described as a significant open question in agent-modeling surveys, and no general solution with provable polynomial-sample, polynomial-time guarantees appears to be established. Related work on feature selection, sparse regression, and inverse reinforcement learning addresses special cases, but a general-purpose method tailored to agent-modeling under unknown sparse history dependence remains open.

paper_title: Autonomous Agents Modelling Other Agents: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
original_question: How can an autonomous agent learn to identify, track, and predict another agent's behaviour when that behaviour may change during the interaction—for example because the other agent is adapting, learning, switching strategies, or is human—rather than remaining fixed or stationary throughout the encounter?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an autonomous agent A interacting over discrete time steps t = 1, 2, ... with another agent B in a shared environment modeled as a (partially observable) stochastic game. At each time t, agent A observes some signal o_t (which may include B's actions, joint outcomes, and environmental state) and must maintain a model M_t of agent B that allows A to (i) identify B's current behavioural type or policy, (ii) track changes to that policy over time, and (iii) predict B's next action a_t^B given history.

Unlike the standard assumption that B follows a fixed (stationary) policy π : S → Δ(A_B), suppose instead that B's policy is non-stationary: B may be adapting, learning, deliberately switching among a (possibly unknown) set of strategies, or may be a human whose behaviour drifts over time. Formally, B's behaviour is a sequence of policies (π_t)_{t≥1} that may change as a function of the interaction history, with no a priori bound on the number, frequency, or magnitude of such changes, and with the underlying class of policies not assumed to be known to A.

Concretely, give an algorithm that produces predictions p_t(a | history) of B's next action together with performance guarantees—e.g., bounds on online predictive regret or KL-loss relative to the true non-stationary policy sequence (π_t), detection guarantees for changes in π_t, and consistency guarantees for any inferred latent type or strategy index—under the weakest possible structural assumptions on how π_t may evolve. Equivalently: characterize the structural conditions on the variation of (π_t) that are necessary and sufficient for such guarantees to be achievable.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a significant open problem in agent modelling: designing methods that effectively identify, track, and predict another agent's changing (non-stationary) behaviour. While related subproblems (non-stationary bandits, opponent modelling in games, change-point detection, meta-learning against adaptive opponents) have substantial partial results, no general framework with provable guarantees under arbitrary behavioural change exists, and recent surveys continue to list this as an unresolved challenge.

paper_title: Autonomous Agents Modelling Other Agents: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
original_question: How can one design efficient methods for modelling other agents in open multiagent systems, where agents may enter and leave the system at arbitrary times without notifying others, the number of agents is not fixed, and knowledge from past systems may need to be transferred into new ones?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open multiagent system defined as follows. Time proceeds in discrete steps t = 0, 1, 2, .... At each time t there is a finite set of agents A_t, and the cardinality |A_t| is not fixed in advance: agents may enter or leave A_t at arbitrary times without announcing their arrival or departure to the remaining agents. Each agent i ∈ A_t selects actions according to an unknown (possibly time-varying) policy π_i, and a designated modelling agent m observes only a sequence of joint observations and actions of those agents currently present.

A modelling method for agent m is an algorithm that, at each time t, maintains for every other agent j ∈ A_t \ {m} a predictive model π̂_j of that agent's behaviour, using only the history of observations available to m up to time t. The modelling method must additionally support transfer: knowledge accumulated about agents encountered in past systems (S_1, S_2, ..., S_k) may be reused to bootstrap models in a new system S_{k+1} whose agent population is unknown and possibly disjoint.

Design such a modelling method that is efficient in the following senses simultaneously:
  (i) its per-step computational and memory cost scales sublinearly in the cumulative number of agents ever encountered;
  (ii) its predictive accuracy, measured by the expected loss between π̂_j and π_j on observed actions, converges (in an appropriate sense) for every agent j who remains in the system long enough; and
  (iii) it correctly handles the entry of previously unseen agents and the departure of agents without prior notification, without catastrophic degradation of the models maintained for the remaining agents.

Provide either a constructive algorithm with provable guarantees of (i)–(iii), or prove an impossibility result delineating the limits of what any such modelling method can achieve.
status_search_result: Modelling other agents in open multiagent systems is widely regarded as an open research challenge. Recent work (e.g., Chandrasekaran et al. on I-POMDPs with open agent populations, and ongoing research on ad hoc teamwork and open ad hoc teamwork by Stone and collaborators) provides partial methods for special cases, but no general efficient method with the stated properties has been established.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: For Einstein's equations coupled to physically reasonable matter, can the weak cosmic censorship conjecture be proved in a mathematically precise form: namely, that generic nonsingular initial data do not evolve into naked singularities visible from infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a $4$-dimensional smooth Lorentzian manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g)\, g + \Lambda g = 8\pi T,$$
where the stress–energy tensor $T$ is required to satisfy a physically reasonable energy condition (e.g.\ the dominant energy condition) and to arise from a well-posed matter model (such as vacuum, a Maxwell field, or a massless scalar field). Consider the Cauchy problem for these equations with initial data $(\Sigma, h, K, \Psi)$, where $\Sigma$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $h$ a Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, $K$ a symmetric $2$-tensor, and $\Psi$ matter data, all required to satisfy the Einstein constraint equations and to be asymptotically flat and nonsingular.

Let $(M,g)$ denote the maximal globally hyperbolic development of such initial data. Say that $(M,g)$ contains a *naked singularity visible from infinity* if its maximal development is extendible in such a way that future null infinity $\mathcal{I}^+$ is incomplete, i.e.\ there exist future-directed null geodesics reaching infinity whose causal past fails to have compact closure in the maximal development.

status_search_result: The weak cosmic censorship conjecture, formulated by Penrose in 1969, remains a major open problem in mathematical general relativity. Important partial results exist (e.g., Christodoulou's proof for the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field system, and recent work on extremal black hole instabilities), but no general proof or disproof is known.

original_question: Can the Penrose inequality relating the area of an apparent horizon to the ADM mass be proved in the general case, or can one construct a genuine counterexample showing that the expected lower bound fails?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $(M,g,k)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations, that is, a complete 3-manifold $M$ with Riemannian metric $g$ and symmetric (0,2)-tensor $k$ (the second fundamental form of an embedding into a spacetime), such that outside a compact set $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus B$ and in the asymptotic coordinates
$$g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}),\qquad \partial g_{ij} = O(|x|^{-2}),\qquad k_{ij} = O(|x|^{-2}),\qquad \partial k_{ij} = O(|x|^{-3}),$$
with the usual decay of scalar curvature and of $\mathrm{div}(k)-d(\mathrm{tr}\,k)$ ensuring a well-defined ADM mass
$$m_{\mathrm{ADM}} = \frac{1}{16\pi}\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}\!\bigl(\partial_j g_{ij}-\partial_i g_{jj}\bigr)\,\nu^i\,dA.$$
Assume the dominant energy condition
$$\mu \ge |J|_g, \qquad \mu := \tfrac12\bigl(R_g+(\mathrm{tr}_g k)^2-|k|_g^2\bigr),\quad J := \mathrm{div}_g(k-(\mathrm{tr}_g k)g).$$
Let $\Sigma \subset M$ be an outermost apparent horizon, i.e. an outermost closed 2-surface satisfying $H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma k = 0$ (future trapped) or $H_\Sigma - \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma k = 0$ (past trapped), and let $A$ denote its area.

Problem. Either prove the Penrose inequality
$$m_{\mathrm{ADM}} \;\ge\; \sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}$$
in this general (non–time-symmetric) setting, or construct an asymptotically flat initial data set $(M,g,k)$ satisfying the dominant energy condition and containing an outermost apparent horizon for which the inequality fails.

The general non–time-symmetric (full spacetime) Penrose inequality remains open. Recent work in 2024–2025 has produced unconditional spacetime Penrose-type inequalities with universally valid but non-sharp lower bounds, and Penrose-type inequalities under additional hypotheses (static, integral energy conditions, matter density), but the sharp general conjecture with full rigidity is not resolved.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Does the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, in which weak turbulence transfers energy to high frequencies and triggers black-hole formation, persist or change qualitatively once one goes beyond the spherically symmetric scalar-field model to more general perturbations and matter models?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of (d+1)-dimensional Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, i.e. the maximally symmetric Lorentzian solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations with negative cosmological constant Λ < 0. With reflecting boundary conditions imposed at conformal infinity, AdS behaves as a confining cavity in which finite-energy perturbations cannot disperse to infinity.

It has been conjectured that AdS is nonlinearly unstable: arbitrarily small generic perturbations evolve so that energy is transferred via a weakly turbulent cascade from low to arbitrarily high frequency modes, eventually producing a trapped surface and hence a black hole. This conjecture is strongly supported in the spherically symmetric model of Einstein gravity coupled to a real massless scalar field.

Question. Determine whether this conjectured nonlinear instability of AdS — together with its weakly turbulent high-frequency cascade and black-hole formation mechanism — persists, qualitatively changes, or fails when one moves beyond the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field setting to:
(i) purely gravitational (non-spherically symmetric) perturbations of AdS governed by the vacuum Einstein equations with Λ < 0;
(ii) perturbations breaking both spherical and axial symmetry;
(iii) AdS coupled to other matter models (e.g. perfect fluids, gauge fields, complex scalars, etc.).

In particular, characterize which classes of small initial data on AdS lead to black-hole formation in finite time and which lead to globally regular, possibly quasi-periodic, solutions, and identify the structural features (resonances, normal-mode spectrum, symmetry assumptions) responsible for any qualitative differences from the spherically symmetric scalar case.
status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Numerical and perturbative work beyond spherical symmetry (Dias–Horowitz–Santos and follow-ups, 2016–2017) shows that the gravitational sector behaves qualitatively differently from the spherical scalar case: many normal modes cannot be extended to periodic horizonless solutions, and resonance structures differ. Recent work (2025) on slowly rotating Kerr-AdS provides further nonlinear instability results without symmetry, but a complete characterization of AdS nonlinear (in)stability for general perturbations and matter models has not been established.

original_question: Are higher-dimensional black holes stable under perturbations, and if not, what instabilities and end states arise in the nonlinear regime?

(a) Establish linear (mode) stability or instability of the solution under gravitational perturbations preserving the asymptotic conditions.
(b) When linear instability is present (e.g., the Gregory–Laflamme mode for sufficiently thin black strings, ultra-spinning Myers–Perry black holes, thin black rings), establish nonlinear instability rigorously and identify the final (end-state) configuration of the nonlinear evolution: does the horizon pinch off in finite asymptotic time leading to a naked singularity (violating weak cosmic censorship in $D \geq 5$), settle into a non-uniform stationary black object, or fragment into multiple black holes?
(c) For solutions believed to be stable (e.g., the higher-dimensional Schwarzschild–Tangherlini black hole), prove full nonlinear asymptotic stability of the family under small perturbations of initial data.

original_question: How structurally stable are generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities when one includes the matter fields expected in the early universe, such as scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and more general matter content, rather than restricting to vacuum or simplified matter models?

Concretely: prove or disprove that there exists an open set (in a suitable topology on initial data or on asymptotic data at the singularity) of inhomogeneous solutions to the Einstein–matter system whose approach to the spacelike singularity is described by the BKL/Kasner-like asymptotics, and characterize how the matter content (scalar, electromagnetic, fluid, etc.) modifies the local oscillatory or monotone regime.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: For binary black-hole systems, can one determine gravitational-wave emission and waveform predictions with sufficient precision for optimal signal detection and parameter extraction in gravitational-wave astronomy?
self_contained_problem:
In general relativity, a binary black-hole system consists of two black holes inspiraling under mutual gravitational attraction, eventually merging and ringing down to a single Kerr black hole. The system radiates gravitational waves whose two polarization time series h_+(t) and h_×(t) (the gravitational-wave strain) depend on the intrinsic parameters (component masses m_1, m_2, spin vectors S_1, S_2, eccentricity e, etc.) and extrinsic parameters (sky location, distance, inclination, polarization angle, time and phase of coalescence).

For a gravitational-wave detector (such as a kilometer-scale interferometer) with one-sided noise power spectral density S_n(f), the standard noise-weighted inner product on signal space is
   ⟨a|b⟩ = 4 Re ∫_0^∞ ã(f) b̃*(f) / S_n(f) df,
and the match between two waveforms is the inner product of their normalized versions, maximized over time and phase shifts. A waveform family h_model(λ) is said to be sufficiently accurate for detection if its mismatch with the true signal h_true(λ) satisfies 1 − match(h_model, h_true) ≲ 1/(2 ρ²) where ρ is the signal-to-noise ratio, and sufficiently accurate for parameter estimation if the systematic bias it induces on each parameter λ_i is smaller than the corresponding statistical uncertainty σ_i for the relevant detector network and SNR regime.

Problem. Provide a theoretical/numerical prescription that, given any point λ in the physically relevant parameter space of binary black holes (including arbitrary mass ratio, arbitrary precessing spins, eccentricity, and the full inspiral–merger–ringdown), produces gravitational-wave waveform predictions h_+(t; λ), h_×(t; λ) that meet both the detection-accuracy and parameter-estimation-accuracy criteria above for current and next-generation gravitational-wave observatories, and quantifies and controls the modeling error throughout this parameter space.
category_tag: Gravitational waveforms from binary black holes
status_search_result: The problem is actively being addressed but remains open in full generality. Effective-one-body, phenomenological, and numerical-relativity surrogate waveform models cover much of the quasi-circular aligned-spin and precessing parameter space, and have been used successfully in LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing runs. However, recent work (2023–2026) shows that waveform-model systematics remain a leading concern: regions of high mass ratio, strong precession, eccentricity, and high SNR still exhibit biases exceeding statistical uncertainties, motivating ongoing development of eccentric numerical-relativity surrogates, accuracy-aware Bayesian inference, and improved precessing models. The general goal of waveforms accurate enough across the entire parameter space for next-generation detectors is not yet achieved.

paper_title: Open Questions in the Understanding of Strangeness Production in HIC – Experiment Perspective
original_question: Across heavy-ion collision energies ranging from sub-threshold beam energies through SPS, RHIC, and LHC energies, what is the full energy dependence of strangeness enhancement, especially for rare multi-strange strange and anti-strange hadrons such as Ξ and Ω, when the enhancement factor is defined by comparing strange-particle yields in nucleus-nucleus collisions with those in proton-proton collisions?
self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion physics, the strangeness enhancement factor for a strange hadron species $h$ at center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ is defined by
$$E_h(\sqrt{s_{NN}}) \;=\; \frac{1}{\langle N_{\text{part}}\rangle}\,\frac{\big(dN_h/dy\big)_{AA}}{\big(dN_h/dy\big)_{pp}},$$
where $(dN_h/dy)_{AA}$ and $(dN_h/dy)_{pp}$ denote midrapidity yields per event of species $h$ in nucleus–nucleus and proton–proton collisions respectively, and $\langle N_{\text{part}}\rangle$ is the mean number of participating nucleons in the AA collision.

Determine, as a quantitative function of $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ across the full range from sub-threshold beam energies through SPS, RHIC and LHC energies, the behavior of $E_h(\sqrt{s_{NN}})$ for the singly-strange and especially for the multi-strange (anti-)hadrons $h \in \{\Lambda,\bar\Lambda,\Xi^-,\bar\Xi^+,\Omega^-,\bar\Omega^+\}$. In particular, characterize the magnitude, monotonicity, and any non-monotonic structure of the enhancement for the doubly- and triply-strange species $\Xi$ and $\Omega$ (and their antiparticles) as a function of collision energy, and explain the underlying mechanism (e.g. canonical suppression of strangeness phase space, transition to a grand-canonical regime, or quark–gluon plasma formation) that governs this energy dependence.
status_search_result: The energy dependence of strangeness enhancement, especially for multi-strange Ξ and Ω hadrons, remains an active experimental and theoretical research topic. While individual measurements at SPS, RHIC and LHC show that enhancement grows with strangeness content and decreases with energy (consistent with canonical suppression at lower energies), a unified quantitative description across all energies is still under investigation, with new measurements (e.g. ALICE pp high-multiplicity, NA61/SHINE, RHIC BES) continuing to refine the picture.

paper_title: Open Questions in the Understanding of Strangeness Production in HIC – Experiment Perspective
original_question: At intermediate heavy-ion collision energies, especially SPS energies and below, how much of the observed strangeness enhancement can be generated by hadronic-medium mechanisms such as multi-step hadronic reactions, resonances, or multi-meson fusion processes rather than by partonic matter?
self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion collisions at intermediate center-of-mass energies (those of the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron and below, i.e. roughly √s_NN ≲ 17 GeV), an enhancement of strange-hadron yields per participating nucleon is observed in nucleus–nucleus collisions relative to elementary proton–proton reactions, with the enhancement being most pronounced for multi-strange baryons. Such an enhancement has historically been interpreted as a signature of a deconfined partonic phase (quark–gluon plasma). However, a dense hadronic medium can also generate additional strangeness through purely hadronic mechanisms, including: (i) multi-step inelastic hadronic reactions producing strange–antistrange pairs, (ii) excitation, propagation, and decay of baryonic and mesonic resonances carrying strangeness, and (iii) multi-meson fusion processes of the schematic form n_1 π + n_2 K + … → Y (with Y a strange or multi-strange (anti-)baryon), which respect strangeness conservation while bypassing high thresholds of binary reactions.

Problem. Provide a quantitative determination of the maximum fraction of the observed strangeness enhancement at SPS energies and below that can be accounted for by hadronic-medium mechanisms alone (multi-step hadronic reactions, resonance dynamics, and multi-meson fusion), as opposed to mechanisms requiring partonic degrees of freedom. Concretely, for each strange species s ∈ {K, Λ, Ξ, Ω, and their antiparticles} and each √s_NN in the SPS range, compute within a consistent hadronic transport framework that includes all of (i)–(iii) the predicted enhancement factor E_s^had(√s_NN), and compare it with the experimentally measured enhancement E_s^exp(√s_NN), thereby establishing whether E_s^had can saturate E_s^exp or whether a residual partonic contribution is required.
status_search_result: Recent literature indicates the question remains open. While multi-meson fusion in hadronic transport models has been shown to reduce the gap between hadronic predictions and measured (multi-)strange anti-baryon yields, a systematic and quantitative evaluation across SPS energies has not yet been completed, largely due to computational cost. Recent NA61/SHINE results (2025) and ongoing transport-model studies continue to investigate the issue without a definitive resolution.

paper_title: 50 Open Problems: Ultraproduct II1 factors
original_question: For a separable II_1 factor N and a positive scalar t, do N and its amplification N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits of Haar unitaries?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with unique normal faithful tracial state $\tau$. A unitary $u \in N$ is called a Haar unitary if $\tau(u^n) = 0$ for every nonzero integer $n$. Fix a free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and let $N^\omega$ denote the tracial ultrapower of $N$. Define an equivalence relation on the set of Haar unitaries of $N$ as follows: two Haar unitaries $u, v \in N$ are equivalent if there exist Haar unitaries $w_0, w_1, \ldots, w_k \in N^\omega$ with $w_0 = u$, $w_k = v$, and $[w_{i-1}, w_i] = 0$ for $i = 1, \ldots, k$ (a "sequential commutation path"). Call the equivalence classes the sequential commutation orbits of $N$.

For $t > 0$, let $N^t$ denote the amplification of $N$ (i.e., $p(N \otimes B(\ell^2))p$ for a projection $p$ of trace $t$ when $t \le 1$, with the standard extension for $t > 1$).

Question: For every separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$ and every $t > 0$, do $N$ and $N^t$ have the same number of sequential commutation orbits of Haar unitaries?
status_search_result: The notion of sequential commutation orbits for Haar unitaries in tracial von Neumann algebras was introduced recently, with the basic dichotomy (1 orbit vs. uncountably many) and structural results established for free group factors and Gamma factors. The question of invariance of the number of orbits under amplification appears as one of the listed open problems and no resolution was found in the search results.

paper_title: 50 Open Problems: Ultraproduct II1 factors
context_brief: Lifting free independence with uniform k-independence
original_question: If u,v are freely independent unitaries in the ultrapower N^U, can they be lifted to sequences of unitaries in N that are pairwise k-independent for every k?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual and faithful normal trace $\tau$, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. Form the tracial ultrapower $N^{\mathcal{U}} = \ell^{\infty}(\mathbb{N}, N)/\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{U}}$, where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{U}} = \{(x_n) : \lim_{n \to \mathcal{U}} \tau(x_n^* x_n) = 0\}$, equipped with the trace $\tau_{\mathcal{U}}([(x_n)]) = \lim_{n \to \mathcal{U}} \tau(x_n)$.

Recall that elements $a_1, \dots, a_m$ in a tracial von Neumann algebra $(M,\tau)$ are said to be free (freely independent) if the unital $*$-subalgebras they generate are free with respect to $\tau$ in the sense of Voiculescu. For an integer $k \geq 1$, two unitaries $x, y \in M$ are called $k$-independent (or free up to order $k$) if for every alternating product $w$ of length at most $k$ formed from centered powers $x^{n_1} - \tau(x^{n_1})$, $y^{m_1} - \tau(y^{m_1}), \dots$ with $n_i, m_i \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, one has $\tau(w) = 0$.

Suppose $u, v \in N^{\mathcal{U}}$ are freely independent unitaries. Do there exist representing sequences $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $(v_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of unitaries in $N$ with $u = [(u_n)]$ and $v = [(v_n)]$ such that, for every integer $k \geq 1$, the unitaries $u_n$ and $v_n$ are $k$-independent in $(N,\tau)$ for $\mathcal{U}$-almost every $n$?

paper_title: 50 Open Problems: Ultraproduct II1 factors
context_brief: Uniqueness of ultrapower embeddings up to unitary conjugacy
original_question: Is there a nonamenable separable II_1 factor N such that every pair of embeddings of N into its ultrapower N^U are conjugate by a unitary in N^U?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable II$_1$ factor with separable predual, normalized faithful trace $\tau_N$, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. The tracial ultrapower $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ is the II$_1$ factor obtained as the quotient of $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N},N)$ by the two-sided ideal of sequences $(x_n)$ with $\lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}} \tau_N(x_n^* x_n)=0$, equipped with the trace $\tau((x_n)) = \lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}} \tau_N(x_n)$. By an embedding of $N$ into $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ we mean a unital, trace-preserving $*$-homomorphism $\pi: N \hookrightarrow N^{\mathcal{U}}$. Two such embeddings $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are said to be unitarily conjugate in $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ if there exists a unitary $u \in N^{\mathcal{U}}$ with $\pi_2(x) = u\pi_1(x)u^*$ for every $x \in N$.

Recall that $N$ is amenable (equivalently, hyperfinite, isomorphic to the unique separable hyperfinite II$_1$ factor $\mathcal{R}$) if it admits an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional $*$-subalgebras with weakly dense union. Otherwise $N$ is called nonamenable.

Question: Does there exist a nonamenable separable II$_1$ factor $N$ such that for every free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, any two embeddings of $N$ into $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ are unitarily conjugate in $N^{\mathcal{U}}$?
status_search_result: A theorem of Jung (extended by Atkinson–Goldbring–Kunnawalkam Elayavalli) states that among Connes-embeddable separable II$_1$ factors, only the hyperfinite factor $\mathcal R$ has the property that all embeddings into its ultrapower are unitarily conjugate. Whether some non-Connes-embeddable (hence nonamenable) separable II$_1$ factor enjoys this "Jung property" is recognized as an open problem; recent work of Atkinson–Goldbring on the generalized Jung property and on non-embeddable factors resembling $\mathcal R$ explicitly leaves this question unresolved.

paper_title: 50 Open Problems: Ultraproduct II1 factors
original_question: For distinct integers m and n, are the free group factors L(F_m) and L(F_n) elementarily equivalent as II_1 factors?
self_contained_problem:
For a discrete group $G$, let $L(G)$ denote the group von Neumann algebra, that is, the von Neumann algebra generated by the left regular representation of $G$ on $\ell^2(G)$. When $G$ has infinite conjugacy classes (icc), $L(G)$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. Equip the class of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with the continuous first-order language of tracial von Neumann algebras (with sorts given by operator-norm balls, the *-algebra operations, the trace, and the $L^2$-metric induced by the trace). Two $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors $M$ and $N$ are called elementarily equivalent, written $M \equiv N$, if every closed formula in this language has the same value when interpreted in $M$ and in $N$.

For an integer $n \geq 2$, let $F_n$ denote the free group on $n$ generators; each $F_n$ is icc, and $L(F_n)$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor (the free group factor).

Question: For all integers $m, n \geq 2$ with $m \neq n$, is $L(F_m)$ elementarily equivalent to $L(F_n)$?
category_tag: II_1 factors and continuous model theory
status_search_result: The question of whether the free group factors $L(F_n)$ are elementarily equivalent for different $n$ (the $\mathrm{II}_1$-factor analogue of Tarski's problem) is widely cited as open. It is closely related to the famous free group factor isomorphism problem, which is itself unresolved. No proof of elementary equivalence (or non-equivalence) for $L(F_m), L(F_n)$ with $m \neq n$ appears in the literature; recent work in continuous model theory of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors (e.g., Farah–Hart–Sherman, Goldbring–Hart) discusses the problem as open, and a recent negative resolution to the $C^*$-algebraic Tarski problem (arXiv:2503.10505) does not address the $\mathrm{II}_1$-factor version.

paper_title: 50 Open Problems: Ultraproduct II1 factors
original_question: Let N_0 be an index-2 subfactor of an ultrapower N^U. Must N_0 be isomorphic to an ultraproduct ∏_{i→U} N_i where each N_i ⊂ N is an index-2 subfactor?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with normalized trace $\tau$, and let $\mathcal U$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$. Form the tracial ultrapower $N^{\mathcal U}$, defined as $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,N)/\mathcal I_{\mathcal U}$, where $\mathcal I_{\mathcal U}=\{(x_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,N):\lim_{n\to\mathcal U}\tau(x_n^*x_n)=0\}$; this is again a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. Recall that for an inclusion $A\subset B$ of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, the Jones index $[B:A]$ is defined via the coupling constant of the standard representation; an inclusion is said to be of index $2$ when $[B:A]=2$.

Suppose $N_0\subset N^{\mathcal U}$ is a subfactor of index $2$. Must there exist a sequence of index-$2$ subfactors $N_i\subset N$ such that
$$N_0 \;\cong\; \prod_{i\to\mathcal U} N_i$$
as subfactors of $N^{\mathcal U}$ (where the right-hand side denotes the tracial ultraproduct of the inclusions $N_i\subset N$)?
status_search_result: The question is posed in a recent (2025) compilation of fifty open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors as Problem 38. paper_title: 50 Open Problems: Ultraproduct II1 factors
context_brief: Embedding matrix amplifications into matrix ultraproducts
original_question: For an arbitrary II_1 factor M, does M_2(C) ⊗ M always embed into the tracial matrix ultraproduct M_U = ∏_{n→U} M_n(C)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$, and let $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of $n\times n$ complex matrices equipped with its normalized trace $\mathrm{tr}_n$. Form the tracial matrix ultraproduct
$$\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{U}} := \prod_{n\to\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C}),$$
i.e., the quotient of $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N},(M_n(\mathbb{C}),\mathrm{tr}_n))$ by the two-sided ideal of sequences $(x_n)$ with $\lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}}\mathrm{tr}_n(x_n^*x_n)=0$; this is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with trace $\tau((x_n)_{\mathcal{U}})=\lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}}\mathrm{tr}_n(x_n)$.

Recall that a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ is called Connes-embeddable if there exists a trace-preserving $*$-embedding $M\hookrightarrow \mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{U}}$ (equivalently, into an ultrapower of the hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor). It is known that the Connes embedding property fails for some $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

Question: For every $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ (with separable predual, equipped with its unique faithful normal tracial state), does there exist a trace-preserving unital $*$-embedding
$$M_2(\mathbb{C})\otimes M \;\hookrightarrow\; \mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{U}}\,?$$

(Note that if $M$ itself is Connes-embeddable, then so is $M_2(\mathbb{C})\otimes M$, and the embedding is automatic.)

While the Connes embedding problem itself has been resolved negatively (MIP*=RE, 2020), this weaker matrix-amplification variant — whether $M_2(\mathbb{C})\otimes M$ always embeds into the matrix ultraproduct — does not appear to be settled in the literature; web searches turn up no resolution.

original_question: Does there exist a II_1 factor N whose ultrapower N^U has a fundamental group that is not full?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, i.e., an infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra with trivial center admitting a unique faithful normal tracial state $\tau$. The fundamental group of $M$ is defined as
$$\mathcal{F}(M) = \{\, t \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} : M^t \cong M \,\},$$
where for $t>0$ the amplification $M^t$ is, up to isomorphism, $p(M\bar{\otimes} B(\ell^2))p$ for any projection $p$ of trace $t$ (with $B(\ell^2)$ equipped with its standard semifinite trace). $\mathcal{F}(M)$ is a subgroup of $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$.

Fix a free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$. The tracial ultrapower $M^{\mathcal{U}}$ is the $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor obtained as the quotient $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N},M)/\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{U}}$, where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{U}} = \{(x_n)_n : \lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}} \tau(x_n^* x_n) = 0\}$, equipped with the trace $\tau_{\mathcal{U}}((x_n)_n) = \lim_{n\to\mathcal{U}} \tau(x_n)$.

Call a subgroup $G \leq \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ full if $G = \mathbb{R}_{>0}$.

Question: Does there exist a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$ such that $\mathcal{F}(N^{\mathcal{U}}) \neq \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, i.e., the fundamental group of the ultrapower $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ is not full?

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Reverse direction of the perfectoid transfer theorem for decidability
original_question: Let p be a prime. The perfectoid transfer theorem of Kartas (2024) provides implications from decidability in positive characteristic to decidability in mixed characteristic: (a) if F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} (the perfect hull of F_p((t)), with t-adic valuation) has a decidable elementary or existential L_val(t)-theory, then Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) have decidable elementary or existential L_val-theories respectively; (b) if F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} has a decidable elementary or existential L_val(t)-theory, then Q_p^{ab} has a decidable elementary or existential L_val-theory. (Here L_val is the language of valued rings and L_val(t) adds a constant for t.) It is also known (from the tilt correspondence) that decidability in L_val transfers from perfectoid fields to their tilts, giving partial converses. The precise open question is: can the argument be improved to obtain decidability in L_val(t) on the positive characteristic side, given decidability in L_val on the mixed characteristic side? That is, if Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory (not merely L_val)? And if Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?
self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime. Let L_val denote the first-order language of valued rings, and let L_val(t) denote the expansion of L_val by a single constant symbol t. Consider the following valued fields:

- F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, the perfect hull of the Laurent series field F_p((t)), equipped with the t-adic valuation; the constant t in L_val(t) is interpreted as the uniformizer.
- F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞}, the perfect hull of F_p^{ac}((t)) where F_p^{ac} is an algebraic closure of F_p, again with the t-adic valuation.
- Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}), the field obtained from Q_p by adjoining all p-power roots of unity, with its unique extension of the p-adic valuation.
- Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), the field obtained by adjoining all p-power roots of p to Q_p, with its unique extension of the p-adic valuation.
- Q_p^{ab}, the maximal abelian extension of Q_p, with its unique extension of the p-adic valuation.

It is known that decidability of the L_val-theory transfers from each of these mixed-characteristic perfectoid fields to its positive-characteristic tilt (so that L_val-decidability of Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) implies L_val-decidability of F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, and L_val-decidability of Q_p^{ab} implies L_val-decidability of F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞}).

Question: Can this transfer be strengthened to the language L_val(t) with a named uniformizer? Specifically:

(i) If Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory? Likewise, if Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?

(ii) If Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?

The analogous questions for existential theories are also asked.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a December 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields, building on Kartas's perfectoid transfer theorem (2024). No resolution has been located; the converse with a named uniformizer t appears to remain open.

Let F_p(t) be the rational function field in one variable t over F_p, with the t-adic valuation v_t (which sends a rational function to the order of vanishing at t = 0). Let (F_p(t)^h, v_t) denote the henselization of (F_p(t), v_t), and let (F_p((t)), v_t) denote the formal Laurent series field over F_p with its t-adic valuation. It is known that (F_p(t)^h, v_t) is existentially closed in (F_p((t)), v_t) in the language L_val of valued rings. Is (F_p(t)^h, v_t) an elementary substructure of (F_p((t)), v_t) in L_val (i.e., do they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences in L_val)?

Let $p$ be a prime number and let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be the finite field with $p$ elements. Let $(\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h, v_t)$ denote the henselization of $(\mathbb{F}_p(t), v_t)$ inside an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{F}_p(t)$, and let $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$ denote the field of formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with its $t$-adic valuation. Consider these as structures in the first-order language $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}$ of valued rings (a language for rings together with a predicate or sort for the valuation ring/valuation). It is known that $(\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h, v_t)$ is existentially closed in $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}$.

context_brief: Completeness of (A) + extremality as axiom system for F_p((t))
original_question: Let p be a prime and F_p the field with p elements. An extremal valued field is a valued field (K, v) such that for every multivariate polynomial f(X_1, ..., X_n) over K, the set {v(f(a_1,...,a_n)) | a_1,...,a_n in O_K} (where O_K is the valuation ring) has a maximal element in vK union {infinity}. This is an L_val-elementary axiom scheme. The L_val-elementary axiom system (A) is: 'henselian defectless valued field of positive characteristic with value group a Z-group and residue field F_p.' It is known (Kuhlmann 2001) that (A) alone is not complete. It is also known (Azgin-Kuhlmann-Pop 2012) that F_p((t)) is an extremal field. Is the axiom system (A) together with the extremality axiom scheme — that is, the theory of henselian defectless valued fields of positive characteristic with Z-group value group, residue field F_p, and extremality — a complete axiom system for the L_val-theory of F_p((t))?

Let $p$ be a prime and let $\mathbb{F}_p$ denote the field with $p$ elements. Work in the language $L_{\mathrm{val}}$ of valued fields. For a valued field $(K,v)$ write $\mathcal{O}_K$ for its valuation ring and $vK$ for its value group.

Call $(K,v)$ extremal if for every $n\ge 1$ and every polynomial $f(X_1,\dots,X_n)\in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, the set
$$\{\,v(f(a_1,\dots,a_n)) : a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathcal{O}_K\,\}\subseteq vK\cup\{\infty\}$$
attains a maximum. Extremality is expressible by an $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-elementary axiom scheme.

Let (A) be the $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-axiom system asserting that $(K,v)$ is a henselian, defectless valued field of characteristic $p>0$ whose value group $vK$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-group (i.e. elementarily equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}$ as an ordered abelian group) and whose residue field is $\mathbb{F}_p$.

It is known that (A) alone is not complete, and that the field $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ of formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with the $t$-adic valuation is extremal and satisfies (A).

Question: Is the theory consisting of (A) together with the extremality axiom scheme a complete axiomatization of the $L_{\mathrm{val}}$-theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$?

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Extremality of the coarse component in a composition of valuations
original_question: A valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every multivariate polynomial f(X_1,...,X_n) over K, the set {v(f(a_1,...,a_n)) | a_i in O_K} has a maximal element in vK union {infinity}. A valuation v can be written as a composition v = w ∘ w-bar, meaning w is a coarsening of v and w-bar is the valuation induced by v on the residue field Kw of w. It is known that if v = w ∘ w-bar is extremal, then the finer component w-bar is also extremal. Does it follow that the coarser component w is also extremal?
self_contained_problem:
A valued field $(K,v)$ consists of a field $K$ together with a valuation $v\colon K\to vK\cup\{\infty\}$, where $vK$ is the value group and $\mathcal{O}_K=\{a\in K:v(a)\geq 0\}$ is the valuation ring. The field $(K,v)$ is called extremal if for every $n\geq 1$ and every polynomial $f(X_1,\dots,X_n)\in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, the set
$$\{v(f(a_1,\dots,a_n)) : a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathcal{O}_K\}\subseteq vK\cup\{\infty\}$$
attains a maximum.

A coarsening of $v$ is a valuation $w$ on $K$ whose valuation ring contains $\mathcal{O}_K$. Given such a coarsening $w$, the valuation $v$ induces a valuation $\overline{w}$ on the residue field $Kw$ of $w$, and one writes $v=w\circ\overline{w}$.

It is known that if $v=w\circ\overline{w}$ and $(K,v)$ is extremal, then the induced valued residue field $(Kw,\overline{w})$ is extremal.

Question: Does it follow, under the same hypothesis, that the coarsening $(K,w)$ is also extremal?

The standard references on extremal valued fields (Azgin–Kuhlmann–Pop and Kuhlmann's "Notes on extremal and tame valued fields") establish that the finer component $\overline{w}$ inherits extremality, but no published result is found establishing or refuting extremality of the coarsening $w$.

paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
context_brief: Does hypothesis (R4) hold? (Large fields existentially closed in function fields with rational place)
original_question: Let K be a field. A field K is called large if it is existentially closed in the power series field K((t)) in the language of rings. Hypothesis (R4) states: for an arbitrary field K, if a function field F|K (a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree at least 1) admits a K-rational place (a valuation on F with residue field isomorphic to K), then K is existentially closed in F. It is known that local uniformization of rational places of arbitrary function fields (in all characteristics and all dimensions) implies (R4). By the work of Hironaka, local uniformization holds in characteristic 0. It is also known (Anscombe-Dittmann-Fehm 2023) that if (R4) holds, then the existential L_val(t)-theory of F_p((t)) (the formal Laurent series field over F_p in variable t, with t-adic valuation) is decidable. Does hypothesis (R4) hold in general (i.e., for all fields K and all function fields F|K with a K-rational place, is K existentially closed in F)?
self_contained_problem:
A field $K$ is called large if it is existentially closed (in the language of rings) in the formal power series field $K((t))$. A function field over $K$ is a finitely generated field extension $F\mid K$ of transcendence degree at least $1$. A $K$-rational place of $F$ is a place (equivalently, a valuation ring) of $F$ whose residue field is $K$-isomorphic to $K$.

Question: Is the following statement true? For every field $K$ and every function field $F\mid K$ that admits a $K$-rational place, the field $K$ is existentially closed in $F$ in the language of rings (i.e., every existential first-order $L_{\mathrm{ring}}$-formula with parameters from $K$ that has a solution in $F$ already has a solution in $K$).

original_question: Does the Palis dichotomy hold generically for central Cantor sets?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions and setup. For a sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive reals with $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n<\infty$, its achievement set is
$$E(a_n)=\Big\{\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n a_n : \varepsilon_n\in\{0,1\}\Big\}.$$
A central Cantor set is constructed from a sequence $(\alpha_n)\subset(0,1)$ as follows. Set $C_0=[0,1]$. Given $C_{n-1}$, which is a disjoint union of $2^{n-1}$ closed intervals each of the same length $\ell_{n-1}$, remove from the middle of each component an open interval of length $\alpha_n\ell_{n-1}$, obtaining $C_n$ as a union of $2^n$ closed intervals each of length $\ell_n=\ell_{n-1}(1-\alpha_n)/2$. The resulting set $C=\bigcap_{n\ge 1}C_n$ is the central Cantor set associated with $(\alpha_n)$. Equivalently, every central Cantor set coincides with the achievement set of the sequence $a_n=\ell_{n-1}(1-\alpha_n)/2$ (so that $C=E(a_n)$).

The space of central Cantor sets is naturally parametrized by sequences $(\alpha_n)\in(0,1)^{\mathbb N}$ endowed with the product topology, making it a Polish space; "generic" below means "for a residual (comeagre) set of parameters $(\alpha_n)$".

The Palis dichotomy for a pair $(C,C')$ of Cantor sets in $\mathbb R$ asserts that the arithmetic difference $C-C'=\{x-y:x\in C,\,y\in C'\}$ either has Lebesgue measure zero or contains an interval.

Problem. Is it true that for a generic pair of central Cantor sets $(C,C')$ (i.e., for a residual set of parameter pairs $((\alpha_n),(\alpha'_n))\in(0,1)^{\mathbb N}\times(0,1)^{\mathbb N}$), the Palis dichotomy holds: $C-C'$ either has Lebesgue measure zero or contains an interval?

paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
original_question: Classify achievement sets in ℝ², that is, sets of all subsums of absolutely convergent series in the plane, up to homeomorphism.
self_contained_problem:
For an absolutely summable sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, define its achievement set (set of subsums) by
$$E(x) \;=\; \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n \;:\; (\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\} \;\subseteq\; \mathbb{R}^2.$$
(For absolutely summable sequences each such series converges, so $E(x)$ is well defined; it is always compact.) On the real line, a classical result asserts that every such achievement set is homeomorphic to one of the following: a finite set, a finite disjoint union of nondegenerate compact intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval (a set homeomorphic to the union of the standard Cantor set together with the open intervals removed at even-indexed steps of its construction).

Problem. Classify, up to homeomorphism, all sets of the form $E(x)\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ as $(x_n)$ ranges over all absolutely summable sequences in $\mathbb{R}^2$. That is, give a complete list of homeomorphism types that arise as achievement sets of absolutely convergent series in the plane.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., on perturbations of multigeometric series in the plane and on achievement sets of series in $\mathbb{R}^2$) has produced at least seven distinct homeomorphism types and various structural results, but no complete classification of homeomorphism types of achievement sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is known. The problem is presented as open in current surveys and ongoing research.

original_question: Find usable sufficient conditions guaranteeing that a planar achievement set E(x_n, y_n) has nonempty interior.

$$E(x_n,y_n) = \left\{\left(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n,\; \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n y_n\right) : (\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2.$$

paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
context_brief: Possible ranges of the cardinality function
original_question: For which subsets C of {0,1,2,…,ω,c} does there exist an absolutely convergent series x such that the associated cardinality function F_x(t), which counts the number of subseries representations of t, has range exactly C?
self_contained_problem:
Let $x=(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be an absolutely convergent series of nonzero real numbers. Define the map
$$f:\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\to\mathbb{R},\qquad f(\varepsilon)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n x_n,$$
and for each $t\in\mathbb{R}$ let
$$F_x(t)=\operatorname{card}\bigl(f^{-1}(t)\bigr)\in\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak{c}\},$$
the number of subseries representations of $t$ (here $\omega$ denotes the countably infinite cardinal $\aleph_0$ and $\mathfrak c$ the cardinality of the continuum; it is known that $F_x(t)$ takes values only in $\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$). The range of $F_x$ is the set $\{F_x(t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\subseteq\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$.

Characterize precisely which subsets $C\subseteq\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$ arise as the range of $F_x$ for some absolutely convergent series $x$ — i.e., determine all $C$ for which there exists such a sequence $x$ with $\{F_x(t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}=C$.
status_search_result: The problem is listed among current open problems on achievement sets and cardinality functions of subseries. A recent preprint "Bounded ranges of cardinal functions" addresses partial cases (bounded ranges) but the full characterization of admissible ranges $C\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$ remains unresolved.

paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
original_question: Whenever the set {t ∈ ℝ : F_x(t) = c} is nonempty, must it contain a Cantor set; and likewise, whenever {t ∈ ℝ : F_x(t) = ω} is nonempty, must it contain a Cantor set?
self_contained_problem:
Let $x = (x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of nonzero real numbers such that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |x_n| < \infty$. Define the continuous map
$$f_x : \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad f_x\big((\varepsilon_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\big) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n,$$
and let the achievement set be $E(x) = f_x(\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}})$. For each $t \in \mathbb{R}$ define the multiplicity (cardinality) function
$$F_x(t) = \operatorname{card}\big(f_x^{-1}(t)\big),$$
which takes values in $\{0,1,2,\dots\} \cup \{\omega, \mathfrak{c}\}$ (where $\omega = \aleph_0$ and $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$).

By a Cantor set we mean a nonempty, compact, perfect, totally disconnected subset of $\mathbb{R}$.

Question: Is it true that for every such sequence $x$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item the set $\{t \in \mathbb{R} : F_x(t) = \mathfrak{c}\}$ is either empty or contains a Cantor set, and
\item the set $\{t \in \mathbb{R} : F_x(t) = \omega\}$ is either empty or contains a Cantor set?
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent (2025) survey on achievement sets of series. Web searches did not surface any published resolution of this dichotomy for the loci where the multiplicity function equals ω or 𝔠, so it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
context_brief: Centers of distances of adjoint Cantorvals
original_question: For q in (0, 1/2), compute the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval associated with the geometric central Cantor set E(q^n).
self_contained_problem:
For a nonempty subset $A$ of a metric space $(X,d)$, define the center of distances of $A$ by
$$S(A):=\{\alpha\in[0,\infty): \forall x\in A\ \exists y\in A\ \ d(x,y)=\alpha\}.$$

Given a sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of positive reals with $a_n\le \tfrac{1}{2}(a_{n-1}+\cdots)$ (so that the construction below produces a Cantor-type set in $[0,1]$), the central Cantor set $C=C(a_n)$ is constructed as follows. Start with $I_0=[0,1]$. At step $n\ge 1$, from each of the $2^{n-1}$ closed intervals of length $\ell_{n-1}$ obtained at the previous step, remove an open middle interval so that each remaining interval has length $a_n$; this yields $2^n$ closed intervals of length $a_n$ and an additional collection of $2^{n-1}$ open "gap" intervals removed at step $n$, whose union is denoted $G_n$. Then $C=\bigcap_{n\ge 0} I_n$, where $I_n$ is the union of the $2^n$ closed intervals at step $n$.

The adjoint Cantorval of $C$ is defined as
$$\widehat C := C\ \cup\ \bigcup_{n\in 2\mathbb{N}-1} G_n,$$
i.e., $C$ together with all gaps removed at odd-numbered steps.

For $q\in(0,\tfrac12)$ let $E(q^n)$ denote the geometric central Cantor set obtained by taking $a_n=q^n$ in the construction above (so the surviving intervals at step $n$ have length $q^n$). 

Determine explicitly the center of distances $S(\widehat{E(q^n)})$ of the adjoint Cantorval of $E(q^n)$, as a function of $q\in(0,\tfrac12)$.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2025) develops the center-of-distances theory for central Cantor sets and Cantorvals (e.g., Banakiewicz–Bartoszewicz–Filipczak; Bielas–Plewik), but no published computation of the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval of the geometric central Cantor set $E(q^n)$ for $q\in(0,1/2)$ was located. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite triangle-free graph with m edges has the largest spectral radius? Equivalently, among all non-bipartite graphs G with m edges and no C_3 subgraph, determine the extremal graph maximizing lambda(G).

A graph is called triangle-free (or $C_3$-free) if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices, and bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two independent sets. Let $m$ be a positive even integer. Among all non-bipartite, triangle-free graphs $G$ with exactly $m$ edges, determine the maximum value of $\lambda(G)$ and characterize all graphs that attain this maximum.

A paper in the Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (v31i1p52) characterizes three kinds of spectral extremal graphs among triangle-free non-bipartite graphs of even size, providing the sharp bound and extremal graphs.

original_question: Fix k >= 2 and an even integer m. Among all non-bipartite graphs with m edges that avoid every odd cycle C_3, C_5, ..., C_{2k+1}, which graph has the largest spectral radius?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $\lambda(G)$ denote its spectral radius, i.e. the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. For an integer $k\ge 2$, a graph $G$ is said to be $\{C_3,C_5,\ldots,C_{2k+1}\}$-free if it contains no cycle of odd length $3,5,\ldots,2k+1$ as a subgraph. A graph is non-bipartite if it contains at least one odd cycle (necessarily of length $\ge 2k+3$ under the above forbidden-cycle hypothesis).

Fix an integer $k\ge 2$ and an even positive integer $m$. Let $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}$ denote the family of all non-bipartite, $\{C_3,C_5,\ldots,C_{2k+1}\}$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. Determine
$$\max\{\lambda(G) : G\in\mathcal{G}_{k,m}\}$$
and characterize all extremal graphs that attain this maximum.
status_search_result: Recent (2024–2025) work has resolved related cases (e.g., the triangle-free non-bipartite case with even size, and strong spectral stabilities for $C_{2k+1}$-free graphs), but the general problem for arbitrary $k\ge 2$ and even $m$ — identifying the extremal non-bipartite $\{C_3,\dots,C_{2k+1}\}$-free graph maximizing the spectral radius — does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature found. It is posed as an open problem in current surveys.

original_question: Fix r >= 1. For all sufficiently large m, must every B_{2,r+1}-free graph G with m edges satisfy lambda(G) <= sqrt(m), with equality only for complete bipartite graphs? Here B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \/ ((r+1)K_1) is the book graph obtained from K_{2,r+1} by adding an edge between the two vertices of degree r+1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $r \geq 1$ be a fixed integer. Define the book graph $B_{2,r+1} = K_2 \vee ((r+1)K_1)$, i.e., the graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,r+1}$ by adding an edge between its two vertices of degree $r+1$. For a simple graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix, and let $e(G)$ denote the number of edges of $G$. A graph is called $B_{2,r+1}$-free if it does not contain $B_{2,r+1}$ as a subgraph.

Prove or disprove: there exists $m_0 = m_0(r)$ such that for every $B_{2,r+1}$-free graph $G$ with $m = e(G) \geq m_0$,
$$\lambda(G) \leq \sqrt{m},$$
with equality if and only if $G$ is a complete bipartite graph.

Search results show several papers addressing closely related book/theta graph spectral problems, indicating partial progress rather than a complete resolution.
