paper_title: Open Questions in Massive Star Research across Cosmic Scales
original_question: How can resolved observations of individual massive stars and clusters be connected to integrated-light observations so that population synthesis correctly maps detailed stellar physics into galaxy-scale predictions? The answer requires determining what multi-epoch spectroscopy, ultraviolet diagnostics, and future facilities such as the Extremely Large Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory must measure to close remaining knowledge gaps in massive-star multiplicity, binary-interaction outcomes, stellar feedback, and integrated population modeling.
self_contained_problem:
Consider populations of massive stars (initial masses ≳ 8 M_sun), which can be studied in two complementary ways: (i) resolved observations, in which individual stars and star clusters are spatially and spectrally distinguished, yielding stellar parameters such as effective temperatures, luminosities, surface abundances, mass-loss rates, rotation rates, multiplicity status, and orbital parameters of binaries; and (ii) integrated-light observations, in which only the spatially unresolved combined spectrum of an entire stellar population (e.g., a distant galaxy or H II region) is available, characterized by integrated spectral energy distributions, emission and absorption line strengths, and ultraviolet (UV) continuum and wind features. Population synthesis is the modeling framework that takes as input distributions of stellar physics ingredients—initial mass function, binary fraction and orbital parameter distributions, prescriptions for stellar evolution including binary interaction (mass transfer, common envelope, mergers), stellar winds, and feedback (ionizing photon production, mechanical and radiative feedback)—and outputs predicted integrated-light observables for stellar populations of given age and metallicity.

Formulate and solve the following problem. Specify a concrete observational and modeling program that establishes a quantitative mapping from resolved stellar measurements to integrated-light predictions such that population synthesis faithfully reproduces galaxy-scale observables. In particular:

(a) Identify the minimal set of multi-epoch spectroscopic measurements (cadence, signal-to-noise, wavelength coverage, sample size as a function of metallicity) required to determine the intrinsic distributions of massive-star multiplicity properties (binary fraction, mass-ratio and period distributions) at metallicities ranging from near-solar down to those representative of the early universe.

(b) Specify which UV diagnostics (e.g., resonance wind lines, photospheric features, nebular continuum) are necessary and sufficient to constrain the outcomes of binary interaction (stripped stars, mergers, accretors, post-common-envelope systems) and their feedback contributions, and quantify the precision needed for these diagnostics to discriminate among competing binary-evolution prescriptions.

(c) Derive the sensitivity, spatial resolution, and spectral resolution requirements that future facilities of the class of a 30–40 m ground-based Extremely Large Telescope and a UV/optical/IR space-based Habitable Worlds Observatory must meet to acquire (a) and (b) for representative samples across cosmic environments.

(d) Construct an explicit prescription by which the resulting resolved-population constraints are propagated into population synthesis models so that integrated-light predictions—ionizing photon production, mechanical feedback energetics, UV spectral morphology, and chemical yields—agree with observations of unresolved stellar populations to within stated tolerances.

Provide either a constructive solution or a rigorous demonstration that such a program is sufficient to close the present knowledge gaps in massive-star multiplicity, binary-interaction outcomes, stellar feedback, and integrated population modeling.
status_search_result: This is an active, open research program in massive-star astrophysics. Connecting resolved and integrated-light observations through population synthesis remains an unsolved challenge highlighted in recent reviews, with major future facilities (ELT, HWO) still in design/planning stages and ongoing surveys (e.g., BLOeM, XShootU, ULLYSES) only beginning to deliver the requisite multi-epoch and UV data. No comprehensive solution exists in the current literature.

paper_title: Neutrino production mechanisms in strongly magnetized quark matter: Current status and open questions
context_brief: Diquark pairing effects on neutrino emission
original_question: When dense quark matter at sufficiently high density forms Cooper pairs and enters a color-superconducting state, how does the specific diquark pairing pattern modify neutrino emission rates and the associated momentum asymmetries in strongly magnetized quark matter? The problem includes determining how different pairing structures, including partially gapped and fully gapped phases, change the neutrino-emission channels relative to unpaired quark matter.
self_contained_problem:
Consider dense quark matter at zero temperature and sufficiently high baryon density that quarks near their Fermi surfaces form Cooper pairs (diquark condensates), placing the system in a color-superconducting phase. Suppose, in addition, that the matter is subject to a strong, uniform external magnetic field B (with eB comparable to relevant QCD scales), so that charged quark states are organized into Landau levels and parity along the magnetic-field direction is broken in the weak-interaction sector.

For each of the following diquark pairing patterns, considered separately:
  (i) the unpaired (normal) phase, used as a reference;
  (ii) the 2SC phase, in which only u and d quarks of two colors pair, leaving one color and the s quark ungapped (a partially gapped phase);
  (iii) the color–flavor-locked (CFL) phase, in which u, d, s quarks of all three colors are fully gapped;
  (iv) other partially gapped variants such as the gapless 2SC/CFL or dCFL phases,

compute the differential and total emissivities of the standard neutrino-producing weak processes (direct Urca q1 → q2 + ℓ + ν̄, and modified Urca with a spectator quark) for quark flavors q1, q2 ∈ {u, d, s} and ℓ ∈ {e, μ}, in the presence of the magnetic field B.

In particular:
  (a) Determine the neutrino emissivity ε_ν(T, μ, B) and its parametric dependence on the temperature T, quark chemical potentials, gap parameter Δ, and magnetic field strength B for each pairing pattern listed above, including the suppression factors associated with gapped modes.
  (b) Compute the momentum asymmetry of the emitted neutrinos along the direction of B,
     A := (∫ d³k_ν k_ν,∥ dε_ν/d³k_ν) / (∫ d³k_ν |k_ν| dε_ν/d³k_ν),
  for each pairing pattern, and compare it to the asymmetry obtained in the unpaired phase.
  (c) Identify which neutrino-emission channels remain active, are exponentially suppressed, or are newly opened (e.g., via Cooper-pair-breaking and formation processes) in each pairing pattern, and quantify how A and ε_ν depend qualitatively and quantitatively on the chosen pattern.

The problem is to provide these calculations and a complete characterization of how the diquark pairing pattern modifies neutrino emission rates and associated momentum asymmetries in strongly magnetized quark matter.
status_search_result: Neutrino emissivity calculations for color-superconducting quark matter (2SC, CFL, gapless variants) exist in zero or weak magnetic fields, but a systematic computation including strong magnetic-field-induced Landau-level structure and momentum asymmetries across the various pairing patterns has not been carried out. The question is identified as an open direction, and no comprehensive solution is found in the literature.

paper_title: Neutrino production mechanisms in strongly magnetized quark matter: Current status and open questions
context_brief: Magnetic fields and color superconductivity interplay
original_question: How do strong magnetic fields alter color-superconducting quark matter and, in turn, its neutrino emission? More specifically, how do intense magnetic fields modify the superconducting gap structure, induce anisotropies in the pairing pattern, and preferentially stabilize particular superconducting phases, and how should these effects be incorporated into a systematic calculation of neutrino emission in magnetized color-superconducting quark matter for reliable models of compact-star thermal evolution and observable signatures?
self_contained_problem:
Consider dense quark matter at finite baryon chemical potential in the presence of an external, uniform, strong magnetic field B. In the absence of the magnetic field, attractive quark–quark interactions in the color-antitriplet channel lead to a color-superconducting condensate characterized by a pairing gap Δ and a definite color–flavor pairing pattern (e.g., the color–flavor-locked (CFL) phase, the two-flavor 2SC phase, and various less-symmetric phases such as dSC, uSC, or crystalline LOFF phases). Neutrino emission from this matter (through processes such as direct Urca, modified Urca, bremsstrahlung, and Cooper-pair-breaking-and-formation) is exponentially sensitive to the gap structure and to the spectrum of low-energy quasiparticle excitations.

Develop a systematic, quantitative framework that answers the following coupled questions in a single self-consistent calculation:

1. Gap structure. Starting from a microscopic Lagrangian for quarks with electromagnetic and color gauge interactions and a four-fermion (or one-gluon-exchange) attractive channel, derive the gap equation in the presence of a magnetic field B that mixes Landau-level dynamics of the charged quark components with the color-superconducting condensate. Determine, as a function of B and chemical potential μ, the magnitude(s) and momentum/Landau-level dependence of the gap(s) Δ_a(B, μ), including the rotated U(1)_{\tilde Q} structure that leaves a residual long-range "in-medium" magnetic field.

2. Anisotropies. Quantify the anisotropy induced in the pairing pattern by B, i.e., the dependence of the gap on the direction of the quasiparticle momentum relative to B, and identify which pairing channels (singlet vs. triplet in spin, symmetric vs. antisymmetric in color and flavor) are enhanced or suppressed.

3. Phase selection. Map out the phase diagram in the (μ, B, T) space, determining which color-superconducting phase (CFL, 2SC, dSC, uSC, magnetic-CFL, paramagnetic CFL, LOFF, etc.) minimizes the free energy as B is varied through the range relevant to magnetar interiors (up to ~10^{18}–10^{20} G).

4. Neutrino emissivity. Using the resulting quasiparticle spectrum and pairing structure, compute the neutrino emissivity ε_ν(T, μ, B) and mean free path for all relevant processes, including direct quark Urca, bremsstrahlung, and pair-breaking/formation, taking proper account of Landau-level kinematics, anisotropic gap nodes (if any), and rotated-charge selection rules. Express ε_ν in a form usable as input to compact-star cooling simulations, and identify observable signatures (cooling curves, anisotropic emission) that distinguish magnetized color-superconducting matter from its B = 0 counterpart and from non-superconducting magnetized quark matter.

Provide either a closed-form result in appropriate limits or a controlled numerical scheme, and characterize the regime of validity of the approximations used.
status_search_result: The interplay between strong magnetic fields and color superconductivity is an active area of research with partial results: magnetic-field-induced modifications of the gap structure, anisotropic pairing, and the stabilization of phases such as magnetic-CFL have been studied (Ferrer–de la Incera and collaborators), and neutrino emissivities in unmagnetized color superconductors are partially known. However, a fully systematic treatment of neutrino emission in magnetized color-superconducting quark matter remains incomplete and is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: For integers n and d with 3 <= d <= n + 1, describe the K-moduli space H^K_{n,d} that parametrizes degree-d n-dimensional hypersurfaces in the range considered in the paper.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and $d$ be integers with $3 \leq d \leq n+1$. A smooth hypersurface $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}_{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $d$ is a Fano manifold (since $-K_X = (n+2-d)H|_X$ is ample under the assumption $d \leq n+1$). 

Recall that a $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety is K-semistable (resp. K-polystable) if its generalized Futaki invariant is non-negative (resp. non-negative, with equality only for product test configurations) for every normal test configuration. By the work on the construction of K-moduli (Jiang, Blum–Xu, Liu–Xu–Zhuang, Xu–Zhuang and others), there exists a projective good moduli space
$$ H^K_{n,d} $$
parametrizing K-polystable $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano varieties that arise as K-semistable degenerations of smooth degree-$d$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{n+1}$, with an open substack parametrizing the smooth hypersurfaces themselves.

Problem. For each pair $(n,d)$ with $3 \leq d \leq n+1$, give an explicit description of the K-moduli space $H^K_{n,d}$: identify all K-polystable degenerations on its boundary, describe its relation (if any) to the GIT moduli space of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{n+1}$, and determine its global geometry (e.g. as a projective variety, possibly with a wall-crossing or VGIT interpretation).
status_search_result: Explicit descriptions of K-moduli spaces of Fano hypersurfaces are known in several specific low-dimensional or low-degree cases (e.g. cubic surfaces, cubic threefolds by Liu–Xu, cubic fourfolds by Liu, quartic threefolds, quartic and quintic del Pezzo cases) and progress continues via the moduli-continuity method and wall-crossing/VGIT techniques. However, a uniform description for the full range $3 \leq d \leq n+1$ remains open in general.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g, let L be a fixed determinant line bundle of degree d on C, and let M_{d,r}(C) denote the Fano moduli space of rank-r polystable vector bundles on C with determinant L. Is M_{d,r}(C) K-stable for every such curve C? In addition, if X_g is the K-moduli space containing the point [M_{d,r}(C)] and X_g has a birational map to the moduli space M_g of smooth genus-g curves, give a modular interpretation of the limiting points of X_g.
self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g \geq 2$ over the complex numbers, let $r \geq 2$ be an integer, and let $L$ be a line bundle on $C$ of degree $d$ with $\gcd(r,d)=1$. Denote by $M_{d,r}(C)$ the moduli space of rank-$r$ stable vector bundles on $C$ with fixed determinant $L$; this is a smooth projective Fano variety.

(1) Prove that for every smooth projective curve $C$ of genus $g$, the Fano variety $M_{d,r}(C)$ is K-stable.

(2) Assuming (1), let $X_g$ denote the (projective) K-moduli space of K-polystable Fano varieties containing the points $[M_{d,r}(C)]$ as $C$ varies over smooth projective curves of genus $g$. The natural assignment $C \mapsto [M_{d,r}(C)]$ induces a birational map $\mathcal{M}_g \dashrightarrow X_g$, where $\mathcal{M}_g$ is the moduli space of smooth projective curves of genus $g$. Provide a modular interpretation of the boundary points of $X_g$ that lie outside the image of $\mathcal{M}_g$ (i.e., the limiting K-polystable degenerations of $M_{d,r}(C)$).
category_tag: K-stability of Fano moduli of vector bundles
status_search_result: The problem appears to be open in general. Recent work (e.g., on K-stability of Thaddeus' moduli of stable bundle pairs on genus two curves, 2024) addresses related but special low-genus or pair-variant cases. K-stability of $M_{d,r}(C)$ for arbitrary genus and rank, and a modular interpretation of the boundary of the corresponding K-moduli component birational to $\mathcal{M}_g$, has not been established in the literature surveyed.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: Is every smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety K-stable?
self_contained_problem:
A Gushel–Mukai (GM) variety is a smooth $n$-dimensional complex projective variety obtained as a dimensionally transverse intersection
$$X = \mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \cap \mathbb{P}(W) \cap Q,$$
where $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5) \subset \mathbb{P}^9$ is the Grassmannian of 2-planes in a 5-dimensional vector space embedded by Plücker, $\mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is the projective cone over it, $\mathbb{P}(W) \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is a linear subspace, and $Q$ is a quadric hypersurface. Smooth GM varieties of dimension $n \in \{3,4,5,6\}$ are Fano. Recall that a Fano manifold $X$ is K-stable if for every nontrivial special test configuration $(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{L}) \to \mathbb{A}^1$ for $(X, -K_X)$, the generalized Donaldson–Futaki invariant satisfies $\mathrm{DF}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{L}) > 0$.

Prove or disprove: every smooth Gushel–Mukai Fano variety (of dimension $3$, $4$, $5$, or $6$) is K-stable.
status_search_result: All smooth Gushel–Mukai threefolds are known to be K-stable (Araujo–Zhuang and related work). paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: Let X be a Fano variety. The class c_1(X) determines a canonical extension 0 -> Omega_X^{[1]} -> E -> O_X -> 0. Give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable then this extension E is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X, and that if X is K-polystable then E is polystable with respect to -K_X.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Fano variety (a normal projective variety over the complex numbers with -K_X an ample Q-Cartier divisor, having at worst klt singularities). Let Ω_X^{[1]} denote the sheaf of reflexive Kähler differentials on X. The first Chern class c_1(X) ∈ H^1(X, Ω_X^{[1]}) determines (via the Atiyah-style construction) a canonical extension of coherent sheaves

  0 → Ω_X^{[1]} → E → O_X → 0.

For a torsion-free coherent sheaf F on X, define its slope with respect to the polarization -K_X by μ_{-K_X}(F) = (c_1(F) · (-K_X)^{n-1}) / rk(F), where n = dim X. The sheaf F is called slope semistable (resp. polystable) with respect to -K_X if for every coherent subsheaf F' ⊂ F with 0 < rk(F') < rk(F) one has μ_{-K_X}(F') ≤ μ_{-K_X}(F) (resp. F is a direct sum of slope-stable sheaves of the same slope).

Prove, by purely algebraic methods (i.e., without invoking the existence of a Kähler-Einstein metric or other transcendental/analytic input), the following two statements:

(a) If X is K-semistable, then E is slope semistable with respect to -K_X.

(b) If X is K-polystable, then E is slope polystable with respect to -K_X.
status_search_result: The result is known via differential-geometric methods (using Kähler-Einstein metrics and Hermitian-Einstein structures on the canonical extension, following work of Tian and subsequent extensions). A purely algebraic proof, in the generality of K-(semi/poly)stable Q-Fano varieties not assumed to admit a Kähler-Einstein metric, is listed as an open problem in current surveys on K-stability and does not appear to have been resolved.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: Let x in X be a 2n-dimensional symplectic singularity with symplectic form omega_X. If one takes the stable degeneration x_0 in X_0 provided by the normalized-volume theory, is X_0 again symplectic, with a symplectic form omega_{X_0} obtained as a degeneration of omega_X?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $x \in X$ be a germ of a normal complex algebraic variety of dimension $2n$. Recall that $(X,x)$ is called a symplectic singularity (in the sense of Beauville) if the smooth locus $X^{\mathrm{sm}}$ carries a holomorphic symplectic 2-form $\omega_X$ such that, for some (equivalently any) resolution of singularities $\pi:\widetilde X 	o X$, the pullback $\pi^*\omega_X$ extends to a holomorphic 2-form on $\widetilde X$. In particular such an $X$ has klt singularities.

For a klt singularity $x \in X$, the Stable Degeneration Theorem (formerly the Li–Xu Stable Degeneration Conjecture) produces a canonical two-step degeneration
$$ x \in X \;ightsquigarrow\; x_0 \in X_0 $$
as follows. The normalized volume function $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{X,x}$ on the space of valuations centered at $x$ admits a (quasi-monomial) minimizer $v$, unique up to scaling. The associated graded ring $\mathrm{gr}_v \mathcal O_{X,x}$ is finitely generated, and $X_0 := \mathrm{Spec}\,\mathrm{gr}_v \mathcal O_{X,x}$ together with the vertex $x_0$ is a K-semistable log Fano cone singularity equipped with a natural torus action. This $x_0 \in X_0$ is called the stable degeneration of $x \in X$.

Problem. Suppose $x \in X$ is a $2n$-dimensional symplectic singularity with symplectic form $\omega_X$ on $X^{\mathrm{sm}}$, and let $x_0 \in X_0$ be its stable degeneration in the sense above. Show that $X_0$ is again a symplectic singularity, and moreover that there exists a holomorphic symplectic form $\omega_{X_0}$ on $X_0^{\mathrm{sm}}$ which arises as a degeneration of $\omega_X$ under the canonical degeneration $X ightsquigarrow X_0$ (i.e., as the leading term of $\omega_X$ in the filtration induced by the minimizing valuation $v$).
status_search_result: The general Stable Degeneration Conjecture for klt singularities has been established (Blum; Li–Xu; Xu; Xu–Zhuang). However, the refined question of whether the stable degeneration of a symplectic singularity is again symplectic, with symplectic form obtained as a degeneration of the original one, does not appear to be resolved in the literature; it is listed as an open problem in current surveys on K-stability of Fano varieties and symplectic singularities. No paper claiming a proof or counterexample was located.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
context_brief: Structure of minimizers for symplectic singularities
original_question: Let x in X be a symplectic singularity. Is the normalized-volume minimizer always a Kollár component E? If so, must its log discrepancy satisfy A_X(E) = r n for r equal to 1 or 2? After taking the extraction Y -> X of E and the index-one cover of that divisor, does the residue of the pulled-back symplectic form define an orbifold contact structure on E with contact line bundle O_Y(-rE)|_E? Finally, is the resulting log Fano pair underlying E always K-polystable, so that every symplectic singularity admits a Kollár component that is a contact Fano variety in the orbifold sense?
self_contained_problem:
Let $x \in X$ be a symplectic singularity of dimension $2n$; that is, $X$ is a normal complex algebraic variety with a holomorphic symplectic form $\omega_X$ on its smooth locus that extends to a regular (possibly degenerate) $2$-form on every resolution of singularities. For a klt singularity $x \in X$, the normalized volume function $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{x,X}$ is defined on the space of real valuations of $K(X)$ centered at $x$ by $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{x,X}(v) = A_X(v)^{\dim X} \cdot \mathrm{vol}(v)$, where $A_X(v)$ is the log discrepancy of $v$. A Kollár component $E$ over $x \in X$ is a prime divisor $E \subset Y$ on a proper birational model $\pi : Y \to X$ such that $-E$ is $\pi$-ample, $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $X \setminus \{x\}$, $\pi(E) = \{x\}$, and $(Y, E)$ is plt. Establish the following conjectures:

(1) The normalized-volume minimizer of $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{x,X}$ is realized (up to rescaling) by the divisorial valuation $\mathrm{ord}_E$ associated with some Kollár component $E$.

(2) For this Kollár component one has $A_X(E) = r n$ with $r \in \{1, 2\}$.

(3) Let $\pi : Y \to X$ extract $E$ as a Kollár component, and let $\widetilde{Y} \to Y$ be the index-one cover of $E \subset Y$ producing $\widetilde{E} \subset \widetilde{Y}$. Then the pullback $\pi^*(\omega_X)$ lies in $H^0(\widetilde{Y}, \Omega^2_{\widetilde{Y}}(\log \widetilde{E})(-r\widetilde{E}))$, and its Poincaré residue $\theta = \partial(\pi^*\omega_X) \in H^0(\widetilde{E}, \Omega^1_{\widetilde{E}} \otimes \mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{Y}}(-r\widetilde{E})|_{\widetilde{E}})$ defines an orbifold contact structure on $\widetilde{E}$ with contact line bundle $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{Y}}(-r\widetilde{E})|_{\widetilde{E}}$.

(4) The log Fano pair underlying $E$ is K-polystable.

(5) Consequently, every symplectic singularity $x \in X$ admits a Kollár component which is a contact Fano variety in the orbifold sense.
status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as an open problem about the structure of normalized-volume minimizers for symplectic singularities. While related rank-one minimizer results and K-semistability/Kollár component theory have been developed (e.g. by Li–Xu, Liu–Xu, Zhuang and recent work on canonical torus actions on symplectic singularities), no source found establishes all five parts (Kollár-component minimizer, log discrepancy $rn$ with $r\in\{1,2\}$, orbifold contact structure from the residue, K-polystability, and contact-Fano realization) for every symplectic singularity. The problem appears to be open.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
context_brief: Uniform local-volume lower bounds in MMP
original_question: Fix a klt pair (X, Delta). Does there exist a positive constant epsilon such that for every (K_X + Delta)-nonnegative birational map X --> X' and every point x in X', the normalized volume of x in (X', Delta') satisfies vol^(x, X', Delta') >= epsilon?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a klt pair, i.e. $X$ is a normal quasi-projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$ and $\Delta$ is an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$ such that $K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and the pair has Kawamata log terminal singularities. For a closed point $y$ on a klt pair $(Y,\Delta_Y)$, the normalized volume of $y$ is
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(y,Y,\Delta_Y)\;=\;\inf_{v}\;A_{(Y,\Delta_Y)}(v)^{\dim Y}\,\mathrm{vol}(v),$$
where the infimum is taken over all real valuations $v$ of the function field of $Y$ centered at $y$, $A_{(Y,\Delta_Y)}(v)$ is the log discrepancy of $v$ with respect to $(Y,\Delta_Y)$, and $\mathrm{vol}(v)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathcal{O}_{Y,y}/\mathfrak{a}_m(v))/(m^{\dim Y}/(\dim Y)!)$ is the volume of $v$.

A birational map $\varphi\colon X\dashrightarrow X'$ to a normal projective variety $X'$ (with $\Delta'$ the strict transform of $\Delta$ on $X'$, so that $(X',\Delta')$ is also klt and $K_{X'}+\Delta'$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier) is called $(K_X+\Delta)$-nonnegative if for every common resolution $p\colon W\to X$, $q\colon W\to X'$ one has
$$p^*(K_X+\Delta)\;-\;q^*(K_{X'}+\Delta')\;\geq\;0.$$

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(X,\Delta)>0$ such that for every $(K_X+\Delta)$-nonnegative birational map $\varphi\colon X\dashrightarrow X'$ as above and every closed point $x\in X'$,
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X',\Delta')\;\geq\;\varepsilon.$$
status_search_result: The question of a uniform positive lower bound on normalized volumes across all points appearing on $(K_X+\Delta)$-nonnegative birational models of a fixed klt pair is listed as an open problem in current surveys on K-stability and singularities. Existing results give pointwise positivity of the normalized volume (Li, Liu–Xu, Han–Liu–Qi) and uniform lower bounds in bounded families, but a uniform bound depending only on the fixed pair $(X,\Delta)$ across all MMP-type birational models has not been established in the literature surveyed.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
context_brief: Valuations computing lct of graded ideals
original_question: Let x in (X = Spec(R), Delta) be a klt singularity, let a_• be an m_x-primary graded sequence of ideals, let c = lct(X, Delta; a_•), and let LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) be the valuations computing that log canonical threshold. Must every valuation in LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) be quasi-monomial? More strongly, does there exist a log smooth model (Y, E) -> X such that LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) is contained in QM(Y, E) and forms a cone over a connected convex set?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(X = \mathrm{Spec}(R), \Delta)$ be a klt singularity at a closed point $x \in X$; here $R$ is a Noetherian local ring (or the local ring at $x$ of a normal variety) with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}_x$, and $\Delta$ is an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$ such that $K_X + \Delta$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and $(X,\Delta)$ has Kawamata log terminal singularities.

Let $a_\bullet = \{a_m\}_{m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}}$ be an $\mathfrak{m}_x$-primary graded sequence of ideals on $X$, i.e. each $a_m \subseteq R$ is $\mathfrak{m}_x$-primary and $a_p \cdot a_q \subseteq a_{p+q}$ for all $p,q \ge 1$. Define the log canonical threshold
$$ c \;=\; \mathrm{lct}(X,\Delta;\, a_\bullet) \;=\; \lim_{m\to\infty} m\cdot \mathrm{lct}(X,\Delta;\, a_m). $$

For a real valuation $v$ of the function field of $X$ centered at $x$, let $A_{X,\Delta}(v)$ denote its log discrepancy, and set $v(a_\bullet) = \lim_{m\to\infty} v(a_m)/m$. Define
$$ \mathrm{LCP}(X,\Delta + c\cdot a_\bullet) \;=\; \bigl\{\, v \;:\; A_{X,\Delta}(v) \,=\, c\cdot v(a_\bullet),\ \ 0 < A_{X,\Delta}(v) < \infty \,\bigr\}, $$
the set of (nontrivial) valuations computing this log canonical threshold.

A log smooth model $\pi:(Y,E) \to X$ is a proper birational morphism from a regular scheme $Y$ with a reduced simple normal crossing divisor $E = \sum_{i=1}^N E_i$ such that $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $X \setminus \{x\}$. For any point $\eta \in Y$ that is the generic point of a connected component of $\bigcap_{i \in I} E_i$ for some $I \subseteq \{1,\dots,N\}$, and any tuple $\alpha = (\alpha_i)_{i \in I} \in \mathbb{R}^I_{\ge 0}$, one obtains a quasi-monomial valuation $v_\alpha$ of $K(X)$ via the regular system of parameters defining $E$ at $\eta$. Let $\mathrm{QM}(Y,E)$ be the set of all such quasi-monomial valuations.

Questions.
(1) Is every valuation $v \in \mathrm{LCP}(X,\Delta + c\cdot a_\bullet)$ quasi-monomial?
(2) (Stronger form) Does there exist a log smooth model $(Y,E) \to X$ such that
$$ \mathrm{LCP}(X,\Delta + c\cdot a_\bullet) \;\subseteq\; \mathrm{QM}(Y,E), $$
and such that, viewed inside $\mathrm{QM}(Y,E)$, the set $\mathrm{LCP}(X,\Delta + c\cdot a_\bullet)$ is a cone over a connected convex set?
category_tag: K-stability and valuations on klt singularities
status_search_result: The weaker form of the Jonsson–Mustaţă conjecture is known to hold in dimension two and reduces in general to the case of graded sequences of valuation ideals on affine space. Existence of some quasi-monomial valuation computing the lct of a graded sequence is established (Jonsson–Mustaţă), and Xu's theorem "A minimizing valuation is quasi-monomial" (Ann. of Math. 2020) settles a closely related minimizing problem. However, the full statement that every valuation in LCP$(X,\Delta + c\cdot a_\bullet)$ is quasi-monomial, and the stronger cone/convexity statement, remain open in general.

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
context_brief: Reduction mod p and Frobenius volume
original_question: Let x in (X, Delta) be a klt singularity over characteristic 0, and for each sufficiently large prime p let x_p in (X_p, Delta_p) be its reduction modulo p. Is the characteristic-zero normalized volume always the limit of the positive-characteristic Frobenius volumes, namely vol^(x, X, Delta) = lim_{p -> infinity} Fvol(x_p, X_p, Delta_p)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a klt pair defined over a field of characteristic zero (say a finitely generated $\mathbb{Q}$-subalgebra $A\subset\mathbb{C}$), and let $x\in X$ be a closed point such that the germ $x\in(X,\Delta)$ is a klt singularity. Recall that the normalized volume function of Li is defined on the space $\mathrm{Val}_{X,x}$ of real valuations of the function field of $X$ centered at $x$ by
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{(X,\Delta),x}(v) \;=\; A_{(X,\Delta)}(v)^{n}\cdot\mathrm{vol}(v),$$
where $n=\dim X$, $A_{(X,\Delta)}(v)$ is the log discrepancy of $v$ with respect to $(X,\Delta)$, and $\mathrm{vol}(v)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\ell(\mathcal{O}_{X,x}/\mathfrak{a}_m(v))/(m^n/n!)$ is the volume of $v$. The normalized volume of the singularity is
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X,\Delta)\;=\;\inf_{v\in\mathrm{Val}_{X,x}}\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{(X,\Delta),x}(v).$$

For each sufficiently large prime $p$, choose a model of $(X,\Delta)$ over $\mathrm{Spec}\,A$ and let $x_p\in(X_p,\Delta_p)$ denote the reduction modulo $p$ of the singularity $x\in(X,\Delta)$ (so $X_p$ is a variety over a field of characteristic $p$). In characteristic $p>0$, the Frobenius-volume (or $F$-volume) of a klt singularity $y\in(Y,\Gamma)$ of dimension $n$ is defined via the Frobenius signature/F-signature-type invariant by
$$\mathrm{Fvol}(y,Y,\Gamma)\;=\;\inf_{\mathfrak{a}\,\mathfrak{m}\text{-primary}} \mathrm{lct}(Y,\Gamma;\mathfrak{a})^{n}\cdot e_{HK}(\mathfrak{a}),$$
or equivalently through the analogous Frobenius-theoretic local volume invariant, where $\mathrm{lct}$ is the log canonical threshold and $e_{HK}$ is the Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity (and one may equivalently use the $s$-invariant / F-signature formulation appropriate to klt pairs in characteristic $p$).

Question: does one always have
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X,\Delta)\;=\;\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathrm{Fvol}(x_p,X_p,\Delta_p)\;?$$

paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
original_question: Is the Frobenius volume Fvol(x, X) of a singularity always an algebraic number?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, x)$ be the germ of a Noetherian local ring of positive characteristic $p > 0$ at a closed point $x$, assumed to be an $F$-finite normal local domain with an isolated non-regular point at $x$ (or more generally a klt-type singularity in characteristic $p$). For each positive integer $e$, let $F^e \colon X \to X$ denote the $e$-th iterate of the absolute Frobenius endomorphism, and consider the asymptotic invariant
$$\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X) \;=\; \lim_{e \to \infty} \frac{1}{p^{e \cdot \dim X}} \cdot \mathrm{(Frobenius\ length/colength\ invariant\ at\ }x\mathrm{)},$$
the Frobenius volume of the singularity $(x \in X)$, defined as the appropriate normalization of the Frobenius pushforward / splitting data attached to the singularity (so that, e.g., for a smooth point $\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X) = 1$).

Question: Is $\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X)$ always an algebraic number, for every such singularity $(x \in X)$?
status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The algebraicity of Frobenius-type singularity invariants (such as Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity, F-signature, and the Frobenius volume) is a well-known open question in the theory of F-singularities; even the rationality of the Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity remains famously unresolved, and no source found establishes algebraicity of $\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X)$ in general.

original_question: For each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems, develop theoretically and practically fast algorithms.
self_contained_problem: Consider families of linear systems of the form A(p) x = b(p), where p ranges over a parameter domain P (for example a compact subset of R^k) and, for each p in P, A(p) is an n by n real or complex matrix and b(p) is a vector of length n, with the entries of A(p) and b(p) depending on p in a prescribed (e.g. polynomial, rational, or affine) way. Such a family is called a class of parameterized benchmark linear systems. For each natural class of such families (e.g. symmetric positive definite, sparse with banded structure, arising from discretized PDEs, Toeplitz/Hankel, low displacement rank, or affinely parameterized), design an algorithm that, given p in P, returns x(p) satisfying A(p) x(p) = b(p), and that is simultaneously: (i) provably fast, in the sense that its worst-case arithmetic complexity is asymptotically smaller (in n and in the parameter encoding size) than that of a generic dense direct solver, with rigorous error and stability guarantees; and (ii) practically fast, in the sense that an implementation outperforms standard general-purpose solvers on representative benchmark instances of the class. State for which classes such algorithms exist and characterize the achievable complexity.
status_search_result: The problem as posed is a broad research program rather than a single conjecture, asking for fast solvers for each class of parameterized benchmark linear systems. No single result resolves all classes; while many specific structured classes (e.g. Toeplitz, banded, hierarchical, reduced-basis parametric systems) have efficient solvers, a complete answer covering all benchmark classes is not established.

Let $A_n C^n x n$, $n>= 1$, be a sequence of random positive definite matrices constructed via A_n = U Lambda_n U*, where U C^n x n is Haar unitary, Lambda_n = diag 1^-p, 2^-p, ..., n^-p . What is the asymptotic behavior of $T_ CG(A_n,b_n,epsilon)$ compared with $T_ RCD(A_n,b_n,epsilon)$ as $n -> infinity$?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and $p > 0$ be fixed constants. For each integer $n \geq 1$, define a random positive definite matrix $\mathbf{A}_n \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ by
$$\mathbf{A}_n = \mathbf{U}\,\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_n\,\mathbf{U}^*,$$
where $\mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ is Haar-distributed on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(n)$, and $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_n = \operatorname{diag}(1^{-p}, 2^{-p}, \ldots, n^{-p})$. Let $\mathbf{z}_n \in \mathbb{C}^n$ be drawn uniformly from the unit sphere, independently of $\mathbf{U}$, and set $\mathbf{b}_n = \mathbf{A}_n \mathbf{z}_n$.

For a Hermitian positive definite $\mathbf{A}$ and right-hand side $\mathbf{b}$, let $T_{\mathrm{CG}}(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{b},\varepsilon)$ denote the smallest number of iterations $k$ such that the conjugate gradient iterate $\mathbf{x}_k$ (started from $\mathbf{x}_0 = \mathbf{0}$) applied to the linear system $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ satisfies
$$\|\mathbf{x}_k - \mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{b}\|_{\mathbf{A}} \leq \varepsilon\,\|\mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{b}\|_{\mathbf{A}},$$
where $\|\mathbf{v}\|_{\mathbf{A}} = \sqrt{\mathbf{v}^*\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}}$. Let $T_{\mathrm{RCD}}(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{b},\varepsilon)$ denote the analogous expected stopping time for the randomized coordinate descent method applied to the quadratic $\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{x}^*\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \Re(\mathbf{b}^*\mathbf{x})$, where at each iteration a coordinate is selected uniformly at random and the iterate is updated by exact minimization along that coordinate, with the same relative error stopping criterion.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $T_{\mathrm{CG}}(\mathbf{A}_n,\mathbf{b}_n,\varepsilon)$ as compared with $T_{\mathrm{RCD}}(\mathbf{A}_n,\mathbf{b}_n,\varepsilon)$ as $n \to \infty$ (in particular, the leading-order growth rates and their ratio, in probability or expectation).

original_question: Find the smallest $p>0$ such that we can solve an $n x n$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $~ O(T_A*bar kappa_p)$ arithmetic operations, where $bar kappa_p$ is the $p$-averaged condition number of the singular values of $A$, whereas $T_A$ is either $n^2$ or $nnz(A)$.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be an invertible matrix with singular values $\sigma_1(A) \ge \sigma_2(A) \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_n(A) > 0$, and for $p > 0$ define the $p$-averaged condition number
$$\bar{\kappa}_p(A) \;=\; \left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{\sigma_1(A)}{\sigma_i(A)}\right)^p\right)^{1/p}.$$
Let $\mathcal{T}_A$ denote either $n^2$ or $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ (the number of nonzero entries of $A$). We say a randomized algorithm solves the linear system $Ax = b$ to high accuracy if, for any input vector $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and any target accuracy $\varepsilon > 0$, it returns (with high probability) a vector $\tilde{x}$ with $\|\tilde{x} - A^{-1}b\| \le \varepsilon \|A^{-1}b\|$, with running time depending only polylogarithmically on $1/\varepsilon$.

Determine the smallest real number $p > 0$ such that there exists an algorithm solving every such linear system $Ax = b$ to high accuracy using $\widetilde{O}\big(\mathcal{T}_A \cdot \bar{\kappa}_p(A)\big)$ arithmetic operations (where $\widetilde{O}$ hides factors polylogarithmic in $n$, $\bar\kappa_p(A)$, and $1/\varepsilon$).
status_search_result: No direct evidence was found that this question (smallest $p$ for which $\widetilde{O}(\mathcal{T}_A \bar\kappa_p)$-time high-accuracy linear solvers exist) has been resolved. General results on averaged condition numbers exist, but a tight characterization of the optimal $p$ does not appear in the readily searchable literature, so the status is unknown.

original_question: Let $A$ be an $n x n$ random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian (or Rademacher, or Bernoulli) entries, and take any $n$-dimensional vector $b$. Is it possible (conditioned on a high-probability event) to solve the linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy faster than $O(n^omega)$?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the exponent of square matrix multiplication, i.e., the infimum of all real numbers $\tau$ such that two $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{R}$ can be multiplied using $O(n^\tau)$ arithmetic operations.

Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ random matrix whose entries are independent and identically distributed, drawn from one of the following distributions:
(i) the standard Gaussian $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$;
(ii) the Rademacher distribution (uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$);
(iii) the Bernoulli distribution (uniform on $\{0,1\}$, or with parameter $1/2$).

Let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be an arbitrary (deterministic) vector. Consider the task of computing, to high accuracy (say to within additive error $2^{-\mathrm{poly}(n)}$ in some natural norm), a vector $x$ satisfying $Ax = b$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, conditioned on an event of probability $1 - o(1)$ over the randomness of $A$, solves the linear system $Ax = b$ to high accuracy in time $O(n^{\omega - \varepsilon})$ for some constant $\varepsilon > 0$ (in either the arithmetic or bit complexity model)?
category_tag: Random linear systems and matrix multiplication exponent
status_search_result: The general question of solving an $n\times n$ dense linear system faster than $O(n^\omega)$ remains open. Peng and Vempala (SODA 2021; JACM 2024) gave an algorithm beating matrix multiplication for sparse linear systems (with $o(n^{(\omega-1)/\log\kappa(A)})$ nonzeros and polynomial condition number), but no analogous result is known for dense random matrices with i.i.d. Gaussian/Rademacher/Bernoulli entries. The dense random case appears to still be open.

original_question: What is the bit complexity of solving an $n x n$ linear system with $nnz(A)$ non-zeros? In particular, does the $~ O(n* nnz(A))$ runtime extend to the Word-RAM model.
self_contained_problem: Consider the problem of solving a linear system $Ax=b$ where $A\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}$ is given as input together with $b\in\mathbb{Q}^n$, and let $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ denote the number of nonzero entries of $A$. The goal is to output, in the Word-RAM model of computation (with words of size $O(\log n)$ bits and unit-cost operations on such words), a vector $\tilde x\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ approximating a solution to within $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ accuracy, while accounting for the bit length of all intermediate quantities. Determine the bit complexity, as a function of $n$ and $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ (and the condition number $\kappa(A)$), of solving such an $n\times n$ linear system. In particular, does there exist a Word-RAM algorithm that achieves running time $\widetilde O(n\cdot \mathrm{nnz}(A))$ (up to polylogarithmic factors in $n$ and $\kappa(A)$) for solving sparse linear systems, matching the bound known in the real-arithmetic / exact-arithmetic model?
category_tag: bit complexity of sparse linear system solvers
status_search_result: The question of whether the $\widetilde O(n\cdot\mathrm{nnz}(A))$ runtime for sparse linear system solving extends to the Word-RAM model has seen recent progress. Peng–Vempala (2020) gave an algorithm faster than matrix multiplication for sparse systems, and follow-up work (e.g., "The Bit Complexity of Efficient Continuous Optimization", 2023, and "Numerical Linear Algebra in Linear Space", 2025) has tightened bit-complexity bounds in the Word-RAM model. However, an exact $\widetilde O(n\cdot\mathrm{nnz}(A))$ Word-RAM bound matching the real-RAM analysis has not been established in full generality, so the question appears to remain partially open.

original_question: Develop a descriptive convergence bound for GMRES applied to nonnormal linear algebraic systems, that particularly describes the (transient) behavior early in the iteration.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a nonsingular, generally nonnormal matrix, let $b \in \mathbb{C}^n$, and consider the linear system $Ax = b$. Starting from an initial guess $x_0$ with initial residual $r_0 = b - Ax_0$, the GMRES method produces iterates $x_k \in x_0 + \mathcal{K}_k(A, r_0)$, where $\mathcal{K}_k(A, r_0) = \mathrm{span}\{r_0, A r_0, \dots, A^{k-1} r_0\}$, that minimize the residual norm:
$$\|r_k\|_2 = \min_{p \in \mathcal{P}_k,\ p(0)=1} \|p(A) r_0\|_2,$$
where $\mathcal{P}_k$ denotes polynomials of degree at most $k$.

For nonnormal $A$ the curve $k \mapsto \|r_k\|_2 / \|r_0\|_2$ frequently exhibits an initial phase of slow decrease (transient stagnation) followed by a faster asymptotic decay, and classical eigenvalue-based bounds (such as those involving the condition number of an eigenvector basis or the spectral $\varepsilon$-pseudospectra) typically fail to be descriptive in the early iterations.

Problem. Derive an upper bound 
$$\frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|r_0\|_2} \le \Phi(A, r_0, k)$$
that is valid for all $k \ge 0$ and that is descriptive in the following sense: it captures, in particular, the transient (early-iteration) behavior of $\|r_k\|_2$ for nonnormal $A$, in that the bound $\Phi(A, r_0, k)$ accurately reflects the magnitude and duration of the initial near-stagnation phase rather than merely the eventual asymptotic rate. The quantities entering $\Phi$ should depend on computable spectral, pseudospectral, field-of-values, or polynomial-numerical-hull information about $A$ and on $r_0$.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers (e.g., Embree's "How descriptive are GMRES convergence bounds?", Meurant's notes, and the 2023 work "Extending Elman's Bound for GMRES") confirm that finding a descriptive convergence bound for GMRES on nonnormal systems—especially one capturing the transient/initial stagnation phase—remains an active research challenge. Existing eigenvalue-, pseudospectra-, and field-of-values-based bounds typically overestimate residual norms during the transient phase, and no fully descriptive general bound is known.

original_question: Explain the convergence acceleration of GMRES after the initial (transient) phase that is observed in some convection-diffusion model problems such as the one in~. In particular, explain whether or not the speed of convergence can be related to eigeninformation (i.e., eigenvalue location and eigenvector conditioning) of the discretized convection-diffusion operators.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a steady linear convection-diffusion boundary-value problem on a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of the form
$$-
u\,\Delta u + \mathbf{w}\cdot
abla u = f \quad	ext{in }\Omega,\qquad u = g \quad	ext{on }\partial\Omega,$$
where $
u>0$ is a (small) diffusion coefficient and $\mathbf{w}\in\mathbb{R}^d$ is a constant convection field. Discretize this problem on a uniform tensor-product grid using either a streamline upwind Petrov–Galerkin (SUPG) finite element method or a standard upwind/central finite difference method, producing a nonsymmetric linear system
$$A x = b,\qquad A\in\mathbb{R}^{N	imes N}.$$
Apply the GMRES iterative method to $Ax=b$ starting from $x_0=0$, and let $r_k = b - Ax_k$ be the $k$-th residual. In numerical experiments on such systems one observes a two-phase convergence behavior: an initial phase of slow ("transient" or stagnation-like) reduction of $\|r_k\|$, followed by a second phase in which the rate of relative residual reduction markedly accelerates.

Provide a rigorous explanation of this convergence acceleration after the initial transient phase. In particular, decide and justify whether the asymptotic (post-transient) rate of GMRES convergence on such discretized convection-diffusion operators $A$ can be quantitatively predicted from spectral information alone—that is, from the location of the eigenvalues of $A$ together with the conditioning $\kappa(V)$ of the eigenvector matrix $V$ in a diagonalization $A = V\Lambda V^{-1}$—or whether the observed convergence rate is intrinsically governed by additional, non-spectral features of $A$ and the right-hand side $b$ (such as the structure of $b$ relative to invariant subspaces, departure from normality measured by pseudospectra or field of values, or the block/Toeplitz structure inherited from the discretization).
status_search_result: For specific convection-diffusion model problems the two-phase GMRES behavior has been explained without using eigendecompositions: an orthogonal reduction to block tridiagonal Toeplitz form yields sharp descriptions of both the initial transient and the subsequent acceleration. More generally, eigenvalue-plus-eigenvector-conditioning bounds are widely accepted as descriptively poor for these highly nonnormal operators, and pseudospectra/field-of-values or right-hand-side-dependent analyses are required. A complete, fully general explanation that covers all discretized convection-diffusion operators remains an active topic, so the broader question is best regarded as only partially resolved.

original_question: Show that the CG and Lanczos algorithms do or do not behave similarly in finite precision arithmetic when used to solve a symmetric positive definite linear system. This will, of course, depend on the implementation of each method, so use standard good implementations of both.
category_tag: Conjugate Gradient and Lanczos methods in finite precision
status_search_result: The question is an open-ended exercise asking for a comparative analysis of CG and Lanczos in finite precision. The general topic has been studied extensively (notably by Paige, Greenbaum, Strakoš, Meurant, and others), who showed that finite-precision CG behaves like exact CG applied to a larger matrix with clustered eigenvalues, and that loss of orthogonality and delay of convergence occur in closely related ways for CG and Lanczos. However, as stated the prompt is a pedagogical/research exercise rather than a precisely formulated conjecture with a definitive solved/open status, so its status is best regarded as unknown.

original_question: Analyze the Lanczos algorithm under general models of inexact matrix-vector multiplication and/or the use of a preconditioner. Progress is made if these bounds generalize Paige's analysis and/or provide new, easier to understand, insight into the behavior of the algorithm.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be a symmetric matrix and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|b\|_2 = 1$. The Lanczos algorithm produces, in exact arithmetic, an orthonormal basis $\{q_1,\dots,q_k\}$ of the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b) = \mathrm{span}\{b, Ab, \dots, A^{k-1}b\}$ together with a symmetric tridiagonal matrix $T_k = Q_k^T A Q_k$ via the three-term recurrence
\[
\beta_{j+1} q_{j+1} = A q_j - \alpha_j q_j - \beta_j q_{j-1}, \qquad \alpha_j = q_j^T A q_j,
\]
with $q_1 = b$ and $\beta_1 = 0$. Paige's classical analysis bounds, in finite precision arithmetic, the residuals
\[
A Q_k - Q_k T_k - \beta_{k+1} q_{k+1} e_k^T = F_k,
\]
the local orthogonality $|q_{j+1}^T q_j|$, and the deviation $|q_j^T A q_j - \alpha_j|$ in terms of unit roundoff $\varepsilon$ and $\|A\|$, and uses these to relate convergence of Ritz values to loss of orthogonality.

Consider now an inexact Lanczos process in which the matrix-vector product $Av$ is replaced by $Av + g(v)$, where $g:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is a perturbation modeling either inexact matrix-vector multiplication (e.g., $\|g(v)\|_2 \le \eta_j \|v\|_2$ for a sequence of tolerances $\eta_j$) or the application of a preconditioner $M \approx A^{-1}$ (so that the recurrence is run with $M A$ or with an inexact action of $M$).

Provide rigorous a-priori bounds, in this inexact and/or preconditioned setting, on:
(i) the columnwise residual $\|F_k\|$ of the perturbed three-term recurrence;
(ii) the local loss of orthogonality $|q_{j+1}^T q_j|$ and the local discrepancy $|q_j^T A q_j - \alpha_j|$;
(iii) the resulting effect on Ritz value convergence,
in terms of $\varepsilon$, $\|A\|$, the perturbation sizes $\eta_j$, and (when applicable) spectral properties of the preconditioner. The bounds should reduce to Paige's bounds when $g \equiv 0$ and no preconditioner is used, and/or should yield qualitatively new, more transparent insight into the behavior of the inexact/preconditioned Lanczos algorithm.
status_search_result: The literature confirms that Paige's analysis governs unpreconditioned finite-precision Lanczos, and that extending such bounds to preconditioned and inexact-matvec variants remains an active and largely open research direction. Recent works (e.g., 2025 results on finite precision block Lanczos) continue to address related cases without producing a unified Paige-style theory for general inexact/preconditioned Lanczos.

original_question: Deterministic Pseudospectral Shattering: Give a provably correct and efficient deterministic algorithm for the following task: on input $A C^n x n$ and $delta>0$, output a perturbation $E$ with $ |E | delta$ such that $kappa_eig(A+E) C(delta/n)^c$, where $C,c$ are universal constants. In this context, efficient means $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ arithmetic operations, either in exact arithmetic or, more ambitiously, in finite arithmetic with $O( ^c(n/delta))$ bits of precision.
self_contained_problem:
For a matrix $M\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ that is diagonalizable as $M=VDV^{-1}$ with $D$ diagonal, define the eigenvector condition number
$$\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(M)=\inf_{V}\,\|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|,$$
where the infimum is over all such diagonalizations and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the spectral norm (set $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(M)=\infty$ if $M$ is not diagonalizable).

Construct a deterministic algorithm with the following provable guarantee. There exist universal constants $C,c>0$ such that, given as input any matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with $\|A\|\le 1$ and any parameter $\delta>0$, the algorithm outputs a perturbation $E\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with
$$\|E\|\le\delta\qquad\text{and}\qquad \kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(A+E)\le C\left(\frac{n}{\delta}\right)^{c}.$$
The algorithm must be efficient, in the sense of using $O(n^3\,\log^{c}(n/\delta))$ arithmetic operations, either in exact arithmetic, or—more ambitiously—in finite-precision arithmetic with $O(\log^{c}(n/\delta))$ bits of precision.

Either exhibit such a deterministic algorithm together with a proof of correctness, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
status_search_result: Existing pseudospectral shattering algorithms (Banks–Garza-Vargas–Kulkarni–Srivastava and the generalized/sparse extensions) are randomized: they rely on adding a random Gaussian (or sparse random) perturbation to achieve the eigenvector-conditioning guarantee. Subsequent work through 2024 (generalized pencils, sparse perturbations) still uses randomness, and no deterministic polynomial-time algorithm achieving the stated guarantee appears in the literature, indicating the problem remains open.

original_question: Give a provable randomized algorithm for backward error diagonalization or Schur form with runtime $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ that only uses $O( (n/delta))$ bits of precision.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ and let $\delta\in(0,1)$. A backward-error diagonalization (resp. Schur form) of $A$ to accuracy $\delta$ is the computation of matrices $V,D$ (resp. $Q,T$) such that
$$\|A - VDV^{-1}\|\le \delta\|A\| \quad\text{(resp. } \|A - QTQ^{*}\|\le \delta\|A\|\text{)},$$
where $D$ is diagonal (resp. $T$ is upper triangular) and, in the Schur case, $Q$ is unitary. The arithmetic is performed in floating-point with $b$ bits of mantissa precision; the runtime is measured in bit operations (or, equivalently, arithmetic operations on $b$-bit numbers).

Construct a provable randomized algorithm that, given any $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with $\|A\|\le 1$ and any $\delta\in(0,1)$, with high probability outputs a backward-error diagonalization or Schur form of $A$ to accuracy $\delta$, satisfying both of the following:
1. The total runtime is $O\!\bigl(n^{3}\log^{c}(n/\delta)\bigr)$ arithmetic operations for some absolute constant $c\ge 0$.
2. The algorithm uses only $O(\log(n/\delta))$ bits of precision throughout.

Equivalently, exhibit such an algorithm or prove that no such algorithm exists.
status_search_result: The best known provable randomized backward-error diagonalization algorithm (Banks–Garza-Vargas–Kulkarni–Srivastava, "Pseudospectral Shattering" / "The Complexity of Diagonalization", STOC 2023) achieves runtime O(T_MM(n) log^c(n/δ)) using O(log^c(n/δ)) bits of precision (polylogarithmic, not logarithmic). Achieving the n^3 polylog runtime together with only O(log(n/δ)) bits of precision remains an open problem; recent works (e.g. randomized normal-matrix diagonalization, 2024–2025) make partial progress for structured cases but do not resolve the general question.

original_question: Let $Q$ be an orthonormal basis for a Krylov space for arbitrary $A ^n x n$ with random starting vector $b$. Is $kappa_V(Q*AQ)$ bounded (by a polynomial in $n$) with high probability? Or is $ [ _ (Q*AQ)]$ (the expected value of the area in $ $ of the $epsilon$-pseudospectrum) bounded by $ (n) ^beta$ for $beta$ close to 2? (This problem is open even when $A$ is a circulant shift matrix.)
self_contained_problem:
Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be an arbitrary matrix and let $b\in\mathbb{C}^n$ be a random starting vector (e.g., with i.i.d. complex Gaussian entries). For an integer $1\le k\le n$, let $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,A^2b,\ldots,A^{k-1}b\}$ denote the associated Krylov subspace, and let $Q\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times k}$ be a matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis of $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b)$. Set $H=Q^*AQ\in\mathbb{C}^{k\times k}$ (the Krylov compression of $A$).

Recall that, for a diagonalizable matrix $M=V\Lambda V^{-1}$, the eigenvector condition number is $\kappa_V(M)=\inf_V \|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|$ over all such diagonalizations, and that the $\varepsilon$-pseudospectrum is 
$$\Lambda_\varepsilon(M)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: \|(zI-M)^{-1}\|\ge \varepsilon^{-1}\}.$$

Address either of the following questions (taking $k=n$, say):

(a) Is there a polynomial $p$ such that with probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$ (over the randomness of $b$),
$$\kappa_V(Q^*AQ)\le p(n)\,?$$

(b) Does there exist $\beta$ close to $2$ and a polynomial $q$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{area}\bigl(\Lambda_\varepsilon(Q^*AQ)\bigr)\bigr]\le q(n)\,\varepsilon^\beta\,?$$

The problem is to be resolved even in the special case where $A$ is the $n\times n$ circulant shift matrix (the permutation matrix corresponding to the cyclic shift $i\mapsto i+1 \pmod n$).
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as open, even in the circulant-shift special case. No web evidence of a resolution was found; recent work on pseudospectral shattering and random perturbations by Banks–Kulkarni–Mukherjee–Srivastava and others addresses related questions for Gaussian-perturbed matrices but does not resolve the Krylov-compression version.

original_question: Consider a general nonnormal matrix $A = V Lambda V^-1$ with largest eigenvalue magnitude $lambda_1$ and finite eigenvector condition number $kappa_V = |V | |V^-1 |$. Is there an algorithm that uses $ ( (nkappa_V),1/epsilon)$ matrix-vector products with $A$ and returns $lambda$ so that $|lambda - lambda'| epsilon |lambda_1|$, where $lambda'$ is any eigenvalue of $A$ with $|lambda' | (1-epsilon) lambda_1$?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ be a (possibly nonnormal) diagonalizable matrix written as $A = V \Lambda V^{-1}$, where $\Lambda = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)$ with $|\lambda_1| \ge |\lambda_2| \ge \cdots \ge |\lambda_n|$, and let the eigenvector condition number be $\kappa_V = \|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|<\infty$ (operator $2$-norm). One is allowed only "matrix-vector product" queries to $A$: in each query, an algorithm chooses a (possibly randomized, possibly adaptive) vector $v \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and receives $Av$.

Given $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, decide whether there exists an algorithm that, using at most
$$\mathrm{poly}\!\left(\log(n\kappa_V),\, 1/\epsilon\right)$$
matrix-vector product queries to $A$, outputs a complex number $\widehat\lambda$ such that
$$|\widehat\lambda - \lambda'| \le \epsilon\,|\lambda_1|$$
for some eigenvalue $\lambda'$ of $A$ satisfying $|\lambda'| \ge (1-\epsilon)\,|\lambda_1|$. Either exhibit such an algorithm or prove that no such algorithm exists.
category_tag: Matrix-vector query complexity for eigenvalue approximation
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. The problem of approximating the top eigenvalue of a general nonnormal diagonalizable matrix in poly(log(n κ_V), 1/ε) matrix-vector queries appears to remain an open question in the matrix-vector query complexity literature; results are known for normal/Hermitian cases (e.g., via Lanczos/Krylov methods), but the nonnormal regime with dependence only polylog in κ_V is not known to be settled.

original_question: Does the QRCP algorithm typically used in practice satisfy the above, or a similar, bound.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \le n$ be positive integers and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$ have orthonormal rows, i.e. $A A^{\top} = I_k$. Apply the Businger–Golub QR factorization with column pivoting (QRCP), as customarily implemented in numerical linear algebra software (e.g. LAPACK's xGEQP3): this greedy algorithm produces a permutation $\Pi \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, an orthogonal $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times k}$, and an upper-trapezoidal $R = [R_{11}\ R_{12}] \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$ with $R_{11} \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times k}$ upper triangular, such that $A \Pi = Q R$, where at each step the pivot column is chosen to be the remaining column of largest Euclidean norm in the current trailing submatrix.

Let $B \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times k}$ denote the submatrix of $A$ formed by the first $k$ columns of $A \Pi$ (equivalently, the $k$ columns of $A$ selected by QRCP). Because the rows of $A$ are orthonormal, $|\det(B)|$ equals the $k$-dimensional volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these columns and is at most $1$.

Question: Does the standard practical QRCP algorithm described above always satisfy a lower bound of the form
$$|\det(B)| \;\ge\; \frac{1}{f(k,n)}$$
(equivalently $\sigma_{\min}(B) \ge 1/g(k,n)$) for some function $f$ (or $g$) growing at most polynomially in $k$ and $n$, matching — or close to — the bound that holds for an optimal column subset of $k$ columns of $A$ with orthonormal rows? More generally, does QRCP as used in practice achieve a strong column-subset-selection bound on matrices with orthonormal rows?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2026 Simons workshop collection on linear systems and eigenvalue problems. Recent literature on QRCP (BQRRP, CQRRPT, randomized column-pivoted QR, and analyses of Businger–Golub pivoting) studies rank-revealing and column-subset-selection guarantees, but no source located establishes a polynomial bound proving that the standard practical QRCP achieves the sought guarantee on matrices with orthonormal rows; classical worst-case examples (Kahan-type) suggest the question remains nontrivial and unresolved.

original_question: Consider $n$ positive real numbers $lambda$, and consider the set of all $n x n$ orthonormal matrices $S$. Prove a tightness bound(s) between the (1) trace error of the optimal column subset selection of the worst case matrix $K$ possessing eigenvalues $lambda$: x_k (lambda) := _V S _ [n], | | = k K - K_:, K_ , ^-1 K_ ,: _K=V^ -> p diag(lambda) V and (2) the objective yielded by volume sampling any such $K$: y_k (lambda) := (E_ k-DPP(K) K- K_:, K_ , ^-1 K_ , :) _K=diag(lambda) = (k+1) e_k+1 (lambda)e_k(lambda) which is dependent on $lambda$ alone in terms of the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_k$.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer, fix $k \in \{1,\dots,n-1\}$, and let $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ be a vector of positive real numbers. Let $S$ denote the set of $n \times n$ real orthogonal matrices. For a positive semidefinite matrix $K \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and a subset $\mathcal{I} \subseteq [n] := \{1,\dots,n\}$, write $K_{:,\mathcal{I}}$ for the submatrix of $K$ formed by the columns indexed by $\mathcal{I}$, $K_{\mathcal{I},:}$ for the submatrix of rows indexed by $\mathcal{I}$, and $K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}}$ for the principal submatrix indexed by $\mathcal{I}$. Define the worst-case optimal $k$-column subset trace error among matrices with spectrum $\lambda$ by
$$x_k(\lambda) := \max_{V \in S}\; \min_{\substack{\mathcal{I} \subseteq [n] \\ |\mathcal{I}|=k}} \operatorname{Tr}\!\left( K - K_{:,\mathcal{I}} K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}}^{-1} K_{\mathcal{I},:} \right) \Bigg|_{K = V^\top \operatorname{diag}(\lambda) V}.$$
A $k$-DPP with kernel $K$ is the probability distribution on size-$k$ subsets $\mathcal{I} \subseteq [n]$ given by $\Pr(\mathcal{I}) \propto \det(K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}})$. Define the volume sampling objective on the diagonal representative by
$$y_k(\lambda) := \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{I} \sim k\text{-DPP}(K)} \operatorname{Tr}\!\left( K - K_{:,\mathcal{I}} K_{\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I}}^{-1} K_{\mathcal{I},:} \right) \Bigg|_{K = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda)} = (k+1)\, \frac{e_{k+1}(\lambda)}{e_k(\lambda)},$$
where $e_j(\lambda)$ denotes the $j$-th elementary symmetric polynomial in $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$.

Establish tight comparison bounds between $x_k(\lambda)$ and $y_k(\lambda)$. Specifically, determine the best (smallest) constants $C_k = C_k(n)$ and $c_k = c_k(n)$, possibly depending on $n$ and $k$ but independent of $\lambda$, such that
$$c_k \cdot y_k(\lambda) \le x_k(\lambda) \le C_k \cdot y_k(\lambda)$$
holds for every vector $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^n$, and exhibit extremal spectra achieving equality.

Standard references (Guruswami–Sinop, Deshpande–Rademacher, Derezinski–Warmuth) provide one-sided bounds via volume sampling but not a matching tightness characterization, so the status is taken to be unknown.

original_question: Randomized SVD: Let (A R^n x d ) be a matrix, fix $r > 0$, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $r$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let $~A = (AOmega)(AOmega)^+A$ denote the randomized SVD approximation to $A$, and let $A_r$ be the best rank-$r$ approximation to $A$ with respect to the Frobenius norm. Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A - ~A |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) |A-A_r |_ F? ]
self_contained_problem:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes d}$ and fix an integer $r>0$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, call a (random) matrix $\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes k}$ an oblivious subspace injection of dimension $r$ with injectivity $1-\varepsilon$ if, for every fixed $r$-dimensional subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}$, with high probability the map $x\mapsto \Omega^{	op}x$ restricted to $V$ satisfies
$$(1-\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\le \|\Omega^{	op}x\|_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\qquad	ext{for all }x\in V.$$
Define the randomized SVD approximation
$$	ilde A \;=\; (A\Omega)(A\Omega)^{+}A,$$
where $(\cdot)^{+}$ denotes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, and let $A_r$ be a best rank-$r$ approximation to $A$ in the Frobenius norm, i.e. a minimizer of $\|A-B\|_F$ over all matrices $B$ of rank at most $r$.

Prove or disprove: there is an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $A$, $r$, $n$, $d$, $k$) such that
$$\|A-	ilde A\|_F \;\le\; (1+C\varepsilon)\,\|A-A_r\|_F.$$
status_search_result: This is the standard guarantee for sketch-based randomized low-rank approximation. Sarlós (2006) and the analyses of subspace-embedding-based randomized SVD (e.g., Clarkson–Woodruff, Halko–Martinsson–Tropp, Woodruff's survey "Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra") establish that if $\Omega$ is an oblivious subspace embedding for $r$-dimensional subspaces with distortion $\varepsilon$, then $\|A-(A\Omega)(A\Omega)^+A\|_F \le (1+O(\varepsilon))\|A-A_r\|_F$. The statement is therefore known to be true.

original_question: Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: Subspace embedding properties of sparse random matrices: Prove or disprove the Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: A SparseStack embedding with parameters $ = O(( r) / epsilon)$ and $k = O(r / epsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with parameters $alpha = 1 - epsilon$ and $beta = 1+epsilon$.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For integers $n \geq m \geq 1$, an $m \times n$ random matrix $S$ is called an oblivious subspace embedding (OSE) with parameters $(\alpha, \beta)$, distortion, and rank $r$, if for every fixed $r$-dimensional linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, with high probability one has
$$\alpha \, \|x\|_2 \;\leq\; \|S x\|_2 \;\leq\; \beta \, \|x\|_2 \qquad \text{for all } x \in V.$$

The SparseStack construction with parameters $(k, \zeta)$, where $k$ is the number of rows and $\zeta$ is the column sparsity, is the random $k \times n$ matrix obtained as follows. Partition the $k$ rows into $\zeta$ equal blocks of size $k/\zeta$. In each block, every column is zero except in one row chosen independently and uniformly at random, where the entry is an independent $\pm 1/\sqrt{\zeta}$ Rademacher random variable. The full SparseStack matrix is the vertical stack of these $\zeta$ independent block matrices.

Problem (Nelson–Nguyen conjecture). Let $r \geq 1$ be an integer and $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$. Prove or disprove: there exist absolute constants such that the SparseStack embedding with column sparsity 
$$\zeta = O\!\left(\frac{\log r}{\varepsilon}\right) \quad\text{and number of rows}\quad k = O\!\left(\frac{r}{\varepsilon^2}\right)$$
is an oblivious subspace embedding for $r$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with parameters $\alpha = 1 - \varepsilon$ and $\beta = 1 + \varepsilon$.
status_search_result: The Nelson–Nguyen conjecture has seen substantial recent progress but is not fully resolved at the exact target parameters. Chenakkod, Dereziński, Dong, and Rudelson (arXiv:2311.10680, 2023) established optimal embedding dimension m = O(d/ε²) with sparsity O(log⁴ d) per column. Dereziński, Yang and collaborators (arXiv:2411.08773, 2024) achieved optimal dimension with near-optimal sparsity Õ(1/ε). A 2025 work (arXiv:2508.14234) is titled "Resolving Nelson–Nguyen Conjecture Up to Sub-Polylogarithmic Factors," indicating the conjecture is settled up to sub-polylogarithmic factors but not at the precise O((log r)/ε), O(r/ε²) bounds.

original_question: Rerandomized subsampled trigonometric transforms: Assume that $n = Omega( r)$. Prove or disprove: The rerandomized SRHT of dimension $k = O(r/epsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with $alpha = 1-epsilon$ and $beta = 1+epsilon$.
self_contained_problem:
Let $H_n \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ denote the (normalized) Walsh–Hadamard matrix on $n$ points (assume $n$ is a power of two), so that $H_n^\top H_n = I_n$. For a positive integer $k \le n$ define the subsampled randomized Hadamard transform (SRHT) by
$$ S \;=\; \sqrt{n/k}\, P\, H_n\, D, $$
where $D \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is a random diagonal sign matrix whose diagonal entries are i.i.d. uniform on $\{\pm 1\}$, and $P \in \{0,1\}^{k \times n}$ is a uniformly random row-subsampling matrix that selects $k$ rows of $H_n D$ (with or without replacement).

A rerandomized SRHT of dimension $k$ is the random linear map obtained by drawing an independent fresh copy $(D, P)$ of the SRHT for each input vector (equivalently, the sketch is allowed to be redrawn for each query rather than fixed once and applied to all of a subspace simultaneously).

For parameters $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, a positive integer $r$, and constants $0 < \alpha \le \beta$, a random matrix $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$ is called an oblivious subspace embedding for $r$-dimensional subspaces with distortion $(\alpha, \beta)$ if, for every fixed $r$-dimensional linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$ \Pr\!\Big[\, \alpha \|x\|_2 \le \|Sx\|_2 \le \beta \|x\|_2 \ \text{for all } x \in V \,\Big] \;\ge\; 1 - \delta, $$
for some absolute constant $\delta \in (0,1)$ (e.g. $\delta = 1/3$).

Assume $n = \Omega(\log r)$. Prove or disprove the following statement: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every $r$-dimensional subspace and every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, the rerandomized SRHT with embedding dimension
$$ k \;=\; C\, r / \varepsilon^2 $$
is an oblivious subspace embedding with $\alpha = 1 - \varepsilon$ and $\beta = 1 + \varepsilon$.
category_tag: randomized numerical linear algebra / subspace embeddings
status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2025) establishes that sparse oblivious subspace embeddings can attain the optimal embedding dimension $m = \Theta(r/\varepsilon^2)$ (resolving the Nelson–Nguyen conjecture up to sub-polylogarithmic factors), and standard SRHT analyses give $k = \tilde O(r/\varepsilon^2)$ with extra $\log$ factors. However, no source directly confirms that the specifically rerandomized SRHT achieves the clean optimal $k = O(r/\varepsilon^2)$ bound under the stated assumption $n = \Omega(\log r)$. The status of this exact statement could not be verified.

original_question: What is the asymptotic error $epsilon_m*$ as a function of $m$ and $delta$?
self_contained_problem:
For a parameter $\delta\in(0,1)$ and an integer $m\ge 1$, let $\mathcal{P}_m$ denote the set of real polynomials of degree at most $m$, and define the best uniform approximation error to the sign function on the symmetric two-interval set $[-1,-\delta]\cup[\delta,1]$ by
$$\epsilon_m^*(\delta)\;=\;\inf_{p\in\mathcal{P}_m}\;\sup_{x\in[-1,-\delta]\cup[\delta,1]}\bigl|\operatorname{sgn}(x)-p(x)\bigr|,$$
where $\operatorname{sgn}(x)=1$ for $x>0$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(x)=-1$ for $x<0$. Determine the precise asymptotic behavior of $\epsilon_m^*(\delta)$ as $m\to\infty$, as an explicit function of $m$ and $\delta$.
status_search_result: The exact asymptotic of the best uniform polynomial approximation error to $\operatorname{sgn}(x)$ on $[-1,-\delta]\cup[\delta,1]$ is known. Eremenko and Yuditskii established that $\epsilon_m^*(\delta)\sim \tfrac{1-\delta}{\sqrt{\pi\delta}}\cdot\tfrac{2}{\sqrt{m-1}}\bigl(\tfrac{1-\delta}{1+\delta}\bigr)^{(m-1)/2}$ as $m\to\infty$, with extremal polynomials described via conformal maps onto comb-like domains. The problem is therefore solved in the asymptotic sense.

paper_title: Pulsars and Millisecond Pulsars I: Advancements, Open Questions and finding Gaps via statistical insights
original_question: How do different binary-system configurations affect the spin-up of neutron stars into pulsars or millisecond pulsars? In particular, how do structural properties of the neutron star, such as its spin and magnetic field, together with orbital parameters such as semi-major axis and eccentricity, change the efficiency and outcome of the accretion-driven transfer of angular momentum that accelerates the neutron star's rotation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a binary system consisting of a neutron star of mass $M_{\mathrm{NS}}$, radius $R_{\mathrm{NS}}$, moment of inertia $I$, surface dipolar magnetic field strength $B$, and initial spin angular frequency $\Omega_0$, in orbit with a companion star of mass $M_c$ on a Keplerian orbit characterized by semi-major axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$. Suppose mass transfer occurs via either Roche-lobe overflow or stellar-wind accretion at a rate $\dot{M}(t)$, and that accreted matter forms (where applicable) a Keplerian disk truncated at the magnetospheric (Alfvén) radius
$$r_m \;=\; \left(\frac{B^2 R_{\mathrm{NS}}^6}{\dot{M}\sqrt{2 G M_{\mathrm{NS}}}}\right)^{2/7},$$
with corotation radius $r_{\mathrm{co}} = (G M_{\mathrm{NS}}/\Omega^2)^{1/3}$. The angular momentum evolution of the neutron star is governed by
$$I\,\dot{\Omega} \;=\; \dot{M}\,\sqrt{G M_{\mathrm{NS}} r_m}\;-\;N_{\mathrm{mag}}(\Omega,B,r_m,r_{\mathrm{co}}),$$
where $N_{\mathrm{mag}}$ is the magnetic propeller/braking torque, which depends on the fastness parameter $\omega_s = (r_m/r_{\mathrm{co}})^{3/2}$.

Determine, as a function of the parameters $(B, \Omega_0, a, e, M_c, \dot{M})$:
(i) the conditions under which the neutron star is spun up to the millisecond regime (final spin period $P_{\mathrm{spin}} \lesssim 10$ ms);
(ii) the total accreted mass $\Delta M$ and timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{rec}}$ required for recycling to that regime;
(iii) the dependence of the spin-up efficiency $\eta = \Delta\Omega/\Delta M$ on orbital eccentricity $e$ and semi-major axis $a$, including the role of periastron-enhanced accretion in eccentric orbits;
(iv) the threshold magnetic field above which the propeller effect prevents spin-up entirely.

Provide quantitative criteria and asymptotic regimes characterizing the outcome (isolated recycled pulsar versus millisecond pulsar versus spin-down) in terms of the listed parameters.
status_search_result: The recycling scenario for millisecond pulsar formation is broadly accepted, but the detailed dependence of spin-up efficiency on binary structural and orbital parameters (especially eccentricity, magnetic-field decay during accretion, and the propeller/accretion transition) remains an active area of research with no closed-form quantitative solution; this is generally treated as an open modeling problem in pulsar astrophysics.
